# 2026-08-02 note: the scroll-sequence converter has been REMOVED (block, routes, settings tab, worker pipeline). What was the sequence worker is now the media worker: video optimise only, no rembg/onnxruntime/numpy/Pillow, no baked-in ONNX models. Everything below about matting, see-through gaps, white un-blend and engines is history, kept because it explains why the Fly app is still called `cactus-seqworker`. See the top Last-updated entry.
# FIELD_NOTES.md

Last updated: 2026-08-23 (**A new entry no longer arrives already marked as paid - `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.16**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1209**.** `TransactionForm.tsx` opened a new entry with `settledDate: today()` alongside `taxPointDate: today()`, so a bill typed in on the day it landed recorded itself as SETTLED unless somebody noticed the pre-filled box and cleared it. That one date is the whole test for settlement everywhere downstream: branch 4 of `LEDGER_SQL` (`lib/ledger.ts`) posts the money side only `WHERE t."settled_date" IS NOT NULL`, falling back to `COALESCE(ba.account_id, ctrl.default_bank, ctrl.suspense)` when no bank account was named, and `agedAnalysis()` (`lib/reports.ts`) counts an entry as outstanding on exactly `settled_date IS NULL`. Net effect on live Deskwell: two unpaid Ionos bills (£1.20 and £2.40, 2026-07-22) took £3.60 out of the bank on paper, parked it on the seeded `bank-current` account because the install predates the Paid-from field, put `bank-current` on the balance sheet under 'Cash at bank and in hand' beside Tide, and left 'Who owes what' reporting nothing owed. **Fix is one default:** `settledDate: ''`, plus a `hint`-styled `<p id="bk-settled-hint">` under the field (`aria-describedby` on the input) saying empty means not paid yet and the entry shows under what is owed until it is filled in. Nothing else moved - `lib/transactions.ts` already reads an absent date as not settled (`input.settledDate ? parseDate(...) : null`) at all three call sites, the form already sent `value.settledDate || null`, and the reconcile (`lib/reconcile-actions.ts` 194, 781) and external-sales (`lib/external-sales.ts` 433, 793) paths supply a real date of their own. Gates: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 173 module tests pass (49 live tests skipped, no DB credentials exported for the run). No schema change, so no backup round-trip gate. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained a 'Date it was paid' paragraph including how to correct entries recorded before this changed. **Housekeeping note:** the two entries below and the category-accounts one still say 'working tree, version NOT bumped, nothing released' - all three shipped in `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.15**, pinned by core **0.5.1208**.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Changing the VAT rate on an existing line grew the total by the VAT - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, version NOT bumped, nothing released.** Chris: bring a line in from a bank statement, open it, move it from zero rated to 20%, and "Total including VAT" went from £20.00 to £24.00. `changeRate()` in `TransactionForm.tsx` always held the NET and recomputed gross as net + VAT, so the one figure that was actually a fact - the money that left the account - was the one it moved. The importer was right all along: `splitGross()` in `lib/reconcile-actions.ts` takes the VAT OUT of the gross, so coding a line on the reconcile screen and coding the same line by opening the entry produced two different receipts. **Fix:** a client-only `anchor: 'net' | 'gross'` on the form's line, set by whichever amount box was last typed in (`changeNet` -> net, `changeGross` -> gross), defaulting to gross for a new line and for every line loaded into the edit form - which is every imported one. Gross-anchored, the total holds and the VAT comes out of it; net-anchored, it goes on top. VAT is the remainder rather than a second rounding, so `gross = net + vat` to the penny and the line's CHECK constraint cannot bite. Anchor is stripped alongside `uid` before the body is sent. **Arithmetic moved out of the component** into `components/admin/format.ts` (`pence`, `fromPence`, `vatForNet`, `netForGross`, new `resplitAtRate`), which is what makes it testable at all - new `components/admin/line-amounts.test.ts`, 8 cases including the £20 statement line, the penny-exactness sweep, the empty-gross fallback, and one asserting it agrees with the importer's own split. Gates: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, `npm test` 2586 passed. No schema change, so no backup round-trip needed. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` says which box holds still.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Receipts open in the browser instead of downloading, and an entry can say no receipt is coming - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, version NOT bumped, nothing released.** Same working tree as the category-accounts entry below. **Viewing.** `app/api/admin/uk-bookkeeping/attachments/[id]/route.ts` forced `Content-Disposition: attachment` on everything, deliberately - the old comment says nothing in an evidence folder should be rendered in the admin's origin, which is the right worry (an uploaded SVG or HTML file is script running with the admin's session). Remedy replaced rather than removed: `VIEWABLE_IN_BROWSER` allowlist (`application/pdf`, `image/png|jpeg|gif|webp|heic|heif`) gets `inline`, everything else still gets `attachment`, and `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` is now load-bearing since the stored mime type comes from what the browser reported at upload - it stops a file declared as a PDF being sniffed as HTML and run. SVG and HTML are NOT on the list and must not be added. `?download=1` forces the save. `EvidenceDropzone` opens the name in a new tab (`rel=noopener noreferrer`) with a small **Download** link beside it. **Evidence not required.** New column `bk_transactions.evidence_not_required BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE` - migration `015_evidence_not_required.sql` (idempotent `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) AND the same column added to `001_initial.sql` in place for fresh installs. Carried through `types.ts`, `TransactionInput`, the INSERT, the UPDATE (`undefined` means KEEP, same trap as `bank_account_id`), `TransactionBody` zod, and `lib/export.ts` (header + SELECT). New `TransactionFilter.evidenceNotRequired` plus the query-string pass-through on the list route. Tickbox at the foot of the entry form's top card; `TransactionDetail` carries it through the edit round trip and passes `notRequired` to `EvidenceDropzone`, which then drops the six-year nag and says why. `TransactionsScreen` prints a grey `✕` in the evidence column when the flag is on and there are no attachments, and its one **Evidence** select now drives TWO filter keys: All / Has a receipt / **Still needs one** (`hasEvidence=0` AND `evidenceNotRequired=0`) / **None needed**. `lib/dashboard.ts` `missingEvidence` excludes flagged entries - the whole point, since a top-up counted as missing paperwork for six years is how a genuinely missing receipt stops being noticeable. NOT done and worth a thought later: shop-handed-over sales (`lib/external-sales.ts`) still count as missing evidence, and their invoice lives in the shop. Gates: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, `npm test` 2578 passed. **Backup round-trip REQUIRED and RUN** (new column): `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` with the OVH credentials exported from the Deskwell folder - 3 tests, real PASS, byte-identical restore. Live suites re-run one file at a time and all green: ledger guards (re-runs every migration), ledger projection, import round-trip, and `category-accounts.live.test.ts` which gained a case proving a marked entry lands in **None needed** and out of **Still needs one**. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained the tickbox note and a 'Looking at a receipt you have attached' section.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Every category now has a ledger account, and an entry can say which account paid it - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, version NOT bumped, nothing released.** Chris needed to record a prepaid balance held with a supplier: twenty pounds paid onto an account against a statement that is not a VAT invoice, then monthly usage invoices WITH VAT drawn off that balance. Two gaps in the way. **(1) A category added through the settings screen had no ledger account.** `lib/ledger.ts` posts the analysis side of a cashbook line to the account its category points at; with none it goes to Suspense, the trial balance stops agreeing and `ledgerHealth()` reports the books unhealthy. `createCategory` never made one and the screen had no field for it. `lib/categories.ts` now creates the category and its account in ONE `prisma.$transaction` - either an account the caller named (`accountId`) or a new one shaped by `accountShapeForCategory()` in `lib/accounts.ts` (new, pure, tested in `lib/category-accounts.test.ts`). The shape is copied from the account the seeded category being filed 'like' already uses (`likeCategoryCode`, which is exactly the question the settings screen already asks): a P&L template lends its `report_group` and `disallowable_percent` while the new category's own direction picks the kind; a BALANCE SHEET template is copied whole, because a second drawings category wants a second equity account and not a cost. No template: `pl-<code>`, named after the category, positioned `1000 + position` - identical to what `006_accounts_and_journals.sql` seeded. `createAccount(input, db?)` gained an optional tx client so it can join that transaction. `pointAccountAtCategory()` clears any other account naming the same category first, since two would be a duplicate mapping the projection has to guess between. New migration `migrations/014_category_accounts.sql` backfills existing installs (two passes, `pl-<code>` then `pl-<code>-<md5>`, both `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`; it does nothing where nothing is missing). Categories POST/PATCH take `accountId`; POST also takes `likeCategoryCode`. Settings screen shows 'posts to X' under every category name, offers a picker on Change, and a 'Which account it posts to' select on the add form. **(2) A hand-typed entry could not say which account paid it.** `bank_account_id` has been on `bk_transactions` since `005_bank_statements.sql` and in `createTransaction`, but not in `TransactionBody` (`lib/validation.ts`) and not on the form, so anything not raised from a bank line settled to `bank-current`. Added to the zod body, so POST and PUT both carry it; `updateTransaction` now writes it with `undefined` meaning KEEP - a blank would have moved every edited reconciled entry onto the main current account, the same trap `is_capital` had. `TransactionForm` grows a 'Paid from' / 'Paid into' select (only when bank accounts exist; blank = main current account, so nothing already recorded changes meaning), `TransactionDetail` carries it through the edit round trip and prints it. `assertBankAccountUsable()` turns a bogus or archived id into a sentence rather than an FK 500; the bulk reconcile path uses `insertTransactionRows` directly and is untouched by it. **The workflow this buys:** a Cash-type bank account named after the supplier, a category pointed at it, top-ups recorded against the bank as outside-the-scope, each usage invoice recorded with its real VAT and Paid from the balance. Balance drains, bank stays honest, VAT lands in box 4 on the invoice date. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained a 'Money you have paid a supplier in advance' section plus Paid-from and posts-to notes. Gates: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, `npm test` 2578 passed. Also run against a real Postgres: new `lib/category-accounts.live.test.ts` (throwaway `cactus_rt_catacc_*` on the OVH VPS, `RUN_LEDGER_GUARDS=1`) proves 014 backfills an account-less category and is idempotent on a re-run, that `createCategory` makes or claims exactly one account, that a second category cannot take an account already spoken for AND that the refusal takes the category row with it, and walks the supplier balance end to end: bank -20.00, balance 15.20, `pl-office` 4.00, `vat-control` -0.80, ledger balanced and healthy. `ledger-guards.live.test.ts` re-runs every migration and stayed green. NB the three live files contend if run in one parallel vitest pass (SSH auth refusals, then a 5s timeout); run them one file at a time. Backup round-trip NOT run and not gated: 014 adds no table, column, sequence or type, only rows.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**A Push no longer dies when one tab loses every one of its rows - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **0.1.70**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1207**.** Google refuses a `deleteDimension` that would take every non-frozen row of a sheet, and this module walks straight into that: `lib/workbook.ts` freezes the header row and `ROW_SLACK = 0` trims each tab to exactly its content, so a tab holding a header and N data rows is N+1 tall with one frozen and N deletable. Let all N rows be doomed at once - a range re-coded so no old variant SKU survives, a listing rebuilt, a tab gone fully blank - and `pushGrids` asks for all N non-frozen rows: `Invalid requests[0].deleteDimension: Sorry, it is not possible to delete all non-frozen rows.` The batch is atomic so nothing landed, and the stepped-job retry budget then spent all eight attempts on the same deterministic 400. **Fix:** new exported `rowPadForDeletes(grid, doomedCount)` in `lib/push-grid.ts` returns the shortfall (`doomed - (rowCount - frozenRowCount - 1)`, floored at 0) and `pushGrids` emits an `appendDimension` for it in the SAME batchUpdate, ahead of that tab's deletes - appended rows sit below every doomed index so they shift nothing, the delete leaves one blank row standing, and the resize pass trims the tab back to real content, so the padding never survives the push it was needed for. `resizeRequests` now works off a `sizes` copy of the grid map carrying `rowCount + pad`, or it would read the padded tab as already the right size and leave the blank row behind; its `grids` param is typed `SheetGrid` rather than the inline shape. `getSheetGrids` (`lib/sheets.ts`) asks for and returns `frozenRowCount`, which is what makes the shortfall knowable, and `SheetGrid` in `lib/capacity.ts` carries it as optional so existing fixtures still build one. 5 new cases in `lib/capacity.test.ts`. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` clean, 226 module tests pass. No schema change, so no backup gate. **Known, not fixed:** `describeFailure` correctly marks a 400 non-transient but `components/useSteppedJob.ts` never reads the flag, so any deterministic failure still burns the whole eight-retry budget.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Sub-category pill strip can be capped at the busiest N with the rest behind a "more" toggle - `shop` **0.1.290**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1206**.** A category with thirty sub-categories printed thirty pills, so the shopper met a wall of navigation before the first product. New Puck field on **Shop: Category Browser** - `pillLimit` ("Pills: show only this many, busiest first (0 shows all)"), default **0** so every existing page renders exactly as it did. **Ordering** is the rolled-up product count, not the direct one: new `getPublicCategoryProductCounts()` in `modules/shop/lib/db/catalogue.ts` (direct counts per category, ACTIVE and `catalogue_hidden = false`, so drafts and variant children are not counted), then `rollUpProductCounts()` in `ShopCategoryPills.shared.ts` sums each category over its own sub-tree in JS from the category list the block already holds - no second query, and cycle-safe with a visited set for the same reason the SQL descendant walk uses UNION. Ties break on name so the strip never reshuffles between renders. The count query only runs when the cap is actually biting (`limit > 0 && limit < categories.length`). **The fold is CSS, never a shorter render**: `splitPillsByPopularity()` returns `{shown, hidden}` and `ShopCategoryPills` prints BOTH, the hidden ones as `.shop-cat-pill-extra`, so every sub-category link is in the HTML for crawlers. Toggle is a visually-hidden checkbox inside its own `<label class="shop-cat-pill shop-cat-more">` (RSC block, no client half to hydrate, so no JS) driving `.shop-cat-pills-limited:has(.shop-cat-more-input:checked)`. All of the hiding sits behind `@supports selector(:has(*))`: a browser without `:has` never hides the extras and never prints the toggle, so it gets the old wrapping strip rather than a dead button over a truncated menu. Focus ring borrowed onto the pill via `.shop-cat-more:has(:focus-visible)` since the checkbox is off-screen. Editor half (`ShopCategoryBrowser.tsx`) folds its sample pills the same way through the same classes, keeping canvas/live parity. Tests: 11 new cases in `ShopCategoryPills.shared.test.ts` (roll-up incl. cycle, ordering, tie-break, no-limit passthrough, `:has` fallback shape). `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` clean, 462 shop tests pass. No schema change, so no backup gate. Wiki: `Shop.md`.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Category and collection long descriptions now fold behind a Read more at EVERY width, not just on a phone - `shop` working tree only, no version bump, nothing released.** Chris on the category and filter-collection pages: the page opens with three paragraphs (the header's short blurb full width, then the long description's two paragraphs in columns beneath it), and he wants only the first showing, with a Read more under it that opens the other two - at all viewport widths, not the mobile-only fold that was there. **`modules/shop/components/public/ShopCategoryDescriptionClamp.tsx` is gone**, replaced by `ShopCategoryDescriptionFold.tsx` (same `shop-cat-desc-fold` / `shop-cat-desc-toggle` class names, so nothing else has to move). The line clamp went with it: the fold is now the whole block, hidden by the `hidden` attribute rather than `-webkit-line-clamp`, so all the machinery that existed only to make a clamp work at one breakpoint is gone too - the `breakpoints` prop, the `@media (max-width: mobileBp)` wrapper, the `columns:auto !important` reset that the clamp needed to beat the caller's inline column rules, the `data-needed` measurement, and the exported `watchFoldSize` helper with its ResizeObserver + resize-listener + `document.fonts.ready` triple (plus `ShopCategoryDescriptionClamp.watch.test.ts`). Nothing measures anything any more: hidden is hidden at every width, so the toggle is always needed. Kept: server-rendered folded (`data-folded="true"` + `hidden`) so there is no CLS, `<noscript>` releasing the fold (`.shop-cat-desc-fold[hidden]{display:block!important}` - `!important` because `[hidden]` is a UA rule) and hiding the inert button, `aria-expanded`/`aria-controls`, the full text always in the markup for crawlers, and the `foldStyle` prop carrying the caller's `columnWidth:26rem; columnGap:3rem` onto the folded box. `ShopDesignedDescriptionBody.tsx` drops its `getShopBreakpoints()` await (nothing else there wanted it) and calls the fold in both branches - one paragraph and many. **The visible first paragraph is the header block's `shortDescription`** (`ShopCategoryHeader.rsc` / `ShopCollectionHeader.rsc`, falling back to `description`), not part of the fold, so on a category with no short blurb the page shows heading then Read more. A *designed* `descriptionPuck` document is still never folded. New `ShopCategoryDescriptionFold.test.tsx` (7) pins the failure modes: arrives folded, full text still in the markup, no `@media` and no `-webkit-line-clamp` anywhere, toggle visible at every width, noscript releases it, toggle wired to the region, `foldStyle` lands on the folded box. **SEO note handed to Chris:** the long description is now `display:none` on desktop too, where it used to be visible prose. `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .`, `npm test` (2556 passed) clean. No schema change, so no backup gate. Wiki: `Shop.md`. No version bumped, nothing committed or released.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Platform and Deskwell split into two projects - core working tree only, nothing released.** Chris: Cactus is meant for lots of people with ordinary needs, and a great deal of Deskwell-only work had piled up inside the platform repo. **Moved out** to `/Users/chris/Git Local/Deskwell/Claude` (new working folder with its own `CLAUDE.md`, `.env`, `notes/infrastructure.md`, `package.json` carrying `pg` + `playwright`): the six site skills (`deskwell-product-import`, `deskwell-sequence-description`, `deskwell-video-logo-outro`, `dynamic-clearance` were tracked under `.agents/skills/` and so shipped to every install through the updater; `deskwell-blog-post` and `deskwell-product-video` were untracked), the `.claude/skills` symlinks, `deskwell_blog/`, `clearance.json`, `variation_slug_rebuild_2026_08_23/`, `.claude/deskwell/` (Neon-era dev env, archived as obsolete), the `deskwell` entry in `.claude/launch.json`, the `deskwell_blog/` gitignore line, and the whole `~/.cactus-3d-tools` toolbox (now `Deskwell/Claude/3d-tools`, symlinked back from `~/.cactus-3d-tools` so every old path still works). Skill scripts and docs re-pointed at the workspace root `.env`; the four-levels-up root discovery in `import_lib.py` still lands on the workspace. 104 Deskwell memory files moved to `~/.claude/projects/-Users-chris-Git-Local-Deskwell-Claude/memory/` with their own index; platform and module knowledge (p3d/pad/pat/svr traps, shop DB seams) stays. **Docs:** `AGENTS.md` Live-infrastructure block (VPS IP, Neon ids, backup paths, media naming) replaced with a keys list and a pointer to the workspace; `CLAUDE.md` gains the platform-vs-site rules (nothing site-specific in core or public modules, a site need becomes a setting/module/option). **Audit result:** core and module code were already clean - every `Deskwell` in `lib/`, `proxy.ts` and the modules is a worked example in a comment. One real hardcode found: `live-chat`'s self-serve provisioning built every new chat server from `registry.fly.io/deskwell-chat:latest`, a private Fly-org image no other install could pull. **`live-chat` 0.1.20** (working tree): `app/api/admin/provision/route.ts` default is now `ghcr.io/cactus-foundation-modules/chatwoot:latest`, overridable by `LIVECHAT_IMAGE` env or a new optional **Chat server image** field on the setup form (validated as a plain registry reference, carried in `provision_state.image`). Deskwell unaffected - pre-provisioned via `LIVECHAT_*`, and machine updates reuse the machine's own image. The public image does not exist yet: `plans/chatwoot-image-public-ghcr.md` holds the workflow diff for the image repo. Wiki: `Live-Chat.md`, `Configuration-reference.md`. `product-checks-for-shop` stays private/Deskwell-only - Chris reconfirmed. **Follow-up same day:** the root `.env` MOVED to the Deskwell folder and a blank, commented `.env` left in its place - the platform repo carries no credentials at all now; `CLAUDE.md`/`AGENTS.md` and memory say so, the backup round-trip gate needs the OVH keys exported per run, and `Deskwell/Claude/scripts/dev.sh` is how the real site is run locally. `cactus-foundation-modules/chatwoot-image` `67249b4` pushed: the build now also publishes `ghcr.io/cactus-foundation-modules/chatwoot:{tag,latest}` - the package still needs flipping to public in GitHub's UI after the first run.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Per-person delivery pricing is REMOVED - `advanced-shipping-for-shop` **0.1.46**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1203**.** Chris: "advanced shipping module, please remove the 'Per-person pricing'/ seats feature". A service price could be ticked **per person**, which multiplied it by a count parsed out of a nominated product attribute's value label ("6 People" -> 6). Checked against live Deskwell before touching anything: `SELECT count(*) FILTER (WHERE per_person) FROM ash_tier_scope_config` = **0 of 149 rows**, so no price anywhere changes; `ash_settings.per_person_attribute_id` held an attribute id but nothing multiplied by it. **Schema:** new `migrations/009_drop_per_person_pricing.sql` drops `ash_tier_scope_config.per_person` and `ash_settings.per_person_attribute_id` (both `DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS`), and `001_initial.sql` no longer creates either - `003_per_person_pricing.sql` is left as history (on a fresh install it re-adds the columns and `009` drops them again, which is harmless). `007`'s INSERT still names `per_person`, but it sits inside a guarded dynamic `EXECUTE` that only runs where `ash_delivery_rules` + `transit_delta` still exist, so a fresh install never parses it. **Code:** `lib/tier-labels.ts` is the load-bearing change - `PricedTier` is now `{price: string}`, `effectiveTierPrice(t)` returns a plain `number` (no count argument, no null), and `tierOptionLabel`/`tierOptionSummary` take `price: number`, so the "(price per person)" label and the `'Per person'` summary chip are gone. That non-null return cascades: `priceEffective` is `number` not `number | null` on both `TierOption` and `UnavailableTierOption` (`lib/estimate-service.ts`), the `shown()` converters in `estimate-service.ts` and `line-resolver.ts` narrow to `(p: number) => number`, and `lib/basket-offers.ts` loses all four unpriceable-line guards (a line can no longer fail to have a price). `lib/resolve.ts` loses `parsePersonCount`, the `pat_product_values` count query, `ProductDelivery.perPersonCount` and `ResolvedTierOption.perPerson`; `lib/line-resolver.ts` loses the "Set the number of people for this item" blocked-line branch and the ` (6 people)` suffix on the order's stored `tierText`; `lib/delivery-timing-provider.ts` publishes `price: number` with no `perPerson`. **Admin/API:** the whole **Per-person pricing** card goes from `SettingsScreen.tsx`, both **Per person** checkboxes and the " per person" price suffix from `TiersScreen.tsx`, and `perPerson`/`perPersonAttributeId` from the three zod bodies (`admin/settings`, `admin/tier-config`, `admin/tier-config/[id]`). **Tests:** `parsePersonCount` suite deleted, `effectiveTierPrice` suite rewritten around flat pricing, the two unpriceable-line `basket-offers` cases dropped (`TierSpec.price` is now `number`), and the deferred-delivery wording case re-worded. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` 2563 passed, and `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS (module migration SQL changed). Wiki: the "Pricing per person" section and the Delivery-settings/basket-offers/Google-Shopping mentions are gone. **No `perPerson` consumer existed outside the module**, so nothing else needed touching - but the published `shop.product-delivery-timing` shape did change (`price` narrowed from `number | null`, `perPerson` removed), which is why the pin below matters.

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**The Sales sidebar link is now **Trading**, and Suppliers is a tab on it rather than a link of its own - `shop` **0.1.288**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1201**.** Chris: the Sales link holds far more than sales - tax and shipping, discounts, customers, reports - and Suppliers took a second link beside it. **Manifest:** `modules/shop/cactus.module.json` `navEntries[1].label` `Sales` -> `Trading`; the path (`/m/shop/orders`) is unchanged, so no redirect is needed and no bookmark breaks. Trading was picked over Commerce/Selling because the section now holds a buying-side screen as well, and Selling would leave Suppliers looking lost. **`lib/admin-nav.ts`:** `SALES_BUILT_INS` -> `TRADING_BUILT_INS`, `resolveSalesNavTabs` -> `resolveTradingNavTabs` (7 call sites: orders, requests, customers, discounts, reports, tax-shipping, and now suppliers). The Suppliers tab is resolved OUTSIDE the built-in list on purpose: it is the only tab gated on a **setting** (`supplierFieldEnabled`) rather than a permission, and it carries the site's own word for a supplier, so it needs `getShopConfigCached()` + `resolveSupplierLabel()` after the built-ins are labelled. It is inserted after `tax-shipping` so the built-ins stay together ahead of any contributed tab (`shop.orders-tabs`, currently just quote-for-shop's Quotes). Pluralisation repeats `SuppliersScreen.tsx`'s own ternary rather than sharing a helper - `SuppliersScreen` is `'use client'` and `lib/config.ts` imports prisma, so importing it there would be a client->server graph leak. **`lib/supplier-nav.ts` is DELETED**, along with its four call sites (`app/api/admin/settings/route.ts` GET and PUT, `products/route.ts`, `dashboard-widget/route.ts`, `orders/route.ts`) and the now-unused `getShopConfigCached` imports in products and dashboard-widget. That file existed only to patch the Suppliers entry into and out of the **stored** `Module.manifest` jsonb, because core builds the sidebar from that copy and a module update rewrites it from `cactus.module.json`. With no sidebar link to maintain there is nothing to patch. **Existing installs need no action:** `app/api/admin/modules/[id]/route.ts:181` writes the incoming manifest at update time, so Deskwell's stored copy picks up `Trading` and drops the Suppliers entry on its next shop update. Worst case (that route's `incoming` being null after a failed manifest fetch) is a stale Suppliers link still pointing at `/m/shop/suppliers`, which still exists as a page - a duplicate link, not a broken one, cleared by the next successful update. **`app/cactus-admin/shop/suppliers/page.tsx`** now renders `ShopSectionNav` with `active="suppliers"` and no longer calls the deleted sync. The route stays reachable with the setting off (SuppliersScreen already handles that case), so old bookmarks land somewhere that explains itself. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found**, `npm test` **2568 passed / 60 skipped**. No schema change, so the backup round-trip gate is not in play. Wiki: `Shop.md`, `Advanced-Shipping.md`, `Quotes.md`, `Google-Sheet-Products.md`, `Architecture-overview.md` updated and pushed. It reaches Deskwell only when the owner updates the shop module there.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**The Google Shopping feed can carry each product's own delivery services and charges - `google-shopping-for-shop` **0.1.6**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1202**; the delivery-module half is NOT mine to release, see the collision note at the end.** Chris: "is it possible to pass google the available delivery options for the product/variation from our advanced shipping module?" Yes, and most of the seam already existed - `shop.product-delivery-timing` (added in ash 0.1.42) already resolved EVERY service a product is offered and then threw all but one away in `chooseTier`. **Provider side (`advanced-shipping-for-shop`, working tree only):** `ProductDeliveryTiming` gains `options: ProductDeliveryOption[]` (key, label, description, price, handlingDays, transitDays) beside the unchanged headline fields, built from `delivery.tiers` with the same `counts()` helper, so a `minLeadDays` floor still folds into HANDLING and never transit. Purely additive - the headline fields, the point name and every existing caller are untouched. **gsf side:** new `migrations/004_delivery_options.sql` adds `gsf_settings.send_delivery_options BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false` + `shipping_country TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'GB'` (both `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; 001 left alone, as with 003). **Off by default on purpose - an item carrying its own `g:shipping` groups OVERRIDES the Merchant Center account's rates for that item**, so it is the owner taking the rates into their own hands, not a default. `lib/delivery-timing.ts` gained `readOption` beside `readTiming` (same distrust-the-seam discipline: a bad or unpriced option is dropped on its own, a duplicate service NAME is dropped because two same-named groups are indistinguishable to Google, and a provider too old to publish a menu simply yields `options: []`) plus `hasDeliveryTimingProvider()` so the settings tab can grey the switch out and say why. `lib/feed-xml.ts` gained `FeedShippingGroup` + `FeedItem.shippingGroups` and renders one `<g:shipping>` per service - country upper-cased, service escaped, price through the same `money()`, and per-group `min/max_handling_time` + `min/max_transit_time` where known (they override the item-level pair for that group; the item-level pair stays as the fallback). A group failing validation (bad country, blank service, negative price) is dropped, never the item. `lib/feed-data.ts` builds them in the existing delivery pass; **new `taxClassByItem` map** because the pass runs over finished items which no longer carry the tax class, and the charge is folded into the line and taxed at the product's own rate - so it must be grossed with the SAME `gross()` the item's price used. **Country has no home in shop config** (`ShpAddress.country` is per-address, `ShopConfig` has none), hence the new setting; `asShippingCountry` forces two upper-case letters and falls back to GB. What a shopper actually sees on Google: **not a menu** - Google quotes the cheapest group that reaches them, so Deskwell's free Flat-Pack is what shows and the paid services sit behind it; the real gain is the per-service transit spread (1 to 16 working days on live data) where today the feed sends only `tiers[0]`'s timing. Checked against live Deskwell before building: `defaultTierKey` is null, so the desk that offers 1-day Express currently tells Google 5 days. **Tax classes checked against live and there is NO gap**: 3,364 of 20,806 ACTIVE physical rows carry `tax_class_id = NULL`, but every one is a variant CHILD whose parent has the VAT class, and `feed-data.ts` already resolves `child.tax_class_id ?? parent.tax_class_id` - so all 3,364 gross correctly, and zero standalone products lack a class. (An earlier read straight off `shp_products` without the parent fallback suggested a hole; there isn't one.) The only tax class on the shop is `VAT` at `0.2000`. Checks before release: `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` clean of anything in these modules (the one failure either side is `product-checks-for-shop`, not in `modules.json` and already broken), full `npm test` 2568 passed / 8 skipped with 9 new tests (4 in `feed-xml.test.ts`, a new `lib/delivery-timing.test.ts` standing a fake provider in the generated registry via `vi.mock`), and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real 3-test PASS** (new columns = the gate applies). Wiki `Google-Shopping.md` gained "Delivery charges", `Advanced-Shipping.md`'s "Other modules can read your delivery times" updated, gsf README updated. **Collision, unresolved at release time:** a CONCURRENT session is mid-rewrite of `advanced-shipping-for-shop` at **0.1.46**, removing per-person service pricing outright (`migrations/009_drop_per_person_pricing.sql`, `effectiveTierPrice` down to one argument, `perPerson` gone from `ResolvedTierOption`), and has already absorbed and adapted the `options` code above. So the provider half was NOT committed, NOT released and the ash pin in `modules.json` was NOT moved by this turn - that release belongs to whoever finishes 0.1.46, and until it lands the gsf switch has nothing to read (`options: []`, no shipping groups, account rates still in charge - which is exactly the graceful path it was built for). **Version trap:** gsf tag `v0.1.5` already existed (Merchant Center links) while the module's own manifest still read 0.1.4, so this shipped as **0.1.6**; core's pin had been caught up to v0.1.5 by another turn mid-session and moves one, to v0.1.6. Also noticed in passing: core `v0.5.1201` is committed and pushed but has NO tag or GitHub release - somebody else's unfinished release, left alone.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Product checks moved off the sidebar and onto Shop → Catalogue as a **Checks** tab - `product-checks-for-shop` **0.1.7**, pushed and released; **no core pin**, since the module is deliberately absent from `modules.json` and installs by URL.** Chris: the module took a sidebar link of its own; it is a view of the catalogue, so it belongs beside Products, Categories and Collections. The mirror also stopped rewriting the whole query string: new `LIST_QUERY_KEYS` in `lib/list-query.ts` names the eleven keys this screen owns, and only those are deleted before the new ones are appended, so the host's `?tab=` survives a filter change (without that, one click would drop the page back to the products list on the next refresh). Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Variation web addresses are now built from the parent listing's slug, and the basket stops quoting an old product name - `shop-variations` **0.1.158** + `shop` **0.1.287**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1199**; 19,652 live Deskwell rows rebuilt.** Chris: adding a variation to the basket linked `.../impulse-crescent-desk-cantilever-leg-160cm-right-hand-maple-silver` on a listing that has been called `impulse-cantilever-crescent-corner-office-desk` for months. Cause: a variant child's name AND slug were snapshotted from the parent's NAME at generate time (`generateMatrix`, `createSingleVariant`, `upsertVariantForCombination` all did `ensureUniqueProductSlug(slugify(name))`), and `syncVariantChildNames` deliberately left slugs alone. New `modules/shop-variations/lib/child-identity.ts` owns both spellings: `variantChildName(parentName, labels)` and `variantChildSlug(parentSlug, labels)` - **from the parent's SLUG, not its name**, so an SEO-rewritten address carries its variations, and **without generateSlug's 100-char cap** (5,281 of Deskwell's 20,366 combinations exceed it; truncating collapses 2,531 into `-2`/`-3` twins). `syncVariantChildIdentity(parentId)` recomposes both set-based in one transaction, parking the set on `tmpslug-<id>` first because children routinely swap addresses; a unique violation falls back to a per-child `ensureUniqueProductSlug` walk. `syncVariantChildNames` is now a thin wrapper over it, so option-value renames, the resequence route, the options refresh route and CSV/Pull all fix addresses too. New manifest extension point `shop.product-saved` / `variations-child-identity` fires on a `name` or `slug` write, which is what makes the editor's new button reach the variations. `modules/shop`: the **Rebuild web address** button now actually exists - `regenerateSlug` was in the editor model and the PUT route but NO UI ever set it (the wiki claimed it was on Details); it sits on the **Search** tab under the SERP preview, moved into `TAB_FIELDS.seo`, previews the pending address via `generateSlug(name)`, new `.spe-serp-address` in `editor-css.ts`. Live data: `variation_slug_rebuild_2026_08_23/` (untracked) - `plan.sql`/`plan.csv` (19,652 changing rows of 20,366), `apply.sql` (four guards: drift, all-children, no intra-plan or foreign address clash, nothing left parked), `rollback.sql`. Applied to live Deskwell; `deskwell.co.uk/impulse-cantilever-crescent-corner-office-desk-160cm-right-hand-maple-silver` 200s, the old address 404s (platform has no redirects, per Chris's standing position). Parents were NOT touched - 441 of 442 already matched their names.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Every product's Google Shopping tab now links straight into Merchant Center, one link per variation - `google-shopping-for-shop` **0.1.5**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1197**.** Chris: "on the edit product page, is it possible to add a link to that product in google merchant centre" - then chose a link per variation (not a grouped/item-group link) and a single shop-wide account number. Google publishes **no URL contract for the Merchant Center console** (only for the Content/Merchant APIs), so the whole address shape lives in ONE function, `merchantCentreItemUrl` in the new `lib/merchant-centre.ts`: `https://merchantcenter.google.com/mc/items/details?a=<merchantId>&offerId=<offerId>&channel=online&language=en` plus `&feedLabel=<label>` when set - **unverified against a live account, and the one line to change when Google reshuffles it again**. `language` is the constant `en` because `app/layout.tsx` hardcodes `lang="en"` platform-wide; `feedLabel` is left OFF when blank on purpose, since Merchant Center then asks which feed is meant rather than confidently opening the wrong country. **The offer id is the feed's own `<g:id>`**, i.e. the variation's hidden CHILD product id where a product has variations and the product's own id where it does not - so `getMerchantCentreLinks(productId)` mirrors `lib/feed-data.ts` exactly: enabled variants only, and a single raw `status = 'ACTIVE'` query over the child ids drops the ones the feed itself skips (a link to an item Google was never sent is a dead end with a tick on it). Excluded products get no links and say so; a shop-wide-disabled feed still lists them but warns they lead nowhere yet. New `migrations/003_merchant_centre_link.sql` adds `gsf_settings.merchant_id` + `feed_label` (both `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, both also written into `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs); `updateGsfSettings` strips the account number to its digits (`replace(/\D+/g,'')`) because owners paste it with spaces, dashes or an "ID:" in front, and blank stores NULL. Surfaced as a new **Your Merchant Center account** card in the settings sub-tab (account number + feed label, one save button each) and a new server component `components/MerchantCentreLinks.tsx` rendered ABOVE `GoogleShoppingPanel` in `ProductGoogleShoppingSection` - links only, so there is no state and no client component. Neither field affects the feed. Additive module columns, so `prisma/core-reconcile/` is not involved; **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` run anyway and a real 3-test PASS** (new columns = the gate applies). `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on the module, module tests 15/15. Wiki `Google-Shopping.md` gained "Jumping straight to a listing on Google".)

The `Split` block (`lib/puck/config.tsx`, retired from the picker but still what Deskwell's checkout layout is built from) gained a `stackOrder` select - `left-first` (default, byte-identical to before) | `right-first`. `SplitBlock` emits one extra `<style>` at `mobileMediaQuery()` only: `[data-split-id="id"]>div:first-child{order:2}` + `>div:nth-child(2){order:1}`. Ordering is the right lever because the collapse to one column is a `grid-template-columns:1fr !important` rule in `lib/design/tokens.ts` - the two zone divs stay grid children, so `order` reshuffles them without touching the desktop ratio. Editor and RSC paths share `SplitBlock`, so parity is by construction. `modules/shop/lib/starterLayouts.ts`: the `split()` helper takes an extra props bag and the Two Column checkout starter now passes `{ stackOrder: 'right-first' }`, so fresh installs get it too. Live: `Layout` row `starter-shop-checkout-classic-live` on the OVH `neondb` had `content[0].props.stackOrder='right-first'` set by `jsonb_set` (backup of the old `builderData` kept in the session scratchpad) - inert until the owner takes a core update, since the prop needs the new block code. `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on both files. No schema change, so no migration and no backup gate.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**The basket's coupon box now hides behind an "Add coupon code" link, and vanishes entirely on a shop with no usable code - `shop` **0.1.285**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1196**.** Chris: the field was shouting at every shopper, most of whom have no code; then, once it collapsed, "if no coupon codes exist, do not show the link or box at all". `CartFullClient` (the island behind the **Shop: Cart** and **Shop: Cart totals** blocks - Deskwell's cart layout uses Cart totals; `/shop/checkout` itself has never carried a coupon field, confirmed against the live `starter-shop-checkout-classic-live` layout, which holds only the ShopCheckout* blocks) gains two states: `couponOpen`, false on mount, and `couponsAvailable`, false on mount and set from the config call it already makes. Collapsed it renders one underlined text-style button labelled by the new Puck field `couponLinkLabel` (`cart-fields.tsx`, default `Add coupon code`, sits with `couponPlaceholder`/`couponButtonLabel` so it reaches Cart, Cart totals and Cart summary at once); clicking swaps in the same input + Apply row as before, autofocused, and Enter now applies as well as the button. **New `hasRedeemableCoupons()` in `modules/shop/lib/db/discounts.ts`** - a single `SELECT EXISTS` over `shp_coupons` with the same four conditions `resolveDiscounts` enforces (`is_active`, started, not expired, `usage_limit IS NULL OR usage_count < usage_limit`); a minimum-order-value the basket cannot meet yet still counts as redeemable, since the shopper can go and meet it. EXISTS rather than a count so it stops at the first row, behind a 5-second cache matching `getShopConfigCached`'s, and `invalidateCouponPresenceCache()` fires from `createCoupon`, `updateCoupon`, `deleteCoupon` and `incrementCouponUsage` (that last one because the redemption that exhausts a code changes the answer for everyone else). Surfaced as `couponsAvailable` on `GET /api/m/shop/public/config`, which every cart surface already calls - no new round-trip. Default false means a shop with no codes never flashes the link up mid-load; `preview` (the Puck editor) seeds it true so the owner can still see and style the block. The fallback `CartPageClient` (used only where a site has no cart layout, so it takes no Puck props) got the same two gates with a hardcoded label. Live Deskwell has 0 coupons, redeemable or otherwise, so the box disappears there outright. Colours are tokens (`--color-text-muted`); one component serves both editor and RSC, so the two halves stay identical by construction. `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, shop lib tests 200 passed. No schema change, so no migration and no backup gate. Wiki `Shop.md` updated.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-23 (**Live chat bubble can drop to its icon alone on phones - `live-chat` **0.1.19**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1193**.** Chris: the bubble's wording was getting in the way of things on mobile. New per-site switch `hide_label_on_mobile` (Settings -> Live Chat -> Widget -> "Hide the label on phones"), OFF by default so nothing moves until it is ticked. New column via migration `003_hide_label_on_mobile.sql` (`BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT false`, idempotent) plus the same column in `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs; carried through `lib/settings.ts` (config, UpdatableSettings, upsert), the admin settings GET/PATCH (zod `hideLabelOnMobile`), and the widget boot payload. `WidgetLoader` wraps the bubble copy in `.lc-bubble-text` and, only when the switch is on, injects `@media (max-width: 640px){.lc-bubble-text{display:none}.lc-bubble{gap:0 !important;padding:0.9rem !important}}` - the `!important` is load-bearing: the bubble's padding and gap are INLINE styles, which outrank any stylesheet rule without it. The 'Starting…' and retry copy sit inside the same span, so the icon never re-widens mid-click. 640px matches the commonest breakpoint already in the tree. Gates: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean. Wiki `Live-Chat.md` updated.)

Previous entry: (**Collection Links column brought into line with the rich text footer columns - `shop` **0.1.282**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1192**.** Chris published the new footer and sent a screenshot: the Collections heading sat higher than What we do / Company / Policy and printed in the body face. Cause: `ShopCollectionLinks.shared.ts` gave its h3 `margin: 0 0 0.75rem; font-size: 1.05rem` while the neighbouring columns are RichTextBlocks whose h3 gets globals.css's `.puck-richtext h3` - `margin: 1.25em 0 0.5em; font-size: 1.25rem; font-weight: 700; font-family: var(--h3-family, var(--font-heading))`. The 1.25em top margin collapses up through each column's wrapper, so every richtext column starts 1.5625rem down the grid cell and the one column without it looked "misaligned" - the fix is to carry the SAME margin, not to strip theirs. Stylesheet now mirrors the richtext rules to the value: h3 metrics as above, ul `margin: 0 0 1em 1.5em; padding: 0; line-height: 1.75`, li `margin-bottom: 1.25em` (their rhythm is li 0.25em + the inner `<p>`'s 1em - the block has no p, so the li carries the sum), inline variant zeroes the li margin and left ul margin. Shared file only - both halves pick it up, no markup change, no core change. Note for whoever releases core next: the v0.5.1191 turn released the tag but forgot its package.json bump (tree said 0.5.1190), so this release jumps the file straight to 0.5.1192.)

Previous entry: (**GoCardless and Square no longer create an order until the money is committed - `shop` **0.1.281**, `gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop` **0.1.13**, `square-payment-for-shop` **0.1.11**, working tree, nothing released.** Chris: orders were appearing the moment a shopper picked one of those two methods, "even when their payment doesnt go through or no payment is even attempted". Confirmed, and it was worse than reported - `CheckoutPaymentClient.prepareIntent` fires on the RADIO BUTTON, not on Place order, so every shopper who so much as looked at Instant Bank Pay left a real `shp_orders` row with a real number in the owner's list. The old design was deliberate (`createPendingOrder`'s comment: "the order exists before the payment intent, so a webhook/confirm can always find something to update"), which is right for a method that takes the money on this site and quite wrong for one that hands the shopper to a bank. **New seam:** optional `orderCreation?: 'immediate' | 'on-payment'` on `ShpPaymentProvider` (`modules/shop/lib/payments/provider.ts`), default `'immediate'` so every other method is untouched. Both redirect providers set `'on-payment'`. **New table** `shp_checkout_drafts` (`modules/shop/migrations/025_checkout_drafts.sql`, same DDL appended to `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs; added to the manifest `teardown` list): id (NOT defaulted - the caller mints it), order_number (unique), payment_method, customer_email/name, total, currency, `payload` JSONB holding the whole `CreateOrderInput`, created_at, expires_at. **The id in the draft IS the id the order gets** - that is the trick that makes the whole thing cheap: the module payment row (`gcp_payments.order_id` / `sqp_payments.order_id`), the provider's `?order=` return URL and the eventual `shp_orders.id` all name the same value from the start, so nothing is ever re-pointed. Order number is reserved at draft time too (it is quoted to the provider and lands on the shopper's bank statement), so an abandoned checkout now costs a GAP IN THE NUMBERING instead of a phantom order. **New** `modules/shop/lib/checkout-draft.ts`: `createCheckoutDraft` (+ opportunistic `DELETE ... WHERE expires_at < now()` on the way past, no cron), `getCheckoutDraft`, `materialiseDraftOrder` - idempotent, `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the draft then insert-order-and-delete-draft in ONE transaction, so the redirect-back and the webhook racing each other (which they routinely do, seconds apart) create exactly one order; the loser finds no draft and re-reads the order. TTL **30 days**, deliberately generous - a draft swept while a bank payment is still in flight would leave a settled payment with no order, which is worse than the bug being fixed. `createPendingOrder` split into `insertOrderRows(tx, data)` + a thin wrapper so the draft path can share the one place an order row is born; `CreateOrderInput` gains an optional `id`, written as `COALESCE(${id}::text, gen_random_uuid()::text)`. **New core type** `PrismaTransactionClient` in `lib/db/prisma.ts` (`Omit<ExtendedPrismaClient, ITXClientDenyList>`) - `Prisma.TransactionClient` is the UNextended shape and tsc rejects it against the extended client, same trap as `ExtendedPrismaClient` right above it. `payment-intent` route now resolves the provider BEFORE writing anything and branches: `'on-payment'` drafts + uses `previewOrderPaymentNotes` (no order to restate lines on yet), everything else is exactly as before. `confirm` route: no order under that id is no longer a 404 - `confirmDraft` asks the provider FIRST and materialises only on success, so a refusal leaves nothing behind. Module side, both `settle.ts` files restructured to the same shape: failure branch first and it **returns without creating anything** when there is no order; then amount/currency checked against the order OR the draft (`paymentMatchesOrder` already took `{ total: unknown; currency: string }`, so it needed no change) BEFORE `materialiseDraftOrder`; then PAID+`fulfillPaidOrder` on collected, `markOrderAwaitingConfirmation` on authorised-not-yet-collected. That last case moved OUT of the two return routes and into settle, so the webhook gets it too. GoCardless also gains `settleFromAuthorisedRequest(orderId)` for its real gap - `ready_to_fulfil`/`fulfilling`/`fulfilled` with no payment resource yet, which is money committed with nothing to settle against. Both return routes now read the order AFTER settling (it is usually born there) and redirect to `/shop/checkout` when there is none, i.e. the shopper never paid. Pre-existing PENDING orders are unaffected: `materialiseDraftOrder` hands back an existing order untouched. `requiresModules` on both payment modules bumped to `shop >= 0.1.281` so the updater refuses them against an old shop. `tsc`, `eslint .`, `npm test` (2551 passed) and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real 3-test PASS** (new table = the gate applies).)

Previous entry: (**New footer block: a fresh random handful of collection links on every page load - `shop` **0.1.279**, pushed and released, pinned by core **0.5.1189**; plus a draft footer layout on Deskwell.** Chris wanted a new footer for the shop era with a few `/shop/collections/` links for SEO, rotating on every page change/refresh. New Puck block **`ShopCollectionLinks`** in `modules/shop/components/puck/ShopCollectionLinks{,.rsc,.shared}.tsx` - manifest `layoutTypes: ["footer"]` only, so it offers itself on footer designs (same mechanism as ShopCartSummary on header; core untouched, name verified absent from core with the git-grep leak check). Editor/RSC/shared three-file split copied from ShopCategoryPills: the shared file carries the stylesheet (`.shop-collection-links`, chevron `::marker` list or a wrapping inline row via `data-scl-layout`), the sample names and the colour sanitiser, so both halves stamp identical classes. Fields: heading, how many (1-24, default 6), stacked/inline, optional "view all" link wording (href built through a `const base` because a literal `/shop/collections` trips `@next/next/no-html-link-for-pages` - established dodge from config.tsx's account links), and four free-text colour fields that default to inherit. RSC half calls `connection()` then new **`listRandomCollectionLinks(limit)`** in `modules/shop/lib/db/catalogue.ts` - deliberately the lightest read on the page (name+slug only, no counts/covers, it runs site-wide), same EXISTS visibility rule as `listCollectionsForIndex` (ACTIVE, not catalogue_hidden), `ORDER BY random()` in Postgres so every request is a genuinely fresh draw; anchors are plain server-rendered `<a>` with NO nofollow (the rotating internal links are the point - note the live footer's richtext links all carry `rel="nofollow"` + `target="_blank"` from the editor defaults, which the new draft deliberately does not). Query proven on the live DB: two consecutive runs returned two different sixes. **Deskwell got a DRAFT `Layout` row `deskwell-footer-shop`** (type footer, status draft - drafts never render, the live `deskwell-footer` row untouched): Grid4 with What we do / Collections (the new block, colours matching the other columns: `light-dark(var(--color-5), var(--color-3))` text, `var(--color-2)` chevrons and hover) / Company / Policy, then the strap, Copyright and LiveChatWidget copied over with fresh `dw-footer2-*` ids; the copied columns' links were cleaned of the nofollow/_blank while at it. Rollback is one line: `DELETE FROM "Layout" WHERE id='deskwell-footer-shop';`. **Order of operations for going live:** release shop with the block, owner updates the module on the install, THEN publish the draft footer - published before the update, the renderer meets an unknown block type. `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, client-graph + manifest + module-layout-blocks guards pass. No schema change so no backup gate. Wiki `Shop.md` gained the block's paragraph.)

Previous entry: (**The bookkeeping overview's "Waiting on you" tile counted the wrong queue - `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.14**, pinned by core **0.5.1188**.** Chris: the overview read "0 imported entries to review - 8 without a receipt" while `/hq/m/uk-bookkeeping/reconcile` had five lines still waiting. Both numbers were right and neither was the point: `getDashboard` in `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/dashboard.ts` only ever counted `bk_transactions` with `status = 'draft'` (half-written entries), and the reconcile screen reads `bk_bank_transactions` with `status = 'unreconciled'` (the bank's own lines with nothing in the books against them). **Two separate tables, two separate queues, and the overview knew about one of them.** Live figures at the time: 0 drafts, 8 posted, 8 reconciled, 5 unreconciled. Fix: `getDashboard` gains one more statement - `COUNT(*)` over `bk_bank_transactions` joined to `bk_bank_accounts` where `status = 'unreconciled' AND archived = FALSE` (archived accounts' leftovers are history, not a job) - returned as `unreconciled` on the dashboard payload. `DashboardScreen.tsx` now builds one `waiting` list of the four queues, each with **its own count next to its own link** (drafts -> `?status=draft`, bank lines -> `/reconcile`, receipts -> `?hasEvidence=0`, assets -> `/assets`), drops any that are zero, and says "Nothing waiting." when all four are. The headline number is `drafts + unreconciled` - the two piles that are literally rows in a queue - so it now reads 5, not 0. Previously the tile printed "0 imported entries to review" as a live link even at zero, which is the part that read as "nothing to do". `npm run typecheck` and `eslint` clean; no schema change, so no migration and no backup gate.)

Previous entry: (**Every refund this platform has ever tried has thrown before it could settle - `shop` **0.1.277**, core **0.5.1183**.** Chris tested a refund after 0.1.275 shipped: "i pressed refund and nothing happened", then a retry gave "A refund is already in progress for this order." **Root cause, proven on a throwaway VPS database, not by reading:** `settleRefund` in `lib/db/refunds.ts` opened with ``await tx.$queryRaw`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(...)` `` and **`pg_advisory_xact_lock` returns `void`** (`SELECT prorettype::regtype FROM pg_proc` - confirmed), which Prisma has no mapping for: `Failed to deserialize column of type 'void'. If you're using $queryRaw and this column is explicitly marked as ``Unsupported``...`. It throws on **every** call. `prepareRefund`'s lock was always fine because `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` returns **boolean** - that one-word difference is the whole bug. Scratch test proved all three cases in one run: void via `$queryRaw` THREW, boolean via `$queryRaw` ok, void via **`$executeRaw` ok**. **The failure sequence**, every symptom accounted for: `prepareRefund` commits the PENDING reservation → `performRefund` returns → `settleRefund` throws on its first statement → transaction rolls back (which is why `pg_locks` showed nothing afterwards, and why I nearly chased a phantom deadlock) → route 500 → `RefundModal`'s `(await res.json()).error` **has no catch**, so parsing a non-JSON 500 body throws inside the click handler and **no message renders at all** → "nothing happened". Row stays PENDING → the next attempt inside 5 minutes hits the 409. `lib/db/shipments.ts:343` (`deleteShipment`) carried the identical line and would have done the same to anyone undoing a dispatch. Both now `$executeRaw`. **New `modules/shop/lib/db/raw-void-calls.test.ts`** - a static sweep of the module's own source asserting no `$queryRaw` calls a void-returning function (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`, `pg_advisory_lock`, `pg_advisory_unlock_all`, `pg_sleep`), explicitly excluding the `pg_try_` variants. **Verified non-vacuous**: reverted the fix, guard reported `refunds.ts:241 - pg_advisory_xact_lock through $queryRaw` and failed; restored, passed. Nothing else could catch this class - it type-checks, it lints, and no unit test here reaches a database. **Second fix, Chris's call:** `bankTransferProvider` and `cashProvider` returned `{success: false}` **unconditionally**, so even with the settle bug fixed a bank-transfer shop could never record a refund - and Deskwell is **19 BANK_TRANSFER / 14 GOCARDLESS_IBP / 7 SQUARE**. Nothing came off the order, stock never returned, the books kept the whole sale and 0.1.275's credit note (hooked on `outcome.success`) could never fire. That last part was my own miss. New `refundMode?: 'provider' | 'manual'` on `ShpPaymentProvider` beside the existing `confirmMode`; both manual providers carry it and return success. `MANUAL_METHOD_COPY` rewritten to say what the button does and does not do - it takes the items off, credits the books and sends the credit note; the money is still yours to send. **Live database write, authorised:** three stranded PENDING rows (£228.00 DW000073, £213.60 DW000078, £246.00 DW000080 - I had reported two on one order, it was three on three) marked FAILED, which is what the code would have written had it not thrown. Backup at `scratchpad/stranded-refunds-backup.txt`, rollback at `scratchpad/rollback-stranded-refunds.sql` (id-scoped, `AND status='FAILED'`). All three orders left COMPLETED/PAID, untouched. Left alone they would have counted against each order's remaining refundable amount and nagged the store by email hourly forever, since bank transfer has no `getRefundStatus`. Checks: `npm run typecheck` no errors, `eslint .` 0/0, `npm test` **203 files / 2551 passed, 8 skipped**. No migration, so the backup gate is untripped. Note for next time: shop 0.1.276 landed from another session mid-flight (itemised invoice/credit-note payloads, built on 0.1.275) - no file overlap with this.)

Previous entry: (**A Shape filter on the media library, and the last of the orphaned working-tree work committed - core **0.5.1187**.** Chris asked for the leftovers to be sorted out. Two things were sitting uncommitted in the shared tree with no session left to claim them; both sessions still running had confirmed neither was theirs. **1. Media library Shape filter** (`app/cactus-admin/media/{MediaLibrary,MediaToolbar,types}.tsx`, `lib/media/library-query{,.test}.ts`). A `Picture shape` dropdown - Any shape / Square (1:1) / Not square - sitting between File type and Usage, with a removable filter chip and a `shape` URL param. **The interesting bit is `SHAPE_FILTER_WHERE`:** it is a column-against-column Prisma field reference (`width: { equals: prisma.media.fields.height }`), because there is no single value 'square' to test for. Both branches also insist on `width`/`height` being non-null, and that guard is load-bearing, not defensive: **drop it and every unmeasured video, model and vector reads as 'not square', because NULL is not equal to NULL**. The test pins exactly that guard and deliberately does not try to re-implement the field reference - a hand-rolled evaluator could not stand in for it honestly. **2. The Space Planner quote wiki pages** - `Quotes.md` and `Space-planner.md`, the documentation for the `space-planner-for-shop` v0.1.29 fix released earlier today. The fix shipped without them because it was committed out of an abandoned tree. **Wiki was missing a page it should have had:** the Shape filter is user-facing and nothing documented it, so `Managing-media.md` gained an entry in the filter list (in toolbar order, between File type and Usage) explaining why unmeasured files are excluded rather than guessed at. **Worth knowing about the wiki's dual tracking:** core tracks its own copies of 41 `wiki/*.md` files AND `wiki/` is a separate checkout with its own `.git`. So a wiki page committed in the wiki repo still shows as modified in core until core's copy is staged too - which is why nine wiki files sat 'uncommitted' in core while only two were genuinely uncommitted in the wiki repo. `wiki/UK-Bookkeeping.md` was tracked in the wiki repo and untracked in core; now added. **Check both repos before concluding a wiki page is unsaved.** Verification, since this was someone else's unverified code: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found**, `npm test` **2551 passed / 60 skipped** (up one file and one test from the 2550 earlier today - the new `SHAPE_FILTER_WHERE` describe block).)

Previous entry: (**Cactus Foundation mark replaced again - the voxel-clay version - core **0.5.1186**.** Second logo swap of the day: the soft clay cactus-in-a-pot is out, an 8-bit-style cactus built from clay cubes on a mound of earth cubes is in, terracotta bloom on the crown. Same ten files as the last swap: `public/{cactus.svg,favicon.svg,favicon.ico,cactus-favicon.ico,favicon-96x96.png,apple-touch-icon.png,web-app-manifest-192x192.png,web-app-manifest-512x512.png}` plus the repo-root `cactus.svg` and `wiki/cactus.svg`. **Source is 500x500 this time, which fixes the previous swap's weak spot** - the 238x403 source meant the 512 PWA icon was a 1.19x upscale; it is now effectively native. **Supplied .svg is still not vector** (one base64 `<image>`, zero paths), its payload is pixel-identical to the supplied .png (0 differing pixels, just better compressed), and the .webp is a lossy copy of the same image (0.28% delta). **Every raster is built from the PNG**, never the webp. **The SVGs carry a 256x256 payload, the rasters a 500x500 one, and that split is deliberate.** Wrapping the full 500x500 put `cactus.svg` at 249 KB, and the admin shell loads it on every page to draw it at 28-44px. Re-encoded at 256 it is 79 KB and nothing renders any differently - 256 is still above every use (28-44px in the shell/login/setup/About, 200x200 for the GitHub App logo, 16-64px for the favicon). The icon set keeps the full-resolution source because the 512 PWA icon genuinely needs it. **A palette PNG is not the shortcut it looks like here:** the soft clay shading gives the mark 37,573 unique colours, so `-colors 256` banded it (0.46% pixel delta). Voxel does not imply flat colour. **Re-tested the one server-side render path at the density the route actually uses**, not a convenient one: `app/cactus-admin/integrations/github/callback/route.ts` reads `public/cactus.svg` through sharp at `density: 144`, and an SVG whose only content is a base64 raster is exactly the case that renders as an empty canvas. Non-zero alpha at 200x200 confirmed after both the 500 and the 256 re-encode. Its dimension comment updated (was 238x403, now 256x256). **B2 cleanup had a wrinkle worth noting:** `cactus-foundation.png` disappeared mid-run and a `cactus-foundation-1.png` appeared - the media library's duplicate suffix, from a re-upload at 23:12 while the original still existed. Confirmed pixel-identical to what had already been installed before deleting it. All four gone; `media/` root is back to its 13 folders. Deskwell is unaffected as before - its own `faviconMediaId`/`appleTouchIconMediaId`/`appIconMediaId`/`logoMediaId` are all set and `resolveBranding()` prefers them. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found**.)

Previous entry: (**All 29 modules now carry their own card art, and 28 pins move with them - core **0.5.1185**, every module released.** Each module repo gained `module-art.webp` (its 1200x675 card image, copied from core's `public/module-art/`) and a centred banner above the H1 in its README, matching the core README's own layout. **Art is resolved from each repo's git remote, not its directory name** - `live-chat/` ships from `live-chat-powered-by-chatwoot` and `contact-form-reply-catcher/` from `reply-catcher`, so a directory-name lookup would have silently blanked exactly those two. Verified byte-identical after copying. **Two modules had no README at all** (`google-sheet-products-for-shop`, `product-addons-for-shop`); both now have a proper one - banner, what it does, dependencies, config table, page-builder blocks. **Five pins jumped more than one version**, which is the real delivery in this release: `filters-for-shop` v0.1.25->v0.1.29, `space-planner-for-shop` v0.1.25->v0.1.30, `gazette` v0.1.21->v0.1.24, `search` v0.1.19->v0.1.22, `product-downloads-for-shop` v0.1.6->v0.1.8. Those versions were released weeks ago and never pinned, so they had reached no site at all. `product-checks-for-shop` is not in `modules.json` (Deskwell pins it itself) so it was released but not pinned here. **space-planner-for-shop needed three separate releases** and is the part worth reading twice. (1) **v0.1.27 was committed, pushed and never tagged** - tags ran v0.1.26 -> v0.1.28 with a real commit stranded between them; tagged at `a0507f6` and released. (2) **The 'Ask for a quote' fix was finished and left uncommitted in the shared tree** by a session that had exited - FIELD_NOTES already described it as '0.1.29, working tree, unreleased'. Typecheck and eslint run against it before committing anything, staged by name, released as v0.1.29. (3) Card art on top as v0.1.30. **Two traps caught in the act, both worth remembering.** First: reading `cactus.module.json` from the *working tree* said 0.1.29 while `git show HEAD:cactus.module.json` said 0.1.28 - the bump was one of the uncommitted files. A peer session caught this before it did damage. **Read HEAD, not the working tree, when deciding what a commit contains.** Second: a `git commit -m "..."` whose message contained double quotes died on shell quoting, but the `&&`-chained `git push` and `gh release create` still ran, because the push of an unchanged HEAD succeeds. That published **v0.1.29 tagged at the 0.1.28 commit** - a release whose manifest disagreed with its own tag. Deleted with `gh release delete --cleanup-tag`, recommitted via `-F`, re-released, and verified tag-sha == HEAD *and* manifest-at-tag == tag. **Commit messages go through `-F`, and a release is not done until the tag is checked against HEAD.** Verified across all 29 afterwards: tag == HEAD, working tree clean, local == remote. `contact-form-reply-catcher` reports no `origin/main` tracking ref (its checkout never fetched one) - compare `git ls-remote --heads` there, not `origin/main`. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found**. **Not done:** nothing reaches Deskwell until the owner updates core and then each module - and with 28 pins moving, that is 28 module updates waiting on the install.)

Previous entry: (**New Cactus Foundation logo, replaced everywhere - core, working tree, unreleased.** The pixel-art saguaro-in-a-dirt-mound is gone; the mark is now a soft clay cactus in a terracotta pot, matching the module card art. **Files replaced:** `public/cactus.svg`, `public/favicon.svg`, `public/favicon.ico`, `public/cactus-favicon.ico`, `public/favicon-96x96.png`, `public/apple-touch-icon.png`, `public/web-app-manifest-192x192.png`, `public/web-app-manifest-512x512.png`, plus the repo-root `cactus.svg` and `wiki/cactus.svg` (README and wiki Home embed those). **The supplied .svg is not vector** - it is a 238x403 PNG wrapped in `<defs><image href="data:image/png;base64,..."><use>`, zero paths. Worth knowing before anyone tries to scale it: 238x403 is the whole resolution there is, which is why the 512x512 manifest icon is a 1.19x Lanczos upscale. It survives because the clay style carries no high-frequency detail. **Rasters are generated from the PNG embedded in that SVG, not from the .webp** - the webp was a lossy copy of the same image (0.003% pixel delta), the embedded PNG is the lossless original and is also the smaller file. **Existing icon conventions kept deliberately**, having measured the outgoing set rather than guessing: favicons transparent, Apple-touch and both manifest icons on white, `favicon.svg` a 1000x1000 white square so the tab shape does not change. **The `.ico` needed watching:** `icon:auto-resize=256,...` produced a 370 KB file against the outgoing 14.7 KB, because the 256 layer goes in uncompressed. Capped at 64/48/32/16 -> 32 KB. **The one server-side render path** is `app/cactus-admin/integrations/github/callback/route.ts`, which reads `public/cactus.svg` through sharp at `density: 144` to upload as the GitHub App's logo. An SVG whose only content is a base64 raster is exactly the case that could render as an empty canvas there, so it was **tested, not assumed** - librsvg decodes the data URI and sharp returns a real 200x200 with a non-zero alpha max. Its stale `(980x1057)` comment updated. **Deskwell is unaffected**, which is the whole point of these being fall-backs: its `SiteConfig` carries `faviconMediaId`, `appleTouchIconMediaId`, `appIconMediaId` and `logoMediaId`, all set, and `resolveBranding()` prefers those - checked against the live database, read only. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found**.)

Previous entry: (**The Modules page is now a store front - core, working tree, unreleased, no version bump.** Chris asked for an app-store-style page: tabs, module pictures, and a look that stands up. `app/cactus-admin/modules/page.tsx` keeps every handler, modal and API call it had and changes only how they are presented. **Four tabs** (`TabStrip`): Installed / Updates available / Browse / Add your own, with count pills and a search box in the strip's `trailing` slot filtering name + description. The landing tab is *derived* - `tab ?? (installed.length ? 'installed' : 'browse')` - rather than set from an effect, so a fresh install opens on the store and an established one opens on its own modules without a `set-state-in-effect` disable. **Cards** carry a 16:9 artwork plate, the name, a status badge, a 3-line clamped description, the version/channel/update badges and exactly one primary button (Update to v… / Enable / Install). Everything that used to crowd the card - enable, disable, the Public/Beta segmented control, the ↻ refresh glyph, Uninstall - moved into a `…` menu (`CardMenu.tsx`, outside-click + Escape), which is the whole reason the card is legible. **Artwork** (`ModuleArt.tsx`) reads `public/module-art/<slug>.webp`. The filename trap worth knowing: `repoName` is the **GitHub repo slug** for a directory row and the **manifest name** for an installed-only row, and those differ for two live modules (`live-chat` ships from `live-chat-powered-by-chatwoot`, the reply catcher from `reply-catcher`). Picking one spelling would have silently blanked those cards, so the component walks both candidates on `onError` and only then shows the initial. **Why the plate is raw palette tokens, not semantic ones:** a single image has to look right on the white light-mode card and the near-black dark-mode one, so the artwork is deep forest green and theme-independent - which means the plate behind it must be too, or a slow-loading tile flashes the wrong colour and a missing one stops matching the set. `--cactus-700`→`--cactus-900` are defined once in the base `:root`, so they qualify as tokens while staying fixed across themes. New CSS lives in a `MODULE STORE` block in `app/globals.css` (grid, card, art plate, kebab menu, search pill, empty state). Loading is a six-card skeleton grid rather than the word "Loading". **The artwork landed the same day.** All 29 arrived at the `media/` root of the live Deskwell B2 bucket at 2752x1536, were centre-cropped to 1200x675 WebP q82 into `public/module-art/` (436 KB for the set, 11-20 KB each), and the originals were deleted from B2 afterwards at Chris's instruction - by filename, folders untouched. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **No issues found** (one justified `no-img-element` disable - the tiles are static assets already shipped at display size). Wiki `Modules.md` rewritten for the new layout, on disk, not pushed; while in there, corrected the update-check throttle from "ten seconds" to ten minutes, which is what `MODULE_UPDATE_CHECK_THROTTLE_MS` has always been.)

Previous entry: (**Buying something that lasts now prompts for the asset register entry that goes with it - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, unreleased, migration `013_asset_prompts.sql`.** Chris asked for a tickbox on an entry so the asset register cannot be forgotten, then for it to be **per line, never per entry** - a receipt for a desk and a chair is two assets. **The gap it closes:** coding a purchase to a capital category kept its cost out of the P&L and that was the entire extent of what happened. `bk_fixed_assets.transaction_id` has existed since `011` and nothing has ever written it. An asset that never reaches the register claims no capital allowances, so `computeCapitalAllowances` is short by its cost, the corporation tax bill is bigger by roughly that, and the only symptom is a number nobody can see. **Two columns, deliberately not one.** `bk_transaction_lines.register_asset` is the tick; `l.is_capital` is left exactly as it was. They are not the same question - a stage payment on a building is capital and is not a second asset, and if unticking had moved `is_capital` the cost would have silently landed in the profit and loss account. `bk_fixed_assets.status` ('draft'|'active', existing rows default `active`) plus `transaction_line_position`. **Keyed on the position, not the line id, on purpose:** `updateTransaction` replaces lines wholesale (they have no identity a human refers to), so an FK to the line row would be cut by any ordinary correction and the next save would raise a duplicate asset. Partial unique index `bk_fixed_assets_source_line_idx` on `(transaction_id, transaction_line_position)` is what makes re-saving a no-op rather than a count-and-compare that races a second tab. **`register_asset` is NOT backfilled from `is_capital`** - doing so would manufacture a draft for every capital line ever recorded the moment it deploys, and hand an owner who already keeps the register by hand a screen full of duplicates of their own work. **Drafts are inert**, and that is enforced by defaulting rather than by remembering: `listFixedAssets` now returns finished assets ONLY unless a caller says `status`, so `previewDepreciation` needed no change, and the raw query in `lib/corporation-tax.ts` gained `WHERE "status" = 'active'`. A draft carries no depreciation rate because nobody has chosen one; `FixedAssetsScreen` suggests 25% in the form and a human still presses the button. `syncAssetDraftsForTransaction` runs after create, update and `postDraft` (never on an import still in review - not a record yet), `removeAssetDraftsForTransaction` before a delete, since the FK's ON DELETE SET NULL is right for a finished asset and useless for a draft. Unticking deletes the draft and can never touch an `active` row. **Tax allowances are no longer a dropdown**: six radio cards, each with the case for picking it (`CA_POOLS` gained `short`/`when`), shared by the add form and the finish-off form. Radios not tickboxes although "tickbox" was asked for - exactly one can be true, so the browser enforces it, arrows move between them and a screen reader says one-of-six; six tickboxes with a rule would need policing in TypeScript and still read as pick-as-many.
