Also: `unfinishedAssets` on the dashboard "Waiting on you" tile, two new `AuditAction`s (`fixed_asset.raised_from_entry`, `fixed_asset.confirmed`), `registerAsset` through `LineBody`/`LineInput`/`insertLines`, and `TransactionDetail` maps `register_asset` back on edit - the same trap the `is_capital` comment there already warns about, which would otherwise untick every edited entry and delete its draft. **Verification worth keeping:** no existing test applies module migrations (`roundtrip.test.ts` applies the CORE init only), so `013` was unproven SQL. Ran it on a throwaway `cactus_rt_*` database on the OVH VPS via `lib/backup/vps-database.ts`: all 13 migrations apply in order, `013` applied TWICE without error, both indexes present, the unique index refuses a second asset for one line and allows two lines of one receipt, the status CHECK refuses anything else, and the real `INSERT ... SELECT ... ON CONFLICT` produced exactly two drafts from a desk + chair + box-of-pens receipt and zero on a second run. That last one matters: Postgres only infers a PARTIAL unique index when the ON CONFLICT clause repeats its predicate, and getting it wrong throws on every save of a capital line at runtime with nothing else to catch it. Temp test deleted, throwaway database dropped, sweep confirms none left. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint modules/uk-bookkeeping` 0/0, `npm test` **2550 passed / 60 skipped**, `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 passed / 0 skipped** (new module migration, so the gate applies). Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` updated, on disk, not pushed. **Not done:** no version bump (the tree already carries an untagged 0.2.10), no commit, no release - and it reaches Deskwell only when the owner updates the install.)

Previous entry: (**The Space Planner offered "Ask for a quote" on a shop that does not sell by quote - `space-planner-for-shop` **0.1.29**, working tree, unreleased.** Chris: the planner shows **Ask for a quote** although Shop settings > Quotes is set to **normal shop**. Confirmed on live Deskwell: `qfs_settings.config->>'mode'` = `SAVE_CART`, `spl_settings.config->>'quoteEnabled'` = `true`, and `qfs_quotes` holds 9 `SAVED` rows and **zero `REQUEST`** - nobody has ever asked. **The gap:** `quoteEnabled` defaults to `true` in `modules/space-planner-for-shop/lib/config.ts:78` and was the ONLY thing consulted, by `app/public/space-planner/page.tsx` (`quoteAvailable={config.quoteEnabled}`) and by `app/api/member/plans/[id]/quote/route.ts`. Nothing anywhere read the quotes module's mode, so the planner was the one surface on the whole site inviting a quote request on a shop with a working checkout - shop's own `quoteCommerceModeProvider` returns `null` in `SAVE_CART` and leaves every buy button and the basket CTA alone, and `/quote` is reachable but unlinked. **Fix:** new exported `quoteRequestsOffered()` in `modules/space-planner-for-shop/lib/quote.ts` = `isQuoteOnly(await getQuoteConfigCached())`, ANDed with `config.quoteEnabled` in **both** the page and the route - the route matters on its own, being all that stands between a hand-written POST and a quote landing in an inbox from a shop that does not take them. Modelled on the existing `rendersEnabled && renderWorkerConfigured()` pair: switched on and actually on offer are two different things. **Note the deliberate disagreement with a sibling module:** `modules/quote-for-shop/app/api/public/requests/route.ts` carries a comment saying requests are available in save-cart mode on purpose, and that route is unchanged - a shop can still take enquiries at `/quote` if the owner links it. What changed is that the planner no longer decides on the shop's behalf. **Admin:** `GET /api/m/space-planner-for-shop/admin/settings` gained a third read-out `quoteRequestsAvailable` beside `renderWorkerConfigured`/`deliveryEstimatesAvailable`, and `SpacePlannerSettingsPanel` suffixes the toggle label and prints a line saying where the real decision lives, so the switch does not read as broken. **Nothing was written to the live database.** Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean for this module - the only two errors in the whole run are `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/fixed-assets.ts` 373 and 544 (`AuditAction` missing `fixed_asset.confirmed` / `fixed_asset.raised_from_entry`), pre-existing in another session's uncommitted work and untouched here; `eslint` on the five changed files **0 issues**; `vitest run modules/space-planner-for-shop` **244 pass / 0 fail / 3 skipped**. No migration SQL touched, so the backup round-trip gate is not in play. Wiki: `Space-planner.md` settings list and `Quotes.md` normal-shop section both say it now. **Not done:** no core pin bump, no commit, no release.)

Previous entry: (**"What it was for" moved onto each line, and shop invoices and credit notes now arrive in the books itemised - `shop` + `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, NO version bump, nothing released.** Chris: the entry form asked "What it was for" once for the whole entry, which is the wrong level - a fuel receipt with a sandwich on it is two things taxed two ways, and one box at the top can only hold one of them. Both column already existed (`bk_transactions.description` AND `bk_transaction_lines.description`, both `TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT ''` since 001), so **no migration**; the line one was simply never asked for. **Form:** `description` is off `TransactionFormValue` entirely and out of the POST body; each line in "What it was made up of" now opens with a full-width `bk-line-<uid>-description` input, placeholder switching on direction ("What was sold" / "What was bought"). **Header text is now derived, not typed:** new exported `describeFromLines` in `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/transactions.ts` + private `resolveDescription`, wired into `insertTransactionRows` and `updateTransaction` - distinct line texts, in order, `a, b, c and N more` past three; a caller that passes its own `description` (importer, external sales) still wins. That keeps `TransactionsScreen`, the CSV export and reconciliation printing something. **Upgrade path for old entries:** `TransactionDetail` seeds each line's description from `transaction.description` when the line has none, so opening an old entry to change a date hands the wording down instead of losing it. `TransactionDetail`'s line table gained a "What it was for" first column. **Shop seam, both directions:** `ShpLedgerItem` (`modules/shop/lib/types.ts`) + `ledgerItems()` (`modules/shop/lib/invoice-tax.ts`) turn a document's `lines` + `taxBreakdown` into item rows; `ShopInvoiceSinkPayload.items` and `ShopInvoiceCreditedPayload.items` are new REQUIRED fields on the shop side, mirrored as OPTIONAL `items?: ExternalSaleItem[]` in `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/external-sales.ts` so an older shop still compiles and files per rate. **The trap `ledgerItems` exists to close: invoice lines do NOT sum to `taxBreakdown`.** Delivery is rated into the buckets in `buildInvoiceMoney` and never becomes a line, and `reconcile()` nudges the largest rate row by a penny to tie to what was charged. So `ledgerItems` emits the leftover at each rate as its own row - labelled `Delivery` only when `Number(invoice.shippingAmount) > 0` and the leftover is positive, `Rounding` otherwise (a test caught "Delivery £0.01" on a delivery-free invoice) - then **checks the tie and returns `[]` rather than guessing** if a line carries a rate the summary never heard of. Credit notes pass no carriage label at all: a refund is against order lines and delivery never rides along, so any leftover there is the rounding penny. **Books side:** new exported `ledgerLines(taxBreakdown, items, categoryId, fallbackDescription, {negate})` replaces the inline per-rate loop in `recordExternalSale` and the whole body of `creditLines` (which keeps its signature plus a 4th `items?` arg). It builds BOTH shapes and uses the itemised one **only when its net, VAT and gross each equal the per-rate one to the penny** - integer pennies, never float compare - falling back silently otherwise, because an entry that disagrees with its invoice is a wrong VAT return and a terse entry is only a nuisance. Descriptions capped at 200 chars with an ellipsis. Rates and treatments still come off the rate summary via `rateCodeFor` either way; the void path needed nothing, `reversalLines` already negates whatever lines the sale has. New tests: `ledgerItems` (10) in `invoice-tax.test.ts`, `ledgerLines`/`creditLines` itemised (12) in `external-sales.test.ts`, new `lib/transaction-description.test.ts` (6). `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, 2548 pass / 60 skipped. No migration SQL touched so the backup round-trip gate is not in play. **Cross-module but order-independent:** shop only adds a field, books only read it when present.)

Previous entry: (**Two raw NUL bytes made `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/audit.ts` a binary file to git - `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.10**, pinned by core **0.5.1180**.** The field separators in `chainHash` (`modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/audit.ts:107`) were literal 0x00 bytes sitting inside the template literal fed to sha256: `chainIndex`, `prevHash` and `canonicalJson(payload)` joined by NUL so no two different triples can collide on one input. Right idea, wrong spelling - somebody typed the byte instead of the escape. The cost was not to the site but to anyone reading the code: `git diff` on that file printed `Bin 10262 -> 10382 bytes` and never a readable line, and `file lib/audit.ts` reported `data`. Pre-existing in the committed blob (`git show HEAD:lib/audit.ts | file -`), not from the recent import/reconcile work. **The bytes had to stay; only their spelling changed.** Every `row_hash` in `bk_audit_log` on the live site was computed with those separators in place, and the chain head is what the operator's emailed submission receipts anchor to - drop the separators and every existing row silently stops verifying against a receipt sitting in a mailbox nobody here can edit. So they are now Unicode escapes, which the template literal turns back into the same NUL characters at runtime. Proven rather than assumed: the digest of the evaluated post-edit template equals the digest of the same string built from `String.fromCharCode(0)`, and both match a reference computed independently in python. `tsc --noEmit`, `eslint .` and `vitest run modules/uk-bookkeeping` (142 pass, 41 env-gated skips) all clean. One wrinkle worth remembering: until the change is committed, plain `git diff` still calls the file binary, because the HEAD side of the diff is - `git diff --text` renders it, and it behaves normally from the next commit onwards.)

Previous entry: (**Refunds now raise a credit note and tell the books - `shop` + `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, NO version bump, nothing released.** Chris asked whether a refund after an invoice produced a credit note "or have i picked up on a genuine gap". Genuine gap, and a costly one: `processRefund` wrote `shp_refunds`/`shp_refund_items`, bumped `refunded_qty` and flipped the order status, and touched neither invoices nor sinks - `grep -rn "credit note\|creditNote\|CREDIT"` across the shop module returned nothing at all. So the books kept the whole sale and its VAT on money handed back, while the shop's OWN tax report at `app/api/admin/reports/tax/route.ts` already nets refunds off (`taxNet = collected - refunded`) - two numbers, one right, no signal which. **Found while building it, and fixed on Chris's say-so: an EXCLUSIVE shop was under-refunding by the VAT, permanently.** `shp_order_items.total`/`unit_price` are NET on an EXCLUSIVE shop (proven on live Deskwell: Orlena chair `unit_price` 218.00, `tax_amount` 43.60), `RefundModal` sent `unitPrice * quantity`, and the per-line cap in `prepareRefund` used `oi.total` while its own comment said "tax-inclusive" - so refunding a £261.60 chair sent £261.60 - £43.60 = £218.00 and the API **rejected the correct figure even when typed**. Both now use `oi.total + (tax_mode='EXCLUSIVE' ? oi.tax_amount : 0)`. Deskwell has had **0 refunds ever**, so nobody was shorted; the first one would have been. **New:** `modules/shop/migrations/024_credit_notes.sql` (+ the same DDL appended to `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs) creating `shp_credit_notes` and `shp_credit_note_number_seq`, with a partial unique index on `refund_id` - one credit note per refund, enforced in the database because the refund route and the retry button can both be in flight. **A separate table, not a `kind` column on `shp_invoices`**: that table has a partial unique index of one live invoice per order, an order can have any number of credit notes, and widening it would leave every existing `shp_invoices` query silently able to pick up a credit note (`getInvoiceForOrder`, the void button). New `lib/credit-note-tax.ts` (pure, 8 tests), `lib/credit-notes.ts`, `lib/db/credit-notes.ts`, `lib/credit-note-number.ts`; new routes `POST/GET /api/m/shop/admin/orders/[id]/credit-note`, page `/shop/credit-note/[number]`, PDF `/api/m/shop/public/credit-notes/[number]/pdf`; new config keys `creditNotesEnabled`, `creditNoteNumberPrefix` (`CN-`, its OWN sequence - never invoice numbers), `creditNoteHeading`, `creditNoteWording`, `creditNoteEmailCustomer`, `creditNotePdfFilenamePrefix`, all with UI on `ShopSettingsTab`; new email template `shop.credit-note-issued` (transactional) + trigger `CREDIT_NOTE_ISSUED`. **The document reuses the `shopInvoice` layout outright** - no new layout type, no new starter. That worked because `injectInvoiceDocContext` matches on BLOCK TYPE NAME (`DOC_PART_TYPES`), never on layout, and `_ctx` is injected at render and never saved, so widening `InvoiceDocContext` with `credit?: CreditDocMeta` touches zero stored layouts. `creditNoteDocContext()` presents a credit note AS a `ShpInvoice` whose `invoiceNumber` is **the credited invoice's** (so the header's existing "Invoice" row stays truthful) with `dueDate: null`. Only two blocks changed: Header prepends its own number, Totals swaps "Paid in full - thank you" for the snapshotted `wording.creditWording`. Lines/Totals/TaxSummary needed **no** branch because every figure is a **positive magnitude** - the document declares direction in its heading, and the consumer negates, exactly as the void path already did. **Money rule:** gross credited = the money that actually moved; the VAT inside it is the rate the line was SOLD at, taken off the invoice line (`tax / gross`), so INCLUSIVE and EXCLUSIVE fall out of one division with no special case. Matching refund line → invoice line is by new `ShpInvoiceLine.orderItemId` (now stamped by `buildInvoiceMoney`), falling back to POSITION for invoices raised before it existed. Unmatchable line **throws** `CreditNoteMoneyError` rather than guessing a rate - an invented rate looks like paperwork and files a wrong return. **Wired at all three settle paths** (refund route, `order-request-actions` approval, and the `reconcile-refunds` cron, the last one sequentially because each may print a PDF); `creditNoteForSettledRefund` swallows everything, since money has already moved at the provider. **Books side:** new point `shop.invoice-credited` (third alongside issued/voided) with payload `ShopInvoiceCreditedPayload`; `uk-bookkeeping` gains `recordExternalCredit` + `ukBookkeepingShopSaleCreditor` registered in its manifest, and pure `creditLines()` (5 new tests). **Always a reversing entry, never a deletion** - the one place it differs from a void: a credit note always happened, and the sale it credits is still real. Dated at the CREDIT's tax point so a filed return is never reopened; `source_ref` is `credit:<number>`; **refuses outright to credit an invoice not in the books**, since `entryType: 'adjustment'` demands a `correctsTransactionId` and filing a bare credit would push turnover below what was sold. Checks: `npm run typecheck` **no errors**, `eslint .` **0/0**, `npm test` **201 files / 2521 passed, 8 skipped**. **Backup gate tripped (new table + new sequence) and RUN FOR REAL: `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` 3/3 PASS, no skips.** It failed twice first with `57P01 terminating connection due to administrator command` inside `applySchema` - a stale `cactus_rt_import_43181` from another session's `uk-bookkeeping` import round-trip, same `cactus_rt_` prefix, being swept mid-run; third run clean once gone. Worth knowing: two sessions running `cactus_rt_*` suites will destroy each other's throwaway databases. Wiki: `Shop.md` gained a **Credit notes** section (and its "a refund does not take the sale back out... by hand for now" paragraph is deleted, being exactly what this fixes), `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained "A refund credits part of it back". **Not done:** no version bump on either module, no core pin, no commit, no release - and another session holds uncommitted work in `uk-bookkeeping` (`import.ts`, `reconciliation.ts`, `guards.ts`, `transactions.ts`, `ReconcileScreen`, new `reconcile-actions.ts`) which is why its version was left alone at the 0.2.7 they set.)

Previous entry: (**The invoice never reached the books' evidence because BACKBLAZE IS REFUSING EVERY UPLOAD to the Deskwell bucket - not a code fault. `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.7** makes the refusal say why; core **0.5.1177** pins it.** Chris: "the invoice is still not attached to the entry in bookkeeping". What the live database showed: OSR-000001's entry is **gone** (the void seam works), OSR-000002 recorded at 19:12:42Z with `sink_results` reading "Recorded as income of 939.60 in the books. The invoice itself could not be attached.", **no `Media` row**, and the `Bookkeeping / 2026 / 08` folders created at 19:12:48 - so the attach printed the PDF (~5.5s), sniffed it, made the folders and then threw at the upload. His manual re-send at 19:23:40 took the "already in the books" branch and failed at the same step, which is the retry path working exactly as built. **Root cause, proven three ways from this Mac:** Backblaze's own `b2_get_upload_url` returns **403 `access_denied`, "Storage class not supported on this cluster: STANDARD"**, and so do the S3 `PutObject` the platform uses and both rclone remotes (`b2:` native and `b2s3:`). Reads are fine (35,570 media rows still serve); the application key is scoped to `Deskwell-Office-Furniture` and **holds `writeFiles`**; the refusal lands before a single byte is sent. So it is the account/cluster, not a permission, not a key, and nothing in Cactus can route around it. **It broke today between 17:11Z and 19:12Z** - last successful write is `media/shop/.../impulse-panel-end-scalloped-*` at 17:11Z, and the 03:30Z nightly `Database-Backups/neondb-20260821-033001.dump` landed fine. **Consequences beyond the invoice, said plainly: every upload on the site is dead (media library included), and tonight's 03:30 database backup to B2 will fail.** Chris has it - a Backblaze console/plan question. Worth knowing for next time: Vercel keeps runtime logs for a live tail only. `/v3/deployments/{id}/events` returns BUILD events, `/v1/.../runtime-logs`, `/v1/observability/logs` and friends are all 404, and `npx vercel logs <url>` tails from now (and exits at once with no TTY, so it is useless backgrounded). A console.error on a deployed site is therefore unreadable minutes later - which is the whole reason for this release. **The fix**: `fileDocument`'s catch in `lib/external-sales.ts` now appends the store's own words - " The invoice itself could not be attached - the file store said: AccessDenied: Storage class not supported on this cluster: STANDARD" - whitespace-normalised and cut to 200 chars, since shop stores this appended to its own sentence and truncates the lot at 500. Diagnosis cost an hour that one sentence would have settled in a minute. Also worth recording: the local `B2_KEY_ID`/`B2_KEY` in root `.env` are a bucket-scoped application key with full write capability (NOT a master key), and Vercel holds the same bucket under `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID`/`B2_APPLICATION_KEY` - different key id, same bucket, and `B2_APPLICATION_KEY` is sensitive so the Vercel API returns it empty even with `decrypt=true`. Version note: this went out as 0.2.7 because another session took 0.2.4, 0.2.5 and 0.2.6 while it was in flight. Checks: `eslint modules/uk-bookkeeping` 0/0, `npx tsc --noEmit` **no errors**, module tests **137 passed / 39 skipped**. No migration, so no backup gate.)

Previous entry: (**Categories can be managed from the screen at last - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, unreleased.** The module has had `POST`/`PATCH`/`DELETE` on `/api/m/uk-bookkeeping/admin/categories` since 001, and nothing in the UI has ever called any of them: all four consumers (`TransactionForm`, `TransactionsScreen`, `ImportScreen`, `BookkeepingSettingsTab`) only ever `GET`. So the twenty-two seeded categories were, in practice, the only categories a site could have. New **Categories** section on `BookkeepingSettingsTab`, sitting under the Save button with the two account lists (they save themselves on the button press, everything above the Save button does not). Add, rename, re-file, reorder with arrows, put away, bring back, remove. **The design decision worth keeping:** a category carries four correlated fields - `sa103_box`, `ct600_group`, `is_trading`, `is_capital` - and they are not independent (box 24 is an administrative expense and it is trade, every time). Asking for them separately would mostly collect ways to get them wrong, and a category with an unrecognised `ct600_group` silently falls through `fallbackGroup()` in `lib/reports.ts` into admin-expenses. So the form asks ONE question - "Where it belongs on the accounts", in HMRC's own box wording - and `FILING_OPTIONS` (23 entries, keyed by the seeded category codes on purpose, so picking one files the new category exactly where that seeded one already goes) sets all four. `filingLabel()` falls back to printing the raw box/group for anything created through the API that the table has never heard of, since the column is deliberately free text - HMRC renumbers. **One server change:** `position` added to the POST body zod schema in `app/api/admin/uk-bookkeeping/categories/route.ts` (`createCategory` already accepted it). Without it every new category lands on the default 1000, two of them share a position, and "move up" is a no-op against a tie - the screen sends `max(position) + 10` instead. `moveCategory` swaps positions with the neighbour, or steps past it where the two are equal (books that predate this screen can hold ties). Ordering matters because it is the order of every category dropdown on every entry form. Archived categories are loaded too (`?archived=1`) so they can be brought back; the external-sales dropdown above now filters them out, which it did not need to before. Deletion is still mostly not deletion - `deleteOrArchiveCategory` archives anything seeded or ever used, and the screen says so. Checks: `eslint .` **0 errors 0 warnings**, `npx vitest run modules/uk-bookkeeping` **137 passed / 0 failed / 37 skipped** (the skips are the `.live.` suites, gated on env). `npm run typecheck` reports **15 errors, none in these files** - all in `import/route.ts` and `import-roundtrip.live.test.ts`, from another session's uncommitted rewrite of `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/import.ts` that dropped `suggestions`/`decisions` before its callers caught up; untouched here. Wiki: `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained a **Categories** section under "Recording entries". **Not done:** no version bump, no commit, no release - and the screen does not reach Deskwell until the owner updates the install onto whatever version carries it.)

Previous entry: (**Card payouts can be settled against several invoices, less the fees - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, on top of the import/reconcile rework below.** Chris asked how a GoCardless or Square payment reconciles when the money arriving is the invoice less the processor's cut. Answer at the time: it does not. `findCandidateEntries` filters `HAVING SUM(gross_amount) = ANY(amounts)` and `scoreCandidates` has `if (!entry.gross.equals(gross)) continue` - exact to the penny, deliberately - so a £118.60 line against a £120 invoice got NO suggestion, and matching it by hand for £118.60 left £1.40 hanging off the invoice for ever with the fee never recorded. Chris confirmed **batched payouts, mixed between the two processors**, which rules out the simple near-miss fix: a Square payout is several invoices, less several fees, less any refunds netted off. **`bk_reconciliations` already had what was needed** - many-to-many with a SIGNED amount, and `refreshBankTransactionStatus` compares `SUM(amount) = b.amount` - so six invoices `+495.00`, a refund `-24.00` and a fee `-7.68` reconcile a line of `463.32` with **no migration**. New `listSettlementCandidates()` + `settleBankLine()` in `lib/reconcile-actions.ts`, `GET /api/m/uk-bookkeeping/admin/bank-transactions/[id]/candidates`, and `action: 'settle'` on the existing `[id]` POST. **Two things worth remembering.** (1) A candidate's contribution is signed by ITS OWN direction, not the line's - an expense entry against a money-in payout is a refund and must pull the total DOWN. The same bug was latent in `matchTransaction`, which did `line.amount.isNegative() ? negated : requested`; now signed from `entry.direction`, which is identical for the ordinary same-direction case and correct for the refund one. (2) `settleBankLine` is all-or-nothing, unlike the bulk actions, and it CHECKS the invariant inside the transaction: after refreshing, it re-reads the line and throws unless the status came back `reconciled`, so wrong arithmetic rolls back instead of leaving a line matched to four of its six invoices with nothing saying the other two are missing. Difference defaults to the seeded `bank-charges` category and **`exempt`, not `zero`** - a merchant fee is VAT-exempt and zero rating it would put it in box 7. No subset-sum guessing: the panel lists everything outstanding within 60 days before / 14 after the line, in date order, with a running total, and entries already tied to THIS line are excluded from the candidates (`insertReconciliations` does `ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE SET amount`, so re-picking one would overwrite rather than add). `SettlePanel` in `ReconcileScreen.tsx` derives its default category from `usable` at render rather than writing it into state from an effect - `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is an error in this repo. Proven on a throwaway VPS database: 8 live tests pass, including the 120 + 95 - 10 - 3.15 = 201.85 payout and a refusal case that asserts the line is left untouched when the difference has nowhere to go. **Still not done: a merchant clearing account.** The proper answer for batched payouts is a "Square takings" bank account that each sale lands in gross and each fee comes out of, with the payout as an internal transfer - but neither `square-payment-for-shop` nor `gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop` records a per-transaction fee anywhere, so there is nothing to build it from yet.)

Previous entry: (**Importing a bank statement no longer asks what any of it was for - `uk-bookkeeping`, working tree, version NOT bumped, nothing released.** Chris: "we dont want to have to explain everything on the statement before importing." The old import made you answer a three-way question on every line - record it as a new entry / tick it off against an existing one / leave it alone - plus pick a category, before a single row was written. Two hundred lines of that is the job nobody finishes, and an abandoned import kept nothing at all. **Import now keeps the bank's lines and stops.** `previewStatement` no longer runs `suggestMatchesForLines` or the per-counterparty category guess; `PreparedLine` lost `suggestions`, `suggestedMatchId`, `categoryId` and `action`; `commitStatement` lost `decisions` and no longer creates drafts or writes `bk_reconciliations` - it inserts `bk_bank_statements` + the fresh `bk_bank_transactions` and returns `{statementId, linesKept, duplicates}`. `LineAction` is gone. The arithmetic checks against the statement's own totals stay, because they are free and they catch a misread column before anything is written. **All the coding moved to Reconcile**, new `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/reconcile-actions.ts` behind new route `POST /api/m/uk-bookkeeping/admin/bank-transactions/bulk` (actions `record`, `accept-suggested`, `ignore`, `unignore`; max 200 ids). `recordEntriesFromBankLines` creates one entry per line from the bank's own date/name/reference/amount, posted by default or `leaveForReview` for drafts, and matches it to the line; `acceptSuggestedMatches` applies `confidentMatch` to a selection; `setBankLinesIgnored` sets a run aside. **The seam worth remembering:** a line is explained for what is LEFT of it (`amount - matched`), never its face value, and every per-line check happens BEFORE the one write transaction, so one refusal is a sentence beside its own row instead of an aborted batch. **Round-trip cost was the design constraint.** `assertDatesNotInClosedPeriod` is two queries per date, which is 400 round trips for a 200-line batch against a route capped at 60s, so `lib/guards.ts` gained `loadClosedRanges()` + `assertDatesNotClosed()` (read the handful of closed periods/years once, check in memory - same errors, same layer, still never a trigger). Same reasoning behind `refreshBankTransactionStatuses()` in `lib/reconciliation.ts` (one UPDATE for the batch; the single-id version now delegates to it), the set-based `bk_reconciliations` insert via `UNNEST`, and `suggestCategoriesForCounterparties()` in `lib/transactions.ts` (one `DISTINCT ON` for a whole page instead of a query per name - the reconcile feed now returns `categoryGuesses` so most rows open with a category already picked). `ReconcileScreen` gained a **Find** box (the `search` filter existed in `listBankTransactions` and nothing had ever exposed it), tick boxes with select-all, paging at 100, a bulk bar (category + VAT rate + leave-for-review), and an outcome card that NAMES every line it would not touch. Selection is cleared in the filter handlers, not in an effect - `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is an error here. Audit gained `reconciliation.recorded`, `reconciliation.set-aside`, `reconciliation.put-back`; one audit row per batch, not per line. **No migration** - `bk_bank_transactions`, `bk_reconciliations` and `match_method` already held all of it, so the backup gate is untripped. `lib/import-roundtrip.live.test.ts` rewritten to the new flow and RUN against a throwaway VPS database: 6 pass, including the VAT back-solve (£4.68 gross → £3.90 + £0.78) and a mixed-direction batch where the money-in line correctly refuses an expense category without stranding the two that go through.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.5** pinned by core **0.5.1175**: the bookkeeping tab strip now scrolls sideways instead of wrapping.** `BookkeepingNav` in `modules/uk-bookkeeping/components/admin/Notices.tsx` was the last hand-rolled tab nav on the platform - a bare `<nav>` with `flexWrap: 'wrap'` and its own inline tab styles. Eleven tabs (`overview`, `transactions`, `journals`, `reconcile`, `director-loan`, `assets`, `vat`, `reports`, `year-end`, `corporation-tax`, `import`) do not fit a narrow window, so they folded onto a second row and pushed the page content down. Now it renders core's `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`, same as shop, gazette, boards, directory, ultimate-seo, twilio, search, space-planner and shop-variations: `overflowX: auto` on a `.no-scrollbar` flex row, with edge fades and ‹ › buttons that mount only when `scrollLeft`/`scrollWidth` say there is somewhere to scroll. `TABS` and the `{ active }` prop are unchanged, so no call site moved. Two knock-ons worth knowing: the tabs are now `next/link` with `prefetch={false}` rather than `<a href>`, so moving between them is a client navigation and not a full page load; and the active tab takes `--color-primary` from TabStrip rather than the `--color-text` the module used, which is what the rest of the admin does. `TabStrip` has existed since core 0.5.191, well under the module's `requiresCoreVersion` of 0.5.1156, so no version floor moved.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.4** released and pinned by core **0.5.1174**: the cashbook and the journals are now ONE ledger, and off the back of that a real balance sheet, a statutory profit and loss account, financial years, a fixed asset register and a corporation tax computation with CT600 box numbers. Four new migrations, nine new libs/screens.** The defect underneath all of it: `bk_transactions` (cashbook) and `bk_journals` (ledger) were never the same books. `trialBalance`/`accountBalances` read `bk_journal_lines` ONLY, so the trial balance showed the year-end adjustments and nothing else; `profitAndLoss` read `bk_transaction_lines` ONLY, so a depreciation or accrual journal reached no report at all. There was no balance sheet, because you cannot draw one from half a ledger. **The fix is `lib/ledger.ts`, `LEDGER_SQL` - a Prisma.Sql PROJECTION, not a table.** Nine UNION ALL branches turn each posted cashbook line into the debits and credits it always implied (analysis net -> the category's account; VAT -> vat-control; gross -> debtors/creditors at the tax point; settlement -> bank + clearing the debtor/creditor) and union that with posted journal lines. Deliberately NOT a postings table: cashbook rows go hard-locked and trigger-protected the moment a return is filed, a derived table would have to stay in step with them through every later edit and through a restore, and any drift would be silent and permanent. Debits and credits are always non-negative (`GREATEST(x,0)`/`GREATEST(-x,0)`), so a credit note comes out the other side rather than as a negative debit, and **every branch balances on its own**. **Cash accounting gets its own treatment**: VAT is parked in a new `vat-deferred` account at the invoice date and transferred to `vat-control` on settlement, because otherwise a cash-accounting business's balance sheet claims a debt HMRC has no claim to yet. The accounts themselves are always accruals - the tax point - whatever the VAT scheme. **`009_ledger_mapping.sql`** is the mapping the projection turns on: `report_group`/`bs_group`/`disallowable_percent` columns on `bk_accounts` (all plain text, no CHECK, same reasoning as `sa103_box`); the five non-trading categories 006 skipped now point at accounts (capital-equipment -> fixed-assets, drawings -> a new `dividends-drawings` EQUITY account, capital-introduced -> equity, vat-payment -> vat-control, tax-payment -> corporation-tax); new `stock`, `vat-deferred`, `loans`, `opening-balances` and `pl-corporation-tax` accounts; new `entertaining` (disallowable 100) and `interest-received` (report_group `non-trade-income`) categories, split out because advertising is allowable and entertaining is not, and because bank interest is taxed under box 170 rather than as trade; and a ledger account per existing `bk_bank_account`, with `lib/bank-accounts.ts` creating them from then on and renaming them in step. Bank opening balances are projected against `opening-balances` so a business that kept its books elsewhere starts from the right place and still balances. Category -> account is resolved with `DISTINCT ON` rather than a unique index: a migration that failed on a live install would be worse than a deterministic choice, and `ledgerHealth()` reports the duplicate instead. **`010_accounting_periods.sql`** `bk_accounting_periods` + `lib/accounting-periods.ts`: closing a year posts the retained-earnings journal (source `year_end`) and freezes the year; reopening deletes it. Enforced in the APPLICATION, not a trigger, for the same restore reason `assertDatesNotInClosedPeriod` is - and `findClosedYearFor`/`assertNotInClosedYear` live in `lib/guards.ts`, not in accounting-periods.ts, to break the cycle (closing needs journals, journals need the check). `assertDatesNotInClosedPeriod` now calls it, so every cashbook path picks it up for free; `createJournal`/`updateJournal`/`deleteJournal` call it directly, `updateJournal` on BOTH dates so a journal cannot be dragged out of a closed year either. **`011_fixed_assets.sql`** `bk_fixed_assets` + `bk_depreciation_charges` + `lib/fixed-assets.ts`: one row answers the accounts (straight line or reducing balance, pro-rated by days OWNED not days in the period, never past the residual, posted as one journal for the whole run) and the tax (`ca_pool`). The charges table is what makes a second run a no-op rather than a double charge, and cost/date go immutable once anything has been charged. **`012_corporation_tax.sql`** `bk_ct_rates` (seeded FY2015-FY2026 from HMRC's published rates, checked 2026-08-21; data not code, because they move most years), `bk_ct_computations`, `bk_ct_adjustments` (14 kinds, always positive, `kind` decides the direction - same reasoning as debit/credit being two columns). `lib/corporation-tax.ts`: profit BEFORE tax from the P&L, automatic add-backs from each account's own `disallowable_percent` (depreciation and entertaining are 100), non-trade and property income lifted OUT of the trade, capital allowances from the register, losses b/f capped at the trading profit, then the rates. **Marginal relief is F x (U - A) x N/A** with augmented profits (TTP + franked investment income) deciding the RATE and TTP deciding what it applies to; limits scaled by days in each financial year AND divided by associated companies + 1. A period straddling 1 April is apportioned by days across both FYs at each year's own rates - which degenerates correctly when the rates are the same. A period of account over twelve months is SPLIT into two tax periods by `splitIntoTaxPeriods`, because that is what it is, and missing that is how a penalty arrives for the return nobody knew about. Capital allowances: AIA capped and pro-rated with the excess spilling to the main pool rather than being lost, full expensing at 100% (and an immediate balancing charge on disposal, since there is no pool for the proceeds), 50% FYA with the balance to the special pool, 18%/6% WDA, the £1,000 small pools write-off, disposals capped at cost, and a negative pool becoming a balancing charge. Rates are days-weighted across the FYs the period touches, which is HMRC's hybrid approach for the 8%->6% type transitions. **Box numbers were transcribed from HMRC's actual CT600 (2026) Version 3 PDF, not from memory** - 145/155/160/165/170/190/205/220/235/245/275/295/300/305/310/315/326/329, the FY rows 330-345 and 380-395, 430/435/440, 475/510/525/528, 620, the allowances boxes 688/689/690/693/695/700/705/710, 760/773/775, and 780. **The module still does not file a CT600 and says so on the screen**: there is no HMRC API for a small company to self-file corporation tax. R&D, patent box, group relief arithmetic, ring fence, NI rates, s455 loans, SBA and the super-deduction are deliberately absent rather than half-implemented; each can be entered as a named adjustment with a reason. **Reports rebuilt** (`lib/reports.ts`): `profitAndLoss` in Companies Act Format 1 order with a same-length prior period beside it, `balanceSheet` with a `balanced` flag that is not decoration (both sides come from one projection, so a difference is proof of interference), `agedAnalysis` for debtors and creditors read straight off the unsettled entries so it agrees with the balance sheet by construction, and `monthlyBreakdown` moved onto the ledger. `nominalLedger` in ledger.ts is the drill-down an accountant asks for first. **New routes** under `app/api/admin/uk-bookkeeping/`: `reports/balance-sheet`, `reports/trial-balance`, `reports/nominal`, `reports/aged`, `accounting-periods[/id][/close]`, `fixed-assets[/id][/dispose]`, `depreciation`, `corporation-tax[/id][/adjustments][/finalise]`. `health` now returns `ledger` alongside the trigger health. **New screens**: `ReportsScreen` rebuilt as six tabs sharing one date range with click-through from any figure to that account's history; `YearEndScreen`, `FixedAssetsScreen`, `CorporationTaxScreen`; `components/admin/ui.tsx` holds the shared table chrome so four screens cannot drift. Nav gains Assets, Year end and Corporation tax. `lib/money.ts` gains `countToDecimal` for the places a DAY COUNT has to divide money - kept separate from `toMoney`, which still refuses numbers outright. **Checks**: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint modules/uk-bookkeeping` 0/0, `npx vitest run` 2508 passed / 42 skipped including 30 new pure tax tests (`lib/corporation-tax.test.ts`), **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real 3 passed / 0 skipped** (four new migrations, so the gate applies), and `npm run test:ledger-guards` 27 passed - now including `lib/ledger-projection.live.test.ts`, 14 tests against a throwaway Postgres that assert the figures AND that total debits equal total credits after every one of them. **Shared-tree note**: another session in this same tree released `uk-bookkeeping` 0.2.3 (shop invoice voiding) while this was in flight, so this takes 0.2.4; its `shop.invoice-voided` extension point and `lib/external-sales.ts` were left untouched, and only this session's own files were staged in each of the three repos. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` and `Home.md` updated and pushed.)

Previous entry: (**Voiding an invoice now takes the sale back out of the books, the invoice is filed against the entry as evidence, and the document stops printing product codes and delivery dates - `shop` **0.1.274** and `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.3**, both in the working tree, NOT tagged, NOT pinned, nothing committed.** Chris voided invoice OSR-000001 on the live site and it went on standing in Bookkeeping as posted income of 3673.20 with 612.20 of VAT on it - "what's worse is it still shows we need to pay the vat on it". Reproduced read-only against the live database first: `shp_invoices` said VOID at 18:06, `bk_transactions` still held the entry (`source='shop'`, `source_ref='OSR-000001'`, posted, unlocked). Cause is a missing seam, not a bug: `voidInvoice` in `lib/db/invoices.ts` only ever wrote the row, and shop published `shop.invoice-issued` and nothing else, so nothing on the other side was ever told. **Shop side.** New point **`shop.invoice-voided`** with `ShopInvoiceVoidedPayload` + `dispatchInvoiceVoided` (`lib/invoice-sinks.ts`; `gatherSinks` is now generic over the point). New `voidInvoiceAndTellSinks` in `lib/invoices.ts` - void the row FIRST, then tell the sinks, results onto `sink_results` - and the admin route's void arm goes through it. `resendInvoiceToSinks` no longer refuses a VOID invoice: it dispatches the void instead, which is the retro-fix path for any invoice voided before this existed, and the order screen's button reads **"Tell the books it is void"** on a voided one. The sink payload also gained **`document`** - `{ filename, mimeType, bytes: () => Promise<Buffer|null> }` - the only field on that contract that is a function rather than a fact, and deliberately so: sinks are called **in-process**, so handing the PDF over directly beats making the other module fetch the site's own URL back over HTTP (which needs a token, meets the PDF route's 5-a-minute rate limit, and dies behind deployment protection). It is lazy because printing runs chromium, and returns null rather than throwing when PDFs are off or the browser will not start. **Bookkeeping side.** `lib/external-sales.ts` registers `ukBookkeepingShopSaleVoider` at the new point and gained two pure, tested rules: `planSaleRemoval` (locked, finalised, reconciled against a bank line, or something corrects it -> **reverse**; otherwise -> **delete**) and `reversalLines` (the original's own lines negated, categories/treatments/rates untouched, gross still net+VAT, and no `-0.00`). Deleting is right for an open period - the sale never happened, and leaving a sale plus its mirror image makes the books harder to read; reversing is right once a return is filed or a bank line is matched, which is what a credit note is. Idempotent both ways: the reversal is written with `source_ref` `<invoice>:void`, so saying it twice changes nothing. `fileDocument` attaches the invoice PDF to the entry through core's media abstraction into Bookkeeping/<year>/<month> exactly as the upload route does it (bytes sniffed, size checked against `attachment_max_bytes`, `Buffer.isBuffer` false for a `Uint8Array` so it is re-wrapped), never throws, and is idempotent on the filename - so the shop's "send to the books again" button files a document that failed the first time. **Document changes** (all still switches in the builder): the Heading block's business name is now three-way and defaults to **'auto'** - printed only where there is no logo, since most logos have the name drawn into them; the Items block's product codes default to **off** (`showSku === 'yes'` now, not `!== 'no'`); the Payment block gained **`footerAlign`**, defaulting to centre with the fallback inside the component rather than only in `defaultProps`, so a layout saved before it existed centres too; and **the delivery promise never reaches an invoice at all** - `lineDetail` in `lib/invoice-tax.ts` drops the field the line's own batch names (`LineMeta.batch.fieldLabel`), because "by Wednesday 2nd of September" belongs on a confirmation email and is history or wrong by the time an accountant reads it. Starters and `INVOICE_FALLBACK_DATA` updated to match. **Live Deskwell write, and why it was needed:** another session had just inserted a real `shopInvoice` `Layout` row (`starter-shop-invoice-standard-live`, byte-identical to v0.1.272's fallback), and a published layout beats the fallback - so the module-side defaults would never have reached Deskwell's invoice. That row's `builderData` was patched in place: `showName` -> `no`, `showSku` -> `no`, `footerAlign` -> `center`. The first two take effect on the live site immediately (both the deployed code and the new code honour `'no'`); the centring waits for the module update. Backup of the row and a one-statement rollback are in this session's scratchpad (`invoice_layout_backup.json`, `invoice_layout_rollback.sql`); nothing else on the live database was touched, and **the standing `bk_transactions` entry for OSR-000001 was deliberately left alone** - once Deskwell is on these two versions, "Tell the books it is void" removes it through the module's own audited path, which beats a hand-written DELETE. Note for the next release: the existing invoice keeps its delivery rows because the lines are a snapshot; only invoices issued after the update lose them. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean for these two modules (12 errors remain in `modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/accounting-periods.ts` and `lib/fixed-assets.ts`, which are **another session's uncommitted in-flight work**, untouched here), `eslint modules/shop modules/uk-bookkeeping` **0 errors 0 warnings**, `npx vitest run` **2478 passed / 42 skipped** including 2 new invoice-line tests and 9 new reversal tests (`modules/uk-bookkeeping/lib/external-sales.test.ts`). No migration in either module, so the backup round-trip gate does not apply. Version note: shop 0.1.273 was taken by another session mid-task (the category-header fix), hence 0.1.274; `uk-bookkeeping` 0.2.3 is free as of writing but the fixed-assets/corporation-tax session in the same tree has not chosen its number yet. Wiki: `Shop.md` invoices section and `UK-Bookkeeping.md` "Sales handed over by your shop" both updated on disk, not pushed.)

Previous entry: (**Quotes layouts now live under the Shop tab at `/hq/layouts`, and Deskwell finally has a real `shopInvoice` layout instead of the invisible fallback.** Two separate things Chris asked for in one turn. **(1) `layoutTypes.host`.** New optional manifest field on `layoutTypes`: name another module and your layout types become sub-tabs on **its** top-level tab instead of opening one of your own. `quote-for-shop` sets `"host": "shop"`, so Quote document and Quote request page join Shop Home / Category / ... / Invoice document rather than sitting in a two-entry "Quotes" tab of their own. Core changes are all in the generator and the two things that gate on installs: `scripts/generate-module-layout-types.mjs` now collects declarations in one pass and merges hosted ones in a second (module order is alphabetical, so `quote-for-shop` is read before `shop`), and every emitted type carries its **own** `moduleName`. That ownership field is the whole point: `moduleLayoutTypeToGroup[key].moduleName` is now the type's module, not its group's, so `isInstalledLayoutType`, `planOrphanLayoutTypes` and `moduleStarterTemplates` keep answering about the module that declared the type. `getInstalledModuleLayoutGroups` (`lib/layout/installed-layout-types.ts`) filters **types** by installed owner and drops a group left empty, so a shop without the Quotes add-on sees the Shop tab minus those two sub-tabs; `declaredLayoutTypesByModule` (`lib/setup/starterLayouts.ts`) keys on the owning module, which is what stops the Shop being credited with (and seeded) the add-on's layouts. A `host` naming a module that declares no layout types in this build warns and falls back to the module's own `groupLabel`, so the tab can never go missing. Shipped as `quote-for-shop` **0.1.17** (`requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.1171, the release that reads the field), pinned here - core's pin was still on v0.1.14 while the checkout sat at v0.1.16, so this pin also picks up those two. Both halves degrade to today's behaviour without the other, so they can reach an install in either order. Wiki: `Authoring-a-module.md` gained a `host` row and a section. **(2) Deskwell's missing invoice document.** `shopInvoice` had **no `Layout` row at all** on the live database, exactly as the release that introduced it predicted: module layout starters seed at install time, Deskwell has had the Shop since 2026-07-16, and `seedPendingModuleLayouts` only re-seeds a module with **not one row across every type it declares** - the Shop has forty-eight, so the new type was never going to be picked up. PDFs looked right anyway because `renderInvoiceDocument` falls back to `INVOICE_FALLBACK_DATA`. Now inserted as a real, editable row: id `starter-shop-invoice-standard-live`, name "Standard invoice", published, `entire_site`, `builderData` **byte-identical to shop v0.1.272's `INVOICE_FALLBACK_DATA`** (v0.1.272 is what the site actually runs, per `Module.version`; the local checkout is ahead at 0.1.273 plus another session's uncommitted edits, and using either would have quietly restyled a live customer's invoices). Same id, name, description and conditions `seedTemplates` would have written, so a later seed run is a no-op. **Consequence worth knowing**: the fallback only applies when nothing is published, so from now on changes to the module's starter defaults no longer reach Deskwell's invoice - it is edited in the builder like any other layout. Rollback is one `DELETE` by that id, which puts the fallback back. No core code was involved in this half.)

FROM` per group with `jsonb_set` over `content[0]` and a `jsonb_agg` re-map of the inner block array keyed on `type`, so block order is preserved and no other prop is rewritten. Live immediately with no revalidate: the header blocks call `connection()`, so these pages render per request. 'The range'`, so a **newly seeded** category layout would have shouted it again regardless of the data fix. The field itself stays, so anyone who wants an eyebrow types one. Nothing on Deskwell moves when this lands: all 51 rows now carry an explicit `''`. `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` 0.2.2: statement import was broken on arrival - `date - bigint` - fixed and pinned in core 0.5.1169.** Chris imported the Tide PDF against the live site and got a 500 and "Something went wrong saving that." Cause: `findCandidateEntries` in `lib/reconciliation.ts` wrote `${dates[0]}::date - ${DATE_WINDOW_DAYS}`, and **Prisma sends a JavaScript number as int8 while Postgres has `date - integer` but no `date - bigint`** - so the match query failed before it ran, on every import, CSV or PDF. Fix: `::int` on all four day-count sites. The lesson is the test gap rather than the cast: it type-checked, it linted, `npm test` was 2467 green, and `test:ledger-guards` passed - because that suite drives a **raw `pg` client**, so it proves the SQL in the migrations and NOTHING about the SQL in the service layer, where every query goes through Prisma's parameter binding. Anything of the form "works in psql, fails through Prisma" was invisible to the whole suite. New `lib/import-roundtrip.live.test.ts` closes it: preview -> match -> commit -> re-import through the **real Prisma client** against a `cactus_rt_*` throwaway database, asserting the matched line ties to its existing entry rather than doubling it and that a second import of the same file keeps nothing. `npm run test:ledger-guards` now runs both files. Reproduced against the live Deskwell database read-only first (the fastest discriminator was checking the `bk_*` tables existed - they did, so it was never a missing migration), then proved on a throwaway. Worth remembering for any module: a JS number in raw SQL arithmetic against a date or an interval needs an explicit cast, and assignment into an int4 column is fine because Postgres has an assignment cast where it has no operator.)

Previous entry: (**Shop invoices, designed in the page builder and handed to the books - `shop` **0.1.272** and `uk-bookkeeping` **0.2.1**, both pushed and released; core **0.5.1168** pins them.** (The bookkeeping half went out as 0.2.1 rather than riding 0.2.0: another session tagged 0.2.0 for its own bank-statement/journals work while this was in flight, and a released tag is never moved.) Chris: a setting to auto-create an invoice once an order is completed, with invoice settings, an editable invoice layout at `/hq/layouts` in the manner of quotes, and - where `uk-bookkeeping` is installed - the same invoice recorded there for the VAT return. **Shop side.** New `migrations/023_invoices.sql` (also written into `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs, per this module's convention): `shp_invoices` + `shp_invoice_number_seq`, everything on the row a **snapshot in JSONB** (`seller`, `customer`, `lines`, `tax_breakdown`, `wording`) rather than a join, because an invoice is what was charged on a day and re-deriving it after a product rename or a change of address would rewrite history. One live invoice per order is enforced by a **partial unique index** (`WHERE status = 'ISSUED'`), not a read-then-write - the order screen and the bulk status bar both react to a status change and can genuinely race; a loser reuses the winner's invoice and the number it burned is simply spent (a gap beats two invoices for one order). Voided rather than edited or deleted, with a mandatory reason. Config gained an Invoices block (`invoicesEnabled` default **false**, `invoiceIssueOn` MANUAL|PAID|DISPATCHED|**COMPLETED**, prefix, payment-terms days, the seller identity fields incl. `invoiceVatNumber`, the wording fields, `invoiceShowToCustomer`, `invoicePdfEnabled`) and a fifth **Invoices sub-tab** on `ShopSettingsTab`. Issue path is `lib/invoices.ts` (`issueInvoiceForOrder`, `resendInvoiceToSinks`, pure `shouldIssueOn`), hooked into `applyOrderStatusChange` (SHIPPED->DISPATCHED, COMPLETED) and `fulfillPaidOrder` (PAID); both **swallow and log** a refusal, because a status change or a payment webhook must not fail over paperwork. Tax point is the paid date where known, else today, computed **in the site's own timezone** (`SiteConfig.timezone`, `en-CA` formatting) - a UTC slice of a payment taken at half past midnight files it in the previous quarter. **The arithmetic is the risky part and is pinned**: new pure `lib/invoice-tax.ts` + 12 tests. Line tax comes from the stored `shp_order_items.tax_amount` (what was charged) rather than a fresh calculation; an order-level discount is apportioned by value exactly as `resolveOrderTotals` did, so line money columns keep their own pre-discount arithmetic while the net/tax/gross that feed the summary are post-discount; **delivery's CHARGE is split by value but its TAX follows each row's own rate** - splitting the tax by value handed a zero-rated row a share of VAT, which is a wrong return and was caught by the mixed-rate test; and the rows are reconciled at the end so the summary sums exactly to the order's own tax and total. **Document**: new layout type `shopInvoice` ("Invoice document", Shop group) with six blocks in `components/puck/invoice-parts.tsx` (Heading, From and to, Items, Totals, **Tax summary**, Payment and terms), one render path shared by editor and RSC, `lib/invoice-doc-context.ts` (+ a sample invoice for the canvas), `components/public/invoice-doc-css.ts` (tokens, with @media print forcing ink on paper), three starters. **It never refuses**: unlike the quote document, a missing published layout falls back to `INVOICE_FALLBACK_DATA` (the standard starter's own blocks), because module layout starters seed at INSTALL time and any shop that already had this module - Deskwell - will never be seeded this type; an invoice may be somebody's only copy of a legal record. Bare page at `app/public/shop/invoice/[number]` (chrome stripped the way the quote view does it), PDF at `/api/m/shop/public/invoices/[number]/pdf` via `lib/invoice-pdf.ts` (puppeteer + @sparticuz/chromium; no core change needed - `next.config.ts` already traces the packs into every `/api/m/**` function). Access three ways: an HMAC link token (`lib/invoice-token.ts`, mirrors `order-receipt-token.ts`, nothing personal in the URL), the member whose order it is, or a staff session; anything else is a **404 not a 403**, since invoice numbers run in sequence. Admin: `GET/POST /api/m/shop/admin/orders/[id]/invoice` (issue / resend / void, void gated on `shop.manage`) and an Invoice card on `OrderDetailScreen`; member order page links to it when `invoiceShowToCustomer`. **The seam**: shop publishes **`shop.invoice-issued`** (`lib/invoice-sinks.ts`) and hands every registered sink a flat, serialisable payload carrying the per-rate net/tax/gross; sinks never fail the invoice, and what each said is stored on `shp_invoices.sink_results` and printed on the order screen, because a sale that quietly failed to reach the books is not noticed until the return is due. **Bookkeeping side** (`uk-bookkeeping`, riding the 0.2.0 another session already has in flight): new `migrations/008_external_sales.sql` adds `external_sales_enabled` (default TRUE), `external_sales_category_id` (FK, NULL = the seeded `sales` category) and `external_sales_status` to `bk_settings`, plus an index on `("source","source_ref")`; new `lib/external-sales.ts` registers `ukBookkeepingShopSaleRecorder` at `shop.invoice-issued`, maps each tax row to a transaction line (percent -> rate code: 0 zero-rated, >=15 standard, else reduced; **zero-rated rather than exempt/outside-scope on purpose** - all three carry no VAT but only zero-rated belongs in box 6, and a shop's tax table only knows the rate), is idempotent on `source`+`source_ref`, and on `BackdatedIntoClosedPeriodError` saves the entry as a **draft** rather than losing it. It imports nothing from shop - the payload type is a structural copy, because the books are installed on sites with no shop and must still compile. Settings section "Sales from elsewhere on this site" added to `BookkeepingSettingsTab`, with the off switch explained: a business that also imports its bank statements would otherwise count every sale twice. **Not built, deliberately** (not asked for): no invoice email to the customer, no invoices list screen of its own (they hang off the order), and **a refund does not credit the books** - a credit note is a separate document, so a refunded order needs a matching entry by hand. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` **0 errors 0 warnings**, `npm test` **2467 passed / 38 skipped**, and the backup gate applies (new table AND new sequence) - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS, **3 passed / 0 skipped**. Worth knowing for next time: it failed twice first, both on `dump.ts`'s 58s interactive-transaction budget (58.5s and 58.8s), and neither failure was the change - the round-trip builds the CORE init schema only, which this touched not at all. Measured cause: the link to the VPS was running ~140ms a query and ~4s a connect that afternoon, so a dump that normally takes 32s ran over the budget; the third run passed in 32s with nothing changed. Separately, because the round-trip never applies MODULE migrations, both new files were proven directly on a throwaway `cactus_rt_*` database (all of shop's 001-023 then all of bookkeeping's 001-008, in order, applied TWICE for idempotency, then: `shp_invoices` present, `shp_invoice_number_seq` present and issuing 1, `bk_settings` carrying the three `external_sales%` columns, a second ISSUED invoice on one order refused by `shp_invoices_order_issued_key`, and the same insert accepted once the first is voided). Wiki: `Shop.md` gained an Invoices section (committed and pushed). `UK-Bookkeeping.md` gained a "Sales handed over by your shop" section, but that whole page is still UNTRACKED in the wiki checkout - it is another session's new page - so the section sits on disk and goes up whenever they add it. **Deskwell:** nothing was applied to the live database; `shp_invoices`, the sequence and the three `bk_settings` columns arrive when the owner updates the install onto these two module versions.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` 0.2.0 in the working tree: PDF bank statements, bank reconciliation, double-entry journals and a director's loan account. NOT tagged, NOT pinned, nothing committed.** Chris attached a Tide PDF statement and asked for it to import, plus journal entries, a director's loan account and - mid-task - reconciliation against statement lines. Four new libraries and three new migrations; see the UK Bookkeeping section for the detail. The parts worth carrying forward: (1) **a PDF bank statement can be read with no dependency at all** - `lib/pdf/*` is a lexer, an object/stream reader and a positioned-text extractor, about 700 lines, because every PDF library is built to render pages and this needs only "what text is where"; the silent killer is that a hex string in a content stream is BYTES (`<000A>` is two bytes, not one code unit) and getting that wrong drops glyphs with no error - the statement came back missing every capital C, every pound sign and half its digits. (2) **The statement's own running balance is a free correctness check** and also settles which way round the statement runs, which is the only thing that can order two payments made on the same day. (3) **Reading the table is layout-driven** - find the header row, take the columns from where its words sit - so a bank we have never seen works; the only bank knowledge is header synonyms. (4) **Journals reach no VAT box, deliberately and permanently**, and are therefore NOT locked by filing a return, because year-end accruals are dated inside quarters that were filed months earlier. (5) The balance check must be a **deferred constraint trigger** - a per-row one would reject every journal ever written and every backup restore. Proven with `npm run test:ledger-guards` (9 tests, real Postgres, includes re-running every migration); backup round-trip a real 3/0; full suite 2453 passed. Wiki page rewritten, not yet pushed.)

Previous entry: (**The Collection Browser block had no editor `render` and took the whole page builder down with it - `shop` **0.1.271**, pushed and released; core untouched.** Chris went to `/hq/pages/<id>` for the collections page to flip the new Include switch and got the admin error boundary, console reading `TypeError: e is not a function. (In 'e(a)', 'e' is undefined)`. Cause: `shopCollectionBrowserPuckComponent` in `modules/shop/components/puck/ShopCollectionBrowser.tsx` was the **only** block config in the whole repo with no top-level `render` (swept every `modules/*/components/puck/*.tsx` editor half to confirm - 1 hit out of 109 blocks). Puck calls `config.components[type].render(props)` unconditionally, so it called `undefined` and threw during the editor's render pass, before the canvas painted - which is why the failure was the whole builder rather than one blank panel, and why every other InfoPage opened fine (`collections` is the only one carrying that block; `home-new` carries `ShopProductGrid` and is unaffected). **Predates all of today's work** and was NOT introduced by 0.1.270, which kept the same shape. The storefront was never affected: `shopCollectionBrowserPuckRscComponent` spreads the base config and then sets its own `render`, so the live page always drew correctly - which is exactly why nothing looked wrong until somebody tried to EDIT a page carrying it. Fix is one line, `render: ShopCollectionBrowser`, pointing at the placeholder component that was already written and exported and had simply never been attached. Worth remembering as a class of bug: an editor-half block config missing `render` is invisible to `tsc` (the config objects are plain literals, not typed against Puck's `ComponentConfig`), invisible to eslint, invisible to every test, and invisible on the storefront - it only ever shows as a dead page builder. If a block is ever added without a canvas render again, the sweep above is the way to find it.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` VAT periods now follow HMRC's real calendar, and the HMRC credentials are pasted into the settings tab instead of the hosting console - module bumped to 0.1.5 in the working tree, NOT tagged, NOT pinned (modules.json still v0.1.4), nothing committed.** Chris reported his registration (EDR 10 Jul 2026) produced a first period of "10 Jul - 09 Oct 2026"; HMRC's actual first period is EDR to the end of the first stagger month - his is 10 Jul to **31 Oct**, due **7 Dec** - because every HMRC period ends on a calendar month end (quarterly stagger groups Mar/Jun/Sep/Dec, Apr/Jul/Oct/Jan, May/Aug/Nov/Feb; verified on gov.uk 2026-08-21). Fix: new pure `lib/period-dates.ts` (month-end-aware calendar maths; "a calendar month after 30 Apr" is 31 May, which is why April's return is due 7 Jun) + `lib/period-dates.test.ts` (16 tests incl. the reported case); `bk_settings` gains **`first_period_end` DATE** via new idempotent `migrations/004_first_period_end.sql` (001 edited in place too for fresh installs - harmless overlap, applied files are skipped by name); `generateLocalPeriods` lays period 1 as [start, first_period_end] (default when unset: frequency out from the start, snapped to that month's end - reproduces 31 Oct for the reported case), later periods calendar-aligned and anchored to the first end, **computes and stores `due_date` for local periods** (1 month + 7 days; annual accounting 2 months, or 1 month for a sub-4-month period - both per gov.uk), backfills a NULL due_date on existing non-submitted local rows via the ON CONFLICT arm, and **sweeps stale scaffolding first** (open + source='local' + no period_key + no snapshots + range not in the new layout → deleted, audited as new action `period.relaid`) so a layout made before the end date was known self-heals instead of blocking the correct ranges for ever. Settings/route/UI carry `firstPeriodEnd` with cross-validation (end >= start). Second ask: the settings tab's HMRC card now takes **HMRC_CLIENT_ID / HMRC_CLIENT_SECRET as paste-in fields** saving through core's `/api/admin/env` (they were already in the managed set via the manifest's `requiredEnvVars` - no core change needed), same pattern as square-payment's tab: booleans-only status, blank field leaves stored value alone, `skipped` surfaced not swallowed, local-mode → ".env.local + restart" text, non-admin → read-only fallback naming the vars; plus a six-step numbered walkthrough linking the HMRC Developer Hub registration and applications pages (sandbox app → subscribe VAT (MTD) + Test Fraud Prevention Headers → redirect URI → paste creds → production application). Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean; `eslint .` 0/0; `npm test` **2427 passed / 29 skipped**; migrations touched so the backup gate applied - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` real PASS **3/3, 0 skipped** on throwaway `cactus_rt_*` VPS databases. Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` §3/§6/§8 rewritten (stagger explanation, due dates, credentials-in-GUI) - on disk, wiki NOT pushed. Release + pin bump + Deskwell's own module pin are the owner's follow-up steps.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` gained `migrations/003_attachment_guard_columns.sql` - the locked-attachment guard now freezes `position`, `uploaded_by_user_id` and `created_at` - **0.1.4**, core **0.5.1165** pins it.** (An earlier session swept this entry's first draft into `v0.5.1164` while it still read "NOT released", and that core release pinned **0.1.3**, which does NOT contain 003 - the module tag was already cut. Hence 0.1.4: a released module migration file is never edited, and neither is a released tag.) Closes the first of the two LOWs the hardening pass below left open: 002's `bk_guard_locked_attachment` comment promised the four storage-pointer columns (`url`, `media_provider`, `media_key`, `media_id`) were the only thing that gets through on a locked row, but the refusal list stopped at `transaction_id`/`name`/`filename`/`mime_type`/`size`/`sha256`/`locked_period_id`, leaving those three freely mutable on evidence for a filed return. 003 is `CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION` + `DROP TRIGGER IF EXISTS`/`CREATE TRIGGER`, idempotent, trigger name unchanged so `lib/health.ts` needs nothing; 002 is left byte-identical - released module migrations are superseded by a later numbered file, never edited - and 003's header states 002's gap plainly instead of repeating the false comment. Nothing legitimate is newly refused: no module code writes those three columns after INSERT (`position` is set once at upload, the media rewriter touches only `url`/`media_key`), and restore safety is unchanged (still a row-local BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE guard; TRUNCATE fires no row triggers). The second LOW - uninstall stranding the seven `bk_guard_*` functions - remains open. Checks: module migration changed, so the backup gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS, **3 passed / 0 skipped**; the migration itself proven on two throwaway `cactus_rt_*` databases on the VPS (control run: 002 alone really does allow all three columns on a locked row; with 003: all three refused, `name`/DELETE still refused, storage pointers still repointable, lock still one-way, unlocked rows untouched, and 003 applied twice cleanly - so the whole-file `client.query` path the migration runner uses parses it); `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` + module tests 56 passed / 0 failed / 10 skipped; `npm run typecheck` clean; `eslint .` **0 errors, 0 warnings**. Two housekeeping changes rode along in the same turn, both at Chris's instruction. **(1) `eslint.config.mjs` ignores `**/.venv/**` and `**/site-packages/**`** - a matplotlib file inside a scratch folder's Python virtualenv was the single warning standing between the tree and the zero-warnings gate, and it was nothing to do with the project. **(2) Every dated scratch folder in the repo root was deleted** - 45 untracked ones, 688 MB, the `*_2026_08_*` working directories other sessions had left. Said plainly because it is not recoverable: **that took 42 `rollback.sql` scripts and a pile of `backup_*` captures of live Deskwell rows with it**, so writes made to the live database this month no longer have an undo on disk, and `filter_pages_batch_2026_08_21/update_rewritten.sql` - queued, never run - is gone too (the entry below is corrected in place). Chris was shown exactly that list of consequences before choosing. **`collections_seo_2026_08_19` went too, on a second explicit instruction** - it was the one folder of the 46 that is committed to git (12 tracked files including its own `rollback.sql`), so unlike the other 45 it IS recoverable, and it currently shows as 12 uncommitted tracked-file deletions in the working tree. Nothing was committed. The repo root now holds no `*_2026_*` folders at all.)

Previous entry: (**`uk-bookkeeping` hardening + feature pass - working tree only, version NOT bumped, NOT released; migrations deliberately untouched so the backup gate is untripped.** Chris: 'scan for bugs and fix them; then implement more advanced features; then best-2026 UX.' Five parallel review agents over lib/HMRC/routes/UI/migrations surfaced ~35 real defects; all fixed except two LOWs that need a schema or core change (the locked-attachment guard not freezing `position`/`uploaded_by_user_id`/`created_at`, and uninstall stranding the seven `bk_guard_*` functions - both noted, neither reachable without a new migration file). **The critical one: every token refresh was killing the HMRC connection.** `tokens.ts`'s guarded write compared `last_refresh_at` (TIMESTAMPTZ, microseconds) against a value that had round-tripped through a JS Date (milliseconds), so the `IS NOT DISTINCT FROM` guard failed ~always, the rotated refresh token was thrown away, and the next refresh presented the already-consumed token -> `invalid_grant` -> 'reconnect' roughly every 4 hours. Fixed with `date_trunc('milliseconds', ...)` both sides; a losing racer now also re-reads the winner's token before declaring death, and 5xx/429 refresh failures no longer burn the connection to 'expired'. **Other heavy hitters**: chain-head reads ran on the global client so `FOR UPDATE` evaporated in autocommit (writeSnapshot now takes the caller's tx; appendAudit retries on 23505 instead of silently dropping the audit row); `recordSubmission` had no status guard, so an unfinalise racing the HMRC call filed the return and locked nothing - it now claims `WHERE status IN ('finalised','open')`, snapshots workings computed BEFORE the network call, and on any local failure preserves the HMRC receipt in the append-only audit log before surfacing `receipt_not_recorded`; `lockPeriodRecords` locks by MEMBERSHIP (scheme+dates, recomputed in-tx) rather than the stale `finalised_period_id` tag; `markSubmittedElsewhere` gained the same records-changed gate the HMRC path has; `reconcileWithHmrc` refused to run on an open period (open->submitted bypass); the closed-period guard is now scheme-aware per period (cash membership is `settled_date` - money could previously settle into a filed return and its VAT never reach HMRC) and covers adjustments (a correction dated inside a filed period would never have been filed at all); finalise/unfinalise/mark are claim-first RepeatableRead transactions computed in-tx; `addMonths` roll-over (31 Jan + 1mo = 3 Mar) replaced by anchored+clamped layout done as ONE `unnest ... ON CONFLICT` insert that also refuses overlapping ranges; CSV export got formula-injection escaping (`=`,`+`,`@`, minus-led non-numbers) and keyset pagination (OFFSET paging over live writes dropped/doubled rows), plus new kinds `snapshots`/`snapshot-lines`/`hmrc-calls` so the 'export everything' claim is true; `updateTransaction` can change `entry_type` without violating the adjustment CHECK; import commit is one transaction with per-row server-side validation (`insertTransactionRows` extracted so createTransaction and the importer share one INSERT); `validateFraudHeaders` no longer reports HMRC 4xx/5xx as 'nothing is wrong'; `Gov-Client-Multi-Factor` carries the session's real sign-in time (from `getSessionCreatedAt`) instead of fabricating an MFA event per call; OAuth `returnTo` constrained to same-site paths both ends (open-redirect after Government Gateway sign-in) and a relative returnTo no longer converts a successful connect into 'exchange-failed'; attachment downloads survive Unicode filenames (ASCII fallback + RFC 5987 `filename*`); `hmrc/liabilities`+`payments` raised from `bookkeeping.access` to `bookkeeping.submit` (they can rotate the single-use refresh token); trigger-message regex covers all four guard texts (409 not 500); `?limit=abc` no longer 500s; settings validate thresholds/dates and **the scheme change is now actually refused** while an open period holds entries (the comment claimed periods.ts did this; nothing did) with empty open periods following the new scheme. **UI**: `addStrings` no longer crashes the whole entry form when someone types '1,000' (BigInt SyntaxError mid-render, form lost); editing an entry no longer silently wipes `is_capital` (detail screen hardcoded false into the edit form and the server replaces lines wholesale - SA103/CT600 groupings quietly wrong); **Send to HMRC now shows HMRC's legal declaration in a focused `role=alertdialog`** before anything moves (previously one unconfirmed click filed a real return); every fetch on every screen catches network failure instead of leaving 'Loading…'/busy-forever (the submit path says plainly that it is UNKNOWN whether the return landed and routes to 'Check with HMRC' via a new `uncertain` state); stale-response races fixed with AbortController + 300ms debounce on the text filter; dates render at UTC so nothing slips a day west of Greenwich and `today()` is the local wall clock (UTC gave a UK owner yesterday between midnight and 1am all summer); import's '?status=draft' link actually filters now (URL params read on mount); line keys by uid not index; labels/aria on every field. **Features**: new **Overview tab** (`overview/page.tsx` + `DashboardScreen` + `GET admin/dashboard` off new `lib/dashboard.ts` - VAT position now, next due + days left, month in/out, drafts + missing-receipt counts, latest entries; navEntries now lands there); **bulk draft review** (`POST admin/transactions/bulk` post/delete, per-row outcomes, tick-boxes appear only when the list is filtered to drafts); **counterparty intelligence** (`GET admin/transactions/suggest` - datalist of known names + auto-category on blur, never overriding a human's pick); **Money with HMRC** on the periods screen (existing liabilities/payments endpoints finally have a UI); **month-by-month report** (`monthlyBreakdown` in lib/reports.ts); category filter on the entries list; snapshot lines written as one `unnest` INSERT (was N+1 under PgBouncer). **UX 2026 pass**: sticky table headers, `tabular-nums` on every money column, loading skeletons, `role=status` live regions, focus moved to the declaration dialog, drag-drop onto the import card, Enter-to-save on the entry form. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on the module, module tests **55 passed / 10 skipped** (8 new pins in `lib/hardening.test.ts`: csvCell escaping, addStrings tolerance, import date roll-over). Wiki `UK-Bookkeeping.md` updated (Overview, import/bulk review, declaration step, Money with HMRC, monthly view, new exports, scheme-change refusal, mid-filing connection loss) - on disk, wiki NOT pushed. Core diffs: none.)

Previous entry: (**Filter collections can now be listed on a collections index, and shop collections gained the category-style description split - `shop` **0.1.270** and `filters-for-shop` **0.1.28**, both pushed and released; core untouched and its pins NOT moved.** Chris wanted the Filter Collections pages (`/hq/m/shop/products?tab=filters-collections`) to appear on `/collections`, with the switch only present when the filters module is installed. Done as a generic seam rather than a shop-knows-about-filters branch: **new extension point `shop.collection-index-sources`** (`modules/shop/lib/collection-index-sources.ts`, client-safe half in `collection-index-sources-shared.ts` - the Puck editor half imports the prop-key helper, so prisma must not be reachable from it).
