A provider returns finished card items `{id, name, href, description, coverUrl, productCount?}`; `resolveCollectionIndexSources()` reads the stored manifests filtered by `INSTALLED_MODULE_WHERE`, same shape as `resolveProductFieldProviders`. **New public probe route** `GET /api/m/shop/public/collection-index-sources` returns `[{id,label}]` (label off the manifest entry, no permission gate - it reveals only which modules are installed, same call search's own sources probe makes). `ShopCollectionBrowser` gained an async `resolveFields` that adds one `Include <label>` Yes/No select per registered source, keyed `include_<sanitised extension id>` via `collectionIndexSourceProp()`; with no such module installed the sidebar is byte-identical to before. The RSC half asks only the sources whose own field says `yes`, wraps each `list()` in try/catch (one source failing must not 500 the index), and appends the items after shop's own. `ShopCollectionCardItem` gained optional `href` (used in preference to the slug-built `/shop/collections/<slug>`, both in cards and in the pills display) and `productCount` became optional - the count line is dropped rather than printed wrong. **filters-for-shop 0.1.28** registers `filtersCollectionIndexSource` (`lib/collection-index-source.ts`) at that point with label "Filter collections", backed by new `listPublishedCollectionsForIndex()` in `lib/db/collections.ts`: PUBLISHED rows only (a draft is staff-only and the link would 404 for the public), `href` = the bare `/<slug>`, `description` = `short_description`, `coverUrl` = `og_image`, and **no productCount on purpose** - counting means running each page's whole filtered query, 169 of them on Deskwell. `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` raised to 0.1.270. **Core diffs: none.** Second half of the same turn: Chris asked for filter collections and collections to share one description format, with nothing lost; asked which direction, he chose "collections gain the rich format". So **`migrations/022_collection_content.sql`** (+ the same two columns written into 001 for fresh installs) adds `short_description` TEXT and `description_puck` JSONB to `shp_collections`, exactly mirroring `012_category_content.sql`; no `image_url` twin, since a collection tile already borrows its cover from its first member. The migration also **backfills `short_description` from `description` where the blurb is still NULL**, so every existing collection reads exactly as it did (the one description had been doing the blurb's job all along) - the long `description` is left in place rather than blanked, as it is the only copy an install has. New Puck block **`ShopCollectionDescription`** (`[Anchor]`, `shopCollection` only, editor/RSC split), new layout type `shopCollectionDescription` (`lib/collection-description.ts`, nothing registers blocks against it, so the builder is core's shared content parts with a bare root), new full-screen builder at `app/cactus-admin/shop/collections/[id]/description` + `StandaloneCollectionDescriptionEditor`, and `ShopCollectionHeader` now prints `shortDescription || description`. `ShopCategoryDescriptionBody` was refactored into a shared **`ShopDesignedDescriptionBody`** (takes `subject` + `layoutType`) with thin category and collection wrappers, so the designed/plain/nothing decision exists once. `listCollections()` stopped being `SELECT *`: it now uses a `COLLECTION_LIST_COLUMNS` projection plus `has_designed_description`, matching `listCategories`, so a listing never drags every builder document across. `listCollectionsForIndex` prints `COALESCE(NULLIF(short_description,''), description)` as the card blurb. Admin API accepts `shortDescription` (POST+PUT) and `descriptionPuck` (PUT, `z.any()` - Puck owns its own schema). **Fixed in passing:** shop's media reference rewriter and media usage provider only ever covered `shp_products.description_puck`, so a designed CATEGORY description's pictures read as unused and were not repointed when a blob moved - both now loop `shp_products`/`shp_categories`/`shp_collections`. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean for shop/filters (two pre-existing uk-bookkeeping errors from another session remain), `eslint` clean, client-graph + backup schema-coverage guards pass, and `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS - 3 tests, no skips. **Deskwell data note:** the new columns are NOT on the live database and were NOT hand-applied; they arrive with the backfill when the owner next updates the install onto shop 0.1.270.)

Previous entry: (**The checkout's two refusals became one red sentence with links in it - `shop` working tree only, version NOT bumped, core untouched, NOT released.** Chris: the review step said "Still to fill in above before you can place this order:" over a bullet list AND, separately, "Choose a payment method above to place your order." - two tellings-off for one refusal. Now one line: "Complete your email and full name above, and then choose a payment method above to place your order.", every outstanding bit a link to the box or choice it names. **New export `checkoutBlockedSegments(missing, decisions)` in `modules/shop/components/public/checkout-state.ts`** (with `CheckoutBlockedSegment = { text: string; fieldKey?: string }`): pure, returns the whole sentence as segments, `fieldKey` set meaning that segment is a link. Blank and wrong get different verbs ("complete your ..." / "correct your ..."), lists join with commas and a final " and ", the two halves join with ", and then ", the sentence opens with a capital wherever the opening word falls (including when it is a link, i.e. when only a payment method is outstanding), and an invalid field's `hint` is appended after the full stop as "Email - that does not look like an email address." `CheckoutReviewClient.tsx` now maps those segments: `fieldKey` becomes a `focusCheckoutField` button styled `color: inherit` + underline, everything else a `<span>`. `blockedReason()` is gone, replaced by `outstandingDecisions(): { key, text }[]` (payment method, tickboxes) which also drives the `placeOrder()` stale-render guard; `blocked = notice !== null`; the old `shop-place-order-missing` id and its `<ul>` are **gone**, `aria-describedby` is now just `shop-place-order-blocked`. Colour is `var(--color-danger)` (spine-500 light 4.9:1 on white, spine-400 dark 4.83:1 on the page background - AA both ways) and never a hex. Two new jump targets so the links have somewhere to go: `data-shop-field="paymentMethod"` on the FIRST radio in `CheckoutPaymentClient.tsx` (the ask is "pick one", not "pick this one") and `data-shop-field="agreements"` on the first REQUIRED tickbox in `CheckoutReviewClient.tsx`. Trap met on the way: both halves of the sentence used the same separator key numbering, so one paragraph got the same React key twice - the joining now happens once, in the pure builder, keyed by index at the render. Seven tests added to `checkout-state.test.ts` (23 pass), 66 shop public tests pass, `eslint` clean on all three changed files; `tsc --noEmit` was clean on this change, and the only errors in the tree at the time of writing are a parse error another session was mid-write on in `cart-line-css.ts`. No schema change, no config key, no new prop, no version bump.)

Previous entry: (**Two filter ticks now have to be answered by the same variation - `filters-for-shop` **0.1.27**, pushed and released; core untouched and its pin NOT moved.** Chris, off the live site: `/red-leather-office-chairs` was showing chairs whose leather is only sold in black and whose red is only sold in fabric. The cause is that `matchesSelection` in `modules/filters-for-shop/lib/filter-logic.ts` was handed one flat list of filter ids per product, so Red and Leather each only had to be true *somewhere* on the listing. It bites hardest across sources: Colour is an OPTION rule (variation option values) and Upholstery is an ATTRIBUTE rule (a `Material (spec)` value on the variation's child product), so Eclipse Plus satisfied Red through its fabrics and Leather through its Black Leather variant. **What changed.** `lib/db/matching.ts` gained `combos: Map<string, string[][]>` on `FltProductMatches` - one entry per enabled variation, holding the filter ids THAT variation resolves, folded and deduplicated in SQL (`array_agg(DISTINCT filter_id)` grouped by variation, then `SELECT DISTINCT product_id, combo`) because a page of 800 listings holds tens of thousands of (variation, filter) pairs and only a few thousand distinct combinations. Specs on the PARENT product are deliberately excluded from combos: they are true of the whole listing however it is configured, so they stay in the matrix only. `lib/filter-logic.ts`: `matchesSelection(filterIds, selection, combos?)` keeps the old flat check as a necessary condition, then works out which ticked groups are answered *only* by things a variation carries and requires one combo to satisfy all of those together; a group answered by a price band, a sub-category or a parent spec is settled listing-wide and constrains nothing. `facetCount` takes the new `FltMatrixEntry` tuple. `components/puck/ShopFilterGrid.rsc.tsx` interns the combos for the wire (a filter-id table, a deduplicated combo table, and per product a list of indices) - spelled out, a whole-catalogue page would have carried about a megabyte of repeated UUIDs. `components/public/FilterShell.tsx` takes the new optional `variations` prop and reads it back once into shared combo rows. **Proof, against the live catalogue.** Every leather option value in the shop: Black on 31 listings, Grey/Brown/White on 2 each, Green/Burgundy/Red on 1 each - so blue, teal, orange, yellow and purple leather chairs do not exist. Re-running all 173 filter collection pages under the new rule moved 15 of them and left 158 untouched: red-leather 12 to 2, green-leather 12 to 2, grey-leather 14 to 4, white-leather 18 to 8, black-leather 34 to 34, the three fabric-colour pages down 1 or 2, three high-back pages down 1, and five pages (blue/teal/orange/yellow/purple leather) to zero. Those five were deleted from `flt_collections`, and so were the four colour-leather pages that survived at 2, 2, 4 and 8 - Chris's call, rather than keep pages that thin; `black-leather-office-chairs` stays, its 34 were right all along. `filter_pages_batch_2026_08_21/update_rewritten.sql` carried the corrected copy for the six remaining pages whose counts move (three fabric, three high-back), to be run once the module update reached the site - **that file no longer exists**: Chris had every dated scratch folder deleted on 2026-08-21 (see the top entry), knowing this one was still queued. The rewrite has to be redone from the live data if those six pages are still to be corrected. The two survivors on the red page were genuine, for the record: Chesterfield in Burgundy Leather and Echo in Red Leather. **Not fixed here.** `modules/product-attributes-for-shop/lib/filter-logic.ts` carries its own copy of the flat matcher for its own spec panel; it was left alone.)

Previous entry: (**Tested `uk-bookkeeping` against HMRC's real sandbox and it found a defect that would have broken every single call - **0.1.2**, core **0.5.1161**.** Chris: 'test it against the hmrc sandbox.' There are no HMRC credentials on this machine, so the honest split is two tiers, and the first one needs none. **THE FINDING: the API hostnames were wrong and do not exist.** `endpoints.ts` had `test-api.service.gov.uk` and `api.service.gov.uk`; the real hosts are `test-api.service.**hmrc**.gov.uk` and `api.service.**hmrc**.gov.uk`. Neither of the wrong ones resolves in DNS at all, so **every HMRC call this module could make would have died with a bare `fetch failed`** - not a 401, not a configuration message, nothing an owner could act on. Transcribed straight out of the plan's §5.4 table without checking, which is precisely the class of thing a real call catches and a unit test never will: the sign-in host genuinely IS `tax.service.gov.uk` with no `hmrc` in it, so the two shapes sit side by side looking equally plausible. Caught within a minute of pointing the probe at the sandbox. **New `lib/hmrc/sandbox.live.test.ts`, gated `RUN_HMRC_SANDBOX=1`** so plain `npm test` never touches the network (it skips 8 tests there, which is why the module count reads 47 passed / 10 skipped). **Tier 1, no credentials, 8 tests, all passing:** every path the module calls answers **401 MISSING_CREDENTIALS** (obligations, returns POST, view-return, liabilities, payments, and the fraud-header validator), with a deliberately made-up path asserted to answer **404 MATCHING_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND** as the control - which is what makes a passing 401 mean 'this resource exists' rather than 'something answered'. **Tier 2** runs HMRC's own fraud prevention header validator via a `client_credentials` token; skipped here for want of credentials. **Two of my own expectations were wrong and the measurements corrected them,** both now pinned as tests: an unserved API version is answered **404, not the 406** content negotiation would suggest (`application/json` is also accepted on these resources, incidentally, though we go on sending the versioned type deliberately); and `/oauth/token` answers the documented shape and the versioned-Accept shape **identically**, so last release's Accept change was a tidy-up rather than the fix the notes claimed - the previous entry above is corrected in place and this release's notes say so. **What no automated tier can prove, stated rather than implied:** every VAT endpoint is user-restricted, so obligations, submission and viewing a return need a Government Gateway sign-in as a Developer Hub test user. That cannot be automated from here and is not pretended at; there is an eight-step manual script on the wiki page instead, ending with 'try to edit the entry you just filed - if it lets you, stop and report it'. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **2391 passed / 27 skipped**, plus `RUN_HMRC_SANDBOX=1` **8 passed / 2 skipped** against the live sandbox. No schema change, so the backup gate is untripped. Wiki: `UK-Bookkeeping.md`; module `README.md`.)
Previous entry: (**HMRC compatibility audit on `uk-bookkeeping` - **0.1.1**, core **0.5.1160** pins it.** Chris: 'ensure numbers are formatted for HMRC. ensure everything is compatible with HMRC's side.' Audited every outbound call against the published VAT (MTD) OpenAPI spec and HMRC's own OAuth examples rather than against memory, and found one thing that would have failed on every single call. **(1) The obligations sync was a guaranteed 400.** HMRC cap the obligations date range at 366 days and answer `INVALID_DATE_RANGE` to anything wider; the sync asked for eighteen months back plus twelve forward - thirty months - so **no install would ever have retrieved an obligation**. Their spec makes `from`/`to` optional *when status is O*, so it is now TWO calls: `status=O` with no dates at all (every outstanding obligation, however far ahead, which is the half that matters) plus one clamped `status=F` window for recent history, deduped by period so an obligation returned twice cannot trip the unique index on (start_date, end_date). A failure on the history call is caught and swallowed - somebody with nothing filed yet is exactly the person who most needs to see what is due. New `lib/hmrc/limits.ts` (pure, 8 tests) holds `clampRange`, and liabilities/payments now go through it too (they cap at 366 days as well, refuse anything before **2017-12-01**, and refuse a `to` in the future). **MAX_RANGE_DAYS is 365, not the documented 366**, on purpose: HMRC's own issue tracker carries a leap-year bug where a genuine 366-day range spanning a leap year is rejected anyway. **(2) The box limits are not all the same, and one shape for all nine was wrong.** `netVatDue` maxes at **99,999,999,999.99** - two orders of magnitude below its neighbours' 9,999,999,999,999.99 - and is the only one with a minimum of 0. `payload.ts` now checks each box against its own transcribed min/max and refuses locally with a sentence rather than spending a call to be told `INVALID_MONETARY_AMOUNT`. It also asserts the two identities HMRC re-check on their side (`VAT_TOTAL_VALUE`: box 3 = box 1 + box 2; `VAT_NET_VALUE`: box 5 = |box 3 - box 4|) - they cannot fail while the box query is the only producer, which is exactly why they are asserted: the day somebody adds a second producer, this refuses it rather than HMRC. **(3) `periodKey` and `vrn` are now validated before a call, not after one** - four characters of `[A-Za-z0-9#]`, nine digits respectively; an invalid one previously cost a round trip and came back as a code the owner could do nothing with. **(4) The versioned Accept header was on `/oauth/token`, and should not have been** - HMRC's own documented curl examples for both the authorization_code exchange and the refresh send `content-type` alone. Changed to match. **CORRECTED 2026-08-21 by measurement:** the rationale written here first ('a version an endpoint does not serve is answered 406') was wrong on both halves - HMRC answer an unserved version **404 MATCHING_RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND**, not 406, and the token endpoint answers both shapes IDENTICALLY (`invalid_client` 401). So this was a tidy-up, not a defect. Still right to match a published example, but the release note that called it something that 'could have had them refuse it outright' overstated it. **(5) New: HMRC will mark our own homework.** Their Test Fraud Prevention Headers API validates the headers on whatever request carries it, so **Have HMRC check the details we send** in the settings tab makes a real call with the real bag and reports their verdict, errors and warnings. Application-restricted rather than user-authorised, so it uses a `client_credentials` token of its own and works before anybody has connected a Government Gateway account - which is the point, since header evidence is a precondition of production approval and the alternative way to find out is ten working days into the application. That token is deliberately not stored: short-lived, authorises nothing about anybody's VAT account, and keeping it would be one more secret at rest for no benefit. Sandbox only; production reports UNAVAILABLE rather than pretending. **(6) `glossHmrcCode` now covers every documented code** for the endpoints this module calls, including `RULE_INSOLVENT_TRADER`, `NOT_FINALISED`, `VAT_TOTAL_VALUE`, `VAT_NET_VALUE`, `INVALID_NUMERIC_VALUE` and the four date/status codes. **(7) `Gov-Client-Public-Port` is never sent and that is now said out loud** in `describeMissingHeaders` - a serverless function cannot see the browser's source port, and HMRC's own page allows for a value that cannot be collected. **Confirmed correct and unchanged:** the `X-CorrelationId` / `Receipt-ID` / `Receipt-Timestamp` response header spellings, `Accept: application/vnd.hmrc.1.0+json` on every API resource, percent-encoding of the `#` in a period key on its way into a URL path, boxes 6-9 carrying `.00`, and the body being composed as text so no float ever exists. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **2391 passed / 19 skipped** (13 new). **Backup gate deliberately NOT re-run and that is correct** - no `migrations/*.sql`, nothing under `lib/backup/**` and no schema change in this pass. Wiki: `UK-Bookkeeping.md`; module `README.md`.)
Previous entry: (**New module `uk-bookkeeping` v0.1.0 - UK bookkeeping with Making Tax Digital VAT returns; core v0.5.1159 pins it.** Built end to end from `plans/PLAN-uk-bookkeeping.md`, all seven phases in one release rather than seven, because the plan's phase numbering (v0.1.0 through v0.7.0) conflicts with this platform's patch-only convention and every module's first release is 0.1.0. **The whole point of the module, and the thing every other decision follows from: no VAT box value is ever typed by a human, in any code path.** There is no service function that accepts one as an argument and no input field on any screen for one; the only way a number reaches HMRC is out of `lib/vat-boxes.ts`. 13 tables under `bk_`, two migrations - `001_initial.sql` (schema + 22 seeded UK categories) and `002_immutability.sql` (ten triggers), split so the guard can be read as one file. **Three corrections to the plan, all from reading HMRC's current documents rather than from memory.** (1) Boxes 6-9 are 'a monetary value (to 2 **zeroed** decimal places)' in the VAT (MTD) API, so they carry `.00` rather than being bare integers. (2) **Form VAT652 was withdrawn on 5 September 2025** - the separate error notification is now HMRC's online service, so every reference points at VAT Notice 700/45 instead; the Method 1 thresholds themselves (£10,000, or £10,000-£50,000 within 1% of box 6) were confirmed current on 2026-08-20 and ship as three settings. (3) The WEB_APP_VIA_SERVER fraud-header set is sixteen headers and does NOT include Local-IPs, Browser-Plugins or Do-Not-Track, which the plan listed, and DOES include `Gov-Vendor-Product-Name`, which it omitted; transcribed into `lib/hmrc/fraud-spec.ts` with the URL and the date it was read. **The one thing HMRC does not answer** is how to round boxes 6-9 to whole pounds - 700/12 is silent and 700 covers invoices - so it is a `box_rounding` setting, `nearest` by default, applied once and identically to all four, with `boxes_unrounded` kept in every snapshot. **Money never becomes a float**: NUMERIC(10,2), summed in Postgres, held as decimal strings, and the submission body is composed as TEXT rather than through `JSON.stringify` over parsed numbers. **The immutability design is written around the restore path** - `lib/backup/restore.ts` truncates and re-inserts without disabling triggers, so UPDATE/DELETE guards are free but the backdating rule is deliberately application-only (a BEFORE INSERT version would reject most of a restore and only show it during a real disaster recovery), and every FK is DEFERRABLE. Two deliberate carve-outs: a locked attachment may still have its four storage-pointer columns repointed (or moving a filed receipt in the media library would fail with an accounting error), and `bk_hmrc_api_calls` is write-once rather than append-only (the row goes in BEFORE the call, so a timeout leaves a trace). Layer 3 cannot bind the table owner, so `lib/health.ts` reads `pg_trigger` and a missing or disabled guard is a red banner on every page - the honest version of 'bulletproof'. **Zero core diffs**: the only changes outside `modules/uk-bookkeeping/` are the `modules.json` pin, the README module list, `wiki/UK-Bookkeeping.md` and this file. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **2378 passed / 19 skipped**, and - new module migrations - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 passed / 0 skipped**.)
Previous entry: (**Category and collection pages now publish a social image, and the SEO screen counts it - `shop` **0.1.267** + `ultimate-seo` **0.1.8**, module dirs only, NOT released.** Both rows have carried `og_image_id` since the SEO columns landed and neither `generateMetadata` had ever emitted it, so a landing page with a hand-written meta title and description still shared as a bare link. New `modules/shop/lib/catalogue-social-image.ts`: `resolveCategorySocialImage` / `resolveCollectionSocialImage`, plus the pure `absoluteSocialImageUrl(url, siteUrl)` (4 tests in `catalogue-social-image.test.ts`). Both `[slug]/page.tsx` files now return `openGraph` (title, description, `type: 'website'`, og:url built the same way `lib/sitemap.ts` builds it - `/shop/categories/<slug>` and `/shop/collections/<slug>`, which never move to the site root however `productUrlStyle` is set) and `twitter: summary_large_image` **only when a picture was actually found**. **The fallback chain is the part that matters.** Category: `og_image_id` -> its own `image_url` (stored as the media URL verbatim, so no lookup) -> the first photograph among the products the category lists. Collection: `og_image_id` -> `image_id` -> the first photograph among the products on the shelf. Read off the live Deskwell database before choosing: **48 categories, 0 with `og_image_id`, only 3 with an `image_url`; 39 collections, 0 with `og_image_id`, 0 with `image_id`**. The literal id-then-own-picture chain would therefore have lit up 3 pages out of 87, which is why the product-photo step is there at all - it is the same move the product page makes when it falls back to its first photograph, and `listCollectionsForIndex` already borrows a member's picture for the collection tiles. `firstListedPhoto` calls `listProducts` (status ACTIVE, `excludeHidden`, `storefront: true`) rather than hand-rolling SQL, so the draft, hidden-variant and out-of-stock rules match the grid below the fold; it scans `PHOTO_SCAN = 12` rows and takes the first with an image, via `getPrimaryProductImages`, so a run of picture-less products at the top cannot lose the page its image. Categories go through `resolveCategoryProductFilter` with the shop's own `categoryProductDisplayMode`, so a rolled-up parent may show a descendant's photo and an 'exact' category may not - same set the page itself lists. **`ultimate-seo` **0.1.8** followed in the same session** (Chris: "fix the ultimate-seo hasOgImage for categories and collections too"): new `modules/ultimate-seo/lib/shop-og-image.ts` - `shopCategoriesWithSocialImage(ids | null)` / `shopCollectionsWithSocialImage(ids | null)`, returning the set of ids that publish a picture, wired into both `lib/inventory.ts` and `lib/run-analysis.ts` in place of `!!og_image_id`. Raw SQL against shop's tables, never an import of shop's code, so this module still works with no shop installed - it reads the shop-wide `categoryProductDisplayMode` out of the `shp_settings` singleton jsonb (defaulting to shop's own `'rollup'`) so an `'exact'` category cannot borrow a descendant's photograph it never lists. Three deliberate differences from shop's own answer, all commented in the file: this asks whether ANY listed product has a photograph where shop scans the first twelve; shop's listing also applies out-of-stock hiding, which lives behind shop's code and a request scope; and a dangling `og_image_id` counts here and resolves to none there. Verified read-only against live Deskwell: **48/48 categories and 39/39 collections** now report a social image, from both the shop resolver and this SQL independently, with `categoryProductDisplayMode` = rollup and no per-category `'exact'` override on the site. **Ordering caveat, accepted:** `ultimate-seo` declares no `requiresModules` at all by design, so on an install still running shop <= 0.1.266 the screen would credit these pages with an image the shop has not started emitting yet. Self-correcting on the next shop update, and the same class of claim the product row already makes. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean (the one warning is bundled matplotlib JS in a python venv, pre-existing), `npm test` **2378 passed / 0 failed**. No schema change, so the backup gate is untripped. Wiki: `Shop.md`, `Ultimate-SEO.md`. **No commit, no push, no release - working tree only.**)
Previous entry: (**The SEO screen could not see the shop's landing pages - `ultimate-seo` **0.1.7**, core and every other module untouched, working tree, NOT released.** Chris: "fix our seo module to discover pages like https://deskwell.co.uk/green-office-chairs". That address is a **filter collection** (`flt_collections`, owned by `filters-for-shop`, claimed at the bare root through `publicRootSlug`), and `lib/inventory.ts` had four sources and only four: `InfoPage`, `gz_posts`, `shp_products` and `dir_entries`. Two more taxonomy types were missing on the same footing - `shp_categories` (48 on Deskwell) and `shp_collections` (39). The proof they were meant to be there all along: `seo_page_meta` on the live database ALREADY held 48 `shop-category`, 27 `shop-collection` and 1 `filter-collection` rows, written by the focus-keyword programme, every one with `score IS NULL` because nothing could ever load them. Those exact `entity_type` strings are the ones now used, so the orphaned rows light up rather than duplicating. **What changed, all inside `modules/ultimate-seo/`.** `lib/types.ts`: `EntityType` was a bare union, so the two zod route schemas hardcoded the same four strings a third and fourth time - now `export const ENTITY_TYPES = [...] as const` with the union derived from it, and both `app/api/admin/pages/analyze/route.ts` and `analyze-bulk/route.ts` take `z.enum(ENTITY_TYPES)`. That drift is exactly how a new type could be added to the inventory and still be rejected by the API. `lib/inventory.ts`: `shopCategories()`, `shopCollections()` and `filterCollections()`, gated on the live `Module` table the same way the existing three are (`shop` gates the first two, `filters-for-shop` the third), raw SQL only - this module never hard-imports another's code. `lib/run-analysis.ts`: `loadShopCategories`, `loadShopCollections`, `loadFilterCollections` plus two shared helpers, `hasDocContent()` and `mergedContent()`. **Judgement calls worth keeping.** URLs: categories and collections never move to the site root however `productUrlStyle` is set (the shop's own `product-url.ts` says so), so they are hardcoded `/shop/categories/<slug>` and `/shop/collections/<slug>`; a filter collection is ALWAYS the bare `/<slug>`. Status: neither shop taxonomy table has a status column - a category exists or it does not - so `isPublished: true`; `flt_collections` does, so `status === 'PUBLISHED'`. Content: these pages print a plain blurb AND a designed document, so `mergedContent()` folds the blurb into the front of the Puck doc as a synthetic `RichText` item rather than analysing them apart - and for a category the plain long description only counts when no designed one has replaced it, mirroring `ShopCategoryDescriptionBody`'s own call. All three set `titleIsH1: true` (verified: `FilterCollectionHeader.rsc.tsx:55`, the two shop `[slug]` pages, and both plain fallbacks all print `name` as the H1). `hasOgImage` reads `og_image_id` for the shop pair and the `og_image` URL column for filter collections. **Known consequence, deliberate:** 0/48 categories and 0/39 collections have an `og_image_id`, and neither page's `generateMetadata` emits `openGraph` at all, so all 87 now report "No social image". That is truthful - those pages genuinely publish none - and it is a gap in the SHOP's category/collection templates, not this module's to fix. Edit deep-links: `/m/shop/categories`, `/m/shop/collections`, and `/m/shop/products?tab=filters-collections` (a contributed tab on the Catalogue page, not a route of its own). `components/admin/PagesClient.tsx` gained the three `TYPE_LABELS`/`EDIT_LABELS` entries - Product category, Product collection, Filter page; the type dropdown builds itself from the data so it needed nothing. **Verified against the live Deskwell database, read-only:** `getInventory()` returns core-page 12, gazette-post 23, shop-product 442, shop-category 48, shop-collection 39, filter-collection 1, and `/green-office-chairs` comes back with its meta title, description, `hasOgImage: true` and the focus keyword already stored; `loadEntities()` on one of each yields 360, 115 and 36 words with 10 internal links on the filter page. `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean (the one warning is bundled matplotlib JS in a python venv, pre-existing), 23 module tests pass. The site audit crawl already covered all three - it reads `/sitemap.xml`, and `filters-for-shop/lib/sitemap.ts` and `shop/lib/sitemap.ts` both publish them. `wiki/Ultimate-SEO.md` updated.)
Previous entry: (**The column beside the pinned checkout summary is now held still while the order scrolls - `shop` working tree, version NOT bumped, NOT released.** Follow-up to v0.1.262: the reserved run is ordinary page scroll, so the form slid up and off the top exactly while the shopper was checking the order against it. Chris picked 'freeze where it ended' out of three options. `CheckoutItemsClient`'s effect gains `neighbours(wrapper)` (the row's other children, empty unless the row is grid/flex with siblings) and `hold(px)`, which sets `transform: translateY(px)` on each of them, `px` = how much of the reserved run has been used (`mapped = clamp(spare - remaining, 0, spare)`). A transform, not sticky: it assumes nothing about what the other column is made of (a dropzone's children are whatever blocks were dropped in it) and changes no layout, so the row keeps the height the floor gave it. Held to the END rather than released at the finish line - at full hold the column's foot sits exactly on the row's foot (measured: never more than -4px past it, so it never reaches the block below), which is why there is no snap when the run finishes and the page carries on. `neighbourHeight` was rewritten off `offsetTop`/`offsetHeight` instead of rects, because rects carry the hold transform and a held column would have raised the floor, which lengthens the hold, which raises the floor - a runaway. Layout values cannot see a transform. Also fixed in the same pass: a JUMP (Home, back-to-top, an anchor, a restored position) carries no deltas to follow, so the list stayed wherever it was - jumping to the top of the checkout showed the order's LAST item. `Math.abs(dy) > innerHeight` now sets `body.scrollTop = mapped` outright. **Verified** in headless Chrome on a throwaway harness (deleted after) across form-taller / list-taller / equal / short-order: during the run the form column moves 0px while the list moves its full remainder, the held column never passes the row's foot, a jump to the top rewinds the list to 0 and releases the hold, and a short order sets no floor at all. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, 59 pass / 0 fail. Wiki: `Shop.md` checkout section.)
Previous entry: (**Filtered category pages sent every click to a 404 - `filters-for-shop` **0.1.26** and `shop` **0.1.265**, both pushed and released; core untouched, core pins NOT moved.** Reported off the live site: `/shop/categories/office-chairs?colour=green` offered the right cards, but clicking one landed on `/shop/products/prism-...-myrrh-green`, which on Deskwell is not an address at all. Deskwell runs `productUrlStyle: 'ROOT'` (confirmed in `shp_settings`), where a product lives at the bare `/<slug>` and `app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx` **deliberately** 404s the prefixed form via `shopClaimsRootSlug` - by design, no redirect. The card link itself was always right (`ctx.productHref`, built by shop's `buildCardContext` through `lib/product-url.ts`); what was wrong was the **swap** link the filter shell writes over it when a filter is ticked. `filters-for-shop/lib/db/matching.ts` string-concatenated `/shop/products/${child_slug}` for `FltSwap.href`, and `FilterShell.dressCard` sets that on `a.shop-card-link` whenever `preselectOnClick` is on - so ticking a colour swapped a working link for a dead one. `getProductFilterMatches(productIds, groups, urlStyle)` now takes the style as a third argument (passed `config.productUrlStyle` from `ShopFilterGrid.rsc.tsx`, which already had the config open) and builds the href through shop's `productHref`; the grid's own `ctx.productHref ?? ...` version-skew fallback goes through the same helper via a new `urlStyle` argument on `renderTaggedCards`. A sweep for the same defect found six more surfaces hardcoding the prefixed address, all of them 404s on a ROOT shop, all fixed the same way: **shop** - `CartDrawerClient`, `CartFullClient`, `CartPageClient` and `UpsellClient` (each already fetches `/api/m/shop/public/config`, which already publishes `productUrlStyle`, so each gained a `urlStyle` state seeded `'SHOP'` and set from that same response), `BuyAgainButton` (now takes a `productUrlStyle` prop from `app/public/shop/account/orders/[id]/page.tsx`, which is a server component with the config already open), the admin Products list's **Preview ↗** button and the product editor's Details panel **Web address** box. Two new bits of wiring: `modules/shop/components/admin/use-product-url-style.ts` `useProductUrlStyle()` - module-scope-cached sibling of `use-currency-symbol.ts`, same shape and same reason (admin screens render client-side with no server config) - and `DetailsPanel` gains a `productUrlStyle` prop, fed the state `ProductEditor` already keeps for the Search panel. No schema change, no new config key, no API change: `productUrlStyle` was already on the public config response. `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .` and `npm test` (2340 passed) clean.)
Previous entry: (**Filter Collections: any filtered view can now be a page of its own - `filters-for-shop` **0.1.25**, core untouched, NOT released.** Chris asked for SEO landing pages like "Green Office Chairs" - what `/shop/categories/office-chairs?colour=green` already shows, but as a page with its own address, page title, description and Puck intro. Three decisions taken with him first: pages answer at a **bare top-level slug** (`/green-office-chairs`), matching where products and Gazette posts already live; preselected filters are **ticked, not locked**, so the panel is the ordinary panel and a shopper can untick green; and all the pages share **one designed layout** rather than one layout each, because the point is building forty of them cheaply. **Zero core diffs** - every mechanism it needed already exists as a manifest hook: `publicRootSlug` (claim in `lib/root-slug.ts`, page at `app/root/[slug]/page.tsx`, asked after info pages, module indexes and shop's own products), `layoutTypes` (new `filterCollection` type, group label "Filters"), `shop.products-tabs` (second tab, id **`filters-collections`**, order 41, so the URL Chris quoted - `?tab=filters-collections` - is the real one), `lib/sitemap.ts` (published, non-noindex pages only), and the two `core.media-*` extension points the module already had. New migration **`003_filter_collections.sql`**: `flt_collections` (name, slug, status, source_type CATEGORY/COLLECTION/TAG/ALL, source_slug, short_description, intro_puck jsonb, meta_title, meta_description, og_image, noindex, position) + `flt_collection_filters`. **The source is a slug, not a foreign key, on purpose** - shop owns those tables and a dependent module must not constrain the module it depends on ([[feedback-module-to-module-isolation]]); a renamed category leaves a page pointing at nothing, which the admin screen reports. The preselected filters ARE a real FK, being this module's own rows, so a deleted filter takes its preselection with it. Three URL states per group, and the middle one is the whole trick (`lib/preselect.ts`, 16 tests): still on what the page started it on -> **no parameter**, so the page keeps its clean address; changed -> the group's parameter; **cleared -> an EMPTY parameter**, because without that an untick is indistinguishable from silence and the page's own tick goes straight back on the next refresh. Read and write round-trip, which the test asserts across every state. One trap found and closed while building: the grid's existing culling (`hideEmptyFilters`, and drop any group left with < 2 filters) would have quietly eaten a page's own preselection - "Chairs Under £200" on a source with one matching band would drop the band and show the lot at any price. Both rules now step aside for a preselected id; if it matches nothing the grid comes back empty, which is the honest answer. New blocks `FilterCollectionHeader` + `FilterCollectionIntro` (editor/RSC split, `[Anchor]`), `ShopFilterGrid` gains `preselectFilterIds` (injected, never an editor field) and the `filterCollection` layout type. Intro built through a private `filterCollectionIntro` layout type nothing registers against, reusing shop's `StandaloneDescriptionBuilder` - an import, not an edit. No published layout yet = a plain built-in shell, so a page works the day it is made. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **2324 pass / 19 skipped**, and - new tables, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. Wiki: `Shop-filters.md` (new "Filter collections" section + the untick-sticks note); module `README.md`.)
Previous entry: (**The pinned checkout summary now gets its own stretch of page once the form beside it runs out - `shop` working tree, version NOT bumped, NOT released.** Follow-up to v0.1.260, which only fixed the chaining half: with the pointer anywhere but over the summary, reaching the end of the form scrolled the page on into the footer while the order list still had items below its fold. `CheckoutItemsClient` now renders a plain wrapper `<div className='sci-fill'>` around the sticky `<section>` (refs `wrapRef`/`sectionRef`/`bodyRef`); `align-self:flex-start` moved off `.sci-sticky` since the wrapper is the grid item now, and `.sci-fill{height:100%;min-height:var(--sci-fill,0)}` sits in the desktop half of `SCI_CSS`. **The floor.** `measure()` sets `--sci-fill` to `max(section.offsetHeight, neighbourHeight(wrap)) + spare` where `spare = body.scrollHeight - body.clientHeight`. `neighbourHeight` walks `wrap.parentElement` (the zone div) -> its parent (the Split's grid) and takes the greatest `child.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - siblingTop` across the OTHER columns' children - the columns themselves stretch to the row height so measuring their boxes says nothing; it returns 0 unless the row is grid/flex with 2+ children, which keeps a single-column layout out of it. `height:100%` preserves the travel the column already had (an auto-height wrapper would unpin the block somewhere up the form) while `min-height` still counts towards the row's intrinsic height, which is what makes the page grow. No feedback loop: our column growing does not move the neighbour's children. **The hand-over.** A passive `scroll` listener banks deltas (`pending`, NOT dropped on the rAF guard - dropping them left the list short of its end on a fast flick) and, when `remaining = wrap.bottom - section.bottom` is within `spare` of zero, adds the same delta to `body.scrollTop`. Nothing is `preventDefault`ed, so trackpad, touch, keyboard and scrollbar all work and a pointer over the list still scrolls it natively. `ResizeObserver` on the body + section and a `resize` listener re-measure; `preview` (the Puck editor canvas) skips the whole effect. **Verified** in headless Chrome (puppeteer-core + the installed Chrome, throwaway static harness mirroring the Split DOM, deleted after): form taller, list taller and equal-ish. In all three the list starts moving one step after the form's last field lands on screen, finishes before the block unpins, and rewinds on the way back up; a short order sets no floor and behaves exactly as before. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean, 59 pass / 0 fail in `modules/shop/components/public`. Wiki: `Shop.md` checkout section.)
Previous entry: (**The tile's arrows and hover-swap now follow the arranged gallery - `shop` **0.1.264** + `shop-variations` **0.1.156**, core untouched, working tree.** Chris, off the live category page after installing 0.1.259/0.1.153: hovering a tile showed the product's own second photograph rather than the variation dragged into second place, and the arrows reached the promoted variations only after every one of the product's own. **Cause:** `buildCardContext` composed the carousel as `[...leadImages, ...ownImages, ...images]` - a straight concatenation. `leadImages` (0.1.222) was the only way a contributor could touch the front, so 0.1.153's provider could express "this one leads" (slot 0) and nothing else; a variation at slot 1 fell into the tail behind the whole of the product's own set. The gallery was arranged in one ordinal space and the tile was still reading two piles, so the tile and the page it opened disagreed - and shop's hover-swap only ever reveals the SECOND picture, so the arrangement it was meant to honour was exactly the thing it could not see. **Fix:** the same insert-at-index treatment `shop.product-detail-images` already got. `PartImage` gains **`position?: number|null`** (its index in the finished carousel, the product's own counted in; absent = after them, which is right for a supplementary colour). New **`modules/shop/lib/card-image-order.ts`** holds the merge - `mergeCardImages(own, contributed, lead)` - deliberately out of `card-template.tsx` so it can be tested without Prisma and the Puck renderer, the same reason shop-variations keeps `lib/gallery-order.ts`. `leadImages` still works and is not deprecated in behaviour: its images, having no positions of their own, claim slots 0..n, so a provider built against the previous contract leads exactly as it did. **One trap worth naming:** the fill loop measures against `images.length`, not a running own-index counter - a picture dropped by the url dedupe must not eat a slot, or every contribution after it drifts one place forward. `card-image-order.test.ts` pins that case explicitly, along with the reported defect (a variation at slot 1 lands second AND keeps `promoted: true`, which is what makes the hover-swap willing to reveal it). **Variations side:** `card-media-provider.ts` now emits `position: v.galleryPosition` on each promoted variation and stops using `leadImages` entirely; `galleryLeadsWithPromoted` and its test went with it, having had exactly one caller for about half an hour. `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` -> **0.1.264**, since positions are ignored by an older shop and the lead would be silently lost. (Both numbers jumped: other agents released shop 0.1.260-0.1.263 and shop-variations 0.1.154-0.1.155 while this sat in the tree, so the versions written into the first draft of this entry were stale before it was committed - a shared tree does that.) **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `npm test` **2324 pass / 0 fail** (8 new), all re-run against the tree as it stood after those other releases landed. No schema change this time, so no backup gate. Released: `shop` **v0.1.264**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.156**, core **v0.5.1154** pinning the pair.)
Previous entry: (**The sitemap was invalid XML from the first entry carrying a query string - core **0.5.1151** + `shop-variations` **0.1.155**.** Reported off the live site within the hour: "error on line 3304 at column 129: EntityRef: expecting ';'". Confirmed against the deployed file - `<loc>https://deskwell.co.uk/academy-…-visitor-office-chair?arm-option=fixed-arms&upholstery-colour=black-fabric&back=black-fabric-back</loc>`, a raw `&`, which is not a character in XML but the start of an entity reference. **Next pastes each entry's `url` into `` `<loc>${item.url}</loc>` `` with no escaping of its own** (`next/dist/build/webpack/loaders/metadata/resolve-route-data.js`), and the sitemap protocol requires entity-escaping there. Of the live file's **19,829** URLs, **18,211** carried an `&` - and an XML parser stops at the FIRST one, so the whole 5.3 MB file was unreadable from line 3304 down, ordinary product pages included. New `lib/seo/sitemap-xml.ts` (`escapeSitemapUrl` / `escapeSitemapEntries`, 8 tests) applied as the last step of `app/sitemap.ts`. **Escaping lives in core's funnel, not in the module**: a module writing its own URLs should not have to know how Next serialises them, and the next module to publish a query string would repeat the fault. The corollary is now a documented contract - a module's `getPublicSitemapEntries` hands URLs over RAW, and anything pre-escaped comes out double-escaped (there is a test pinning that, so the trade-off is written down rather than remembered). Proof rather than reasoning: the deployed 5.3 MB file was pulled down, `<loc>` contents re-escaped by the same rule, and `xmllint --noout` went from `parser error` to clean. `shop-variations` 0.1.155 is a manifest-only bump to `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.1151`, so the broken pairing (0.1.154 + core 0.5.1150, which is what shipped an hour ago) cannot be installed by anyone else. Wiki: `Architecture-overview.md`, `Authoring-a-module.md`. **Also reported and NOT a fault:** that the sitemap page "needs us to login". Checked rather than reasoned about - a real browser with no cookies at all was pointed at `https://deskwell.co.uk/sitemap.xml` and got **200 `application/xml`**, address bar unchanged, one network request, no redirect. Site status is `live`, `hideFromCrawlers` false, the members gate is not provisioned on this install, the SEO screen's **View sitemap.xml** button is an absolute `/sitemap.xml` in the deployed version, and nothing in core or any module emits `WWW-Authenticate`. Chris withdrew it. Worth keeping the negative result: the only proxy branch that redirects to the admin login needs a path already starting with the admin prefix, so a future report of this shape is about the URL that was opened, not about the sitemap route.)
Previous entry: (**The SEO Pages screen grew up, product variations went into the sitemap, and /favicon.ico finally answers with the site's own icon - core **0.5.1150** working tree plus `ultimate-seo` **0.1.6**, `shop-variations` **0.1.154**, `shop` **0.1.261**, NOT released.** Three asks in one turn. **1. `/hq/m/ultimate-seo/pages` was very basic.** `PagesClient.tsx` had a search box, a content-type dropdown and a five-column table in whatever order `getInventory()` happened to return - 800-odd rows, all of them, no sorting at all. Now: **eight sortable columns** (page, type, status, description, focus keyword, issues, score, analysed), each starting the way round it is useful (`INITIAL_DIR` - worst score first, most problems first, longest-unlooked-at first, missing descriptions first) and reversing on a second click, with `aria-sort` on the `<th>` and a real `<button>` inside it; **rows with no score, no keyword or no date sort to the bottom in BOTH directions** (`missingFor` in `sortRows`) because absent is not "worst" and a wall of blanks would bury what was asked for. Eight **clickable stat tiles** above the table (total, average, good/needs work/poor, never analysed, no description, score out of date) that each apply their own filter. Filters for content type, published state, score band and **issue**, the issue list built from what the analyser actually found (`issueOptions`, commonest first with counts) plus two synthetic keys: `_unanalysed` and `_stale`. **Stale** is new and is the one nobody asks for: `analyzedAt < updatedAt` means the score describes a version of the page that no longer exists - flagged in the row, in the detail panel and as a filter, and deliberately never inferred where either date is null (a Directory entry records no `updatedAt`). Also: tick boxes with **Analyse selected** and **Select all *N* matching**, pagination (25/50/100/all), **CSV export** of the current view in screen order (BOM, quoted cells, `'` prefix on a leading `=+-@` so a title cannot run as a formula), and view state (filters, sort, page size) remembered in `localStorage`. All the decisions live in new pure `modules/ultimate-seo/lib/page-view.ts` (`toRow`/`filterRows`/`sortRows`/`summarise`/`issueOptions`/`toCsv`) with 18 tests in `page-view.test.ts`; the component holds state and markup only. Bulk analysis is unchanged underneath - same 25-per-request walk, same `AbortController` Stop. **2. Variation URLs in the sitemap.** New `modules/shop-variations/lib/sitemap.ts` publishes one URL per enabled variation as the parent's address with the storefront's own option parameters on it - `?headrest=with-headrest&upholstery-colour=rivet-forge`, exactly the form `lib/url-selection.ts` reads back. Three queries (variants with `array_agg` of their value ids, options, values), the child row aliased **`p`** so `outOfStockSql()` splices in against the thing that actually carries the stock, the shopper's answer on hidden stock and never the staff exemption, `shopStatus === 'CLOSED'` short-circuits, 5-minute in-process memo keyed on `siteUrl|urlStyle|outOfStockVisibility`. **Only complete combinations are published**: a variation missing a value for one of the product's options never resolves on the page, so its URL would advertise an address that quietly renders the bare listing - hence options are read in their own query (LEFT of the values) so an option with no values still counts towards "every option answered". A product whose two options slugify to one parameter name is dropped whole rather than guessed at. Hard cap **45,000** (protocol limit is 50,000 for the whole file; going over gets the file rejected entire, taking the ordinary product pages with it) and both the cap and the drops are `console.warn`ed, never silent. Live figures read off Deskwell read-only: 20,366 variants -> **19,700 publishable combinations across 344 products**, so ~20.7k URLs in the file with room to spare. **The canonical had to move with it or the whole thing is theatre**: the product page declared the bare listing canonical for every configured address, so a sitemap of 19,700 URLs the page itself disowns would be worse than none. New single-winner extension point **`shop.product-canonical-query`** (`modules/shop/lib/product-canonical.ts`, pattern-copy of `product-social-image.ts`), asked from `generateMetadata` **only when the request carries a query string**, with `canonicalUrl()` in the product page appending the answer. `shop-variations`' provider (`lib/canonical-query-provider.ts`) declines on a partial selection (a half-chosen listing IS the listing, and there is no end to the half-chosen addresses a crawler can invent), runs the same `withStrandedFilled` -> `withAutoSelected` -> `resolveVariant` derivation the storefront does, and then spells its answer **from the variation's own `optionValueIds`**, not from what was typed - so alias values and a hand-reordered query string fold onto the one address. Both sides go through the shared `buildVariationQuery` in `url-selection.ts`, which is the point: two spellings and the sitemap would be recommending a URL the page refuses. **Deliberately unchanged:** a variation's own child-slug deep link (the cart's, the Google Shopping feed's) still canonicalises to the bare parent. Builds in either update order - the provider's import of shop's type is `import type`, so it erases. **3. `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs` was never collecting either hook from a module without a `publicBasePath`.** Both `existsSync` checks sat behind the `if (!base) continue` guard, so `ultimate-seo`'s Sitemap & robots screen has been saving rules, listing them back, and changing nothing on the live `/sitemap.xml` and `/robots.txt` since it shipped - and `shop-variations` could not have contributed either. Moved above the guard. Live Deskwell had one orphaned rule waiting (`/home-new`, "staging preview of the new home page"), which now actually applies. **4. `/favicon.ico`.** `/sitemap.xml` showed the Cactus icon because the root layout's `<link rel="icon">` only reaches responses with a document head; everything else falls back to asking the origin for `/favicon.ico`, where `public/favicon.ico` sat. `public/cactus-favicon.ico` holds the bundled Cactus default (`BRANDING_DEFAULTS.favIcoFallback`) so the route can redirect to it without meeting itself; new `app/api/branding/favicon/route.ts` (force-dynamic, `resolveBranding()`, 307 to the admin-set favicon or the bundled default, `max-age=3600` + SWR), and a **`beforeFiles`** rewrite in `next.config.ts` - `beforeFiles` runs ahead of the static file handler, so there is no public-versus-route precedence to argue about. `/api/branding/` added to `proxy.ts` `ALWAYS_PASS` so the icon answers during setup and while the site is closed, exactly as the static file did. **Shared-tree note:** the `git mv` of `public/favicon.ico` was staged and another session's `git add`/release (v0.5.1149) swept it in, after which 45c80fa put `public/favicon.ico` back "until the branding rewrite lands". Both files are in HEAD right now. That is harmless - the `beforeFiles` rewrite intercepts `/favicon.ico` ahead of the static handler either way - but `public/favicon.ico` is dead weight once this lands and should go with it. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on everything touched, `npm test` **2305 passed / 0 failed**. No schema change anywhere, so the backup gate is untripped. Wiki: `Ultimate-SEO.md`, `Shop-variations.md`, `Appearance-and-design.md`, `Architecture-overview.md`, `Authoring-a-module.md`. **No commit, no push, no release - working tree only.**)
Previous entry: (**The product checks page turned from a static table into a working list - `product-checks-for-shop` working tree, core untouched, version NOT bumped, NOT released.** Chris: "so we can filter by checks done/not done, as well as sort by oldest check and sort by how many checks have been completed, and sort by notes or no notes. page just needs a mega update ... way too basic." The old `app/cactus-admin/product-checks-for-shop/page.tsx` was 109 lines of server component: `listProductChecks()` pulled **every** visible product with its record, sorted the lot in JS by `stalenessSortKey`, and printed five columns. No filter, no choice of sort, no paging - and 442 products on Deskwell, of which 395 have never been checked at all, so the outstanding column read "Everything" 395 times. Now a server shell (permission gate, category options, `parseListQuery(searchParams)`) around a client screen that fetches a page at a time. **Filtering and sorting moved into SQL** (`lib/db/list.ts`, new): one inner select per product LEFT JOINing `pck_product_checks` plus a LATERAL first-image lookup, deriving `current_count` / `checked_count` / `oldest_checked` (`LEAST` skips nulls) / `has_notes` / `neglect_at`, wrapped in an outer select that applies the whole-record state filter and the ORDER BY. `neglect_at` reproduces `stalenessSortKey` exactly - `CASE WHEN checked_count < 12 THEN TIMESTAMPTZ 'epoch' ELSE LEAST(...) END` - so the list and the card strip still agree about what "most neglected" means. Every raw fragment is built out of the `CHECK_ASPECTS` constant (`Prisma.raw` on column names this repo wrote); every value is a parameter. **Filters**: search (name/slug/SKU, `%`/`_` escaped), status, category **including its descendants** (a recursive CTE resolves the ids first, so the tree is one query and the list query stays a plain `= ANY`), record state (any / all done / outstanding / never / gone out of date / partly), one aspect at a time in one of four states (done, not done, never, out of date), notes or no notes, and a **stale window** of 3/6/12 months that is a property of the VIEW - nothing saved changes. **Ten sorts**, including the three asked for: oldest check either way, checks-done either way, notes either way, plus last-saved either way and name either way; column headings sort too and reverse on a second click. **Counts**: `queryChecksStats()` runs the same base with the state/aspect/notes filters dropped, so the six tiles and the twelve per-aspect chips keep showing what else is there while a filter is on - each one is a button that applies its own filter. **New routes** under `/api/m/product-checks-for-shop/admin/`: `list` (GET, the page + `stats`), `bulk` (POST, stamp or clear a set of aspects across up to 250 ids - inserts any missing rows off `shp_products` first so "mark the lot checked" works on a catalogue nobody has touched, then one UPDATE, both in a transaction), `export` (GET, the current filters as CSV with a BOM and formula-injection guarded cells, capped at 2000 rows). **In the rows**: twelve squares per product (green current / amber out of date / dashed never), each one a button that PATCHes that single aspect to today through the existing `admin/product/[id]` route and patches the row in place; the caret opens the existing `ChecksPanel` inline, which gained one optional prop, `onSaved`, so the list refreshes behind it - the panel is otherwise untouched and the storefront strip and editor section pass nothing. The query mirrors into the address bar with `history.replaceState` (no navigation, no `useSearchParams`, so no Suspense boundary needed), and `parseListQuery` defaults rather than rejects, so a stale bookmark still shows a list. `listProductChecks()` and `PckProductListRow` deleted from `lib/db/checks.ts` - the rewritten page was their only caller. New `lib/list-query.ts` + `lib/list-query.test.ts` (16 cases: defaults, round-trip, nonsense falls back), `lib/aspects.ts` gains `countCurrent`/`countChecked`/`outstandingAspects` with tests. No schema change, so the backup gate is untripped. Verified against the live Deskwell database read-only: all ten sorts, all six states, all four aspect states, notes both ways, search, category rollup (Office Accessories 67 including descendants) and the stats totals (442 = 3 all-done + 439 outstanding, 395 never checked, 1 note). `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` clean for the module; **the page itself has not been opened in a browser** - local dev points at the live database, so it wants Chris's eyes on a deploy.)
Previous entry: (**The checkout total shows from the off, and the pinned order summary stops swallowing the page - `shop` working tree only, version NOT bumped, core untouched, NOT released.** Two defects off the live checkout. **1. The pinned summary trapped the wheel.** `CheckoutItemsClient`'s injected `SCI_CSS` had `overscroll-behavior:contain` on `.sci-scrolls .sci-body` - on the two-column checkout the pointer sits over that column, so running the order list to its end froze the page under the mouse with no way on. Now `overscroll-behavior-y:auto`: the wheel scrolls the list, then chains to the page and carries the summary away with it. CSS only, no props, no layout change. **2. `CheckoutReviewClient` hid the totals behind the form.** It returned an early 'Your order total appears once these are filled in above:' block whenever `missingCheckoutFields()` was non-empty and never called the session route, so a shopper could not see what the order came to without typing a full address. The block now fetches totals from the moment `getCart()` is non-empty and renders the figures always; the outstanding-field list (still `focusCheckoutField` link-buttons) moved down beside the **Place order** button, which is disabled when `missing.length > 0 || blockedReason() !== null` (`describedBy` joins `shop-place-order-blocked` + new `shop-place-order-missing`). `placeOrder()` re-checks `missingCheckoutFields` itself as the stale-render guard. New `awaitingDelivery` state (no postcode or no `shippingRateId`) prints 'Delivery is added to this once your postcode and delivery choice are in above.' under the `<dl>`. Traps handled: the route's `customerEmail` is `z.string().email()`, so a half-typed address would 400 the total away mid-keystroke - it is sent only once `/\S+@\S+\.\S+/` passes, else null; every keystroke republishes checkout state, so the fetch is keyed on a JSON `lastQueryRef` (skip when unchanged) and debounced 350 ms (0 ms on the first load), with a `requestRef` ticket so a slow earlier answer cannot land on a later one, and the key cleared on an error response so a refused total can be asked again. `incomplete` state removed. No schema change, no config key, no API change, no backup gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on both files, `vitest run modules/shop/components/public` 55 pass / 0 fail. Wiki: `Shop.md` checkout section.)
Previous entry: (**Promoted variation photos are now tiles IN the product editor's Images grid, dragged about with the product's own - `shop` **0.1.259** + `shop-variations` **0.1.153**, core untouched, all working tree, NOT released.** Chris: drop the two tick boxes, show the "Image up front" variations in the Images box, let them be reordered, marked as variation images, removed from up-front without losing the picture, and given a description. **What went:** `svr_product_gallery` and both its flags (`base_images_last` from 014, `card_image_from_variation` from 015), `lib/db/product-gallery.ts`, `GalleryOrderPanel.tsx` and the `baseImagesLast`/`cardImageFromVariation` switches. Two piles and a coin toss could never say "the oak one, then our two studio shots, then the walnut", which is what a gallery actually is. **What replaced it:** one ordinal space. **`svr_variants.gallery_position`** (INTEGER NULL, `migrations/016_variant_gallery_position.sql`, mirrored into 001) is the variation's index in the FINISHED gallery, the parent's own photographs counted in; NULL = "after the parent's own", which is the starting state and exactly the old default. 016 backfills it from the old flags (either flag on -> the promoted rows take slots 0..n in matrix order, which is what those products already looked like), then `DROP TABLE IF EXISTS svr_product_gallery` - a table of two dead booleans reads as settings that still do something. Live count before the change: **1** product with `base_images_last`, **0** with `card_image_from_variation`. **Shop side (generic, empty without a contributor):** new **`components/admin/product-editor/gallery-extras.tsx`** - `GalleryExtrasProvider` wraps the whole Images panel (grid AND the `shop.product-editor-media-sections` contributions, since the latter are what register), a module calls **`useRegisterGalleryExtras(items, handlers)`** from a client component inside the tab, and `MediaPanel` draws the tiles among its own. Registration is keyed off `JSON.stringify(items)` so a caller need not memoise, and handlers live in a ref (they change every keystroke; depending on them would loop the grid). `GalleryExtraItem` = `{id, url, altText, badge, caption?, removeLabel?, position}`; handlers = `{reorder, setAltText, remove}` - shop reports the gesture and never decides what it means. `MediaPanel` was rewritten around **`mergeGalleryRows(media, extras)`** (exported, insert-at-index, forgiving: a tile asking for slot 7 of a four-picture gallery lands at the end) and a single **`commit(rows)`** that every mutation - drag, arrows, ×, Add images - goes through, splitting the merged list back into `state.media` plus each extra's new index. That single funnel is what stops the two orders drifting when an image is added or deleted next to a contributed one; **Add images** appends to the end of the WHOLE gallery, not the end of the product's own. New CSS `.spe-media-tag` (top-right badge, `--color-info-bg`/`--color-info`/`--color-info-border`) and `.spe-media-note` (the caption line) - **Cover** stays top-left so a variation dragged to the front carries both. `lib/detail-images.ts` gained a per-image `position?: number|null` and kept `placement` optional, translating `'before'` into positions `0..n`, so a module built against the old contract still places its pictures. **Variations side:** new **`lib/gallery-order.ts`** - `mergeGalleryItems(own, promoted)` (the one merge every surface shares, 9 tests in `gallery-order.test.ts` pinning the round-trip and the shuffle-up) and `galleryLeadsWithPromoted(positions)`, which answers "does the tile lead with a variation?" as `position === 0` and so needs **no image rows at all** - that is how `card-media-provider.ts` lost `getCardImageFromVariationSet` and its per-grid query. `GET/PUT admin/products/[id]/gallery` rewritten: GET returns `{images:[{variantId,label,url,altText,position}]}`, PUT takes the whole arrangement plus `demoted[]` (every id checked against `getVariants(id)` first, so another product's matrix cannot reach through) and returns the reloaded set. New `setVariantGalleryPositions` (one VALUES-join UPDATE, same shape as `setVariantPositions`). New client **`GalleryVariationImagesPanel.tsx`** replaces `GalleryOrderPanel`; `ProductGalleryOrderSection` (manifest id unchanged) still gates on "has options, not a variant child". **The description is the picture's own alt text on the variation's hidden child** - not a copy kept here - so it is the same words everywhere that photo appears; payload carries it as `VariantSelectorVariant.imageAlts[]` beside `imageUrls[]`. The **×** is `show_image_in_gallery` going off and nothing else: the photo stays on the variation, and its slot is cleared so re-promoting puts it at the end rather than somewhere it was two months ago. `VariantSelectorPayload.baseImagesLast` is gone; `use-variation-selection` now exposes **`galleryImages`** (merged, `{url, alt}`) instead of `featuredImages`, and both galleries (`VariantParts.tsx`, `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx`) consume it - the latter falling back to shop's server-rendered `images` until the payload lands, so the strip is still drawn on first paint. `social-image-provider.ts` and `detail-images-provider.ts` both go through the same merge. **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `npm test` **2260 pass / 0 fail**, and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` re-run and PASSED (3/3, real throwaway VPS databases)** because a new module column trips the gate. No dev server, no build, per standing rules - and note local dev could not have shown this anyway: `.env` points at live Deskwell, where 016 has not run and must not be applied by hand. Wiki: `Shop-variations.md` ("Letting the promoted ones lead" -> "Arranging them among your own pictures"), `Shop.md` Images bullet, `Authoring-a-module.md` (new "Putting your own pictures in the host's grid"). `shop-variations`' `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` -> **0.1.259**. **Released:** `shop` **v0.1.259**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.153** (both prereleases), wiki pushed, and core **v0.5.1150** pins the pair in `modules.json`. Update order is enforced rather than advised - `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.259` makes the install's update path refuse shop-variations first, naming which to do in which order, so the pair cannot be installed the wrong way round.)
Previous entry: (**A product page can now hide the delivery services the chosen variation cannot have - `advanced-shipping-for-shop` working tree, core untouched, NOT released.** New singleton setting `ash_settings.show_unavailable_services` (BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true) added in **`migrations/008_show_unavailable_services.sql`** and carried in `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs; `AshSettings.showUnavailableServices` in `lib/types.ts`, read/written in `lib/db/settings.ts` (FALLBACK true, `mapRow` reads `r.show_unavailable_services !== false` so a pre-column row still reads as on, INSERT/UPDATE both carry it), accepted as `showUnavailableServices: z.boolean().optional()` by `PATCH /api/m/advanced-shipping-for-shop/admin/settings`. Previous entry: (**Google Shopping's "Unsupported image type [image_link]" was the media Worker, not the feed - `workers/media-worker/index.ts` only, core working tree.** The feed itself is clean: 19,739 items, every `g:image_link` on `media.deskwell.co.uk`, 19,732 `.webp` and 2 `.jpeg`, no off-host urls, no query strings, no non-ascii - and WebP is on Merchant Center's accepted list, so the format was never the problem. Measured against live: 400 distinct feed image urls at 12 in parallel returned **6 x HTTP 502 `text/plain` "Upstream error"** (~1.5%; 1% serial, 5% at 20 parallel), and **all six returned 200 on an immediate serial retry** - transient object-storage failure, not missing files. The Worker turned any non-404 upstream status straight into that 502; Google downloads the four-word plain-text body, finds it is not an image, and disapproves the item. Across ~19,400 unique images that is hundreds of rejections, mostly variation children because they are the bulk of the feed. Two fixes. **(1) Retry:** new `fetchFromProviderWithRetry` wraps `fetchFromProvider` - 3 attempts, backoff 150 ms then 300 ms, retrying only `RETRYABLE_UPSTREAM_STATUS` (408/429/500/502/503/504) or a thrown fetch; 404 and every other 4xx return first time (an answer, not a failure); the failed attempt's body is `cancel()`ed before sleeping. **(2) HEAD:** the Worker answered `HEAD` with `405 Method not allowed` in `text/plain` - the same shape of "not an image" reply, and the trap already written up in the blog-post and product-video skills. HEAD now takes the GET path, carries the upstream `Content-Length` through, cancels the body and returns it bodyless; `Access-Control-Allow-Methods` gains `HEAD`. The 502 fix is the proven one, the HEAD fix is cheap correctness. Nothing in `google-shopping-for-shop` changed. **Not live until the Worker is redeployed** from admin > config > Media - `lib/media/worker-source.generated.ts` is regenerated at build from this source, so a core release alone does not move it.)
