Previous entry: (**New agent skill `.agents/skills/deskwell-product-video/` - a product URL in, a 30 s 1080p promo video out.** Tooling only: no core code, no module, no schema. Six scripts and a reusable set. **`resolve_product.py`** turns a URL or slug into the listing, its options and every variation child with its model urls - the 3D hangs off the CHILD products through `svr_variants`, never the parent, and option values join through `svr_variant_values.variant_id` (there is no `child_product_id` on that table). A parent with no `p3d_models` rows is normal and is NOT a product without 3D; reading it that way on the Oslo back-to-back listing cost a whole wrong render. **`fetch_models.py`** pulls the files from `b2:Deskwell-Office-Furniture/media/<path>` with rclone and three retries - `media.deskwell.co.uk` answers `405 Not authorised` to a plain request with or without a Referer, so https is never the way in. **`inspect_models.py`** dumps each file's objects, materials, heights and what part they look like, which is what the paint map is written from. **`plan.py`** builds the shot plan: hero = biggest value of every count/size option but the FIRST value of a finish, then one beat per remaining option value, finishes first (a 26 mm band does not read from six metres), then counts, then sizes end-on; camera keys are derived from where the beats actually land, so the close-up lasts exactly as long as the finish beats do. **`scene.py`** is the set and is meant to stay put so every product video matches: 19 x 17 m room, 2.95 m ceiling, oak boards, sage accent wall with a doorway onto a corridor that runs PAST the opening, plain walls elsewhere, skirting, daylight panel + ceiling fill + warm bounce, all lamps `visible_camera = False`. Room depth is not decoration - a 6.8 m orbit in a 12 m deep room puts the camera through the wall on the short axis. **`render.py`** renders one continuous move (full 360 eased across the whole lap, then the keyed beats) and each segment runs `2 * overlap` frames PAST its own end, because `xfade` starts the incoming clip at the transition rather than at its own timestamp - get that wrong and every boundary slides half a second out of step. **`assemble.sh`** stitches with 16-frame dissolves and hands off to `deskwell-video-logo-outro`. Cost, measured: Cycles 1920x1080, 16 samples + OpenImageDenoise, fast GI, ~11-12 s/frame on the M3, so ~1,075 frames for 30 s at 30 fps = about three and a half hours; 64 samples doubles it for no visible gain; two Blender processes on the one GPU are SLOWER than one (~30 s/frame between them). The skill therefore makes preview stills a required step before the long render. `references/traps.md` carries the rest, each of which produced a wrong render at least once: FBX landing on its side when the importer's empty is deleted before unparenting, `materials.clear()` resetting every polygon's `material_index` so the legs get painted with the banding, a plane rotated about Y swapping width for height into a 12 m tall wall, and an area lamp whose corner pokes through a zero-thickness wall painting a hard wedge of light on it. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` not applicable (no TypeScript touched); pipeline proved end to end on the Oslo back-to-back listing - resolve 18 variations/9 models, fetch, inspect, plan, and preview frames rendered for four beats. Nothing committed.)
Previous entry: (**The minimum never reached the checkout at all - second fix, `shop` **v0.1.255**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.151**; working tree, core untouched.** Chris: "i added 4 to my cart, then reduced the quantity to 1 (below the minimum order requirement) and it allowed me to checkout." Two separate holes, both now shut, and the first one explains BOTH of his reports. **Hole 1 - the figure was never visible to the server.** A cart line is the hidden CHILD product, and `resolveCartLines` read `product.minOrderQuantity` off that child. Proved against live Deskwell: the ISO chair parent (`52d993e1-a490-4dad-870a-85e6d68f96aa`) carries `min_order_quantity = 4` and **all 97 of its variant children carry NULL** - so the child resolved to "no minimum" and NOTHING was ever enforced. The parent fallback only ever ran in shop-variations' STOREFRONT payload, which is why the product page insisted on four (a client-side stepper floor) while the basket and the checkout happily took one. So the fix is not just pooling: the resolver now hands shop the FIGURE as well as the pool. `CartLineResolution.minOrderGroup` (string) became `minOrder?: CartLineMinOrder | null` = `{ key, quantity? }`; `variant-title-cache.ts` banks `parentMinByProduct` in the batched pass it already ran, and `getVariantMinOrder` returns `{ key: parentId, quantity: resolveMinOrderQuantity(child, parent) }` with the same prefetch/direct-lookup fallback as `buildVariantTitle`. `resolveCartLines` takes `Math.max(product's own row, the resolver's figure)` so neither source can talk the other down, and the line's min is now computed AFTER `resolveLineMeta` rather than before it. **Hole 2 - `resolveLineMeta` dropped the field on the floor.** It does not pass a resolution through; it rebuilds one field by field, and a new field left out of that literal is silently lost - which is precisely how the first version would have shipped enforcing nothing even with the parent's figure to hand. It now merges: first resolver to name a pool keeps the key (a line is one way of buying one listing), strictest `quantity` wins. **Checkout now says why.** Both 409 sites (`/checkout/session`, `/checkout/payment-intent`) return the shared `availabilityReason` when the blocked lines agree on one, instead of "Some items in your basket are no longer available" - useless wording for a minimum-order shortfall, and the payment step already renders `data.error` in red. Several distinct reasons still fall back to the general wording. Tests: `min-order-pooling.test.ts` grew from 8 to **14** - three over `resolveLineMeta` (carried through, raised-not-lowered, absent) and three over `resolveMinOrderQuantity` (blank child inherits, own figure overrides, 1/0/null all mean no minimum), which are the exact cases the live basket found. No schema change, no backup gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 355 pass / 0 fail. Nothing written to Deskwell. **Version note:** other sessions released shop 0.1.252, 0.1.253 and 0.1.254 while this was in hand and their bump overwrote mine in the manifest, so this lands as **0.1.255**; `shop-variations` `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` follows.)
Previous entry: (**Media filing put right across Deskwell, and the media page's stat bar made to arrive at all - core (`lib/media/references.ts`, `lib/media/upload.ts`, new `lib/media/references.test.ts`), `shop` (working tree, version left as another session set it), `search` **0.1.20**, `gazette` **0.1.22**, `filters-for-shop` **0.1.22**, `quote-for-shop` **0.1.15**, `product-downloads-for-shop` **0.1.7**, `space-planner-for-shop` **0.1.26**. No schema change, no backup gate.** Chris spotted `shop/office-chairs/reception-visitor-chairs` sitting beside `shop/office-seating/visitor-reception-chairs` in the library. Cause: a product's storage path is stamped from its master category's NAME when each file is written and only ever re-derived on a **product** save (`reorganiseProductMedia`), so every category rename since the 2026-07-30 restructure stranded its files under the old spelling. Measured on live: 31,424 shop files, ~27,900 of them under a path matching no current category. **(1) The sweep** (scripts + backups + rollback in `media_reorg_2026_08_19/`, deliberately NOT the site's own code path, because several surfaces had no rewriter yet): 29,957 objects server-side copied in B2 to their current `shop/<category trail>/<product>` path (1,117 directory pairs, 6.88 GB, 8 rclone workers; rclone's post-copy "set modification time" 404s on B2 are noise and are ignored, every destination is then verified by name AND byte count), then one transaction repointing 29,074 `Media` rows plus `shp_product_media.url` 27,311, `p3d_models.url` 18,978 + `media_key` 11,939, `pdl_files.url`/`media_key` 656 each, `srch_documents.image_url` 389, and 200 blob rows (`shp_products.description_puck`, `p3d_fabric_configs.config`, `gz_posts.builder_data`, InfoPage/Layout `builderData`/`publishedData`/**`history`**, `qfs_quotes.lines`, `spl_*`, `gsp_preview_job.*`). **Trap that bit: 5,471 `p3d_models.url` values carry a `?v=N` cache-buster**, so exact-equality rewrites missed them - a `requery` pass matches on `split_part(url,'?',1)` and carries the suffix across (4,349 + 960 rows). A second pass caught 303 models/downloads whose product folder held no images and so was never a source. **911 objects the site used with no `Media` row at all** (the storage check's "in use, but with no entry here") were adopted as rows first - `model/gltf-binary`, `optimised = true`, matching the 951 rows the 3D pipeline already writes - because a folder move relocates ROWS, so unadopted files would have been left behind. Afterwards: every referenced url resolves (69,766 of 69,831; the other 65 were already dead before this work - InfoPage/Layout `history`, `gsp_preview_job` scratch), **0 product images, variation swatches, models, downloads or attribute swatches left on an old path**, 1,110 emptied `Folder` rows pruned. **Cleared afterwards, once Chris had Pushed the variations sheet** (its Image column held the old urls, so a Pull before that Push would have reverted them - see `reference_product_media_url_drift`): 30,302 orphans hidden (superseded copies + the 42 that pre-dated the sweep), then 1,611 unreferenced library files under `media/shop/` (251 MB) deleted with their blobs, then 3 category card pictures re-filed (a category picture only moves when that category is saved, so `task.webp`/`ergonomic.webp`/`24-hour.webp` had stayed on `office-seating` paths) and 3 `srch_documents` rows for deleted products removed. All deletes are rclone hides with `hard_delete=false`, so every version is recoverable; row backups + `restore_deleted_media.sql` in the work dir. **`media/dynamic` (4,776 files, 840 MB) was deliberately left**: nothing references it because the import and 3D tooling reads it by SKU. End state 35,563 objects = 35,563 `Media` rows, 1,197 folders, zero either way. One stale branch survives on purpose - `shop/office-seating/task-operator-chairs/eclipse-plus-ii-.../` holds one picture five live customer quotes still snapshot. **(2) The stat bar.** `computeLibraryStats` classified 36k rows with three `haystack.includes()` calls each over a ~10 MB haystack; a MISS scans the whole string three times, and Deskwell's thousands of unreferenced `media/dynamic` files made that ~35 s of pure string search, past the function ceiling, which is why the tiles never arrived. `MediaUsageIndex` now also carries **`referenced: Set<string>`** built once by the new exported `extractReferenceTokens` (urls, `media/...` keys, and `[a-z0-9]{20,40}` id-shaped tokens; query/fragment stripped, decoded form kept as well), and the new exported `isMediaInContent` does set lookups - benchmarked 300 misses: 2,083 ms → 3 ms. The old substring scan is KEPT as a fallback for any url/key carrying a character extraction cannot capture (`isPlainReference`), because "unused" is the verdict that arms a bulk-delete button. `getMediaReferencesBulk` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) uses the same helper. 13 new unit tests; `lib/media` suite 156 pass. **(3) Prevention.** Five modules that hold media urls had **no `core.media-reference-rewriters` provider at all** and now do - `product-downloads-for-shop` (`pdl_files.url`+`media_key`), `search` (`srch_documents.image_url`), `filters-for-shop` (`flt_filters.swatch`), `gazette` (`gz_posts.builder_data`), `quote-for-shop` (`qfs_quotes.lines`); shop's now also rewrites **`shp_products.description_puck`** (its designed description's feature videos) and space-planner's `spl_render_jobs.params`. New `modules/shop/lib/media/refile.ts` (`findMediaDrift`, `refileProducts`) + `GET|POST /api/m/shop/admin/products/media-drift` (POST capped at 10 products per request); the category PUT reads the row **before** the write and returns `mediaDrift: {products, files}` when a rename or re-parent stranded anything, and `CategoriesScreen` shows a warning strip with **Tidy up filing** that walks the list ten at a time with a running count. Deliberately NOT automatic: one rename can mean tens of thousands of blob copies. Previous entry: (**A minimum order belongs to the LISTING, not to a basket line - `shop` **v0.1.255**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.151**; working tree, core untouched, pins NOT moved.** Chris, testing the ISO stacking chair on live: "it's demanding we can only add 4 of the same variation! the customer should be able to add 4 different variations, but if they only add 3 for example, then block checkout until they've added the minimum of 4." The first cut enforced the minimum per RESOLVED LINE in `resolveCartLines`, which is wrong for exactly the product the feature was asked for: four chairs in four colours are four chairs. **The check is now a second pass over the whole resolved basket** (`applyMinimumOrderQuantities` in `lib/checkout.ts`, pure and exported for the test). Lines bucket under a key a cart-line resolver hands back, and stand alone otherwise - so an ordinary product is unchanged, its pool being itself, and two personalised lines of one product now correctly add up. **New seam: `CartLineResolution.minOrderGroup?: string | null`** - shop-variations' `line-resolver.ts` returns the PARENT listing's id for a variant child, read from `variant-title-cache.ts`, which now banks `parentByProduct` in the same batched pass it already did for titles (new `getVariantParentId`, same prefetch/fallback shape as `buildVariantTitle`, so no extra query). Shop never reads the key, only groups by it. **A pool's requirement is the LARGEST minimum among its lines**, so one combination sold only in tens raises the bar for the listing rather than being rounded down to the parent's four. A short pool fails EVERY line in it (the shopper has to touch one of them to fix it) with `minOrderShortfallReason` naming both the rule and the shortfall - "Sold in 4s - add 1 more from this product, in any mix of options" - and the checkout's existing all-lines-available gate does the blocking, at both `/checkout/session` and `/checkout/payment-intent`. A line already failing for another reason keeps the reason it had. **Floors changed to match:** `ResolvedCartLine` gains `minOrderPooled`, echoed by `/cart/validate`, and the three baskets use `pooled ? 1 : min` as the stepper floor - a pooled line MUST go down to 1 or the mixed basket is unreachable. Both variations buy rows now hold `qty` as `number | null` (null = untouched, so the box shows the current combination's minimum and keeps up as the shopper changes their mind) with `shownQty = max(1, qty ?? min)`, and `use-variation-selection`'s `add()` no longer clamps. Wording split on `pooled` throughout; the product-page note reads "order at least 4 in total, in any mix of options" on a product with options. Admin hints on both the Stock tab section and the grid's Min qty column say the count is across the product. **No schema change** - the column and its resolution rule are untouched, so no backup round-trip gate. New `modules/shop/lib/min-order-pooling.test.ts` pins the rule with 8 cases (mixed colours pass, short pool fails both lines, one listing never bleeds into another, strictest member wins, an out-of-stock line keeps its own reason). Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 349 pass / 0 fail across both modules. **Working tree note:** another session shipped shop 0.1.249/0.1.250/0.1.251 (product-url client bundles, Collection Browser, collection curation) while this was in hand - hence the jump past 0.1.252-0.1.254 - and core has moved to v0.5.1139; nothing of theirs was staged or touched. No dev server, no build, nothing written to Deskwell. Wiki: `Shop.md` and `Shop-variations.md` both rewritten on this point.)
Previous entry: (**The Collections admin screen rebuilt from a list of names into a real curation screen - `shop` **0.1.251**, core **v0.5.1136** (module pin only), no schema change, no backup gate.** Chris: "needs a complete redesign to add more collection management tools as well as links to open each collection in a new tab. page is way too basic." The old `CollectionsScreen.tsx` was 60 lines: a name, Rename, Delete. Everything a collection actually carries - description, SEO, order, and above all its membership - was either unreachable or reachable only one product at a time from the product editor's Organisation panel. **New surface.** Each row now shows a stack of its first four member products' pictures, the name, the live count (or an amber **Empty** badge - an empty collection renders an empty page), an **SEO** badge when it carries its own search wording, and its public address under the name. Row actions: up/down + a drag handle (collection order, hidden while a search filters the list, since reordering a filtered list is a lie), **View &#8599;** which opens `/shop/collections/<slug>` in a new tab, **Copy link** (clipboard, falls back to an alert holding the url when the browser refuses), **Products**, **Edit**, **Duplicate**, **Delete**. Header prints `N collections · M product places filled · K still empty`. Opening a row gives two tabs. **Details** - name, an editable **Web address** with the `/shop/collections/` prefix printed beside it, description, and a search-listing block (meta title/description with 60/160 counters that go amber rather than truncate, plus a live preview of roughly what Google prints, falling back exactly as the page does: title then name, meta description then blurb). One Save covers the lot. **Products** (new `components/admin/CollectionProductsPanel.tsx`) - search-to-add against the existing admin products list route with thumbnails, a status badge on anything DRAFT/ARCHIVED (which will not appear on the collection page), an **Already in** state, and an **Add all N matches** shortcut; the current list drag-reorders or moves by arrows, sorts A-Z, removes, and links each product into its editor in a new tab. Every change writes immediately - a curated list half-saved is worse than either state. **Routes** (`app/api/admin/collections/`): `reorder` POST `{orderedIds}`; `[id]/products` GET/POST/PUT (list / append / replace-in-order, each returning the fresh list so the panel never re-fetches); `[id]/duplicate` POST. `[id]` PUT gained an explicit `slug` which beats `regenerateSlug`, both routed through `slugify` + `ensureUniqueCollectionSlug` so no amount of punctuation in the box makes a broken or colliding address; an emptied box falls back to the name rather than saving an unreachable collection. The list GET now returns `{collections, productCounts, previewImages}`. **Data layer** (`lib/db/catalogue.ts`): `getCollectionProductCounts`, `getCollectionPreviewImages` (CTE ranks members per collection AFTER dropping the image-less ones, or a collection whose first four happen to have no picture would come back empty-handed despite being full), `listCollectionProducts`, `addProductsToCollection` (appends from `MAX(position)+1`; `setCollectionProducts` replaces the whole membership and is right for a reorder, wrong for an add - hence both), `duplicateCollection`. **Route ordering matters here**: `reorder` must sort before `[id]`, which `sortRoutesBySpecificity` in the router generator already guarantees - verified in the regenerated `lib/modules/router.ts`. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `npm test` 2146 pass / 19 skipped / 0 fail. Every new raw SQL statement was run against the live Deskwell database first - the four SELECTs executed, the two INSERTs through `EXPLAIN` only, so nothing was written. No dev server, no build. **Version trap, and it bit:** the Collection Browser session committed and RELEASED shop v0.1.250 out of the same working tree while this was being built, so what started as 0.1.250 had to be cut as **0.1.251** - re-read the manifest and `gh release list` immediately before writing any version, never at the start of the work. Committed, pushed and released on request: shop **v0.1.251**, core **v0.5.1136** pinning it. A CORE release does not reach Deskwell - the owner clicks update, and must update the Shop module separately for any of this to appear. Wiki: `Shop.md`.)

Previous entry: (**The client-graph guard now names the module VERSION behind each step - core v0.5.1134, `scripts/check-client-graph.mjs` only.** Three failed Deskwell deploys printed identical file paths while the real answer was "the install is still on shop v0.1.248". Each step under `modules/` now carries `  [<module> <version>]`, read from `modules.json` (the list `checkout-modules` actually used) with `cactus.module.json` as the fallback for a directory not listed there. The CLI then prints one summary line - `module versions in those trails: shop v0.1.248, product-addons-for-shop v0.1.26` - followed by the sentence that matters: a core update does NOT move an install's module pins, update them from the admin Modules page. Summary regex matches the two-space label form `  [x vN]` specifically, because a bare bracket match also swallowed the `[id]` out of `app/cactus-admin/layouts/[id]/page.tsx`. Verified both ways by reinstating the deleted dynamic import in the local shop checkout.)
Previous entry: (**The guard fired on the install and was right - Deskwell pins its OWN module versions, and a core update does not change them.** Core v0.5.1132 reached Deskwell, `checkout-modules` cloned `shop` **v0.1.248** and `reviews-for-shop` **v0.1.7** from the INSTALL's `modules.json`, so the leaking `product-url.ts` was still there and `scripts/check-client-graph.mjs` aborted the build in 200ms naming 12 client files - all twelve funnelling through the same `product-url -> config -> prisma` edge, including shop's own `ProductEditor.tsx`, `seo.tsx` and the whole Puck editor chain (`lib/puck/config.tsx` -> `module-components.ts` -> `ShopProductAddons.tsx` -> `AddonsBox.tsx`). Those extra ten were never a separate defect: shop v0.1.249 clears every one. **The lesson: a core release does not carry module pins to an install - the owner updates each module from the admin Modules page, one at a time, each triggering its own build.** So a fix split across two modules must not be ORDER-DEPENDENT. reviews-for-shop **v0.1.9** therefore drops the import of shop's new `lib/product-url-server.ts` (which exists only from v0.1.249) for its own `lib/product-url-style.ts` reading `getShopConfigCached` directly - builds against v0.1.248 and v0.1.249+ alike, so Shop and Reviews can be updated in either order with no failed deploy in between. Core **v0.5.1133** repins reviews to v0.1.9. Deskwell's Vercel build machine stayed on fixed `standard` (4 cores/8GB) - this failure was the guard, not the machine, and the build never reached Turbopack.)
Previous entry: (**Deskwell's update to v0.5.1131 died at build: 27 Turbopack errors, all one import edge - `shop` **v0.1.249**, `reviews-for-shop` **v0.1.8**, core gains a backstop test.** `modules/shop/lib/product-url.ts` carried `getProductUrlStyle`, whose `await import('./config')` is an edge the bundler follows exactly like a static one. `product-addons-for-shop` v0.1.25 started importing `productHref` from that file into two CLIENT components (`AddonsShowcase.tsx`, `AddonsBox.tsx`), and Deskwell pinned it for the first time on this update - so the browser graph ran client -> `product-url` -> `config` -> `payments/registry` -> `lib/modules/extension-points` -> every module's server code, putting `sharp`, `nodemailer`, `cloudinary`, `draco3d` and `next/headers` in the browser bundle ("Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'/'net'/'tls'/'dns'/'child_process'", "next/headers ... in the Pages Router"). Every one of the 27 traces bottomed out at the same edge. Fix: new **`modules/shop/lib/product-url-server.ts`** holds `getProductUrlStyle` alone; `product-url.ts` is now pure string work plus `import type { ShpConfig }` and nothing else. Callers repointed - shop's `app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx` and `lib/menu-entity-provider.ts`; reviews' `lib/emails.ts` and `lib/db/reviews.ts`. product-addons needed no change and stays on v0.1.26. New **`lib/modules/client-graph.test.ts`** (plain `npm test`, 50ms, no key, no skip) walks every `'use client'` file's import graph - static, re-export and dynamic `import()`, `import type` erased - and fails on any route to `@/lib/db/prisma`, `@/lib/modules/extension-points`, `sharp`, `nodemailer`, `cloudinary`, `next/headers` or `server-only`, printing the shortest trail. Verified by reinstating the deleted dynamic import: the test reproduces the exact two leaks Vercel reported. `tsc` and `eslint` both stayed green throughout the outage, which is the whole reason the test exists. Also: the Deskwell Vercel project's build machine moved off elastic (it had self-upgraded to Enhanced, 8 cores/16GB, reason `sustained-high-cpu`) to **fixed `standard`** at Chris's request.)
Previous entry: (**Two products can be add-ons of each other - `product-addons-for-shop` **v0.1.26**, module working tree, core untouched.** Chris, on the Neo round coffee table: it offers the single chair and the twin sofa, but adding the table back onto either of those was refused with "That would make these products add-ons of each other in a loop - one of them has to stand alone." The loop the guard was protecting against is a RENDERING loop - `buildAddon` in `lib/payload.ts` walks each add-on's own links to build the chain beneath it - so the fix is a link that ends its branch rather than a graph that forbids the pair. New **`config.hideChildAddons`** (jsonb, no DDL, so the backup round-trip gate does NOT apply): `buildAddon` skips `getLinksForProduct` entirely for such a link and returns `children: []`. `wouldCreateCycle(productId, addonProductId, hideChildAddons = false)` follows only links WITHOUT the flag (`COALESCE("config" ->> 'hideChildAddons', '') <> 'true'` - a string compare, not a `::boolean` cast, so a hand-mangled config cannot throw the query) and returns false outright for a new link that carries it. The POST route takes it as an optional body flag and answers a refused link with **`loop: true`** alongside softer copy, which `ProductAddonsEditor` turns into a one-click **"Add <name> without its own add-ons"** button under the error; PATCH re-asks the question before letting a link's chain run on again, so re-ticking cannot re-open what the tick closed. Per-link checkbox **"Offer its own add-ons here"** sits beside the space-planner toggle (saves with the Save add-on rules button, like the rest of `config`). Absent flag = the old behaviour exactly, so nothing already linked changes, and the read-time visited set + `MAX_CHAIN_DEPTH` still stand behind all of it. No Deskwell data written - the links themselves are the owner's to add. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 29/29 pad tests. Wiki: `Product-Add-ons.md`.)
Previous entry: (**Minimum order quantity, on products and on variations - `shop` **v0.1.248**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.150**, `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.68**, core **v0.5.1129** (registry pins).** Chris: "our shop and variations modules need to support adding a minimum order quantity to products and variations please." **No new table and no shop-variations schema change at all**: one nullable `shp_products.min_order_quantity` INTEGER (`modules/shop/migrations/021_min_order_quantity.sql`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, mirrored into 001) covers both, because a variation IS a hidden `shp_products` row - the same bargain `018_sale_sku.sql` struck. Nullable rather than `DEFAULT 1` so an existing catalogue keeps its rows untouched and the editor can tell "blank" from "one". **Resolution rule, in one place** - new dependency-free `modules/shop/lib/min-order.ts`: `minOrderQuantity(stored)` reads null/0/negatives/fractions all as 1, `resolveMinOrderQuantity(child, parent)` gives a variation its own figure or the parent's when it has none (blank child = "as the product says", NOT "no minimum"), plus the two wordings every surface prints. Dependency-free on purpose: the storefront islands import it, so it must not drag the server-only data layer into the browser bundle. **Enforcement is at the one place that is trusted**, `resolveCartLines` in `lib/checkout.ts`: a line under its minimum fails with `Sold in Ns - please order at least N`, exactly as an out-of-stock line does. Deliberately NOT silently rounded up - the steppers already stop at the floor, so a short line came from a stale basket or a hand-edited request, and neither is a reason to add money to someone's order without saying so. `ResolvedCartLine` gained a required `minOrderQuantity: number` and `/public/cart/validate` echoes it, so the basket's own pickers know the floor. **Surfaces:** product editor Stock tab gains a **How many at a time → Smallest order** section (blank/1 stored as null, validated as a whole number ≥ 1); `AddToCartButton` opens ON the minimum, floors the − button and the typed value at it, and prints `minOrderSentence` under the row in a new `.spd-minqty`; `QuantityStepper` (used by all three baskets) takes a `min` prop - 0 still removes a line, anything else is held at or above the floor. The `shop.product-detail-parts` PurchaseArea contract gained optional `minQuantity` and `classNames.minQuantityNote`, both optional so a provider built against the old contract still compiles. **Variations side:** the storefront payload carries a PRE-RESOLVED `minOrderQuantity` per variant plus `baseMinOrderQuantity` for the parent, so the buy row reads one number rather than doing the fallback in the browser; `use-variation-selection` exposes `minQuantity` and `add()` clamps to it whatever the caller was showing. Both buy rows (`DetailSlotPartsClient`'s and `VariantParts`' standalone one) derive `shownQty = Math.max(min, qty)` rather than pushing the prop into state - state set from a prop needs an effect, and an effect there would show a stale, too-small figure for a frame after every option press. Variations grid gains a **Min qty** column beside Stock whose placeholder is the PARENT's figure, so an empty cell reads as "as the product says"; `EditorPayload.product` gained `minOrderQuantity` to carry it. **Round-trips everywhere the other columns do**: shop CSV `min_order_quantity` (appended, optional, numeric); variations CSV **Min Qty** (after Stock); and the Google-Sheet mirror's `variationRowChanged` normalises 1/0/blank to null before comparing, or every row carrying a 1 would read as an edit on every Pull, forever. `requiresModules` minVersions bumped (shop-variations → shop 0.1.248; google-sheet-products-for-shop → shop 0.1.248, shop-variations 0.1.150). **Schema change - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` run for real: PASS (3/3, ~83s, throwaway `cactus_rt_*` databases on the OVH VPS).** Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean project-wide, `eslint .` clean, `vitest run` 562 pass / 0 fail across the three modules plus the backup schema-coverage backstop. No dev server, no build, nothing written to Deskwell. Wiki: `Shop.md` (Stock & delivery bullet), `Shop-variations.md` (grid + spreadsheet), `Google-Sheet-Products.md` (what the sheet covers). Committed, pushed and released on request: all three module repos, plus core **v0.5.1129** pinning them in `modules.json`. A CORE release only - it does not reach Deskwell until the owner clicks update on the live site.)

Previous entry: (**The Gazette Feed block collapses on a phone - `gazette` **v0.1.21**, module working tree, core untouched.** Chris, having had to build Deskwell's new homepage "From the Gazette" row out of the *listing* block instead: `GazetteFeedBlock.rsc.tsx` computed `gridCols = layout === 'List' ? 1 : layout === 'Compact' ? 4 : 3` and wrote it straight into an inline `gridTemplateColumns: repeat(N, 1fr)` with no media query - measured on deskwell.co.uk at 375px, **three columns of 98.3px**. The sibling `GazetteEntryList` never had the problem because it renders `PostCardGrid` (`.gz-post-grid` + `data-cols`) and the rules in `GazetteStyles` collapse it - 1fr under 640px, two columns to 960px, then the pinned count. So the feed now renders the SAME grid rather than a second set of breakpoints: new exported `feedColumns(layout)` in the editor half maps List/Compact/Grid -> `'1'`/`'4'`/`'3'`, and the RSC half hands that to `PostCardGrid` with `toPostCards` doing the media/author/href lookups it used to do by hand (comment counts come along for the ride - one extra query, one code path). **Props are untouched**, so saved pages keep working: layout/count/tagSlug/showExcerpt/showAuthor/showDate/showImage/readMoreLabel all still mean what they meant. Two behaviours deliberately preserved rather than inherited: an empty feed returns `null` (a homepage row has no business printing PostCardGrid's "Nothing published yet" - that message is for the listing pages), and comment/view counts stay off (`showComments`/`showViews` forced false) because the feed never showed them. `readMoreLabel` is the one thing a listing card has no concept of, so it became an optional prop on `PostCardGrid`/`PostCard` (left off = exactly the markup the listing always rendered) with `.gz-post-card-more` added to `GazetteStyles`. The editor skeleton in `GazetteFeedBlock.tsx` carries the same class and `data-cols`, importing `GazetteStyles` - safe in the editor's client bundle, it is a bare `<style>` with no imports of its own and nothing near prisma. Visual side-effects of sharing the card: gap 1rem -> 1.5rem, card padding 0.875rem -> 1rem, heading 1.0625rem -> 1.125rem, and a hovered card now underlines its own title like every other Gazette card. No schema change, no backup gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide; no dev server, no build, nothing written to Deskwell. Wiki: `Gazette.md` says what the feed does as the screen narrows. Core's `modules.json` still pins gazette **v0.1.20** - the pin bump and its core release were not asked for.)
Previous entry: (**Google Shopping tells Google how long each product takes - `advanced-shipping-for-shop` **v0.1.42** + `google-shopping-for-shop` **v0.1.3**; working tree, core untouched, registry pins NOT moved.** Chris: "google shopping module, can we provide Transit time label and provide the earliest delivery date from our advanced shipping module for each product?" - then chose the day-counts scope (option a), leaving `transit_time_label`/`shipping_label` out. **There is no delivery-date attribute in the Merchant Center spec**: Google renders "get it by Thursday" itself from `min/max_handling_time` + `min/max_transit_time` in business days, and `transit_time_label` is only a grouping key onto a transit table configured in the MC account, so it does nothing on its own. The one real date attribute is `availability_date`, required on `preorder`/`backorder` - which the feed was emitting **without**, a standing MC disapproval risk now fixed. **Seam: a new generic extension point `shop.product-delivery-timing`**, so neither module gains a dependency on the other - ash publishes `advancedShippingDeliveryTiming(productIds, now?)` from `lib/delivery-timing-provider.ts` (manifest id `advanced-shipping`), gsf reads it out of core's generated `moduleExtensionPointComponents` registry in `lib/delivery-timing.ts` and gets `{}` on an install without ash, so no path to a module that is not there and no static import to break the build. Core needed NO change: point names are free-form (`lib/modules/manifest.ts` `point: z.string().min(1)`), the generator emits whatever the installed manifests say. **Counts, not dates, deliberately** - a date is only true for the instant it was computed, so a cached feed would publish yesterday's promise; the counts move only when settings do. `handlingDays = max(0, settings.dispatchLeadDays)`, `transitDays = max(0, tier.modifiers.transitDays)`, and a service's `minLeadDays` floor is folded into **handling** (`if (floor > handling + transit) handling = floor - transit`) so the pair never under-promises while transit stays an honest courier time. Service chosen = `settings.defaultTierKey` where the product is offered it, else `delivery.tiers[0]` (same order the cart uses). `availabilityDate` computed only for pre-order/backorder rows, as local midnight on `computeEstimate().dispatchDate` via `cutoffInstant(date, '00:00', tz).toISOString()` - a bare date would be read in the consumer's zone. **Chunking measured, not guessed:** cost is almost all round-trip latency, not rows - live Deskwell reads of 500 / 2000 / 8000 ids took 2028 / 2079 / 3528ms, so the first-draft `CHUNK = 2000` was paying the fixed cost eleven times over; **`CHUNK = 10_000`** (a variant child drags its parent in, so worst case ~20k of Postgres's 65535 parameter ceiling) does the whole live catalogue - 20,806 ids, 20,462 timed - in **13.4s from a laptop over the internet** to the OVH VPS, and the public feed route is NOT the `/api/m/` dispatcher so it does not carry the un-overridable `maxDuration = 60`. Live spread: 2610 `standard-delivery` h=1 t=5, 1128 `made-to-order-flat-pack` h=1 t=10, 136 `made-to-order-pre-assembled` h=1 t=15, 75 `standard-pre-built-delivery` h=1 t=5, 51 flat-pack h=1 t=16; **100% of variant children resolve**, while bare listing parents mostly do not (delivery is keyed off the Range attribute, which is a per-variation option on Deskwell) - harmless, because the feed publishes children, and the 344 unresolved ids are standalone products no rule covers, which correctly emit nothing. `lib/feed-xml.ts` renders each pair only when BOTH ends are whole and non-negative (`handlingAndTransit`; Google rejects a half-stated range, and a `0` must still be printed rather than dropped), and `g:availability_date` only when `availability` is `preorder`/`backorder`; `collectFeedItems` attaches them in ONE pass over the finished items, never per item. 5 new feed-xml tests (125 pass). **Not measured end-to-end against live:** `collectFeedItems` throws `column "brand_from_supplier" does not exist` against the Deskwell database - the install has not taken gsf 0.1.2's `002` migration yet, pre-existing and nothing to do with this change.)
Previous entry: (**The Dimensions section can be switched off per layout - `shop` **v0.1.246**, core **v0.5.1126** (registry pin only).** Chris: "some pages have a Dimensions tab in the top tabs bar. can we please add an option in the 'Product: Tabs' puck block to hide Dimensions tab?". The gate went into `buildDetailSections(ctx, opts)` in `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx` - new `opts.hideDims`, which skips the `dims` push - because that function is the ONE source of truth all three detail blocks build from, so a hidden section can never be left with a link pointing at it. **The ask alone would only have half-worked**: `ShopDetailTabs` is nav-only (the panel bodies live in `ShopDetailSections`, and on Deskwell the single `Default` shopProductDetail layout carries BOTH blocks), so hiding the tab would have left the Dimensions facts table sitting on the page unreachable. So the same `dimsTab` select ('yes'/'no') is on all three: `shopDetailTabsPuckComponent` (**Show Dimensions tab**), `shopDetailSectionsPuckComponent` (**Show Dimensions section**), `shopDetailSectionNavPuckComponent` (**Show Dimensions link**). Default `'yes'` in every `defaultProps`, and the test is `props.dimsTab === 'no'`, so an already-saved layout with no such prop reads as shown - nothing changes on any live page until an author sets it. Editor previews filter their hardcoded `['Description', 'Specification', 'Dimensions']` label array on the same prop, keeping editor/RSC markup parity. Products with no measurements recorded never got the section anyway (`dimRows.length > 0` still guards first). No schema change, no migration, no backup gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide. Wiki: `Shop.md` gained a paragraph in the Product Detail tabs run.)
Previous entry: (**The old product address is GONE (404, no redirect), and the SEO module stops crying wolf over social images and H1s - `shop`, `ultimate-seo`, `search`, `reviews-for-shop`, `product-addons-for-shop`, `product-attributes-for-shop`; working tree, uncommitted.** Chris, emphatically: "i dont want any redirect". So on the ROOT product-URL style `/shop/products/<slug>` simply `notFound()`s - one product, one address, nothing forwarded. Gated on `shopClaimsRootSlug(slug)`, the very predicate core asks before serving the bare slug, so it closes ONLY where the root address genuinely answers; on the default SHOP style the claim is false and nothing changes. **THE TRAP**: `app/root/[slug]/page.tsx` re-exported the product page's DEFAULT, so putting the 404 there would have closed the new address too - page.tsx now exports a named `ShopProductPageView` (address-agnostic, no gate) which the root route takes as its default, while the default export is the prefixed route's gate. Mirrors gazette's split, though gazette REDIRECTS its old post address (308) - the two modules deliberately differ now, do not "harmonise" them. **CONSEQUENCE that makes the rest non-optional**: with no redirect, every hardcoded `/shop/products/<slug>` in any module is a live 404 for shoppers, so all of them were fixed - `search/lib/adapters/shop.ts` (reads `shp_settings.config->>'productUrlStyle'` by raw SQL, NOT an import: search has no `requiresModules` shop by design; **the url is baked into each stored document, so changing the style needs a REINDEX**), `product-attributes-for-shop/.../ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx` (now `ctx.productHref`, which CardPartContext already carried), `reviews-for-shop` (its own hardcoded `productHref` helper deleted in favour of shop's; `RvwReview` gains a server-resolved `productHref` so the admin screen needs no style of its own; `toReview(row, urlStyle)` takes the style, resolved once per query), `product-addons-for-shop` (`PadBoxPayload.productUrlStyle` + `ShowcasePayload.productUrlStyle`, both optional so older serialised payloads read as SHOP; `LearnMoreModal` now takes a `productHref` prop - **its `/details` iframe is a DIFFERENT route that does NOT move, leave it alone**). Those three modules' `requiresModules` shop floors bumped to 0.1.245. **`lib/product-url.ts` had a static `getShopConfigCached` import**, so importing `productHref` from ANY client file would have put prisma in the browser bundle - moved to a dynamic import inside `getProductUrlStyle`; that is what lets AddonsBox/AddonsShowcase/ProductEditor use it. `ultimate-seo`: (a) it warned 'No social sharing image set' on EVERY product of EVERY shop ever, reading only `shp_products.og_image_id` - a column the product editor has NO UI for (API accepts it, nothing writes it) - while the page publishes its first photograph as og:image since shop 0.1.244; now counts non-VIDEO_URL `shp_product_media` rows too. (b) 'No top-level (H1) heading' on every product/post/entry: the analyser only saw the description HTML, while the H1 is the NAME the template prints. New `AnalysisInput.titleIsH1` + `EntityDetail.titleIsH1`, threaded through `run-analysis.ts` AND `bulk-analysis.ts`, set for shop-product/gazette-post/directory-entry (all three verified to render `<h1>{title}</h1>`), false for core pages whose headings genuinely all come from the builder; counted ALONGSIDE content H1s so a description opening with its own H1 is correctly flagged as the second. (c) its Pages screen listed products at `/shop/products/<slug>` and posts at `/gazette/<slug>` regardless of either module's style - now reads both modules' settings rows by raw SQL, never a cross-module import.)
Previous entry: (**Google Shopping takes its brand from the supplier - `google-shopping-for-shop` **v0.1.2**, core **v0.5.1125** (registry pin only).** Chris: "google shopping module, Brand should be pulled from the supplier/retailer name (Dynamic on most of our products)." The feed knew two brand sources - the per-product `gsf_product_data.brand` and the shop-wide `gsf_settings.default_brand` - and neither was filled in on Deskwell, where 20,390 of 20,808 `shp_products` rows already say `supplier = 'Dynamic'` (418 blank). Now three, first answer wins: per-product brand -> the parent product's `supplier` (trimmed; blank falls straight through) -> default brand. Gated by new `gsf_settings.brand_from_supplier` BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT **true** (`migrations/002_brand_from_supplier.sql`, `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`; 001 carries it too so fresh installs match), surfaced as **Use the supplier as the brand** in the settings sub-tab - default on because a shop that files by supplier usually means the maker, off for shops whose suppliers are middlemen. `identifiersOf` in `lib/feed-data.ts` now takes `{supplier, defaultBrand, useSupplier}` instead of a bare default, fed by a per-run `brandFallbacks(...candidates)` closure that picks the first candidate with anything in it (trimmed, so a blank column does not swallow the one behind it). **A variation reads its CHILD row's supplier first, the parent's only behind it** - the important detail, and not the obvious guess: on Deskwell the importer fills `supplier` in on the rows it creates, which are the children, so of 440 feed-eligible listings only **24** parents say `Dynamic` while all 346 variation parents have children that do (346/346 with exactly one distinct supplier each, 0 mixed, 0 all-blank). Parent-first would have branded 24 listings out of 440. Both raw queries gained the column (`ParentRow` via `p."supplier"`, `ChildRow` in the per-child read); standalone items read `ShpProduct.supplier`, which `listProducts` already maps - all 96 standalone listings are blank there and fall through to the default brand. Column is additive to a module table, so `prisma/core-reconcile/` is not involved and the backup gate does not trip (no core schema touched). Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, module tests 10/10. Nothing applied to Deskwell - `brand_from_supplier` does not exist there yet and lands when the install picks the module up on its next update. Wiki: `Google-Shopping.md` gained a "Where the brand comes from" section.)

Previous entry: (**Product pages can live at the site root, and every catalogue product got a focus keyword plus an internal link - `shop` **v0.1.245**, `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.21**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.149**, `google-shopping-for-shop` **v0.1.1**; core untouched, Deskwell live-data programme in `seo_keywords_2026_08_19/`.** Two asks in one turn. (1) **SEO across the catalogue.** Every parent product (442, incl. 2 drafts) and every shop category (48) now carries a `seo_page_meta.focus_keyword` - the ultimate-seo module's own store, entity types `shop-product` and `shop-category`. Note `shop-category` rows are FORWARD-PROVISIONING: ultimate-seo 0.1.4 inventories core pages, gazette posts, shop products and directory entries only (`lib/inventory.ts`), so category rows sit unread until the module grows category support. Keywords are category-phrase + the product's distinguishing values, lowercase, 2-7 words, unique site-wide (a locked `keywords.tsv` registry in the programme folder rejects clashes; 0 duplicates across 490 entities), and always a contiguous substring of the SCORED title (`meta_title` if set, else `name` - that is what `analyze.ts` scores). Each keyword also appears >=1x in the description body, in `meta_description`, and - the trap that cost a rebuild - in text a VISITOR sees: the storefront renders `description_puck`, not `description`, so a weave into the html-only intro paragraph is invisible on the live page. `tool.py` therefore mirrors h4-prose edits into their twin `TextBlock`s (`sync_prose_to_puck`) and refuses any pack whose keyword is not in `puck_visible_text(...)`. **Internal links**: one varied sentence per product appended to `description` as `<p class="seo-related">` (the marker that makes re-apply idempotent) AND mirrored into `description_puck` as a `RichTextBlock` inserted BEFORE any trailing `FeatureVideo` blocks; hrefs restricted to `/shop/categories/<slug>` for categories the product is actually in. Category descriptions stayed plain text (the category page renders them through `ShopCategoryDescriptionBody` with no HTML path) so their keywords went into meta title/description/description copy instead; category pages already link heavily via breadcrumbs and cards. 26 batch agents, all writes through the one validated tool (per-row backups + rollback SQL), zero skips, zero flags. Final sweep **442/442 products + 48/48 categories PASS**. `oslo-air-piste-height-adjustable-office-desk`, the owner's model page, was excluded at first per the 2026-08-14 no-editing instruction and failed the sweep with no meta_title and no meta_description at all (the title fell back to the name and the description to a 337-char short_description Google simply truncated); the owner asked for it later the same day and it was fixed on its own - explicit meta_title, a 134-char meta_description carrying real figures, two keyword weaves into h4 prose sections and a category link. `tool.py` still REFUSES that id by default; the guard lifts only for a run passed `--allow-model-page`, never silently, and `verify` no longer exempts it from the link checks. (2) **Root-level product URLs, no redirects.** New `shp_settings.config.productUrlStyle` (`'SHOP'` default / `'ROOT'`, zod on the existing jsonb column - NO schema change, so the backup gate does not trip). On ROOT a product page answers at `/<slug>` via core's `publicRootSlug` seam (added by another session in core `29a4d70`, unreleased at the time): `modules/shop/lib/root-slug.ts` exports `shopClaimsRootSlug` (one settings read returns false while on SHOP; matches ANY product row, hidden variant children included, so deep links keep working), and `app/root/[slug]/page.tsx` simply re-exports the existing product page - it is address-agnostic. Resolution order stays **InfoPage -> module index -> claim**, so core content always wins. Chris asked for NO redirects, so the old `/shop/products/<slug>` address keeps rendering; what moves the indexing is that BOTH routes emit `alternates.canonical` in the chosen style (`lib/product-url.ts` `productHref`/`productUrl`, the single seam every link goes through - gazette's `post-url.ts` pattern) and the sitemap lists products at the canonical form. Style-aware now: sitemap, menu entity provider (resolved live per render, so no menu needs re-saving), card grids (a new `CardPartContext.productHref` resolved once in `buildCardContext` from `pricing.productUrlStyle`, which is why the config object is already spread in by every caller), back-in-stock emails, member order lines, and the Google Shopping feed. `filters-for-shop` reads `ctx.productHref` with a `?? '/shop/products/'` fallback so an older shop build still links correctly (its `ShopFilterGrid` is the grid on all 48 Deskwell category layouts). `shop-variations`' `productSlugFromPath` gained the bare-single-segment case, else every variation control on a root-style page would render its no-product preview. Setting lives at **Settings -> Shop -> General -> SEO**. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean (generator logs `root-slug claims: gazette, shop`), `eslint .` clean project-wide, 309/309 tests across the touched modules. No schema change anywhere, so no backup round-trip needed; no build, no dev server, nothing written to Deskwell's config - the style stays SHOP there until someone flips it.)

Previous entry: (**Google Shopping arrives - new module `google-shopping-for-shop` **v0.1.0**, `shop` **v0.1.243** (canonicals + honest JSON-LD offers).** Chris: "does our shop currently support google shopping? including showing each variation as its own listing?" - it didn't; now it does. New module (prefix `gsf_`, publicBasePath `google-shopping`, requires shop >= 0.1.243 + shop-variations >= 0.1.146) serves a Merchant Center RSS 2.0 feed at `/google-shopping/feed.xml?key=<token>`: **one item per enabled variation** (`g:id` = child product id - NEVER a SKU, codes stay withheld; `g:item_group_id` = parent id; `link` = the child slug deep link the cart already builds), plus standalone PHYSICAL products; parents whose only svr rows are options/add-ons fall through to the standalone side rather than vanishing. Enumeration rides `getProductIdsWithVariations()` -> `getEditorPayloadsBatch()` (the CSV export's seam - the selector payload is WRONG here, it nulls sku/stock behind `canSeeProductCodes()`); one extra raw read fetches the child columns the payload lacks (slug/status/availability inputs/tax class/weight unit). Prices forced **gross** whatever `priceDisplayTax` says (`displayAmount` with mode INCLUSIVE + default-zone rates - Google UK wants VAT-inclusive); availability mirrors the availability-provider rule (preorder outranks stock, BACKORDER = backorder); out-of-stock items drop only when the shop hides them (sitemap parity). Variant axes map option names -> `g:color`/`g:size`/`g:material`/`g:pattern` by heuristic (first match wins, several size-likes join " x ", losers live in the title). `gsf_settings` singleton (enabled off by default, crypto-minted feed token with NULL-guarded first-read race, default brand/condition) + `gsf_product_data` (brand/gtin/mpn/google category/condition/excluded per parent, FK CASCADE) - **backup round-trip gate run: real PASS** (3 tests, OVH throwaway DBs). Admin: settings sub-tab hosted in `shop.settings-sub-tabs` (feed URL + copy, mint-new-address, defaults) and a `shop.product-editor-sections` tab (per-product Google fields; hidden on variant children - they inherit, each variation's barcode is its GTIN via `normaliseGtin` 8/12-14 digit gate). `lib/robots.ts` disallows `/google-shopping`. 10 unit tests on the pure XML builder (`lib/feed-xml.test.ts`). Shop 0.1.243: `generateMetadata` now emits `alternates.canonical` - self on a product's own slug, **parent** on a variation deep link (the page that renders IS the parent's) - and the product JSON-LD switches to `AggregateOffer` (lowPrice = the cards' own From figure, display-tax adjusted) whenever `resolveCardFromPrices` prices the product, so a variation's feed price can never contradict a single parent-price Offer. Variant URLs stay OUT of the sitemap on purpose: they canonical to the parent, and Merchant reads the feed. NOTE staging: shop's `page.tsx` carried another session's uncommitted social-image work - my hunks were staged via a HEAD-based blob + `git update-index --cacheinfo`, their tree untouched. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 2140/2140 tests, round-trip PASS. Wiki: new `Google-Shopping.md`.)
Previous entry: (**Product pages carry social preview images, and a configured product travels by URL - core (shop page metadata) + `shop-variations` + `product-addons-for-shop`, working tree, not yet released.** Chris: social images should be the product's main image, a shopper's option/add-on selection should survive link-sharing, and the shared preview should show the chosen combination's photo. Three pieces. (1) **og:image/twitter on product pages**: `modules/shop/app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx` generateMetadata now emits `openGraph` (title, description, og:url carrying the query string, image) + `twitter: summary_large_image`; base image = first non-video `getProductMedia` row, relative URLs absolutised via `getSiteUrlOrNull()`. (2) **New extension point `shop.product-social-image`** (`modules/shop/lib/product-social-image.ts`, single-winner, server-safe, precedent: product-page-resolver) - asks companion modules which picture the page will OPEN on for this request; `shop-variations` answers by replaying the gallery's opening-image derivation (`lib/social-image-provider.ts`: preselect ids from deep link OR URL params -> withStrandedFilled/withAutoSelected -> resolveVariant -> variant imageUrls[0], else baseImagesLast/promoted/base logic). Request plumbing: new `modules/shop/lib/product-page-params.ts` cache() slot - page + generateMetadata park raw searchParams, companion modules read their own params back; shop learns nothing about param meaning. (3) **Selection <-> URL**: `shop-variations` writes each raw pick as `?<option-name-slug>=<value-slug>` (`lib/url-selection.ts` codec; `syncSelectionToUrl` in `use-variation-selection.ts` fires from setOptionValue/resetOptionValues via history.replaceState, guarded by a new `Entry.seeded` flag + path check so blocks on other pages never touch the address bar; on a variant deep-link URL the first change rewrites the path to the parent slug so params never fight the child slug's preselect). Server restore: `getVariationBootstrap` falls back from deep-link preselect to `selectionValueIdsFromParams` - so shared links open with options chosen IN THE FIRST HTML. `product-addons-for-shop` writes one `pad=<linkId>[.<valueId>...][.q<qty>]` param per enabled add-on (`lib/url-state.ts`; AddonsBox restore-once-then-write effects, restore sets chosen+overridden=true which self-degrades to 'following' when equal to the followed value; qty only travels when hand-set). Add-ons restore client-side only - they never change the main gallery, so the social image never needs them. Manifest: shop-variations gains extensionPoints entry `variations-social-image`. Deep-link child URLs also gained self-canonical to the parent (someone else's concurrent edit - alternates.canonical was added to the same file mid-task; kept). Gotcha for future param features: option params are matched by slugified option name against value slugs, unknown/foreign params are ignored fail-safe both sides; `pad` would collide with a product option literally named 'Pad' - both codecs ignore each other's garbage by construction.)
Previous entry: (**The SEO Pages screen can analyse the whole site in one go, and its detail panel scrolls - `ultimate-seo` **v0.1.4**, pinned by core **v0.5.1119**.** Chris: "we need a function to analyse all pages in bulk" - clicking Analyse on 445 Deskwell products one at a time was never going to happen. New **Analyse all *N*** button beside the Pages filters; it walks whatever the filters currently show (label becomes **Analyse these *N*** the moment a search or type filter is on), in chunks of 25 per request, with a real progress bar and a **Stop** button wired to an `AbortController`. Client-driven chunking rather than one long request because every module route shares the core dispatcher's 60s ceiling - see the module-route note - so a bigger catalogue is a longer wait, never a torn-off run. Server side, `lib/bulk-analysis.ts` `analyzeBatch()` pays the fixed costs once per batch instead of once per page: `run-analysis.ts` was refactored so its four entity loaders take **id arrays** (`loadEntities(entityType, ids)`, `= ANY($1::text[])`, one query per content type; the single-page path is now the batch of one), the inventory and settings load once, and every score is written back in a **single** multi-row `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` (`bulkUpsertPageMeta` in `lib/db.ts`) - which is why the batch is deduped by `(entityType, entityId)` first, since Postgres refuses to let one INSERT touch the same conflicting row twice. **Focus keywords are never touched by a bulk run**: the upsert's DO UPDATE sets score/checks/analyzed_at only, and each page is re-scored against the keyword it already had. New `lib/duplicates.ts` `DuplicateIndex` replaces the O(n) "is any other page using this title/description" scan with a counted index that discounts the page's own contribution - the sweep goes from quadratic to linear, and `analyzePage` still gets the array corpus it expects (a one-element answer is as truthful as the full site list). 5 unit tests in `lib/duplicates.test.ts`. New route `admin/pages/analyze-bulk` POST (max 100 items, `seo.view`, matching the existing single analyse). Second, unrelated fix in the same screen from Chris: the detail panel is `position: sticky` and could grow taller than the viewport with nowhere to go - it now carries `maxHeight: calc(100vh - 2rem)` + `overflowY: auto` + `overscrollBehavior: contain`. The admin shell is `min-height: 100vh` with the topbar scrolling away, so viewport units are the right measure here. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, new tests pass. No schema change, so the backup round-trip gate does not apply. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Ultimate-SEO.md`.)

Previous entry: (**A Pull that reported the same 13,691 variations and 96 products for ever now reports them once - `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.60**, working tree only (NOT released).** Live Deskwell symptom: the sheet check said 13,691 variations and 96 products to update, the Pull ran clean (`gsp_sync_log`: `updated_count` 13,691, no errors), and the next check said exactly the same. Two independent defects, both of the same shape - `rowChanged` reporting a change `applyImportedRow` then declines to make. **1. The read-only twin poisoned the write path's label cache.** shop-variations' `importVariationsCsv` calls `provider.rowChanged` and then `provider.applyImportedRow` with the SAME preloaded ctx (`lib/csv.ts`, the `providerChanged` block). `cellChanged` resolves a label with `findAttributeValueByLabel` (never creates) and cached the result - `null` included - in `AttrImportCtx.labelCache`, which `applyCellValue` reads first. So for a label the vocabulary had not seen, apply read the cached `null`, compared it with the stored `null`, and returned without writing: the value was never created and the cell never written. Proof on the live data: all 13,691 rows carried a non-empty `Shipping` cell, all 29 distinct labels were absent from that attribute's 36-value vocabulary, and not one of the 13,691 children had a `pat_product_values` row for its parent's Shipping helping. Fix: `missCache: Set<string>` on both ctx types, filled and read ONLY by the read-only halves; positive hits still share `labelCache` (an id found is the id an ensure would return), so the per-row query storm the cache exists to stop stays stopped. The comment claiming the two halves never share a context was simply wrong and is corrected in place. **2. Auto-attach detection reported an attach the write path declines.** `upsertVariationAttribute` / `upsertProductLevelAttribute` insert an un-named helping and reuse an existing one only when it is already of the kind they want; where the un-named slot is held by a helping of the OTHER kind they return null and leave the product alone (the v0.1.58 anti-hijack guard). Neither `rowChanged` knew that - the product-level one even carried a comment calling it "slower but never wrong" - so a heading naming such an attribute counted as a change on every single Pull. That is the 96: e.g. `AC000001` carries `Catalog` and `Range` as un-named use-for-variations helpings and no product-level twin, while the Products tab has both columns filled. Fix: new `listAutoAttachDeclines(productIds, wantVariations)` in `lib/db/membership.ts` (one query: an un-named helping exists for the pair AND no helping of the wanted kind does), preloaded into `declines: Set<"productId|attributeId">` by every `beginImport`/`beginImportMany`, checked in both attach loops next to the existing `blocks`. NO schema change, no core change, no reconcile, no round-trip gate. `google-sheet-products-for-shop` needed only its `pull-diff.test.ts` membership mock extending (no version bump - it is already unreleased at v0.1.66). `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .` clean; full suite 2,102 passed / 19 skipped, 5 new tests across the two provider suites, each verified to FAIL against the old code. Wiki unchanged: `Product-attributes.md` already documents the decline ("the heading is declined and the product left alone") - the behaviour was right, the counting was not.)

On screen: `SettingsScreen` field label "Range attribute" → **"Shipping attribute"** (+ its empty option and help copy), `scope-picker.tsx` `SCOPE_LABELS.RANGE` "A range" → **"A shipping attribute"** (+ placeholder, `aria-label`, `(deleted shipping attribute)`), and the three `TiersScreen` help paragraphs that said "range". **New tab** (4th `shop.tax-shipping-tabs` entry, manifest id `missing-shipping-rules`, order 25, permission `shop.manage`, `components/admin/MissingRulesScreen.tsx`): lists every value of the nominated shipping attribute that NO delivery service prices, and beneath it the values only SOME services price with the services missing from each.
