Previous entry: (**The marker is gone - a PLAIN heading attaches, and removal is remembered instead - `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.59**, `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.66**, working tree only (NOT released).** Owner rejected the star outright ("i dont want to have to add a star!!") after v0.1.58 shipped. A plain heading naming an existing attribute now attaches it, exactly as the pre-v0.1.35 behaviour did - so the re-assert loop the marker was there to break needed a different answer. **The answer: remember the REMOVAL, not the request.** New `pat_variation_attach_blocks(product_id, attribute_id, blocked_at)` (module migration `011_variation_attach_blocks.sql`, folded into 001 for fresh installs per the 003 precedent, added to `teardown`). `setProductAttributes` reads the product's use-for-variations attribute ids BEFORE its writes and compares after: removed -> INSERT a block, added -> DELETE it, both inside the SAME transaction as the save (a block outliving a rolled-back save would refuse an attach for ever). `upsertVariationAttribute` enforces it as a `NOT EXISTS` inside the INSERT rather than a read-then-write, so a save removing the attribute cannot slip between check and insert. So: the sheet proposes, the owner disposes, and an attach nobody wanted is one deletion away from being permanently gone - which is the property the marker was standing in for. **Both v0.1.58 guards stay:** `upsertVariationAttribute` still never flips a product-level helping (that is what put spec fields on ~20 live products in July), and `RESERVED_VARIATION_HEADERS` + the option-pair pattern still refuse `Supplier` / `Option 1`. **A trailing star is now TOLERATED and stripped** (`attachHeaderName`) so a sheet written against v0.1.58 keeps working; gsheets' marker-consumption code in `formula-preserve.ts` is left exactly as shipped, and clears the star on the next Push. gsheets' only change this round is its `pull-diff.test.ts` membership mock (the new export), hence the version bump - the tagged tree should be green. Ctx gains `blocks: Set<"productId|attributeId">`, preloaded by `beginImport`/`beginImportMany` for `rowChanged` ONLY - the write path deliberately leans on the SQL guard instead, because a product created mid-import is absent from any preload and "absent" must not read as "not blocked" on a path that writes. Block key carries the product for the same reason `attached` does: one context covers many parents. **Known and accepted, since it is what was asked for:** the first accidental attach is still possible - any heading matching any attribute name attaches on a non-blank cell, including a label another module contributes to the variations tab. It is now undoable, which it was not in July. **Gate: `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS (3 tests, 47s, no skips)** - new table. Full suite 2097 passed / 19 skipped, typecheck + eslint clean; provider tests rewritten to the new behaviour (38 in the file, 8 of them the block). Wiki: Google-Sheet-Products.md + Product-attributes.md rewritten off the star - edited, NOT pushed.)
Previous entry: (**Sheet auto-attach is back, behind a one-shot marker - `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.58**, `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.65**, working tree only (NOT released).** Restores what v0.1.35 took out in July, without the two faults that made it dangerous. **The ask:** adding a column to a variations tab and Pulling did nothing unless the attribute was already ticked use-for-variations on that product. **The marker.** A heading with a trailing star - `Shipping *` - asks for the attach; a plain heading still attaches nothing. `attachMarkerName()` in `variant-field-provider.ts` strips it. **A star, not a leading `+`:** Sheets parses a cell beginning `+` as a formula and leaves `#NAME?` in the header, so a plus marker could never have been typed. **Fault 1, the re-assert loop, fixed by CONSUMING the marker.** Old behaviour attached, the next Push wrote the heading back, and a column deleted on the Attributes tab came straight back on the next Pull because the sheet still said so. Now the attached column arrives from the database as plain `Shipping`, and gsheets' `formula-preserve.ts` treats a marked old heading as its own plain name in all three places that align columns - `orderColumnsLikeSheet` (registers the bare name as an alias for that position), `ownerColumnStart` (a marked heading whose plain twin is in the pushed grid is NOT owner data to shift right), `pushedColumnsAligned` (not a shift, so formulas and row order survive the write that eats the star). Miss any one of the three and the Push appends a second column instead, leaving the star to be read for ever. **Fault 2, the hijack, fixed in SQL.** The old code called `upsertProductAttribute(..., useForVariations: true)` whose `DO UPDATE` flipped an existing product-level helping into a per-variation column - that is what put spec fields on ~20 live products. New `upsertVariationAttribute(productId, attributeId)` in `lib/db/membership.ts` is the exact twin of the existing `upsertProductLevelAttribute`: INSERT the un-named helping `use_for_variations = true`, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then reuse only a helping that is ALREADY use-for-variations, else null and the product is left alone. **Also:** the old `cols.length === 0` early return meant a product with NO variation attributes could never attach one - lifted. `RESERVED_VARIATION_HEADERS` (+ `Sale SKU`, which the old list missed) and the option-pair pattern still refuse `Supplier *` / `Option 1 *`. The ctx memo is keyed `productId|attributeId`, NOT attribute alone - `beginImportMany` (v0.1.57) now shares one context across parents, so an attribute-only key would hand parent B the helping created for parent A. `columnCache.delete(productId)` after an attach. `rowChanged` mirrors it read-only: an attach with nothing stored is a change, a marker outliving its Push over a column that already holds that value is NOT (or the preview would report phantom work for ever). Value writing/comparing factored into `applyCellValue`/`cellChanged` so both halves cannot drift. **NO schema change** (existing table, existing unique key), no core change, no reconcile, no round-trip gate. **Cross-module note with no way to express it as a dependency:** pat has no hard dep on shop-variations or gsheets, so each owns its own marker helper - but pat 0.1.58 running against gsheets 0.1.64 attaches and never gets the marker consumed, i.e. the old loop. Both must be pinned together on an install. `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .` clean; 473 tests across the three modules pass, 13 new for the marker in `variant-field-provider.test.ts` and 4 in `push-layout.test.ts`. Wiki: Google-Sheet-Products.md (new "Putting an attribute on a product from the sheet"), Product-attributes.md (bulk-editing section) - edited, NOT pushed.)
Previous entry: (**Backdrop-logo columns DROPPED from the live Deskwell database - core v0.5.1105, no code change.** The feature was reverted in v0.5.1104; the owner then asked for the four `SiteConfig` columns off the live database too. **Order was the whole job:** Deskwell was still serving v0.5.1102 at the time, whose Prisma client selects those columns on every `SiteConfig` query, so dropping them first would have thrown `P2022` on every page of a live shop. A `core-reconcile` drop file does NOT dodge this - reconcile DDL runs during the build while the OLD deployment still serves traffic, so it is the same outage, just shorter. Correct sequence, and the one used: release the revert → owner presses update → verify the deployed bundle no longer references the feature → then drop. **Verified before the DDL** by fetching every `_next/static/chunks/*.css` href off the live homepage at the current `dpl_` id and grepping for `cactus-backdrop`/`data-backdrop`: 84,711 bytes, 0 hits (the pre-update bundle had them). Checking the `<html>` tag alone is NOT sufficient - the attributes only render when the feature is switched on, so an off switch looks identical to absent code. DDL run: one `ALTER TABLE "SiteConfig" DROP COLUMN IF EXISTS` for `backdropLogoEnabled`/`backdropLogoScale`/`backdropLogoMode`/`backdropLogoSurface`. Values at drop time were `f|50|dark|page`; a rollback script recreating the columns and restoring those values was written first. Post-drop smoke test: `/`, `/shop`, `/about-us`, `/office-seating`, `/contact`, `/privacy-policy` all 200. No reconcile file ships for this - Deskwell is the only install, it has been done by hand, and a drop file would only endanger anyone still on old code.)
Previous entry: (**A dead update stops blocking the next one, and stops answering with gibberish - core working tree only (NOT released).** During a GitHub incident (their status page: API Requests / Git Operations / Webhooks degraded) three Deskwell core updates in a row died at the 60s function ceiling. A hard-killed function runs no catch, so each one left `DeployLock` stranded and every retry got a permanent-feeling 409 until the blanket 15-minute sweep; the browser meanwhile got Vercel's **HTML** timeout page, and `res.json()` on that threw Safari's `The string did not match the expected pattern.` as the entire explanation. Four changes, all of which had to be true at once for the owner to be stuck. **1. `DeployLock.expiresAt` (TIMESTAMP(3), nullable)** - whoever takes the lock stamps how long its work can credibly run (`acquireDeployLock(lockedBy, holdMs = DEFAULT_LOCK_HOLD_MS = 90s)`); `getActiveDeployLock()` sweeps a row past it. NULL (older build, or an unstamped caller) falls back to `STALE_LOCK_MS`, unchanged at 15 min. 90s fits every current caller because all of them release the lock BEFORE the build they trigger - the hold cannot outlive its `maxDuration = 60` function, whatever `lock.ts`'s old comment claimed. **2. A soft deadline** (`lib/updates/deadline.ts`, `ROUTE_WORK_BUDGET_MS` = 60s - 10s headroom). `syncCoreFromUpstream(..., {deadlineAt})` checks it after the tag tree reads, per file in the blob-fetch pool, and before opening the push - which needs `PUSH_MIN_BUDGET_MS` (15s) to be worth starting - and deliberately NOT inside the createTree→createCommit→updateRef transaction, where finishing is what keeps the repo consistent. `retryTransient` takes `deadlineAt` too and refuses to sleep past it: its default budget is 8 attempts up to a 60s cap, i.e. minutes, which inside a 60s route guaranteed the very kill this exists to avoid. Aborting throws `DeadlineExceededError` ("Nothing was changed - this usually means GitHub is responding slowly"), so the handler rolls its queued module rows back, releases the lock, and answers 503. **3. `lib/github/health.ts`** reads `githubstatus.com/api/v2/summary.json` (60s cache, 2.5s `AbortSignal.timeout`, every failure = "no known problem" - a status page that won't answer must never block an update) and reports any non-operational component among API Requests / Git Operations / Webhooks. The core-update handler calls it ONLY on failure and appends e.g. "GitHub is currently reporting problems with Git Operations (major outage).", downgrading to 503. **4. `lib/updates/read-json-response.ts`** replaces `res.json()` in both admin surfaces: a gateway status (502/503/504) or an HTML body becomes "The update ran out of time before your site heard back. Nothing was changed...". `looksLikeGitHubProblem` gained `timed out` / `ran out of time` / `responding slowly` / `github is currently reporting problems` so all of the above still get the status-page link underneath. 409s now read `lockBusyMessage(lock)` - names the actual wait in seconds rather than "Please wait". `prisma/core-reconcile/023_deploy_lock_expiry.sql`, init migration edited in place. New unit tests: `lib/deploy/lock.test.ts`, `lib/updates/deadline.test.ts`, `lib/updates/read-json-response.test.ts`. `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .`, `npm test` (2081 passed) clean; `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real PASS (schema touched). Wiki: Architecture-overview.md (two new sections), Self-hosting-and-operations.md.)
Previous entry: (**A blocked live chat now says so instead of disappearing - `live-chat` **v0.1.17**, working tree only (NOT released).** Where the site's banner carries the `live-chat` category, `WidgetLoader` used to `return null` until it was granted, so a visitor who had not answered the banner - or had answered and left live chat off - saw no bubble at all. That reads as "this site has no live chat", not "live chat is waiting on you", and left anyone who declined with no route back short of hunting for a cookie settings link. The bubble now always renders; clicking it while blocked toggles a small `role="dialog"` card above it (**Live chat needs a cookie**) instead of starting anything, with a button underneath calling core's `window.cactusConsent.open()`. Two wordings, chosen by new `consentAnswered()` in `lib/consent.ts` - core's `cactus-consent` cookie exists or it does not, since `window.__cactusConsent` flattens "not asked" and "declined" to the same `false`; only the cookie's EXISTENCE is read, the payload stays core's business. New `openConsentSettings()` in the same file, optional-chained throughout, since on an ungated site the global is core's no-op stub. `askedWhileBlockedRef` is set only by that button, so a visitor who grants the category from OUR prompt gets the chat they asked for opened automatically, while one who grants it from the footer link elsewhere just gets the bubble back. The notice is derived (`!allowed && consentNotice`) and also cleared when `allowed` flips true (one `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` disable, justified inline) so a later withdrawal cannot make an old notice reappear unbidden. Nothing chat-related loads in the blocked state - no script, no cookie, no contact, no journey buffering; the only extra DOM is the already-hidden Turnstile host. `requiresCoreVersion` moves **0.5.1026 → 0.5.1098**: on older core `cactusConsent.open()` opens the manage view holding the site defaults, so saving from the prompt would quietly reset the visitor's other categories. Zero diffs outside `modules/live-chat/`. `npm run typecheck`, `eslint .` and `npm test` (2065 passed) clean. Wiki: Live-Chat.md (privacy behaviour), Architecture-overview.md + Authoring-a-module.md (the inert-placeholder pattern, and that the cookie's existence is the "asked yet?" signal).)
Previous entry: (**A pinned checkout summary scrolls its own list - `shop` working tree only (NOT released, module version NOT bumped - 0.1.239 is another change's).** Follow-up to the arrival grouping in 0.1.238: a sticky Your order block taller than the window hangs its foot below the fold with nothing able to reach it, because the page scroll is moving the checkout fields, not the block. Two new props on `ShopCheckoutItems` / `CheckoutItemsOptions`: `scroll` ('auto'|'on'|'off', default 'auto' = scrolls exactly when `sticky === 'on'`) and `scrollHeight` (CSS length, empty = window-fitted). Implemented in the block's injected `SCI_CSS` only - new `.sci-scrolls .sci-body` rule inside the existing `min-width:641px` query, `max-height:var(--sci-max, calc(100vh - var(--sci-top,1rem) - 6rem))` + `overflow-y:auto` + `overscroll-behavior:contain` + a thin `--color-border` scrollbar. `--sci-max` is only set inline when the owner names a height. Desktop-only on purpose: under 641px the page scrolls the summary and the mobile collapse toggle already folds it, so a box scrolling inside a scrolling page never appears. Existing published layouts carry no `scroll` prop, so they take 'auto' - Deskwell's checkout (sticky 'on', offset 7rem) starts scrolling on its next update with no layout edit. NO schema change. Wiki: Shop.md checkout section.)
Previous entry: (**Cookie preferences can be changed from the privacy policy page - core working tree only (NOT released).** Until now a visitor's only route back to their cookie choice was the `CookieSettingsLink` block reopening the banner, and that block is optional - a site without one in its footer offered no way back at all. New `components/consent/ConsentPreferencesPanel.tsx`: the same category switches, rendered inline above the content of whichever page `SiteConfig.privacyPolicyPageId` points at, with **Save preferences** / the configured Accept all / Reject all labels and an `aria-live` line reading either "Saved…", the date the choice was last set, or "not set… yet". It hydrates from the `cactus-consent` cookie in an effect (cookies are browser-only, so first paint shows the configured defaults and server/client markup stay identical) and returns null when every category is `required` - a site with no optional categories would otherwise draw a row of locked switches. New `lib/consent/client.ts` owns the cookie names, the versioned payload, `resolveCurrentDecision` and `saveConsentDecision` (cookie write → `notifyConsentChange` → POST `/api/consent`); `ConsentBanner.tsx` was rewritten onto it rather than keeping a second copy, and the cookie stays the source of truth for the UI so a 429 or a dead network never blocks a decision. **Bug fixed in passing:** `window.cactusConsent.open()` opened the manage view holding `buildDefaultDecision(...)`, not the visitor's stored choice - the footer link was quietly offering to reset the settings of anyone who clicked it to review them. `open()` now calls `resolveCurrentDecision(config)` first. **Placement** is decided by `resolveConsentPanel()` in `lib/puck/renderInfoPage.tsx` (banner enabled AND page id === `privacyPolicyPageId` AND `showPrivacyPagePanel !== false`), reading the already-`cache()`d `getSiteConfig()` so it costs no extra query; on a page with a layout the panel goes INSIDE the content slot, or it would render above the site header. New `showPrivacyPagePanel: boolean` on `ConsentBannerConfig` (default true) + `z.boolean().default(true)` in `ConsentBannerConfigPatch`, deliberately NOT in `bumpConsentVersions`' `copyKeys` - moving a control onto a page must not re-prompt everyone who has already decided - and absent-counts-as-on, so installs configured before this get the panel without anyone finding the switch. Admin checkbox on the GDPR & Legal tab under the retention fields. Colour tokens only, both themes. No schema change, no core-reconcile, no module change. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` clean. Wiki: Configuration-reference (field row + "Privacy page panel"), Architecture-overview (consent gate section).)
Previous entry: (**Payment logos can be switched off, bank transfer gets one, and the checkout steps get some air - `shop` working tree only (NOT released, module version NOT bumped).** **Spacing.** `CheckoutShippingClient`, `CheckoutPaymentClient` and `CheckoutReviewClient` (both its incomplete and its full-summary returns) add `marginTop: '2rem'` to their `<section>` - the checkout steps are separate Puck blocks in one zone, so nothing else was putting a gap between Delivery address / Payment method / Order review. Contact is first and untouched. **Logos on a switch.** New `hiddenPaymentMethodLogos: z.array(z.string()).default([])` on `ShpConfigSchema` (jsonb config, no migration), held as the list of the ones NOT shown so an empty list means "all of them" and a method contributed by a module installed later still shows its mark without being listed anywhere. `getPaymentMethodLogos(hidden)` in `lib/payments/registry.ts` takes the list and drops those entries, and `GET /api/m/shop/public/config` passes `config.hiddenPaymentMethodLogos` in - a mark switched off never reaches the browser at all, rather than being hidden with CSS. **Bank transfer mark.** `lib/payments/logos.ts` gains `bankTransferLogo` (a bank building, `#1F2937` light / `#FFFFFF` dark - no brand to be true to, so it needs both colourways like PayPal's), wired onto `bankTransferProvider` along with a shipped `description` ("Pay straight from your bank account. We send the account details with your order."), which the owner can write over like any other. Cash still has neither. **Admin.** `ShpAdminPaymentMethod` gains `logo: ShpPaymentLogo | null` (type-only import, so nothing server-side travels with it), filled by `/api/admin/settings` from `provider.logo`. The Payments tab's "The line under each method" section is now **"How each method reads at checkout"**: one bordered card per method holding the mark at checkout size (rendered with the same `data-logo-variant` pair core's logo-swap CSS keys off), a `Switch` writing `hiddenPaymentMethodLogos`, and the existing description box underneath. A method with no mark gets no switch. No core change, no reconcile, no schema change. Wiki: Shop.md payment-methods section.)
Previous entry: (**A failed update now says when the fault is GitHub's - core v0.5.1096.** A GitHub incident surfaced in the update dialog as `Update failed: Core update push failed (0.5.1094 → 0.5.1095: 3 writes, up to 0 deletions): Resource not accessible by integration` - accurate, unactionable, and reading like the site's fault. New `lib/updates/github-outage.ts`: `looksLikeGitHubProblem(message)` matches GitHub-side signatures case-insensitively (`resource not accessible by integration`, bad gateway / service unavailable / internal server error, `BadObjectState`, "was submitted too quickly", rate limit, socket hang up / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / ENOTFOUND / fetch failed / network error, `http 5xx`, `status: 5xx`), plus `GITHUB_OUTAGE_HINT` and `GITHUB_STATUS_URL` (`https://www.githubstatus.com/`). The core-update confirm dialog (`app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx`) and the Modules page's danger alert (`app/cactus-admin/modules/page.tsx`) keep printing the raw error and add the hint + a new-tab link to the status page underneath when it matches. `Resource not accessible by integration` is deliberately in the list even though it usually means the GitHub App lacks write access - GitHub returns it while their App auth is degraded too - so the hint's wording covers both and the wiki says to check the App's permissions if the status page is green. No schema change, no reconcile, no module change. Wiki: Self-hosting-and-operations.md in-product update section.)
Previous entry: (**Checkout lists deliveries, not products - `shop` **v0.1.238**, `advanced-shipping-for-shop` **v0.1.36**, working tree only (NOT released).** The checkout's Your order block drew a flat column of lines, each repeating its own `Delivery: Flat-Pack - by Tuesday 25th of August` field, so a five-line basket printed the same sentence five times and the shopper did the grouping in their head. New generic seam, shop's own contract rather than a module's: `LineMetaBatch` on `LineMeta` (**modules/shop/lib/types.ts**) = `{id, sort, heading, uniformHeading?, detail?, fieldLabel?}`. Shop compares ids, sorts on `sort` and prints the wording it was handed - it never composes a heading or parses one. `resolveLineMeta` folds it first-writer-wins beside `group`/`data` (**lib/line-meta.ts**), so it persists onto `shp_order_items.line_meta` like they do. New `batchLines()` in **lib/cart-group.ts** (+ new **lib/cart-group.test.ts**, 8 cases, first tests this file has had): buckets by `id`, buckets ascend by `sort` (ties: heading, then first appearance), attachments follow their main into the MAIN's bucket whatever their own batch says, unbatched lines trail in one unheaded bucket. A bucket is `uniform` when every line whose OWN batch is that bucket shares one `detail` - then it takes `uniformHeading` and the restated field is hidden; mixed, it keeps `heading` and each line prints its `detail` underneath. A line carried in behind its main keeps every field it has, so nothing is ever promised on its behalf. **CheckoutItemsClient.tsx** renders one `<ul>` per bucket under an `<h3>` in `--color-primary`; SAMPLE_LINES carry batches so the Puck canvas shows it. `advanced-shipping-for-shop/lib/line-resolver.ts` emits the batch: `id`/`sort` = the ISO target date ALONE (a flat-packed desk and a built chair landing on one Tuesday are one delivery to the shopper), `heading` = 'Arrives by <date>', `uniformHeading` = the existing `paidDeliveryValue` sentence, `detail` = `tierText`, `fieldLabel` = `DELIVERY_FIELD_LABEL`. An older shop ignores `batch` entirely and lists per-line fields as before. Cart page, confirmation page, emails and quote documents are UNCHANGED - checkout only. NO schema change, no core change, no reconcile. Wiki: Shop.md checkout section, Advanced-Shipping.md shopper-facing list.)
Previous entry: (**Stripe and PayPal marks, and an owner-editable line under every payment method - `shop` **v0.1.236**, `square-payment-for-shop` **v0.1.9**, `gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop` **v0.1.11**, working tree only, NOT released.** Follows the brand-mark seam added in shop 0.1.232. **Marks.** New `modules/shop/lib/payments/logos.ts` holds shop's own two: Stripe one colourway (brand purple `#635BFF` carries on either theme), PayPal two (`#003087` light, `#FFFFFF` dark - its navy vanishes on a dark page), both wired onto `stripeProvider`/`paypalProvider`. Bank transfer and cash get none; they are not brands. **The line.** New optional `description?: string` on `ShpPaymentProvider` - the provider's own default - plus `paymentMethodDescriptions: z.record(z.string(), z.string()).default({})` on `ShpConfigSchema` for the owner's override, keyed by method id so a module method is nameable without shop knowing it exists (jsonb config, no migration). `resolvePaymentMethodDescriptions(overrides)` in `lib/payments/registry.ts` is pure and takes the map rather than reading config: override.trim() || provider default, and a method with neither is absent from the result entirely. `GET /api/m/shop/public/config` returns it as `paymentMethodDescriptions`; `CheckoutPaymentClient` prints it under the name in `--color-text-secondary` at 0.8125rem, and the radio row moved to `alignItems: flex-start` (centring floated the radio and the mark into the gap between the two lines). **Admin.** `ShpAdminPaymentMethod` gains `defaultDescription` (filled by `/api/admin/settings` from `provider.description`), and the Payments tab's methods list grows a "The line under each method" section - one box per method, placeholder = the provider's own wording. An emptied box DELETES its key rather than storing `''`, so clearing a box restores the shipped wording instead of leaving the method silent. Defaults: Stripe/Square "Credit and debit card payments are securely handled by our payment partner X.", PayPal balance-or-card, GoCardless "Instant bank transfers…". **Also**, at the owner's request, the reassurance under the checkout phone box ("Only ever used about this delivery - a slot, or a question on the day.") is gone from `CheckoutShippingClient`; the error line above it is untouched. Both payment modules type-import from shop again, so their `requiresModules` shop `minVersion` moves to `0.1.236` - an object literal with an unknown `description` key is a compile error against an older shop, not a quiet no-op. Verified by rendering all four rows against the real light/dark token values in headless Chrome.)
Previous entry: (**Edit a whole saved address, with the checkout's own address lookup - `shop` working tree only (NOT released, module version NOT bumped).** `/shop/account/addresses` only ever let a customer change the phone number on a saved address (an inline box + Save per row); everything else about it was uneditable, so a moved office meant add-new-then-delete-old. `modules/shop/components/public/AddressesClient.tsx` rewritten around a shared `AddressForm` child used by both **Edit** (one per row, opens in place of the card's body) and **Add address** (a button now, not a permanently-open form) - `editing` is a single `string | null` (`'new'` or a row id) so only one form is ever open, and the edit form is keyed on the row id so switching rows does not carry half-typed values across. The form is the checkout form's fields, in the checkout's order and with the checkout's messages: real `<label>`s (the old page was placeholder-as-label), first/last name, phone, the optional business-name field gated on `businessName.enabled` from `/api/m/shop/public/config` (which also supplies `requirePhone`), line 1, line 2, town, postcode; required-field errors are touched-gated and all fields are marked touched on Save so a straight click at Save says which box is short. Phone keeps the existing rules (`isValidUkPhone` + `formatUkPhone` on blur and on save). Saving an edit still PUTs the **whole** address object - `PUT /api/m/shop/member/addresses/[id]` replaces the stored jsonb, so a partial body would empty the rest of the door; no API or schema change was needed, both routes already accepted the full shape. **Address lookup**: `app/public/shop/account/addresses/page.tsx` now calls `resolveCheckoutAddressLookup()` (from `modules/shop/lib/checkout-address-lookup.ts`) and passes the component down as `addressLookup`, exactly as the checkout page and `ShopCheckoutShipping.rsc.tsx` do - resolved server-side on purpose, since the generated extension registry statically imports Prisma-touching code and must never reach a client bundle. Line 1 is wrapped in the provider via `renderInput` so shop keeps sole ownership of the markup; `onSelect` applies line1/line2/city/county/postcode in one `setForm` update. No new extension point - the existing `shop.checkout-address-lookup` provider is reused as-is, so `address-lookup-for-shop` is unchanged. Card/button styling moved to shared `CSSProperties` consts using colour tokens only. `wiki/Shop.md` (customer accounts) and `wiki/Address-Lookup.md` updated, not yet pushed.)
Previous entry: (**Order updates by text message - core **v0.5.1088**, `shop` **v0.1.233**, `twilio` **v0.1.27**, working tree only (NOT released).** New core text-message half of the email registry, deliberately mirrored rather than merged: `lib/sms/registry.ts` (`SmsTemplateDef` = `{key,label,body,mergeTags,requiredTags?,transactional}`, module-contributed only - core sends no template texts of its own), `lib/sms/render.ts` (override overlay, `{{tag}}` interpolation with **no** escaping, `{{#if}}` reused from the email renderer, `smsSegments()` for the GSM-7/UCS-2 160-vs-70 count), `lib/sms/send.ts` (`isSmsAvailable()`, `normaliseSmsNumber()`, `sendSmsTemplate()` - never throws, answers `{sent,reason}`). Storage is a new core `SmsTemplate` model (key/body/isActive, no subject and no wrapper), init migration edited in place plus idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/020_sms_templates.sql`, which ALSO does `ALTER TYPE "NotificationChannel" ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS 'SMS'`. New manifest seam `smsTemplates` (same shape as `emailTemplates`) collected by `scripts/generate-module-sms-templates.mjs` into gitignored `lib/modules/sms-templates.ts`; `memberExtensions.notificationCategories` entries gained `channels: ('EMAIL'|'SMS')[]` (default `['EMAIL']`) and `required: boolean`. New permission `sms.templates`, separate from `emails.templates` because texts cost per send. Admin API `/api/admin/sms/templates` (+ `[key]` PATCH/DELETE, `preview`, `test-send` - the test send takes a typed number, since an admin account has an email and not a phone); the **editor UI belongs to the twilio module**, as a new **Templates** sub-tab on the Twilio settings tab (`modules/twilio/components/admin/TwilioSmsTemplatesCard.tsx`), on the grounds that a site with no SMS provider has no business being shown one. `/api/members/notifications` now speaks both channels: GET returns `emailOffered/smsOffered/email/sms/required` per category plus `smsAvailable`, PATCH takes `channel` and **refuses to disable the last remaining channel of a `required` category**; `NotificationsSection.tsx` is a checkbox per channel (digest select hidden on required categories). New `lib/members/notification-prefs.ts` holds the defaults in one place - **email defaults on, SMS defaults off**. `lib/members/digest.ts` now filters `channel: 'EMAIL'` (SMS rows are always INSTANT, but the query had no business matching them). Shop side: migration `020_order_notification_channels.sql` adds `notify_email` (default true), `notify_sms` (default false) and `notify_phone` to `shp_orders` (001 edited to match for fresh installs), `lib/sms-templates.ts` declares 9 `shop.*` texts (customer-facing milestones only - admin alerts stay email), and `lib/order-notify.ts` is the single resolver + sender: **a member order reads the account preference, a guest order reads the order's own columns**, SMS falls away if the number is not a UK mobile, and if that would leave nothing the email goes anyway. Four call sites moved from `sendShopEmail` to `notifyOrderCustomer` (order-fulfillment, order-status, shipment-email, the three customer-facing order-request sends); admin alerts untouched. New public `POST /api/m/shop/public/orders/notifications` (same receipt-token/order+email lock and rate limit as the status route) writes the order columns AND, for a member order, the matching `MemberNotificationPreference` rows, so the confirmation page and the account page can never disagree; `GET .../orders/status` now returns a `notifications` block. `OrderConfirmationClient.tsx` gained the **How shall we keep you posted?** card (only when `smsAvailable` and the payment did not fail), with Save disabled while both boxes are unticked - the server refuses it too. Round-trip backup gate run for real: PASS.)
Previous entry: (**A name on the account, a phone number on each address - core **v0.5.1088**, `shop` working tree only (NOT released, and 0.1.232 is what core pins).** New nullable `Member.fullName` (init migration edited in place, plus idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/019_member_contact_details.sql` for existing installs) with `GET/PATCH /api/members/contact` behind it and `components/members/account/ContactDetailsCard.tsx` on the account overview above the summary cards. Neither is gated on `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` or `registrationCollectDisplayName` **on purpose** - Deskwell has both off, so the profile tab a name would otherwise live on does not exist there. `lib/members/export.ts` carries `fullName` in the GDPR export. **No `Member.phone`, by decision:** a number is how a courier reaches whoever is at a particular door, not a fact about the account, so shop keeps one per saved address in the `shp_saved_addresses` jsonb it already had a `phone` key in. Shop side: `CheckoutContactClient` is email + name only and prefills the name from `/api/members/contact`; the phone box moved to `CheckoutShippingClient`, under First/Last name and above the business name, writing BOTH `shippingAddress.phone` and `customerPhone` in one `updateCheckoutState` call - `customerPhone` is still what the order carries and what `payment-intent` enforces, so nothing server-side changed. Picking a saved address brings its number with it; `missingFromSaved` now counts a numberless saved address as short when `requirePhone` is on, otherwise picking one hides the only box that could answer it. `missingCheckoutFields` lists Phone after Last name to match the form. The address book page and its account tab are now **Addresses & Phone Numbers**, with an inline per-address phone editor (PUT sends the whole address back - the endpoint replaces the stored object) and a phone box on the add form, both refusing a number `isValidUkPhone` cannot read. No shop version bump here: another session already has 0.1.232 in flight in the same tree. **Same batch, the one-page account:** new `membersConfig.accountSinglePage` (default false, toggle on Users → Settings → Account sections) draws every enabled section down the overview instead of a page each. `lib/members/account-layout.ts` is the new shared list of section key/label/path/anchor - deliberately server-import-free, since `AccountNav` is a client component; the nav, the overview and the summary-card links all read it, so the three cannot disagree. `AccountNav` gains `singlePage`: core tabs become `basePath#anchor`, click is intercepted for a smooth `scrollIntoView`, and a rAF-throttled scroll spy lights the tab for whatever section has passed `--cactus-header-offset + 96px` (the last section wins once the page bottoms out, or a short one could never light its own tab). `TabStrip` items may now carry `onClick` alongside `href` - the handler runs with the navigation and calls `preventDefault` itself. The bar goes `position: sticky` at `top: var(--cactus-header-offset, 0px)`, z-index 5, so it pins UNDER a sticky site header (z-index 100) rather than behind it; sections carry a matching `scroll-margin-top`. The five section pages call the new `redirectWhenSinglePage()` (`lib/members/account-sections.ts`) so a bookmarked `/account/security` lands on the anchor - one copy of the truth, not two pages that disagree about which tab is lit. Module tabs (shop's Orders, Addresses & Phone Numbers) stay real pages: they hold rather more than a section's worth and have their own data. **Greeting:** the overview now says "Hi, <first word of `Member.fullName`>" where there is one, falling back to displayName → username → email local part as before, and "Hi there" only when the member has no full name AND the Profile section is off - i.e. only when there is nowhere for them to correct it.)
