Shop never names either module; the seam is the existing `shop.payment-providers` extension point. Verified by rendering the radio rows against the real light/dark token values in headless Chrome. No schema change, no migration.)
Previous entry: (**The check, the push and the pull were re-reading their own 4MB working row - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.64**, core **v0.5.1083**.** Live symptom: a sheet check sat at "Products compared 300 of 445" after 6m18s with 4 steps retried, while the same compare measured 0.2s locally. It was not the compare. Each job keeps its working state as jsonb on its own row - on Deskwell `gsp_preview_job` is 2,196kB + 1,872kB = 4MB, and `gsp_push_job` measured the same in flight - and every reader was `SELECT *`. `stepPreviewJob` read the whole row FOUR times per step to answer three questions that never needed a grid, and `/preview/status` read it again every 1.5s for the whole run. Sampled live at 250ms: 2,091 of 2,265 active-query samples during the Products phase were that one query (36 executions, mean 5,482ms, p90 16.7s, max 35.0s), and **210 of 228 wait samples were `Client/ClientWrite`** - the database holding rows while a busy Node process failed to drain 4MB off the socket. Not IO, not locks, not the pool (the 131 PgBouncer clients were a consequence). Variations was the control: 20,954 rows in 25s against 445 rows in 171s. **Fix.** `PreviewJobLight`/`PushJobLight`/`PullJobLight` OMIT the heavy fields rather than nulling them, so reading a grid you did not load is a compile error, not "the check lost its copy of the Products tab" at run time. `get*JobLight` for every caller but the stepper (the poll, the guards, the Pull adopting a finished check, 3 of the step's 4 reads); `get*JobForStep` for the one heavy read, gated in SQL on the phase - PRODUCTS never loads the variations grid, VARIATIONS never loads the products one, and READ tests `tabTitles` instead of carrying the 2.2MB Products tab through a 383-tab read. Measured A/B against rows in flight: check `SELECT *` 16,742ms -> light 552ms; push `SELECT *` 4,593ms -> light 477ms, gated step read 2,123ms. Before-figures for the after-comparison: check 272s/193s/132s/491s (the spread is the contention), push 479s end to end of which 83s was DONE->COMPLETED, a finalise that does almost no work. **Nets.** New `lib/push-run.test.ts` and `lib/pull-run.test.ts`, twins of `preview-run.test.ts`; each fakes the SAME phase gate the SQL applies, since no unit test can reach a CASE arm. Both mutation-tested: starving the pull's gate fails 4 of its 5 tests, but starving the push's CLEANUP arm does NOT fail loudly - `job.variationTabs ?? []` quietly writes an EMPTY tab manifest and the damage lands on the NEXT sync, so that arm is asserted explicitly. Gates verified against the live database; each phase vocabulary is closed by a CHECK constraint matching its TS union (5 check / 6 push / 4 pull). No schema change, no migration. Note: the v0.1.63 entry below says "working tree only, NOT released" - it was released, and Deskwell was pinned to it.)
Previous entry: (**One database blip binned a whole check - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.63**, working tree only, NOT released.** Live on v0.5.1081: check died at 3m30s, 300 of 445 products compared, showing the owner a raw Prisma error naming `db.dwoffice.furniture:6432`. Site healthy, PgBouncer up and reachable, 39/100 Postgres connections used - but 131 client connections on the neondb pool, so a momentary refusal under load. **CAUSE 1, the abort.** `sheetFailureReason` falls through to `err.message` for anything non-Google, and the runners' catches used it (or `err.message`) directly - so a connection error became a FAILED job like any other, and the client's budget of 5 attempts with backoff capped at 8s spans about THIRTY SECONDS. A pooler busy for longer than that exhausted it and the check gave up, discarding three and a half minutes of banked work. Infrastructure recovers on its own if you let it; the budget was set against failures that repeat instantly. Now 8 attempts with doubling backoff to a 20s cap - about two minutes of patience - and progress still resets the count. **CAUSE 2, the leak.** That same fall-through put a hostname and port in front of a furniture retailer, along with `prisma.$queryRaw` and the query's shape. New `lib/failure.ts`: `describeFailure(err, what)` returns `{ message, transient, detail }` - owner-safe sentence, whether it is worth retrying, and the specifics for the log only. `OwnerMessageError` marks the text we wrote FOR the owner so it passes through unchanged; everything else gets a plain sentence. Wired into all three runners' phase catches AND their lease-machinery catches (the lease claim is itself a query, so it is the likeliest place a connection error lands - found in pass 26, after the first fix) and into POST /push's start path. `rowFailureReason` for per-row reasons keeps a useful domain message ("SKU already in use") but swaps a connection failure for the plain sentence. **CAUSE 3, our share of the pressure.** `PARENT_CONCURRENCY` was 10 and `PRODUCT_COLUMN_CONCURRENCY` 8, both set when every parent cost its own round trips. Since the beginImportMany batching a parent is in-memory work - 349 of them compare in 32ms - so concurrency buys nothing and only holds connections open. Both to 4; measured 7,203ms vs 6,997ms for the whole variations phase, ie noise. Push step budget 35s -> 20s as well, matching the other two under the 60s ceiling. **Tests**: new `failure.test.ts` asserts the live error string never yields a hostname, port, `prisma` or `queryRaw` to the owner and IS classified transient; `preview-run.test.ts` gained a blip mid-check that must leave the job FAILED-but-not-fatal, message free of `6432`, and the check completing afterwards with every row counted exactly once. **Flagged, not investigated**: a category page measured 11.2s against 1.5s for the homepage. Probably unrelated to any of this, but if the shop is under connection pressure generally it is worth someone knowing.)
Previous entry: (**Batched the per-parent variant-provider contract - `shop-variations` **v0.1.144**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.57**, `product-3d-views-for-shop` **v0.1.92**, `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.62**, working tree only, NOT released.** Live check after the v0.5.1080 release: read and products phases tick past correctly, and the run then sits in VARIATIONS for the bulk of 10m 22s. (The retry line worked - "2 steps had to be tried again".) **Cause, measured not guessed:** `VariantFieldProvider.beginImport(productId, childProductIds)` is called ONCE PER PARENT, which is right for importing one product and wrong for anything sweeping a catalogue. Timed serially across 349 parents on live: **product-attributes 184,240ms, product-3d-views 148,204ms** - 698 round trips for answers that fit in three queries. `PARENT_CONCURRENCY` hid it at 10-way, which is why it read as ~28s rather than five and a half minutes. **New optional `beginImportMany(parents)` on the contract** (shop-variations owns it): ONE context covering many parents, handed to `applyImportedRow`/`rowChanged` for every parent in the batch, so everything it holds must be keyed by something globally unique (child product id, or the parent's own id). Back-compatible - a provider with only `beginImport` still works and callers fall back. Implemented in both providers: 3d never cared which parent a child belonged to so it is one `getModelsForProducts` over every child; attributes gained `listVariationColumnsForProducts` + `getVariantAttributeValuesForProducts` (parent scoping kept exactly as the single-product query has it - redundant in practice, but not a predicate to widen when it decides what a variant is currently set to). `prepareVariationDiff` preloads once for every parent; `diffOneParent` uses that and only asks per parent for a provider with no batched form. **`importVariationsCsv` deliberately stays per-parent** - it handles a handful of parents per call and it WRITES, so a catalogue-wide snapshot taken before the writes would be the wrong shape. Half-migrated only in the sense the contract is designed for. **Measured live, same harness as before -> after:** variations compare **28,375ms -> 33ms**; variations phase 34.3s -> 7.0s; **whole catalogue side of a check 85s -> 19s** (products setup 5.6s + compare 0.2s, removals 6.5s, variations setup 6.2s + compare 0.03s). Against ~15 minutes when this started. **Pass-23 catch:** `applyImportedRow` had started reading columns from the batched preload, where "absent" means "no columns" - true of the parents a batch covered, false of a product created mid-import, and on the WRITE path that silence would drop a new product's attributes rather than miscount them. It is pinned back to the per-product lookup with the reasoning written down. On splitting the workbook into several sheets (Chris asked): agreed with the advice against - `batchGetGroups` already packs ~40 tabs per call so 350 tabs is ~9 API calls, reading was never the slow part, Google's quota is per project not per document, and the cell-limit pressure that might once have argued for it was already solved by sizing each tab to its contents.)
Previous entry: (**The double comparison, the 5xx, and the silent removals stage - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.61**, `shop` **v0.1.229**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.56**, working tree only, NOT released.** Live evidence on released v0.1.60: check completes but takes ~15 minutes, then pressing Pull re-runs the WHOLE comparison before applying (the apply itself is fine - 14s, clear, correct wording), plus 8x 500/504 on `/api/m/[module]/[...path]` that Vercel's own analysis attributed to timeouts in the pull preview workflow. **CAUSE 1, the double comparison - a one-word bug.** `adoptPreview` computed `age = Date.now() - job.createdAt`, and `createdAt` is when the check STARTED. `PREVIEW_MAX_AGE_MS` was 15 minutes and the check took about 15 minutes, so a brand-new summary was already "too old to trust" the instant the owner could press Pull: adoption refused, and v0.1.60 fell back to redoing the entire sweep. **The time a check spends working is not time its answer has spent going stale.** Now aged from `updatedAt` (finish), window 30 min, `PreviewJob` maps `updated_at` (column already existed, no migration). The Drive `modifiedTime` match remains the real guard on the sheet; the age cap only ever guarded against the CATALOGUE moving. **CAUSE 2, the 5xx.** `STEP_TIME_BUDGET_MS` was 30s (check) / 35s (pull) against a hard 60s platform ceiling - only 25-30s of headroom for the chunk already in flight, and on v0.1.60 the PRODUCTS setup alone was minutes. Both budgets now **20s**, with `MODULE_ROUTE_CEILING_MS = 60_000` named and used: `mayStartChunk` refuses to START the guaranteed chunk inside the last 15s, and a phase that could do nothing at all now throws `setupTooSlow()` so a wedge surfaces instead of looping in silence. **CAUSE 3, the silent removals stage.** `deletionsDone` was added to the PULL dialog in an earlier pass; the CHECK's removals phase had nothing at all - it is bulk queries with no per-row cursor, so there is no bar to draw. `planPullDeletions` now takes an `onProgress` callback and narrates ("Reading your catalogue", "Checking the variations on N products"), throttled to 900ms, rendered as a named line. **SPEED, measured live end to end.** Whole catalogue side of a check: **92s** (PRODUCTS setup 6.1s + compare 0.2s; DELETIONS 10.1s; VARIATIONS setup 5.9s + compare 35.2s), against ~15 minutes before. `PARENT_CONCURRENCY` 6 -> 10 took the variations compare to **28.4s**, so ~85s total. `PRODUCT_ROW_CHUNK` 50 -> 150 now that a chunk is sub-second. Remaining hot spot, flagged not fixed: the variations compare at ~80ms/parent is shop-variations' per-parent `beginImport` contract; batching it would need a change to that provider interface (a fourth module). **Retries are now visible** - the hook counts them and the dialog says "N steps had to be tried again", because a run that covered for 8 failed requests looked flawless to the owner while showing up as 5xx in the site's monitoring, and only one of those two was being told. **The intermittent halt at 250 explained**: steps were 504ing at the ceiling, so `updatePreviewJob` never ran during the long PRODUCTS setup and `updated_at` froze; the retry budget then ran out, the owner pressed "Try again", `POST /pull/preview` ran `expireStalePreviewJobs()` FIRST, which judged the job idle, flipped it to CANCELLED and NULLED its grids - so the dialog showed "Check stopped." on the old job's last snapshot and a brand-new job started from tab one. Intermittent because it needed both the retry budget to run out AND the 3-minute idle window to have elapsed. All three legs are fixed: lease claims bump `updated_at`, heartbeats before each long setup, the sweep marks FAILED and keeps the grids, and the route resumes before it expires anything.)
Previous entry: (**"Check stopped." at 250 of 445, and Check again threw the 250 away - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.61**, `shop` **v0.1.229**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.56**, working tree only, NOT released.** Second live report after v0.1.60. Two faults, **both mine, both from the Pass-3 idle sweep**. **(1) A working check was being killed.** `claimPreviewStepLease` did NOT touch `updated_at`, and a phase with long setup writes nothing until its first chunk lands - so a step the platform killed mid-setup left `updated_at` frozen while the browser was busily asking for step after step. `expireStalePreviewJobs` then judged it idle and flipped it to **CANCELLED**, which is why the dialog said "Check stopped." as though that were a normal ending. **(2) And it gutted it**: that sweep also nulled `products_grid`/`variations_grid`/`raw_tabs`, so the 250 products already compared became unrecoverable - and because the sweep ran FIRST in `POST /pull/preview`, before the join lookup, the very button offered to continue destroyed the job and created a fresh one. **Fixes**: the lease claim now bumps `updated_at` (claiming a lease IS activity); `heartbeatPreviewJob()` called before each long setup (products, variations, removals) so a phase mid-call still reads as alive; the sweep now marks **FAILED** (the module's own "did not finish, cursor intact") and **keeps the working columns**; new `getResumablePreviewJob()` + `resumePreviewJob()`, and `POST /pull/preview` **carries on before anything else** - joins a RUNNING check, resumes a stopped one, and only creates a new job when there is nothing to carry on with or the owner passes `{fresh:true}`. The dialog now offers "Carry on from 250 products" as the primary button with "Start again" beside it, and says "The check stopped part-way - nothing is lost." A stepped FAILED job self-heals anyway, since `stepPreviewJob` only short-circuits on COMPLETED/CANCELLED. `resumePreviewJob` also guards against the one-RUNNING index rather than letting it 500. **The 16 minutes, measured and fixed at source.** Live timings, before -> after: `buildProductCsvRows` 128,852ms -> 5,742ms -> **7,581ms** (shop N+1: four lookups PER PRODUCT, now four batched queries - new `getProductCategoryIdsForProducts`/`TagIds`/`CollectionIds` beside the existing media one); `diffProductRowRange` per 50 rows **11,148ms -> 348ms first chunk, 9ms warm** (product-attributes: `listProductLevelColumns` was 204ms x 445 products = 91s of pure round trips; new `listProductLevelColumnsForProducts` preloaded in `beginImport`, read through `columnsForWithCtx`). `prepareProductDiff` 150,029ms -> **16,134ms**, the rise from 6s being that preload moving INTO setup where it is paid once. Products phase ~240s -> **~16s**. Whole check now ~85s locally over ~5-6 steps, less on Vercel next to the database. `applyImportedRow` deliberately still queries per product - it can be called for products created mid-import, which no preload covers. **Structural guarantee added first, and it caught its own bug**: `mayStartChunk()` in both runners - a step must land at least ONE chunk whatever the clock says - and the new regression test showed the guaranteed chunk was then discarded by `BANK_INTERVAL_MS`, so banking now also fires when a step is about to end (`willContinue`). Tests: `preview-run.test.ts` gained "still makes progress when the setup alone outlasts the step budget" (45s setup vs 30s budget, asserts completion inside the real 60s ceiling) and "carries on from its cursor after being stopped part-way". **Still not driven end-to-end through Google from here**: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not on the dev machine so the stored OAuth tokens do not decrypt - correct, and not worth defeating. Everything catalogue-side measured against live.)
Previous entry: (**The stall MOVED rather than went - "Products compared - 0 of 445" - `shop` **v0.1.229**, `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.61**, working tree only, NOT released.** After v0.1.60 shipped and Chris updated Deskwell, the live check read all 350 product tabs (READ genuinely fixed) then sat on **Products compared - 0 of 445** with the clock running. **Diagnosed by measurement against the live database, not by reading:** `buildProductCsvRows` for 445 products = **128,852ms**; the whole per-step setup `prepareProductDiff` = **150,029ms**; step budget 30s, platform ceiling 60s. So no step ever reached its compare loop, the cursor never left 0, and every retry repeated the identical 150s of setup. **Root cause was shop's, not the sheet module's**: `buildProductCsvRows` called `getProductMedia` + `getProductCategoryIds` + `getProductTagIds` + `getProductCollectionIds` **once per product**, sequentially. Added `getProductCategoryIdsForProducts` / `getProductTagIdsForProducts` / `getProductCollectionIdsForProducts` beside the existing `getProductMediaForProducts` and made the loop use all four. **Re-measured live: 128,852ms -> 5,742ms; prepareProductDiff 150,029ms -> 6,173ms (24x).** Single-product versions stay - they have plenty of callers on the product pages. This also speeds the Push's BUILD_PRODUCTS and shop's own CSV export. **Measured the REST of the check too**, so the fix would not just move the stall again: `planPullDeletions` 7.7s, `prepareVariationDiff` 6.2s, `diffVariationGroupRange` ~1s per 12 parents (349 parents ~29s), `getEditorPayloadsBatch` 4.9s over 349 parents, 20,954 variation rows. Whole check now projects to ~8-12 steps. **The structural fix, so this class cannot recur:** `mayStartChunk()` in BOTH `preview-run.ts` and `pull-run.ts` - a step must always land at least ONE chunk whatever the clock says, because "setup outgrew the budget" must never again mean "make no progress at all". **That fix was itself buggy and a new regression test caught it**: the guaranteed chunk landed but `BANK_INTERVAL_MS` (5s) then declined to persist it, so the cursor still never moved. Banking now also fires when the step is about to end (`willContinue`), so the last chunk of every step is always banked - a latent waste on the normal path and fatal on the one-chunk path. New test `preview-run.test.ts` "still makes progress when the setup alone outlasts the step budget" drives setup at 45s against the 30s budget and asserts the check completes inside the platform's real 60s ceiling. **Still NOT verified end to end through Google**: `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is not on the dev machine, so the stored OAuth tokens do not decrypt locally - correct behaviour, and not worth defeating by copying a production secret onto a dev box. Everything on the catalogue side was measured against the real live data. Remaining known hot spot, flagged not fixed: the products compare is ~200ms/row (~10s per 50) from product-attributes' per-row `rowChanged` lookups, so the products phase is ~90s of real work; batching `columnsFor` and the label vocabulary in that module would cut it further. Also noticed and NOT touched: several per-product N+1s in shop's storefront rendering (`getProductTagIds` inside loops in category/collection/tag pages, ShopRelatedProducts, ShopAttributeFilterGrid) - real, but the live storefront and out of this fault's scope.)
Previous entry: (**"Pull from sheet" stuck on "Reading your sheet and comparing it with your catalogue…" - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **v0.1.60**, module working tree only, `modules.json` NOT touched. NO core release.** **The bug.** `POST /pull/preview` was ONE request that had to, inside the module dispatcher's `maxDuration = 60`: fetch Drive modifiedTime, read the Products tab, list every tab, read every candidate's header row, read the body of every product tab (~24 batched calls on Deskwell's ~350-tab workbook), write the whole snapshot to `gsp_sheet_snapshot`, run `buildProductCsvRows()` (which is ~4 queries PER product), `getProductsBySlugs`, every product-field provider's `beginImport`, `planPullDeletions` (paged `listProducts` + `getEditorPayloadsBatch` over every variable parent + `createdAtByIds`), and `diffVariationRows` (the same payload batch again, plus **one `beginImport` per parent per contributing module, strictly sequentially** - ~350 parents x 2 providers). Minutes of work; on Vercel it 504s, locally it just never returns. **And pressing Pull then did the whole lot a second time before a single row was imported.** Plus a **TEMP-DIAG left in since v0.1.41** that JSON-stringified every Products row's attribute cells into a `console.error` AND shipped them in the response. **The fix - the check is now a resumable job.** New `gsp_preview_job` (migrations/012) + `lib/preview-job.ts` + `lib/preview-run.ts`, mirroring the Pull/Push job shape exactly (step lease, cursors, "never write to a cancelled job", atomic finalise). Phases **READ -> PRODUCTS -> DELETIONS -> VARIATIONS -> DONE**, 30s budget per step, cursors banked after every chunk (READ counts tabs, PRODUCTS rows, VARIATIONS **parent products**). New routes `/pull/preview` (start, 202 + id), `/pull/preview/step`, `/pull/preview/status`, `/pull/preview/cancel`. `lib/preview.ts` (`buildPullPreview`) deleted - its logic now lives in the phases. **The second sweep is gone.** The finished job stores `filtered_products`/`filtered_variations`, both row maps, the deletion plan and `detected`, and `POST /pull` now takes `{ previewJobId }` and **adopts** them - guarded by an EXACT Drive `modifiedTime` match plus a 15-minute age cap, falling back to the old full path when either fails. What the dialog listed is now literally what runs. **Push start was the same class of stall** and is now two new phases, `BUILD_PRODUCTS` and `BUILD_TABS` (migrations/013 replaces the 007 phase CHECK; `createPushJob` no longer takes grids). `POST /push` returns in milliseconds; the snapshot is built by the first two steps. **Diff internals**: `diffProductRows`/`diffVariationRows` split into `prepareProductDiff` + `diffProductRowRange` and `prepareVariationDiff` + `diffVariationGroupRange` (one-shot wrappers kept, so the existing tests are untouched); parents now diff **6 at a time** (`PARENT_CONCURRENCY`) and each parent's provider preloads run in `Promise.all` rather than one after another. New `keptRowsFromResults` for chunk-wise accumulation. **Settled failures no longer retry**: `SettledError` (renamed/missing product tab, no product tabs at all) and `GoogleAuthError` set `fatal` on the job, and the browser loop stops at the first one instead of five retries with backoff. **UI.** New `components/useSteppedJob.ts` - the step/poll/retry/stop loop was written out three times and had started to drift; it is now one hook driving Push, Pull and the check. Dialogs: sticky footer, Escape closes, `aria-live` headline, elapsed clock, phase pills, tally tiles on the confirm screen, per-phase bars for the check, danger-boxed deletions, capped lists (`PREVIEW_LIST_CAP` 200) with `…Total` counts beside them so the response can never be unbounded. `PullPreview` gained `toCreateTotal`/`toUpdateTotal`/`toDeleteTotal`/`rowErrorsTotal`. Settings tab gained a "Where things stand" panel (connection, sheet, last push/pull, what is running now) and folds the six-step Google walkthrough away once connected; Reset sheet is blocked while anything is running. `/settings` GET now also returns `variationTabCount` and `busy`. **PASSES 2-5, a from-scratch re-audit each time, as asked.** **P2-1 the removals stage was the next stall of the same family.** `applyProductDeletions`/`applyVariationDeletions` were two unbounded `DELETE ... IN (...)` statements with no cursor - and a product delete cascades through media, categories, variants, variant values and every module's per-product rows, so a big plan is real work. Past 60s the platform killed it and the retry started the plan again: stuck on "Removing items…" for ever. Now chunked at 100 with the step's time budget and a cursor (**migration 014**, `prod_deletions_done`/`var_deletions_done` on `gsp_pull_job`), plus its own progress bar (`PullStatus.deletionsTotal/Done`, totals taken from `detected` so they survive the plan being cleared) and the right verb - it said "Updating <product>…" while deleting it. **P2-2 the last unbounded path is gone.** `POST /pull` kept a fallback that read and diffed the whole sheet when no check could be adopted - i.e. exactly the 60s blowout, on the click after the one that was just fixed. It now **requires** an adoptable check and answers `409 {stalePreview:true}` otherwise; the browser re-runs the (bounded, progress-reporting) check and shows the new list. The route is ~100 lines shorter and can no longer be the thing that hangs. **P2-3 `buildProductsGrid` asked every product for its contributed columns one at a time** - one round trip per product per provider, strictly serial, the slowest thing in a Push. Batched at 8; `getValues` calls now go together too. `product-fields-pass` preloads its providers in parallel likewise. **P2-4 my own Pass-1 write amplification**: the check re-serialised its whole accumulating blob (read tabs, filtered grids, row maps) after EVERY chunk - dozens of multi-megabyte writes. Heavy columns are now banked on a 5s clock and always at phase end, in the same write as the cursor they account for; the light column (the name being compared) still writes per chunk so the dialog keeps moving. **P2-5 Reset left the old workbook's state behind** - the manifest of product tabs, so the first check of the fresh sheet stopped with "these product tabs are missing" about a sheet that was fine. Cleared now, and Reset refuses server-side while anything is running (the settings tab's grey-out is a view, not a guard). **P3-1 a stranded check blocked Push for ever**: nothing resumes a check, so a browser closed mid-check left a RUNNING row that `getRunningPreviewJob` answered "yes" to indefinitely. Freshness-filtered (3 min idle + expired lease) plus `expireStalePreviewJobs()` called before a check and before a Push. **P4-1 a real defect in my own runner**: a phase that completes with ZERO chunks never wrote its accumulators - so a sheet whose variation rows all failed the grouping (no "Parent Slug" column) threw away every row error and reported a clean sheet. Both phase-closing writes now carry them. **P5-1 `gsp_sheet_snapshot` had become write-only** - the check keeps its own grids and `POST /pull` adopts the job wholesale, so nothing read it back, while every check wrote the whole workbook into it. Dropped (**migration 015**), `lib/sheet-snapshot.ts` + test deleted, teardown list updated. Also: the elapsed clock now times the current stretch of work rather than since the job was first created. **PASSES 6-8.** **P6-1** a renamed or deleted **Products** tab (Google 4xx "unable to parse range") was retried five times with backoff before the owner got the sentence telling them what to fix - `isSettled()` now covers any Sheets 4xx that is not 429, alongside the module's own guards and `GoogleAuthError`. **P6-2** `getSheetModifiedTime` answers **null** rather than throwing when Drive will not say, and `adoptPreview` required a stored time - so on a site where Drive is quiet the check would finish and the Pull could never be started, for ever. Now: Drive answered then, it must answer now and agree; Drive was silent then AND is silent now, fall back to a 2-minute freshness window; silent then but talking now, refuse and re-check. **P7-1** three step-failure logs passed the raw error object where the rest of the module deliberately logs `err.message` - a Prisma error can carry the datasource URL into the platform log. **P8-1** dead code the rework orphaned: `lib/pull-variations.ts` (both exports lost their last caller when the preview took over the tab reading) and `filterGridByDiff` (replaced by `keptRowsFromResults`) deleted; `ensureVariationTab` (dead since `createVariationTabsBatch`, pre-existing) deleted with it. `diffProductRows`/`diffVariationRows` are kept deliberately as the whole-grid form the unit tests drive, and now say so. **PASSES 10-12.** **P10-1** `finalisePreviewJob` flipped the status to COMPLETED and wrote `detected` AFTER - a Pull pressed in that gap found a finished check with no counts and was told to check again for nothing. Counts are written first now (idempotent), the flip second. **P10-2** `useSteppedJob` re-POSTed the instant a step returned, so a step that honestly did NO work - another tab holding the lease, or a platform-killed request whose 90s lease had not expired - became a round trip every ~100ms for up to a minute and a half. Idle steps now back off 400ms doubling to 4s, reset by any real progress. **P11-1** that backoff immediately exposed the Pull's `progressOf` key missing `deletionsDone` (removals only grew a cursor in P2-1), which would have paced the whole removals stage at 4s a step and stopped the retry budget resetting while it worked. **P12 EMPTY** - fresh from-scratch pass over the finished tree found nothing: no markers, no dead exports beyond the deliberately-kept API wrappers, migrations sequential and idempotent, versions and teardown in step. **NEW TEST `lib/preview-run.test.ts`** - drives the real `stepPreviewJob` at Deskwell's shape (383 tabs, 450 product rows, 350 variable parents) over a faked Google, a faked diff and an in-memory job row, with a SIMULATED CLOCK so the time budget genuinely bites. Proves the thing the rework is for: **104s of work completes in 6 bounded steps** (READ → PRODUCTS → DELETIONS → VARIATIONS → VARIATIONS → DONE) where the old single request had 60s; every row compared exactly once; the filtered grid and its row map stay the same length; a step killed before it can bank resumes without losing or double-counting anything; a cancel mid-run stops it and further steps do nothing; heavy columns written <60 times rather than once per chunk. Harness note: the fake job row round-trips through JSON like a jsonb column does - sharing the object let a step mutate what it had already banked, which is exactly the bug a fake database must not have. **NOT changed, flagged instead:** `ROW_SLACK = 0` trims the Products tab to exactly its content, so typing a brand-new product on the row below means using Sheets' "add rows" control first - the zero was settled deliberately and twice, and the padding it fixed lives on the hundreds of product tabs, not on this one; a 50-row slack on the Products tab alone would cost ~0.02% of the cell budget if Chris wants it. **Gate**: `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` real PASS (no skips) after every schema change. `tsc --noEmit` + `eslint .` clean, full suite green.)

Previous entry: (**LIVE DB WRITE + the regression it exposed - `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.19**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.55**, pinned by core **v0.5.1078**.** **The writes (authorised by Chris, backups + rollback at ~/DeskwellBackups/scroll-and-badge-2026-08-15/).** 48 shopCategory layouts: added `paginate:'scroll'` and `pageSize:24` to the single ShopFilterGrid in each. **Written to `builderData` AND `publishedData`** - the instruction said publishedData, but `resolveThemeLayout` selects and renders **builderData** (publishedData is explicitly NOT selected, see its own comment), so publishedData alone would have done NOTHING. Both kept in step. Nothing else altered: `limit` stays 100, columns/filterPosition/showCounts/layoutRef untouched, shopIndex's single ShopProductGrid untouched. Plus one shp_tags row: New.badge_text_dark #F2F1EE -> #2B2D30 (2.2:1 -> 8.6:1 dark mode). **The regression the live check caught, and the rule to remember.** Straight after the write, deskwell.co.uk served 214 cards with 190 correctly marked `data-flt-offpage` and **all 214 visible anyway**. Cause: **React runs ALL layout effects before ANY passive effect.** The Phase-4 change (v0.1.16/v0.1.52) moved the PAGING pass to useLayoutEffect while the FILTER pass stayed a plain useEffect, silently inverting them - paging hid 190, then the filter pass set `display=''` on everything and put them back, leaving the markers behind. **So: every pass that writes to the cards - filter, sort, paging - must share ONE phase, and declaration order then decides the rest, which is what those comments always claimed.** All three are now `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect`; the IntersectionObserver effect stays passive on purpose (it attaches a listener, it has no business blocking paint). Customer impact while live was benign - everything visible and reachable, still better than the old 100 ceiling - but it was not the requested behaviour. Verified after the fix on the real 214-product category: 24 visible on load, 190 hidden AND consistent, growth 24->214 by the same handler the sentinel calls, button gone at the end, zero stray markers, no page-number row. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**Second pass over the infinite-scroll work - `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.18**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.54**, pinned by core **v0.5.1077**.** The Phase 4 pass ran BEFORE the scroll rework, so the scroll work had never had one. Re-audited from scratch. **Structural, all mechanical**: guard test green (21); generator still registers **105 blocks**; prop diff across all six modules touched since the first pass shows **zero props removed or renamed**, additions only (the scroll mode is a new VALUE on the existing `paginate` prop, not a new prop, so it correctly shows nothing). **One real finding, fixed**: both shells' `showMore` grew `shownLimit` without a ceiling while shop's `ShopGridPager` clamps the same counter with `Math.min(n + size, total)`. Not reachable in practice - the `moreToShow` gate unmounts the button and the sentinel once everything is shown - but the number the observer drives had no bound, and two implementations of one idea disagreed about whether that mattered. Clamped in both. **Checked and sound**: the sentinel renders inside the pager `<nav>`, NOT inside the grid div - inside it would become a phantom grid cell. The observer effect deliberately does not depend on `shownLimit`; it depends on `moreToShow`, so it is not torn down and rebuilt on every growth step but IS torn down when there is nothing left to load. **Honestly inconclusive**: I twice tried to demonstrate in-browser that an IntersectionObserver does not re-fire while its target stays intersecting (the failure mode that would load every remaining page on one scroll). Both harnesses failed to fire at all in this environment, so both results are worthless and neither is being reported as evidence. The behaviour is specified - the callback fires on intersection STATE CHANGE - and the clamp above plus the `moreToShow` gate bound the damage even if it were wrong. Worth a real device check before this is switched on. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**The three deferred findings, now done - A6, C4 and the rest of C1. `shop` **v0.1.228**, `shop-variations` **v0.1.143**, `square-payment-for-shop` **v0.1.7**, `gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop` **v0.1.7**, pinned by core **v0.5.1076**.** **A6 - the email in the confirmation URL.** The page carried `?orderNumber=DW000123&email=someone@example.com`, so the address travelled into access logs, browser history and the Referer sent to every third party the confirmation page loads (a chat widget, on this shop). New **modules/shop/lib/order-receipt-token.ts**: `signOrderReceiptToken`/`verifyOrderReceiptToken`, HMAC-SHA256 over `receipt:<orderNumber>` keyed on `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, base64url, constant-time compare - deliberately the same shape as the `unsubscribe-token.ts` beside it, so no table, no row, no expiry sweep. **It is also STRONGER than what it replaced**: order numbers are prefix+sequence, so `email` was the whole lock and near-guessable; a 256-bit HMAC is not. Issued by the payment-intent route (`receiptToken` in its JSON), carried by CheckoutPaymentClient, and by BOTH payment modules' return routes. The status route accepts EITHER `email` (the guest order-LOOKUP form, where the shopper types both halves - untouched) OR `t`. OrderConfirmationClient still reads `email` when that is all it is given, so a link bookmarked or emailed before this change keeps working. NOT time-limited, matching the route it replaces - a receipt is a thing people come back to. **C4 - card parts brought up to their detail equivalents.** `Card: Price` gains showSave/size/align - showSave defaults **'no'**, unlike the detail block's 'yes', because a card that never carried a Save badge must not grow one on upgrade. `Card: Name` gains size/align. `Card: Image` gains ratio/fit **as CSS custom properties on the wrapper** (`--shop-card-ratio`, `--shop-card-fit`) rather than inline rules on the `<img>`, because the picture may belong to the ShopCardMedia carousel island rather than to us - the stylesheet reads the properties and both paths pick them up. New `cardAlignStyle`/`cardSizeStyle`/`mergeStyle` helpers all return **undefined** for defaults so no style attribute is emitted. **C1 - the last four settingless blocks.** shop's `Product: Pre-order notice` (opening word, dispatch date, product note, align); shop-variations' `Shop: Personalisation` (heading, blank = nothing, as always), `Shop: Variant Price` (the same was/save/RRP trimmings shop's own Price offers, since this block REPLACES it on a variations product) and `Shop: Variant Gallery` (thumbSize as a `--svr-thumb` custom property, so a contributed 3D thumbnail - styled by the module that supplied it, reachable only by class name - resizes with the photographs). **Live-layout coverage checked before releasing**: ShopCardPrice/Name/Image, ShopDetailPreorder and ShopVariantPrice are all on live layouts and were verified in the browser emitting no style attribute, aspect-ratio still 1/1, object-fit still cover, zero Save pills. ShopVariantGallery and ShopVariantPersonalisation are on NO live layout. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**Infinite scroll on all three product grids - `shop` **v0.1.227**, `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.17**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.53**, pinned by core **v0.5.1075**.** Chris wants categories to load as the shopper scrolls, not to offer page numbers. New `paginate` value **'scroll'** on all three blocks. **Three decisions, none forced, all stated because they were choices:** (1) **'Show more' stays a real button AND becomes the scroll trigger.** An `IntersectionObserver` on a 1px sentinel below the grid calls the same handler the button does (`rootMargin: '400px 0px'`, so the next row is usually there before the shopper arrives). The button is NOT hidden in scroll mode: an observer cannot be reached by a keyboard, is invisible to a screen reader, and fires never where the page does not scroll - which on a filtered grid is the COMMON case, since two ticks can leave nine products. The auto-load is a convenience over a control that works without it. Also degrades cleanly where `IntersectionObserver` is undefined. (2) **Numbered paging is NOT removed.** 'scroll' is a fourth value beside 'none'|'more'|'pages'; default is still 'none'. Scroll was asked for on categories; nobody asked for numbers to leave every surface. (3) **SEO needs nothing special, for a specific reason worth remembering**: every card is ALREADY server-rendered into the initial HTML - the client only shows and hides them - so all 217 products are in the source with real hrefs whatever the mode. Verified live on /shop/categories/office-chairs: 100 cards, **100 unique /shop/products/ hrefs, all present**. This is a display device over a complete document, not a data-loading trick. **Implementation**: 'scroll' and 'more' share ONE window - `visibleRange` (shop) and the `growing` flag (both shells) treat them identically - so every guarantee proved for one holds for the other, and the tests assert that equivalence rather than restating the arithmetic. Verified against the real 100-card grid by driving the growth loop: 24 -> 48 -> 72 -> 96 -> 100, monotonic, never overshooting, identical to 'more' at every step, DOM restored after. **Note**: `paginate` is set on ZERO live layouts (checked), so the numbered paging shipped in v0.1.226/0.1.15/0.1.51 was inert on the live site and no shopper ever saw it. Turning any mode on across the ~50 category layouts remains Chris's write and is still unauthorised. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**Phase 4, the second audit pass over the whole shop - `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.16**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **v0.1.52**, pinned by core **v0.5.1074**.** A from-scratch re-audit of all 14 modules after Phase 3, looking for what the first pass missed and what the fixes themselves broke. **Structural guarantees, all verified mechanically rather than by eye**: `lib/puck/module-layout-blocks.test.ts` green (21); generator still registers **105 blocks**, the same count as before any of this work; a scripted diff of every Puck component's `fields`/`defaultProps` keys across all 14 modules against each one's pre-audit commit shows **87 puck files, zero props removed or renamed**, additions only; a manifest diff shows **no block deregistered and no `layoutTypes` changed** in any module. Frontend parity re-checked live: category page still 100 cards all visible, no pager, no `data-flt-offpage`, same `shop-grid` class and `--shop-cols`; product page price wrapper and `.spd-blurb` still emit NO style attribute; delivery blocks unwrapped; variant options still in stored order. **Two real defects found in MY OWN Phase 3 work, both in the paging shells:** (1) the paging pass ran in a plain `useEffect`, which runs AFTER paint - a 217-product category drew every card and then hid 193, a visible flash with the scrollbar jumping. Moved to `useLayoutEffect` behind a `useIsomorphicLayoutEffect` wrapper (`typeof window !== 'undefined' ? useLayoutEffect : useEffect`), because both shells are server-rendered and React warns if useLayoutEffect runs during SSR. NB shop's own `ShopGridPager` never had this - it slices during render. (2) the paging state was named `shown`, shadowing the `let shown = 0` counter in the filter effect directly above it. Harmless as written but a trap for the next edit to that effect; renamed `shownLimit`. **Also corrected from Phase 1**: the address-lookup 'cross-module import' finding was wrong (see the previous entry), B4 'chat launcher covers the cookie banner' was the Next.js dev indicator and does not exist in production, B5 'cart page has no metadata' was false (it exports metadata; the blank title was the page erroring on a pool timeout), and C6 'cart totals cannot relabel every row' was a misread - shop deliberately prints the resolver's own charge label. NO schema change anywhere in Phase 3 or 4, so the backup round-trip gate was never triggered.)

Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, parts eleven to fourteen - `reviews-for-shop` **v0.1.6**, `quote-for-shop` **v0.1.14**, `product-3d-views-for-shop` **v0.1.91**, pinned by core **v0.5.1073**. Phase 3 complete: all 14 modules done.** **B10, reviews.** The module had NO `memberExtensions.dataExportPath` at all, while holding author name, author email and `submitted_ip` per review. New **app/api/member/gdpr-export/route.ts** on shop's pattern (internal bearer via `verifyInternalExportBearer`, called self-origin by core's `assembleMemberExport`, never session-reachable). Matches on `member_id` OR the Member's own email lower-cased - a guest review under the same address is the same person's data - and the email is read from the Member row, never from the request. Includes `rvw_invites`. NB `rvw_invites` is (id, order_id, product_id, email, sent_at): no `status`, no `created_at` - the first draft assumed both and was corrected against the live schema before shipping. **quote-for-shop.** The public request form's only guard was the in-memory per-IP limiter, which resets on a cold start, and every request emails the owner. Added a honeypot named `website`: hidden by off-screen POSITION rather than display:none/hidden (cruder bots skip the obviously hidden), with tabIndex=-1 + aria-hidden + autoComplete=off so keyboards, screen readers and password managers never reach it - without those a honeypot catches honest customers, which is worse than catching nobody. Optional in the zod schema so a client that never rendered it is not punished; a FILLED one returns `{ok:true}`, the same shape success has, because naming the failed check is free advice to a bot. **product-3d-views.** `FILES[file]` in **lib/decoder-assets.ts** is a plain object literal, so 'constructor'/'toString'/'__proto__' returned truthy off Object.prototype, fell through the allowlist, joined `undefined` into a path and answered 500 instead of 404. Never readable - the read throws and is caught - but it logged errors that looked like a fault. `Object.hasOwn` + the module's first tests. **address-lookup-for-shop: NO CHANGE, and deliberately.** The Phase 1 note about it importing `@/modules/shop/lib/rate-limit` being a module-boundary smell was WRONG: every `-for-shop` companion declares shop in `requiresModules` and imports its db, config and card-template libs freely - that IS the architecture. Duplicating a rate limiter to avoid one import would be the actual defect. NO schema change in any of these.)

Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, parts six to ten - `product-downloads-for-shop` **v0.1.6**, `product-checks-for-shop` **v0.1.3**, `product-addons-for-shop` **v0.1.18**, `advanced-shipping-for-shop` **v0.1.34**, pinned by core **v0.5.1072** (product-checks NOT pinned - see below).** **B9, downloads.** `app/api/public/files/[id]/route.ts` reads the whole file into a Buffer before answering - the price of renaming it on the way past, which is the entire reason the bytes come through the route instead of the shopper being linked at storage. New `MAX_DOWNLOAD_BYTES = 64MB`: past it, a 413 and a console.error rather than an OOM with no explanation. Deliberately refused, not streamed - streaming means giving up the filename. Largest live `pdl_files` row is 5.0MB, so nothing real is near it. **C1, the settingless blocks.** Eleven blocks shipped `fields: {}`. Cleared four modules' worth: `ShopProductChecks` gains `initialState` (ChecksPanel always took `initiallyOpen` - the admin editor passes it - but the block hardcoded it shut); `ShopCardProductChecks` gains `show` ('all'|'stale', the count line still reads out of the full ten, only the listed rows narrow, via new `staleOnly` on CardChecksStrip); `ShopProductAddons` and `ShopAddonsShowcase` gain a heading override that falls through to the module's own noun when blank, and the showcase additionally a `maxCards` cap (0/blank = all); the three advanced-shipping blocks (`ShopDeliveryEstimate`, `ShopDeliveryCartSummary`, `ShopDeliveryBasketOffers`) gain `align` via new shared **components/puck/block-fields.ts**. **The alignment pattern is worth copying**: `alignStyle` returns `undefined` for the default rather than `{textAlign:'left'}`, and the wrapper div is only rendered when it returns something - so a layout saved before the setting existed emits byte-identical markup with no extra element and no style attribute. Applied identically in the editor and RSC halves of all three. **product-checks-for-shop is deliberately NOT added to core modules.json.** It is live on Deskwell (pck_product_checks exists; the install pins it itself) but core has never pinned it, so every generator prints '[generate] ignoring 1 module dir(s) not in modules.json' and core's own build/router/puck registries do not include it. Pinning it would make core's build clone `usersaynoso/product-checks-for-shop`, which is PRIVATE and on the wrong org - every other shop module lives on `cactus-foundation-modules`. Moving the repo is a GitHub admin action and wiring a private cross-org repo into core's build could break the deploy, so it is Chris's call. The module itself was fixed and released regardless. NO schema change in any of these.)

Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, part five: both payment modules now check the money before fulfilling - `gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop` **v0.1.6** + `square-payment-for-shop` **v0.1.6**, pinned by core **v0.5.1071**.** **A3, the important one.** Each module has TWO settlement paths and the amount check was on the wrong one. `provider.confirmPayment` (reached from shop's /checkout/confirm) compared `payment.amount` against `toPence(order.amount)` and refused a mismatch. `lib/settle.ts` `settleFromPayment` - reached from BOTH the webhook and the redirect-return route, i.e. how most payments actually settle - called `markOrderPaid` + `fulfillPaidOrder` on `isPaymentCollected(status)` alone, never looking at the money. New exported `paymentMatchesOrder(payment, order)` in each module's settle.ts, comparing minor units and currency (case-insensitive), now applied before anything is marked paid. A collected payment that does NOT match is left unfulfilled and console.error'd - deliberately neither PAID (ships goods against money never charged) nor FAILED (the money HAS been taken; saying otherwise is its own wrong). Note it reads `order.total`, not `order.amount` - `getOrderById` returns the row, and the `ShpOrderDraft` shape confirmPayment uses is a different thing. **A4, GoCardless only.** Its webhook caught every event so one poison event could not fail the batch (correct - GoCardless retries the whole batch and the handlers are idempotent) but then returned 200 regardless, telling GoCardless the batch was handled. A transient DB failure while settling was the last anyone heard of that payment: order stuck AWAITING_CONFIRMATION, shopper's money gone. Failures are now counted and the response is 500, matching what Square's webhook already did. New **lib/settle.test.ts** in both modules (9 each) - neither had any tests. NEITHER MODULE IS ENABLED ON DESKWELL (`enabledPaymentMethods: ['BANK_TRANSFER']`), so nothing live is affected; live payment config was not touched. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, part four: dead variant choices need not lead the row - `shop-variations` **v0.1.142**, pinned by core **v0.5.1070**.** **B6.** `OptionControl` drew `option.values` in stored order, so whichever value came first led the row whether or not it could be picked - the Prism chair opens its Headrest row with a struck-through 'With Headrest - Out of Stock' above the one in stock. Page reset on filter change done during RENDER via pageResetKey/lastResetKey, not an effect. **The no-attributes early-return branch pages too** - it renders the same grid and its products were just as unreachable. `attributePageNumbers` is a deliberate LOCAL copy of the window helper, not an import from filters-for-shop or shop - module-to-module isolation. Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, part two: the filtered grid can page - `filters-for-shop` **v0.1.15**, pinned by core **v0.5.1068**.** This is the block every Deskwell category layout actually uses, so this is where the unreachable-products fault really bit: `ShopFilterGridRsc` fetched `perPage: props.limit ?? 24` against shop's old flat 100 clamp and rendered the lot, so Office Chairs (217 rolled up) drew 100 cards and 117 products were reachable from nowhere. **New props** on `ShopFilterGrid`: `paginate` ('none'|'more'|'pages', default 'none'), `pageSize`, `moreLabel`. At 'none' the RSC half fetches `limit` with the default ceiling and passes `paginate='none'` to the shell, which returns from the paging effect before touching a thing - verified in the browser as 100 cards, all visible, no pager, no `data-flt-offpage`, same `shop-grid` class. Switched on it fetches to shop's `HARD_MAX_PER_PAGE` (`maxPerPage` too) and pages client-side. **The pager lives INSIDE FilterShell**, not wrapped around it: the set being paged is the FILTERED set, and a pager outside the shell would page the raw server list and let the filters punch holes in each page. It applies its window by walking `:scope > [data-flt-product]` and skipping anything already carrying `data-flt-hidden` (the filter pass's own marker), writing the same `display` property - the two never disagree because paging only ever hides cards filtering has already shown. **Effect order matters**: the paging effect is declared AFTER both the filter effect and the sort effect, because effects run in declaration order and the sort physically re-parents the card nodes; declared earlier it would window the pre-sort order. **Page reset on filter/sort change** is done during RENDER via a `pageResetKey` + `lastResetKey` pair (React's adjust-state-on-input-change pattern), not in an effect - an effect paints the wrong page then corrects it, and trips `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`, which is exactly what it did on the first attempt. Without the reset a shopper on page 7 who filters down to nine products lands on an empty grid. **`filterPageNumbers`** exported from FilterShell for the tests; deliberately a local copy of shop's window helper rather than an import, so the module owns its own UI. New **lib/pager.test.ts** pins the window arithmetic (217/24 covers every index exactly once; remainder on the last page; pageSize 0 survives). New CSS `.flt-pager*` in **components/public/filter-css.ts**, 44px targets, colour tokens only, only emitted when paging is on. **Verified against the real live grid** by replicating the effect's exact selector and slice over the 100 rendered cards: pages of 24, no overlap, every card reachable exactly once, 0 duplicates, 'show more' growing 24->48->100, DOM fully restored after. End-to-end with `paginate` actually set on a layout is NOT yet verified - that needs a write to `Layout.publishedData` on ~50 live rows, which is Chris's call. NO schema change.)

Previous entry: (**Pre-launch shop audit, part one: every product is reachable and delivery is taxed - `shop` **v0.1.226**, pinned by core **v0.5.1067**.** **Pagination.** `lib/db/products.ts` gains `maxPerPage` on `ListProductsFilter` plus exported `DEFAULT_MAX_PER_PAGE` (100, what every caller got before) and `HARD_MAX_PER_PAGE` (500). The old flat 100 clamp was serving two masters: a DoS guard on the unauthenticated public list, and a silent truncation on storefront grids whose page size comes from an owner-authored layout - Deskwell's Office Chairs rolls up 217 products and the page rendered 100 with no route to the rest. New client island **components/public/ShopGridPager.tsx** (exports `ShopGridPager`, plus pure `visibleRange`/`pageNumbers`, tested in **components/public/grid-pager.test.ts**) slices server-rendered cards into 'show more' or numbered pages - cards are never re-rendered client-side, so paging cannot drift from the Product Card layout. `ShopProductGrid` gains props `paginate` ('none'|'more'|'pages', default 'none'), `pageSize`, `moreLabel`, `countTemplate`; at 'none' the RSC half fetches and renders exactly as before, same `shop-grid` div and `--shop-cols`. `renderCards` in **lib/card-template.tsx** now declares `Promise<React.ReactNode[]>` (it always returned an array). The un-designed category page **app/public/shop/categories/[slug]/page.tsx** fetched `perPage: 60` with no pager; now fetches to `HARD_MAX_PER_PAGE` and pages at 60. **Shipping VAT.** `resolveOrderTotals` never taxed `shippingAmount` at all. New exported `shippingTaxRate`/`shippingTaxAmount` in **lib/checkout.ts** tax it at the value-weighted average rate of the taxable lines (UK apportionment; the goods' own rate on a single-rate shop, 0 on a zero-rated basket, 0 when delivery is free or absent - so no existing Deskwell order moves, it has no shipping rates). `OrderTotals` gains `goodsTaxAmount`; the checkout-session route passes THAT to `displayOrderTotals`, because the net/gross subtotal conversion must not divide by tax on a charge that sits below the subtotal. Tested in **lib/shipping-tax.test.ts**. `round2` is now exported and the payment-intent route rounds line unitPrice/taxAmount/total before writing. **Money display.** `formatMoney` groups thousands via `toLocaleString('en-GB', ...)` - locale pinned so the RSC and client passes cannot disagree and cause a hydration mismatch on every price. Tested in **lib/money.test.ts**. Not used by any CSV/export path. **Hardening.** Rate limits added to **app/api/public/orders/status/route.ts** (20/15min - order numbers are prefix+sequence, so the email was the whole lock) and **app/api/public/checkout/confirm/route.ts** (20/15min - cannot fake a payment, could walk order ids and fail other people's). `lib/rate-limit.ts` buckets now carry `expiresAt` and are swept every 512 writes instead of living forever. `components/public/cart.ts` `persist()` no longer throws out of `addToCart` when localStorage refuses writes (Safari private browsing, full quota); new module-level `memoryCart` that `getCart` prefers once the store has proved unwritable. `lib/robots.ts` disallows /shop/cart, /shop/checkout, /shop/account, /shop/downloads, /shop/orders on an open shop. **Admin.** **app/api/admin/reports/tax/route.ts** takes optional `from`/`to` (yyyy-mm-dd, `to` inclusive of the whole day) and nets refunds off per rate - refunded tax is derived from the original line's own tax_amount/total fraction because `shp_refund_items` has no tax column; CSV gains tax_refunded and tax_net columns. New **lib/contrast.ts** (`contrastRatio`, `meetsAaNormal`, `parseHex`, `AA_NORMAL_TEXT`, tested in **lib/contrast.test.ts**) drives a readability warning beside the existing badge preview in **components/admin/TagsScreen.tsx** - Deskwell's own New tag is #F2F1EE on #4DB3AC in dark mode, 2.2:1. Warns, never blocks. **Puck.** `Product: Price` gains `align` (default 'left', applied via the existing `textAlignStyle` which returns undefined for left, so no style attribute appears); `Product: Short description` had a declared `size` field with no entry in defaultProps; `ShopProductGrid.showFilters` has never been read by anything and is relabelled to say so - the prop stays because saved layouts reference it by name. NO schema change, so no migration and no backup round-trip gate.)

VAT` with the figure in the display face, and the variations block printed a bare 1.5rem number instead. **Three separate faults.** (1) The `ShopVariantPrice` block styled itself inline and never carried a struck-through was, a Save badge or an RRP; it now emits its own `.svr-price-*` CSS mirroring shop's `.spd-price-*` rules (display family, 34px, `--color-primary`, success-token pill) - copied rather than imported because shop only emits that CSS when ITS price part renders, which on a layout using the block it does not.
