Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Safari's toolbar takes the site's Theme colour, with the header looking exactly as it did - `lib/puck/config.tsx`, `app/layout.tsx`, `app/globals.css`, shipped as **v0.5.1064**. This un-reverts v0.5.1062 and adds the part that was missing.** Confirmed working in Chris's own Safari on a real page load before release, orange toolbar over an unchanged off-white header. **The documented Safari 26 precedence** (github.com/andesco/safari-color-tinting): a **fixed or sticky element with a `background-color`, within 4px of the top, >=90% wide on macOS and >=3px high, beats everything**; then `body`'s `background-color`; then `html`'s; then white/black by scheme. `<meta name="theme-color">` is parsed and ignored. **That single rule explains every symptom**: the composable header is sticky at `top: 0`, full width, 96px, with a background - so it qualifies and outranks the `body` colour v0.5.1062 set, which is exactly why **the admin tinted and the front end never did** (no qualifying sticky element in the admin, so it falls through to `body`). It also explains "dark mode does not tint": nothing special about dark, the dark header was simply being sampled. **Fix:** `headerRootRender` now puts `var(--cactus-theme-color, <the real background>)` on the header's own `background-color` and paints the real background on a full-bleed `position:absolute; inset:0` child sitting under the content, which gets `position:relative; z-index:1` to outrank it. Safari reads the property, the visitor sees the child. `inset:0` resolves against the **padding** box, so the header's own borders still paint and a shrink-on-scroll header's overlay follows the height for free (measured: overlay 1280x95 inside a 1280x96 header carrying a 1px bottom border). **Opt-outs:** `bgMode === 'color'` only - the two transparent header modes have nothing opaque to hide the tint behind, and a header that disqualifies itself just lets Safari fall through to `body`, which carries the same colour anyway - plus an explicit `rgba()`/`hsla()` background, which would let the tint leak through the overlay. Unset Theme colour makes the `var()` fall back to the real background, so the element is byte-identical to before. `app/layout.tsx` and `app/globals.css` are v0.5.1062 restored verbatim (`--cactus-theme-color` on `<html>` from the `cache()`d `resolveBranding()`; `body` split into `background-color` = the tint plus a flat `linear-gradient` of the page colour; `html` painted so `body`'s background cannot propagate to the canvas and tint the overscroll band). **The `body` longhands must never be collapsed into the `background` shorthand** - that resets the image and paints the Theme colour across every page. **Method, the expensive lesson of this session:** every console test we ran was worthless - **Safari works the tint out at page load and does not re-evaluate on a JS style mutation**, so four separate "that didn't work" results (`html` transparent, `body` gradient removed, an 8px orange `border-top`, an orange header background) were all false negatives, one of which triggered an unnecessary revert. Test by loading a real page. Two throwaway static pages served over `http://localhost:8787` settled it in one go. Checks: `npm run typecheck` + `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger, nothing written to any database. Legacy all-in-one `SiteHeaderBlock` deliberately untouched - different block, and it is not the header any public Deskwell page renders. `package-lock.json` was left at 0.5.1062 by the v0.5.1063 release; this bump squares it up. Wiki: `Appearance-and-design.md` - the Safari note now says it works, and why a see-through header opts out.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**REVERTED v0.5.1062: Safari's toolbar tint is not reachable from the page at all, and the theory that shipped it was wrong - `app/layout.tsx`, `app/globals.css` restored to their pre-1062 state, working tree, version bump and release still pending.** v0.5.1062 (below) shipped on the belief that Safari 26 derives its toolbar colour from `body`'s `background-color`, so `body` carried the Theme colour while a `linear-gradient` painted the page colour over it. **It does not work, and it was disproved on the live site with no deploys, in Safari's own console.** With the code live and `body` computing `rgb(227, 168, 87)`, Chris ran, in order: `html` background to `transparent` (no change), `body` `background-image: none` so the page itself rendered orange edge to edge (no change), an `8px solid #E3A857` `border-top` on `header[data-header-root]` (no change), and finally the header's whole `background` to `#E3A857` (no change). Toolbar stayed Safari's default dark throughout. **So the tint reads neither `body`, nor `html`, nor the topmost element's background, nor the painted pixels at the top of the page** - every mechanism the fix could have used is ruled out by experiment. Contributing factor, unconfirmed: his tab bar was in Safari's **Separate** layout, and the tinting has historically only applied in **Compact** (the preference is literally worded "Show colour in compact tab bar"), so the window may simply never have been tinting regardless of the page. **What the reverted commit leaves behind if kept, and the reason to revert rather than let it sit:** `body` was split into `background-color` (the tint) plus `background-image` (a flat gradient of the real page colour), and the pair is only safe together - anyone collapsing them back to the `background` shorthand, the obvious tidy-up, resets the image and paints the Theme colour across every page on the site. A booby trap with no upside once the trick is known not to work. The `html { background-color }` line added alongside it goes too: it existed solely to stop `body`'s tint propagating to the canvas. `<meta name="theme-color">` and `generateViewport()` are untouched and were never the problem - the tag still drives Chrome on Android, Safari before 26, and the installed-app theme via `app/manifest.ts`. **Method note for next time: the console tests above cost nothing and would have settled this before the release, not after it.** Wiki: `Appearance-and-design.md` - the Theme colour bullet drops the Safari claim and the "note on Safari" paragraph now says plainly that Safari ignores the setting and nothing in Cactus changes that. **Version files deliberately untouched**: another session holds `package.json` at 0.5.1063 uncommitted (lock still 1062) mid-release, so this revert commits without a bump and the release is cut once that clears.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Safari 26 gets the site's Theme colour as its toolbar tint again, without changing a rendered pixel - `app/layout.tsx`, `app/globals.css`, shipped as **v0.5.1062**.** Chris: the Theme colour was doing nothing in Safari - first teal, then `#E3A857`, neither tinted anything - and the white toolbar strip above the header's new top border was what he had originally reported as "a few pixels above the top border". **Cause: Safari 26 no longer reads `<meta name="theme-color"`>.** It still parses the tag and then ignores it, deriving the browser-UI colour from **`body`'s `background-color`**, falling back to `html`'s, defaulting white/black. Safari 15-25 did honour the tag, media attribute and all. Deskwell's `body` is `var(--color-page-bg)` = `#FFFFFF` light / `#16181A` dark, i.e. near-white and near-black, which is why the toolbar looked untinted rather than wrong. Proven in-browser before touching anything: the page was serving `<meta name="theme-color" content="#E3A857">` correctly, and the header measured flush at `top: 0` with nothing above it in the DOM - `elementsFromPoint` returned `HEADER` at y=0..8, every preceding sibling `display:none` - so the "gap" was never page. **Fix, CSS only, no wrapper element:** `body` carries `background-color: var(--cactus-theme-color, …)` for Safari to sample and `background-image: linear-gradient(<page bg>, <page bg>)` painted over it, so the *property* is the theme colour while the *pixels* are the page colour exactly as before. **The two must stay longhands** - the `background` shorthand resets the image and leaks the tint across every page. `--cactus-theme-color` is published as an inline custom property on `<html>` from `RootLayout` via `resolveBranding()`, which is `cache()`d, so it shares the query `generateMetadata`/`generateViewport` already make; unset, the `var()` fallback is the old single page colour, so a site that never set a Theme colour renders byte-identically. **`html` gains `background-color: var(--color-page-bg, var(--color-bg))`** and that is not cosmetic: without it `body`'s background propagates to the canvas (html had no background of its own - measured `rgba(0, 0, 0, 0)`), and the tint would paint the overscroll band and any page shorter than the viewport. Verified on the 404 page, body 275px in an 800px viewport: the strip below the body box resolves to `HTML` at `rgb(19, 18, 16)`, not orange. Verified both themes on the homepage: `body` computes `rgb(227, 168, 87)` in each while the gradient renders `rgb(255,255,255)` / `rgb(22,24,26)`, screenshots identical to before the change. Considered and rejected: a full-height wrapper div inside `body` - same trick, but it restructures the DOM on every route including admin, and a sticky header plus `min-height` chains are not worth the risk for a toolbar tint. Checks: `npm run typecheck` + `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger, nothing written to any database. Wiki: `Appearance-and-design.md` - the Theme colour bullet now mentions Safari on a Mac, plus a short "A note on Safari" paragraph. Note the tag is still emitted and still matters for Chrome on Android, Safari before 26, and the installed-app theme via `app/manifest.ts`.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**A product card printed one tag badge however many it had earned - `modules/shop/lib/card-template.tsx`, `components/puck/parts/part-context.ts`, `components/puck/parts/card-parts.tsx`, module working tree only, unreleased.** Chris, on `deskwell.co.uk/shop/categories/office-chairs`: the cards show a single badge in the top-left of the photo where the product carries several badge-bearing tags. By design until now - `badgeFor()` was a precedence chain returning `CardBadge | null` and took `owned[0]`, the lowest-`position` tag, dropping the rest. The product PAGE has printed the lot since `shop` 0.1.214 (`DetailPartContext.tagBadges` + `ShopDetailBadgesRsc`), so the grid and the page it leads to disagreed. **Fix:** `badgeFor` becomes `badgesFor` returning `CardBadge[]` in print order - Out of stock / Pre-order first (a shopper needs those before "Bestseller"), then every owner tag badge in admin order, then the built-in `new` / low stock / `trade`, with the same stand-down rule the page uses (`ownedSlugs.has('new'|'trade')`, so a tag whose slug is one of those and which carries its own badge does not also print the hardcoded one). `CardPartContext` gains `badges: CardBadge[]`; **`badge` stays** as `badges[0] ?? null` so a companion module's card surface built against the old shape keeps compiling, and `ShopCardBadge` falls back to it when a not-yet-rebuilt surface supplies no `badges`. Each kind still answers to its own switch on the part (`showNew`/`showLow`/`showTrade`/`showTag`/`showMuted`) - the filter now runs per badge rather than on the single winner. **Markup:** the part root is a new `span.shop-card-badges` and the badges are its children, because four absolutely-positioned `.shop-card-badge`s would sit on top of each other. The stack carries the `position:absolute !important` (the editor sets `position:relative` inline on every part root, so it has to outrank that - same reason as before, moved up a level), `top/left:10px`, `z-index:3`, `display:flex;flex-direction:column;align-items:flex-start;gap:4px` and `max-width:calc(100% - 20px)`; `.shop-card-badge` keeps the pill look and loses its own positioning. Per-tag colours still ride in as `--shop-tag-*` inline on each badge, so a stack of owner-coloured badges is still one server render for both themes. No Puck layout edits and no data change: the part's props are untouched and an absent toggle still reads as on. Editor path and RSC path are the same component, so the canvas skeleton (one sample "New") and the live card build identical markup. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger, nothing written to the live database, no version bumped. Wiki: `Shop.md` - the tags section no longer says "a product card only ever wears one badge", and the product-grid paragraph says a product wearing several shows all of them. **Follow-up, working tree, unreleased:** Chris wanted them side by side rather than one under the other, so `.shop-card-badges` drops `flex-direction:column` for the default row plus `flex-wrap:wrap` - the existing `max-width:calc(100% - 20px)` is what makes the wrap land inside the card rather than running the row off a narrow column. CSS only; no markup, prop or context change.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Every live product page and the checkout lost their whole two-column half - retiring `Split` from the pickers unregistered it from every module layout. `lib/puck/config.tsx` + new `lib/puck/module-layout-blocks.test.ts`, working tree only.** Chris, on `deskwell.co.uk/shop/products/brixworth-uk-crafted-soft-seating-reception-armchair`: the product image, the 3D model, the buy area and the add-ons had all disappeared. True of every product page - `main` opened straight at the tabs nav, whose "Configure" link pointed at an `#spd-buy` that was not in the document, and the page carried on into Description, Specification, Downloads, Reviews and related products as if nothing were missing. 200, correct `<title>`, correct JSON-LD (quoting `price: "0.00"`, since the price part never rendered either), two 401s from `product-checks-for-shop`'s admin endpoints that are just a logged-out visitor and not the fault. **Cause, and it is the previous entry's own fix.** v0.5.1053 retired `Split` by dropping the name from `categories.layout.components` in `puckConfig`, `footerPuckConfig` and `layoutPuckConfig`, on the understanding that a category list is only a picker. It is - except in `getModuleLayoutSharedParts()` (`lib/puck/config.tsx:4379`), the one place in the file that builds a **component set** from the category lists rather than from `puckConfig.components`: `MODULE_LAYOUT_CATEGORY_KEYS.flatMap(k => puckConfig.categories[k].components).map(name => [name, puckConfig.components[name]])`. Both `getModuleLayoutPuckConfig` and its RSC twin in `lib/puck/config.rsc.tsx` spread that set, so removing the name from the picker **unregistered the block** from every module-declared layout type, and Puck renders precisely nothing for a type its config has never heard of - not the empty two divs of the gazette bug, no wrapper at all. `starter-shop-detail-default-live`'s `Split` (`pdp-cols`, top level in `content`, zones `pdp-cols:left`/`:right`) took the gallery, badges, title, SKU, price, blurb, pre-order, variation options, variant price, shipping options, add to cart and `ShopProductAddons` down with it. `starter-shop-checkout-classic-live` holds a `Split` too. Live since the owner's **v0.5.1054** update at 08:18 this morning; **v0.5.1050** at 07:18 was the last good deploy. **Fix:** a `RETIRED_BLOCKS = ['Split', 'Grid']` constant added back into `sharedComponents` (and only there - not into `sharedCategories`, so neither returns to a picker), with the derivation filtered so a name with no component behind it is skipped rather than seeding an `undefined` entry. `Grid`, the dynamic predecessor of Grid2/3/4, had been silently in the same state since its own retirement and is restored by the same line. Verified on a local dev server against the live database: the product page renders `id="spd-buy"`, 12 `spd-gallery`, 6 `spd-add`, 18 `puck-split` and `ShopProductAddons`, none of which appear in the live HTML. **New regression test**, `lib/puck/module-layout-blocks.test.ts`: walks every starter in `lib/setup/module-starter-layouts.ts` for the block types it uses and asserts each **core** one is registered in that layout type's config, plus that Split and Grid specifically still are. Core-owned is `puckConfig.components` minus `moduleComponents` - `puckConfig` carries the module blocks too, and which layout types a module block is offered on is its own manifest's `layoutTypes` to answer, not core's. Emptying `RETIRED_BLOCKS` fails it 15 ways across boards, directory, gazette, quotes, search and shop, which is the real blast radius: 13 of the 19 module layout types ship a `Split` in their starters. Two genuine gaps it found and did **not** fix, both module-side and both with zero live effect on Deskwell (no published layout uses either): shop's `ShopPromoBanner` misses `shopCategory`/`shopCollection` and `ShopUpsellProducts` misses `shopConfirmation` in `modules/shop/cactus.module.json`, so those starters' banners would render as nothing if anyone seeded them. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `lib/puck` 48/48. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. Nothing written to the live database. Wiki: `Architecture-overview.md`'s retired-Split row gains the caveat that dropping a name from a picker also unregisters it from module layouts, plus the `RETIRED_BLOCKS` rule and the test that holds it; `Managing-pages.md` needs nothing - what it tells owners ("Splits already sitting directly on a page or layout carry on working") is true again.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**A Push could no longer add a product tab: "This action would increase the number of cells in the workbook above the limit of 10000000 cells" - `google-sheet-products-for-shop` **0.1.57**, module working tree only, unreleased, `modules.json` NOT touched.** Chris hit it mid-Push on Deskwell, at `requests[45].addSheet`. **Not a data problem - blank grid.** Google counts every cell of every tab in a spreadsheet, full or empty, and caps one workbook at ten million. `createVariationTabsBatch` fired `addSheet` with no `gridProperties`, so each of the 349 product tabs got Google's default 1000 rows, and `headerFormattingRequests` then set column widths out to `endIndex: 45` - a dimension request past the last column GROWS the sheet to reach it, so every tab was 1000x45 = 45,000 cells to hold an average of 60 variants. Live figures (read-only): 21,399 products, 349 of them variable, 20,954 variants, max 588 on one product. Real content is ~21,300 rows across every product tab; the workbook was ~94% padding. **Three fixes, all in the module.** (1) **New tabs are created at the size they need** - `addSheet` now carries `gridProperties` from `targetRows`/`targetColumns` (content + 50 rows / + 5 columns, floors 100 x 26), and every `headerFormattingRequests` caller passes the tab's own width so the width request is clamped and can never re-inflate it. (2) **A pushed tab is trimmed to what it uses** - new `resizeRequests` in `lib/push-grid.ts`, appended to the same atomic structural `batchUpdate` as the column inserts and row deletes. This is the only place that can trim safely: the batched pre-read has just returned the tab's REAL used extent, **the owner's own columns and rows included** (values.get returns everything anyone put there, not only what we wrote), so their work is inside the target. Shrink only, never grow, and the current size is adjusted for the inserts/deletes queued ahead of it in the same batch since `getSheetGrids` was read before them. (3) **A capacity pre-flight** - new pure `lib/capacity.ts` (`planCapacity`, `CELL_BUDGET` 9M against Google's 10M ceiling). Before any tab is created the VARIATION_TABS phase projects the whole phase's new tabs against the workbook; a sheet with room spends nothing, a sheet without gets a rows-only reclaim across the tabs this module owns first (`reclaimRowTarget`, content + 200 rows, floor 250 - **rows only, deliberately**: the reclaim has not read those tabs, so it cannot know where the owner's columns end and must not guess), and only if it **still** does not fit does it stop with `workbookFullMessage()` - one plain sentence, no cell counts, naming the two things that actually make room. (4) Fell out of the same audit: `productsValidationRequests` hard-coded `endRowIndex: 5000`, which on a short Products tab grew the grid to 5,000 rows to meet it and would have undone the trim; it now takes the tab's own `rowCount` (`applyProductsValidation` reads it via the new `getSheetGrids`). `getSheetIds` is unchanged and still used by the orphan sweep and the Pull. Projected effect on Deskwell: ~9.6M cells down to under 1.5M once every tab has been through a Push. **No rebuild of the sheet is needed** - the trim runs on the existing tabs in place, keeping formulas, owner columns and row order. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest **181 pass / 0 fail** including new `lib/capacity.test.ts` (14 cases pinning the sizing, the reclaim, the give-up, and that a trim never eats the owner's columns or grows a tab). No schema, no migration, no dev server. Read me tab gained an "IF THE SHEET SAYS IT HAS RUN OUT OF ROOM" section; `wiki/Google-Sheet-Products.md` updated (tab-per-product section).)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**A header layout's border can be on the top edge, the bottom, both, or neither - `lib/puck/BorderField.tsx`, `lib/puck/config.tsx`, shipped as **v0.5.1058**.** Chris: the header layout's page settings **Border bottom** needs to offer border bottom, border top, no border, or top and bottom. `BorderFieldValue.show` was `'show' | 'hide'` and every consumer read `show === 'show'`; it is now `'show' | 'hide' | 'top' | 'both'`. **`'show'` keeps meaning "the one edge this field was always about"** - bottom on a header, top on the footer - so every layout saved before this renders byte-identically and no data migration exists or is needed. The four-way choice is **opt-in per field** via a new `sides: true` key read as `(field as { sides?: boolean }).sides`, because `BorderField` also backs `footerPuckConfig.root.fields.border` (labelled "Border top") and the legacy all-in-one `SiteHeaderBlock`'s field (labelled "Border bottom") - both of those render a single hardcoded edge, so a four-way picker there would offer settings that do nothing. Only `headerPuckConfig.root.fields.border` sets it, and its label drops from "Border bottom" to plain **"Border"**. Options are Bottom only / Top only / Top and bottom / No border. The colour swatch rows are unchanged and still gate on `show !== 'hide'`, so they stay visible for `top` and `both` and the existing `light-dark()` dark-mode arm applies to whichever edges are on. `headerRootRender` derives `borderTop`/`borderBottom` from one `borderLine` string rather than the old single inline ternary, and **the header element gains `boxSizing: 'border-box'`**: it carries an explicit pixel height, so without that a top border would add 1px and shove a sticky header's content down - and `--cactus-header-offset` is published from that same declared height, so a grown header would leave sticky grid columns 1px short. Single render path checked: `grep "show === 'show'"` finds only the three consumers above, and `data-header-root` is emitted only by `headerRootRender`, which serves both the builder preview and the live page. `npm run typecheck` + `eslint .` clean, re-run against 41981f0 (the v0.5.1057 blank-product-page fix) before the cut, since that fix landed in the same `lib/puck/config.tsx` while this work was held unstaged in the tree - its hunks are elsewhere in the file and the two do not overlap. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. **Deskwell's own header is untouched** - its saved props have no `show: 'top'`, so it keeps its bottom line until the owner picks otherwise in Appearance > Layouts. Wiki: `Appearance-and-design.md` gains a **Border** paragraph beside the Height and Side padding ones.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**The media page's storage check can no longer offer a file the site is using as a "leftover" - `lib/media/reconcile.ts`, `app/api/admin/media/storage-check/route.ts`, `app/cactus-admin/media/MediaStorageCheck.tsx`, working tree only.** Chris asked whether Deskwell's 1,127 leftovers were safe to delete. They were not: **717 of them were live**. "Leftover" only ever meant *storage object with no `Media` row*, and `getMediaReferencesBulk` can only reference-check **by `Media.id`**, so an object with no row got no reference check at all - while the UI's one button posts the whole list. Proven read-only against the live database: 36,644 objects under `media/` vs 35,517 rows (0 missing), and regexing every text/varchar/jsonb column in the public schema for `media/...` found 717 of the 1,127 referenced - 661 by `p3d_models.url`, 574 by `p3d_models.media_key`, 550 inside `p3d_fabric_configs.config`, 52 by `shp_product_media.url` (52 real products). Cause: bulk 3D attach and some bulk image writes insert a url with **no `Media` row** (16,124 of 16,147 `p3d_models` rows have no matching `Media.key`). **Fix:** `reconcileMediaStorage` now builds a claim test once per scan (`buildClaimTest`) from `loadMediaUsageIndex()` - the same index the Unused tile uses, so every module's `core.media-usage-providers` contribution counts - and `diffStorageAgainstRows` takes it as an optional `isClaimed(key)` predicate, filing a rowless-but-referenced object under a new `claimed`/`claimedBytes` bucket instead of `orphaned`. `extractReferencedKeys` pulls keys out of the haystack into a `Set` (regex `media/[^\s"'\\)>,\]}|]+`, query string stripped, raw + decoded form both kept) because `haystack.includes()` per object over a multi-MB string across 36k objects does not finish. Degraded index, or one that throws, claims everything - no leftovers reported rather than a guess, the same direction `isMediaInUse` already leans. The delete route needed no new guard: it re-derives `orphaned` server-side, so a stale page asking for a claimed key is simply skipped. The media page grows a fourth, button-less group, "In use, but with no entry here". Five new unit tests on the predicate plus five on `extractReferencedKeys` (17 in the file, `lib/media` suite 143 pass); `npm run typecheck` + `eslint .` clean. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. **Separately, at Chris's ask, the live Deskwell database was written to**: 717 `Media` rows + 193 `Folder` rows created for the in-use files (folder resolved from an existing sibling in the same key directory, since this site's folder tree and key paths have drifted; 170 of the new folders are `3d` children of existing product folders), so the leftover count is now 410 (42.5 MB) and genuinely spare. Rollback SQL at `~/Desktop/deskwell-media-registration-rollback.sql`.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Puck grids: a sticky column stopped losing its top edge under the site header, and an over-tall one now scrolls itself - `lib/puck/config.tsx`, working tree only.** Chris: a sticky column should still scroll when its contents are too tall for the page; and on `deskwell.co.uk/gazette` (and a post page) the pinned column's top was being cut off while scrolling. Both faults live in `GridBlock`'s per-column sticky style. **(1) The cut-off top is the header.** `col{n}Sticky:'on'` emitted `top: col{n}StickyOffset || '0px'`, so with the offset left blank the track pinned to viewport y=0 - underneath Deskwell's 96px `position:sticky` header (z-index 100), which paints over its first 96px for good. Measured on the live page before the change: `top:0px`, pinned rect top 0, header height 96. `headerRootRender` now publishes its own height as `:root{--cactus-header-offset:<height>}` (desktop inline in a `<style>`, tablet/mobile through `responsiveMediaCssFor(':root', ...)`), **only when `sticky === 'yes'`** - a static header has nothing to clear - with `'auto'` height falling back to the 48px floor the header itself uses, since a content height isn't knowable at render. A sticky column left on the default blank offset uses `top: var(--cactus-header-offset, 0px)`; the fallback keeps every headerless surface (footer, layout previews, a page whose header doesn't stick) at 0px exactly as before. **An author-set offset is still taken literally** - `/^0[a-z%]*$/i` treats `0`/`0px` as blank, anything else wins outright - because an owner who already typed 96px to clear the header would otherwise get 192px and a column shoved down the page. **(2) Over-tall columns.** `align-self:start` keeps the box content-height, so a column taller than the viewport pinned its top and stranded everything below the fold permanently unreachable: the page scroll has stopped moving it and the column had no scroll of its own. Now `max-height: calc(100vh - <that same top value>)` + `overflow-y:auto`, so it caps at the visible band and scrolls internally only when it actually overflows. Note this makes a sticky column a scroll container whether or not it overflows, so an absolutely-positioned child (a dropdown) would be clipped by it - only reachable on a column explicitly set sticky, and header nav sits in a header, not a sticky page column. The stack-mode media rules that already drop `data-col-sticky` back to `position:static` now also reset `max-height:none;overflow:visible`, so a stacked phone column is byte-identical to before. Proven on the live `deskwell.co.uk` DOM by injecting the exact emitted CSS (no deploy): pinned rect top moved 0 -> 96, and at a 500px-tall viewport the 604px column reported `scrollHeight 604 / clientHeight 404` and scrolled to its own bottom. `npm run typecheck` + `eslint` clean; no schema, no new field, no release.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Gazette: options on the Category Header block (custom heading text among them) and two more on the Entry List (image shape, card hover) - `modules/gazette` working tree, unreleased, riding the same 0.1.17/0.1.18 tree as the filter-block work below; core untouched bar docs.** Chris: the Category Header anchor needs options including one to change the heading text; and the Entry List needs an image ratio (Deskwell wants 1:1) plus a hover that grows the card like the shop's product cards on a category page. **Category Header** (`components/puck/GazetteCategoryHeaderBlock.tsx`, one file serving both halves - it has no server-only imports, hence the manifest's `rscImport` pointing at itself) had `fields: {}`. Now nine: `headingText`, `level` (h1|h2|h3), `size` (theme|sm|md|lg|xl), `eyebrow`, `align`, `showDescription`, `descriptionText`, `divider`, `spaceBelow`. **`headingText`/`descriptionText`, never `heading`/`description`**: the block is in `CATEGORY_CONTEXT_BLOCKS` and `injectCategoryContext` `Object.assign`s the context over its props, so a field named after a context key is overwritten at render - the same trap the filter blocks' `title` field dodges. **`{title}` in either box is replaced with whatever the page injected** (`resolveHeaderText`), because one Listing layout serves index/tag/series/author/archive and a fixed string would otherwise flatten five different headings into one; blank keeps the injected wording exactly as before. Level and size are separate knobs on purpose - a listing wanting a modest H1 shouldn't have to demote itself to an H2 to get one. `undefined` reads as the old behaviour throughout (h1, theme size, description on, no rule, no extra space); `divider` is the one opt-in, checked as `=== 'true'` rather than through the default-ON `shows()` helper. The block used to `return null` with no injected heading; it now renders whenever any of heading/description/eyebrow has something in it, which only matters where nothing is injected. Editor half renders **the same markup as the live one** with stand-in wording ("Page heading", "The page's own description") at 0.6 opacity, rather than the old grey bars - bars can't show what nine options do. `resolveFields` drops the description wording when the description is off. **Entry List** gains `imageRatio` (16-9|3-2|4-3|1-1|auto, default 16-9 = what every card was) and `cardHover` (none|lift|grow, `defaultProps: 'lift'` for newly added blocks, `undefined` = none so saved layouts don't start moving on update). Both are grid-level, so they ride as `data-ratio`/`data-hover` on `.gz-post-grid` beside the existing `data-cols`, with the rules in `GazetteStyles.tsx`: **`lift` is the shop's exact effect** - `translateY(-4px)` + `var(--shadow-lg)` + `scale(1.03)` on the picture (cf. `.shop-card:hover` in `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/card-parts.tsx`) - `grow` is `scale(1.02)` on the whole card, and a `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` block kills both transitions and transforms. Shadow is the core token, not the shop's raw rgba. Transitions hang off `[data-hover]` rather than `.gz-post-card`, so a listing left on "Nothing" has nothing to run. `PostCardGrid`/`PostListLoadMore` take the two as optional props and pass them through, so an appended page hovers like a rendered one; the six hardcoded listing pages call `PostGrid` without them and are unchanged. `resolveFields` drops the image shape when the image is off, and the "Load more" label for **Numbered pages/None only** - infinite scroll renders that button too. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger, no core code touched. Not verified in a browser: gazette changes only reach a site through a module release and the owner's update button, and there is no local dev server. **Nothing committed, no version bump, `modules.json` not repinned** - another agent holds `cactus.module.json`/`package.json` for the next cut and these blocks ride along with it. **Deskwell's existing listing layout will not pick up the square pictures or the hover on its own**: its saved block props predate both fields, so the owner picks them in Appearance > Layouts once the release lands. Wiki: `Gazette.md` gains a Category Header settings table and two rows on the Entry List one.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Gazette: three listing filter blocks (series/author/tag) and a proper options panel on the Entry List block - shipped as `gazette` **0.1.19**, pinned by core **v0.5.1054**.** Chris: the listing needs blocks to filter posts by series, author and tags, and the Entry List anchor needs options - posts per page, pages vs infinite scroll, and so on. **Filters.** Three new removable `gazetteCategory` blocks, each an editor half plus a `.rsc` half over one shared `components/puck/filterBlockShared.tsx` (fields, chip building, editor preview) and a presentational `components/public/FilterChips.tsx`. Seven fields each: `title` (blank hides the heading), `variant` Pills|List, `sortBy` Name|Count, `limit` (0 = all), `showCounts`, `showAll`, `allLabel`. **The heading field is `title`, not `heading`, on purpose**: all three are in `CATEGORY_CONTEXT_BLOCKS` and `injectCategoryContext` does `Object.assign(block.props, ctx)`, so any field sharing a name with a context key (`heading`, `description`, `page`, `baseUrl`, `year`, `month`) would be silently overwritten at render. **Chips link to `/gazette?series=&author=&tag=`, never to the single-filter routes** - `/gazette/tag/<slug>` pins exactly one dimension, so linking there would quietly drop whatever else the visitor had picked; `lib/filter-links.ts` (client-safe, no prisma) writes the params in fixed order so one filter set is one URL rather than six. The index page parses them, resolves `author` username → id (unknown username drops the filter rather than 404ing), passes all three to `getVisiblePosts` - which already ANDed them, no query change - and folds the query string into `baseUrl`, so `Pagination` and the injected context carry the filters to page 2. `generateMetadata` returns `robots: { index: false, follow: true }` when any filter is on: the canonical single-filter routes are already indexed and the combinations multiply. Counts come from three new `lib/db.ts` helpers that count **visible** posts (the existing `getTagsWithCounts`/`listSeries` include drafts and private posts, which would have a chip promise nine and deliver two) and drop anything at zero, so no chip leads to an empty page. A trimmed list still keeps whatever is currently selected. Editor preview renders real chip markup with stand-in labels and `href="#"` - a live href would sail the builder's preview frame off to the listing on a stray click. Blocks render `null` when there is nothing to filter by, as `GazetteFeatured` does on an empty blog. **Entry List.** Was `fields: {}`. Now `perPage` (0 = the `posts_per_page` setting, 48 ceiling), `paging` (Numbered pages | Load more | Infinite scroll | None), `loadMoreLabel`, `sortBy` (Newest|Oldest|Most viewed|A to Z - pinned posts stay on top whichever, via a new `sort` option on `getVisiblePosts`), `columns` (Auto|1-4), and six display toggles (`showImage`, `showExcerpt`, `showAuthor`, `showDate`, `showComments`, plus `showViews` as auto|yes|no where auto follows `settings.showViewCounts`). **Every default is read as `?? default` / `!== 'no'` so a stored `props: { id: 'list-1' }` renders exactly as it did before** - Puck does not apply `defaultProps` to data saved before a field existed, and Deskwell's listing layout holds nothing else. Load more and infinite scroll needed a client half: `PostGrid` split into `lib/post-cards.ts` (`toPostCards`, the media/author/comment-count lookups, **and the date formatted server-side** - the browser's timezone is not the server's and a hydrating card would otherwise show a different day), presentational `PostCardGrid`, and `PostListLoadMore` (`'use client'`), fed by the new `GET /api/m/gazette/public/posts`. `PostCard` now takes the flat `GazettePostCard` + `PostCardDisplay`; `PostGrid` keeps its old `posts`/`showViewCounts` signature so the six hardcoded listing pages and `RelatedPosts` are untouched. Infinite scroll keeps its button (keyboards, and browsers without `IntersectionObserver`) and stops observing after a failed fetch rather than hammering away; appended pages are de-duped by id, since a post published mid-scroll shifts the window. Pinned columns collapse to one on a phone (`.gz-post-grid[data-cols]` + two media queries). Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger, no core code touched. Not verified in a browser: gazette changes only reach a site through a module release and the owner's update button, and there is no local dev server. **Released at Chris's ask as `gazette` v0.1.19** (0.1.17 and 0.1.18 went out from a parallel agent in the same tree while this was being written, so the filter work took the next number), pinned in core `modules.json` by **v0.5.1054**. That release also carries the parallel agent's Category Header options and the Entry List's image-shape/hover settings: they were written into the same files in the same working tree and could not be separated out, and both were green on the same checks. Wiki: `Gazette.md` gains an Entry List settings table and a "Letting visitors filter the listing" section.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Gazette: the Entry Header block gets options (image on/off among them) and the Table of Contents block stops floating - `modules/gazette`, module working tree only, unreleased.** Chris, straight after the blank-post fix below: the Entry Header block needs options, including show/hide the image; and the Table of Contents block needs to sit above Series Navigation properly. **Entry Header** (`components/puck/GazetteEntryHeaderBlock.tsx` + `.rsc.tsx`) had `fields: {}` - it drew image, headline and meta line with nothing to say about any of it. Editor preview honours `showImage`/`imageRatio`/`imageRadius`/`align` and the number of meta chips so the panel gives feedback. **Table of Contents** (`components/public/TableOfContents.tsx`): its desktop rule was `position: sticky; float: right; width: 200px; margin-left: 2rem`, which is right for the built-in post page it was written for - the article wraps around it - and wrong the moment it became a block in a column of its own. On Deskwell it floated out of the 30% sidebar and the `.gz-series-nav` card underneath wrapped its text around it **one character per line** ("P/a/r/t/3/of/3"). New `variant?: 'float' | 'flow'` prop, **default `'float'` so the built-in page at `app/public/gazette/[slug]/page.tsx` is byte-identical**; the Puck block passes `variant="flow"`, which is `position: static`, no float, no fixed width, full column width, plus a `Contents` heading above the links (a bare link list in a sidebar had nothing naming it). One `<style>` block, variants split on a `data-toc-variant` attribute selector rather than two class names. Deliberately NOT sticky in flow mode: a sticky first child in a column overlaps the siblings below it as it travels - core's Grid `col{n}Sticky` pins the whole column, which is the setting that actually wants using. No schema change, no core change, no manifest change (no new block types). **Version deliberately not bumped**: another agent is mid-flight in this module on Gazette*Filter blocks (author/series/tag + `FilterChips` + `lib/filter-links.ts`), has already cut `v0.1.17` and holds `cactus.module.json`/`package.json` for the next release - these two blocks ride along with whatever they cut. Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Every Gazette post published a blank body - a Split inside a Section renders nothing on the server. Live layout row repaired; `Split` retired in `lib/puck/config.tsx`, working tree only.** Chris: gazette posts are failing to show anything. True of every post, not one: `/gazette/<slug>` returned 200 with the right `<title>`, the header and footer, and **nothing between them** - while `/gazette` listed all fourteen posts with their excerpts, so the data and the queries were never in question. The published HTML said it outright: `<div data-split-id="columns-1" class="puck-split ..."><div></div><div></div></div>`, and the RSC payload gave each column `"children":"$undefined"`. **Cause.** `Split` is the last container still on Puck's legacy DropZone API - its columns live in `data.zones['<id>:left'|':right']` and only ever reach the block as `puck.renderDropZone`. Puck passes that down from `DropZoneRenderItem`, i.e. for blocks sitting in ordinary page content. It does **not** pass it from `SlotRender`'s `Item` (`@puckeditor/core/dist/chunk-SSXLOL3N.mjs`), which is what renders the children of a slot field on the RSC path - so `puck?.renderDropZone?.()` is `undefined` and the optional call quietly yields two empty divs. The client editor's own `Item` (`chunk-ELDOSC5Y.mjs`) **does** pass it, via `DropZoneProvider`, which is why the layout looked perfectly correct in the Layouts editor. Textbook editor/RSC parity break, and silent - no error, no 500, a 200 with a hole in it. Deskwell's `gazetteEntry` layout (`cmstzzl1r0001l10494f6xmrd`, "Media-Forward with Sidebar", published, `entire_site`) had its `Split` moved inside a `Section` - the starter template ships the Split at top level, where it works. Every other core container (`Section` `content`, `Grid2/3/4` `col{n}`, `Group` `items`) is slot-based, so Split is the only block that can fail this way; the two other live layouts holding zones (`starter-shop-checkout-classic-live`, `starter-shop-detail-default-live`) keep their Split at top level and were never affected. **Live fix (data only, no code, applied at Chris's ask this turn):** the nested `Split` swapped for a `Grid2` on `columnSizes: '70-30'` - same 7fr/3fr, same `gap: lg`, `spaceBelow: none`, `stackColumns: mobile` - with `columns-1:left`/`:right` moved into its `col1`/`col2` slot props and `zones` emptied. Section, its max-width and every block id untouched, so `injectEntryContext` still finds each block (it recurses any array-valued prop) and the page is visually what it was meant to be. `gazette_entry_layout_fix_2026_08_15/` holds `before_builderData.json`, `after_builderData.json`, `update.sql`, `rollback.sql`. Verified live straight after: post body, byline, reading time, tags and the whole right-hand rail (`gz-toc`, series nav, author bio) all render, `data-grid-id="columns-1"` in place of the empty split. **Core fix (working tree, unreleased):** `Split` is retired exactly as the dynamic `Grid` was - still registered in `puckConfig`/`footerPuckConfig`/`layoutPuckConfig` so existing data renders and edits unchanged, but dropped from all three `categories.layout.components` pickers and added to a new `SLOT_DISALLOW` constant named in the `disallow` of every core slot field (`Section.content`, `makeGridColumnComponent`'s `col{n}`, the legacy dynamic `Grid`'s `col1`-`col4`, `Group.items`, `MemberGate.content`, `TrustedMemberGate.content`). The editor can no longer build the broken shape, which is the only thing that could be done without a platform-wide data migration: giving Split real `left`/`right` slot fields would be the other repair, but Puck's `mapFields` runs `defaultSlots`, which fills a declared-but-absent slot with `[]` - so the moment Split declares slots, every existing zones-backed Split (both live shop layouts, plus the `split()` helper in five modules' `starterLayouts.ts`) renders empty unless its data is migrated first, and that data is spread across `Layout`, `InfoPage`, gazette post bodies, shop `description_puck` and saved blocks. Not worth it for a block Grid2 already supersedes. No module was touched; their starters keep top-level Splits, which still work. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `lib/puck` + `lib/layout` + `lib/setup` 96/96. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. Wiki: `Managing-pages.md` marks Split retired and points at Grid; `Architecture-overview.md`'s block table carries the full mechanism and the `disallow` list.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**Core: a module can no longer end up with no layouts at all - `lib/setup/starterLayouts.ts` + `lib/deploy/reconcile.ts`, working tree only.** Chris, after the gazette mess: there should always be default enabled layouts. Three changes, no schema. **(1) `publishByDefault` is a preference, not a precondition.** New pure `planModuleSeedTemplates(entries)` decides per layout type: templates marked `true` win; nothing marked at all takes the **first** template of that type; at least one explicit `false` and none true seeds nothing (a module saying "leave this to the owner" out loud, which is different from never having thought about it). `seedTemplates()` no longer filters on the flag itself - it writes what it is given and **returns how many rows it created** - so core still seeds only its own flagged templates while modules go through the planner. **(2) The stamp follows the work.** `reconcile.ts` writes `layoutsSeededAt` only when the seed actually created something, or when the module declares no layout types; a run that writes nothing now leaves the door open instead of shutting it. **(3) A stamped module with nothing at all gets another go.** `planPendingModuleSeeds` is replaced by `planModuleSeeds(installed, inBuild, declaredTypes, typesWithRows)`, which takes a module whose stamp is NULL **or** which owns not one row across every type it declares - the gazette state exactly. Deliberately narrow: a module with layouts for some types and none for others is left alone, because deleting one type's layout to fall back to a hardcoded page is a decision and re-minting it would change a live site unasked. `declaredLayoutTypesByModule()` exports the build's type map; `seedPendingModuleLayouts()` now does one `distinct: ['type']` read over `Layout` alongside the module read. **Blast radius, fresh installs:** shop gains three seeded types it deliberately left all-draft - `shopCategory`/`shopCollection`/`shopTag` now seed their first starter, so a new storefront's category pages render through Puck rather than the hardcoded grid. Every other module's plan is unchanged (verified by printing the before/after plan for all six). **Existing installs:** nothing moves unless a module owns zero layouts, which on Deskwell is `search` alone - it will self-seed `searchResults` on the first request after this core version deploys, and that page renders identically either way (`app/public/search/page.tsx` hand-renders the same arrangement as its fallback). Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, **full suite 1838 pass / 0 fail / 19 skipped**, with 8 new cases across the two planners including "every layout type of every module in this build gets a default". No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. Wiki: `Authoring-a-module.md`'s seeding section rewritten around the new rules. Shipped as core **v0.5.1051**; shop keeps the three newly-seeded types at Chris's call, so a fresh storefront gets designable category, collection and tag pages out of the box.)

Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**The hole under a category's opening paragraph - `shop` **0.1.223**, pinned in core **v0.5.1049**.** Chris, on `/shop/categories/office-pedestals`: a large empty band between the first and third paragraphs on the left. `components/public/ShopCategoryDescriptionBody.tsx` flowed a plain-text description's paragraphs through `display:grid` with `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(26rem,100%), 1fr))`, and a grid gives every cell in a row the height of the tallest one. That category's three paragraphs run short/long/medium, so row 1 took its height from the 6-line second paragraph, the 3-line first sat at the top of a cell three lines too tall, and the third paragraph began a fresh row **below** the hole. Nothing to do with the copy, and it hits any category whose paragraphs are unevenly sized. Replaced with multi-column text: `columnWidth: '26rem'` + `columnGap: '3rem'` on the wrapper, `breakInside: 'avoid'` + `marginBottom: '1.25rem'` per paragraph. Columns have no rows to line up, so the paragraphs simply carry on down one column and into the next and the browser balances them; on this category the left column now holds paragraphs one and two with the third beside them. Two points worth keeping: the 26rem is now a **column width** rather than a track minimum, which counts columns the same way at every width the old `auto-fit` did, and the paragraph's own `maxWidth: '40rem'` still holds the measure at the in-between widths where only one column fits - so no media query, as before; and the gap goes **below** each paragraph, never above, because a top margin landing at the head of the second column would push that column out of line with the first. Phone stays one column. The block half (`ShopCategoryDescription`) is a skeleton placeholder in the editor and unchanged, so Puck parity is untouched. Verified against a standalone repro of the real copy at the real 1228px band (before/after/two-paragraph/375px) driven through headless Chrome - no dev server, live site read-only. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide. No schema change, so no backup-gate trigger. Wiki unchanged: `Shop.md` describes what the Category Description block prints, never how the paragraphs were arranged. Shipped: module `v0.1.223`, core `v0.5.1049` (pin + this note, no core code). **The storefront will not change until the owner updates Deskwell.**)

Previous entry: 2026-08-15 (**A grid can now lead with a promoted variation's photo instead of the product's own cover - `shop` **0.1.222** + `shop-variations` **0.1.137**, core unchanged, all working tree.** Chris: on the product editor's **Images** tab, under "Order on the product page", an option that uses the "Image up front" variation photo as the main product photo on **category pages**. 014 had already settled the product page; the same product still showed its own primary on every tile, so a range whose own shots are line drawings read as a handsome product page reached from a dull card. **Shop side (generic, empty without a contributor):** `ShopCardMediaPayload` gains **`leadImages`** and `ShopCardExtra` gains a `leadImages: PartImage[]` bucket, merged in `resolveShopCardExtras` exactly like `images`. `buildCardContext` composes `[...leadImages, ...ownImages, ...images]` through the existing url dedupe, so the card's `image` (the tile's main picture) is the lead one and the product's own pictures simply follow behind the arrows - nothing is dropped and no surface needed changing: grid, related, featured, single card, search and every module grid all go through `buildCardContext`. One a11y wrinkle handled there rather than in the provider: a contributed image carries `alt: ''` by design (supplementary picture), which is wrong the moment it LEADS, so card-template fills a blank alt on `images[0]` alone with the product name. Shop still learns nothing about variations. **Variations side:** `svr_product_gallery` gains **`card_image_from_variation`** BOOLEAN default false (`migrations/015_card_image_from_variation.sql`, mirrored into 001) - the same table as 014 because it is the same decision, and the row-exists-only-while-something-is-on rule now means the writer deletes the row when BOTH flags go off. `lib/db/product-gallery.ts` reshaped around `ProductGalleryFlags` (`getProductGalleryFlags` / `setProductGalleryFlags`, `getBaseImagesLast` kept as a one-line reader) plus **`getCardImageFromVariationSet(productIds)`**, one set-wide query per grid returning only the products with the flag on - the same batched bargain the price and card-media providers already strike. `card-media-provider.ts` picks the FIRST enabled variation that is both ticked "Image up front" and actually has a still photo, and hands it back as `leadImages` instead of appending it; every other variation photo appends exactly as before, and a product whose promoted variations have no picture falls through to its own cover unchanged. `GET/PUT admin/products/[id]/gallery` now carry both flags, both optional on PUT (an omitted key keeps what is saved rather than reading as off), and `GalleryOrderPanel` holds a `Flags` object with a second switch, **"Use the variation image on category pages"**, saved by the editor's own Save button like the first. **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, **231 pass / 0 fail** across both modules plus `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts`, and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` re-run and PASSED (3/3, real throwaway VPS databases)** because a new module column trips the backup gate. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop-variations.md` ("Letting the promoted ones lead" gains the tiles half), `Shop.md` Images bullet, `Authoring-a-module.md` (one tick box became two). `shop-variations`' `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` → **0.1.222**, since `leadImages` is a compile-time dependency. Nothing committed, pushed or released - left in the working tree for review.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-13 (**Custom modules from any GitHub URL + new `product-checks-for-shop` module - both released the same day: core **v0.5.1042**, module **v0.1.0** (private repo `usersaynoso/product-checks-for-shop`, prerelease like every other module, so it installs on the **Beta** channel). Deskwell untouched - installing it there is the owner's own step.** Chris asked for (1) core: an owner can install a module from any GitHub repo URL, private repos included, without it appearing in any other site's module directory, and (2) a new module recording when each aspect of a Deskwell product listing was last verified. **Core half:** `POST /api/admin/modules` gained early `parseGitHubRepo` validation right after body parse (clear 400; a well-formed non-GitHub URL previously threw unhandled inside `getLatestRelease` as a bare 500), an `octokit.rest.repos.get` probe before release resolution whose 404 names the real fix (install the Cactus GitHub App on the owning account and grant it the repo - previously this case surfaced as the misleading "publish a release first"), and a refusal for a private repo when no clone credential exists (`MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` / ready `GithubAppConnection`) rather than committing a module the next build cannot fetch. The modules admin page gained an "Add a custom module" panel (URL box + channel toggle into the same `handleInstall`, server errors surfaced verbatim, plain trust warning). `buildInstalledEntry` (directory route) reads `description` off the stored manifest JSON so an off-directory module's card is not blank forever - deliberately NO `Module` column and NO schema change anywhere in the core half, so the backup gate is untripped by it. `scripts/checkout-modules.mjs` now clones anonymously first and retries with a lazily-resolved credential only on failure (`MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` → GitHub App installation token via new `scripts/lib/module-clone-auth.mjs` → `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`); auth-on-retry rather than up front matters twice - public repos behave byte for byte as before with no credential even resolved, and an App installation token presented for a public repo outside its own installation is refused by GitHub, which would have broken every directory module's clone. The helper reads `GithubAppConnection` with `pg` + node crypto + a hand-built RS256 JWT, never Prisma and never TS imports - checkout runs BEFORE `prisma generate` in the prebuild and is plain .mjs. Credential rides as `-c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=` command-line config (never in the URL, nothing persists into `.git/config`, key form scopes it to github.com), `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` makes an anonymous clone of a private repo fail fast instead of hanging the build, and all captured git output is scrubbed of the token and its base64 form before logging. `MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` registered optional in `getEnvStatus()`. **Module half:** new `modules/product-checks-for-shop/` (prefix `pck_`, one table `pck_product_checks`: one row per product, ten nullable timestamptz aspect columns - title, short/long description, images, 3D models, variations, add-ons, downloads, specification, shipping - plus one shared `notes`, `checked_by`, FK to `shp_products` ON DELETE CASCADE; teardown declares the real lowercase name). API `GET/PATCH admin/product/[id]` gated `requireShopUser('shop.products')` - the ONLY authorisation in the feature. Puck block `ShopProductChecks` (layoutTypes `shopProductDetail`; RSC half resolves the product via shop-variations' `currentProductSlug()` and renders an empty client island for EVERYONE, so shopper and staff receive identical HTML and page caching can never leak an admin render - the strip fills in only after the API answers, 401/403 = render nothing). A `shop.product-editor-sections` "Checks" section (order 54) reuses the same `ChecksPanel` component initiallyOpen. Admin staleness list at `/m/product-checks-for-shop` (one navEntries link, `shop.products`): LEFT JOIN from `shp_products` so never-checked products surface FIRST (sort key 0), catalogue-hidden variant children and archived products excluded. Stale threshold six months, a named constant (`STALE_AFTER_DAYS` in `lib/aspects.ts`, pure + unit-tested). **Deliberately NOT in root `modules.json`** - repo will be `usersaynoso/product-checks-for-shop`, the owner's own account, which is what keeps it out of every other site's directory; it was temporarily registered purely to run the generators + typecheck against the wiring, then the registry restored byte-identical (learned en route: `scripts/lib/module-names.mjs` filters every generator to `modules.json` entries, so an unregistered directory wires NOTHING - the older claim that generators scan the directory registry-free is stale). Manifest `requiresCoreVersion` **0.5.1042** - the core version this release ships in. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean WITH the module wired, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **1818 pass / 0 fail** (27 new core tests: `parseGitHubRepo` table in `lib/modules/manifest.test.ts`, clone-auth tiers/scrubber/JWT/decrypt in `scripts/lib/module-clone-auth.test.mjs`; plus the module's `lib/aspects.test.ts`), and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` re-run and PASSED (3/3, real throwaway VPS databases)** because the new module table trips the backup gate. Module runtime paths (API, storefront strip, staleness list) are honestly unverifiable before Deskwell installs it - no `Module` row means no table anywhere reachable, and the live DB is not a sandbox. Wiki updated and pushed: `Authoring-a-module.md` custom-module section, `Configuration-reference.md` `MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN`, new `Product-Checks.md`.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-12 (**Add-ons no longer wait for the main product to be configured - `product-addons-for-shop` **0.1.17**, working tree only.** Chris: a shopper should be able to configure an accessory and add it to the basket even if the desk above is untouched. `AddonsBox.tsx` had a `blockedBy` gate: any *match* or *default* mapping whose main option was unchosen greyed out every picker in the row, the quantity field and the reset link, and printed "Choose your Frame Colour above first". `blockedBy` and the `blocked` prop on `renderOptionPicker` are **gone**. A *default* mapping with nothing to follow was already rendered as a picker, so it simply works now (a pick registers as an override and sticks, which is that mode's own semantics). A *match* mapping with nothing to match used to render **nothing at all** - the option only entered `shown` via the post-loop `unshift` that needs `r.value` - so the combination could never complete and the row's own Add button stayed dead; it now pushes a plain `choose` picker carrying the new `matchesLater: string | null` field (the main option's NAME) on every `shown` entry, and the row prints "Pick one now, or choose your width above and it will match that" under the choices (`.pad-hint-opt`, `clear:both` for the floated option name). **The match still wins once the main option is settled** - the pre-existing branch takes over and locks it, which is the point of a matched option and matters for physical fit; a line already in the basket is untouched. Dead helper `listPhrase` removed with its only caller; the `allOptionsChosen === false && shown.length === 0` special-case hint collapsed to "Pick the options above to include it." since an all-match add-on now always has visible pickers. Grouping, the purchase-companion stamp and `mainTargetId` already fell back to the listing id for an unconfigured main, so an accessory bought alone renders flat in the basket with its "Accessory for" field, exactly as an orphan add-on always has. No schema change, no server change, showcase untouched. **Same turn, second ask:** the add-on quantity control now copies the main product's. The main product's is shop's `.spd-stepper` pill (CSS in `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`, markup drawn by shop-variations' `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` through the `PurchaseArea` slot's `classNames.stepper`) - minus / text input in `inputMode="numeric"` with non-digits stripped / plus, minus disabled at 1. The add-on box had a bare `type="number"` (`.pad-qtyinput`, 64px, 6px radius), so it wore the browser's own spinner arrows and was the only control of its kind on the page. Replaced with a `.pad-stepper` copy of shop's rule - same 9999px radius, same 46px buttons and 52px centred bold count, same `!important` hover fill (the site's Styles > Buttons blanket `button:hover` rule carries one) - with **one deliberate difference**: `align-self:stretch` instead of shop's fixed 52px height, because `.pad-addbtn` beside it is the smaller button and a pinned height left the pill standing proud of it. `.pad-qtyinput` deleted with its only user. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint modules/product-addons-for-shop` clean, 6/6 module tests pass. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Product-Add-ons.md`. **Nothing committed, pushed or released.** Previous entry: **A 3D add-on tag can now carry the shopper's own choice, so an accessory that comes in sizes gets a model per size - `product-addons-for-shop` **0.1.15**, working tree only; plus 12 combined GLBs and the matching rows written to live Deskwell.** Chris: the Oslo Air Piste desk's 3D should show a Steel Mobile Pedestal when that accessory is added, under the desk on the right. The pedestal comes in **30cm and 39cm**, and `pad_links.model_context_key` is a single string - one key can only ever show one size, whichever one was modelled - so he asked for the code to change rather than a size to be picked. **New optional `config.modelContextOptions`** (add-on option NAMES, max 4, in order) on the link's existing jsonb - no migration. New pure `composeContextKey(baseKey, optionNames, addonOptions, selection)` in `lib/mapping.ts` appends each nominated option's chosen value slug, reduced to `[a-z0-9-]` by the also-new exported `contextPart`: `pedestal` + Width -> `pedestal-30cm` / `pedestal-39cm`. Used by `addonContextKey` in `AddonsBox.tsx` (so both the broadcast and the cart line's `modelContext` bag get the same key) and by the admin coverage count. **A nominated option with nothing settled announces NOTHING, not the bare key** - matching is exact-or-base at the 3D end, so falling back to the bare key would show a size nobody asked for. `lib/db/links.ts`'s defensive `parseConfig` had to learn the field or it stripped it on every read; the PATCH route's zod gained it; `AdminLinkView.modelCoverage` went from one object to an **array**, one row per expected key (cartesian product of the nominated options' values, capped at 24), counted from one `SELECT DISTINCT product_id, context` rather than a LIKE per key; the editor grew a tick-box row ("Which choices change the combined model") and a warning when a nominated option no longer exists. **6 new tests** in the module's first test file, `lib/mapping.test.ts`. **Deskwell data (live DB, written this turn, `rollback.sql` kept):** 12 combined GLBs built by new `~/.cactus-3d-tools/dw-build-oslo-with-pedestal.mjs` (6 desk files x 2 pedestal widths), uploaded to the desk's own `3d/` folder on B2 and inserted as `p3d_models` rows tagged `pedestal-30cm`/`pedestal-39cm` against the six variation children; the link row now carries key `pedestal` + `modelContextOptions: ["Width"]`. Placement, settled over three passes the same day (files rebuilt and re-uploaded over the same keys each time, `size` re-read into the rows): left-hand face **20mm** inboard of the LEFT leg, far face 10cm inside the desktop's back edge, on the floor, turned a half turn about Y **in place** so the drawers face **-Z**, the desk's handset side. **The leg's inner face is measured per file off the `piste_frame_L` node, and that is the whole lesson of the third pass**: the piste legs are inset a fixed 108.5mm from the desktop edge, so they MOVE with the width (-0.493 / -0.593 / -0.693 on the 1200 / 1400 / 1600). Hardcoding the 1200's number - which is what the first two passes did, taken off one `perprim` run on one file - put the pedestal 120mm from the leg on the 1400s and 220mm on the 1600s while the 1200s looked right, which reads as "still too far away" and not as a bug. The frame, not the telescopic column, is the part to measure (on the 1400 the frame reaches -0.593 where the column stops at -0.610) and its 0.005..0.459 height band sits inside the pedestal's, so the gap is a real one. The builder now throws if the node is absent rather than guessing. The turn is undone in the arithmetic (place the TURNED box on the target) so the pedestal spins on the spot rather than swinging its box round; the combined bounding box is byte-for-byte the desk's own either way, which is what keeps one `heightManual` right for all eighteen files. Both pedestal files' body material is renamed to **`Pedestal Finish`** on the way in (the 39cm file calls it `Plastic matt white`, the 30cm one `Steel finish`), so **one** new `p3d_fabric_configs` row on the desk parent - its first - paints either from the pedestal's own Finish option id through `extraValueIds`. Two traps worth keeping: merging a **meshopt** file into a **Draco** one silently leaves the merged geometry uncompressed (1.3MB where 320KB does) and `draco()` alone will not fix it - the EXT_meshopt extension has to be **disposed** after `dequantize()` first; and `dedup()` must be given an explicit `propertyTypes` list excluding materials, or the desk's white frame and the pedestal's white body collapse into one and the Finish chooser paints the desk legs. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 6/6 new tests pass. No schema change anywhere, so no backup-gate trigger. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Product-Add-ons.md`. **Nothing committed, pushed or released** - and note the storefront will not change until the module is released and Deskwell updated: the deployed 0.1.14 announces the bare `pedestal`, which matches no file, so the base desk keeps showing.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-12 (**Second go at the promoted-variation gallery: the up-front photo and model now hold until EVERY option is chosen** - `shop` **0.1.217**, `shop-variations` **0.1.135**, `product-3d-views-for-shop` **0.1.90**, pinned in core **v0.5.1036**. The v0.5.1034 fix narrowed the promoted lists by the picks so far instead of emptying them at the first click. Chris, on the same desk: "loads showing the variation upfront 3d model and image, but as soon as we select 1 option, another 3d model loads and the upfront variation image disappears!! that should only happen when all options are selected, not just 1!" He is right, and the narrowing rule was the wrong shape: promoting 120cm+With for its photo and 140cm+Without for its model, then picking 120cm, ruled the 140 model out and swapped the stage to a 120 model the shopper had not asked to look at. **A part-made choice is not an answer.** So the gate is now `!variant` - the promoted media stays exactly as it opened for the whole configure and goes the instant `resolveVariant` returns a combination, which is the one moment the shopper HAS said what they want, and is also when the chosen variation's own photographs and model take over. Reset options brings it back. **Reverted with it**, all three now being pointless under that gate: `matchingVariants` in `lib/selection-logic.ts` and its 7 tests, `candidateModelChildIds` on the hook, `ShopGalleryExtraThumbsProps.candidateProductIds` (added in shop 0.1.215, removed in 0.1.217) and `visibleItems`' fourth argument with its 6 tests - `lib/visible-items.ts` is comment-only against 0.1.88 again. The bare-gallery fallback goes too and is not needed: with the promoted media up through the whole configure there is no gap to fill, and a product whose owner promoted nothing was already opening empty before any of this. **Consumer pin note:** shop-variations 0.1.134 and 3D 0.1.89 PASS the prop, so they must not be run against shop 0.1.217 (a compile-time error on that install); both consumers' `requiresModules: shop` moved to 0.1.217 and core pins all three together, which is how an install takes them. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on all three, **332 pass / 0 fail**. No schema change, no backup-gate trigger. No dev server, no build, per standing rules.)
Previous entry: 2026-08-12 (**A product's own photographs can now sit BEHIND the variations promoted with "Image up front" - `shop` 0.1.216 + `shop-variations` 0.1.134, core unchanged, all working tree.** Chris: a tick box on the product editor's **Images** tab that puts the product's own pictures after the promoted variation ones. The ordering rule lived entirely in shop-variations (`thumbs = variantImages, baseImages, featuredImages`), but the tick box was asked for on shop's own tab - so the honest shape was a **generic seam in shop plus the data and UI in the module that means something by it**, not a `shp_products` column that only makes sense with variations installed. **Shop side (generic, empty without a contributor):** new extension point **`shop.product-editor-media-sections`**. `resolveProductEditorTabs` became `resolveEditorEntries(point, user)` and is called twice; the media entries render as server components and travel into `ProductEditor` as `mediaSections: ReactNode[]` → `MediaPanel`, which renders them under its own Images section. No `label` (nothing to name), `order` only sorts contributions against each other, and because they mount inside the Images tab, `useProductEditorSave` registers them against tab id `media` for free - unsaved dot and failure message both say **Images**. **Variations side:** new table **`svr_product_gallery`** (`migrations/014_product_gallery_order.sql`, mirrored into 001) holding `base_images_last`; a row exists only while the flag is ON (`setBaseImagesLast(id,false)` DELETEs), so no backfill and no default row per product. New `lib/db/product-gallery.ts`, new `GET/PUT admin/products/[id]/gallery`, new `ProductGalleryOrderSection` (server; null for a variant child or a product with no options) → `GalleryOrderPanel` (client; fetches its own state, saves on the editor's Save button). `getVariantSelectorPayload` reads the flag into optional `VariantSelectorPayload.baseImagesLast` (optional for the usual cached-JSON reason), `use-variation-selection` exposes it and now computes `image` from it, and **both** galleries - `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx` and `VariantParts.tsx` - swap the two blocks (`baseImagesLast ? [...promoted, ...base] : [...base, ...promoted]`) and pick the stage image to match. The chosen variant's own photos still lead regardless; nothing about cards, cart or search changed. **Checks:** `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, 237 pass / 0 fail across both modules, `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` PASS and **`npm run test:backup-roundtrip` re-run and PASSED** (3/3, real throwaway VPS databases) because a new table triggers the backup gate. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop-variations.md` (new "Letting the promoted ones lead"), `Shop.md` (Images bullet), `Authoring-a-module.md` (the sibling point). `shop-variations`' `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` → 0.1.216, since the seam is a compile-time dependency. Nothing committed, pushed or released - left in the working tree for review.)
Previous entry: (**A product whose pictures all live on its variations went blank the moment one option was picked - `shop-variations` + `product-3d-views-for-shop` + `shop` seam, all working tree, core unchanged.** Chris, on `oslo-air-piste-height-adjustable-office-desk`: "all its images and 3d model come from variations which is great, however, when i select just 1 option, all images and 3d models disappear." Confirmed on live Deskwell: parent has **0** `shp_product_media` rows and no `p3d_models` row, 6 variations (2 ticked "Image up front", 1 "3D up front"), 2 options. **Two gates, both firing at once.** `useVariationSelection` computed `featuredImages`/`featuredModelChildIds` behind `!anyOptionChosen`, so the promoted media emptied on the FIRST pick; `resolveVariant` needs EVERY option chosen, so nothing more specific replaced it; and with no base gallery to fall back on the strip and the stage had nothing at all between the first pick and the last. On the 3D side `visibleItems` saw `activeProductId === null` (no whole combination) and an empty featured list, and the product's own model list was empty too. **Fix: narrow, don't empty.** New pure `matchingVariants(payload, selection)` in `lib/selection-logic.ts` - every switched-on variation still consistent with the picks so far, asked through `variantAnswersTo` so aliases narrow like the value they stand in for, and deliberately UNdirectional unlike `isValueAvailable` (that one ignores picks below the option it is asked about; this must not, or picking the panel first would still offer every width). The promoted lists are now filtered through it, which also does what the old gate was for - a rival finish leaves the strip the instant a pick rules it out, rather than the whole lot going at once. **Fallback for a bare gallery:** where the product carries no `baseImages` and the picks have narrowed past every promoted variation, the surviving variations ARE the gallery (`galleryIsBare && anyOptionChosen`). Held behind `anyOptionChosen` so an untouched page still opens on the owner's curated pick rather than every finish in the range. **Cross-module half:** shop's `ShopGalleryExtraThumbsProps` gains optional **`candidateProductIds`** and both shop-variations galleries pass the new `sel.candidateModelChildIds`; `visibleItems` takes it as a fourth argument and consults it ONLY when the product has no model of its own and no promoted variation is still standing. It had to be a second list rather than widening `featuredProductIds`: shop-variations cannot know whether the 3D module holds anything for the product itself, and the 3D module cannot know what the picks are. `Gallery3dThumbs` still passes `effectiveProductId`, so a mid-reconfigure gap keeps the settled model up and reaches neither list. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint` clean on all three modules, **345 pass / 0 fail** across the two modules' tests incl. **7 new** `selection-logic.matching.test.ts` and **6 new** `visible-items` cases. No schema change, no migration, so no backup-gate trigger. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Released as `shop` **0.1.215**, `shop-variations` **0.1.133** and `product-3d-views-for-shop` **0.1.89**, all three pinned in core **v0.5.1034**; both consumers' `requiresModules: shop` moved to 0.1.215, since the new prop is a compile-time dependency. Reaches Deskwell when the owner presses update.)
Previous entry: (**The GDPR tab's Live Chat cookie category would not save, and the live chat bubble now hides until that category is granted - core + `live-chat` 0.1.16.** Chris hit a bare "Invalid" adding the module-suggested Live Chat category on `/hq/config` (a 400 from `PATCH /api/admin/config`). Cause: the live-chat manifest declared its category as prose - `"Live chat"` - and the suggestion pill in `app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx` pushed that string straight into the row's **key**, which `ConsentCategoryPatch` requires to match `/^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*$/`. Zod's default regex message is the word "Invalid", so the banner said nothing useful. **Core fixes:** the manifest key regex now carries a written-out message naming the shape and an example; suggestions are folded through new `consentCategoryKey()` / `consentCategoryLabel()` helpers so a loosely-worded manifest still adds cleanly (`"Live chat"` -> key `live-chat`, label `Live chat`), the pill shows the label rather than the key, and the Key input folds what is typed as it is typed (trailing hyphen left alone so `live-chat` is reachable one keystroke at a time). **Second bug found in the same save path:** `dismissLabel` was never in `ConsentBannerConfigPatch`, so zod stripped it on every save - Deskwell's stored `consentBannerConfig` has no such field and a notice-only banner rendered an unlabelled button. Added to the patch schema and to `copyKeys` for the copy-version bump, with `|| 'Got it'` in `components/consent/ConsentBanner.tsx` for rows already saved without it. Also removed a runtime `require('@/lib/consent/gate')` from that component's `window.cactusConsent.onChange` (a client-bundle `require`, latent breakage) in favour of the imported function. **New consent seam:** `lib/consent/gate.ts` `notifyConsentChange()` now also dispatches `window` CustomEvent **`cactus:consent-change`** (exported as `CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT`) carrying the decision map.
