Modules bundle separately and cannot assume they share the listener `Set`; the event crosses bundles and pairs with `useSyncExternalStore`. **live-chat 0.1.16:** manifest `cookieCategories` is now `["live-chat"]`, matching the key the module code already checked. New `modules/live-chat/lib/consent.ts` (`CONSENT_CATEGORY`, `CONSENT_CHANGE_EVENT`, `consentMap()`, `chatConsentGranted()`) shared by the boot route and the widget. `app/api/widget/boot/route.ts` GET renames `journeyGate` to **`consentGate`** and adds `consentCategory`; the server still decides whether the gate applies at all (banner enabled AND the site's list actually carries the key), because the client cannot tell "no banner" from "not granted" - `window.__cactusConsent` is defined either way by the pre-paint script in `app/layout.tsx`. `components/WidgetLoader.tsx` reads the grant via `useSyncExternalStore` and returns null when it is absent, so **no bubble renders for a visitor who has not answered the banner, or who answered and left live chat off**. Withdrawal mid-visit closes the panel, removes `.woot-widget-holder`, clears the sessionStorage journey + active-panel keys and re-dispatches `chatwoot:closed` so the bubble state resets without a `setState` inside the effect (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect`; reading `startedRef.current` in render trips `react-hooks/refs`, hence the event). Staff agent console is untouched - signed-in staff tool. Wiki: Configuration-reference (key shape + Dismiss label row), Architecture-overview (event seam section, module contract), Authoring-a-module (`cookieCategories` row, event + `useSyncExternalStore` snippet, new "Gate the UI too" step), Live-Chat (privacy behaviour). `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` clean. Owner still has to add the category on the GDPR tab; until it exists the bubble shows to everyone as before.)
Previous entry: (**Tags grow up: a Tags screen, owner-coloured card badges, a page per tag, and a pre-made self-applying "On Sale" tag - `shop` 0.1.212 + `shop-variations` 0.1.132, core unchanged.** Chris tried to tag a product and hit "No tags yet. Add some under Shop, then Products." - copy pointing at a screen that was never built. `shp_tags` had held id/name/slug since 001 and the admin API had GET/POST/DELETE with no UI on the end of it. **New `migrations/019_tag_display.sql`** (mirrored into 001 for fresh installs) adds `description`, `storefront_visible`, `badge_enabled`, `badge_label`, four colour columns (`badge_bg`/`badge_bg_dark`/`badge_text`/`badge_text_dark`), `position`, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, `auto_rule`. Colours are **frozen values, not `var(--color-N)` palette references** - the palette vars are index-numbered and re-point the moment somebody reorders Appearance - and every one of them goes through core's `cssValue()` before it reaches an inline style. **New admin screen** `components/admin/TagsScreen.tsx` + `app/cactus-admin/shop/tags/page.tsx`, a fourth Catalogue tab beside Products/Categories/Collections. Slug is its own field with a confirm before it changes, never regenerated behind a rename: it is what `tagSlug` blocks, `?tag=` and the tag's page all hold. Colour pickers reuse core's `ColourPickerRow` fed from `GET /api/admin/appearance`, so the site palette's swatches are offered alongside a free picker; light and dark are separate fields with side-by-side previews. **Badges**: `CardBadge` gained a `'tag'` variant plus `colours`, painted through `--shop-tag-*` custom properties so one server-rendered card serves both themes (`.shop-card-badge-tag` + the two dark selectors the design tokens use). Precedence is out of stock → pre-order → lowest-`position` badge tag → the legacy hardcoded `new`/`trade` slugs, which still work. `buildCardContext` takes an **optional** ninth arg `tagsById` and `buildTagMaps(tags)` builds both lookups - optional deliberately, so filters-for-shop and product-attributes-for-shop keep compiling unrebuilt. **New public page** `/shop/tag/[slug]` (no `shopTag` layout type yet - that would mean touching `layoutTypes` on a dozen blocks). **The "On Sale" tag** is seeded by 019 (`auto_rule = 'sale'`, red badge, `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`) and is never written to `shp_product_tags`: membership is computed, so it cannot go stale when a price moves. Cards read it from `isOnSale(product)` OR the new optional `ShopCardFromPrice.onSale`; lists read it from **new extension point `shop.product-on-sale`** (`lib/product-sale.ts`, SQL providers like `shop.product-search`/`shop.product-availability`, aliased `p`), which shop-variations fills from `lib/sale-provider.ts` - a variations listing's own sale column is always empty, the money is on the hidden children. Sale prices switched off shop-wide makes the tag page empty rather than everything. Product editor: auto tags get no checkbox (ticking one would write a row nothing reads), and there is now an inline "Add tag" box beside the list. Two more companions rebuilt to pass the new arg so their grids print tag badges too - `filters-for-shop` 0.1.13 and `product-attributes-for-shop` 0.1.48, both a one-line `buildTagMaps` swap plus the extra argument, `shop` floor moved to 0.1.212 on each. Backup round-trip re-run and PASSED against a throwaway VPS database, not skipped. **Follow-up in the same sitting - `shop` 0.1.213, `filters-for-shop` 0.1.14, `product-attributes-for-shop` 0.1.49:** the tag page gained a `shopTag` layout type after all. New `components/puck/ShopTagHeader{,.rsc}.tsx` (anchor block, breadcrumb + name + description, returns null for a storefront-hidden tag), `lib/inject-tag-context.ts` (fills `tagSlug` on ShopTagHeader/ShopProductGrid/ShopFilterGrid/ShopAttributeFilterGrid - the last two named as strings, since a module may not import another's block), two starters in `shopTagStarters()`, and the page now prefers a published `shopTag` layout exactly as the category and collection pages do. Blocks offered in it: ShopTagHeader, ShopProductGrid, ShopProductCard, ShopFeaturedCollection, ShopPromoBanner, ShopFilterGrid, ShopAttributeFilterGrid. **Second follow-up, `shop` 0.1.214:** the product PAGE was still on the two hardcoded slugs while the cards had moved on - a reduced product showed a Sale badge in the grid and nothing but "In stock" on the page it led to (verified on the live site before the fix). Badge resolution moved out of card-template into `lib/tag-badges.ts` (`resolveTagBadges`), shared by both; `CardBadge` gained an optional `slug` so the page can tell that a hardcoded New/Trade badge would be repeating a tag badge and stand down. `DetailPartContext.tagBadges` is the resolved list - the page prints every badge earned rather than the card's single winner - and `ShopDetailBadges` gained a `showTag` switch plus `.spd-badge-tag`, the same `--spd-tag-*` custom-property trick `.shop-card-badge-tag` uses. The page asks `resolveCardFromPrices([product.id])` for the variation answer, so a listing reduced only on one variation badges there too. No Puck layout edits were needed anywhere: both live blocks carry no props, and an absent toggle reads as on.)
Previous entry: (**Buying codes on the storefront product page, staff only - `shop` 0.1.211 + `shop-variations` 0.1.131, both pinned in `modules.json`, core v0.5.1028.** Chris: product, variation and sale SKUs on the front end, admins only, and the variation code only once its options are chosen. New `modules/shop/lib/admin-codes.ts` exports `canSeeProductCodes()` - `getSessionFromCookie()` then `hasShopPermission(user, 'shop.products', { allowAccess: true })`, deliberately the same READ gate as `admin-stock.ts` beside it, since a colleague with read-only shop access already sees every one of these codes in the admin product list. Awaited in the existing `Promise.all` in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` and carried as the new required `DetailPartContext.showAdminCodes`. **`ShopDetailSkuRsc` now renders two things, not one**: the product's own SKU as before, plus, for staff, a `.spd-sku-staff` dashed box reading `Sale SKU: <code>` with a literal "staff only" marker (same visual language as the stock chip). The sale code is written out whenever the product carries one, on offer or not - the owner reading their own page needs to know which code the stock is currently ordered under, and `onSale` gating would hide it exactly when someone rings up about it. **New `audience` field on the SKU block** (`Show the code to`: `staff` (default) / `everyone`). Shipped for one release as `everyone`-by-default on the reasoning that a shop quoting SKUs to customers would lose them overnight; Chris asked for staff-by-default immediately after, which is why the resolution reads `skuIsPublic(value) => value === 'everyone'` rather than testing for `'staff'`. That inversion is load-bearing: a block saved before the field existed carries no `audience` value at all, and those are precisely the layouts (Deskwell's included) that had to flip without anyone editing a page. `staff` adds a " · staff only" suffix to the line so the author can tell at a glance which way round it is. The sale SKU is never on that switch - a supplier's clearance code is staff-only whatever the author picks. The part's early return moved from `if (!_ctx || !_ctx.product.sku)` to "nothing to show at all", so a product with no SKU but a sale SKU still renders for staff. **On the variations side the code belongs to the chosen combination**, so `getVariantSelectorPayload` calls the same `canSeeProductCodes()` and **withholds rather than merely ignores**: `sale_sku` joins the child-row query, `VariantSelectorVariant` gains `saleSku`, and BOTH `sku` and `saleSku` are nulled for shoppers - `sku` had been in the public payload since it existed, unused by the storefront, which is the same defect `stockCount` had before 0.1.112 fixed it. New payload flag `showCodes`, optional for the usual JSON-shape reason (a payload serialised before this shipped carries no such key). New client `AdminSkuNote` in `VariantParts.tsx` renders `SKU:` / `Sale SKU:` in a dashed staff-only box, rendered beside `AdminStockNote` in both places that one appears (`VariantAddToCartPart`, `VariantSlotPurchaseClient`) - which is what puts it under the buy button on Deskwell, whose layout carries `ShopVariantOptions` + `ShopVariantPrice` + shop's own `ShopDetailAddToCart`, so `PurchaseArea` is uncovered and the slot renders. It needs no permission check of its own: a shopper's payload has nothing in it. **Held back until `sel.variant` resolves** (all options chosen) and skipped entirely when `!sel.hasOptions` - a half-built configuration matches no row, a stale code from the last complete choice is worse than none since it is the code someone would go and order, and on an options-free product shop's own SKU part has already written the same codes further up the page. No schema change (`sale_sku` shipped in shop 0.1.207/migration 018), so the backup round-trip gate does not apply. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean project-wide, `vitest run` on both touched modules clean (371 tests). No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop.md` (sale SKU box + the new Show the code to setting), `Shop-variations.md` (the combination's codes under the buy button). The admin-sidebar work below (0.1.209 / 0.1.130) had already landed on `main` in both module repos by the time this shipped, so this round is a plain patch on top of it: shop 0.1.209 -> 0.1.210, shop-variations 0.1.130 -> 0.1.131 (whose `requiresModules.shop.minVersion` moves to 0.1.210 alongside it, since it now imports shop's new `admin-codes.ts`). Both committed, pushed to `main` and released (`--prerelease`) on their module repos. Core `package.json` 0.5.1026 -> 0.5.1027, `modules.json` pins moved to `v0.1.210` / `v0.1.131`, committed and pushed to `origin` on `main`, GitHub release `v0.5.1027` (`--prerelease`) cut. **Follow-up, same day**: shipped default was `everyone` (unchanged behaviour) rather than `staff` - Chris checked his own live product page, found the SKU still public, and it turned out to be the correct default doing exactly what it said, not a bug. He asked for staff-by-default anyway. `shop` 0.1.211 flips it: `skuAudienceOptions` reordered (staff first), `defaultProps.audience` -> `'staff'`, and the resolution changed from testing `props.audience === 'staff'` to testing `skuIsPublic(props.audience) === (props.audience === 'everyone')` - deliberately the inverse test, because a SKU block saved before the `audience` field existed (every product page on every live site, Deskwell included) carries no value at all, and `!== 'staff'` would have kept treating that absence as public. `npm run typecheck` and `eslint modules/shop` clean, shop's `vitest run` clean (230 tests). Committed, pushed, released (`--prerelease`) on the shop repo; core `package.json` 0.5.1027 -> 0.5.1028, `modules.json` pin moved to `v0.1.211`, committed, pushed, released. This is a core release only - it does not reach Deskwell until the owner clicks update on the live site.)
Previous entry: (**Admin sidebar tidy: 48 links down to 17, module links 39 down to 7, nothing deleted.** With everything installed the rail carried 48 items, 39 of them from modules - shop alone took 9 and its five companion modules another 5, gazette 6, boards 4, space planner 4, SEO 4. The rule applied throughout: **one sidebar link per module where the surfaces are related, everything else a tab on that page**, and anything that is really configuration living under Settings. Core's own 9 links are untouched at the owner's request (Menus, Modules and Layouts keep theirs). **Three new whole-page tab extension points**, all resolved by one new shared server helper `lib/modules/extension-tabs.tsx` (`resolveExtensionTabs(point, user)`: reads installed manifests, drops entries whose `permission` the role lacks, falls back to a tidied id when the install-time schema has stripped `label`, sorts by `order`): `core.inbox-tabs` (new `/cactus-admin/inbox` screen, a host with nothing of its own - contact-form and live-chat each gave up a link for a tab on it), `core.media-tabs` (gemini-watermark-remover became a tab on Media), and `shop.orders-tabs` (quote-for-shop became a tab on Sales), joining shop's existing `shop.products-tabs` which now also carries filters-for-shop, product-attributes-for-shop, product-addons-for-shop and reviews-for-shop. **The Inbox link is the first `conditional: true` core nav item**: a conditional item is dropped from `resolveAdminMenu` *and* the Navigation editor unless the caller passes its id in `availableCoreItemIds`, and passing nothing means "nothing available" - a missed call site hides a link rather than advertising a dead one. **Shop went 9 links to 2** (Catalogue, Sales) on a new shared `ShopSectionNav` + `lib/admin-nav.ts` resolver, with each section's contributed tabs opened by `?tab=<id>` on its first page so the strip stays plain links every page in the section can share; `ProductsScreen` lost its internal tab state entirely. Tax & shipping was going to move to Settings and did not - it hosts other modules' panels via `shop.tax-shipping-tabs`, which only a server component can resolve, and core's settings page must not know a shop-specific point - so it rides the Sales strip instead. Off the sidebar either way. **search** and **twilio** folded their admin screens into their own existing Settings tabs as sub-tabs ("Index & searches", "Calls & texts"). **gazette/boards/space-planner/SEO** went 6/4/4/4 links to one apiece - the first two already rendered a cross-page `TabStrip` so only their manifests changed; the other two gained `SpacePlannerNav.tsx` / `SeoNav.tsx` on the same pattern. **Settings > Users folded into the Users page**: Roles (with its `core.roles-page` extension resolution) and the five member-settings sub-tabs moved out of `ConfigPageClient`/`config/page.tsx` onto `/cactus-admin/users`, whose gate widened from `users.manage` alone to any of `users.manage`/`members.settings`/`roles.manage` with each tab gated separately - a role holding only `roles.manage` would otherwise have lost the editor in the move; the `users` nav item's `defaultPermissions` widened to match, and `/config?tab=users` plus every old `?sub=` deep link now redirects. **Nothing was deleted**: all 34 retired routes still exist and `redirect()` to wherever their screen now lives, so bookmarks, the command palette and older modules' links keep working; the admin search index was repointed too. One genuinely dead file removed - live-chat's `InboxLinkButton.tsx` and its `contact-form.inbox-actions` entry, a button linking one inbox to the other, pointless once both are tabs of the same screen. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, `vitest run` 1776 pass / 0 fail / 19 skipped. No schema change anywhere, so the backup round-trip gate does not apply. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Versions bumped but **not committed, pushed or released** - left in the working tree for review: core stays at 0.5.1025 in `package.json` (the modules that publish into the new core points declare `requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.1026, i.e. the next core release), and 16 module repos carry a patch bump each - shop 0.1.209, shop-variations 0.1.130, product-attributes-for-shop 0.1.47, product-addons-for-shop 0.1.14, filters-for-shop 0.1.12, reviews-for-shop 0.1.4, quote-for-shop 0.1.12, contact-form 0.1.34, live-chat 0.1.15, gemini-watermark-remover 0.1.11, search 0.1.17, twilio 0.1.26, gazette 0.1.15, boards 0.1.16, space-planner-for-shop 0.1.24, ultimate-seo 0.1.3. `modules.json` is untouched - the pins can only move once those tags exist.)
Previous entry: (**The showcase card's hover colour was the SITE THEME all along, not the browser - product-addons-for-shop and shop, both committed to `main`, NOT tagged/released.** 0.1.11 blamed native button chrome and reset `appearance`; that was wrong, and the tan fill carried on. The real source is core's own `lib/design/tokens.ts`, which turns the site's **Styles > Buttons > hover** settings into a blanket `main button:hover,main .cactus-btn[data-variant="primary"]:hover{background:var(--btn-hover-bg) !important}`. It cannot tell a call to action from an element that is only a `<button>` so a keyboard can reach it - so 0.1.10's `.pads-text` (the card's clickable name/blurb/price) was painted with the site's button fill on hover, `background:none` and `appearance:none` both being powerless against an `!important`. Fixed the way shop already fights the identical rule for its quantity stepper (`detail-parts.tsx:774`, comment and all): `.pads-text:hover,:focus,:active{background:none !important}`. `.pads-imgbtn` got the same treatment - harmless behind an opaque photograph, and the theme's fill glowing through a cut-out product picture otherwise. **`.pad-learn` in the box had the same defect and nobody had noticed**: its intended `background:var(--color-bg-subtle)` hover was being overridden by the theme's fill too, so it now carries `!important` as well. The `appearance:none` from 0.1.11 stays as ordinary hygiene for a button dressed as text, with its comment corrected to stop claiming credit for a fix it never made. **Separately, in shop**: the Learn more popup iframes shop's chrome-free `/shop/products/<slug>/details` view, whose `.spd-bare-imgs` strip is a plain `display:flex` - so a product with one photograph had it hard against the left edge of a 920px modal. Now `justify-content:safe center`. The `safe` keyword is load-bearing, not decoration: plain `center` on a horizontally-scrolling flex row puts the overflow on BOTH sides and browsers cannot scroll back past the start, so a product with eight pictures would lose the first of them outright - `safe` falls back to start alignment exactly when the row overflows, which is when centring stops being wanted anyway. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. Two syntax errors were made and fixed during this task, both the same one: backticks inside the CSS template literal, closing the string early - a comment in a `const CSS = \`...\`` block cannot quote a CSS selector in backticks. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. **Neither module's `cactus.module.json`/`package.json` was touched**: another session has unrelated, substantial admin-navigation work in flight uncommitted on both repos (product-addons-for-shop and shop, mirrored in core's own admin nav too), so their version fields already carry that work's numbers - staging them here would have swept someone else's half-finished changes into this commit. Both fixes are plain commits, pushed to `main` on their module repos, no tag. Core's `modules.json` pin is untouched, so this reaches Deskwell only once the concurrent work lands its own version bump - which will carry this fix forward with it - or a later session tags these repos properly on its own. No core commit, no core release this round.)
Previous entry: (**A Sale SKU field, separate from the ordinary SKU - shop 0.1.207, shop-variations 0.1.129, google-sheet-products-for-shop 0.1.56, core v0.5.1024.** Overwriting `shp_products.sku` with a supplier's clearance code (as the dynamic-clearance skill used to) breaks the supplier's own stock spreadsheet, which still calls the item by its catalogue code - the two codes do different jobs and both are needed at once. New nullable, NOT UNIQUE column `shp_products.sale_sku` (`modules/shop/migrations/018_sale_sku.sql`, `ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`) holds the code to order under while an offer runs; `sku` is never written by any of this. Not unique on purpose - a supplier can put one clearance code across several lines, unlike `sku` which is the shop's own identity. Lands on both plain products and shop-variations' variant children (a variation IS a hidden `shp_products` row), so no shop-variations schema change was needed, only the read/write plumbing. Surfaced: product editor's Pricing tab gets a **Sale SKU** box beside the sale price (shown only when the sale price type is switched on, same gate as the price box itself); the Variations grid gets a **Sale SKU** column under the same gate; the cross-product Variations browser and the Products list both show "on offer: <code>" under the SKU when the row is actually on sale (`onSale(p)` / `isOnSale`), not just whenever the field happens to be filled - a leftover code on a product back at full price is history, not an instruction. Round-trips through the shop's own CSV export/import (`sale_sku` appended to `CSV_COLUMNS`, optional so an old export still validates), shop-variations' own Variant CSV (`Sale SKU` column, positioned next to `Variant SKU` rather than with the prices - it's a code, not a figure), and the Google-Sheet mirror (Push/Pull/diff all pick up the new column automatically off the same header lists, one line each in `push-variations.ts`/`variation-tabs.ts`/`pull-diff.ts`). `requiresModules` minVersions bumped accordingly (shop-variations now wants shop >= 0.1.207, google-sheet-products-for-shop wants shop >= 0.1.207 and shop-variations >= 0.1.129) since all three now read/write a column that older sibling versions don't have. **`.agents/skills/dynamic-clearance` rewritten to match**: it now writes `sale_sku` instead of swapping `sku`, matches on `sale_sku` first (a row already carrying the clearance code there is one an earlier run touched), and - because `sale_sku` isn't UNIQUE - no longer needs the "two rows claiming one code" clash guard that `sku`'s uniqueness used to require. It also recognises and repairs rows the OLD version of the skill left with a clearance code sitting in `sku`: the catalogue code is read back off the clearance listing's own image filename and restored to `sku`, with the clearance code moved into `sale_sku`; where there's no catalogue code to restore (or another row already holds it), the row still gets its price and sale code, flagged `skuNeedsAttention` in `plan.csv` for a human. The planner also checks up front that `shp_products.sale_sku` actually exists and says so in plain English if the site hasn't been updated to shop >= 0.1.207 yet, rather than surfacing a raw Postgres error. `rollback.sql` now undoes `sale_sku` (and, for a repaired row, the SKU restore) instead of `sku`. Wiki: `Shop.md` (Pricing tab), `Shop-variations.md` (grid, cross-product browser, CSV export), `.agents/skills/dynamic-clearance/SKILL.md`. **Schema change (new column) - gated on `npm run test:backup-roundtrip`: ran for real, PASS** (3 tests, ~46s, against a throwaway `cactus_rt_*` database on the OVH VPS - not skipped). Checks: `npm run typecheck` and `eslint .` both clean on the touched modules (`shop`, `shop-variations`, `google-sheet-products-for-shop`); a pre-existing, unrelated syntax error in `product-addons-for-shop/components/public/AddonsShowcase.tsx` (already broken in the working tree before this task started, untouched by it) blocks a project-wide `npm run typecheck` run - out of scope for this task, flagged rather than fixed. `vitest run` clean across all three touched modules (401 tests). No dev server, no build, per standing rules - this is a database/API/admin-UI change with no independently browser-checkable surface beyond what the tests already cover. Committed, pushed and released on request: shop v0.1.207, shop-variations v0.1.129, google-sheet-products-for-shop v0.1.56, all three module repos; core v0.5.1024 pins them in `modules.json`. This is a CORE release only - it does not reach Deskwell until the owner clicks update on the live site.)
Previous entry: (**product-addons-for-shop 0.1.12: the showcase card's price now matches shop's own category-card price.** `.pads-price` was `font-size:0.875rem;color:var(--color-text-muted)` - the same weight as the muted staff note under it, reading as an afterthought. Shop's `.shop-card-price` (`modules/shop/components/puck/parts/card-parts.tsx`) is `font-weight:600;color:var(--color-primary)` - bold, brand colour - so `.pads-price` now carries the same two declarations, size unchanged. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean. No dev server, no build, per standing rules - not visually checked in a browser this round.)
Previous entry: (**product-addons-for-shop 0.1.11: the showcase card's hover was the browser, not us, and it wanted a proper lift instead.** 0.1.10 wrapped the card's name/blurb/price in a `<button>` (`.pads-text`) with `background:none` and nothing else touching its resting or hover background - and yet hovering it painted a grey highlight anyway. Cause: neither `.pads-text` nor `.pads-imgbtn` had ever had `appearance` reset, so Safari and Chrome were drawing their own native control chrome underneath the pointer regardless of what `background` said - a rule only bites the states it names, and neither of these buttons had ever named `:hover` at all, so there was no CSS rule to inspect for the bug; the highlight came from a rule that was never written. `appearance:none; -webkit-appearance:none;` on `.pads-text` removes it. In its place, `.pads-card` now gets the SAME hover shop's own category cards use (`.shop-card` in `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/card-parts.tsx`) - `transform:translateY(-4px)` plus the identical shadow, transitioning on `box-shadow,transform`, with `.pads-img` zooming to `scale(1.03)` alongside it on a matching `transform .4s ease`. Matched exactly (same offset, same shadow values) rather than merely similar, so a card here reads as the same sort of thing as everywhere else in the shop. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. No dev server, no build, per standing rules - not visually checked in a browser this round.)
Previous entry: (**product-addons-for-shop 0.1.10: five follow-ups on the add-ons panel and showcase.** (1) **"Learn more" now sits beside the price rather than on its own line.** 0.1.9 put it in the flow under the name, which fixed the overlap by giving the button a line of its own and squeezed nothing - but the ask was for it next to the price. `.pad-head` is now a **four-column, two-row grid** (tick box, picture, words, button) instead of a flex row: the tick box and the picture span both rows, the name takes the words column AND the button's on a phone (`.pad-title{grid-column:3/5}`) so it keeps the full width, and the button drops to row 2 beside the price. At `min-width:640px` the name stops at column 3 and the button moves up to row 1 - the corner it has always wanted. **The absolute positioning is gone entirely**, along with the `padding-right:6.25rem` reservation it needed: a grid column cannot be overlapped, so the whole class of defect goes with it. This required splitting the one `<label>` that wrapped name and price into two labels pointing at the same tick box (ordinary HTML, both still tick it) - a single label is one grid item and could not have the button placed inside it, the button being interactive content that a label may not hold. (2) **The Learn more popup shows a spinner while it loads** (`LearnMoreModal.tsx`). It iframes a whole page through the whole pipeline, so on a cold route it was a few seconds of blank white rectangle with a title on it, which reads as broken rather than busy. New `loaded` state set from the iframe's `onLoad`; until then a `role="status"` ring plus "Fetching the details…" covers the frame, and the frame fades in rather than showing half-painted through it. The frame is hidden, **not unmounted** - it has to be in the document to do the loading. `prefers-reduced-motion` stops the rotation and leaves the wording to carry it. (3) **The showcase card's writing opens the description.** Name, blurb and from-price are now wrapped in one borderless `.pads-text` button (`aria-label="Learn more about <name>"`), so the tab order gains one stop rather than three and it is announced as an action rather than read out as the whole card. The three lines became `<span>`s because a button may only carry phrasing content - a `<p>` in there is invalid markup. The staff out-of-stock note and the action row stay outside it (a button cannot hold another button, and the note is not a description). The existing Learn more button stays as the discoverable affordance. (4) **A lone showcase card no longer stretches the full width of a desktop.** New `pads-one` modifier when `cards.length === 1`: a single `minmax(230px,340px)` track with `justify-content:center`, overridden back to `1fr` on a phone, where half a screen is a stamp rather than a card. (5) **Two showcase cards per row on a phone, matching shop's own category grids.** Was `repeat(auto-fill,minmax(230px,1fr))` at every width, so a phone got one card per row and a short list of accessories became a long scroll. Now `repeat(2,minmax(0,1fr))` with a 12px gutter under `mobileBp`, with the wording stepped down (name 0.875rem, blurb 0.75rem and clamped to 2 lines, price 0.8125rem), the body padding tightened, and the Learn more / Add pair **stacked** - side by side they want more width than half a phone has, and a wrapped button row is worse than a stacked one. **The breakpoint is the site's own** (Styles > Spacing & Breakpoints), not a bespoke pixel: `ShowcasePayload` gains an optional `breakpoints`, `buildShowcasePayload` resolves it with `getShopBreakpoints()` alongside the shop config it already awaited, and the stylesheet became `showcaseCss(bp)` behind a `useMemo`. Optional because the payload crosses to the browser as JSON and sits in caches predating the field - one serialised before this shipped falls back to `DEFAULT_BREAKPOINTS`, which is what a site gets until it changes them anyway. The default is imported from `breakpoints-shared` (no database, so a client island may hold it) rather than `breakpoints`, which would drag prisma into the page builder's bundle. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. No schema change, no build, no dev server.)
Previous entry: (**Add-ons on a phone: "Learn more" stopped landing on the add-on's name, and the pinned gallery now stays up while add-ons are being configured. shop-variations 0.1.128 + product-addons-for-shop 0.1.9, both pinned in `modules.json`.** Two separate defects, both only visible on a narrow screen. (1) **`.pad-learn` was `position: absolute; top: 0.45rem; right: 0`** inside `.pad-row` (`components/public/AddonsBox.tsx`), so it was out of the flow and reserved no space. On a phone the add-on's name has the full width and still wraps - "Air Screen for Back-to-Back Desk" runs to two lines - and the second line ran straight under the button. The button is now in the flow by default (`justify-self: start`, pulled left by its own padding so the label lines up with the row's edge), sitting on its own line under the name, and only takes the corner at `min-width: 640px`; that branch also gives `.pad-head` a `6.25rem` right padding, because a long name in a narrow desktop buy column would otherwise reach under the button there too. No DOM change, so the editor and RSC paths stay identical. (2) **The pinned mobile gallery let go the moment the shopper scrolled into the add-ons box.** `lib/use-sticky-mobile-gallery.ts` measured a single `.svr-options` element and released the strip once its bottom passed the strip's resting line - and the add-ons box sits BELOW the options, under the add-to-cart button, so configuring an add-on happened with the picture already gone. Which is precisely when it is needed: choosing an add-on changes the 3D model on the stage. The hook now measures the union of `.svr-options` plus anything carrying the new exported `GALLERY_HOLD_ATTR` (`data-svr-hold-gallery`), judging each candidate on its own - it must have a box at all (so one in a hidden tab panel is ignored), must sit below the gallery, and must overlap it horizontally - and holds the pin until the LAST such element has scrolled past. The `ResizeObserver` picks holders up as they appear rather than once at effect time, since the add-ons box mounts after its own payload arrives and opens right out as each add-on is ticked. `AddonsBox` wears the attribute on `.pad-box`; the showcase panel deliberately does not. Cross-module coupling is the published-seam kind pad already uses (it imports `selection-broadcast`, `purchase-companions` and `selection-logic` from shop-variations); `requiresModules.shop-variations.minVersion` moves 0.1.121 -> 0.1.128 accordingly. No schema change anywhere, so no backup round-trip gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Not released - working tree only.)
Previous entry: (**shop-variations 0.1.127: the locked buy button's shrink-to-fit was quietly clipping instead, on top of the wrap fix in 0.1.124.** `FitLabel`'s single-line branch computed its font size by straight arithmetic (natural width ÷ room, rescaled) and trusted it outright - but glyph widths only scale with font-size APPROXIMATELY (subpixel rounding, hinting), so the computed size could come out a fraction too big, and because the label always carries `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, that shortfall never showed as visible overflow - it just ate the label's last word or two under an ellipsis. Looked, on a live product page, exactly like "not shrinking, just trimming" - which is what it was reported as. Fixed by treating the arithmetic as a seed rather than an answer: apply it, measure `label.scrollWidth` for real, creep down 0.5px at a time until the box actually holds the text (mirrors what the two-line branch already did). Caught a second bug proving it: the two-line branch's ceiling seed (`estimate × 1.8`) was applied and checked BEFORE being clamped to the `min` floor, so an extreme case (four-plus outstanding options on a phone) could settle a hair under the documented 11px minimum if that first attempt happened to fit outright - now clamped with `Math.max(min, ...)` before the first attempt, not just on the way down. Verified with a standalone Playwright repro built from shop's actual `.spd-buy-row`/`.spd-add` CSS: four sentences (37-97 characters) at four widths (700/560/390/300px) - zero clipped width, zero clipped height, minimum font size never below 11px, button always on the stepper's line. Not pinned in core yet.)
Previous entry: (**"Missing Stock" filter on the cross-product Variations browser - shop-variations 0.1.126, core v0.5.1020.** Same shape as the existing "Without SKU"/"Without Image" pair (`Shop-variations.md`, "Browsing every variation"): the **Nothing set** group in `VariationsBrowser.tsx` gains a third built-in entry, `{ id: 'stock', label: 'Stock Number' }`, alongside `sku` and `image`. `variations-list.ts` answers it in SQL beside the other two - `(c."track_inventory" = true AND c."stock_count" IS NULL)` - deliberately gated on `track_inventory`, because a variation that never tracks stock hasn't got a missing number, it's got no number by design. `stock_count = 0` does NOT match: nought is a real stock figure (out of stock), not an absent one, which was the whole point of the ask - a plain `IS NULL OR <= 0` would have swept every genuinely-empty variation into the same bucket as the ones nobody has counted yet. `BUILT_IN_MISSING` (a `Set`) got `'stock'` added alongside `'image'` and `'sku'`, so the filter is answered in SQL rather than mis-read as a contributed-column id and sent to the field providers. No schema change - `stock_count`/`track_inventory` already existed on `shp_products` - so no backup round-trip gate. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop-variations.md`, "Browsing every variation".)
Previous entry: (**v0.5.1019: the space planner's customer half finally exists, a platform-wide contrast sweep across 21 modules, and core's plain-text emails stop losing their links.** Three separate pieces. (1) **space-planner 0.1.23.** Five server features had been complete, gated and rate-limited since 0.1.0 and had never once been called - `GET plans/[id]`, `/bom`, `/email`, `/quote`, `/share`, `/versions` - verified back through every tag, so never wired rather than regressed. The consequences were not cosmetic: the owner's four toggles under Shop > Space Planner governed nothing, `spl_plans.share_token` was never written so `/space-planner/shared/[token]`, its robots rule and the admin's "Shared" badge were unreachable, `spl_plans.quote_id` was never written so "Quotes asked for" was permanently 0, and version history was archived on every save and readable by nobody - which matters because several "this is recoverable" comments in that module lean on it. Four new dialogs in `SpacePlanner.tsx` (Share a link / Email it to me / Ask for a quote / Earlier versions), each saving the layout first the way `PhotoDialog` already did, plus a delivery column on the item list read off `/bom`. New props: `quoteAvailable`, `emailAvailable`, `turnstileSiteKey`, `member` - Turnstile matters, because `verifyTurnstile` fails CLOSED on a site that configures it, so a missing widget is those two buttons never working rather than a cosmetic omission. `glbExportEnabled` and `roomIdleFlagMonths` removed from `lib/config.ts` and the settings panel: no readers, and the first could not have done its advertised job anyway (the planner fetches GLBs into the browser to draw them, so devtools can save them - said out loud in the config comment, the README and the release notes rather than quietly deleted). `plan.added-to-cart` and `cartHandoffsThisWeek` removed: the handoff happens entirely in `lib/client/cart-bridge.ts`, so there was no server call to count. Keyboard: `Plan2d` gains a corner picker, arrow-key nudge (100mm, 10mm with shift), typed Across/Down, "Add a corner" (midpoint of the wall after the chosen one); `OpeningsBar` gains "Along the wall" for `offsetMm`; `ObstructionsBar` gains a typed centre dispatching `move-obstruction`. `LengthField` grew a `min` prop because a POSITION of nought is legal and a width of nought is not. `Plan2d`'s canvas goes `role="application"` -> `role="img"` (it never took focus or read a key); `View3d`'s canvas takes `tabIndex={0}` and `role="application"` for real, and `makeControls` now calls `controls.listenToKeyEvents(canvas)` - the comment claiming "the arrow keys are already orbit" was simply false, OrbitControls only binds keydown when asked. Terminology: space not room, layout not plan, the side panel's Cart tab is now Waiting, admin nav labels match their page headings. Contrast, module-local: the metre grid was `withAlpha(line, 0.55)` = **1.12:1** light / **1.24:1** dark against a 3:1 requirement, now faded ink at 0.52 = **3.27:1** / **5.02:1** / **3.60:1** on the PDF palette; unavailable variation pills were `opacity: 0.45` = **2.68:1** while deliberately staying clickable (so WCAG's inactive-component exemption does not apply), now `--color-text-secondary` plus a dashed edge = **5.39:1** / **7.16:1**. (2) **The muted-token sweep, 21 modules, 466 placements.** Every `--color-text-muted` in a module's admin components moves to `--color-text-secondary`. Measured, not eyeballed: muted is 2.11-3.30:1 across every surface those screens use, secondary is 5.07-7.16:1. The CORE TOKEN IS UNTOUCHED - this is a swap of placements, not a redefinition, and other things read it. Every one of the 21 got its own patch release; `modules.json` moves 22 pins. (3) **Core: `lib/email/render.ts` built its plain-text alternative from the TEMPLATE.** Tags were stripped before interpolation, so an anchor's href went with the tag and the address never reached text/plain at all - every "click here to confirm" email gave a plain-text reader nothing to click, across EVERY module. Merge values were then interpolated unescaped, so a typed product name carrying a tag landed as markup. New exported `htmlToPlainText(html)` works from the RENDERED body: links out first ("label (url)", skipped when the label already is the url or is a mailto:), then tags away, then entities decoded - and that order is load-bearing, because decoding first turns an escaped `&lt;b&gt;` back into a tag one line before the stripper runs. Space Planner's visible-plain-url workaround is deliberately left in place, since the module can be installed on an older core. 1776 tests project-wide, up 12.)
Previous entry: (**New agent skill `.agents/skills/dynamic-clearance` - puts the supplier's clearance stock on sale on Deskwell.** Tooling only: no core code, no module, no schema, nothing released. Three scripts, and only the last one writes. **`scripts/fetch-clearance.mjs`** reads `dynamicofficeseating.co.uk/collections/clearance` **without a cookie** - the collection's HTML renders as a not-found shell to anything that is not a browser, but `/collections/<handle>/products.json?limit=250&page=N` answers fine. That endpoint does **not** carry barcodes; `/products/<handle>.js` does, per variant, so the fetcher pays one extra request per listing to get them. Today's page: 16 listings, 31 variants, 9 with a barcode. **`scripts/plan-sale-prices.mjs`** matches against the live catalogue and computes `sale_price = ceil(clearance price x 1.06)` - the same 6% already inside `price = ceil(RRP x 0.37 x 1.06)`, and confirmed to reproduce live prices exactly (Chester Boutique Desk: RRP 522 -> 205.00 stored). It also swaps `shp_products.sku` to the clearance code (`OP000115` -> `PR1291`), because that is what the item is ordered under while it is on clearance. **That swap is why barcode is the first-choice match key**: once the SKU has moved, the catalogue code is no longer in the row to match on, and only the barcode still ties the two catalogues together. `shp_products.barcode` is populated on 20,825 of 21,222 rows and Dynamic returns the same EANs, so the join is exact. Second key is the supplier code, which Dynamic prints nowhere in its data but leaves at the front of every image filename (`OP000115_1_<uuid>.jpg`). Both keys together resolved 12 of 31 variants. **Everything else is guessed at and handed back for confirmation rather than written**: the planner **prints a numbered list to be relayed straight into the chat** - one entry per unresolved clearance variant, **one best guess** (not a shortlist), the clearance item's own Dynamic url, the guessed Deskwell product url, its price and a 0-1 confidence. Answers come back by number - `--confirm "1=yes,2=no,16=I003259"` - resolved against the previous run's `plan.json`, which is read before this run overwrites it; `yes` takes the guess, `no` records "we do not stock it" as a decision, a SKU overrides the guess, and anything unmentioned stays open for the next run. Decisions accumulate in `decisions.json` and are handed to a later run in a different folder with `--decisions`; each records the product it was made about, and Dynamic reuse their `PR` codes, so a decision whose product name no longer matches is **dropped rather than applied to whatever now wears that code** - a stale "we do not stock this" would hide a real item in silence. There is deliberately no spreadsheet in the loop. **Re-running is idempotent**, which took a third match key to achieve: a row already carrying the clearance code is one an earlier run swapped over, so it is the right row by construction - without that, every item first matched by its catalogue code came back a stranger on the second run, because the code it was found by is the very thing the first run replaced. Similarity is idf-weighted over the shop's own 21k names, so "trapezium" and "moonstone" decide matches while "office", "chair" and "black" barely register; price agreement against `ceil(was x 0.37 x 1.06)` is a **deliberately weak** tie-breaker at 0.08, because weighting it at 0.3 demoted two obviously-correct matches (the clearance "was" is the RRP of the day the item entered clearance and has drifted). Only rows carrying a SKU are ever suggested - a parent listing has none, and a confirmation has to name something. A confirmed pairing outranks every other key. **`scripts/apply-sale-prices.mjs`** is the only writer: one transaction, every row re-read `FOR UPDATE` and compared against what the plan saw (price, sale price and SKU), any drift aborts the whole run, and `--apply` is required or it rolls back and reports. Every run leaves `rollback.sql` naming the exact row ids, restoring both the previous sale price **and** the displaced catalogue code - which is the end-of-clearance move, not a hand-written UPDATE. Guards: a sale price not strictly below `price` is skipped (`isOnSale` would ignore it anyway, so writing it would only make the admin lie); `sku` is UNIQUE, so a clearance code already held elsewhere, or claimed by two rows in one run, is skipped with the clash named. Sale prices are already switched on for Deskwell (`shp_settings.config.enabledPriceTypes` = `["sale","cost","retail"]`), so nothing needs enabling. **Applied to live Deskwell 2026-08-10: 14 rows** - 12 matched outright, plus 2 confirmed by hand (Impulse Desk High Pedestal 60cm White, Impulse Semi-Circle Table Grey Oak). The 14 Flex cantilever visitor chairs, the Pose monitor arm, the 90x60 pin board (we stock the 60x45) and the Melia sofa were confirmed as not stocked and are recorded as such. `clearance_sale_2026_08_10/rollback.sql` holds the undo, including the displaced catalogue codes. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean; re-running the whole sequence afterwards asks nothing and changes nothing.)
Previous entry: (**space-planner 0.1.22, round two: a second and third review pass over the FIRST round's own diff, plus what both had missed.** Same rule as before - module dir only, zero core diff, `modules.json` pin NOT moved. Five fresh read-only reviews, two of them pointed squarely at the previous round's 47-file diff, because a fix that is subtly wrong is worse than the bug (it now looks handled). **Eight defects were in the first round's own new code**, which is the headline: (1) `createRenderJob` caught `error.code === '23505'`, but Prisma does not surface a raw query's SQLSTATE there - it reads `'P2010'` with the 23505 buried in the message (see `lib/db/stale-plan.ts:31`, which already documents this), so `RenderAlreadyLiveError` could NEVER fire and the second of two taps got an unhandled 500 - the exact case migration 004 was added for. Now `ON CONFLICT ("plan_id") WHERE "status" IN ('QUEUED','RUNNING') DO NOTHING` + `if (!row) throw`, **proved against a real Postgres 18 throwaway database** (conflict target matches the partial index; a finished job still permits a new one; other plans unaffected). (2) `applyShape` translated the vertices and the furniture by the origin shift but NOT `geometry.obstructions`, which was harmless while the client only tested `itemInsideRoom` and became live the moment `withDisplacedStaged` started reading `itemHitsObstruction` - dragging a wall 300mm staged every desk near where the pillar used to be. (3) `displacedItems` early-outs on `item.parentId`, so a child stranded outside a shrunken room was no longer rescued (the old client code tested every item) - `withDisplacedStaged` now adds stranded children back. (4) `stageFromCart`'s "read the tray BEFORE the await" fix was a no-op: `state.items` is a render-scoped constant inside a `useCallback` that depends on it, so before and after the await are the same array. Replaced with a `clear-staged` action the reducer resolves against current state. (5) The render rate limit counted every job row, including ones that never dispatched, so a shop with broken storage told the member "you have asked for a few pictures just now" having produced none - now `AND "started_at" IS NOT NULL`. (6) `interiorPoint` recomputed the inward normal assuming the canonical winding, 470 lines below `walls()`' own comment saying not to assume it; on a reversed outline (which a half-finished corner drag writes to localStorage) every probe went outwards, `clampItemIntoRoom` gave up, and furniture dragged through a wall stayed outside. Now uses `wall.inwardX/inwardY`. (7) The clamp's escape bias was a FRACTION of the distance to the interior point, so "flush against the wall" was 3mm out in a small office, 20mm in a warehouse, and different on facing walls - now a distance in millimetres. (8) The L-shape regression test passed against the pre-fix code (its own first assertion proved the box centre was INSIDE the room) - replaced with a 2000mm-leg L whose centre is genuinely in the notch, and **verified by reverting the fix and watching it fail**. **What both earlier passes had missed:** the measuring pass permanently lost every product sharing a model file with 200+ siblings - the route caps a batch at 200, the client pushed one row per product before checking the size, and `flush()` treated the resulting 400 exactly like a network blip, so `eclipse-plus-ii-office-chair-with-draughtsman-kit.glb` (262 products on Deskwell) dropped 286 measurements on every run, for ever; now sliced to 200 with a 4xx counted as lost immediately rather than retried. `listCategoriesWithoutDefaults` (added last round) counted raw `shp_product_categories` rows, but `resolveOne` only ever consults ONE category (`getPrimaryCategoryForProducts` = lowest id) and variation children inherit their listing's - so the worst-first list recommended categories where the work would change nothing (Cafe & bistro tables ranked 2nd, would have fixed 0) and buried the ones that pay (Screens & Partitions showed 8, truly 431). Rewritten as a CTE mirroring the resolver exactly, guarded with `to_regclass` for a site whose shop-variations migrations have not run, and **proved on a throwaway database** with a product filed in three categories (counted once, under the lowest id) plus its children. A category default saved with all three sizes BLANK re-badged every product under it from "no idea" to "typical for its category" while the generic 800x600x750 block was still doing the work - `usedDefault` was true from the generic fallback and the test was merely `categoryDefault ? ...`; split into `usedCategoryDefault`/`usedGenericBlock`, the editor now refuses an all-blank save, and 7 tests pin it (**verified they fail against the old rule**). Stop-then-Start on the rebuild created a fresh job at cursor 0 against the card's own promise that it picks up where it left off (`cancelBackfill` writes CANCELLED, which `getActiveBackfill` cannot see) - new `resumeStoppedBackfill()`; Stop is also available when a job is live but this tab is not driving it. A crashed render locked that plan out of pictures until the 03:20 cron, because migration 004's index made "one live job" absolute - `failStaleRenderJobs()` now runs at the top of the render POST. The dashboard widget declared no `permission`, so any admin saw the planner's numbers and product names and then hit a denial (core filters on exactly that field). `.form-input` does not exist anywhere in this codebase - 9 admin controls were rendering as unstyled browser defaults; all moved to core's `.field` wrapper. Five admin call sites printed the literal word "Forbidden" at an access-only user, and the rebuild's 403 read "The rebuild lost its connection. Press Start to carry on" - all now name the manage permission (and skip the refresh that would have wiped the message). **Public UX:** the browse panel said "Nothing matches that" for the first 250ms of every visit (loading started false); one failed catalogue fetch killed the panel permanently (no retry path, because the pager only renders past 24 results); Enter in draw mode hijacked every focused button; the sign-in wall raised the browser's own "Leave site?" box and, on Stay, left a note with nothing to click (now `goSignIn` clears `dirty` first); an expired session showed "Sign in to save your plans" as a red error with no link (now `NeedsSignIn` re-runs the sign-in path); route errors like `Not found` went straight into the shopper's alert bar (now `saveError` names the two cases worth naming and gives one plain sentence otherwise); hosting-provider text (`Fly said no (403): ...`, and a "paste a key in" instruction meant for the OWNER) reached customers - now logged server-side, sanitised on both the POST and the polling GET, with the REAL text still stored for the admin render log and the two genuinely shopper-appropriate messages kept via a new `SplFlyError.shopperSafe` flag. A ticked PDF picture that failed to capture vanished with no explanation; `buildItems` had no try/catch so a failed 3D build sat on "Putting the room together…" for ever AND cost the PDF export its full 15s timeout. Clash warnings were a red outline and nothing else - now said in words with a "Show me" button, which matters because the server stages anything left inside a column on the next save. The message bar is permanently mounted (a live region that appears with its text is one most screen readers never announce) and each message says "Note:"/"Problem:" (the two variants differed only by a 3px border colour). All four side panels stay mounted and hidden, so `aria-controls` no longer dangles. `--color-text-muted` measures **2.25:1 in light and 3.30:1 in dark** (verified by computing it, not by eye) - every customer-facing use moved to `--color-text-secondary` (5.39:1 / 7.16:1), including both disclaimers on the shared page a customer forwards to whoever signs the order; the delete button's own label went to full `--color-text`. Touch targets: the alert close (17x19px, the only way to dismiss a message) and the rename pencil joined the coarse-pointer block, as did the `-sm` control sizes that opted out of it. The room's name now travels through the sign-in wall in the scratch copy. **The counting rule moved to one place** (`lib/plan-counts.ts`, imported by both the server's `buildBom` and the browser's item list) after the previous round left the header and the paperwork counting different things - and companion product ids are now fetched, or they counted towards the total as nothing. A "from" price no longer multiplies into a definite line total. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, **191 module tests** (up from 160 at the start of the day; 1718 project-wide), **backup round-trip PASS 3/3 not skipped**, and migration 004 additionally proved end-to-end on a throwaway VPS database - applies in order, settles a planted duplicate-live-job mess with a correct `(created_at, id)` tie-break, refuses a second live job with 23505, still permits a finished one, and re-applies idempotently. Throwaway databases swept afterwards; `neondb` never named. **Round three, and the worst single defect of the day was here rather than in the diff:** `upsertFileMeta`/`upsertProductMeta` used `ON CONFLICT ("model_id")` / `ON CONFLICT ("product_id")`, but 001_initial creates BOTH of those as PARTIAL unique indexes (`WHERE "model_id" IS NOT NULL`, because a product-scope row leaves it null). Postgres refuses to infer a partial index as the arbiter without the matching predicate - **42P10 at plan time** - so every yaw correction, every "leave the detail alone" tick and every "mark as checked" the Model corrections screen has ever sent has failed, and the screen told the owner to check their broadband. Corroborated by the live data: all 11,600 `spl_model_meta` rows came from one bulk script, with 0 reviewed and 0 non-zero yaw offsets - not one row bears this code path's fingerprint. Both clauses now repeat the predicate, **proved against a throwaway Postgres 18** (bare form refused with 42P10; predicated form inserts, updates, and each single-field patch preserves the others). `lib/db/jobs.ts` had it right all along, in the same module. Also this round: **`buildBom` priced non-ACTIVE products** - the browser drops them (the public products route filters on status) while the server did not, so archiving a product a customer had saved made the screen show "-" and the PDF, email, quote and admin screen charge full whack for something shop's own checkout refuses to sell; `buildBom` and `findSnapshotDrift` now treat non-ACTIVE as gone and fall through to the snapshot, which is what `missing` is for. **`buildProductSnapshot` never recorded bundled companions** (`plan.items.map(item => item.productId)`), so once `buildBom` started pricing them, a screen bought with a desk and later deleted vanished from the list, the total AND the "no longer in the shop" banner - now `planProductIds`. **Column edits skipped the displacement rule entirely** (`add-obstruction`/`set-obstruction`/`move-obstruction` all just wrote geometry), and the consequence was backwards: the desk stayed inside the pillar on screen, while saving PUTs the room first and the room route ran the rule over EVERY OTHER layout, dumping their furniture into their trays. New `withObstructions` helper; four tests through the actions the toolbar actually dispatches, because the previous round's test went via `set-geometry`, a path the column UI never takes. **Renaming a room committed unsaved geometry**: the rename PUT had to send `geometry` because the schema made it mandatory, so typing a new name wrote whatever wall drag was in progress and restaged every other layout against it - geometry is now optional on that route, a rename skips validation, the displacement pass and the geometry write, and the client sends `{ name }` alone. **Yaw was unbounded**: nothing wrapped it, the save schema caps at 3600, so 41 presses of Turn 90 or one typed 99999 made every later save 400 for ever - and the bad value sat in localStorage, so reloading did not clear it. New `normaliseYaw` on both write paths. **"Start again" re-staged the whole basket** (the effect's "once per mount" comment was untrue - Start again sets `started` false and first-run sets it true), now guarded by a ref like its sibling. **The item quota counted the tray**, so arriving from a 20-line basket produced "that is 240 things in one room, and we top out at 200" about an empty room; it counts placed items now, the 400 hard cap carries a sentence instead of "Array must contain at most 400 element(s)", and the tray gained a bulk clear. Plus the half-landed `anyFrom` from round two (per-line said "From", both totals stated a flat figure), the ModelsScreen row label saying "Saving…" on all fifty rows, and the clash warning repeating the very live-region mistake the comment 40 lines above it warns about. **Round four, mostly fixing round three's own fixes plus two that had survived every pass.** The one that mattered most to a customer: **"Refresh from basket" permanently deleted furniture a redrawn room had put in the tray.** The tray holds two different things - what came from the basket, and what the room could no longer fit - and `clear-staged` took both, under a tab whose only buttons are "Refresh from basket" and "Clear the list", with no `commit()` so it was not even undoable. That is the module's flagship "reshaping a room never deletes your work" promise, deleted by the button next to it. Now `basketOnly` spares anything with no `basketLine`, and the refresh commits first. **My own round-three fix had made column drags far too eager**: `move-obstruction` fires per pointer move, so running the displacement rule on each one meant dragging a column across a room swept every desk it passed over onto the waiting list, and dragging it back brought none of them home - now gated on a `settle` flag like `set-shape` has always been, with the settle dispatched from Plan2d's pointer-up. Then the opposite error in the same helper: `withObstructions` staged everything CURRENTLY displaced rather than what this edit displaced, so renaming a column took a desk standing in it out of the room. Fixed twice over - the exempt baseline is the room without the column being edited (not the room a moment ago, which a settled drag has already changed), and a label-or-height-only patch does not run the pass at all. **`clashingIds` counted the `'obstruction'` sentinel as an item**, so one desk in a pillar read "2 things are overlapping" and "Show me" selected an id that does not exist; the sentinel is now an exported constant and filtered. Also: **`spl_dimension_cache.stale` had no writer at all** - the column exists, is indexed, and is read by all three freshness paths, so typing a category fallback changed precisely nothing until somebody ran the full 22k rebuild; new `markCategoryDimensionsStale` marks the category's products AND their variations (guarded on `to_regclass` for svr_variants), **verified on a throwaway Postgres**. **A save that changes nothing is no longer a version**: three UI paths save quietly on their way elsewhere (keeping a viewpoint, exporting a PDF, asking for a photograph), so twenty Export PDFs evicted every real version with twenty identical copies - and moved `updated_at`, which made a photograph arrive labelled "the room as it was, you have moved things since" when they had moved nothing. **Quote-only shops leaked prices everywhere except the PDF**: `pricesHidden` was consulted in exactly two places, so a shop that hides prices published its list prices on the share link - a page anybody with the url can open - and in the emailed plan. `buildBom` now answers it once and every surface consuming a `Bom` follows; the numbers stay on the object for the quote flow that needs them. Plus `itemQuotaExceeded` counting the tray, the yaw wrap reaching attached children, and the `'Saving…'` label on all fifty model rows. **Round five, and two of the three were round four's own fixes not doing what their comments claimed.** (1) `Bom.pricesHidden`'s doc says "every priced surface in the module consumes a Bom" - two do not. `/api/public/products` (a PUBLIC route) formatted `priceFormatted` unconditionally and returned a raw `price`, and the planner's on-screen item list, running total and browse panel are computed in the BROWSER from exactly that. So a quote-only shop said "price on application" on the PDF, the email, the share page and the quote while the planner itself printed real money and the public endpoint handed list prices to any caller - the same leak the fix's own comment cites as its reason for existing. Both `/api/public/products` and `lib/catalogue.ts` now resolve `pricesHidden` themselves; the route also returns `price: 0` and `priceVaries: false` when hidden, so nothing downstream can add a figure up. (2) The no-op-save guard compared `JSON.stringify` of both sides, which is only order-stable for schema-declared fields - `basketLine.meta` and `basketBundle[].meta` are `z.record(z.unknown())` bags, and jsonb canonicalises their keys by length then bytes while the incoming copy keeps the browser's order. product-addons writes `productAddons` before `modelContext`; jsonb stores `modelContext` (12 chars) first. So the guard could NEVER fire for a plan staged from the basket - the module's primary way in - and every quiet save went on archiving a version and moving `updated_at`. Now compared through a recursive key-sorting canonicaliser, **verified against the reviewer's exact repro** including that plain stringify really does differ and that a change inside the opaque bag is still detected. (3) A dead `pricesHidden` import left by the PDF fix, which `tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals` catches and the standing gates do not - the same gate gap noted below, twice in two rounds. **A second, independent round-five review then found four more, two of which had survived all five passes because nothing in the module contradicts them - only the live data does.** (a) **The photograph was of the plan as it stood when the machine got round to it, labelled with the plan as it stood when the button was pressed.** `createRenderJob` banks `plan.updatedAt`, but the page the worker photographs read the LIVE rows - so a shopper who pressed "Make a photo", was told to close the dialog, and then moved a desk during the 20-60s Fly cold start got a picture of the new layout stamped with the old date, described in the email as showing the room "as it was", and offered a re-render of the picture they were already looking at. Reshape the room in that window and the photograph is of a room nobody asked to photograph, from a viewpoint chosen for a different shape. Migration 001's own comment says the module avoids exactly this. The layout now travels with the job in `spl_render_jobs.params` (a `||` merge, so the later `uploadKey` write cannot clobber it, and `register()` only ever reads `uploadKey`); the render page prefers it and falls back to live rows for jobs queued before the change. (b) **The documented attribute preference order was decorative.** `HEIGHT_ATTRIBUTES = ['overall height (spec)', 'overall height', 'height']` says "in the order it prefers them" and `readAttributeDimensions` never read a name's position - it looped values on the outside and axes on the inside, taking whichever value arrived first, from a query with no `ORDER BY`. So heap order decided. On Deskwell **335 products carry both height names and 294 of them publish different figures** (a Chiro task chair says 108cm one way and 110.4cm the other), and the cache shows the split: **168 products took the preferred name, 126 took the second**. It is not even stable - a bulk update or a table rewrite reshuffles the heap and flips a different subset on the next rebuild. Today most of those also have a measured model so the wrong figure only feeds `parsed_from` and the conflict badge, but the moment a range loses its model the wrong number goes into the room. Loops inverted to walk each axis's list in order (a name present but unparseable still falls through to the next), **verified by reverting the fix and watching the new test fail with "expected 1104 to be 1080"**. (c) **Add-on contexts were resolved one at a time on an unauthenticated route**: a `for` loop with a sequential `await`, capped at 80 by the schema, each iteration 3 queries warm and around 11 cold - so a shopper arriving from a basket of desks-with-screens paid ~240 round trips in a row, on a PUBLIC route with a 60-second ceiling and a connection pooler the whole storefront shares. The three independent lookups are now batched across the whole set and the fabric resolves go through the same `FABRIC_CONCURRENCY` wave `resolveFabric` already uses. (Refactoring it dropped three things, all caught by reviewing my own diff rather than by any gate: the base entry's `mountOverride`, its recorded real size - a wall-hung unit is still wall-hung with its add-ons on - and the per-iteration `out.has(key)` test, which had been silently deduplicating requests. A plan holding six identical desks-with-screens sends one request per grouped line, so without it the batch resolved the same combination six times CONCURRENTLY, meaning all six missed the cache the first would have filled. `lib/model-resolver.test.ts` is new and pins all of it - 9 tests through the public function, each **verified to fail against the pre-fix code**; this path had no test at all while it was a sequential loop, which is how a refactor came to be the only thing standing between it and three silent regressions.) (d) **A size derived from the generic block was banked as "measured from the model".** With no recorded real size, `modelScaleFor` on an approximate item returns the median of the plausible planned/measured ratios - and for a `marker` item "planned" is the invented 800x600x750 block, which says nothing about the product. A five-metre bench desk exported at 5000x800x730 had its width ratio thrown out as implausible, kept 1.03 on height and 0.75 on depth, and was drawn at their median: the room showed a 4441mm desk, the flat plan adopted it as `glb`, the approx. badge came off, and the PDF and emailed plan quoted a size 11% out on every axis that nobody had measured. It never re-fires either, because adoption only looks at `marker`/`category_default`. A new `generic` flag (marker only, kept apart from `approximate` because a category default IS a statement about the product) draws it at the size its file was exported - the same answer the function already gives when no ratio survives. Plus the minors: `stageFromCart` had no cap, so 200 basket lines at 50 each is 10,000 reducer items and above ~1,700 the payload-size check fires first, replacing the carefully worded "take a few out" with a bare 413 - now capped at `MAX_ITEMS` less what is already placed, with a sentence saying how many are waiting and that the basket still has them (the count comes from a ref updated in an effect declared ABOVE the staging effect, so it is right for a saved plan opened with a basket waiting; writing it during render is a `react-hooks/refs` error). `ProductSnapshotEntry.parentId` and `.optionSummary` are documented as carrying a variant's identity and are hardcoded null/'' - the docs now say so, rather than being removed from a shape that is in every saved plan since the first release. Ladder rung 4 (`source = 'manual'`) has no writer anywhere and never has - the shopper's typed size lives on `PlanItem.manualSize` - so the comment says that too, while the guards stay. A plan deleted mid-render orphans the worker's upload (the job row cascades away, so the callback 403s before anything is filed): left as a 403 deliberately, since filing media for a job that cannot be authenticated is the one thing that check exists to prevent, and the cost is a few stray megabytes on a rare race. **Round six ran three independent reviewers - client state, server/data/admin, and UX/copy/accessibility - and came back with about fifty findings, of which the worst was a purchasing bug.** **"Add to basket" doubled the basket.** shop's `addToCart` is `existing.quantity += quantity`, and a line staged from the basket carries the basket's own `lineId` back with it - so the module's headline journey (basket → "plan your space" → put all four desks in the room → Add to basket) left eight desks, under a message saying four had been added. Plain lines doubled too, matched on product id. Now written as a SHORTFALL: placing eight of something the basket holds four of still takes it to eight, placing two leaves all four alone (this button says add, not remove), and `added: 0` says "your basket already holds everything in this room" instead of "0 things added". `lib/client/cart-bridge.test.ts` is new - 7 tests, **five of which fail against the old code**. **The 404 recovery advice was false and the room version was destructive**: `savedPlanId`/`savedRoomId` were never cleared, so "press Save again" PUT to the same dead id for ever, and the room message said "press Start again" - which throws the room outline away, so following the instruction destroyed the work it was meant to rescue. New `SavedCopyGone` error clears the id that 404ed (only that one - a dead layout does not mean a dead room). 413 now passes the route's own sentence through as well; "try again in a moment" was advice that could never work on a payload too big. **The floor plan kept the old theme's ink after a theme switch**: the canvas is painted from `getComputedStyle` in an effect keyed on geometry and selection, and the platform switches theme with a `data-theme` attribute entirely outside React - so the stage flipped to dark instantly and the plan stayed light-theme at about 1.1:1 until an unrelated pan forced a repaint. Now a `MutationObserver` on the attribute plus a `prefers-color-scheme` listener bump a nonce into the paint deps. **Two caps were quoted to the same shopper on different denominators**: the browser promised the schema's hard 400 (counting the tray) while the server refused at `maxItemsPerPlan`, default 200 (counting placed only), so a 250-line basket staged happily and then would not save. The setting now reaches the client and both the cap and the sentence use it; the refusal says "layout" rather than "room", which is what the cap is and what the owner's own label calls it. **Dragging a column or a door yanked the plan back to centre and then made the thing jump**: the re-fit effect guarded corner drags only, and columns and doors mutate geometry on every pointer move too - worse, their drag arithmetic reads back through the view, so the discarded pan became the next frame's delta. Panning to find a column, which on a phone is the only way to reach one, and then dragging it was reliably wrong. **Undo could strand the toolbar**: `obstructionSelection` is React state of its own and `load` never cleared it, so undoing a column left the columns toolbar on screen finding nothing, taking Undo, Redo, Save, Add to basket, More, Room and Start again away with it - the whole of the chrome on a phone. Both selections are now derived against the live geometry, so every path that removes a column fixes itself. **Selecting anything while Preview was open tore down and rebuilt the entire 3D scene** (the description memo depended on all of `state`, and `select` must return a new object) - every model re-cloned and every product photo re-requested for a change the scene does not contain. **The placeholder photo loader leaked GPU textures**: `disposeGroup` can only free what is attached when it runs, so a decal whose image was still in flight was added to an already-disposed group afterwards - the exact leak that function's own comment describes, arriving by the one door it cannot watch. A `DISPOSED` flag now disposes the late texture instead. **The 3D view could hang for ever** - `buildItems` had no timeout and a url that connects and never answers leaves the promise pending, so the busy flag (which the PDF export waits on) pinned permanently; now raced against a minute, with a Try again button where there was no way back at all. **The export dialog was an inescapable modal for up to ninety seconds** showing one unchanging word: Cancel disabled, Escape refused, backdrop refused. Now it names the phase it is in and closing is allowed. **Three admin numbers could only ever read nought**: `planner.opened`, `planner.opened-from-cart` and `planner.opened-from-product` have been declared since the first release and never recorded, so "Opened this week" told an owner nobody was using a module in daily use. Now recorded server-side. **`item.placed` was recorded only when a plan was first CREATED**, so everything added later counted for nothing - and that number is the whole worst-first ordering of "worth getting modelled" and of the Model corrections screen. Now also recorded on save, for products not already placed in that plan. **"Measurements we could not read" was 100% false positives** - 505 rows on Deskwell, every one of them a product whose text parsed perfectly well. `parsed_from` holds the text that SUCCEEDED unless nothing parsed at all, and the card selected non-empty `parsed_from` on a fallback row, which is exactly the shape of a partial parse. New migration `005_dimension_junk_text.sql` gives the junk a column of its own (it was being computed and discarded), backfills only the rows where the two meanings agree, and the card now selects on it. **The PDF, email and quote rate limits were resettable by deleting a plan** - they count events by the member's CURRENT plan ids, and `spl_events` records no member, which is why 004 moved the render limit onto `spl_render_jobs`. New `006_events_member.sql` adds `member_id`; the three limits now count per member. **Both migrations proved on a throwaway Postgres 18** - apply in order, backfill the genuine junk row, leave the partially-parsed row out, count per member, re-apply idempotently, and still leave the good row out on a second pass. Throwaway database and role dropped, prefix swept, `neondb` never named. Backup round-trip re-run afterwards: **PASS 3/3**, plus schema-coverage green for the two new text columns. **Two more public price leaks** (the pass-five sweep missed two doors): `/api/public/catalogue` masked the formatted string and still returned the raw number, and `/api/public/variations` returned the product page's whole payload - a `price` and a `salePrice` per variant, unauthenticated, with no check at all. Both zeroed on a quote-only shop, and the variation picker's own fallback formatting now prints the shop's wording rather than "£0.00". **`buildProductSnapshot` refreshed a withdrawn product's price**, defeating `buildBom`'s deliberate rule about pricing gone products from the snapshot: archive something at £100, re-price it to £250 for next season, and the next save quoted £250 under a line labelled "no longer sold". **`updateRoom` always rewrote the geometry**, against its own route's comment saying it did not - and what it wrote back is the geometry as READ, which substitutes a plain 4x3m box on any parse failure, so a rollback after a schema bump plus a customer renaming a room would overwrite their measured space with the default. Now guarded per column like `updatePlan`.
