Plus: the admin's ~40 `--color-text-muted` placements swept to `--color-text-secondary` (2.36:1 → 5.47:1 light; it was carrying every status and every error on two screens, the security warning about handing over supplier models, and the only instruction that stops an owner ruining a measuring pass); `--color-primary-contrast` does not exist anywhere in core, so its `#fff` fallback WAS the value on every primary button; dialog focus restoration was broken in four of five dialogs (the opener was captured in a passive effect, after React's own autoFocus had already moved focus INTO the dialog, so it refocused a detached node - now captured in a lazy state initialiser during render); the admin sizes dialog declared `aria-modal` and implemented none of it; number fields could not be edited by select-and-retype (the floor was enforced on every keystroke, so with a minimum of 10 no value starting with 1 could be typed, and clearing a min-0 box silently set "keep usage counts" to nought, which the sweep reads as "for ever"); five admin tables had no scroll container; no `<th>` had a `scope`; two progress bars had no role, name or value; "Everything has been looked at. Well done." was shown to a shop with no 3D models at all; "Tap a wall to put a opening in it"; "4 items are showing as a plain block - its picture would not load", which was also factually wrong (most are items over the model budget, which the planner chose not to draw); the share page said "the rest is unchanged" when withdrawn lines stay in the table and the total, with no badge to tell which - the badge the admin has always had; "Copy this into your own planner" opened an empty planner, because no copy parameter exists anywhere in the module; an expired share link was the site's bare 404 to whoever signs the purchase order; a `?product=` that no longer resolves staged nothing and said nothing; the catalogue's empty state said "try a shorter word" with an empty search box; an armed admin delete had no way to stand down; admin error messages were wiped by the refresh in their own `finally`; Refresh on the Pictures screen did nothing visible and left one blip's error up permanently against a five-second poll; "Row of four" spaced copies along +x by the item's width whatever way it was facing, so turning a desk 90 degrees and pressing it laid them out along the axis the desk no longer measured that way; the render worker's failure page printed black on black; the basket button was rendered on the server and removed after hydration, flashing in the cart header; and the shopper's Delete button opted out of the module's own touch rule with an inline 36px height that `@media` cannot reach, alongside the plan's zoom/fit buttons and the phone-only undo/redo pair at ~24px. **Reported, NOT fixed, and deliberately so:** `plan.added-to-cart` cannot be recorded without a new public endpoint, so "Sent to the basket" still reads nought; `roomIdleFlagMonths` joins `glbExportEnabled` as a setting with no reader anywhere (a fifth dead switch, and unlike the others there is no finished server feature behind it); full keyboard operability of the two canvases is a feature, not a fix - adding, moving and removing a corner, a door's position along its wall and a column's position have no non-pointer path at all; the module's remaining marginal contrast ratios (`--color-danger` at 4.48:1 on dark surface, the metre grid, the faded "not available" pills) are core token questions; and `.spl-root`'s grid track minimums may overflow below about 830 CSS px, which wants a device rather than a reviewer. **Verified but NOT acted on, because it is a product decision rather than a bug: five server features have no caller and four owner-facing switches therefore do nothing.** Grepped every client fetch of `member/plans`: the browser only ever calls `/render`, `/pdf` and the plan PUT. `GET plans/[id]`, `plans/[id]/bom`, `plans/[id]/email`, `plans/[id]/quote`, `plans/[id]/share` and `plans/[id]/versions` are complete, gated, rate-limited server routes that nothing has ever called - checked back through every tag from 0.1.0, so never wired rather than a regression. Consequences: **Shop settings → Space Planner → "What customers can do with a plan"** offers "Ask for a quote", "Email themselves the plan" and "Show delivery dates" whose only readers are those unreachable routes, and **`glbExportEnabled` has zero readers anywhere in the module** while carrying a paragraph warning the owner that customers could download their suppliers' 3D models - a risk that does not exist. `shareToken` is never set, so `/space-planner/shared/[token]`, its robots rule and the admin list's "Shared" badge are unreachable; `spl_plans.quote_id` is never written, so "Quoted" never shows and the "Quotes asked for" counter is permanently 0; version history is archived on every save and every reshape and no member can read it back, which is what several "this is recoverable" comments lean on. Building five features is not a bug sweep, and quietly deleting the switches would be removing behaviour without sign-off - so it is written down here and put to the owner. **Gate gap worth knowing:** a half-landed fix left `const anyFrom = ...` computed and never read, and NEITHER gate caught it - `tsconfig.json` does not set `noUnusedLocals` and the eslint config has no `no-unused-vars`. So "typecheck clean, lint clean" does not mean "every value you computed is used", and a fix that lands in one of three places looks finished. `npx tsc --noEmit --noUnusedLocals` reports zero for this module now and is worth running by hand after a multi-site change; turning it on project-wide is a core decision, not a module one. **Known, NOT fixed and deliberate:** core's `lib/email/render.ts` text-alternative bug (strips tags before interpolating, so an href's url is lost and a rawTag injects HTML into text/plain) affects every module's emails and is core's to fix - mitigated module-side with a visible plain url; `getPrimaryCategoryForProducts` picks the lowest category id rather than `shp_products.master_category_id`, which is arguably wrong for 36 Deskwell products but changing it moves live product sizes and wants the owner's say-so; the admin screens' own `--color-text-muted` use is left alone because every sibling module shares it and diverging one module is worse than the inconsistency.)
Previous entry: (**space-planner 0.1.22: whole-module bug sweep plus front-end, mobile and admin work.** Module dir only - zero core diff, `modules.json` pin NOT moved. Five parallel read-only reviews (client/geometry, API+DB, public UI, admin, output pipeline) then the fixes. **The two that cost money or truth:** (1) `buildBom`/`planToCartLines` iterated `plan.items` only, so `item.basketBundle` companions - the screens riding inside a combined desk model, drawn in the room and replayed into the basket by `addPlanToCart` - appeared in NO priced output: the item list, the PDF, the plan email, the shared page and the quote were all short by the price of every add-on in the plan. Both loops now also count `companion.qtyPerMain` per non-staged item; no double-count risk because `stage:'self'` companions become their own items and are excluded from the bundle list (cart-bridge 213-220). (2) `export-doc` page 1 hardcoded `bomTable(bom, false, '')` while `quotePage` honoured `pricesHidden`, so a quote-only shop posted its own trade prices on page 1 of the very document whose page 2 said "we will price this and come back to you"; the pdf route now reads `getQuoteConfigCached()` unconditionally (it read it only when the quote page was ticked) and threads `hidePrices`/`hiddenPriceLabel` into both pages. **New migration `004_render_and_event_indexes.sql`** (indexes only, no new tables/columns, nothing for the serialiser to learn; **backup round-trip run and PASSED, 3/3, not skipped**): partial unique `spl_render_jobs (plan_id) WHERE status IN ('QUEUED','RUNNING')` because "one live job per plan" was check-then-act and two taps of Make a photo started two paid Fly machines - the file settles any pre-existing duplicate to FAILED first, or the index would refuse to build; `spl_render_jobs (member_id, created_at DESC)` because the render rate limit counted `spl_events` against the member's CURRENT plan ids, so deleting a plan orphaned its events and bought a fresh allowance of machine time (now `countRecentRendersForMember`); `spl_events (event, plan_id, created_at DESC)` for the PDF/email/quote limiters. `createRenderJob` maps 23505 to a new `RenderAlreadyLiveError` the route answers with the running job. **Security/data:** `/api/public/products` filtered `items` on `status !== 'ACTIVE'` but returned `toClientModels(models)` unfiltered, so a guessed DRAFT id was refused a name and price and then handed a freshly signed url to its geometry, fabrics and real size - models are now filtered by the same allowed-id set. `render-callback` ran `register()` (a plain `prisma.media.create`) BEFORE learning the job was already settled, so an at-least-once retry filed a second Media row against the same stored object - a row nothing references, which is exactly what the unused-media sweep deletes, taking the shared blob and the real picture with it; the settled check now comes first. `resolve-dimensions` banked a marker row for ids with no product row (never freshness-testable, so every call re-wrote them - up to 400 caller-chosen ids per request inflating the admin size report until the nightly sweep, which then re-created them); now `if (updatedAtById.has(id))`, matching `applyMeasurements`. `media-usage-provider` + `media-reference-rewriter` were blind to `product_snapshot` image urls on `spl_plans`/`spl_plan_versions` (jsonb, stored verbatim) - after a product is deleted that copy is the only description left, and the sweep was pointing at it. Cron sweep now `timingSafeEqual`; `payloadTooLarge` measures `Buffer.byteLength` not UTF-16 length (a cap named in bytes admitted ~3x in non-Latin scripts); admin plan search escapes `%`/`_` (a search for "50%" matched every plan); `archivePlanVersion` gained `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` (MAX(version)+1 inside the INSERT, so two saves 500'd the loser); `updatePlan` now writes only the columns named in the patch (the quote route's `{quoteId}` patch put back a whole snapshot read moments earlier, undoing a save that landed in between); GDPR export sized from the shop's own quota (`maxRooms*maxPlans`, was a flat 500 under a 625 default) and every render not the first 20. **Geometry/reducer:** new `normaliseGeometryWinding` renumbers openings when a reversal renumbers walls (wall m -> n-2-m, offset mirrored) - one gesture dragging a corner across the room could leave the outline simple-but-reversed and the front door on the opposite wall; all four call sites moved to it. `clampItemIntoRoom` walked towards the BOUNDING BOX centre, which in an L-shape sits in the cut-out, so an item dragged out was "clamped" into the notch - new `interiorPoint` probes wall-midpoint normals when the box centre is outside. The reducer judged displacement with `itemInsideRoom` alone while the room route used `displacedItems` (obstructions too, children follow parents), and the client's answer was written over the server's on the next save - now both use `displacedItems` via `withDisplacedStaged`. `move-items` banked what the parent ACTUALLY did (snap can add 250mm of wall pull and rewrite yaw) and orbits children about the parent's new centre, as `rotate-items` already did; `attach` guards the one-level invariant from BOTH ends. `clearanceAround` measured corners-to-edges one way only, missing the commonest close pass (a neighbour's corner against the middle of a long edge) and over-reporting the walkway several-fold. **Three.js:** `disposeGroup` never disposed `material.map`, and placeholder product photos (the 19-in-20 path) re-upload on every item nudge with THREE.Cache off - one leaked texture per nudge; label-sprite textures stay exempt (shared LRU). `RenderFrame` keyed its model map by bare productId while the live view keys composites `productId@@context`, so a product placed both plain and with add-ons lost one to the other and rendered grey boxes; `SceneNode` gained `context` and the `realMetres` lookup tries the composite entry first (a desk+screens model was scaled by the bare desk's recorded height). **Public UI:** VariationPicker's option-list effect depended on a callback the panel cannot hold stable (it closes over the room's `placeProduct`), so ANY furniture drag re-ran the fetch and wiped the shopper's picks - now a ref. `fetchProducts` throws on !ok instead of answering `[]` (an empty answer read as "no longer sold" told customers their basket was discontinued over a dropped connection); `stageFromCart` reads the tray ids BEFORE the await (a refresh took a just-placed item back out of the room). NumberField holds text while focused (clearing it read `Number('')` = 0 and teleported the item to the origin, and every digit banked an undo step); Plan2d's ResizeObserver reads `fit` through a ref (it re-fitted to mount-time geometry after any resize); draw mode ignores a duplicate tap; View3d skips `registerCapture` when WebGL is unsupported (PDF export waited out the full 15s timeout); SpaceDeleteButton shows its error in the armed branch; saved-view menus close on outside click and Escape; FirstRun's typed-measurements screen is a real form (Enter did nothing); photo dialog gained a download link; catalogue paging scrolls back to the top. Dialog backdrops are `position: fixed` at every width (on desktop they only covered the canvas, leaving the toolbar and side panel clickable behind an `aria-modal` dialog); the phone view-chip menu escapes the strip's forced overflow clip; `.spl-eye-label` uses `--spl-muted` (the sub-AA token this sheet exists to avoid). **New front-end:** running room total in the header, item count on the Item list tab, and undo/redo on the stage for phones (they were behind More, with no Ctrl+Z). **Admin:** Rooms & plans rows open to the full priced item list + room facts + a two-step delete (the detail and DELETE endpoints existed and nothing called them); Sizes gained a category fallback editor with a worst-first "no fallback yet" list counting affected products (`listCategoriesWithoutDefaults`); Model corrections shows product names beside filenames. Fixed: `takeDown` never checked `response.ok`, so a 401/403/500 body was written in as a WorkerView and the card claimed success while the Fly app still billed; settings GET serialised an un-awaited `renderWorkerConfigured()` promise (`{}` is truthy, so every site claimed the picture service was set up); the `mounted` ref pattern in all four screens left `mounted.current` false forever under Strict Mode (dev-only, but every screen sat on "Loading…"); `provisionRenderWorker` orphaned the previous Fly app; `waitForMachine`'s 30s Fly-side wait raced the 30s local abort so the friendly timeout and proactive destroy were unreachable; ModelsScreen disables all rows during a save; settings surfaces the zod message and carries real `min` floors; `cactus.module.json` teardown was missing `spl_render_worker` - the table holding the Fly org token. **Known, NOT fixed (core, not module):** `lib/email/render.ts` builds the text alternative by stripping tags from the template BEFORE interpolating, so any url living in an href is stripped with its tag and a `rawTags` value injects raw HTML into text/plain - affects every module's emails, so the module-side mitigation is a visible plain url in both templates. Checks: `npm run typecheck` clean, `eslint .` clean, 165 module tests green (5 new: winding-flip opening remap, L-shape clamp, child-follows-parent-snap, both-ends attach guard, winding no-op), backup round-trip PASS.)
Previous entry: (**v0.5.1017: pin shop-variations 0.1.124 - fixes the locked buy button growing instead of shrinking.** 0.1.123 (pinned in v0.5.1013) gave the new `FitLabel` a host span at `width: 100%`; a nowrap line's min-content is the whole sentence, so the button inherited an intrinsic minimum the length of the reason, grew to fit it, and shoved itself off the end of the quantity stepper rather than shrinking the words. Host is now `width: 0; min-width: 100%`, so percentages carry no weight in the button's own sizing. Also: a message too long to read at the 11px floor on one line now wraps to a genuinely-measured second line inside the pill instead of clipping mid-word. See the `FitLabel` entry below for the full mechanism.)
Previous entry: (**v0.5.1016: pin product-3d-views-for-shop 0.1.87.** Registry bump only - `modules.json` v0.1.86 -> v0.1.87, no core diff. Ships the per-file real size for add-on-context models (`FabricConfig.modelSizes` + the **Sizes with add-ons in shot** panel section) described in the entry below. Deskwell's own `modules.json` still pins separately, so this reaches that install only when its owner updates.)
Previous entry: (**p3d 0.1.87: a model tagged to an add-on combination can declare its own real size.** New `FabricConfig.modelSizes` - `{ modelUrl: '130cm' }`, keyed by `modelScaleKey` like the measurements beside it - read by `composeFabricBundle` in place of the product-level size wherever the SHOWN file has an entry. Why: the calibration is real size over MEASURED size, and the measured half (`modelHeights`) is the file's own bounding box. A context-tagged file shows the product WITH an add-on on it, so its box is taller, and calling that box 86.5cm re-scales every finish on the file - the product's own parts included - by the ratio of the two. Silent: the colours all paint, only the weave is wrong. Admin: FabricConfigPanel grows a **Sizes with add-ons in shot** section listing every distinct tagged file (plus any file already carrying a value, so nothing goes un-editable), each with a size box, a red 'no size' tag when it is missing or unparseable, and the file's measured units + derived cm-per-unit beside it so a mm/cm slip shows on the spot. An emptied box DELETES the key rather than storing `''`. `parseSwatchCm` moved from `lib/fabric/resolve.ts` to the leaf `lib/fabric/constants.ts` (re-exported from resolve, so callers and tests are unchanged) because the panel is a client component and resolve.ts imports Prisma. Storage unchanged - one more key in an existing jsonb blob, absent = previous behaviour exactly, so no migration and no backup gate. tsc/eslint clean, 191 module tests green. Wiki: Product-3D-views.md gains 'Models that show an add-on as well' and 'Showing a product with its add-ons'.)
Previous entry: (**pad 0.1.7 + space-planner 0.1.20: the combined desk+screens model reaches the planner again.** Regression from pad 0.1.2 (accessories buy on their own button): that change deleted `mainModelContext` and made every add-on line `stage: 'self'`, so the desk's basket line carried no `contexts` at all - the planner staged a base desk plus a loose screen, exactly the reported symptom on `air-back-to-back-height-adjustable-bench-desk`. Not a data problem: 504 `p3d_models` rows are tagged `context='screens'` and the pad link's `model_context_key` is set. Fix moves the truth from the main line to the ADD-ON lines, because with per-add-on buttons the main line is stamped before anyone knows what it will end up with, and the shopper can remove an add-on on the basket page long after the box has unmounted. New `addonContextKey(r)` (extracted from `activeContextKeys`) is written onto each add-on line as `modelContext.contextKey` + `valueIds`; a line carrying one is inside the combined model, so `stage: 'none'` returns (it no longer leans against the wall as a loose panel). `mainModelContext(group)` now DERIVES `{contexts, extraValueIds, bundleKey}` by reading those add-on lines back out of the basket, and is stamped on the main line from both directions: `addAddonToBasket` (which also now finds the group's ALREADY-stamped main line - the old lookup only matched an unstamped one, so from the second add-on on it silently did nothing) and the purchase-companion `collect` (accessories-first buying order). Both meta writes go in ONE `setLineMeta` call because the first write gives a plain line a `lineId` and moves the key a second call would target. New marker `contextsFrom: 'bundle'` on the main bag tells the planner the list is a re-derivable summary: `cart-bridge.cartAsStagedItems` now recomputes contexts from the group's live lines when it sees the marker (so removing the screens in the basket puts the plain desk back in the room) and keeps the stored list without it (older baskets/plans). Wiki: Product-Add-ons.md "Space planner" section rewritten + a developer bullet documenting the whole meta contract. tsc/eslint clean, planner suite 160 green; no schema, no core diff, no backup gate.)
Previous entry: (**Catalogue-palette repair on model upload.** `lib/media/model-palette-pin.ts` takes a tiny pCon shading atlas off any material whose faces can no longer read one cell of it - the cause of banded desk tops on four live Air B2B GLBs - and pins the mean value it stood for into the material's own factors; wired into `optimiseModelBytes`, which now returns a repaired file even when it is not smaller. Offline gate `~/.cactus-3d-tools/preflight-3d-upload.mjs` + shop-wide `sweep-shop-models.sh`.)
Previous entry: (**v0.5.1009: pin live-chat 0.1.14.** Follow-up to v0.5.1008, which released live-chat 0.1.14 (the `admin/availability` handler-type fix) but deliberately left the pin on 0.1.12 because 0.1.13 was another session's released-but-unpinned change. Owner asked for it: pin now moves 0.1.12 → 0.1.14, carrying 0.1.13's console-poll effect tidy with it. Both versions are internal only - no runtime or user-visible change in either.)
Previous entry: (**pad 0.1.4: add-on pictures open in a picture modal, variation shots first.** New `components/public/AddonImageModal.tsx` (portal, overlay, big stage + thumbnail strip, prev/next, ArrowLeft/Right + Escape, active thumb `scrollIntoView`, group hairline in the strip, `dedupeGalleryImages` helper exported for the callers) - deliberately NOT the Learn more iframe modal, which frames the whole details page. The box's row thumbnail and the showcase card's picture became buttons that open it. Image order is the requirement: the row's `displayImages` THEN `selector.baseImages`, deduped by URL keeping the earlier position, so a picture filed under both appears once as a variation shot. `displayImages` is the single source for the thumbnail AND the modal (they cannot disagree): the resolved `variant.imageUrls` when complete, else `settledVariantImages()` - first ENABLED variation carrying images that answers every value settled so far (aliases via svr's `variantAnswersTo`/`valueToOptionMap`). That partial fallback was the reported defect: colour locked by the link, fabric still open, nothing resolves, and the row fell back to the listing photograph - routinely a different finish beside a colour the shopper cannot change. Deliberately MORE eager than svr's own gallery, which waits for a complete combination. A `plain` add-on contributes no variation shots. Caption/alt say "the variation shown", not "your chosen combination", because a partial match is not a finished choice. The SHOWCASE (tab/block, a separate island inside shop's tab strip with none of that state) was still on the listing photograph: new `lib/addon-images.ts` window seam `cactus-shop-addon-images` (`{parentProductId, images: Record<linkId,string[]>}`, `window.__cactusAddonImages` snapshot, JSON-deduped publish, same shape as model-context/selection-broadcast) - the box publishes its `displayImages` for every add-on incl. chain children, ticked or not; the showcase snapshots on mount + listens, and uses them for the card picture AND the modal (variation first, then `card.images`, deduped - identical rule to the box). Chose publish-and-repeat over re-deriving in the showcase: re-deriving means shipping the whole box payload into the tab a second time and keeping two copies of the maths that can disagree. An add-on with nothing better than its listing shot is ABSENT from the bag (not empty), so "no box on the page" and "no variation pictures" both fall back to the server-rendered listing picture. Markup change in the box: `.pad-head` is no longer a `<label>` wrapping everything (interactive content in a label is invalid) - it is a div, the checkbox got an id, and `.pad-title` is the label. Both new buttons take `disabled={preview}` rather than switching element type, so the Puck editor and RSC paths keep identical markup. Showcase cards carry a new OPTIONAL `images` field (payload caches predate it; absent = unclickable picture as before), fed from `selector.baseImages` in `showcase-payload.ts`. ALSO in 0.1.4: **add-on reordering** in the product editor's Add-ons tab - per-row "n of m" + ↑/↓ (shop's CategoriesScreen pattern), new `POST admin/products/[id]/links/reorder` (`{orderedIds}`, 409 unless the list is exactly that product's links, `reorderLinks()` renumbers in one `$transaction` with every statement pinned to product_id as well as id). `position` was always the sort key for every read, so the order lands on the box AND the showcase with no storefront change. The editor moves optimistically and does NOT re-fetch after a move - a re-fetch replaces each `link` object and resets unsaved drafts; rows are keyed by link id so component state survives the swap. tsc/eslint clean; no schema, no core diff, no backup gate. **Also fixed, found by regenerating the router:** live-chat's `admin/availability` route failed the generated router's `ApiHandlerModule` type - TypeScript normalises a union of object literals returned from ONE function by adding the missing keys back as optional-undefined, so `resolveToken`'s success branch carried `error?: undefined`, `'error' in r` could not narrow it away, `r.error` read as `Response | undefined` and both handlers inferred `Promise<Response | undefined>`. Now an explicit `ResolvedToken` union + `if (r.error)` truthiness narrowing (runtime behaviour identical - errorResponse always returns a Response). **The lesson is the bigger half**: `next.config.ts` sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true`, so `tsc --noEmit` is the ONLY gate on module API handlers - and it type-checks them only through `lib/modules/router.ts`, a gitignored generated file that `npm run typecheck` does NOT regenerate (only `npm run dev` and `npm run build` do). A module route added since the last generation is invisible to the gate, which is how this sat unnoticed since live-chat v0.1.5. **Closed**: `package.json` `typecheck` is now `node scripts/generate-all.mjs && tsc --noEmit` (generate-all is 0.4s, pure gitignored-file writes - no checkout, no database, no network, the same generators `npm run dev` runs), so the gate can no longer read a stale router. A bare `tsc --noEmit` still can - run the npm script.)
Previous entry: (**Product add-ons decoupled from the main add + same-origin framing.** Core `proxy.ts`: `frame-ancestors 'none'`→`'self'`, `X-Frame-Options DENY`→`SAMEORIGIN` - the pad "Learn more" modal iframes the site's own `/shop/products/<slug>/details` view and the old policy blanked it (dev never shows this: `withSecurity` is production-only). pad: new mapping mode `recommend` ("Pick a recommendation, changeable" - admin-picked value via the shared `fixedValueSlug`, shown pre-selected, overridable, degrades to plain choose when the value vanishes; zod enum + editor + coverage warning extended); each add-on row now carries its OWN qty input + Add to cart button (styled to mirror svr's add-to-cart part) and add-ons never ride along on the main add - the purchase-companion provider now only stamps the main line's group meta (and only when related add-on lines are already in the basket), while `addAddonToBasket` retro-stamps a main line already there via `setLineMeta`, so grouping forms in either buying order; group key is `deterministicGroupKey(mainTargetId, [])`; addon lines stage per-line in the planner (`stage: plannerStandalone?'self':'none'`, no combined-context stamp on the main line any more); row thumbnail switches to `variant.imageUrls[0]` once resolved; Learn more button padded; modal gained a Close button footer; Accessories detail tab order 15→25 (now after Specification 20); line-resolver drops the "Add-on for" field on grouped lines (the ↳ caption already says it - it printed twice), orphans keep it. shop: cart full/table/drawer suppress the divider between a line and its own attachments and the attachment name cell/row lost its vertical border-left. Data (live Deskwell, backed up + rollback in session scratchpad): 396 bench-screen children's Range retagged Unknown/Furniture→"Impulse Plus & Sch Screens" so advanced-shipping scope matches every variation (360 previously matched no delivery service).)
Previous entry: (**live-chat 0.1.12 pinned (core v0.5.1005) - the notifications that never arrived.** Two stacked causes, console closed OR open on the list: (1) every status fetch was a same-URL GET with no cache directives - the browser's HTTP cache served stale JSON to the 15/30s polls indefinitely, so the unread count froze until a hard refresh; `cache: 'no-store'` on every console/inbox fetch + `Cache-Control: no-store` on the conversation route responses. (2) The cable-event refresh fired exactly once, at event time - but the socket event comes straight from the chat server while the MIRROR is still being written by the (Sidekiq→Vercel) webhook, so the read raced the write and saw the old count; refreshes now staggered 0/2.5/8s. Lesson: any module admin poll endpoint should send no-store explicitly - Next API responses carry no cache headers by default and browsers will heuristically cache them.)
Previous entry: (**live-chat 0.1.11 pinned (core v0.5.1004) - the polish batch.** (1) Straight-to-conversation: `jumpToMessages()` assigns the widget iframe's src with only a `#/messages` fragment change - an in-place hash navigation, no reload - landing on the composer and skipping the widget home screen's Start/Continue interstitial; verified against a fresh visitor on the live server before implementation (route holds, no bounce). (4) Dark mode: widget gets `chatwootSettings.darkMode = siteIsDark ? 'auto' : 'light'` from the root `data-theme` at boot (Chatwoot has no hard 'dark'; the site-dark+OS-light corner stays light, documented); the console/inbox get a full `[data-theme="dark"] .lc-*` override block.)

Previous entry: (**live-chat 0.1.8 pinned (core v0.5.1001) - cold-boot honesty for the widget.** Root cause of the "disappearing widget": BOTH field repros landed while the chat machine was mid-boot after a restart (image update, then the rack-attack restart) - `window.$chatwoot` appears while the server is still coming up, so 0.1.6's existence-only ready-poll fired, hid the bubble, and left a 0x0 panel. The poll now also requires `.woot-widget-holder` to have real height (>50px); a 45s deadline removes the dead holder and shows "Chat unavailable - tap to retry" (tap reloads). The earlier 429s in the console were Chatwoot's Rack::Attack per-IP throttle from rapid testing - `ENABLE_RACK_ATTACK=false` now set on the machine (single-tenant; Turnstile is the abuse gate), see the 0.1.7 entry.)
Previous entry: (**live-chat 0.1.7 pinned (core v0.5.1000) + Rack::Attack off on the chat machine.** The embedded widget going BLANK mid-test (bubble clicked, panel opened empty, bubble gone) was Chatwoot's own per-IP Rack::Attack throttle returning 429 on /widget after tonight's rapid test-clicking - standalone /widget kept working once the window expired, which is what made it look haunted. `ENABLE_RACK_ATTACK=false` staged on the Fly app + machine restart: a single-tenant server behind our own site does not want per-IP throttles (Turnstile is the abuse gate). 0.1.7: boot GET hides the widget entirely (`enabled: false`) when nobody is online AND the site has no SMTP_* configured - an offline message would otherwise land where no notification can follow; reappears next page load once either changes.)
Previous entry: (**live-chat 0.1.6 pinned (core v0.5.999) - journey context + three widget behaviours.** Journey: the widget now sets the page attributes as CONVERSATION custom attributes as well as contact ones (the webhook mirrors conversations, not contacts - the original wiring could never surface them), the webhook merges `custom_attributes` over `additional_attributes` into lc_conversations.meta (Chatwoot's natively captured `referer` becomes the fallback "on page" display), and the consent gate is SERVER-decided via boot GET `journeyGate` - core's layout defines `window.__cactusConsent` even with the banner disabled, so the client-side "no banner = allowed" branch could never fire and the journey was always blocked on bannerless sites. Widget: the `chatwoot:ready` listener attaches BEFORE `sdk.run` with a 500ms poll fallback (warm caches fired the event before the old listener existed - bubble stuck on "Starting…"), the bubble returns when the chat panel closes (`chatwoot:opened`/`closed` events; previously closing the panel left NO opener at all), and boot GET reports agent availability so an Offline switch shows "Leave us a message" instead of the online copy.)

Catalogue-placed items remain bare product ids. tsc/eslint clean, planner suite 160 tests green; no schema/migration, so no backup gate.)

Previous entry: (**v0.5.993-995: footer module blocks, CSP_EXTRA_ORIGINS, and a version-bump correction.** v0.5.993: `footerPuckConfig`/`footerPuckRscConfig` never spread the module by-layout-type buckets, so `layoutTypes: ["footer"]` rendered nothing on the public footer and never reached the footer editor palette - the header always had both spreads (`headerModuleBlocks` / `moduleRscByLayoutTypeWrapped['header']`); footer now mirrors it (`footerModuleBlocks` + conditional Blocks category + RSC spread). v0.5.994: the `proxy.ts` CSP allowed script/connect/frame only from 'self' + Stripe (+ media worker), so live-chat's click-to-load ended at "Chat unavailable" - new generic env `CSP_EXTRA_ORIGINS` (space/comma-separated https origins, regex-validated) appends each origin to script-src, frame-src, img-src and connect-src plus a wss: twin (an explicit https origin does not authorise the WebSocket upgrade in every browser); Deskwell's Vercel env carries `https://chat.deskwell.co.uk`. v0.5.995: the 993/994 commits shipped with package.json still reading 0.5.992 (broken release chains skipped the bump), so an install updating to them self-reports 0.5.992; 995 corrects the version and carries these notes. Also 2026-08-08 (**A card's short description can fill the row's spare space** - `shop` **0.1.199**, pinned in core **v0.5.983**; core diff is this file, `modules.json`, `package.json` + `wiki/Shop.md`. Chris, with two category screenshots: products with fewer options leave a big blank band at the bottom of their cards (grid rows stretch every card to the tallest neighbour); wanted the short description under the name filling ONLY that band, ellipsis at the cut, "i really dont want the description to then make the card even longer though", working at 3 desktop and 2 mobile columns. The `ShopCardBlurb` part's `lines` select gains a fourth value **`fill`** ("Fill the spare space") in its own `blurbLineOptions` list (the Name part keeps the fixed 1-3; a name that breathed with its neighbours would look broken). **The never-taller guarantee is structural, not measured**: fill mode renders a `.shop-card-blurb-fill` wrapper - `flex:1 1 0;min-height:0;position:relative;overflow:hidden` - whose paragraph is absolutely positioned (rule scoped `.shop-card .shop-card-blurb-fill .shop-card-blurb`, also `visibility:hidden` + `-webkit-box`), so the wrapper contributes ZERO intrinsic height (basis 0, only out-of-flow content) and the row is still sized purely by pictures/names/options/prices; the wrapper then grows into whatever slack the grid stretch hands the card. New client island `components/public/ShopCardFillBlurb.tsx` measures that slack (ResizeObserver on the wrapper, `lines = floor((wrap.clientHeight - p.offsetTop)/lineHeight)` - offsetTop pre-pays the paragraph's own top margin so the breathing gap is not clipped off the last line), sets `-webkit-line-clamp` to the whole-line count and lifts visibility; under one whole line it stays hidden (no lone "…" on the row's tallest card). Hidden-until-measured doubles as the no-JS story: scripts off, the card looks exactly as before the option existed. Breakpoints re-measure themselves - the observer fires when the card crosses 3-col -> 2-col or `--shop-card-scale:.75` shrinks the type. The editor scoping trick: the card layout editor has NO `.shop-card` ancestor, so the absolute/hidden rules never apply there and the sample paragraph stays a plain in-flow element - same component, same markup, parity by CSS scope. In `beside` mode the card is a grid not a flex column, so a fill blurb simply gets no slack and shows nothing (graceful, documented limitation); `fill`(overlay) cards are still flex and work. **Deskwell's live card layout row was deliberately NOT touched**: its running module (0.1.198) would render `lines:'fill'` as NO clamp at all (`clampStyle` -> `Number('fill')` NaN -> undefined -> full-length blurb ballooning every card), so the part must only be switched to fill AFTER the install updates. 416 of the live products carry a short description (read-only count). Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean. No schema change, no backup gate. No dev server, no build, per standing rules.)

Also 2026-08-08 (**Text option values on cards wrap like prose, not like chips** - `shop-variations` **0.1.119**, follow-up to 0.1.118, pinned in core **v0.5.982**. Chris, with two desk-card screenshots: "image 1 shows the first option moved to the second line, despite the same option in image 2 showing on the same line". 0.1.118 made every value an atomic inline-block chip - right for swatch dots, wrong for phrases: "1 Drawer Fixed Pedestal," a whisker too wide for the space beside the label fell WHOLE onto the next line (image 2 only fitted because its single shown value carries no comma - one value, no `lastComma`). Two-part fix in `components/public/card-option-rows.tsx`: (1) text values are `display: inline` with a trailing space INSIDE each wrapper (a space is a break opportunity, a margin is not; hidden values take their space with them; comma still glued inside so a line never opens with one) - words now wrap mid-phrase exactly like the pre-0.1.118 prose, but with the label sharing the line. (2) The live card layout has `preview: "yes"` (checked read-only in Deskwell `Layout` row cmrntf7g10007l404uwucnvr7), and a `<button>` is an ATOMIC box by CSS specification - it can never fragment across lines - so interactive TEXT values became `<span role="button" tabIndex=0>` with Enter/Space in onKeyDown; swatch triggers stay real buttons (atomic is correct for a dot). `InteractiveValue.onClick` widened to a structural `{preventDefault; stopPropagation}` so keyboard events pass. `components/public/FitOptionRow.tsx` measurement now reads each value via `getClientRects()` (first fragment = start, last = end; line numbers from clustering fragment tops within half a line height) since a text value can now span lines; marker-fit check uses the END fragment, and the text gap falls back to ~0.35em where there is no margin to read. No schema change, no backup gate. tsc, eslint, 141 module tests green. NOTE: the 0.1.118 entry below was accidentally dropped from this file by the v0.5.981 commit (written from a stale copy) and is restored here.)

Previous top entry: 2026-08-08 (**Only one value per row is marked on a card preview** - `shop-variations` **0.1.117**, pinned in core **v0.5.978**; one line in `components/public/card-option-rows.tsx`. Chris, on the feature released an hour earlier: "when we hover over an value, the previous value for the same option stays enabled ... so 1 option is showing two values as selected". The mark was `interaction.active || interaction.pinned`, so a TAPPED value went on drawing while the shopper hovered a different one in the same row - two values looking chosen, one photo, and the picture could only agree with one of them. Now drawn from `active` alone, which is `picks[optionIndex]` and therefore single-valued by construction: exactly one value per row, always, and it is by definition the one the photo is showing. `pinned` is kept and still feeds `aria-pressed` (it is genuinely a pressed toggle) and still survives leaving the card - `picks` reverts to it on card mouseleave, which is what re-lights it. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, `modules/shop-variations` **136 pass / 0 fail**. No wiki change needed: the page already said "whichever value the picture is currently showing is marked", which is now true rather than aspirational.) Previous top entry: 2026-08-08 (**Pointing at a value on a product card shows that variation's photo** - `shop-variations` **0.1.116**, module dir only, no core diffs, no schema change, so no migration and no backup-gate trigger. Chris: on category pages, hover/click 120cm and see the 120cm desk, then walnut and see 120cm walnut, then a black frame and see all three - "and also, show the variation image but if there's a variation 3d model, ensure that if they click the 3d icon they see the same 3d model as the image". **The 3D half needed no code at all**: shop's card carousel already hands its active image's `sourceId` to the overlays (`ShopCardMedia` -> `CardOverlayProps.activeSourceId`), and `CardModel3dOverlay.openViewer` already opens on that slide, so constraining the photo constrains the model. **Nothing writes the `<img>` src.** The island uses shop's published contract for exactly this, the one `filters-for-shop` uses: allowed sourceIds into `data-shop-media-sources` on `.shop-card` plus a `shop:card-media-sources` event - a src written from outside is undone by the carousel's next render. Good-neighbour behaviour with the filter is explicit: base value remembered on mount, restored on clear and on unmount, and a foreign write (`ownWriteRef` guard) drops our picks entirely rather than outranking a fresh filter. New Puck field **`preview`** (radio, defaults `'no'`) on `ShopCardVariationOptions`, so every card design already published is untouched and ships no client JS; `'yes'` swaps the server rows for `components/public/CardOptionPreview.tsx`. Rows extracted to `components/public/card-option-rows.tsx` (**no** `'use client'` - imported by both paths so the markup is identical either way, which is the card-part parity rule). Payload: `CardOptionsFacts` gains optional `preview.variants` as `{s, v[]}` - **seat numbers, not uuids**, because a grid ships this per card and 36-char ids per value per variation is most of the weight for nothing anyone sees; `CardOptionValue` gains `vi`. `buildCardOptionsFacts` seats every value of every card-shown option **including ones trimmed off by `cardLimit`** (unhoverable, but still the answer to a choice made elsewhere), drops variations left with no card-shown value, and **collapses variations differing only in an option the card never prints, first wins**. `resolvePreviewSource` gives up choices from the BOTTOM until something matches - the same directional rule as `isValueAvailable`, so a finish that does not come in the chosen width leaves the width showing rather than blanking. Hover/focus sets a working pick that reverts on **card** mouseleave (not block mouseleave - that would drop the preview on the way to the 3D icon); click pins one that survives, which is the phone story and what keeps the model on the chosen variation. Buttons sit at `zIndex 2` over the stretched `.shop-card-link` with `pointerEvents: none` on the root and `auto` on the buttons alone, inline so it also beats shop's `.shop-card-img.fill-mode ~ *{pointer-events:none}`. Provider cost: two extra set-wide queries per grid (`getVariantsForProducts` + `getVariantValueMapForProducts`) and only for products that actually tick an option onto their card. Known limits, both deliberate: alias values (`svr_variant_alias_values`) are not consulted, and a constraint naming a photo the carousel does not carry falls back to the full set (shop's own behaviour) rather than blanking. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, `card-options.test.ts` **21 pass / 0 fail** incl. 11 new. No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Wiki: `Shop-variations.md` gains "Showing the photo for the one they're pointing at". Released as **0.1.116** and pinned in core **v0.5.977**.) Previous top entry: 2026-08-08 (**A variation can be shown on the product page before anyone has chosen anything** - `shop` **0.1.196**, `shop-variations` **0.1.115**, `product-3d-views-for-shop` **0.1.85**, all working tree; core diff is this file and the two wiki pages, `modules.json` pins NOT moved. Chris: an option on each variation to show that variation's first image on the main product before any options are selected, and to hide it again once a different variation is chosen - same for 3D models. Built first as one flag, then **split into two on Chris's say-so** ("yes i want them split in two please") once he saw the single-checkbox version, since the combination worth leading with in 3D is not always the one with the best photo. **Two independent flags**: new `svr_variants.show_image_in_gallery` + `show_model_in_gallery` (BOOLEAN default false each, `migrations/011_variant_show_in_gallery.sql`, mirrored in 001 - edited in place to add the second column rather than stacked as 012, since 011 had not reached any real install; the **backup round-trip gate applied and was run for real on the final two-column shape: 3 pass / 0 fail / 0 skipped**, plus `schema-coverage` green). Surfaced as **"Image up front"** and **"3D up front"** tick boxes on the Variations grid, saved through the product editor's own Save like every other cell (`VariantEdit` + PATCH `showImageInGallery`/`showModelInGallery` -> `setVariantShowImageInGallery`/`setVariantShowModelInGallery`). **The gate is `!anyOptionChosen`, deliberately not "a whole combination resolved"**: the promoted media is there to show the range, and the instant the shopper picks ANYTHING they have said what they want, so a rival finish in the strip is answering a question nobody asked. It is also the only gate that holds still - a resolved variant blinks in and out as they work down the options, and hanging the strip's contents off that would have thumbnails appearing and vanishing under the cursor. Reset options brings them back. Computed once in `useVariationSelection` as two independent filters over the same variant list (`featuredImages` off `showImageInGallery`, `featuredModelChildIds` off `showModelInGallery`) so both galleries and every contributor agree. **Cross-module seam, no cross-module reads**: rather than have the 3D module read `svr_variants` (it does keep a read-only svr_ bridge, but a new column would need a presence probe and would couple the two schemas), shop's `ShopGalleryExtraThumbsProps` gains optional **`featuredProductIds`** and shop-variations passes `featuredModelChildIds` down the existing contract; `visibleItems()` takes it as a third argument - the image-only flag never reaches 3D at all, it only ever feeds the galleries' own `thumbs` arrays. Also 2026-08-07 (**Hiding products that have sold out, at three depths** - `shop` **0.1.195**, `shop-variations` **0.1.113**, `filters-for-shop` **0.1.10**, `product-attributes-for-shop` **0.1.44**, `search` **0.1.14**, `space-planner-for-shop` **0.1.16**, core **v0.5.971**. Chris wanted a shop setting to hide out-of-stock products, optionally only from shoppers, optionally only from the listings, optionally including the product page and staff. Two config keys on the existing `shp_settings` JSONB - `outOfStockVisibility` (SHOW\|HIDE_FROM_LISTS\|HIDE_EVERYWHERE) and `outOfStockHiddenFromStaff` - **no schema change, so no backup round-trip gate**. All the reasoning lives in new `modules/shop/lib/stock-visibility.ts`; no surface works out "out of stock" for itself. Three properties held deliberately: (1) SHOW is a total no-op - no provider asked, no cookie read, no SQL added, so an untouched shop keeps its cacheable public pages; (2) the session cookie is read ONLY when hiding is on AND staff are exempt, the one case where two visitors must see different pages (`canSeeHiddenOutOfStock()` in `lib/access.ts`, `shop.access` bar, same as the closed-shop preview); (3) the admin Products screen and the CSV export never hide anything, which is why the filter is a new explicit `storefront: true` on `listProducts` rather than being folded into the existing `excludeHidden` that admin passes too. **The hard part was variations**: a parent listing carries no stock of its own (proved again on live Deskwell - all 355 variation parents have `track_inventory = false`), so shop's own columns would have hidden nothing. New extension point **`shop.product-availability`** takes two `Prisma.Sql` fragments per provider (`ownsSql`, `outOfStockSql`, product row aliased `p` by contract) and composes them as `CASE WHEN owns THEN oos ... ELSE <shop's own rule> END` - first provider to claim a product decides, same rule as `shop.product-card-prices`. SQL rather than id lists because it goes in the grid's WHERE: filtering after the LIMIT gives short pages and a count that disagrees with them. Provider is `shopVariationsAvailability` (`shop-variations/lib/availability-provider.ts`): a listing is sold out only when every enabled variant with an ACTIVE child is, mirroring the `inStock` flag the picker itself computes. Measured three formulations against live data on the worst query (every active listing, no category filter): OR-chain 75ms, CASE 65ms, single-pass `BOOL_OR` **193ms** (no short-circuit - rejected), against a 1.6ms baseline; only paid when the setting is on. Second new point **`shop.product-listability`** (`shop/lib/listability.ts`, `hiddenProductIds(ids)`) exists purely so `search` can drop the same products without importing shop's lib - it already resolves `shop.product-card-prices` through the core registry the same way, and this covers both its card mode and its plain-row mode. Surfaces carrying `storefront: true`: category + collection fallback pages, `ShopProductGrid.rsc`, `ShopFeaturedCollection.rsc`, `public/products`, `public/categories/[slug]`, `public/collections/[slug]`, plus **filters-for-shop's `ShopFilterGrid.rsc` and product-attributes' `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc` - Deskwell's category pages are all Filtered Grid layouts, so without that one word the feature would have done nothing where it matters most**. Recommendation strips filter through `visibleRecommendations` in `lib/db/recommendations.ts` (automatic fallback filters in SQL so a strip asked for four still returns four; a manual list is judged for emptiness BEFORE filtering so an owner's all-sold-out picks stay their empty strip rather than silently becoming automatic suggestions). Sitemap uses `hidesOutOfStockFromShoppers(config)` - config only, never the staff exemption, because one file is served to the whole world. `HIDE_EVERYWHERE` 404s the product page and `generateMetadata` (both, so a future `global-not-found` convention cannot publish the name) and `public/products/[slug]`; staff on such a page get `ShopStockHiddenBanner` beside the existing closed-shop one. **`space-planner-for-shop` 0.1.16** takes it too: `browseCatalogue` fixes `storefront: true` in the same `Omit` as `status`/`excludeHidden` so no caller can override it, which also means `?stock=out` on its public catalogue route returns nothing once hiding is on - the shop's answer wins over the panel's own filter. Live read-only check: the composed SQL was printed from the real provider through vitest and run verbatim on Deskwell - valid, 10 of 452 listings would hide (4 with every variation sold out, 6 plain tracked products at zero). Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **1637 pass / 19 skipped / 0 fail** incl. new `lib/stock-visibility.test.ts` (6, pinning that SHOW never reaches for a cookie and that the staff exemption dies when switched off). No dev server, no build, per standing rules. Also 2026-08-07 (**Core now mints its own `CRON_SECRET`** - `lib/vercel/cron-secret.ts` (new), wired into setup, core update and module install; `CRON_SECRET` added to `SENSITIVE_KEYS` (`lib/vercel/env.ts`) and to the optional list in `getEnvStatus()` (`lib/config/env.ts`). Trigger: installing Stock Imports on Deskwell failed the required-env gate on `CRON_SECRET`, and the investigation found something worse - **Deskwell has never had a `CRON_SECRET` at all** (41 project vars, none of them it), so every scheduled job on that site, core's four member crons included, has been answering 503 since the day it went live, invisibly. The design point: `CRON_SECRET` is not a third-party credential like `SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, it is an internal shared secret with no meaning outside the site, so making an owner invent one was always the wrong shape. `ensureCronSecret()` never overwrites an existing project value (`pending`) - rotating it would break live crons - and only ever lands in `process.env` via the redeploy the caller already triggers. `app/api/admin/modules/route.ts` provisions when the manifest declares `cronJobs` **or** names `CRON_SECRET`, whichever, then drops it from the required-env gate unless provisioning genuinely failed; a module that merely schedules work no longer installs into a silently dead cron. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` clean on every file touched, new `lib/vercel/cron-secret.test.ts` **8 pass**, `lib/vercel` + `lib/config` + `lib/modules` suites **27 pass / 0 fail**. The 7 `tsc` errors outstanding in the tree are another agent's in-flight best-selling/popularity work in `modules/filters-for-shop` and `modules/shop`, untouched here. Wiki: `Configuration-reference.md` (`CRON_SECRET` row rewritten - nothing to fetch, and what breaks without it), `Authoring-a-module.md` (module authors must **not** declare `CRON_SECRET` in `requiredEnvVars`; keep the 503 guard in the route). Note on scope while reading Vercel billing: the plan lives on the **team** that owns the project (`deskwell`, pro), not on `GET /v2/user` (the personal account `chris-9831`, hobby) - so Stock Imports' hourly tick is fine on Deskwell. Env writes against a team-owned project work without a `teamId` query param, as `lib/vercel/env.ts` has always done; the token resolves the project by id across the scopes it can reach. **New module: Stock Imports for Shop 0.1.0** - `stock-import-for-shop`, table prefix `stk_`, repo `cactus-foundation-modules/stock-import-for-shop`, registered in `modules.json` at v0.1.0 (core v0.5.965). Chris asked for stock to be refreshed from a supplier CSV url (`https://edi.dynamicos.co.uk/Uploads/178/STK.csv`) against the SKU, on a frequency adjustable in **Settings → Shop → Stock**, plus a **Fetch Latest Stock** button on the Products page. Full detail in the module's own section below; the four things worth knowing up front: (1) **the frequency cannot be a Vercel Cron schedule** - those are baked in at deploy time - so the manifest registers one hourly tick (`5 * * * *`) and `isRunDue` decides whether the owner's chosen interval has elapsed, with 10 minutes of tolerance because strict arithmetic would drift a daily run an hour forward and start skipping days; **this needs a plan that allows sub-daily crons, which Hobby does not** (Deskwell is Pro, checked - **and check it the right way**: the project is owned by the team `deskwell` / `team_hhDdTpPWm3S23M3N4xXZn1q8`, whose `billing.plan` is `pro`. `GET /v2/user` reports the *personal* account `chris-9831`, which is `hobby` and has nothing to do with this project - reading that and concluding "Deskwell is on Hobby" is a mistake already made once. `GET /v9/projects/{id}` → `accountId` tells you which scope owns a project; `GET /v2/teams` carries the plan). (2) **The 60-second route ceiling is the design constraint**: 21,577 shop SKUs against a 53,497-row 6.4MB file that takes 5.5s just to download, so a run is a resumable job - fetch and diff, park the writes in `stk_import_job.pending`, then apply 1,000 at a time with progress saved per batch and a 45s budget; the button loops `run/step` until done, an unattended run is resumed by the next tick, and a 90s lease (claimed via one `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE ... WHERE`) stops the button and the cron treading on each other while expiring by itself so a dead request cannot wedge it. (3) **Only changed rows are written**, and the pending pairs carry the shop's own SKU spelling read back out of `shp_products`, so `applyStockBatch` compares `p."sku" = v."sku"` and uses the unique index instead of an `upper(btrim(...))` expression that would seq-scan once per 1,000-row batch. (4) **An unreadable stock cell never becomes a zero** - `parseStockValue` returns null and the product is left alone and reported, because guessing there is how a shop refuses orders it could have taken; `missing_behaviour: ZERO` is opt-in for the same reason. Verified against the live catalogue read-only before writing a line: 20,857 of 21,577 Deskwell SKUs match that file directly, no transformation. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest **65 pass / 0 fail**, and - new tables, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. No dev server, per standing rule. New `wiki/Stock-Imports.md`, linked from `Home.md` and `Modules.md`; core `README.md` module list updated.)

Also 2026-08-07 (**Best-seller ordering: shop 0.1.193, shop-variations 0.1.110, filters-for-shop 0.1.9** - Chris wanted the shop sortable by best sellers, and asked first whether the supplier's own site could supply sales figures. It cannot: Shopify never exposes units sold, per product or per variant. What `dynamicofficeseating.co.uk` does expose is `?sort_by=best-selling`, an ordinal product ordering, and its theme prints the rendered page's products as a JSON array (`"collection": [...]`) complete with every variant's `sku` and `inventory_quantity`. Crawled all 58 pages: **1,141 products, 27,116 distinct SKUs**, rank 1..1141, `sort_by` verified to survive pagination and the ordering verified different from every other sort. Read-only match against live Deskwell: **20,517 of our 21,577 SKUs and 449 of our 477 parent listings get a rank**. Design (Chris picked both): seed from the supplier and let real sales take over; one `popularity` column on `shp_products` owned by shop and handed to filters-for-shop as a sort key. Shipped as **two** columns, because only one of them is derived - `popularity_seed` is given (importable, hand-editable, never touched by the recompute) and `popularity` is seed + real sales and is what every grid sorts on. `POPULARITY_SALES_WEIGHT = 100_000` makes one genuine sale outrank any seed, so a borrowed ranking retreats on its own without anyone remembering to switch it off; 365-day window; only `payment_status IN (PAID, PARTIALLY_REFUNDED)` and `status NOT IN (CANCELLED, REFUNDED)` count, refunded units subtracted. **Orders reference the hidden variation child, not the listing** (confirmed on live data), so sales roll up through a new extension point **`shop.product-sales-rollup`** -> `modules/shop/lib/popularity.ts`, provider `shopVariationsSalesRollup` in shop-variations (`lib/sales-rollup-provider.ts`, reusing the existing `getVariantParentsByChild`) - shop still knows nothing about variations. Recompute is **nightly only**, folded into the existing `api/cron/low-stock-alerts` route in a try/catch: the money path in `db/orders.ts` is deliberately untouched, and daily is also the only thing that ages sales out of the window. New sorts: `ProductSort 'popular'` (admin, `popularity DESC NULLS LAST`) and `FltSortValue 'best-selling'` (storefront, unranked last, not zero). Seeding tooling lives in `.agents/skills/deskwell-bestseller-seed/` (crawler + importer + the rank CSV); the importer is **dry-run by default**, does the identical work in a transaction and rolls it back so its counts are real, and refuses to run until shop 0.1.193 has actually reached the site. **Nothing has been written to Deskwell** - the columns do not exist there until the owner takes the update, and hand-applying DDL to a live install is not on. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, filters sort suite **10 pass**, `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` **1 pass**, and - module migration SQL, so the gate applies - `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 pass / 0 skip**. The seeding SQL itself was proved on a throwaway `cactus_rt_seedcheck` database on the OVH VPS (rollup to the best-ranked variation, refund subtraction, cancelled/unpaid/out-of-window all excluded, unranked left NULL), dropped after. Wiki: new **Best selling** section in `Shop.md`, sort list in `Shop-filters.md`.)

The existing `.flt-sheet-body .flt-group:first-child{border-top:0}` needed no change: with chips present the first group is no longer first-child, so its rule quietly becomes the separator under them. Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Google Sheet Products 0.1.55: stock count and trade price can be kept out of the sheet** - `modules/google-sheet-products-for-shop`, **released as v0.1.55** and pinned in `modules.json` (core v0.5.964). Chris asked for an include/exclude option on **Settings → Shop → Google Sheet** for `stock_count`/`Stock` and `trade_price`/`Trade Price`. **Migration `011_column_toggles.sql`** adds `include_stock` and `include_trade_price` to `gsp_connection`, both `BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT true` via `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, so an existing sheet is unchanged until the owner switches one off; `mapConnection` reads them as `!== false` so a row read before the migration still reports true. `001_initial.sql` untouched, matching this module's convention (every post-001 column lives only in its numbered file). New pure `lib/columns.ts` is the single contract - `ColumnPrefs`, `DEFAULT_COLUMN_PREFS`, `columnPrefsFrom(conn)`, `excludedProductColumns` (`stock_count`, `trade_price`) and `excludedVariationColumns` (`Stock`, `Trade Price`) - with `lib/columns.test.ts` (11 cases). **The whole mechanism is the Push**: `productColumns(prefs)` filters `CSV_COLUMNS`, `buildProductsGrid(prefs)` follows, and `splitWideGridByProduct(wide, excludedColumns)` drops the named fixed columns from every product tab. Nothing in the Pull needed a special case, because a column absent from the sheet was already inert on the way back: `diffProductRows` only compares header columns it finds, shop's import engine `put()`s a field only when `hasColumn()`, and shop-variations' importer guards every optional column with `col >= 0`. Push's existing narrower-grid clear (`planTabPush`, `ownsColumn` still names both columns) sweeps the switched-off column out of the sheet on the next Push. **The one real trap, fixed:** `mergeVariationTabs` always emitted the full `FIXED_MIDDLE_COLUMNS` header and padded absent ones blank - a `Stock` column of blanks reads to the importer as "clear every variant's stock", the exact opposite of leaving it alone. It now emits a fixed column only when at least one tab actually carries it (which also fixes the same hazard for a column an owner deleted by hand); a column *some* tabs carry is kept and pads as before. `missingProductsColumns(grid, excluded)` filters the switched-off columns out of the Pull's refusal (`stock_count` is not in shop's `OPTIONAL_CSV_COLUMNS`, so an off sheet would otherwise be bounced); `lib/preview.ts` now calls it instead of `missingFormatColumns` so the preview and the Pull agree. `PATCH /settings` takes `includeStock`/`includeTradePrice` booleans (new `saveColumnPreferences` in `lib/db.ts`, per-key writes) and its `ENCRYPTION_KEY` guard moved inside the credentials branch - a checkbox PATCH stores nothing encrypted and must not 503 for want of a key. Settings tab gained a "What goes in the sheet" card with two save-on-click checkboxes that revert on a failed save. Read me tab gained a "COLUMNS YOU CAN LEAVE OUT" section. Both version fields 0.1.54 → 0.1.55. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, module vitest **170 pass / 0 fail**. No dev server, no DDL applied by hand - the migration runner picks 011 up on the install's next deploy. `wiki/Google-Sheet-Products.md` updated with a "What goes in the sheet" section.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Search: an exact product name did not return that product** - `modules/search`, working tree, unreleased, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki. Version fields deliberately NOT bumped and `modules.json` NOT touched - no release asked for, and `modules.json` already carries another session's edit. Chris reported that searching the exact title "Oslo Air Height Adjustable Office Desk" did not bring back the product of that name, on a freshly rebuilt index. **Root cause, proven on the live index before any edit:** `tsQuery` in `lib/query.ts` ORed the trailing-word prefix term over the whole query - `websearch_to_tsquery(q) || to_tsquery('desk:*')` - so the last word stood alone as an alternative to everything before it. The strict half `'oslo' & 'air' & 'height' & 'adjust' & 'offic' & 'desk'` matches that one product and nothing else; the OR turned the search into "anything containing desk", **208 documents**, and the product landed at **position 62**. Second, compounding defect: the rank was `ts_rank_cd` alone, which is cover-density and so rewards repetition - `search_vector` does carry `setweight` A/B/C from the indexer, but a long body that says "desk" thirty times still beats a six-word exact title, which is why the exact match sank rather than merely being diluted. **Fixes, all in the module:** (1) the prefix term is now ANDed - `websearch_to_tsquery(head) && to_tsquery('last:*')`, with the bare `to_tsquery('last:*')` form for a one-word query so `websearch_to_tsquery('')` never fires its NOTICE. Verified on live: the fixed query returns that product **alone, at position 1, rank 1002**. (2) New `titleBoostSql` added to the rank - 1000 title equals query, 100 title starts with it, 10 title contains it - tiers spaced so a title match cannot lose to a body match. (3) Relaxed retry: strict count 0 triggers one `looseTerms` any-word pass (`a:* | b:* | ...`), adopted only if it actually finds something, so a single stray or misspelt word gives near misses rather than a blank page. **The analytics trap that came with it:** the relaxed pass would have quietly emptied the owner's "searches that found nothing" report, which is the single most useful thing on that screen. `SearchQueryResult` gained `relaxed: boolean`, and `app/api/public/search/query/route.ts` now logs `strictTotal` (0 when relaxed) to both `logQuery` and the `syncIndexAlert` gate. The pure query-text half moved out to new `lib/query-terms.ts` (no prisma import, so it is testable) with new `lib/query-terms.test.ts` - 13 tests pinning the AND split, the one-word and short-token cases, and the deliberate bail-outs on quoted phrases, `-negation` and `or`/`OR`, which the split would otherwise corrupt into their opposite. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, full vitest **1641 pass / 0 fail / 7 skipped**. No dev server run, per standing rule; verification was read-only SQL against the live Deskwell index. `wiki/Search.md` updated - visitor-facing behaviour, the owner's analytics caveat, and the developer notes.)

Previously: 2026-08-07 (**Space Planner 0.1.15: columns invisible in 3D, the how-to note swallowing a phone screen, no way to delete a saved room or layout** - `space-planner-for-shop`, working tree, unreleased, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki. From Chris's report on live. **Columns:** `buildRoom` in `lib/three/planner-scene.ts` drew each obstruction as a single `ShapeGeometry` LID translated to `heightM`, over a floor whose shape had the obstruction punched out as a `Path` hole - so a pillar was a flat plate edge-on from every angle but straight down, which is why they read as not rendering at all. Now an `ExtrudeGeometry(shape, {depth: heightM, bevelEnabled: false})`, `rotateX(PI/2)` then `translate(0, heightM, 0)` - the rotation puts the extruded end BELOW the floor, hence the lift - front faces only, `transparent: true` at `OBSTRUCTION_OPACITY = 0.72` per Chris's follow-up so furniture behind a column still shows; one shared material for the room, meshes named `obstruction:<id>`. New `lib/three/obstruction-solid.test.ts` pins solid-not-lid, sits-on-floor, not-mirrored-in-z, transparent, floor-unbroken (6 tests; the old code fails the first). **The note:** `.spl-coach` always had `pointer-events: none` so it never actually ate a drag - the complaint is that on a phone the 3D stage measures **351x189px** (measured on live) and the three-line desktop hint covered most of it, and the only thing that cleared it was an interaction with the view underneath. Now two copies of the copy in the DOM picked by `@media (pointer: coarse)` (SSR-safe, no measuring), a `HINT_LIFE_MS = 7000` self-dismiss in `View3d`, and at <=640px the box goes smaller, tighter and bottom-RIGHT to clear the eye-height column at bottom-left. **Delete:** both `DELETE` handlers already existed at `/api/m/space-planner-for-shop/member/rooms/[id]` and `/member/plans/[id]`, member-scoped, and `spl_plans.room_id` is `ON DELETE CASCADE` - the spaces page simply had no UI. New `components/public/SpaceDeleteButton.tsx`, the only client island on that server page: two-tap arm/confirm rather than `confirm()` (suppressed in some in-app browsers, where it resolves false and the button silently no-ops), `router.refresh()` on success rather than hiding the row locally. Room confirmations name the layout count. Plan rows restructured so the button is a SIBLING of the row `<Link>`, never nested. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean bar the two pre-existing `truelayer-pay-by-bank-for-shop` Buffer errors, `eslint .` clean, module vitest 160 pass / 3 skipped. Both version fields bumped 0.1.14 -> 0.1.15; root `modules.json` NOT touched.)

Also 2026-08-06 (**Space Planner: the simplifier was tearing models apart at the seams** - `space-planner-for-shop`, since released as 0.1.11, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki, no schema change, **live data write - see below**. Reported as the Oslo oval boardroom table drawing correctly on the product page and wrong in the planner. Not scale, not the fabric: `decimate()` in `lib/three/planner-model.ts`. **A glTF loader splits one mesh into one geometry per material, so parts finished differently arrive as separate geometries SHARING A RIM** - `oslo-oval-boardroom-table-2400.glb` is a `Table top finish` slab and a 26 mm `Table Edge` band. `decimate()` simplifies each geometry independently, so each end of that shared rim moved by a different amount and the two stopped meeting. Measured offline against the real file (17,528 tris, Draco, `spl_settings` `decimationEnabled: true` / `decimationTarget: 0.45`, no `spl_model_meta` row so no exemption): the band held at 2400 x 26 x 1000 mm (err 0.0001) while the slab pulled to 2382 x 33 x 992 from 2394 x 33 x 994 (err 0.0092) - a 12 mm crack at the rim, the oval's ends reduced to chords, and a hole through one end. **The error term hides it rather than catching it: meshoptimizer reads `target_error` as a fraction of the MESH EXTENT, so `0.01` on a 2.4 m table permits ~24 mm of wander - most of the edge band's entire height.** No threshold could have saved it. Two changes, both in `decimate()`/`build()`: **(1)** `simplify(..., 0.01, ['LockBorder'])` - open boundary vertices are pinned, which is exactly the shared rim. Verified: the slab comes back untouched (2396 tris, bbox identical, err 0.0000) and the band still gets its 55% (3014 tris). **(2)** new `DECIMATION_FLOOR_TRIANGLES = 30_000`, checked with the existing `countTriangles(object)` before the pass runs - at 17.5k tris the Oslo table was giving up its silhouette to save ~8k triangles against a 14-model budget, which is no trade at all. The per-file `no_decimation` tick remains the escape hatch. Also corrected a comment in the same function claiming nothing in this catalogue is Draco compressed; `extensionsUsed` on that file is `EXT_texture_webp`, `KHR_draco_mesh_compression`, `KHR_texture_transform`. **LIVE DATA WRITE, at the owner's explicit request, on `db.dwoffice.furniture:5432/neondb`:** `spl_model_meta` was empty (0 rows); one `'file'`-scope row now exists per `p3d_models` row - **11,600 rows, all `no_decimation = true`**, notes `Decimation off - simplifier damaged shared rims (2026-08-06)`. No other table touched, no DDL. This makes the fix visible on Deskwell without a release, and is scoped-deletable by that notes string; rollback SQL and the (empty) pre-write CSV were written to the session scratchpad, and the notes string is the whole of what identifies the rows. **Note the two now overlap:** the tick wins over the floor and the `LockBorder` flag alike, so nothing decimates on Deskwell at all until those rows are cleared. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` - 9 errors, all pre-existing and in other modules (`crezco-*` not checked out, `truelayer` `signing.ts`), none in this one; `eslint` clean. **Not verified in a browser** - the planner is `adminOnly` and no dev server was run; the before/after evidence is an offline Draco decode + meshopt run + software rasterise of the real file. `wiki/Space-planner.md` updated.)

Also 2026-08-05 (**Space Planner draws a model at the size the shop recorded for it, instead of stretching it onto the spec sheet** - `space-planner-for-shop`, **working tree, unreleased, version not yet bumped past 0.1.8**, module dir only apart from this file and the wiki, no schema change. Reported as models scaled "really strangely". Cause: `buildItems` fitted every mesh to `node.size`, which is the size ladder's answer - and a spec figure is frequently not the model's overall size (a seat height, a range, a width taken to the worktop), so per-axis division deformed the model to fit a number that was never describing it. The catalogue already holds a better statement: p3d's material setup records the product's real overall height or width **per variation** (`FabricConfig.scaleAxis` + `heightAttributeId`/`heightManual`, surfaced as `FabricBundle.realCm`), the number its fabric already tiles to and its AR already stands up at. New `realSizeScale()` in `lib/three/model-scale.ts` and an optional 4th argument to `modelScaleFor` - present, it returns one **uniform** factor and the plan's figures are not consulted at all; absent, the 0.1.6 reconciliation is unchanged and still the fallback for the 75 modelled listings with no config. Plumbed as `realMetres`/`realAxis`: `FabricBundle` -> `PlannerModel`/`ClientModel` (`lib/model-resolver.ts`, cm->m converted once) -> `SceneModelSource` -> both renderers, the live `View3d` and the Fly render page's `sources` (a still that disagreed with the planner it came from would be a new bug, not a fix). Read **per node `productId`** in `buildItems`, deliberately not off `bySource`, which is keyed file-plus-paints and would give two seat heights of one chair in one fabric a single height. Guarded 0.02-20 m against a units slip. **Second, load-bearing fix:** `lib/three/planner-model.ts` measured with `Box3.setFromObject(object)` - the conservative form that inflates an off-axis part up to 30%, which was harmless while the measurement was only compared against the plan (both sides inflate) and is not harmless now the real size is DIVIDED by it - exactly the trap p3d 0.1.84 fixed in AR the same day. Now `(object, true)`. Live coverage read from the Deskwell database: 138 of 213 modelled listings carry a fabric config, every one of them with a size source set, 137 height-axis and 1 width-axis. Caveats: a room over `MAX_FABRIC_RESOLUTIONS` (60 distinct products) loses the real size along with the colours for the overflow, as before; and the ladder's own `node.size` is untouched, so the 2D plan footprint still comes off the spec sheet. Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint` clean, module suite 146 passed / 3 skipped (live calibration, needs env), 15 in `model-scale.test.ts` including the new real-size cases. `wiki/Space-planner.md` updated.)

Also 2026-08-05 (**View in your room stopped guessing a model's size from a rough outline and started reading its real shape** - `product-3d-views-for-shop` **v0.1.84**, released and pinned (core **v0.5.952**), module dir only, no schema change. `measureModelHeight`/`measureModelWidth` (`lib/three/load-model.ts`) and the three AR sizing points in `lib/three/ar.ts` (`bakeUsdzUrl`'s scale factor and floor lift, `startWebXrAr`'s equivalent) all called `Box3.setFromObject(model)` with no second argument - three's CONSERVATIVE form, which transforms the eight CORNERS of each mesh's own local box rather than its vertices, exact only while every node's rotation is a multiple of 90 degrees. A part mounted at an angle - not rare, just unremarked - reports a box legitimately larger than the geometry inside it, up to 30% on the worst case found. Nothing else caught it: fabric tiling divides the product's real size by this same measurement, so an inflated box and an inflated divisor cancel and the weave stays correct, while AR scales the box DOWN to the real size and renders the product short by exactly the excess - a desk stated at 82cm standing in a shopper's room at 65cm, with every existing check green. All five calls now pass `true` (precise, per-vertex; `InstancedMesh` ignores the flag and is unaffected either way, so the 16 GPU-instanced models on the live catalogue cost nothing extra). Verified against real three.js before and after (a sphere under one supplier file's own quaternion inflates 29.94% at the cheap setting, 0% at an exact 90deg one) and by pulling the live public fabric endpoint post-deploy. **Not a database question at any point** - the stored `modelHeights`/`modelWidths` were correct throughout; only the live measurement disagreed with them. Found 5 files inflated over 1% (three Air height-adjustable desks, 28%/28%/22%, 22 products between them; Penza 3.8%; Florence Sled 1.8%) - fixed same day by baking the offending node's rotation into its own vertices and re-uploading over the same object keys (script `bake-offaxis.mjs`, texel density verified unchanged to <0.06%, no DB row touched) - and 7 more under 0.5% (Eclipse Plus, Impulse B2B extension kit, Chiro Plus, Chesterfield, Galaxy, Eclipse XL Plus, Evolve Plus boardroom) now caught automatically by this release with no file needing to change. Separately, unrelated code path: **Storm High Back chair's stated real height was `10.5cm` for a 105cm chair**, a data-entry slip rather than this defect - corrected directly in `p3d_fabric_configs`, no release involved. 11 FBX/OBJ-modelled products remain unverified either way; the audit toolchain (`~/.cactus-3d-tools/`) is glTF-only.)

New `paintedModel()` in `lib/three/planner-model.ts` **clones the materials** named in the slots before painting them, because prepared models are shared by every placement and three.js clones share materials by reference.
