Bundles are cached per server instance for 60s and resolved 6 at a time: each is ~8 queries, one of which reads the shop's whole swatch vocabulary, and 20 fired off together is 160 queries arriving at PgBouncer at once (measured 38.5s cold / 1.5s warm for 20 products from a laptop with 700ms RTT). **Rung 1 of the size ladder finally exists.** The README has always said `scripts/calibrate.mjs` writes the measured rows; there is no such script and there never was, so in three releases **not one `glb`-sourced row was ever written** - 0 of 100 on the live site, and so 0 conflicts ever flagged. It cannot run in a route (60s, ~4 MB a file), so it runs in the ADMIN'S BROWSER: new `GET/POST /api/m/space-planner-for-shop/admin/dimensions/measure` + a **Measure** card on the Sizes screen that loads every distinct model file with the same code that draws them, grouped by file rather than by product, clearing the prepared-model cache every 8 files and posting extents back in batches of 25. New `applyMeasurements()` in `lib/resolve-dimensions.ts` writes `source: 'glb'` with the conflict note computed against the spec sheet, **never over a hand-typed size**, and refuses an implausible measurement outright. Verified against the live Deskwell database: all four Galaxy products now resolve 675 x 640 x 1110 with distinct fabric keys per colour, and the Air height-adjustable desks 665 mm rather than 67 mm. **Existing cached rows are still wrong until somebody presses the buttons** - Sizes -> Measure, then "Work the sizes out again". ~27 rows were rewritten with correct values during that verification. `wiki/Space-planner.md` and the module README updated.) Also 2026-08-03 (**The burger drawer measures the header instead of guessing at it** - `lib/puck/components/MenuBlockClient.tsx`, finishing what the entry below started. `top: '100%'` resolves against the drawer's offset parent, which is the header's *content box* - and that box is centred in the header, so 100% is the bottom of the ROW, not of the header. Identical only when the header has no spare height, which was exactly the case at the one height every header used to be (96px header, 32px row). Deskwell's mobile header at 48px has 17px spare, so the drawer opened 9px high and painted its own background over the header's bottom rule. New `measureDrawerTop()` takes `header.getBoundingClientRect().bottom - offsetParent.getBoundingClientRect().top` off the toggle button (whose offset parent IS that content box) **on click, before the drawer renders**, so there is no first-frame jump; `drawerTop` state, `top: drawerTop ?? '100%'` keeps the old behaviour when there is no `<header>` ancestor at all (the block is not header-only). Re-measured on resize and capture-phase scroll while open, the same treatment `SearchBoxClient`'s bar already had - which is precisely why the bar measured flush at 0 and the drawer did not. Deskwell's header is now `height: {desktop:'96px', mobile:'48px'}`, applied after the 0.5.927 deploy for the reason the entry below gives; 42px was tried first and the row (31px, the burger button being the tallest thing in it) sat too tight in it.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The composable header's height is a per-screen-size setting, and the burger drawer stops assuming 96px** - `lib/puck/config.tsx` + `lib/puck/components/MenuBlockClient.tsx`. `headerPuckConfig.root.fields.height` was a `select` of six fixed values (`auto`/48/64/72/80/96) applying at every width, so a phone header holding one row of 20px icons could not be shortened without shortening the desktop one, and no preset matched what was wanted anyway. Now a `ResponsiveUnitValueField` in px/rem/vh, mirroring the `paddingX` field added the same day: desktop stays inline on the element, tablet/mobile come out of `responsiveMediaCssFor('header[data-header-root]', …)`, blank resolves to `64px` (the old default) and `'auto'` still means content height floored at 48 at whichever breakpoint asks for it. Old data was a plain string and normalises, so every saved header renders byte-identically. `splitUnitValue` already shows an unparseable keyword as-is rather than blanking it, which is what lets `auto` survive the field-type change. Specificity checked: the new rule is `header[data-header-root]` (0,1,1) against the shrink-on-scroll override's `header[data-shrink-root][data-shrunk]` (0,2,1), so a shrunk header still wins on scroll despite both carrying `!important`. The legacy all-in-one `SiteHeaderBlock` render keeps its own plain-string height - different block, not the composable header. Second half: `MenuBlockClient`'s hamburger drawer was positioned `top: 64`, absolute inside the header's centred content box. That box's bottom edge IS 64 when the header is 96px tall and the row is 32 - which it always was - so the constant was a coincidence that broke the moment a header wasn't 96. Now `top: '100%'`, which is the same pixel today (63.5, a half-pixel from the hardcoded value) and follows any height. **Deskwell's own header data is deliberately NOT updated yet**: a responsive object in `root.props.height` reaching the currently-deployed render would land as `height: [object Object]` and collapse the live header to content height at every width, so the 42px mobile value goes in only once the install has taken this release.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The search field stops iOS zooming the page in on itself** - `modules/search` **0.1.12**, one CSS rule. The cause is not layout at all - **iOS Safari zooms the whole page whenever a focused input computes under 16px**, and the bar autofocuses, so the zoom fires the instant it opens and takes the field's left edge off-screen with it. The block's size vars are 13px (small), 15px (medium) and 17px (large), so two of the three tripped it. New `@media (pointer:coarse){.srch-input{font-size:max(16px,var(--srch-font))}}` floors the live input on touch pointers only - a mouse or trackpad keeps the chosen size exactly and no desktop layout moves. Deskwell's own block also moved from Medium to **Large** as the immediate fix, since that clears 16px on the deployed 0.1.11 without waiting for a release; the trigger is unaffected either way because `fieldStyle: minimal` zeroes its padding and `iconSize: 20` pins the glyph, verified after the change - search glyph still 20x20 at x=50, midY 47.5, every gap still 16. The site's viewport meta is `width=device-width, initial-scale=1` with no `maximum-scale`, which is correct and stays that way: suppressing zoom to dodge this would take pinch-zoom off every visitor who needs it.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Members can change their own email address, and the Security tab is now Account & Security** - the tab was named after half of what it holds; the half it was missing is the address every sign-in link, code and receipt goes to, which a member previously could not change at all (an admin could, from the Users screen, which is a support ticket for something that should be self-service). Renamed in `AccountNav.tsx`, the `SecuritySection` heading, the overview card in `app/(public)/cactus-account/page.tsx` (link label **Manage account**) and the **Settings → Users → Sections** toggle in `MembersSettingsTab.tsx`; the config key (`accountSectionsEnabled.security`), the route (`/{memberAreaPath}/security`) and every API path are untouched, so nothing stored or linked has to move. The change itself is two-step, mirroring the staff-side `app/api/account/email/route.ts` and for the same reason it was rebuilt that way: applying an address the moment it is typed hands the account - and its verified marker - to a mailbox nobody has proved exists, quietly redirecting every future sign-in link and recovery code into it. New `app/api/members/email/route.ts` (GET status / POST request / PUT confirm) parks the requested address on a `MemberEmailChallenge` row with the new purpose `email_change` and emails a six-digit code **to the new address**; `Member.email` moves only when that code comes back. Schema: `MemberEmailChallenge.pendingEmail` (nullable TEXT, no backfill) - init migration edited in place plus idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/017_member_email_change_pending.sql`, the twin of `011_email_change_pending.sql` on the `EmailChallenge` side. `lib/members/email-challenge.ts` gained the purpose, the optional `pendingEmail` argument, `pendingMemberEmailChange(memberId)` and a `pendingEmail` on its success result (verifying deletes the row, so that is the caller's only chance to learn which address was confirmed). Two new registry templates, `member.email-change-code` (to the new address) and `member.email-change-notice` (to the old one, so a member whose session has been taken finds out while they can still act), both transactional, both added to `MemberEmailTemplateKey` and `listMemberEmailTemplateKeys()`. Refusals a site owner will actually meet: an admin-linked member (`Member.userId` set) is sent to the admin account page rather than allowed to desync the two rows, and a site with no email sending configured is told plainly instead of being offered a code that can never arrive. Otherwise the usual guards - section enabled, `email_change`/`email_code` rate limits, current password when one exists, `isEmailDomainAllowed`, and a case-insensitive clash check run at request **and** confirm time. Completing it stamps `emailVerified`/`emailVerifiedAt` (the code proves the mailbox), records an `email_changed` activity event with `{from, to}` - new label in `ActivitySection.tsx` and the overview's `CORE_ACTIVITY_LABELS` - and sends a `member.security-alert` to the old address. Sessions and trusted browsers are deliberately left alone: no sign-in credential changed. `wiki/Members.md` gained a **Changing their email address** section; backup round-trip re-run and PASSED for the new column.)

Deliberately NOT at `createPendingOrder`: an abandoned checkout would otherwise file an address nobody committed to. Guest orders (`memberId` null) are a no-op, and the whole thing is try/caught - a shop that cannot write an address book has still taken a real order. **Dedupe**: new exported `addressDoorKey()` in `lib/db/addresses.ts` - `line1|line2|postcode`, whitespace stripped, lower-cased - plus `rememberAddressForMember()`, a single `INSERT ... SELECT ... WHERE NOT EXISTS` that rebuilds the identical key in SQL (`lower(regexp_replace(coalesce(address->>'line1','')||'|'||..., '[[:space:]]', '', 'g'))`; POSIX class, not `\s`, which a tagged template would eat). One statement rather than read-then-write because confirm and webhook can land together. Name and phone are deliberately outside the key: same door, different recipient, one entry. `is_default` is set only when it is the member's first row, via a second `NOT EXISTS` in the same statement. **JS and SQL keys must be changed together** - verified equal against the live Postgres at build time; the JS half is pinned by new `lib/db/address-door-key.test.ts` (6 cases). **Reading**: `CheckoutShippingClient` fetches `/api/m/shop/member/addresses` on mount (skipped in the Puck preview), draws a **Deliver to** radio fieldset above the fields listing each saved address plus **Use a different address**, and prefills from the default (or first) address only when `shippingAddress.line1` is empty, so a part-typed or stepped-back-to checkout is never clobbered. Picking one calls `chooseSaved` (fills the form, clears `touched`); editing any field or picking an address-lookup suggestion drops the radio back to "a different address", since the fields no longer describe the stored entry. A 401 (signed out) leaves the list empty and the form exactly as it was. `AddressesClient` gained `addressTitle()` so label-less automatic rows show the recipient's name rather than three identical "Address" headings, and the page's standfirst now describes what actually happens. `wiki/Shop.md` Customer accounts section updated. Module version NOT bumped and nothing committed - awaiting the word.)

First, `CheckoutPaymentClient.tsx` printed "Tick the boxes at the bottom of the page and this payment method will be set up for you." whenever `awaiting === 'agreements'`; the boxes are on the same screen, next to the button that is about to ask for them, so the render is now gated on `awaiting === 'details'` only and the agreements branch says nothing. `awaiting` still tracks both states - it gates the prepare, which is what it was for. Second, the `shop.order-payment-state` note (advanced-shipping's "Nothing is dispatched until your payment reaches us…") only ever arrived on the `payment-intent` response, and that route refuses until the contact/delivery details are complete AND every compulsory tickbox is ticked - so the one sentence explaining what bank transfer costs the shopper in delivery time appeared long after they had chosen it. New `previewOrderPaymentNotes(paymentMethod, lines)` in `modules/shop/lib/order-payment-state.ts` runs the same registered providers against a **prospective** order: `prospectiveOrder()` carries the real payment method and `PENDING` payment status with every other figure a placeholder (`id: ''`, zero totals, empty address), `prospectiveItems()` carries the real server-resolved `lineMeta` off `ResolvedCartLine`, and only `note` is kept - `items` restatements are dropped, so nothing is written and no order or provider intent is created. New optional `preview?: boolean` on `OrderPaymentStateInput` says so in the contract: a provider that reads only its input can ignore it, one that re-reads its own order row or writes anything must return null. New route `POST /api/m/shop/public/checkout/payment-note` (`modules/shop/app/api/public/checkout/payment-note/route.ts`) takes `{ lines, paymentMethod }`, runs `resolveCartLines`, filters to available lines and returns `{ notes }`; guarded by `shopClosedResponse()`, no rate limit since it creates nothing. Client-side a new effect fetches it on method change and re-fetches on `subscribeCart` (the sentence quotes the longest lead time in the basket), discarding the response if the method changed mid-flight or a real prepared order for that method already set its own notes. `advanced-shipping-for-shop` is unchanged - its existing `restateDeliveryForPayment` provider takes the unpaid branch, which does no database reads - so an install picks this up on a shop update alone. Shipped as shop `0.1.184`, pinned in core `modules.json`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**A signed-in site admin is let into the member area instead of being asked to sign in again** - staff sign-in and member sign-in stay separate identities (MEMBERS_SPEC.md amendment 1: separate tables, cookies, token namespaces), which was right for the credentials and wrong for the person holding them: an admin opening `/{memberAreaPath}` had no `Member` row, so the account layout bounced them to a sign-in form on their own site. New nullable unique `Member.userId` → `User` (SetNull) is the link, so an admin gets a member account of their own rather than the admin session being given a second meaning. Init migration edited in place **and** `prisma/core-reconcile/016_member_admin_link.sql` for existing installs; backup round-trip re-run and passing. New `lib/members/admin-link.ts` (`findOrCreateMemberForUser`, + `admin-link.test.ts`): returns the already-linked member, else adopts the row with the same email (activating a `PENDING_VERIFICATION` one - staff sign-in verifies that address; refuses SUSPENDED/DELETED, and never steals a row linked to a different `User`), else creates one - ACTIVE, `emailVerified`, seeded "Members" role, staff username when free and `generateUsernameFromEmail` when not. New `GET /api/members/auth/admin-continue` does the session-issuing; `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` redirects there instead of to `login?redirect=` when a staff session is present. Sign-out still means something: both member logout routes set `cactus_member_admin_optout` (session cookie) for a linked member, the layout honours it, and the login page's new "Continue to your account" panel clears it - that panel also covers a direct visit to `/{memberAreaPath}/login` while signed in as staff. Loop guard `cactus_member_admin_attempt` (60s) turns a dropped cookie into `login?admin_link=failed` with an explanation rather than an endless bounce. The required-sign-in-method gate is skipped for linked members (they come in on staff credentials, which carry the site's own admin sign-in requirements), and `POST /api/members/delete-account` 403s for them - the staff half would only mint another. `MembersSignInRsc`/`MembersAccountLinkRsc` show the signed-in face to a staff session with no member session, since the account page now admits it. Admin **Users** list marks the member half of a staff account with a "Staff account" badge (`linkedToStaff` added to `GET /api/admin/people`), so the same person appearing twice reads as deliberate.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The composable header's side gutter is a setting, per screen size** - new `paddingX` root field on `headerPuckConfig.root` (`lib/puck/config.tsx`), a `ResponsiveUnitValueField` in px/rem/%/vw labelled "Side padding (blank = 1.5rem)". `headerRootRender` previously hardcoded `padding: '0 1.5rem'` on `[data-header-inner]`, so the gap between the screen edge and the logo (and the actions on the other side) could not be touched at all - a phone header with a narrow logo column wasted a chunk of its width on dead space it could not reclaim. Desktop stays inline on the element; tablet/mobile come out of `responsiveMediaCssFor('[data-header-inner]', …)`, which only emits a breakpoint whose value differs from desktop and carries `!important` so it beats the inline base. Blank at every breakpoint resolves to `1.5rem`, so every header saved before the field existed renders byte-identically. Selector is the bare attribute (no per-instance id) because the root render has no `id` and there is one header per page. `headerPuckRscConfig` spreads `headerPuckConfig`, so the RSC path inherits the same root render and needs no override.)

New `SECTIONS_BEFORE_EXTRAS = ['profile','security']` splits the built-in section items and the extras go in the seam - `findIndex` on the first non-before key rather than a fixed offset, since any section can be switched off in **Settings → Users → Account sections** (`-1` = every enabled section belongs in front, extras go on the end, which is what happens when only Profile/Security are on). Also 2026-08-03 (**A magic sign-in link lands on the member's account, not the homepage** - `app/(public)/cactus-account/login/page.tsx` only. `sendMagicLink` builds `/{memberAreaPath}/login?magic_token=…` with no `?redirect=`, and the page was calling `sanitizeRedirect(redirect)` whose default fallback is `/`, so `LoginForm`'s post-consume `window.location.href = redirectTo` sent every link sign-in to the homepage. Fallback is now `basePath`. The `isPublicMemberPath()` loop guard is unaffected: `basePath` itself is not a public member subpath. Same fix covers password and passkey sign-ins reached by typing `/{memberAreaPath}/login` directly. Previously: **A member with no password and no passkey gets the sign-in link emailed on Continue, instead of a second step holding one button** - `components/members/LoginForm.tsx` only, no API change. `handleContinue` now keeps the resolved `AuthMethods` in a local instead of only in state, and when it comes back `{passkey:false, password:false, magicLink:true}` - the day-one shape, and also the enumeration-safe answer `/api/members/auth/methods` gives an address with no account - it awaits `handleMagicLink(address)` and skips the `methods` step entirely. `handleMagicLink` takes the address as an argument (defaulting to the `email` state) because `setEmail(address)` has not landed by then; its one existing caller became `onClick={() => handleMagicLink()}` so the click event is never passed as the address. The Continue button reads "Sending…" while that request is in flight. The `magic-sent` screen gained a "use a different email address" link back to step one, since a typo can now reach it without anyone pressing a button for it. A lookup that fails still falls back to `siteMethods`, so a link-only site auto-sends there too.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Each sign-in method is now one Off / Optional / Required setting, and Required is actually enforced** - `membersConfig.authMethodPolicies` replaces the old `allowedAuthMethods` array plus separate `passwordsEnabled` boolean (two switches that both had to agree before passwords were offered); `normaliseLegacyAuthMethods` reads the old pair so no stored row changes meaning, and every caller goes through `isAuthMethodEnabled`/`isAuthMethodRequired` in `lib/members/config.ts`. `MAGIC_LINK` deliberately has only two states - there is nothing to enrol, the credential is a verified mailbox. Required bites in two places: the registration form asks for a password when `PASSWORD` is not `OFF` (required at `REQUIRED`, hashed in the register route *before* the enumeration-safe existing-email branch so a weak password cannot be used to probe for an address), and the account layout redirects to the new `/{memberAreaPath}/setup-signin` while `memberOutstandingAuthSetup()` returns anything - a required password only counts as done once a verified second factor exists alongside it, since password login refuses outright without one. Removing a last passkey or a password is refused while that method is required. Saving with every method off is refused; saving with the email sign-in link off warns that brand-new members then have no way in at all, passkeys and passwords both being enrolled from inside an account they cannot yet reach. New: `lib/members/auth-policy.ts` + tests, `components/members/account/RequiredSignInSetup.tsx`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**A hover dropdown no longer shuts while you are on your way into it** - `MenuBlockClient.tsx`. A top-level panel sits 4px below its trigger, and the pointer crossing that gap is over neither element, so the `<li>`'s `onMouseLeave` fired and the menu closed. The existing transparent bridge covered only `width:100%` of the trigger, and a panel is nearly always the wider of the two (`min-width:180px` against a ~80px menu item), so any diagonal approach to the middle or right of a row passed through ~100px of no-man's-land - measured live on Deskwell as trigger `x 404.4-486.5`, panel `x 404.4-584.4`, `elementFromPoint` outside the li for every x past 486. The panel now hangs in a new `DROPDOWN_ANCHOR` box at `top:100%` whose transparent `padding-top:4px` *is* the gap, with the sizing (`minWidth`/`width:max-content`/`maxWidth`/`zIndex`) moved off the panel and onto that anchor so the padding spans the panel's full width; the panel keeps `PANEL_CHROME` (the old visual styles, split out) and `SUBDROPDOWN_PANEL` absorbs its own copy, sub-panels hanging flush at `left:100%` with no gap to bridge. The 6px strip stays for the reverse case, a menu item wider than the panel it opens. Rendered position is unchanged to the pixel, so nothing moves.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Every email the site sends now lives on one tab, inside a design you build in the layout editor** - a single registry, `lib/email/registry.ts`, holds core's `member.*` (12), `auth.*` (8) and `system.*` (1) templates plus whatever the installed modules declare through the new manifest `emailTemplates` seam. The eight `auth.*` ones (login code, email verification, email-change code + notice, recovery link/requested/completed, password changed) were hardcoded strings in `lib/email/index.ts` and are now editable like the rest; each declares `requiredTags`, and a save that has dropped one (`{{code}}`, `{{recoveryUrl}}`) is refused. Editor moved from Settings > Users > Email templates to **Settings > Email > Templates** (`?tab=email&sub=templates`; the old `?sub=email-templates` deep link still lands there), and the permission renamed `members.email-templates` -> `emails.templates` (core-reconcile `015_email_templates_unified.sql` moves existing grants, and makes `EmailTemplate.subject`/`bodyHtml` nullable + adds `wrapperLayoutId`/`isActive`). New core layout type **`emailWrapper`** with its own Puck config (`lib/puck/email-config.tsx`) and its own block set - none of the site blocks are offered, since classes and `var(--…)` arrive at an inbox as unstyled text. Each block is one `toHtml()` function in `lib/email/blocks.ts` emitting inline-styled tables; the editor previews by dropping that same string through `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`, so canvas and inbox cannot drift. Colour fields hold a design-token id resolved to its light-mode hex at send time. Wrapper per email is a dropdown on the Templates tab, default = highest-priority published wrapper. Three starter wrappers seed on a fresh install (Default/Plain/Branded + Blank). Six module repos moved onto the seam: **shop** (its 10 order emails, `shp_email_templates` table and its own settings sub-tab retired - migration `014` carries across only wording an owner had actually edited), **quote-for-shop** (4), **reviews-for-shop** (2), **boards** (2, and the digest's thread titles are escaped now), **twilio** (2), **contact-form** (2 owner notifications; the auto-reply and an owner's own typed reply are deliberately left alone).) Also **the frontend member sign-in form is identifier-first**: email address + Continue, then only the methods that address actually has, from the new public `POST /api/members/auth/methods` (rate limit `member_auth_methods`, 30/15min/IP). Passkey button only for a member with a `MemberPasskey`, password button only for one with a `MemberPassword`, sign-in link whenever the site allows it - so a member with neither is offered the link and nothing else. Unknown addresses, unparseable bodies and rate-limited callers all get that same link-only answer; a failed lookup client-side falls back to every method the site allows. New `.field input[readonly]` styling in `app/globals.css` for the settled email field.

Also 2026-08-03 (**A collapsed menu button can fill its slot, and stops overflowing it** - `MenuBlock` gains the per-breakpoint `navButtonWidth` field (`auto`, the default and old behaviour, or `full`), which sizes the "Dropdown (current page)" trigger to the slot it was dropped into and pushes its bars to the far edge like a select; at `auto` the button is exactly its content's width, so there is no free space and both values render identically - every existing menu is untouched. `fitOneLine` ("Keep on one line") now reaches that trigger too: it caps the button at `max-width:100%` and shrinks the label through `HeadingFitText` instead of letting a long page name wrap or spill past its column. The trigger carries `data-menu-dd-id="<block id>"` so the width rules scope to one block. Threaded through `lib/puck/config.tsx`, `MenuBlockClient.tsx`, `MenuBlockEditorPreview.tsx` and both editors. Alongside it, the **search module** (0.1.8) makes the Search Box's `size` per-breakpoint: `searchSizeStyles()` returns the desktop `srch-size-*` class plus, only where a breakpoint differs, a media rule re-declaring `--srch-pad`/`--srch-font`/`--srch-icon` scoped to `[data-srch-id="<block id>"]` - so a header box reads smaller on phones with desktop untouched. `SRCH_SIZE_VARS` in `search-css.ts` is now the single source for the three sizes, and the client config carries `sizeClass`/`sizeCss`/`blockId` in place of the old flat `size`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The member account is a real account area now, and a shop customer can manage their own orders in it** - core gains two seams so a module can live *inside* the account rather than beside it: **`members.account-nav`** (`lib/members/account-nav.ts`, collected by `getMemberAccountNavExtras()` from installed manifests; a provider that throws is dropped rather than locking a member out of their own security settings) contributes `{key,label,href,badge?}` tabs to the account tab bar, and **`components/members/account/MemberAccountShell.tsx`** is the chrome (container, `AccountFlash`, deletion banner, `notice` slot, `AccountNav`) lifted out of `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` so a module's own member pages - which are outside that route group and never saw the layout - wear the identical thing. `AccountNav` now matches Overview exactly and every other tab by prefix, so a module's detail page still lights its tab. The overview stopped being two lines of signposting and became a dashboard: avatar, email, member-since, an unverified-email nag with a working resend button (`VerifyEmailNudge.tsx`), and four cards (security posture, profile gaps, notifications, last three activity events) in one `Promise.all`. **shop 0.1.181** takes both seams: Orders and Addresses are tabs with a pending-request count pill, and every `/shop/account/*` page wraps `MemberAccountShell` instead of rendering bare - which was the actual defect, a shopper clicking "Order history" landed on a page with no tabs and no way back. Order history gained dates, thumbnails, status/fulfilment pills and JS-free `?show=` filters; order detail gained the totals breakdown, both addresses, per-parcel carrier + tracking, itemised refunds, pre-order and dispatched/refunded per-line badges, Buy again, and a printable receipt at `/shop/account/orders/[id]/receipt`. **Customer cancel and return requests** are new end to end: migration `015_order_requests.sql` (mirrored in 001) adds `shp_order_requests` + `shp_order_request_items`, with a partial unique index on `(order_id) WHERE status='PENDING'` as the real race guard; `lib/order-requests.ts` holds the eligibility rules ONE place so the button and the endpoint cannot disagree (cancel only before anything is dispatched, return only after and only inside `returnWindowDays` counted from the LAST parcel out, never from the order date); `lib/db/order-requests.ts` records under the same advisory lock refunds and dispatch already share (now exported from `lib/db/shipments.ts` rather than copied a fourth time); `lib/order-request-actions.ts` decides what approving MEANS - record the decision first so two admins cannot both run the refund behind it, then the optional refund, then the status change, with a failed refund reported in `refundError` rather than silently swallowed or rolled back. Member APIs `POST /api/m/shop/member/orders/[id]/requests` and `DELETE /api/m/shop/member/requests/[id]`; admin queue at **Shop → Cancellations & returns** (`/m/shop/requests`, `RequestsScreen.tsx`, `GET|POST /api/m/shop/admin/requests[/id]`) where the refund tickbox is a deliberate second step because money leaving should never be one stray click. Four new email templates (`shop.request-received`/`-approved`/`-declined`/`shop.admin-new-request`) and three config keys (`cancelRequestsEnabled`, `returnRequestsEnabled` both default true, `returnWindowDays` default 30). Auto-approval was deliberately left out: money leaving on a timer is not a default anyone should inherit.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Registration survives a broken mail server, and the username/display-name fields are optional** - `POST /api/members/register` no longer throws when `sendVerificationEmail` fails: the `Member` row already exists by then, so the failure is caught, `console.error`ed and reported as `verificationEmailSent: false` in the 200 body. Throwing produced a bare 500 whose non-JSON body made the browser's own `Response.json()` parse failure the error the member saw - in Safari, "The string did not match the expected pattern." - while the account sat unusable on `PENDING_VERIFICATION` with no link ever sent. `RegisterForm` now parses error bodies with `.catch(() => ({}))`, and on `verificationEmailSent === false` stays put with a warning rather than sending them to `/verify-email` to wait for a link that was never sent. The existing-email branch sends for real too (magic link if ACTIVE, verification link again if PENDING_VERIFICATION and past the resend throttle) so the new flag means the same thing on both branches and stays enumeration-safe. `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend` likewise catches and logs - a 500 there answered "is this address registered?" out loud. Two new `MembersConfigSchema` keys, both default true: `registrationCollectUsername` and `registrationCollectDisplayName`. Off hides the field AND makes the API ignore anything sent for it; with the username off, `generateUsernameFromEmail()` (new, `lib/members/registration.ts`, `lib/members/registration.test.ts`) builds one from the local part plus 4 random digits, widening to 8 after 15 collisions and falling back to `member` when the address leaves nothing usable. Admin toggles live in the Members → Registration tab. Separately, `RegisterForm`'s username `pattern` was `[a-z0-9_-]{2,32}`, which browsers compile with the regex `v` flag where a bare trailing `-` in a class is a syntax error: the attribute was skipped, so it had been validating nothing in every browser. Now `[a-z0-9_\-]{2,32}` - previously: **A payment method can be named by the site owner** - `ShpPaymentProvider` gained an optional `getLabel(): Promise<string>`, resolved per request by the new `resolveProviderLabel()` in `modules/shop/lib/payments/registry.ts`; `getPaymentMethodLabels()` is async as a result, and its three consumers now await it (`GET public/config`, `GET public/orders/status`, `GET admin/settings`'s `listPaymentMethodsForAdmin`). The static `label` is the fallback whenever `getLabel` is absent, returns blank, or throws - a checkout radio with no wording beside it being worse than a stale one. First user: `square-payment-for-shop` v0.1.3, whose **Payment description** setting now names the method everywhere instead of only reaching Square's own hosted page - previously: **Shop Payments settings rebuilt around one method per tab** - `modules/shop/components/admin/PaymentsSettings.tsx` (new) replaces the flat block that was `ShopSettingsTab`'s Payments sub-tab. A chip strip runs across the top: **Payment methods** (the list) then one chip per method that has settings of its own. The list shows EVERY registered method - shop's own four plus whatever modules contributed - each with an on/off `role="switch"`, a live status badge (Showing at checkout / Not finished / Off), a one-line reason, a Set up link into its own chip, and drag-handle + ▲▼ reordering that sets the order the checkout offers them in. Two new `ShpConfig` keys back it: `disabledPaymentMethods` (the shop-wide veto, and the ONLY off switch a module-contributed method ever had - being named there beats a provider reporting itself ready) and `paymentMethodOrder` (the arrangement; empty falls back to `enabledPaymentMethods` order, so an existing shop's checkout does not reshuffle itself). `getAvailablePaymentMethods()` was rewritten around one per-provider rule (`paymentMethodAvailability`) plus `sortPaymentMethods`. The ordering and switched-on rules live in the new client-safe `modules/shop/lib/payments/admin-methods.ts` (unit-tested in `admin-methods.test.ts`) because the settings screen cannot import shop config without dragging Prisma into the browser bundle. `GET admin/settings` now also returns `paymentMethods[]` ({id,label,builtIn,ready,panelId}), and `registry.ts` gained `getModuleProviderEntryIds()` so a method row can find its module's own panel. The `shop.payments` hosted slot is now consumed as the **labelled** shape (`hostedSettingsPanels`), one chip per panel, not merged - previously: **The member area gated its own sign-in page** - `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` is the session gate for the whole member area, and in Next.js a layout wraps *every* page beneath it, so `login`, `register` and `verify-email` were gated too. Signed out, `/{memberAreaPath}/login` redirected to `/{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=<itself>`, and each hop `encodeURIComponent`-ed the entire previous URL into the next one, doubling the encoding every round until the address outgrew what a browser will load. The shop's post-purchase "Create an account" link into `/{memberAreaPath}/register?email=…` walked straight into it and dead-ended on Safari's "can't open the page". The gate now excepts those three sub-paths through a new pure `isPublicMemberPath(fullPath, basePath)` in `lib/members/paths.ts` (with `MEMBER_PUBLIC_SUBPATHS`, unit-tested in `lib/members/paths.test.ts`) and renders them bare - no `AccountNav`, no deletion banner, since neither belongs to a visitor without a session. The login page separately drops a sanitised `?redirect=` that points back at a signed-out member page, so a stale link cannot restart the loop. Announcing the flip needs three new flags - `watched` (only the shopper who sat through the wait is told it cleared), `pollGaveUp`, and `basketCleared`, the last because a payment that fails AFTER settling began has already had its basket emptied, so the retry copy must point at the shop rather than an empty checkout - previously: **A failed open-banking payment now actually lands, and "awaiting confirmation" stops meaning two opposite things** - `markOrderPaymentFailed`'s default branch guarded on `payment_status = 'PENDING'`, but the GoCardless return route had already moved the order to `AWAITING_CONFIRMATION`, so the failure webhook that followed matched no rows and the order sat in that queue for good; The flashing was the un-blend faithfully amplifying that wrong alpha: composited over a page of luminance `bg` an un-blended pixel is `C - (1-a)*(255-bg)`, a flat offset on every pixel, so a per-frame alpha wobble shifts a whole region together instead of cancelling (measured 8.66 levels of swing vs 4.33 with no un-blend; a gain cap does not help since mesh alpha is high). New `_key_white_gaps` derives coverage from the frame's own colour (`(255-L)/(255-L_localmin)`, two ramps guarding flat pale surfaces and dark textured fabric), run before the un-blend: swing drops to 3.26 and the holes show the page colour. (**Per-person tier pricing (advanced-shipping-for-shop 0.1.10)**: any service-tier price can now be flagged **per person** and is multiplied by a person count read off a shop-nominated product attribute, generic to any shop (not tied to any one range/attribute name) - built for ranges like "Bench Desks" priced per seat via a "Seats" attribute ("2 People"/"6 People"), but works for any per-head pricing. Previous entry follows.) (**"High quality" scroll-sequence preset was OOM-killing the worker every job; birefnet removed, worker cap raised (core + sequence-worker repo)**: every conversion failed with "The conversion service restarted and lost this job." Root cause on the OVH box (shared with live Postgres): the `quality` preset ran the **birefnet** engine, which needs **3 GB+ of RAM even on a 640px frame** (it does not downscale internally the way isnet does), so the kernel OOM-killed the `MemoryMax=2G` unit mid-matte; systemd restarted it, the in-memory job vanished, `GET /jobs/{id}` 404'd, and the status route flipped the job to Failed. (A separate earlier fix had already defaulted `ALPHA_MATTING_MODE` off - matting is a second, smaller memory hog - but birefnet alone still blew the cap.) Fix, core: `lib/media/sequence-presets.ts` drops `birefnet` from `SEQUENCE_ENGINES` (now `['isnet']`) and the `quality` default engine becomes `isnet` (still fps 30 / maxWidth 1920); removing the enum value **self-heals any stored `sequenceConfig` that still names birefnet** - `parseSequenceConfig`'s `safeParse` rejects it and falls back to the isnet defaults, so no DB edit is needed. The engine picker is gone from `SequenceSettingsPanel.tsx` (only one engine now; `type Engine = 'isnet'`), `MediaSequenceDialog.tsx`'s preset summary drops the engine phrase (`describePreset` = fps + width), and the quality blurb now reads "more frames + wider image" (its real difference) rather than "sharper edges" (birefnet's). `MediaTabs.tsx` + `lib/media/sequence.ts` `Engine` unions narrowed to `'isnet'`. Fix, worker (`services/sequence-worker`, own repo, deployed to the box): `app.py` `ENGINE_MODELS` drops birefnet so a birefnet request returns a clean **400** instead of taking the box down; `sequence-worker.service` `MemoryMax` **2G -> 2.5G** (isnet peaks ~1.85 GB in the long-running process as onnxruntime holds its arena; the cap still leaves ~1.3 GB for DB+OS and keeps this service the kernel's OOM victim if anything ever exceeds it). **Verified on the box:** two full 1920px isnet jobs ran start-to-finish (0->100%, frames+manifest uploaded to B2), RSS flat at ~1.85 GB, no OOM; a birefnet POST returns 400. isnet is model-bound (~constant RAM 1280-1920px, resizes internally to 1024²), so lowering width would not have bought headroom - the cap bump was the lever. tsc + eslint clean. Core needs a patch bump + release; worker already committed/pushed (`cactus-sequence-worker`) and live on the box. Previous entry follows.) (**Scroll-sequence Recent jobs: manual Refresh + live worker poll + orphaned-job auto-fail (core, working tree)**: `app/cactus-admin/media/SequenceSettingsPanel.tsx` gains a **Refresh** button in the Recent jobs header. Root fix: a job's notification only advances via the convert dialog (while open) or the worker's final done/error callback, so a job whose dialog was closed froze at its last-seen % and both the button and the 8s poller (which only re-read `/api/admin/media/sequence-jobs`) showed nothing new. `loadJobs` now, for every job still `queued`/`running` (tracked via a `jobsRef`), first pokes `/api/admin/media/sequence-status?jobId=…` (best-effort, `cache:'no-store'`) - which proxies the worker's live progress and rewrites the notification - then re-reads the list; the button and the poller share it. Second fix: the worker keeps jobs in memory only, so a restart makes it answer **404 `job not found`** for an in-flight job forever, stranding it at "Building 0%". `lib/media/sequence.ts` `SequenceWorkerError` now carries the response `status` (constructor 2nd arg; `getSequenceJob` passes `res.status`), and `app/api/admin/media/sequence-status/route.ts` on a 404 marks the notification `error` ("The conversion service restarted and lost this job. Convert the video again.") and returns `{status:'error'}` instead of a bare 502 - so the next Refresh auto-flips a stranded job to Failed rather than leaving it stuck. No schema/backup change; tsc + eslint + sequence/alerts tests clean. Previous entry follows.) (**Advanced delivery admin moves from its own sidebar group into tabs on Shop → Tax & shipping (advanced-shipping-for-shop + shop, working tree)**: the module's four admin screens (Delivery rules / Service tiers / Holidays / Delivery settings) no longer appear as a standalone **Delivery** sidebar section - they are now tabs alongside the shop's own Tax & shipping tab. (**Scroll sequence Puck block (core, working tree)**: new core Puck block "Scroll sequence" (Media category) that plays a converted sequence as a scroll-scrubbed animation. `lib/puck/components/ScrollSequence.tsx` ('use client'): fetches the manifest, preloads frames (deferred via an IntersectionObserver near-viewport gate), draws to a `<canvas>` sized to the frame aspect (transparent, so it sits on any light/dark page background); scroll-scrubs the frame index across a sticky spacer (height = `(1 + scrubScreens) * 100vh`), loops at the end via rAF at the manifest fps, and fades opacity on enter/exit via an IntersectionObserver ratio; the editor path shows a static poster (never scrolljacks the builder), and a failed manifest degrades to the poster/message. `lib/puck/config.tsx`: `ScrollSequence` registered in `puckConfig.components` + the `media` category; fields sequenceUrl/scrubScreens/loop/fade/maxWidth/ariaLabel; the render only hands props to the client component (editor-safe, and the RSC/published path reuses it via `getModuleLayoutSharedParts`, so no config.rsc.tsx change — it therefore appears in the shop product-description editor, which is core shared-categories only). `lib/puck/MediaPickerField.tsx`: `MediaPickerModal` gains `kind: 'image' | 'sequence'` (sequence mode filters by `isSequenceType`, fetches `type=other` then narrows, hides the upload control, shows poster thumbnails); new `SequenceUrlPickerField` + `SEQUENCE_PICKER_FIELDS`, both wired through the existing `withImagePickerFields` (now swaps image AND sequence fields), so the block's `sequenceUrl` field becomes a sequence picker that stores the picked item's manifest url. (**Media library: video upload + convert video → transparent scroll sequence (core, working tree)**: the media library now accepts video (mp4/webm) and can turn a video into a "scroll sequence" — a folder of alpha-WebP frames + `manifest.json` in object storage, produced off-platform, shown as ONE library tile. `lib/media/limits.ts`: `VIDEO_DIRECT_TYPES` (video/mp4, video/webm) wired into `isUploadableType`/`isDirectUploadType`/`EXTENSION_TYPES`/`UPLOAD_ACCEPT_ATTR` (video rides the direct-to-Worker path, never raster/optimisable); plus `SEQUENCE_MIME` (`application/vnd.cactus.sequence+json`) + `isSequenceType`. `workers/media-worker/index.ts`: accepts a video PUT and SERVES video inline with `Range`/206 (Safari needs it) via its own `SERVABLE_VIDEO_TYPES` set (kept out of `SERVABLE_IMAGE_TYPES`, which a test guards); mp4/webm added to its mirrored `EXTENSION_TYPES` — **the Worker must be redeployed (Settings → Media) for video upload/preview**. `proxy.ts`: added a `media-src` CSP directive (self + Worker origin) so the `<video>` preview isn't blocked (media-src otherwise falls back to default-src 'self'). Media UI (`MediaCard`/`MediaList`/`MediaDetailPanel`/`format.ts`): 🎬 video tile + `<video controls>` preview; 🎞️/poster sequence tile (poster derived via new `sequencePosterUrl` in `format.ts`); "Convert to scroll sequence…" action on video items; `fileKind` returns "Scroll sequence" for the mime. New `lib/media/sequence.ts`: off-platform worker HTTP client (`enqueueSequenceJob`/`getSequenceJob`), a signed callback-context token (`signSequenceContext`/`verifySequenceContext`, SESSION_SECRET-derived, carries folderId+name across the long job), `verifyCallbackSignature` (HMAC over the raw body with the shared worker secret), and `buildDestPrefix`/`prefixFromManifestKey`/`posterKeyFromManifestKey`. New routes: `app/api/admin/media/[id]/convert-sequence` (enqueue on the worker), `app/api/admin/media/sequence-status` (progress proxy, hides the worker secret), `app/api/webhooks/sequence` (worker completion callback that records the single pointer `Media` row — placed under `/api/webhooks/` so the edge middleware ALWAYS_PASSes it; HMAC-gated, not session-gated; idempotent on the manifest key). `lib/media/upload.ts`: `deleteMediaTree(provider, prefix)` (S3 list+batch-delete) + `deleteMediaBytes(media)` (sequence-aware) now called by both delete routes so deleting a sequence tile takes its whole frame folder. New env: `SEQUENCE_WORKER_URL` + `SEQUENCE_WORKER_SECRET` (`lib/config/env.ts` getters + `isSequenceWorkerConfigured`); unset = the Convert action returns 503 (feature simply unavailable). Tests: `lib/media/video-types.test.ts` (app↔Worker type-table lockstep for video, mirrors the model one), `lib/media/sequence.test.ts` (token round-trip/tamper, callback signature, destPrefix traversal guard, key helpers). The conversion worker itself lives in its OWN repo (usersaynoso), NOT in core — `/services/` is gitignored; it runs on the OVH box as a `nice`d, CPU/mem-capped systemd service so it can never starve the co-located live Postgres. **Pending: the Puck scroll-sequence block** (scroll-scrub → loop → fade canvas) that consumes the manifest. tsc + eslint + 32 media tests clean. Previous entry follows.) (**Product-level attribute columns auto-attach on Pull (product-attributes-for-shop, working tree)**: the Products tab now behaves like the Variations tab - typing a value into a column that names an existing attribute a product does not yet use at product level attaches that attribute to the product and ticks the value, instead of ignoring the cell. `product-field-provider.ts` gained the auto-attach block (mirrors the variant provider's): an `attributesByName()` 10s cache off `listAllAttributes()`, a `RESERVED_PRODUCT_HEADERS` guard built from shop's `CSV_COLUMNS` (so an attribute named "Supplier" can never hijack the fixed supplier column), and `isAutoAttachHeader`. `applyImportedRow` refactored to a shared `resolveWanted`/`applyAssignment` pair used by both the already-assigned-columns loop and the new auto-attach loop; `rowChanged` gained the read-only detection twin. Crucially it never flips a variation helping to product level: new `upsertProductLevelAttribute(productId, attributeId)` in `db/membership.ts` inserts a product-level un-named helping `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, then reuses only an existing helping that is ALREADY `use_for_variations=false` - when the un-named slot is owned by a variation helping it returns null and the product is left alone (over-reported by `rowChanged` as a harmless no-op row). The `ProdImportCtx` now carries `assigned` (product id -> attribute id -> assignment id) to upsert once per attribute. Multi-select preserved (comma-separated cell). 8 new provider tests; tsc + eslint + 161 module tests clean. Previous entry follows.) (**Tax class imports by name OR code, and a bad value is now loud not silent (shop + google-sheet-products-for-shop, working tree)**: a Google-Sheet Pull (and any CSV import) that set a product's tax class silently did nothing whenever the cell wasn't an exact, case-sensitive match on the class `code`. The mirror writes the code (`vat`), but an owner filling a blank cell types the name they see in Shop settings (`VAT`), so `getTaxClassByCode('VAT')` missed, the engine set `taxClassId = null`, and the edit "failed to import" with no word why. New `buildTaxClassRefIndex()` in `modules/shop/lib/db/tax-shipping.ts` builds one case-insensitive lookup keyed by every class's code AND name; `import-engine.ts` resolves the cell through it (blank = clear, match = set, non-empty miss = a per-row error "Unknown tax class \"X\"…" that leaves the current class untouched instead of blanking it). `google-sheet-products-for-shop/lib/pull-diff.ts` resolves both sides through the same index (`taxClassEqual`) so a name-vs-code spelling of the same class reads as unchanged - no perpetual re-flag - while a genuinely different or unknown value still counts as a change so the row reaches the importer and its error surfaces. `getTaxClassByCode` kept (unused now, exact-code lookup). 4 new tax cases in `pull-diff.test.ts`; tsc + eslint + tests clean. Known follow-up, NOT fixed: product-level attributes have no auto-attach on Pull (unlike variation attributes), so typing a value into a product-level attribute column for a product that doesn't yet use that attribute is still ignored. (**Cart delivery options carry their own date, columns align (shop + advanced-shipping, working tree)**: each cart delivery option's label now bakes in its own promised date, so the shopper sees when every tier lands without selecting it - advanced-shipping `lib/line-resolver.ts` computes `computeEstimate` per tier (all pure/IO-free, no extra queries) and `tierOptionLabel` renders "Standard Delivery by Monday (included)" / "Express Delivery by Monday (+£4.95)"; new `formatDeliveryByLabel(date, today)` in `lib/working-days.ts` gives the weekday alone within 7 days ("Monday") and the full "Monday 10th of August" beyond it (new `ordinal`/`calendarDaysBetween` helpers + full weekday/month name tables). (**Full-screen description pop-out (shop, working tree)**: the product editor's inline Puck description builder gained an "Open in a new tab ↗" button that opens the same description on its own chrome-free page - new route `modules/shop/app/cactus-admin/shop/products/[id]/description/page.tsx` (dispatcher path `products/[id]/description`) whose inline `<style>` hides the admin sidebar/topbar and fills the viewport, mounting new client `StandaloneDescriptionEditor.tsx` (full-height `<Puck>`, header suppressed, own Back/Save bar, partial `PUT {descriptionPuck}`). (**Cart line layout: name / variation / delivery (shop + shop-variations, working tree)**: the Puck `Shop: Cart` block (`CartFullClient`) now puts the product name on its own line, a variant's chosen options on a muted line beneath it, and any per-line delivery picker in its OWN column between the product and the price. New generic **`displayTitle` on `CartLineResolution`** (`{ name, secondary? }`, shop `lib/line-meta.ts`): a cart-line resolver may split how a line is titled; shop folds it first-claim-wins like `control`, threads it `resolveLineMeta` -> `resolveCartLines` -> `ResolvedCartLine.displayTitle` -> `POST /cart/validate` response, and both `CartFullClient` and the `CartPageClient` fallback render `displayTitle.name` as the linked title with `displayTitle.secondary` as a muted sub-line (falling back to `product.name` when absent). (**Cart speed pass (shop 0.1.111 + advanced-shipping 0.1.6)**: root cause of the 7-8s deskwell cart was ~18 sequential DB round-trips per `cart/validate` × transatlantic latency (Vercel fn `iad1`, Postgres OVH France) × `pgbouncer=true` making each Prisma query BEGIN/DEALLOCATE ALL/query/COMMIT (~4 RTT). Fixes: ash `lib/ttl-cache.ts` cross-request 10s TTL memos (settings/rules/tiers/tier-config/holidays/timezone, invalidated on admin writes), category-ancestor chains batched into ONE recursive CTE, estimate route slug lookups batched (was N+1); shop `line-meta.ts` module-registry reads merged 2→1 behind 30s memo, validate media query parallel with line resolve, `recommendations.ts` `mapProductRows` de-N+1'd, new `POST /cart/upsells` batch endpoint, `UpsellClient` refreshes on cart-membership change only, cart islands single-flight validate (`validated-cache.ts` `postCartValidate`) + sessionStorage stale-while-revalidate instant paint, delivery-picker price moves optimistically via new optional `priceAdjust` on control options (ash sends it, server stays authoritative). Steady-state validate ≈6-8 queries. Region flip iad1→cdg1 is the other half, pending. Previous entry follows.) (**Variation deep links now work: a variant child's own URL - the `/shop/products/<child-slug>` link the cart already builds - opens its parent's product page with that combination pre-selected, instead of 404ing.** New generic **`shop.product-page-resolver`** extension point: shop `lib/product-page-resolver.ts` (`resolveAliasedProduct`, discovered through active-module manifests + `INSTALLED_MODULE_WHERE`, first-claim-wins, exactly like `resolveShopDetailProvider`). Shop's product page and `generateMetadata` (`app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx`) now offer a slug they would 404 - a `catalogue_hidden` row - to each module's resolver before giving up; a resolver returns the product whose page should render under that URL, and shop renders it off `product.slug` (layout scoring + `injectProductContext`) while the address bar keeps the variant link. Shop still names no variants; `git grep` leak check stays clean. Live consumer `shop-variations` (`lib/product-page-resolver.ts` `shopVariationsProductPageResolver`, id `variations-deep-link`): `resolveVariantDeepLink` (`variants-service.ts`) maps the hidden child slug -> parent + the variant's option-value ids via `getVariantByChildProductId` + `getVariantValueMap`, and stashes the ids in a new request-scoped slot (`rememberPreselectOptionValues`/`currentPreselectOptionValues` in `variation-bootstrap.ts`, same per-request `cache()` trick as the product slug). `getVariationBootstrap` carries them into `VariationBootstrap.preselectOptionValueIds` (filtered to values the payload actually holds); `use-variation-selection`'s `seededEntry`/`optionValuesFromValueIds` seeds them as the opening `optionValues`. Server HTML and client hydrate on the SAME slug - the parent's, handed down as the explicit slug prop, so `window.location` (the child slug) is never read and there is no mismatch - with the variant chosen, its live price/gallery already showing. All three storefront layouts (granular Product-Detail parts, the detail-slot takeover, the composite `ShopVariantPurchase` block) inherit it through that single bootstrap seed, so nothing in the block/part components changed. Deep-link tab title takes the variant's own descriptive name. No schema change (no backup gate). tsc + eslint clean.) Also: **Shop admin Orders list and single order screen rebuilt (shop, working tree)** - `OrdersScreen.tsx` and `OrderDetailScreen.tsx` replaced wholesale, sharing a new `orders-screen-css.ts` (`sox-` prefix, colour tokens only, light/dark and print). List gains overview tiles that double as filters, server-side search/payment/dispatch-state/date/sort filters kept in the query string, per-page paging, bulk status changes via a new `admin/orders/bulk`, and a filtered CSV export via a new `admin/orders/export`. Order screen becomes two columns with a single merged History timeline, per-parcel Undo, digital-download links, customer/payment/totals panels and a print packing-slip layout, and finally gives `POST .../email` a UI (`EmailCustomerModal.tsx`). Supporting work: `lib/order-status.ts` extracts `applyOrderStatusChange` so the bulk route cannot bypass the pre-order hold, `lib/order-filters.ts` is the one parser the list and the export share, `lib/db/orders.ts` gains fulfilment/date/sort/open filters plus `getOrderRowMetrics`/`getOrdersOverview`/`getCustomerSummary` and finally maps `listOrderNotes`/`listOrderEmails` to camelCase (`isInternal`/`createdAt` had been silently undefined on the order screen). No schema change (no backup gate). tsc + eslint clean, 1273 tests pass. **The verify-email page no longer looks like you can change your address there** - it always drew an editable email box, seeded from `?email=`, which reads as "fix your typo here"; it never was that. The box only ever fed `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`, which re-sends to an address that is already `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and answers `{ok:true}` to everything else, so a corrected address got the same 60s countdown and no email. `page.tsx` is now a server component reading `membersConfig`, and the client half moved to `components/members/VerifyEmailPanel.tsx`: with a valid-looking `?email=` it prints the address as text with a "Send it again" button, and only the paramless case (bookmarked/stale link) still asks for one. Sending now says so - the wording promises nothing about whether that address is registered, keeping the page as enumeration-safe as the endpoint. A mistyped address is unrecoverable by design, so the panel offers a "sign up again" link to `/{memberAreaPath}/register`, passed in only when `enabled && registrationMode !== 'INVITE_ONLY'` - an invite-only site would be offering a door needing a key the visitor hasn't got. `?email=` is checked against a basic address shape before being rendered, so a crafted link can't put arbitrary wording on the page under the site's name. No schema change (no backup gate). **A verified email now lands in the member area, not on the verify page** - `VerifyEmailPanel` takes a new required `accountHref` prop (`/{memberAreaPath}`, from the page) and on success stores the wording via `setMemberFlash()` then `router.replace(accountHref)` instead of rendering it as an inline `alert-success`; the account layout's gate hands a signed-out visitor straight on to `login?redirect=…`, which is where the message is wanted anyway. New `lib/members/flash.ts` (+ `flash.test.ts`, jsdom) is a one-shot sessionStorage hand-off - `setMemberFlash()` / `takeMemberFlash()`, read once then cleared, validated and capped at 300 chars on the way out, every storage access wrapped in try/catch for private-browsing setups. New client `components/members/account/AccountFlash.tsx` renders it as a fixed pill at the top of the viewport (`.member-flash*` in `globals.css`, `z-index: 9990` - above a sticky menu at 100/101, below the consent banner at 9998/9999), auto-dismissed after 9s with a manual close. It is mounted on **both** sides of the account layout's gate and its take effect is keyed on `usePathname()`, not mount: verify-email and login both render the layout's signed-out branch, so the component keeps its slot across that navigation and a mount-only effect would never look again. `VerifyEmailPanel` also gained a `submitted` ref so the one-shot token is POSTed once even though the effect now depends on `router`/`accountHref`.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**The shop's post-purchase prompt now carries the registration form, not a link to it** - `RegisterForm` gains two optional props: `showHeading` (default `true`; embedded uses already sit under a heading of their own, so its `<h1>Create an account</h1>` would be the second one on screen) and `verifyEmailUrl` (default keeps the old `window.location.pathname.replace(/\/register$/, '/verify-email')` derivation, which only ever worked on the register page - an embedded form reloaded its own URL with `?email=` on it instead). Shop's `GET /api/m/shop/public/orders/status` widens `accountPrompt` from `{registerUrl}` to also carry `verifyEmailUrl`, `registrationMode`, `collectUsername`, `collectDisplayName` and `privacyPolicyUrl` - read from `getMembersConfig()` plus a `SiteConfig.privacyPolicyPageId` → `InfoPage.slug` lookup, the same sources the register page reads, so an owner who drops the username picker doesn't find it back again on the confirmation. `OrderConfirmationClient` renders `<RegisterForm>` inside `.soc-account` in place of the `soc-btn` anchor, falling back to that anchor when `registrationMode` is absent (an older cached bundle answers with `registerUrl` alone). Two CSS rules added to `ORDER_CONFIRMATION_CSS`: `.soc-account form{margin:0}` and `.soc-account form p.field-hint{color:var(--color-text-muted)}`, the latter undoing the box's own `p` colour rule. The form styles itself with core's global `.field` / `.btn` / `.alert` classes. Shop 0.1.179 raises `requiresCoreVersion` from `0.5.571` to `0.5.885`, the core release carrying the two `RegisterForm` props - without them an older core ignores both and the box gets a second "Create an account" heading plus a redirect back onto itself. No schema change (no backup gate).)

Also 2026-08-03 (**New `MembersSignIn` Puck block, label "Members: Sign In"** - one click-to-sign-in control for headers and pages, modelled deliberately on the shop's `ShopCartSummary` cart widget so the pair look like siblings. Icon (person / person-in-circle / padlock / key / door-arrow / none) + optional label, bordered/filled/plain box with colour and radius knobs; `clickAction` either links to `<memberArea>/login?redirect=…` or opens `components/members/SignInModal.tsx` over the page, hosting the real `LoginForm` (lazily imported, `ssr:false`). Signed-in state is an account link, an account link plus sign-out, or nothing, optionally showing the member's own avatar. `audience: 'admin'` is the shop cart's try-it-live gate, reproduced: withheld from the public, rendered only for a signed-in site admin. **The field is `audience`, never `visibility`** - core injects a same-named responsive-visibility field into every block and strips it from render props. Editor half + block def in `lib/puck/config.tsx` (`MembersSignInBlock`, always the signed-out preview, modal inert), server half `MembersSignInRsc` in `lib/puck/components/MembersBlocksRsc.tsx`, RSC overrides in `config.rsc.tsx` for the page/layout/header configs. `LoginForm` gained optional `showHeading` and `basePath` so the modal can drop the form's own `<h1>` and keep its `verify-email` / SMS-enrolment detours absolute; the sign-in page passes neither and is unchanged.)

Also 2026-08-03 (**Notifications can be cleared in one go, from either place they appear** - the collection route `/api/admin/notifications` gains `PATCH {read: boolean}` (bulk `updateMany`: true stamps `readAt` on every unread row, false clears every read one) and `DELETE` (bulk `deleteMany({})`), both still behind `config.manage`. They deliberately act on the whole table rather than the slice the caller is holding - the page renders 100 rows and the bell 20, so a "mark all as read" scoped to what was on screen would leave the badge stubbornly non-zero. New `app/cactus-admin/notifications/NotificationBulkActions.tsx` puts "Mark all as read" (disabled at zero unread) and "Delete all" beside the total in the page header; the bell dropdown carries the same pair as quiet text buttons in its header (`.admin-bell-dropdown-headaction`), sharing the existing per-item loading/error maps under a `__bulk__` sentinel key. **`DELETE` deliberately spares open deployment notifications** (`{type: 'deployment', deployInitiatedAt: null}`, excluded via `NOT`): everything else is re-derivable - a video-optimise job still encoding rewrites its notification on the next progress tick and the update alerts are re-raised by the next check, all keyed by `dedupeKey` - but nothing re-creates the open deployment record, so deleting it would leave the site serving saved-but-unshipped config with no reminder and no Redeploy now button. It returns `{deleted, kept}`; both UIs disable Delete all when only the spared row is left, and both confirms say the pending changes are kept. The page's confirm names `total - pendingDeploy` (a fourth `count()` in its existing `Promise.all`), which can still be larger than the hundred rows rendered; the bell re-reads via `fetchNotifications()` after a delete rather than assuming an empty list, since the survivor may sit outside its twenty rows and still counts towards the badge.)

Flat factual inventory of the platform's routes, models, permissions, modules, env vars, components, scripts, and config - the current state, not a changelog. Per-release history lives in git and the GitHub releases. Update the affected sections plus this date after any substantive change.

---

## Core Application

### Routes

Pages (public):

- `/` - `app/(public)/page.tsx` - redirects to `/setup` until setup completes; renders the InfoPage set as `homepageId` (draft only for admins, with draft banner), else a welcome card with siteName/tagline/description. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]` - `app/(public)/[slug]/page.tsx` - renders an InfoPage by slug; drafts 404 for non-admins; `generateMetadata` (title, metaDescription, OG image), `generateStaticParams` for published slugs, `revalidate = false`. On an InfoPage miss, falls back to a module's public index via `resolveModulePublicPage(slug, [])`, then to `resolveModuleRootSlugPage(slug)` for a module claiming the bare slug for content of its own (InfoPage always wins a collision, and a module index beats a claim) - calls `getSessionFromCookie()` first so that fallback path always renders dynamically rather than being cached under `revalidate = false`.
- `/[slug]/[...path]` - `app/(public)/[slug]/[...path]/page.tsx` - generic catch-all for a module's public sub-pages, via `resolveModulePublicPage`. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]/feed.xml` - `app/(public)/[slug]/feed.xml/route.ts` - delegates to a module's `feed.xml` route via `dispatchModulePublicRoute`; a dedicated literal segment because `route.ts` can't share a folder with the `[...path]` page catch-all. `force-dynamic`.
- `/[slug]/[a]/feed.xml`, `/[slug]/[a]/[b]/feed.xml` - `app/(public)/[slug]/[a]/feed.xml/route.ts`, `app/(public)/[slug]/[a]/[b]/feed.xml/route.ts` - generic nested-feed delegates (Boards' per-board and per-sub-board RSS), same passthrough pattern one and two segments deeper. `force-dynamic`.
- `/logged-out` - `app/(public)/logged-out/page.tsx` - client page, 3-second countdown then redirect to `/`.
- `/page-preview/[id]` - `app/(public)/page-preview/[id]/page.tsx` - draft preview of an InfoPage; requires session + `pages.read`; always renders `builderData` with a fixed preview bar; noindex.
- `/layout-preview/[id]` - `app/layout-preview/[id]/page.tsx` - preview of a Layout; requires `layouts.manage` (was `isAdmin`, i.e. the protected role only - so the Preview button 404'd for every non-Admin role that had been granted layouts.manage); renders with the type-matched Puck RSC config plus placeholder content blocks; noindex. Outside the `(public)` group so header/footer are not applied.
- `app/(public)/layout.tsx` - public shell: resolves header/footer Layouts via `resolveThemeLayout`, injects design-token CSS + Google Fonts link, `AosInit`, `ConsentBanner` when enabled, favicon override from `faviconMediaId` (plus a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` icon from `faviconDarkMediaId` when set), and threads `logoDarkUrl` into the header/footer template context for the dark-mode logo swap.
- `app/layout.tsx` - root layout: Instrument Sans + JetBrains Mono fonts, theme flash-prevention inline script (`localStorage cactus-theme` → `data-theme` attribute), consent-init inline script (`cactus-consent` cookie → `window.__cactusConsent`, deny-by-default). Now uses `generateMetadata`/`generateViewport` (not a static `metadata` export) reading `resolveBranding()` (`lib/config/branding.ts`, React-`cache()`d) so the site's icons + app name + theme colour apply on EVERY route (fixing the default-cactus-favicon fallback); a custom favicon fully replaces the cactus svg/png/ico set (+ optional dark variant via `prefers-color-scheme`). The web-app manifest is generated dynamically by `app/manifest.ts` (`force-dynamic`, reads `resolveBranding`, served at `/manifest.webmanifest`); the old static `public/site.webmanifest` was removed.
- `app/not-found.tsx` - 404 page; renders the resolved `notFound` Layout via Puck if published, else a plain 404 card. `force-dynamic`.
- `app/robots.ts` - dynamic robots.txt; disallow-all when no site URL, `hideFromCrawlers`, or status ≠ live; else allow with disallows for `/cactus-admin/`, `/setup/`, `/cactus-status/`, `/api/`.
- `app/sitemap.ts` - site URL root plus all published InfoPage slugs, then `collectModuleSitemapEntries(siteUrl)` for every module shipping a `lib/sitemap.ts` (shop's products/categories/collections, shop-variations' one URL per buyable option combination, gazette, boards, directory, ultimate-seo's admin-managed extras).
- `app/api/branding/favicon/route.ts` - what `/favicon.ico` actually serves. `next.config.ts` `rewrites().beforeFiles` maps `/favicon.ico` here (ahead of the static handler, so no public-vs-route precedence question); resolves `resolveBranding()` and 307s to the admin-set favicon, else to `/cactus-favicon.ico` (the bundled Cactus default, moved out of `/favicon.ico` so this route can redirect to it without meeting itself). `Cache-Control: public, max-age=3600, stale-while-revalidate=86400`. Exists because the root layout's `<link rel="icon">` only reaches responses with a document head - `/sitemap.xml`, `/robots.txt` and any downloaded file fall back to the origin's `/favicon.ico`. `/api/branding/` is in `proxy.ts` `ALWAYS_PASS`.

Pages (status screens, reached only by proxy rewrite):

- `/cactus-status/coming-soon` - `statusPage` Layout (ctx `siteStatus: 'coming_soon'`) or fallback card. `force-dynamic`, noindex.
- `/cactus-status/maintenance` - same with `maintenance`; fallback "Down for maintenance" card.

Pages (setup):

- `/setup` - `app/setup/page.tsx` - client wizard, three steps: `connect` (Vercel token + project selection via `/api/setup/vercel-connect`), `database` (sub-states for Vercel bootstrap, Neon auto-provision, existing-project reuse, manual DATABASE_URL, local mode), `configure` (admin account + passkey or TOTP, admin path, site essentials, optional env vars, complete). Polls `/api/health` and `/api/setup/env-check` across the redeploys it triggers.
- `app/setup/layout.tsx` - `setup-shell` wrapper, noindex, absolute title.

Pages (member area, live under internal `/cactus-account/*`, reached only via the rewritten `/<memberAreaPath>/*` - Phases 1-3 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md):

- `/{memberAreaPath}/register` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/register/page.tsx` - server component: 404-styled message when `membersConfig.enabled` is false; in `INVITE_ONLY` mode, validates `?invite=` server-side and shows an "invite-only" message instead of the form when missing/invalid; otherwise renders `RegisterForm` with the resolved privacy-policy page link, the `collectUsername`/`collectDisplayName` flags and `passwordPolicy` (`authMethodPolicy(config,'PASSWORD')`) from `membersConfig` (the Puck `MembersRegister` block passes the same three; its editor preview keeps the defaults, as it already does for `registrationMode`). `RegisterForm` shows a password field whenever that policy is not `OFF`, marked required at `REQUIRED` - left the prop undefined it fetches `/api/members/auth/config` itself and treats a failed lookup as `OFF`, so the editor preview and any embedded copy show what the live page shows without being told. Also reads `?email=` and passes it as `initialEmail` (a starting value for the field only - still editable, still verified; shop's post-purchase account prompt links here with it so the customer signs up under the address their guest order was placed with).
- `/{memberAreaPath}/setup-signin` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/setup-signin/page.tsx` + `components/members/account/RequiredSignInSetup.tsx` - where the account layout's required-setup gate sends a member, and the only member-area page that gate lets through. Session-gated like the rest; redirects back to `/{memberAreaPath}` for anyone who bookmarks it with nothing outstanding. The client component works its own outstanding list out from live status (`GET /api/members/passkeys` + `GET /api/members/password`) rather than a server snapshot, so finishing one step updates the page without a reload: "add a passkey" (same WebAuthn calls as `SecuritySection`), "set a password", and - only once a password exists - a second step via `2fa/setup-options`+`setup-verify`, offering email codes when `isEmailConfigured()` and always the authenticator app (TOTP needs no delivery, so a site with no mail can still satisfy a required password). First-time recovery codes are shown before a manual "Continue to your account" button rather than an automatic bounce, since they are shown once. A "Sign out" escape hatch is offered throughout, for the member whose device cannot do what the site asks.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/verify-email` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/verify-email/page.tsx` - server component: reads `membersConfig` and passes `registerHref` (`/{memberAreaPath}/register`) to `VerifyEmailPanel` only when `enabled && registrationMode !== 'INVITE_ONLY'`, plus the always-present `accountHref` (`/{memberAreaPath}`); all behaviour lives in the panel.
- `components/members/VerifyEmailPanel.tsx` - client half of the above (wrapped in `Suspense` for `useSearchParams`); with a `?token=`, POSTs it (once - a `submitted` ref, since the effect depends on `router`/`accountHref` and a spent token answers "invalid or has expired"). On success it puts the wording (branching on the response: "Your email is verified and you are signed in. Welcome." when `signedIn`, the awaiting-approval variant on `PENDING_APPROVAL`, "You can now sign in." otherwise) into the session-storage flash and `router.replace(accountHref)`s, so the news arrives as a pill on the member area (or the sign-in page its gate hands them to) rather than as an inline alert on a page whose only remaining purpose is to be left; the panel keeps a muted "Taking you to your account…" line with a plain link, for a browser that doesn't move. Failures still render here, with the resend form. The resend half branches on `?email=`: a value matching a basic address shape is shown as text with a "Send it again" button (no input - the box implied a typo could be corrected here, which the resend endpoint cannot do), anything else (missing, or not address-shaped, so a crafted link can't print arbitrary wording under the site's name) falls back to the labelled email field. 60s client-side countdown mirrors the server throttle, and **starts at 60 on arrival whenever `?email=` is present**: a link was just sent, `canResendVerification()` refuses another within 60s of the last token, and it refuses in silence (it must - "too soon" is only knowable for an address genuinely awaiting verification), so a button offered immediately reported success and sent nothing. That was the whole of "I clicked resend and still got no email" on the live Deskwell site: seven POSTs to the resend route, one verification token, all clicks inside the throttle window. The post-send confirmation is worded to promise nothing about whether the address is registered, keeping the page as enumeration-safe as `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`. When `registerHref` is set, a "typed your address wrong? sign up again" link - the only actual fix for a mistyped sign-up.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/login` - `app/(public)/cactus-account/login/page.tsx` - server component reading `redirect`/`magic_token` straight from `searchParams` (no client `useSearchParams`, so no Suspense boundary needed); sanitises `redirect` via the shared `sanitizeRedirect` in `lib/auth/redirect.ts` (an earlier inline copy omitted the `/\` backslash guard, so `/\evil.com` normalised to `//evil.com` post-login) **with `/{memberAreaPath}` as the fallback, not `/`** - a magic-link email carries only `?magic_token=`, so the default fallback landed every link sign-in on the homepage. A sanitised target that is itself a signed-out member page (`isPublicMemberPath()`) is dropped for `/{memberAreaPath}` - signing in to land back on the sign-in page is a loop. Renders `LoginForm`.
- `components/members/RegisterForm.tsx` - client form: email/username/display name (email seeded from the optional `initialEmail` prop), privacy-policy consent checkbox, optional `TurnstileWidget`, submits to `POST /api/members/register`; redirects to `verify-email?email=…` when verification is required, else shows the final status inline (PENDING_APPROVAL vs ACTIVE copy). Optional `showHeading` (default true) drops its own `<h1>` for embedded uses, and optional `verifyEmailUrl` names the verify-email destination outright instead of deriving it from the current path - both used by shop's post-purchase prompt, which renders this form inside the order confirmation.
- `components/members/LoginForm.tsx` - client form, identifier-first: step one is the email field and a "Continue" button and nothing else; Continue POSTs `/api/members/auth/methods` and step two offers only what that address can use - passkey if they have one, "sign in with a password" if they have one, "email me a sign-in link" whenever the site allows it, with the first of those as the primary button and a "use a different email address" link back. A member with neither a password nor a passkey has nothing to choose between, so step two is skipped altogether: Continue sends the sign-in link itself (`handleMagicLink(address)`, address passed explicitly since `setEmail` has not landed) and goes straight to the "check your inbox" screen, which carries its own "use a different email address" link back. A failed lookup (network blip, non-200) falls back to every method `GET /api/members/auth/config` says the site allows, so a passkey holder is never left without the button. The email is trimmed once on Continue and shown read-only from then on (with `autoComplete="username"`, so password managers still match the saved credential). Auto-consumes a `?magic_token=` on mount; either path redirects to `verify-email` on a `redirectToVerify` rejection, else to the sanitised `redirectTo`.
