Optional `showHeading` (default true) drops its own `<h1>` for embedded uses, and optional `basePath` ("/account") makes its two internal detours - the `verify-email` redirect and the SMS-enrolment landing - absolute instead of relative to the current URL; both used by `SignInModal`, which floats this form over an arbitrary page where a relative `verify-email` would resolve against that page. The sign-in page passes neither, so its behaviour is byte-identical to before.
- `components/members/SignInWidgetClient.tsx` - client island behind the `MembersSignIn` Puck block. Owns the look (icon set, label, bordered/filled/plain box, colours, radius; resting/hover text colour ride custom properties `--ms-fg`/`--ms-fg-hover` consumed by `.member-signin-trigger` colour rules in `app/globals.css` - blank `hoverColour` falls back to `--color-primary`, the same hover token as the theme toggle and Icon Link, and a set `iconColour` pins the icon out of the hover exactly as ThemeToggle does), the click behaviour (anchor to `<memberArea>/login?redirect=…`, or a button that lazily imports `SignInModal`), and the signed-in variant (account link, optional sign-out `<form method="POST">` to `/api/members/auth/logout`, optional `MemberAvatar` in place of the icon). Hides itself on the sign-in page via `usePathname`, and resolves a blank `redirectTo` to the current path. Exports `SignInWidgetOptions`, `SignInWidgetState`, `SIGN_IN_WIDGET_DEFAULTS`. Session state and the `audience` gate are decided server-side (`MembersSignInRsc`), never here - this island is trivially inspectable, so it can't be a security boundary. Icon-only renders (blank `label`, or blank `signedInLabel` on the signed-in face - the shape a header uses) also emit the shared hover/focus tooltip: `className="member-signin-trigger"` on the anchor/button plus an `aria-hidden` `.member-signin-tip` span naming it ("Sign in" / "My account"), styled in `app/globals.css` to match `.theme-toggle-tip` but hanging below the icon. Skipped entirely when a text label is set, and the sign-out button never gets one.
- `components/members/SignInModal.tsx` - the sign-in panel `SignInWidgetClient` opens in modal mode. `createPortal` to `document.body` (a header is very often a positioned/overflow-clipped stacking context), `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, escape to close, tab trap, body scroll lock, focus to the close button on open, backdrop click closes. Hosts the real `LoginForm` (with `showHeading={false}` and `basePath`), plus an optional sign-up link. Reached only through `next/dynamic` `ssr:false` from the widget, so `LoginForm` and `@simplewebauthn/browser` stay out of the bundle of every page that merely shows a sign-in button.
- `components/members/TurnstileWidget.tsx` - loads the Cloudflare Turnstile script on demand and renders/tears down a widget instance; reads/writes `window.turnstile` via a local type cast rather than a global `Window` augmentation, because `modules/gazette`'s comment form already augments `Window.turnstile` with a narrower shape and TypeScript requires merged global augmentations to match exactly - core must not depend on or collide with an optional module's globals.
- `components/members/account/AccountFlash.tsx` + `lib/members/flash.ts` (`flash.test.ts`, jsdom) - one-shot message handed from one member-area page to the next and shown as a fixed pill at the top of the viewport (`.member-flash*`, `globals.css`, `z-index: 9990`, auto-dismissed after 9s, manual close, `role="status"`). Session storage rather than a query string because the account gate folds the URL it was given into `?redirect=`, so a flag on the URL arrives buried inside another parameter; taken (read then cleared) so a refresh doesn't replay it, validated and capped at 300 chars, every storage access in a try/catch for private-browsing setups. The take effect is keyed on `usePathname()`, not mount: the layout is shared by every member-area page, so verify-email → login leaves the component in the same slot and a mount-only effect would never look again. Only used by email verification so far.
- `/{memberAreaPath}` + 5 sections (`app/(public)/cactus-account/{layout.tsx,page.tsx,profile,security,notifications,activity,danger-zone}`) - session-gated (redirects to `login?redirect=…` otherwise); `layout.tsx` wraps **every** member-area page including `login`/`register`/`verify-email`, so its gate excepts those three via `isPublicMemberPath()` from `lib/members/paths.ts` and renders them bare (no nav, no banner) - without the exception the gate sent `/login` to `/login` and folded the whole previous URL into the next one's `?redirect=` on every hop, growing it exponentially until the browser refused to load it (the shop's post-purchase "Create an account" link into `/{memberAreaPath}/register?email=…` hit this). A missing `x-cactus-member-full-path` header falls through to the gate, which is one safe hop. A second gate sits below the session one: `memberOutstandingAuthSetup()` redirects to `/{memberAreaPath}/setup-signin` while any sign-in method the site marks `REQUIRED` is still unset, so "required" is enforced rather than suggested; it skips the redirect entirely when that header is absent, since a redirect on an unidentifiable path would point the setup page at itself (proxy.ts 404s direct `/cactus-account` hits, so the header is always there in practice), and the check short-circuits with no query at all when nothing is required. `layout.tsx` mounts `AccountFlash.tsx` on **both** sides of that gate - the pill it shows is usually the news that got the visitor bounced through it. `layout.tsx` also shows a cancellable deletion-grace banner and the `AccountNav.tsx` tab bar (reuses `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`), filtered by `membersConfig.accountSectionsEnabled`. Overview (`page.tsx`) is a dashboard, not a signpost: avatar + display name + email + "member since", an unverified-email nag with a resend button (`VerifyEmailNudge.tsx` -> `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend`), and four summary cards (Sign-in & security: passkey count / password set / 2FA on / active session count; Profile: which fields are still blank; Notifications; Recent activity: last 3 `MemberActivityEvent` rows) gathered in one `Promise.all`, each card filtered by the same `accountSectionsEnabled` flags as the tab bar. It also renders any `members.account-section` extension-point contributions (content-injection only, not a new nav tab). Two seams let a module live inside the account rather than beside it: **`members.account-nav`** (`lib/members/account-nav.ts`, `getMemberAccountNavExtras()`) collects `{key,label,href,badge?}` tabs from installed modules' manifests - a provider that throws is dropped rather than locking a member out of their own security settings - and **`components/members/account/MemberAccountShell.tsx`** is the chrome (container, flash, deletion banner, `notice` slot, tab bar) extracted out of `layout.tsx` so a module's own member pages, which are outside this route group and never see this layout, can wear the identical thing. `AccountNav.tsx` matches Overview exactly and every other tab by prefix, so a module's detail page (`/shop/account/orders/<id>`) still lights its tab. `ProfileSection.tsx` (avatar, displayName/bio/website, per-field visibility toggles - its page is the one section that also **enforces** its `accountSectionsEnabled` flag, `notFound()`ing when off rather than merely losing its tab, with the same gate on all four routes it saves through), `SecuritySection.tsx` (passkeys, password, 2FA incl. QR setup, sessions, trusted browsers, recovery codes - the single biggest client component), `NotificationsSection.tsx`, `ActivitySection.tsx`, `DangerZoneSection.tsx` (data export request/download/expiry via a blob-download helper - same pattern as `app/cactus-admin/account/page.tsx`'s `handleExport`, not a raw `<a href>`, deletion request/cancel).

Pages (public member profile, Phase 4 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md - fixed paths, no proxy rewrite involved):

- `/members/[username]` - `app/(public)/members/[username]/page.tsx` - see the Middleware/Authentication sections for the full visibility matrix; old-username redirect; `members.profile-section` extension point.
- `/members` - `app/(public)/members/page.tsx` - paginated directory (24/page), gated on `directoryEnabled`.
- `components/members/MemberAvatar.tsx`, `GeneratedAvatar.tsx` - see Media Layer section.

Pages (admin, live under internal `/cactus-admin/*`, reached only via the rewritten `/<adminPath>/*`):

- `/cactus-admin` - dashboard: page/user/media counts, site-status badge, optional-feature checklist (media, email, Turnstile, Edge Config, GitHub, Sentry) with links into Settings tabs. Below that, a generic grid renders any module's contributions to the `core.admin-dashboard-widgets` extension point (permission-filtered live from `Module.manifest.extensionPoints`, same pattern as the Settings → Users → Roles subtab's `core.roles-page` section) - currently Boards' `boardsDashboardWidget` (thread/post/open-queue counts, link into the module admin).
- `/cactus-admin/login` - server `page.tsx` wrapper (calls `resolveBranding()` and a `SiteConfig.designTokens` read, **both `.catch()`-guarded** - this is the page a locked-out or expired session lands on, so a passing DB failure must cost the site's colours, not the sign-in form; it was an unguarded `Promise.all` and produced a bare 500), passes `siteName`/`faviconUrl`/`faviconDarkUrl` down) + `LoginForm.tsx` ('use client', the whole former page): passkey (default, WebAuthn prompt fires automatically on page load unless a recovery token is in the URL; fallback options hidden behind "Use another way to sign in" until the auto attempt fails/is cancelled - a cancelled auto attempt (`NotAllowedError`) shows no error banner), password → email OTP (trust-device checkbox), authenticator (TOTP), recovery-token completion, no-passkey fallbacks (register new passkey or recovery email), lost-access instructions including Neon console link. Logo above "Sign in" shows the site's uploaded favicon (light/dark variant swap via `data-logo-variant`, same mechanism as the admin sidebar logo) falling back to the Cactus mark when the admin hasn't set one.
- `/cactus-admin/account` - profile (displayName), change email, passkeys add/remove, TOTP set-up/remove, password add/change (with sign-out-other-sessions), active sessions list/revoke, GDPR JSON export, self-delete account. Split into a server `page.tsx` wrapper + `AccountPageClient.tsx` ('use client', the whole former page): the wrapper resolves `admins.account-section` extension-point contributions (permission-filtered live from `Module.manifest`, same pattern as the dashboard's `core.admin-dashboard-widgets`) and passes them via an `extensionSections` prop, rendered between the "Your data" row and the Delete account card. First consumer: Twilio's `TwilioAdminSmsSection` (self-service SMS login-code enrolment).
- `/cactus-admin/pages` - InfoPage list with pagination, bulk select + delete (`PagesTable.tsx`); gated per `pages.write`/`pages.delete`.
- `/cactus-admin/pages/new` - title/slug form (+ optional menu assignment when `menus.manage`), creates a builder-format draft then opens the editor.
- `/cactus-admin/pages/[id]` - full-screen Puck editor (`PuckEditor.tsx`): content only saves on an explicit Update/Publish click (no background autosave - **changed 2026-07-08**, was 1.5s debounced), gated on `pages.publish`, preview link, delete. Unsaved edits trigger a `beforeunload` warning and a confirm on the in-app back link. Sidebar gained Settings/SEO/History/Saved Blocks tabs (see Puck Integration) - History tab lists live + up to 10 archived versions with restore into editor. Markdown pages are silently migrated to builder format on open.
- `/cactus-admin/menus` - menu list: create, rename, delete (with main-menu warning), item counts, a Created column + "empty" badge, a name filter (shown when >1 menu), **Set as main** (promote to header menu without leaving the page), and **Duplicate** (deep-clone the whole menu + items). Create/rename inputs take Escape-to-cancel; create is blocked client-side on a duplicate (case-insensitive) name.
- `/cactus-admin/menus/[id]` - menu item editor: add page/module-content/external items, edit label/url/new-tab, delete. Reordering: drag a row via its handle, or use ↑/↓ (siblings-only swap, keyboard/click-friendly, no native drag required). Per-row actions are Edit/Delete plus a "⋯" kebab: a **Who can see this** section (Everyone / Signed-in only / Signed-out only / Admins only → `PATCH item {visibility}`), add child item (pre-sets the parent; disabled past the 3-level depth cap), promote one level if nested, and a depth-aware "nest under" select. Non-PUBLIC items show an inline audience badge (Members/Guests/Admins only). A header summary line counts items · limited-visibility · needs-attention; **attention badges** flag a deleted page/entity (error) or a draft page / unpublished entity that's hidden from the live site (warning). Destination cell links out (PAGE → page editor, external/module → live URL, new tab). An item filter (matches label/destination, keeps whole matching branches; disables drag/reorder while active) and Collapse all / Expand all (per-parent chevrons) tame large menus. Add-item lightbox has a "Who can see this?" picker and Escape-to-close. Header shows a "Main menu" badge when this menu is the one assigned in Settings → General.
- `/cactus-admin/media` - media library with folders + tags (redesigned 2026-07-13: full restructure). **2026-08-10:** `MediaTabs.tsx` (Library | Video) now also carries a `moduleTabs` prop - whatever the installed modules publish into the `core.media-tabs` extension point, resolved server-side by `resolveExtensionTabs` (`lib/modules/extension-tabs.tsx`) and passed down as rendered nodes. Contributor today: gemini-watermark-remover ("Watermark remover"), which gave up its sidebar link for it. Server `page.tsx` loads the flat folder list (+ per-folder + root media counts), the tag list (+ counts), the root's first page (`queryMediaLibrary`), AND a whole-library overview (`computeLibraryStats`, `lib/media/library-stats.ts` - one pass over every row + the usage index: `totalFiles/totalSize/imageFiles/optimisedFiles/optimisableFiles/unusedFiles/unusedSize`), then hands off to `MediaLibrary.tsx` (client orchestrator). **Folder is in the URL (2026-07-28): `?folder=<folderId>`.** `page.tsx` reads it, verifies the id with a `prisma.folder.findUnique` (`root`/`all`/unknown → root) and renders that folder's first page instead of the root's; `MediaLibrary` seeds `currentFolderId` from the new `initialFolderId` prop (initial state, not a post-mount effect, so server and client open on the same folder and there's no root-then-refetch flash), and an effect mirrors every folder change back into the address with `window.history.replaceState` - replace, not push, so folder clicks don't stack up in the back button and no router navigation re-runs the server page. Refresh/bookmark/paste-a-link therefore lands in the folder you were in. **Perf (2026-07-26): `computeLibraryStats` is no longer awaited in the page's `Promise.all` - it was the one thing forcing a full-library scan + usage-index build before first paint, so an empty root still felt slow. The un-awaited promise is now passed to `MediaLibrary` as `statsPromise` and resolved client-side via React `use()` inside a `<Suspense fallback={<StatsBarSkeleton/>}>` (a four-tile placeholder in `MediaLibrary.tsx`), so the grid + folder tree paint at once and the tiles stream in. Paired with `queryMediaLibrary` now short-circuiting the usage-index build when a page has zero rows (`lib/media/library-query.ts`), the empty-root first paint no longer touches the page/layout builder JSON at all.** Layout top-to-bottom: page header (title + `MediaUpload`); `MediaStatsBar.tsx` (4 tiles - Files[+folder count], Storage used, Unused→click filters to unused, Optimisable→click filters to images; the two action tiles take a warning/info accent while there's work and drill into the WHOLE library via a `browseAll` flag); then a **resizable** split of `FolderTree.tsx` sidebar + content: a three-column grid `${folderPaneWidth}px 8px 1fr` whose middle column is `FolderPaneResizer.tsx` (new 2026-07-28) - a `role="separator"` drag handle (pointer events + pointer capture, so trackpad/pen/touch all work and the drag survives leaving the strip), arrow-key resize (±16px, ±48px with Shift), Home/End to the limits, Enter/Space or double-click to reset. Width is clamped 160-520px (default 220) and persisted to `localStorage['cactus.media.folderPaneWidth']`, hydrated in a post-mount effect like the view/sort prefs so the server render can't mismatch. `FolderTree` is unchanged behaviourally (recursive/expandable, path-to-current force-open, each row a nav button + `(count)` + drop target, folder rows draggable to move via `PATCH /api/admin/media/folders/[id]` `{parentId}` [self/descendant drops rejected by `isDescendant`], rows accept OS files dropped onto them when `media.upload`, hover rename/delete icons, "+ New folder") plus a new `browsingAll` prop that drops the active-row highlight while a search/tag/stat drill-down spans all folders. Content: breadcrumb (Media / … drop targets; shows "All folders" when spanning the tree), `MediaToolbar.tsx` (search-all box, sort/type/usage/tag selects, a grid|list **view toggle** persisted to `localStorage['cactus.media.view']`, and a removable **active-filter chip** strip + "Clear all"), a sticky selection/clipboard bar (Cut/Copy/Move to…/Optimise/Mark as optimised[flips to "Mark as not optimised" when every eligible selected item is already flagged]/Change ratio…/Resize…/Delete/Paste-here/Clear), then either a **grid** of `MediaCard.tsx` or a dense **list** `MediaList.tsx` (table: select-all header, thumb, sortable Name/Size/Uploaded headers wired to the sort state, Type, Folder, Usage pill; rows draggable + right-click + row-click-to-open). Nav/sort/filter/search/tag changes refetch `GET /api/admin/media` (first render reuses server items via a `firstRun` ref; `folderScope='all'` when search/tag/`browseAll`); further pages via an `IntersectionObserver` sentinel. Content pane + folder rows are OS-file drop targets (when `media.upload`) → `POST /api/admin/media`. Cards/rows are draggable (dragging a selected one drags the whole selection) onto any tree node/breadcrumb → `POST /api/admin/media/move`. Right-click opens `ContextMenu` (Open details / Optimise[raster unoptimised] / Mark as optimised|not optimised[raster+GLB, either state; acts on the whole selection when right-clicking inside one, but only on the items sharing the clicked item's flag] / Replace file…[library-accepted types] / Edit image…[raster] / Change ratio…[raster] / Resize…[raster] / Cut / Copy / Paste here / Rename… / Move to… / Tags…[opens the detail panel] / Delete); Cut/Copy fill a clipboard (cut items dimmed), Paste calls `/move` (cut) or `/duplicate` (copy). Opening a thumbnail/row opens **`MediaDetailPanel.tsx`** - a right-hand **slide-over** that replaced the old full-screen `MediaLightbox`: large preview (**3D models draw live from 2026-07-28** - `ModelPreview.tsx`, `next/dynamic` + `ssr:false` so three only loads once a model is opened: own `WebGLRenderer` + `OrbitControls` (damped, autoRotate until first pointer, no pan) + `RoomEnvironment` PMREM, model normalised to a 2-unit box and re-centred (scale MULTIPLIED, never assigned - FBX roots carry a unit conversion), loader chosen via `extensionForModelType` (GLB/glTF via `GLTFLoader` + `MeshoptDecoder` + `DRACOLoader` at `/draco/`, OBJ/FBX/3DS via their own loaders), bytes fetched by plain `fetch` in parallel with the loader chunks, everything disposed on unmount/step-to-next), In use/Optimised badges, metadata (type/size/folder/alt/uploaded), an **inline tag editor** (type-to-create + autocomplete, Save/Reset, `PUT /api/admin/media/[id]/tags`), Prev/Next with ArrowLeft/Right (ignored while typing), and an action footer (Open original / Optimise[raster unopt, `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/optimise`] / Mark as optimised|not optimised[raster+GLB, label follows `item.optimised`, `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-mark-optimised` with one id] / Replace file…[library-accepted types] / Edit image… / Change ratio… / Resize… / Rename… / Move… / Cut / Copy / Delete). Rename (`NameDialog`) / move (`MoveDialog`) / folder rename+delete (`NameDialog`/`DeleteFolderDialog`) / name-clash (`CollisionDialog` Keep both=suffix/Replace/Skip[move]/Cancel) dialogs are unchanged. Delete (single or bulk) always runs the in-use warning flow (`POST /bulk-delete` without force → still-referenced items return in `skipped`, dialog switches to "Delete anyway"). Edit image… opens `MediaImageEditor.tsx` (unchanged: crop box w/ 8 handles + rule-of-thirds + aspect presets Free/1:1/3:2/4:3/16:9/2:3/3:4/9:16 + custom W:H, "Save (replaces original)" [confirm] / "Save as new…" [filename], posts the source-pixel crop rect to `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/edit`). **Change ratio…** opens `MediaAspectDialog.tsx` (new 2026-07-16) - reshapes one image (detail panel / context menu) or the whole selection (selection bar) to a target ratio by **padding**, never cropping or stretching: ratio presets 1:1/3:2/4:3/16:9/2:3/3:4/9:16 + custom W:H, fill picker (Blurred image [default] / Colour [`<input type=color>` + White/Black shortcuts] / Transparent), a live CSS preview mirroring the server output (contain + pad; chequerboard for transparent), and Save-as-new [default] vs Replace-original [confirm step]. Transparent is disabled and derived away when any selected item is a JPEG (mirrors `supportsTransparentFill`). Bulk 'new' sends no `newName` (one name across many would collide) so the server suffixes each with the ratio. Posts to `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/aspect` (single) or `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-aspect` (bulk). **Resize…** opens `MediaResizeDialog.tsx` (new 2026-07-17) - aimed the same three ways (detail panel / context menu / selection bar), scales one image or the whole selection **down** to fit a box, keeping the ratio and never enlarging: longest-edge presets Extra large 2400 / Large 1600 / Medium 1000 / Small 600 (each sent as `{width: px, height: px}` so fit-inside caps the longest edge whichever way round the image is) + custom W/H (either side blank = unconstrained), a preview, and Save-as-new [default] vs Replace-original [confirm step]. `Media` has **no width/height columns**, so the dialog reads `naturalWidth`/`naturalHeight` off the loaded preview `<img>` purely to show "is 4000x3000, would become 1600x1200" and to disable the button when a single image already fits - the server measures the real bytes itself and is the authority. Bulk sends no `newName` (collision) so the server suffixes each with its own new size; the bulk toast reports `bytesSaved`. Posts to `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/resize` (single) or `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-resize` (bulk). `isReshapable` renamed `isRasterImage` in `MediaLibrary.tsx` (+ `reshapableSelected` → `rasterSelected`) - reshape and resize want the same predicate for the same reason. **All mutations report via toast notifications** (`MediaToasts.tsx`, bottom-right stack) instead of the old layout-shifting inline error/busy lines; a persistent "busy" toast shows while an op runs. Shared helpers: `format.ts` (bytes/date/filename/kind), `types.ts` (`LibraryItem`/`TagInfo`/`Sort`/`TypeFilter`/`UseFilter`/`ViewMode`/`SORTS`). In-use status computed via `lib/media/references.ts`. `MediaCard.tsx` slimmed (thumbnail, filename, kind·size, usage dot, ✓ Optimised badge, tag chips, hover-revealed select checkbox - no more per-card Optimise/Delete buttons). REMOVED: `MediaLightbox.tsx`, `MediaDelete.tsx` (single-delete UI folded into the bulk-delete in-use flow); `MediaGrid.tsx` was already gone. Below the library, `page.tsx` renders **`MediaStorageCheck.tsx`** (new 2026-07-19) when the viewer holds `config.manage` - an on-demand "Storage check" card (never part of the server render: it lists every object the providers hold) with a Run check button, then three groups (Leftover files / Files that have gone / Sizes recorded wrongly), each capped at 20 listed rows with an "…and N more". "Correct these" posts `correct-sizes`; "Delete all leftovers" (only when `media.delete`) confirms then posts `delete-orphans`; both re-scan afterwards rather than patching the list client-side.
- `/cactus-admin/appearance` - server redirect to `/appearance/styles`.
- `/cactus-admin/appearance/styles` - design-token editor (v2 tokens): tabs colours/typography/headings/buttons/images/formFields/spacing, colour presets, ~50 Google-font list, saves via `PATCH /api/admin/appearance`. Every colour field (global palette + all `themeStyle` colours: background, links, body, caption, display, h1-h6, buttons + hover, image border, form fields) offers an optional **dark-mode override**; `ColourInput` renders a light row plus a "Dark mode override (optional)" sub-row via the shared `ColourPickerRow` helper (native colour picker + palette swatches using each global colour's dark variant). Overrides persist as parallel `*Dark` keys on the design tokens; unset = reuse the light colour. Colour presets also seed dark-mode link colours (`ColourPreset.linkColourDark`/`linkHoverColourDark`), so applying one sets both light and dark links. Headings tab: a site-wide **Headings font (all headings)** `FontPickerField` at the top of the Headings section, stored as `themeStyle.headingsFont` (optional string; per-level `family` overrides it, empty inherits the body font) - `buildTokenStyles` merges it as the family fallback into every `h1`-`h6` (vars + `main hN` scoped rules) and Display, and `buildFontHref` loads it (incl. per-level weights on inheriting levels); the "Display (hero heading, largest - above H1)" section was REMOVED from the tab (its `setDisplay` helper too) - `themeStyle.display` tokens/emission stay honoured for existing rows and the Heading block's display level, there's just no UI editing them any more. Colours tab also has a **Status boxes** section: one accent colour per Callout type (info/success/warning/error, `STATUS_KEYS`) with optional dark override, stored as `themeStyle.status`; `buildTokenStyles` derives `--status-{key}` (accent), `--status-{key}-bg` (tint towards white in light / black in dark) and `--status-{key}-title` per mode via `statusVars()`. The Buttons and Form Fields tabs each end with a **sticky bottom live preview** (`StickyPreview` + `ButtonsPreview`/`FormFieldsPreview` in `page.tsx`): light and dark panes on the site's page-background colours, styles computed inline from the current unsaved token state (fallbacks mirror the ButtonLink block and contact-form field defaults), with the tokens' Google fonts loaded in-admin via a `buildFontHref` `<link>`. Buttons tab also has **Secondary variant**/**Outline variant** sections (`buttons.secondary`/`.outline`, each optional colour set + hover, `setButtonVariant`/`setButtonVariantHover` helpers) styling the ButtonLink block's other two options independently of Primary; `ButtonsPreview` renders all three. Colours tab has a **Badges** section (`themeStyle.badges`, `BADGE_COLOUR_KEYS` = blue/yellow/red/gray, each `{bg,text,+Dark}`, `setBadge` helper) plus a **Badge / pill corner radius** field (`themeStyle.pillRadius`, `setPillRadius`) shared by the Badge and Eyebrow blocks.
- `/cactus-admin/layouts` - layout cards filtered by type tab (all/header/footer/infoPage/notFound/statusPage/emailWrapper + one per module group), each with a `LayoutPreview` thumbnail, display-condition summary, and Edit/Preview/Duplicate/Delete. Every layout is editable and deletable (no starter rows, no read-only cards). "+ New Layout" carries the active tab's type through as `?type=`. Name/description **search box** with an `n of m` count in the `TabStrip` trailing slot; tab switches are guarded by a request token so a slow earlier fetch cannot land under a later tab. Status badge reads the conditions, not just the column: **Live** (published with ≥1 complete include rule), **Not shown** (published but no rule that matches anything - it renders nowhere), **Draft**. Delete uses an in-app dialog that says out loud when the layout it is about to remove is live on the site (the old `window.confirm` could not).
- `/cactus-admin/layouts/new` - the starter picker. One tabbed page (shared `TabStrip` + `lib/layout/layout-type-tabs.ts`, second-level tabs for a module group's sub-types), a card per starter template with a `LayoutPreview` drawing of its structure. Clicking a card `POST`s the template's `data` to `/api/admin/layouts` and routes straight into the builder - no naming step, the layout takes the template's name and is renamed in the editor's Settings tab. Templates come from `getStarterTemplates(type)` (in-code, imported directly - no fetch). Replaces the old 3-step wizard (type → sub-type → name + starter radio list). **Module group tabs (and so their templates) appear only if the site has that module installed** - see the module-layout-types entry under Puck Integration.
- **`emailWrapper` layout type (2026-08-03)** - the design wrapped around every email the site sends. Own Puck config (`lib/puck/email-config.tsx`, selected in `LayoutPuckEditor`'s `getConfig`), own block set, and none of the site blocks: classes and `var(--…)` reach an inbox as unstyled text, so reusing them would look right in the editor and broken in the email. Blocks are `EmailBodySlot` (where the message lands - appended automatically if a wrapper is built without one), `EmailLogo`, `EmailHeading`, `EmailText`, `EmailButton`, `EmailImage`, `EmailTwoColumn`, `EmailDivider`, `EmailSpacer`, `EmailSocialRow`, `EmailFooterText`; root props cover preview line, page/card background, card border, width, corner rounding, outer padding and font. Each block is a single `toHtml(props, ctx)` in `lib/email/blocks.ts` emitting inline-styled `role="presentation"` tables, and the Puck render is `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` of that exact string - editor and inbox cannot drift. Colour fields hold a design-token id (resolved to its light-mode hex at send time via `lib/email/palette.ts`), a literal hex, or blank for the block's own fallback. `href`/`src` are filtered to http(s)/mailto/tel/relative, so a `javascript:` link is dropped rather than rendered. **No Conditions tab** in its editor - which email uses which wrapper is set per email on Settings > Email > Templates, not by a URL rule; `defaultConditionsForLayout('emailWrapper')` returns `entire_site` so it can still be published. The site default wrapper is the highest-priority published one. `/layout-preview/[id]` renders an `emailWrapper` through `wrapEmailHtml` in a sandboxed iframe rather than through a Puck RSC config, since it has none. `EmailLogo`/`EmailImage` `src` fields are wired into `IMAGE_PICKER_FIELDS` so they get the media picker.
- `/cactus-admin/layouts/[id]` - layout Puck editor (`LayoutPuckEditor.tsx`, 1.2s debounced autosave). Sidebar gained Settings/Conditions/History/Saved Blocks tabs (see Puck Integration) - Conditions tab is `DisplayConditionsPanel` (include/exclude rules; publish requires ≥1 **complete** include rule - Save is disabled while any rule still has a blank value, and `module` rules finally get a text input, having previously been unfillable), History tab lists live + up to 10 archived versions with restore into editor (restore asks before it fetches, and a published layout's restore re-publishes so the replaced version is archived rather than lost).
- `/cactus-admin/inbox` - **new 2026-08-10.** A host with nothing of its own: it renders whichever tabs the installed modules publish into the `core.inbox-tabs` extension point (`app/cactus-admin/inbox/page.tsx` + `lib/modules/extension-tabs.tsx`'s `resolveExtensionTabs`), each already gated by its own module's permission. Which tab is open lives in `?tab=<entry id>` rather than client state, because the panels are server components that read their own query params (the contact inbox filters with `?status=` and pages with `?page=`) - client-side switching would leave those params describing a panel no longer on screen; an unknown `?tab=` falls back to the first. Contributors today: contact-form (`Contact form`, order 10) and live-chat (`Live chat`, order 20). Nothing installed → a plain "nothing is using the inbox yet" note, and the sidebar hides the link entirely (see Admin UI).
- `/cactus-admin/users` - unified People table (`PeopleListClient.tsx`, self-fetching `GET /api/admin/people`): staff (User) and site members (Member) in one search+paginate list, a type badge distinguishing them, and a Role-or-status column; staff rows keep the role select / suspend / delete actions (`UserActions.tsx`, non-admins cannot act on protected-role users), member rows link out to `/cactus-admin/members/[id]` for the full suspend/trust/approve/delete action set (bulk multi-select on members was dropped in the merge - use the per-member page, or the still-present but now UI-unlinked `GET/POST /api/admin/members/bulk`).
- `/cactus-admin/modules` - module directory (org `cactus-foundation-modules`), install with public/beta channel choice, update / enable / disable / uninstall (code-only or code+data teardown), per-module update channel, release-notes modal, stale-`deploying` reconciliation, "Update all" button (shown when ≥1 module has an update pending) batching all pending module updates into a single deploy. Since 2026-08-13 (working tree) also an **"Add a custom module"** panel - URL box + channel toggle posting into the same `handleInstall`/`POST /api/admin/modules` path, server-side error messages surfaced verbatim (they are the entire diagnostic story for a custom install), with a plain trust warning that a pasted-URL module runs inside the site's own runtime. **Rebuilt as a store front 2026-08-21 (working tree):** four `TabStrip` tabs - Installed / Updates available / Browse / Add your own, count pills, and a name+description search box in the strip's `trailing` slot. Landing tab is derived (`tab ?? (installed.length ? 'installed' : 'browse')`), not an effect. Cards are `.module-card` (new `MODULE STORE` block in `app/globals.css`): a 16:9 artwork plate, name + status badge, 3-line clamped description, version/channel/update badges, and a single primary button. Everything else moved into a per-card `…` menu (`app/cactus-admin/modules/CardMenu.tsx` - outside-click + Escape): check for updates, turn on/off, view the code, **Which releases** (public/beta, ticked), uninstall. Artwork is `app/cactus-admin/modules/ModuleArt.tsx` → `public/module-art/<repo-slug>.webp`, 1200×675, opaque; it tries the repo slug then the manifest name before falling back to an initial, because `repoName` is the GitHub slug for directory rows and the manifest name for installed-only rows (`live-chat` vs `live-chat-powered-by-chatwoot`, `contact-form-reply-catcher` vs `reply-catcher`). The plate's gradient uses raw `--cactus-700/--cactus-900` rather than semantic tokens **on purpose**: one artwork file serves both themes, so the plate behind it must not follow the theme. "Update all" and "Check for updates" moved to the page header. Every handler, modal and API call is unchanged - this was a presentation change only.
- `/cactus-admin/notifications` - notification list with per-type icon, reasons list, read/unread toggle, delete, "Redeploy now" for open deployment notifications (`NotificationActions.tsx`), plus header-level "Mark all as read" / "Delete all" (`NotificationBulkActions.tsx`, hidden when the table is empty; Mark-all disabled at zero unread, Delete-all disabled when `total - pendingDeploy` is zero; the delete confirm names that deletable count, which can still exceed the hundred rows rendered, and says pending changes are kept).
- `/cactus-admin/config` - Settings, 8 core tabs + module-registered tabs (see Admin UI section). Server component fetches active modules' `manifest.settingsTabs`, permission-filters, passes to client `ConfigPageClient`.
- `/cactus-admin/config/privacy-generator` - 6-step privacy-policy wizard; assembles markdown from `lib/privacy/template.ts` and creates a draft InfoPage, optionally linking it as the privacy policy page.
- `/cactus-admin/m/[module]/[...path]` - generic module page host; delegates to `resolveModulePage` in generated `lib/modules/router.ts`.
- `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx` - admin shell: reads `x-cactus-admin-path` / `x-cactus-is-login` headers, secondary session check, module nav entries from `Module.manifest.navEntries` (permission-filtered), unread notification count, admin white-labelling (primary colour family + sans font only). Nav entries are grouped: a module with no `manifest.navGroupLabel` renders as plain links directly under Dashboard, no section heading (currently just contact-form's Inbox); a module that sets `navGroupLabel` (Gazette `"Gazette"`, Boards `"Boards"`) gets its own `admin-nav-section-label` heading with just its own links, rendered after the System section - both via `AdminShell`/`AdminNav`'s `moduleNavGroups` prop (`Array<{label: string|null, links}>`), split in `AdminNav.tsx` into `ungroupedModuleLinks` (flattened, no header) vs `labelledModuleGroups` (own collapsible section).

API route handlers (core):

- `GET /api/health` - `SELECT 1` liveness check; `{status, database: connected|disconnected}`.
- `GET/POST /api/consent` - GDPR consent record append (action, decision map validated against configured categories, truncated IP, SHA-256 UA hash; sets 2-year `cactus-consent-id` httpOnly cookie); GET returns the latest decision for the cookie's consentId.
- `POST /api/webhooks/vercel` - HMAC-SHA1 signature check against `VERCEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET`; on `deployment.succeeded` for the tracked deployment: promotes `deploying` modules, releases DeployLock, clears the redeploy gate; on error/canceled: rolls modules back and resolves the `'pending'` sentinel to the real deployment id.
- `GET|POST|PATCH|DELETE /api/m/[module]/[...path]` - generic module API dispatcher via generated `lib/modules/router.ts`; `force-dynamic`, `maxDuration = 60`.

Auth API:

- `GET /api/auth/config` - public: `emailConfigured`, `turnstileConfigured`, `turnstileSiteKey`. **`neonProjectId` was removed (2026-07-23)** - this payload is served before anyone authenticates, and the project id is infrastructure metadata that nothing on the login screen actually needs; `LoginForm.tsx` no longer reads it and its lost-passkey help now links to the plain `https://console.neon.tech` rather than a project deep link.
- `POST /api/auth/login` - password step of password+OTP login; 503 when email unconfigured; Turnstile; rate limit (`login`, ip+account_email); constant-time-ish hash compare; sends 6-digit `login_otp` EmailChallenge; returns `{step:'otp', userId}`.
- `POST /api/auth/email-code` - verifies the OTP (skipped when trusted-device cookie valid); creates session; optional trusted-device cookie for `trustDeviceDays`. Rejects a suspended account (`suspendedAt`) before minting the session, matching the password/TOTP/passkey mint sites.
- `POST /api/auth/logout` - deletes session, clears cookie, redirects `/logged-out`.
- `POST /api/auth/passkey/authenticate-options` - rate limited; if the given email's account has zero passkeys returns `{noPasskeys: true}` and **no userId** (handing an internal id to an unauthenticated caller was step 1 of an account takeover); else WebAuthn authentication options (challenge stored in `WebAuthnChallenge`, 5 min TTL). User verification is `required`.
- `POST /api/auth/passkey/authenticate-verify` - verifies assertion (challenge extracted from `clientDataJSON`), suspended check, creates session, updates passkey counter. `requireUserVerification: true`.
- `POST /api/auth/passkey/register-options` - Origin must match SITE_URL (rpId guard); a body `userId` is honoured **only while the setup bootstrap window is open** (`isSetupBootstrapOpen`, `lib/auth/setup-window.ts`), otherwise the target is taken from the session and the body value ignored; excludeCredentials from existing passkeys; stable WebAuthn user handle encoded from userId.
- `POST /api/auth/passkey/register-verify` - session required outside the setup window; target userId comes from the stored challenge (not spoofable from the body) and must equal the signed-in user, else 403; labels the passkey from the user agent.
- `POST /api/auth/passkey/register-login` - **DELETED** (security). It registered a passkey and minted a session for any account with zero passkeys, using nothing but a body `userId` as the identity claim - a full takeover of any staff account that had never enrolled one. A passkey is now only ever added to an already-authenticated session (or during first-run setup); the login page offers password / authenticator / recovery link instead.
- `POST /api/auth/totp/setup-options` - generates a TOTP secret (base32, 20 bytes), otpauth URI and QR data URL; secret stored encrypted (AES-256-GCM via `ENCRYPTION_KEY`), unverified; body userId trusted only pre-setup.
- `POST /api/auth/totp/setup-verify` - verifies the first code (window ±1, replay-guarded via `totpLastStep`), sets `totpVerifiedAt`; setup-wizard mode also creates the session.
- `POST /api/auth/totp/verify` - email+code login; single generic error to prevent account enumeration; rate limited; creates session.
- `POST /api/auth/recovery/request` - always returns 200 (no enumeration); Turnstile; rate limited; emails a recovery link (`/api/auth/recovery/complete?token=…`, 30 min TTL) plus a "recovery requested" notification.
- `GET /api/auth/recovery/complete` - validates the token then redirects to `/<adminPath>/login?recovery_token=…`.
- `POST /api/auth/recovery/complete` - validates the optional new password FIRST and only then consumes the token (a rejected password no longer burns the link), invalidates all sessions and trusted devices, creates a fresh session, sends a completion notification email.

Members API (Phase 1 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md - registration/verification only; no member session system yet, so nothing here requires or issues a member auth cookie):

- `POST /api/members/register` - 403 when `membersConfig.enabled` is false; Turnstile; rate limit `member_register` (5/60min per IP, `lib/auth/rate-limit.ts`); `INVITE_ONLY` mode requires and validates+consumes a `MemberInvite` token; email domain allow/blocklist (`isEmailDomainAllowed`); username format/blocklist/uniqueness (only when `registrationCollectUsername` is on - off, any supplied `username` is ignored and `generateUsernameFromEmail()` makes one after the email is known to be new; `registrationCollectDisplayName` off likewise drops any supplied `displayName`); an optional `password`, accepted only when `authMethodPolicies.PASSWORD` is `OPTIONAL`/`REQUIRED` (ignored when `OFF`) and demanded when `REQUIRED` - strength-checked and hashed *before* the existing-email branch below, since rejecting a weak password only on the fresh path would leak the difference that branch exists to hide, then written as a nested `MemberPassword` create; email uniqueness (409); creates the `Member` row (status `PENDING_VERIFICATION` when verification is required and email is configured, else immediately `ACTIVE`/`PENDING_APPROVAL` per `registrationMode` - see `deriveInitialStatus`/`deriveActivatedStatus` in `lib/members/registration.ts`); writes a `MemberConsentRecord` (`privacy_policy`); sends a plain (non-templated - Phase 6 adds `EmailTemplate`) verification email via `sendVerificationEmail`. A send failure is caught, logged and returned as `verificationEmailSent: false` alongside `status`/`verifyEmailRequired` - never thrown, since the member row already exists and a 500 here left an unusable account plus a browser parse error in place of a message.
- `POST /api/members/verify-email` - consumes a `MemberVerificationToken` (24h TTL, single-use, `lib/members/tokens.ts`); on success moves the member from `PENDING_VERIFICATION` to `PENDING_APPROVAL` or `ACTIVE` per `registrationMode`, **then signs them in** where the resulting status allows it: `createMemberSession` + `setMemberSessionCookie` + a `login` activity event with `metadata.method = 'EMAIL_VERIFICATION'`, gated on `loginRejectionForStatus(member.status)` returning null exactly as every other sign-in route is, so `PENDING_APPROVAL`/`SUSPENDED`/`DELETED` still get no session. Safe because a verification token can only ever belong to a `PENDING_VERIFICATION` member (the register route and the resend route are the only issuers, and resend refuses every other status), so this can never step past a second factor. Response is `{status, signedIn}`.
- `POST /api/members/verify-email/resend` - enumeration-safe: always `{ok:true}` regardless of whether the email exists, is already verified, or is throttled; resends only when the member is `PENDING_VERIFICATION` and the 60-second per-member throttle (`canResendVerification`) has elapsed.
- `POST /api/members/auth/methods` - public, `{email}` in, `{passkey, password, magicLink}` out; the identifier step of the sign-in form. Intersects what the account has (`MemberPassword` row, ≥1 `MemberPasskey`) with what the site allows (`authMethodPolicies` via `isAuthMethodEnabled`, plus `isEmailConfigured()` for the link). Rate limited `member_auth_methods` (30/15min per IP). A rate-limited caller, an unparseable body or an unknown address all get the same link-only answer a member with nothing set up gets, so "no account" and "account that only ever used sign-in links" - the state every account starts in - are indistinguishable; members who have since added a password or passkey are not. Member status is deliberately not consulted: each method's own route gates on it and returns the real reason ("verify your email first"), which beats hiding a passkey the member knows they have.
- `POST /api/members/auth/passkey/authenticate-options` - rate limited (shared `passkey_authenticate` bucket with admin); always returns a generic unscoped challenge (empty `allowCredentials`, discoverable-credential flow), byte-identical whether or not the email maps to a member or that member has a passkey, so the shape never reveals account existence/status. Members have no bootstrap-without-a-session path - see the `lib/members/passkey.ts` note.
- `POST /api/members/auth/passkey/authenticate-verify` - verifies the assertion, rejects via `loginRejectionForStatus` for any non-ACTIVE member, else creates a `MemberSession` + sets the `cactus_member_session` cookie.
- `POST /api/members/auth/passkey/register-options`, `POST /api/members/auth/passkey/register-verify` - add a passkey to the *signed-in* member (`getMemberFromCookie`, 401 without a session); register-verify cross-checks the challenge's stored `memberId` against the session's member before saving.
- `POST /api/members/auth/magic-link/request` - enumeration-safe (always `{ok:true}`); rate limited (`member_magic_link`, 5/15min/IP); sends whenever the member exists, regardless of status (status is gated at consume time, not here); no-ops when magic-link isn't enabled/allowed.
- `POST /api/members/auth/magic-link/consume` - single-use, 15-min TTL; `loginRejectionForStatus` gate; creates the `MemberSession` + cookie on success.
- `POST /api/members/auth/password/login` - password step (requires `authMethodPolicies.PASSWORD` ≠ `OFF`); skips 2FA when the browser is trusted; else `{step:'2fa', method}`; 403 if 2FA is mandatory but not yet configured for that member. Trusted-browser `done` responses also carry `smsEnrolmentRequired` (see `lib/members/sms-policy.ts`) so the login form can land the member on the account overview's enrolment card.
- `POST /api/members/auth/2fa/verify` - second factor (EMAIL code or TOTP, whichever the member has), optional `trustBrowser`; creates the session; success response carries `smsEnrolmentRequired` (same contract as the login route).
- `POST /api/members/auth/recovery-code/consume` - one-time code as a 2FA fallback; creates the session.
- `GET /api/members/auth/admin-continue` - signs a *staff* session into the member area as itself: `getSessionFromCookie` → `findOrCreateMemberForUser` (`lib/members/admin-link.ts`) → `MemberSession` + `cactus_member_session` on the redirect response, then `?redirect=` (sanitised, defaults to the member area root). GET because the account layout redirects here. Every failure path lands on `/{memberAreaPath}/login?admin_link=failed|unavailable` rather than looping. Sets `cactus_member_admin_attempt` (60s) as the loop breaker and clears `cactus_member_admin_optout`.
- `POST /api/members/auth/logout` - clears the session + cookie, redirects `/logged-out`; sets `cactus_member_admin_optout` when the member is admin-linked (or when there is no member session but a live staff one), so the account layout stops signing the admin straight back in.
- `POST /api/members/auth/logout-all` - session-gated; deletes every `MemberSession` for the member (including the caller's own - forces full re-auth); same opt-out cookie for an admin-linked member.
- `GET /api/members/auth/config` - public: `authMethodPolicies` (the per-method `OFF`/`OPTIONAL`/`REQUIRED` map, read by the registration form to decide whether to ask for a password), `enabledAuthMethods` (the flat list of what is switched on at all, read by the sign-in form), `turnstileSiteKey`.

Member account API (Phase 3 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md; every route below requires a member session via `getMemberFromCookie`, 401 otherwise):

- `GET/PATCH /api/members/contact` - `Member.fullName`, the real-world name an order is made out to. GET returns `{email, fullName}`; PATCH takes `{fullName}` (trimmed, max 120, empty string clears it). Deliberately NOT part of the profile route below and NOT gated on `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` or `registrationCollectDisplayName`: a checkout-only members system turns both of those off and still needs a name. Read by shop's `CheckoutContactClient` to fill the checkout's name box for a signed-in shopper (401 for a guest, which fills nothing).
- `GET/PATCH /api/members/profile` - displayName/bio/websiteUrl. Username is read-only here (change-with-cooldown is Phase 4). GET also returns `usernameEnabled`/`displayNameEnabled`/`usernameChangesEnabled` (mirrors of `registrationCollectUsername`/`registrationCollectDisplayName`/`usernameChangesEnabled`) so the client `ProfileSection.tsx` can hide the boxes for fields the site never asks for, and the change form when changes are off (default) since `POST /api/members/username` 403s; PATCH drops a supplied `displayName` when `registrationCollectDisplayName` is off, the same "a hidden field is not a field" treatment as the register route. PATCH also 403s outright (`profileSectionOffResponse()`) when `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` is off - rejected rather than dropped, since with the whole section gone there is no form the request could have come from. GET is not gated: it returns the member's own data and nothing else.
- `POST/PATCH/DELETE /api/members/avatar` - upload (gated on `avatarUploadsEnabled` + media provider configured; replaces and deletes any previous uploaded avatar) / choose which of the three sources to show (`{ avatarChoice }`, re-checked against `gravatarEnabled` and `avatarUploadsEnabled` + a stored `avatarMediaId`, so a crafted PATCH cannot park a member on a source the site has switched off) / remove the stored file (keyed on `avatarMediaId`, not on the active choice, so an upload kept behind a Gravatar is still deleted; only an `avatarChoice` of UPLOAD is then reassigned, to GRAVATAR or GENERATED per `gravatarEnabled`, and the resulting choice is returned in the response). All three are also gated on `accountSectionsEnabled.profile`, since the picture controls exist only on that page; on DELETE the check runs **before** the media is deleted.
- `GET/POST/PUT /api/members/email` - the member's own sign-in address, changed in two steps. GET returns `email`/`emailVerified`/`canChange`/`reason`/`requiresPassword`/`pendingEmail` (the address an unexpired challenge is waiting on, so a reload lands back on the code box). POST parks the requested address on a `MemberEmailChallenge` row with purpose `email_change` and emails a code **to that address**, leaving `Member.email` alone; PUT applies it only once the code comes back. Guards, in order: `accountSectionsEnabled.security`, an admin-linked member (`Member.userId` set - their address belongs to the staff User row, so it is changed on the admin account page), `isEmailConfigured()` (no sender = no code = no honest way to confirm), `email_change` rate limit, current password when a `MemberPassword` exists, not-already-yours, `isEmailDomainAllowed` (the same allow/block lists registration uses) and a case-insensitive clash check against every other `Member` - re-run on PUT, since the ten minutes the code is valid is long enough for another account to take the address. On success: `email` + `emailVerified`/`emailVerifiedAt` (verified by definition - the code only reaches whoever can read that mailbox), a `member.email-change-notice` to the **old** address at request time and a `member.security-alert` to it again on completion, and an `email_changed` activity event carrying `{from, to}`. Mirrors the staff-side `app/api/account/email/route.ts` deliberately, including why: applying a change before the new address is proved moves every future sign-in link and recovery code to a mailbox that may not exist.
- `GET/DELETE /api/members/sessions`, `DELETE /api/members/sessions/[id]` - list (current flagged via `isCurrent`) / revoke-all-but-current / revoke one.
- `GET /api/members/passkeys`, `DELETE /api/members/passkeys/[id]` - list / remove, with two guards on the last passkey: refused outright when `authMethodPolicies.PASSKEY` is `REQUIRED` (the setup gate would only ask for it straight back), and otherwise refused unless `MAGIC_LINK` is enabled or a password exists (members always have magic link as a fallback if it's enabled, unlike admin whose only fallback is a password).
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/members/password` - status (`hasPassword`, `hasTwoFactor`, `passwordsEnabled`, `passwordRequired`) / add-or-change (`signOutOtherSessions` option) / remove. DELETE is refused while `authMethodPolicies.PASSWORD` is `REQUIRED`, same reasoning as the last-passkey guard.
- `GET/DELETE /api/members/2fa` - status / remove (refused with a clear error while a password still exists, since 2FA is mandatory whenever one is set).
- `POST /api/members/2fa/setup-options` - EMAIL sends a code; AUTHENTICATOR_APP returns a QR + secret (stored unverified).
- `POST /api/members/2fa/setup-verify` - verifies either method; a member has one active method at a time (setting a new one deletes the other); auto-generates and returns recovery codes once, only on the member's *first* successful 2FA setup ever.
- `GET/DELETE /api/members/trusted-browsers`, `DELETE .../[id]` - list (current flagged) / revoke-all / revoke one.
- `GET/POST /api/members/recovery-codes` - remaining count / regenerate (requires 2FA already configured; shown once).
- `GET/PATCH /api/members/notifications` - categories are entirely module-contributed (`getModuleNotificationCategories`) - core has none of its own yet. Two channels since 2026-08-16: GET answers `{smsAvailable, categories:[{category,label,required,emailOffered,smsOffered,email,sms,digestMode}]}`; PATCH takes `channel` ('EMAIL' default) and refuses to disable the last enabled channel of a `required` category, refuses SMS on a category that does not offer it, and 503s enabling SMS with no provider configured. Defaults live in `lib/members/notification-prefs.ts` (email on, SMS off).
- `GET /api/members/activity` - last 50 `MemberActivityEvent` rows.
- `GET/POST /api/members/data-export`, `GET /api/members/data-export/download` - GET returns the latest request's status; POST runs the whole assemble→upload→ready flow synchronously within the request (`maxDuration = 60`, same "no background job system" constraint the Gazette/Boards importers already accept) and refuses a second request while one is `PENDING`/`PROCESSING`; download streams the stored JSON back through this authenticated route rather than ever handing the browser the underlying (if unguessable) storage URL, since this file contains personal data unlike ordinary public media.
- `POST /api/members/delete-account`, `POST /api/members/cancel-deletion` - sets/clears `deletionRequestedAt`/`deletionScheduledAt` (grace period from `membersConfig.deletionGracePeriodDays`).
- `GET/PATCH /api/members/profile-visibility` - per-field public-profile show/hide (`showBio`/`showJoinDate`/`showWebsite`). PATCH is gated on `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` (the switches live on that page); the site-wide `profileVisibility` setting is a separate admin control and is unaffected.
- `POST /api/members/username` - Phase 4; requires `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` (checked first - the change form is on that page and nowhere else) then `usernameChangesEnabled`; `usernameChangeCooldownDays` off `usernameChangedAt`; stamps `previousUsername`/`previousUsernameExpiresAt` (`usernameRedirectDays`) so `/members/[username]` can redirect old links.
- `GET /api/members/avatar-proxy/[id]` - public, no session required; Phase 4 - see Media Layer section.

Member cron routes (`Authorization: Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, same pattern as module crons):

- `GET /api/cron/members/purge` - hard-deletes every member whose `deletionScheduledAt` has passed (cascades take every child row per the schema).
- `GET /api/cron/members/exports` - expires every `READY` data-export request past its 48h `expiresAt`, deleting the underlying media file.
- `GET /api/cron/members/digest?mode=daily|weekly` - see the Email section for what a digest actually batches.

Account API (all require session):

- `DELETE /api/account` - self-deletion in a transaction; blocked when it would leave zero active admins; InfoPage/Media/ConsentRecord ownership nulled.
- `GET/PATCH /api/account/profile` - email/username/displayName; PATCH displayName (max 128).
- `POST /api/account/email` - change email; requires current password when one is set; 409 on conflict.
- `GET/POST /api/account/password` - status (`hasPassword`, `emailConfigured`); add/change password (refused when email unconfigured; breached-password check; optional sign-out-other-sessions preserving the current one by token hash).
- `GET /api/account/passkeys`, `DELETE /api/account/passkeys/[id]` - list; deletion of the last passkey blocked unless a password exists.
- `GET/DELETE /api/account/sessions`, `DELETE /api/account/sessions/[id]` - list (current session flagged), revoke all, revoke one.
- `GET/DELETE /api/account/totp` - enabled status; removal blocked when TOTP is the only sign-in method.
- `GET /api/account/export` - GDPR Art. 20 JSON download: profile, role, passkey metadata (no key material), active sessions, consent records.

Admin API:

- `GET/PATCH /api/admin/config` - `config.manage`. GET returns the full SiteConfig row plus derived branding preview URLs `logoUrl`/`logoDarkUrl`/`faviconUrl`/`faviconDarkUrl`/`appIconUrl`/`appleTouchUrl`/`icon192Url`/`icon512Url` (media rows resolved via a shared `lookup` helper for the Branding tab). PATCH validates every field with zod (incl. all branding media ids `logoMediaId`/`logoDarkMediaId`/`faviconMediaId`/`faviconDarkMediaId`/`appIconMediaId`/`appleTouchIconMediaId`/`webManifest192MediaId`/`webManifest512MediaId` nullable, plus `appName`/`appShortName`/`themeColor`/`backgroundColor` text); adminPath blocklist; consent-banner "necessary" category enforced, `categoriesVersion`/`copyVersion` auto-bumped on meaningful changes; Edge Config sync for adminPath/status; a mediaProvider change returns a per-provider Media breakdown.
- `GET/PATCH /api/admin/appearance` - GET requires a valid session (public layout reads design tokens directly via Prisma, not this endpoint - only admin editors call it); PATCH requires `appearance.manage` and accepts only null or a `version: 2` token object.
- `GET/POST /api/admin/appearance/presets` and `PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/appearance/presets/[id]` - user-created colour presets (`UserColourPreset` model). GET requires a session; POST/PATCH/DELETE require `appearance.manage`. POST rejects a name that case-insensitively clashes with another user preset or a default `COLOUR_PRESETS` name (409). The Styles > Colours preset bar renders these rows first, then the hardcoded defaults; each user preset card gets a delete (✕) affordance the defaults don't have. The Save/Update button above the bar reads "Update preset" (PATCH, confirm-gated) when the current colours exactly match an existing user preset, else "Save as preset" (POST, opens a name-entry modal) - it never offers to overwrite a default preset.
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/admin/env` - protected-role only; `maxDuration 60`. GET: boolean set/unset per allowlisted key (Vercel API, or `process.env` read-only in local mode). POST: upserts allowlisted vars to Vercel env, records a deployment-needed notification. Keys that were filled in but are not managed are **reported, not dropped in silence**: they come back in a `skipped: string[]` alongside `written`, and a request where every filled-in key is unmanaged is a `400` naming them (a "Saved" over a write that never happened is how a credential ends up looking set when it is not; a request carrying only blank values still returns `{ ok: true, written: 0 }` as before). The allowlist is `ALLOWED_KEYS` plus every installed module's manifest `requiredEnvVars` names (`getManagedKeys()`), minus the strictly protected infra keys (`PROTECTED_KEYS`: DATABASE_URL, SESSION_SECRET, SITE_URL, VERCEL_API_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID) - so module settings tabs (e.g. Twilio) can manage their own credentials without a core edit. DELETE ("Reset Everything"): deletes every project env var, writes the `pendingRedeployId: 'pending'` sentinel, triggers a redeploy in `after()`.
- `GET/PUT /api/admin/navigation` - `config.manage`. GET returns the stored `SiteConfig.adminMenuConfig` blob; PUT full-replaces it (zod `AdminMenuConfigSchema` from `lib/nav/admin-menu.ts`) - the admin-sidebar customisation (per-item order/rename/visibility) written by the Settings → Navigation builder. An empty `{items:{},sections:{}}` = back to built-in defaults.
- `POST /api/admin/config/test-email` - `config.manage`. Sends a test email to `to` (defaults to the caller's own email). Optional `credentials` body (`provider: 'brevo'|'smtp'` + key/host/port/user/pass strings) tests unsaved values typed into the settings form via `sendTestEmailWithCredentials` before a save/redeploy; blank fields fall back to the current server env. Without `credentials`, sends via the ordinary saved-env `sendTestEmail`.
- `POST /api/admin/branding/generate-icons` - `media.upload`. Body `{sourceMediaId}`; sharp resizes the uploaded app-icon source into favicon 96 / apple-touch 180 / PWA 192 / 512, stores each via `uploadMedia`+`saveMediaRecord`, returns ids+urls. Backs the Branding tab's one-shot App icon flow (see Admin UI).
- `POST /api/admin/media/deploy-worker` - protected-role, `maxDuration 60`. Uploads the Cloudflare media Worker to the user's account (creds from the request body, then the Vercel project's saved values, then `process.env`) and persists the CF creds + `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` via Vercel env. Every request field is optional once a deploy has succeeded. Backs the Media tab's "Set up the Worker automatically" box (see Admin UI / Media Layer).
- `GET /api/admin/github-app` - `config.manage` OR `modules.manage`; ENCRYPTION_KEY presence/format, GitHub App connection + installation state, `hasPat`.
- `GET/DELETE /api/admin/redeploy-status` - GET requires only a session (deliberately no permission gate; the admin shell's deploy status surfaces poll it for every admin role). DELETE (`config.manage`) clears the gate, releases DeployLock, reconciles `deploying` modules against the actual latest Vercel deployment state.
- `POST /api/admin/reset-database` - protected-role only. `deleteSetupData: true` = TRUNCATE all tables (preserving only adminPath) → setup wizard; the hard-reset TRUNCATE list now also includes `GithubAppConnection` (its encrypted App private key / webhook / client secrets have no FK into the old set and were surviving a factory reset), plus `SavedBlock`, `Folder`, `Tag`, `Notification`, `EmailTemplate`. Soft mode = truncate content tables, keep the current admin and SiteConfig, delete all other users, re-seed starter content (Home page, Main Menu, starter layouts, Styles page).
- `GET /api/admin/backup/database` - protected-role only, `maxDuration 60`. Streams a full logical SQL backup (init migration schema + data) straight to the browser as a download - no object storage/B2 needed. Tables/columns/FKs discovered at request time via `information_schema` (module tables included automatically, nothing hardcoded), topologically sorted for FK-safe restore order; **`_prisma_migrations` and `ModuleMigration` are excluded from the dump** (`getTables`) - both are build-time bookkeeping about the physical schema of the DB they live in, not portable content, and carrying a module's ledger into a restore made the target claim tables it doesn't have (see restore + runner self-heal, 2026-07-15); self-referencing tables (`MenuItem.parentId` and module equivalents) additionally row-ordered by BFS since plain FKs aren't deferrable. Restore target is always a fresh empty DB. Depends on `next.config.ts`'s `outputFileTracingIncludes` entry to ship the migration file into the function's Vercel bundle (a runtime `fs.readFileSync`, not a static import, so the file tracer needs the explicit hint). Dump logic lives in `lib/backup/dump.ts` (`buildBackupSql(db, schemaSql, generatedAt)`, takes a client so the round-trip test can drive it); the route is a thin auth + file-read wrapper. **The whole read phase runs inside ONE interactive transaction at `RepeatableRead`, `SET TRANSACTION READ ONLY` (2026-07-23)** - `maxWait` 10s, `timeout` 58s, deliberately just inside the route's 60s ceiling - so table discovery, every table's rows and the sequence counters all see a single snapshot. Without it a dump taken while the site was serving traffic could be internally inconsistent: a sequence read at N while a row using N+1 was read afterwards (restore rewinds the sequence and the next insert collides on a UNIQUE column), or a child row written mid-dump referencing a parent whose table had already been read (restore fails the FK). Neither shows up until RESTORE, which is the worst possible moment to find out. Consequently `BackupDb` now requires `$transaction` and a narrower `BackupTx` (just `$queryRawUnsafe`/`$executeRawUnsafe`) types the read helpers, because Prisma's interactive-transaction client deliberately has no `$transaction` of its own. Generated/identity columns are excluded (they can't be inserted into). **Sequences are dumped too** - a trailing `SELECT setval(...)` section - because they are not tables and nothing else would see them; without it a restored shop reset `shp_order_number_seq` to 1 and the next checkout generated an already-used `order_number` (UNIQUE) and hard-failed.

Value serialisation lives in `lib/backup/serialize.ts` (`serializeValue(value, ColumnType)`, unit-tested in `serialize.test.ts`). **Two invariants:** (1) the column's `information_schema` `udt_name` is the discriminator, NEVER the JS value shape - a `json`/`jsonb` column always emits a quoted JSON literal, a SQL-array column (udt starts with `_`) emits `ARRAY[...]::<elem>[]` with the cast (mixed-case enum element types quoted); (2) **it never guesses** - an unrecognised udt, or a value whose shape contradicts its column type, throws `UnsupportedColumnError` and aborts the whole dump (surfaced by the route as a 500 with a human message). The old silent "least-worst rendering" fall-through is what turned a small bug into an unrestorable backup: a bad literal is written happily and only fails at RESTORE time, months later, in an emergency. Bugs this caught: deciding on `Array.isArray` alone rendered `jsonb` array columns (`InfoPage.history`/`Layout.history`) as `text[]`, so restore died with `column "history" is of type jsonb but expression is of type text[]` (42804) on any site with a republished page; and `bytea` columns (`Passkey.publicKey`) came back from Prisma raw as a `Uint8Array`, not a `Buffer`, so the `Buffer.isBuffer` check missed them and they were JSON-stringified into garbage - every passkey silently unrestorable. Byte columns now accept any `Uint8Array`. **`date`/`time`/`timetz` gained branches of their own (2026-07-23, `TIME_OF_DAY`)**: `isSupportedUdtName` claimed them as supported while they sat in the string-only `TEXTUAL` set, and Prisma hands those columns back as a JS `Date`, so the first install carrying a DATE column would have thrown `UnsupportedColumnError` and aborted its own backup. They cannot share the `TEMPORAL` branch either - that emits a full ISO datetime, which a `date` column rejects for the time part and a `time` column rejects for the date part. Caught by the schema-coverage backstop's own rule that a claimed-supported udt must have a real branch.
- `POST /api/admin/backup/import` (protected-role) and `POST /api/setup/import-backup` (unauthenticated, but 404s the moment `setupCompleted && userCount > 0`, so it can never wipe a live site) - restore a `.sql` backup. Both delegate to `restoreDatabaseFromSql(sql, db = prisma)` in `lib/backup/restore.ts`, 100 MB cap. Destructive and total: TRUNCATE every table (bar the preserved ledgers `_prisma_migrations` **and `ModuleMigration`**) → replay the backup's INSERTs in file order → apply its `setval`s, all in ONE transaction, so a failure changes nothing. **`ModuleMigration` is preserved (2026-07-15)**, not wiped or restored - it records which module migrations THIS database physically ran; overwriting it with the source's ledger left a fresh restore target claiming module tables (created by migrations, absent from a backup's schema section) were applied, so the runner skipped them forever. INSERTs targeting a preserved table (an older backup made before the dump exclusion) are ignored. INSERTs for tables the target lacks (module not installed here) are skipped and reported; setvals for absent sequences likewise. **Version skew is checked BEFORE the TRUNCATE** (`assertSchemasMatch`): a column in the backup that the target lacks = backup is from a newer Cactus → refuse with a plain-English error telling the owner to update first (never silently drop the data); a target column that is NOT NULL with no default and absent from the backup = backup is from an older Cactus → refuse. Parsers (`splitSqlStatements`, `insertTargetTable`, `insertColumns`, `setvalTargetSequence`) unit-tested in `restore.parse.test.ts`. **Last step inside the transaction: `clearUnreadableSecrets(tx)` (`lib/backup/secrets.ts`)** - see below. `RestoreResult` therefore also carries `clearedSecrets: string[]` (plain English, shown by both restore UIs, which suppress their auto-redirect when it is non-empty) and `secretsChecked: boolean`. **After the transaction commits: `checkRestoredMediaStorage(db)` (`lib/backup/media-check.ts`, 2026-07-15)** adds `mediaWarnings: string[]`. A backup carries the Media catalogue but never the file bytes (those live in an external bucket - see dump), so a restore onto a site not connected to the source's storage leaves every image pointing at objects it can't serve. The check is **deterministic and network-free on purpose**: it never fetches the restored `url`s (they come from an uploaded file - fetching them would be an SSRF vector, especially on the pre-auth setup route), it just asks `isMediaProviderConfigured(provider)` (`lib/config/env.ts`) for each provider the restored `Media` rows use and warns about any this install has no credentials for. Conservative - it can't catch "right provider, wrong bucket" (creds look fine); that closes with the planned media-inclusive backup. Both restore UIs (`app/setup/page.tsx`, `app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx`) render `mediaWarnings` alongside `clearedSecrets` and hold the auto-redirect when either is non-empty. Unit-tested in `media-check.test.ts` (mock db + env, no network). The Backup download panel copy now also states the backup is database-only and the storage bucket must stay in place.
- **Encrypted-secret reconciliation on restore** - `lib/backup/secrets.ts`. `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is minted per install (`/api/setup/vercel-connect` generates a fresh random one), but a backup file is portable, so restoring onto a fresh install ALWAYS lands AES-256-GCM ciphertext (`lib/crypto/secrets.ts`) that this site's key cannot read - and a backup deliberately does not carry the old key. Left in place it is worse than absent: the `GithubAppConnection` row made the site report GitHub as connected while every call died with OpenSSL's `Unsupported state or unable to authenticate data`, and a two-factor enrolment pointed at a secret nobody could produce a code for. So after the INSERTs and setvals, still inside the transaction, every `*Encrypted` text column in every table (discovered from `information_schema`, so module columns following the convention are covered for free) is trial-decrypted. Values that are not `looksLikeEncryptedSecret()` are left alone - not ours, no guessing. Values that are ours but unreadable are neutralised: **NOT NULL column → the row is deleted** (a `GithubAppConnection` is nothing but its credentials), **nullable → set NULL**, plus `COMPANION_CLEARS` for state that depended on it (`User.totpSecretEncrypted` also clears `totpVerifiedAt`/`totpLastStep`, or the login offers an authenticator step that can never succeed). **`MemberTwoFactor` is the exception: rows are demoted to the `EMAIL` method, never deleted** - member sign-in 403s an account with no two-factor config at all (`Two-factor authentication is required but not yet configured`), so deleting would lock the member out exactly as thoroughly as the dead secret did; demotion keeps a real second factor (an emailed code) until they re-enrol. If `ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing or malformed the sweep is skipped entirely (`secretsChecked: false`) - with no key there is no telling "wrong key" from "key not set yet", and wiping a site's secrets on the strength of a missing env var is not a trade worth making. Covered by the round-trip test's second case (restores under a different key and asserts the GitHub row is gone, the admin's TOTP flags are cleared, the member keeps an EMAIL factor, and content is untouched) and by `lib/crypto/secrets.test.ts` (no network, plain `npm test`).
- **Backup round-trip test** - `lib/backup/roundtrip.test.ts` + `lib/backup/vps-database.ts`. The only test that proves a backup actually restores, and the only one that catches bugs nobody predicted (it found the `bytea`/`Uint8Array` corruption on its first real run). Provisions its OWN throwaway databases on the self-hosted OVH Postgres VPS (moved off Neon 2026-07-22, no API key any more): SSHes in with `sshpass` using `OVH_SERVER`/`OVH_USER`/`OVH_PASSWORD` from root `.env`, creates role `cactus_rt_role_<stamp>` and database `cactus_rt_src_<stamp>`, applies the core init migration, seeds the awkward shapes on purpose (jsonb-holding-an-array on `InfoPage.history`/`Layout.history`, a populated `text[]` and an empty one, `bytea`, quotes-in-JSON), dumps it, restores the dump into `cactus_rt_dst_<stamp>` (a `CREATE DATABASE ... TEMPLATE` clone of the seeded source, replacing the old Neon copy-on-write branch), then compares an order-independent md5 content hash of EVERY table. Two further cases: restoring the same backup under a DIFFERENT `ENCRYPTION_KEY` (the normal case for a restore) clears every secret it cannot read and leaves the content alone; and a newer-Cactus backup is refused and changes nothing. Cleanup is unconditional: `afterAll` drops both databases and the role, and `dropStaleTestObjects` sweeps anything `cactus_rt_*` before AND after every run. `vps-database.ts` refuses to drop any name outside `/^cactus_rt_[a-z0-9_]{1,48}$/`, so the live `neondb` sharing that server is never named, opened or altered. Skipped unless `RUN_BACKUP_ROUNDTRIP=1` (set by `npm run test:backup-roundtrip`), so plain `npm test` never hits the network. **A skipped run is NOT a pass** - see `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` for the gap-filler that runs unconditionally.
- **Backup schema-coverage test** - `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts`, runs in plain `npm test`, no key, no network, no skip. Statically parses every column type out of the init migration AND every `modules/*/migrations/*.sql` (both `CREATE TABLE` column lists and `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN` lines), maps the SQL type syntax to the `information_schema.udt_name` `lib/backup/serialize.ts` switches on, and asserts `isSupportedUdtName` (new export, pure lookup against `serialize.ts`'s own type sets, no behaviour change) is true for every one. Exists because the round-trip test's database-server requirement gives it an escape hatch (missing `OVH_*` details -> "skipped", not "failed", and a skipped suite still reports green) - this test has none: add a column of a type the serialiser has never seen (verified by deliberately injecting an `INET`/`TSVECTOR` column and confirming the run goes red) and `npm test` fails on the PR that added it, full stop.
- `GET/POST /api/admin/updates` - `config.manage`, `maxDuration 60`. GET: core update status by channel (public/beta), raises/clears the `core-update` notification, lists modules with updates when a core update exists. POST: acquires DeployLock via `acquireDeployLock()` (90s expiry), optionally queues module updates into the same deploy, `syncCoreFromUpstream(..., {deadlineAt})` under a 50s soft deadline, arms the redeploy gate via `startDeferredRedeploy({committedSince})`; falls back to a deferred notification without Vercel credentials. On failure it rolls the queued module rows back, releases the lock, appends a live GitHub status reading (`gitHubOutageNote()`) when GitHub is degraded, and answers 503 for a deadline abort or a known outage (nothing was written either way) instead of a blanket 500. A held lock answers `lockBusyMessage(lock)`, which names the remaining wait.
- `GET /api/admin/release-notes` - any authenticated session (no permission gate; upstream releases are public), `maxDuration 30`. `?page=N` (default 1) returns one page of the full upstream release history newest-first via `getReleaseNotesPage` (`lib/updates/core.ts`): `{ items: {version,tag,publishedAt,html,url}[], hasMore }`. Unlike `/api/admin/updates`, returns EVERY published release regardless of prerelease flag (About dialog is history, not an update prompt). Powers the infinite scroll in the About dialog's Release notes panel.
