- `GET/POST /api/admin/layouts`; `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/layouts/[id]` - list/create/update/delete Layouts. **All five handlers require `layouts.manage`** - the two GETs used to accept any valid session, so an ordinary member's cookie could read every layout on the site. `GET` selects explicitly (no `publishedData`, no `history` - the latter is up to ten whole Puck payloads per layout, previously shipped to the browser on every list load), orders published-first then `updatedAt` desc, and calls `ensureLayoutsCurrent()` so an admin-only site still gets the post-update prune. `POST` rejects an unknown `type` (`isKnownLayoutType`) and seeds `defaultConditionsForLayout(type)` when the caller sends none. `PATCH` validates every field it accepts (non-empty `name`, `status` in the enum, known `type`, integer `priority`, shaped `displayConditions`) instead of handing them to Prisma raw and returning a 500; with `status: 'published'` it refuses unless the layout is left with ≥1 **complete** include condition (`isCompleteRule` - a rule with a blank value shows nothing), then archives the previous `publishedData` into `history` (cap 10, mirrors the pages publish route) before writing the new `publishedData`/`publishedAt`/`publishedById`.
- `POST /api/admin/layouts/[id]/duplicate` (`layouts.manage`) - forks any layout: `"<name> (Copy)"`, counting up to `(Copy 2)`, `(Copy 3)` … when that name is taken, same type/description/builderData/priority, always `draft` with empty display conditions. Surfaced as a Duplicate button on every card in the admin Layouts list (alongside Edit/Preview/Delete, no longer starter-only).
- `GET /api/admin/layouts/[id]/history` (`layouts.manage`) - `?index=live|N` for full blobs, no param for the version list. Mirrors `GET /api/admin/pages/[id]/history`. Restoring a **published** layout re-publishes through `PATCH` (`status: 'published'`), so the version it replaces is archived and the tab's "Live" entry stays true; a bare `builderData` PATCH would have put the restored content live while `publishedData` still described the old one.
- `POST /api/admin/layouts/[id]/publish` - **removed** (v0.5.401). Zero callers, and it flipped `status: 'published'` while skipping the display-conditions guard and never writing `publishedData`/`history`: a back door that could put a layout live with no rules and no history. Publishing goes through `PATCH`.
- `POST /api/admin/layouts/[id]/use-sitewide` - **removed**. It only ever accepted `isStarter` rows, which no longer exist. A layout is published site-wide from the builder's Conditions tab like any other.
- `GET/POST /api/admin/saved-blocks` (`pages.read`/`pages.write`); `DELETE /api/admin/saved-blocks/[id]` (`pages.write`) - reusable Puck block snapshots (`SavedBlock` model), shared by the page and layout editors' Saved Blocks tab.
- `GET/POST/DELETE /api/admin/media` - **GET single item: `?id=<mediaId>` (2026-07-23)** short-circuits ahead of the listing and returns just that row (`id`, `key`, `url`, `altText`, `originalName`, `mimeType`, url passed through `signAssetUrl`), still shaped as the usual `{ items: [...], total, page, perPage, hasMore }` envelope so callers need no second code path; an unknown id returns an empty `items` array rather than a 404. The parameter was previously ignored, so anything asking for one item by id (the OG-image and media-picker previews) silently got the default newest-first listing and rendered the last-uploaded image instead. GET list (session only) via the shared `queryMediaLibrary`/`parseLibraryQuery` (`lib/media/library-query.ts`): params `folder` (id / omitted=root / `all`), `q` search, `tag`, `type=all|image|video|model|other` (2026-08-20 - video and 3D files were previously swept into `other`; the four are a partition, asserted in `library-query.test.ts` against `TYPE_FILTER_WHERE`), `sort=newest|oldest|name|name_desc|largest|smallest|largest_dim|smallest_dim` (the `_dim` pair orders by `Media.pixels` with **nulls last** in both directions - an unmeasured row is not a small picture), `filter=all|in-use|unused`, **`optimisable=1`** (raster, not SVG, `optimised=false` - the same predicate `computeLibraryStats` counts for the Optimisable tile, in SQL; the tile's drill-down used to set `type=image` and so listed every already-optimised image beside the handful still to do), `page`/`perPage`; returns `{ items, total, page, perPage, hasMore }`, each item carrying `inUse` (`loadMediaUsageIndex`/`isMediaInUse`), `folderId`, `tags[]` and `width`/`height` (null = never measured), and each item's `url` passed through `signAssetUrl` (a no-op for everything but 3D models, which the Worker refuses untokened - the library's own picker previews one in a viewer); the default `all` usage tab paginates at the DB (count + skip/take), the in-use/unused tabs load-classify-slice. Backs `MediaLibrary.tsx`. POST upload (`media.upload`; active provider selected AND configured; content-sniff via sharp) now also reads a `folderId` form field and threads its `resolveFolderPath` into `uploadMedia`/`saveMediaRecord`. This serverless multipart path is now the FALLBACK only (SVGs, non-S3 providers, or when the direct path is unavailable/fails); it's size-guarded at `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (4 MB) from `lib/media/limits.ts`. **The key now keeps the uploaded filename** (`buildLibraryUploadKey` in `lib/media/upload.ts`, passed to `uploadMedia`'s new `presetKey` argument): the exact-name key is used when no `Media` row already holds it, else `-2`, `-3` … up to 50, and only then the old `<nanoid>-<label>` form. `Media.originalName` is unchanged (still the verbatim name for display); this is about what the bucket and the served URL say.
- **Direct-to-Worker upload (50 MB cap - `MAX_DIRECT_UPLOAD_BYTES`, raster images on S3-compatible providers; 3D models ride the same road, see below):** client-side `uploadOneFile` (`lib/media/upload-client.ts`, driven by `MediaLibrary.enqueueFiles` via the shared upload queue, **3** files in flight at once after all name-clash prompts are answered (`CONCURRENT_UPLOADS`, cut from 6 on 2026-07-24; each job needs two of the browser's ~6-per-host connections - the signing call here, the byte PUT to the media host - so a six-wide pool sat on the ceiling with nothing spare for the page's own thumbnails. NB the "bulk uploads fail en masse in Safari" bug was NOT this - see the read-access guard note below - so don't read the 6→3 cut as its fix); takes an optional `onProgress` fraction callback) routes raster types (`RASTER_DIRECT_TYPES`: jpeg/png/webp/gif) through: (1) `POST /api/admin/media/upload-url` - `media.upload`; returns `{ available, uploadUrl, key, token }` when the active provider is S3-compatible (`isS3Provider`) AND `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` is set, else `{ available:false }`; `key` from `buildLibraryUploadKey` (exact filename, deduped `-2`/`-3` … against existing `Media.key`s, nanoid form only as a last resort), `token` from `signUploadToken`. An optional **`replaceId`** aims the same machinery at an item that already exists (see `[id]/replace`): the key comes from `planMediaReplacement` instead of `buildKey`, and `{ available:false }` also when the row sits on a provider the site has since moved off (the Worker only carries the ACTIVE provider's credentials, so those fall to the serverless path, which writes with the app's own) (`lib/media/upload-token.ts`, HMAC over `key\n<exp>` with a key derived from `SESSION_SECRET` via `deriveUploadSigningKey`, 15-min TTL). (2) Browser `PUT`s the file bytes to `<worker>/<key>` with `Authorization: Bearer <token>`; the media Worker (`workers/media-worker/index.ts`) verifies the token, resolves the provider from the key path, and does a SigV4 PUT (real payload hash, body buffered) to storage. **The Worker takes the stored content-type from the KEY's extension, never from the client's `Content-Type` header** (the key is covered by the signature and its extension comes from an already-validated MIME type, so it's the one type claim a client can't forge - trusting the header let a `media.upload` holder store `text/html` + script and have it served back as executable HTML from the media origin). It requires a `Content-Length`, rejects anything over 50 MB before buffering, rejects a body whose real length disagrees with it, and refuses SVG outright (only the serverless path sanitises SVG). On GET it always sends `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, echoes an upstream content-type only if it's a known image type, and serves anything else as `application/octet-stream` + `Content-Disposition: attachment` - which retroactively defuses any object poisoned before this. (3) `POST /api/admin/media/record` - `media.upload`; **requires the signed upload `token` back** (same signature the Worker checked, so a row can only point at a key this session was issued) and derives `mimeType` from the signed key rather than the body; size clamped to 50 MB; writes the `Media` row via `saveMediaRecord`. **`sizeBytes` is no longer taken from the body either** (2026-07-19): the body figure is the client's own `file.size`, which describes the file it meant to send rather than the object that landed, and on this path the bytes never pass through the app to be measured - `confirmedSizeBytes` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) HEADs the object and records the real length, keeping the claimed value only when the provider cannot say. The body value still serves the 50 MB cap check. `[id]/replace`'s direct path does the same via `adoptReplacementBlob`. Core's `/record` stays **image-only** (`isRasterDirectType`) even though `contentTypeForKey` now types model extensions too: the library's own routes upload photographs, and the module that uploads models signs its own keys and records its own rows. The two direct-to-Worker `PUT`s (fresh upload + replace) go through `sendWithRetry` (`upload-client.ts`, 3 attempts, 400 ms/1200 ms backoff, progress rewound to 0 before each retry) which retries **only a status-0 result** - no reply at all, i.e. the browser refused the connection - and hands back untouched any status the server actually chose (401/413/415/500), since retrying a real answer only reaches it again more slowly. **Only the PUTs retry** - a PUT rewrites the same bytes to the same signed key and is idempotent, whereas the serverless `POST`s create a `Media` row / drop a superseded blob, and status 0 says only that no reply arrived, not that the server never acted, so retrying one could file the same picture twice. Added 2026-07-24: a status-0 refusal was being read as "the direct route isn't available" and fell straight through to the serverless path, which the browser refused for the same reason, and *that* second failure produced the misleading "the connection dropped before the server replied". Any failure in this chain falls back to the serverless path, so an un-redeployed Worker degrades to current behaviour - **but the Worker must be redeployed (Settings → Media → Deploy Worker) for the upload/serve hardening to take effect.** The Worker gains `OPTIONS`/`PUT` handlers + CORS + `UPLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET` env, pushed on Worker redeploy by `deploy-worker/route.ts`. `uploadErrorMessage` (`limits.ts`) still special-cases the serverless 413. DELETE `?id=&force=` (`media.delete`; 409 + reference list unless `force`). Reference check is `getMediaReferences` in `lib/media/upload.ts` (logo/favicon light+dark, page OG images, member avatars, data exports, and Puck builder JSON) - kept in step with `lib/media/references.ts`. Its haystack hit is now labelled **"page, layout or module content"**, since the same haystack carries module-contributed references and a substring hit can't say which matched.
- `PATCH /api/admin/media/[id]` - `media.upload`. Rename and/or move one item. Body `{ newName?, targetFolderId?, collision? }` → `moveOrRenameMedia`; a name clash under the default `error` mode returns `409 { collision, name }`. **Also handles a metadata-only edit** `{ altText?: string|null, isDecorative?: boolean }` (present WITHOUT `newName`/`targetFolderId`): a plain `prisma.media.update` (no collision path) - trims/nulls empty alt text, and forces `altText=null` when `isDecorative` is true. Backs the detail panel's alt-text editor + Decorative toggle (`MediaDetailPanel.onSaveMeta` → `MediaLibrary.saveMeta`). `DELETE /api/admin/media/[id]` unchanged (path-param twin of the query DELETE).
- `POST /api/admin/media/move` - `media.upload`. Bulk move. Body `{ ids, targetFolderId, collision? }`; `error` mode stops at the first clash with `409 { collision, name, id, moved, skipped }`, other modes (suffix/replace/skip) resolve inline. Backs drag-drop + Move to….
- `POST /api/admin/media/duplicate` - `media.upload`. Body `{ ids, targetFolderId }`; clones each blob into the target as a new row (paste-copy), names auto-suffixed on clash, no reference rewrite (nothing points at a fresh copy).
- `POST /api/admin/media/name-check` - `media.upload`. Body `{ folderId, names[] }` → `{ clashes: [{ name, existingId, suggestedName }] }`. Asked by the library's uploader BEFORE any bytes move, so an upload whose name is already taken in the destination can offer Replace / Keep both / Skip / Cancel instead of silently auto-suffixing. `suggestedName` is the free `name-1.ext` form - hyphen, not " (1)", because it ends up in the storage key and so in the public url. Runs `checkUploadNamesBulk` (`lib/media/organise.ts`): the whole batch is answered in a bounded number of queries (chunked `IN` to find clashes, one folder-names snapshot for suffixing) - the per-name `checkUploadName` was 2 queries × N, i.e. 50k sequential round trips for a 25k-file drop, which timed out before any upload began. Suffix suggestions are reserved across the batch so two clashing names can't be handed the same free name.
- `GET/POST /api/admin/media/folders` - GET (session) returns every folder (flat, with direct-child `mediaCount`) + `rootCount`; POST (`media.upload`) creates a folder `{ name, parentId? }`. `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/media/folders/[id]` - GET (session) the cascade-delete summary `{ folders, media, inUseNames }`; PATCH (`media.upload`) rename `{ name }` OR move `{ parentId }` (string/null) via `moveFolder` - rejects cycles + destination name clashes, relocates every descendant item either way; DELETE (`media.delete`) permanent cascade of the whole subtree (blobs + rows, via idempotent `deleteMany` so a re-submitted confirm no longer throws P2025).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/media/tags` - GET (session) all tags with counts; POST (`media.upload`) upsert-create `{ name }`. `PUT /api/admin/media/[id]/tags` - `media.upload`. Body `{ tags: string[] }` replaces the item's tag set (missing tags created on the fly, removed ones unlinked, Tag rows kept for reuse).
- `DELETE /api/admin/media/[id]` - path-param twin of the above DELETE (`DELETE /api/admin/media/<id>`); same session/permission/reference-check/deletion logic. (The admin media UI now deletes via `bulk-delete` for both single and multi; this route remains for any direct/path-param callers.)
- `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-delete` - `media.delete`. Body `{ ids: string[], force?: boolean }`; per-id same reference check as the single-delete routes (skips items still in use unless `force`), continues through the rest of the list regardless of any one item's outcome. Returns `{ deleted: string[], skipped: {id, references}[], notFound: string[] }`. Backs the media library's delete flow - single (detail panel / context menu) and multi-select bar (`MediaLibrary.tsx`).
- `POST /api/admin/media/optimise` - `media.upload`. Body `{ mediaId }`. Downloads the item's original bytes, runs sharp (`resize` fit-inside max 1024px, no enlargement → lossless `webp` effort 6, `animated:true`), stores the result as a new media row and returns `{ optimised:true, id, url, before, after }`; if the WebP came out no smaller it keeps the original and returns `{ optimised:false, before, after }`. Original row left untouched. Used by the Branding tab's logo "Optimise" button.
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/optimise` - `media.upload`. Optimises a single media item **in place** via `optimiseMediaInPlace` (`lib/media/upload.ts`): re-encodes to lossy WebP (`quality:82, effort:6, animated:true`, no downscale), and if smaller keeps the same `Media.id` while pointing `key`/`url`/`mimeType`/`sizeBytes` at the new blob, sets `Media.optimised`, rewrites any url/key refs embedded in Puck `InfoPage`/`Layout` builder JSON **and runs every module-registered `core.media-reference-rewriters` provider** (so `shp_product_media`/`svr_option_values` urls follow the blob), then deletes the pre-optimise blob. Returns the `OptimiseResult` (`{optimised:true, before, after}` or `{optimised:false, reason, before?, after?}`). Skips SVG/non-raster and already-optimised rows. Distinct from `/optimise` above (which mints a new row for Branding). Backs the media library's per-card "Optimise" button.
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/edit` - `media.upload`. Crop/edit one raster image via `editMediaImage` (`lib/media/upload.ts`). Body `{ crop: {left, top, width, height}, mode: 'replace'|'new', newName? }`; crop rect is in the source image's own pixels (clamped to bounds server-side). Downloads the original, `sharp().extract(rect)`, re-encodes in the source's own format (`encodeCrop`: jpeg/png/webp/gif/avif, else WebP; reads first frame only so an animated source becomes a still). `replace` swaps the blob under the existing row (same `Media.id`, `optimised` reset to false, rewrites embedded url/key refs in Puck JSON, deletes the pre-edit blob - the optimise-in-place pattern). `new` uploads the crop and `saveMediaRecord`s a fresh row in the same folder, original untouched. Returns `{ ok, item }`. Skips SVG/non-raster. Backs the media library's Edit image tool (`MediaImageEditor.tsx`).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/media/measure` (2026-08-20) - GET (session) `{ remaining }`, the count of raster images with no `width`; POST (`media.upload`, `maxDuration 60`) body `{ limit }` (default 40, cap 200) measures the next unmeasured batch newest-first and returns `{ ok, measured, failed, remaining }`. The caller does not choose the rows - the batch is whatever is still unmeasured - so the media page loops it until `remaining` hits 0 and resumes wherever a closed tab left off. `lib/media/dimensions.ts` does the work: `probeDimensionsByUrl` range-requests the first 128 KB (the media Worker forwards `Range` to storage), falls back to the whole object only when a full-length partial fails to parse, and six probes run at a time. Client loop breaks when `remaining` stops falling, because failed rows stay unmeasured and would otherwise be re-fetched for ever.
- `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-optimise` - `media.upload`. Body `{ ids: string[] }`. Runs `optimiseMediaInPlace` over each id sequentially (each re-encode is CPU-heavy), one failure never aborts the rest. Returns `{ optimised: string[], skipped: {id, reason}[], failed: {id, error}[], bytesSaved }`. Backs the media library's multi-select "Optimise" bar (`MediaLibrary.tsx`), which since 2026-07-20 calls it once per id through `runBulkImageJob`'s 6-worker pool rather than handing it the whole selection - the route is unchanged and still accepts any length.
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/aspect` - `media.upload`. Change one raster image's aspect ratio via `changeMediaAspectRatio` (`lib/media/upload.ts`). Body `{ ratioW, ratioH, fill: {kind:'blur'|'colour'|'transparent', colour?}, mode:'replace'|'new', newName? }` (parsed by the shared `parseAspectRequest`, `lib/media/aspect-request.ts`; ratio capped at 20:1). **Pads, never crops or stretches**: geometry from the pure `planAspectChange` (`lib/media/aspect-plan.ts`) grows only the short axis so every source pixel survives, then `blur` composites the whole image over a cover-cropped+blurred copy of itself, while `colour`/`transparent` use `sharp().extend()`. Returns `{ ok, changed:true, item, width, height, downscaled }`, or `{ ok, changed:false, reason }` when the image is already that ratio or a JPEG asked for transparency (`supportsTransparentFill`). Skips SVG/non-raster. Backs `MediaAspectDialog.tsx`.
- `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-mark-optimised` - `media.upload`. Body `{ ids: string[], optimised?: boolean }` (defaults true). Sets/clears `Media.optimised` via `markMediaOptimised` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) - **no bytes are read or written**, so unlike its neighbours it takes the whole selection in ONE request rather than an id at a time through `runBulkImageJob` (one SELECT + one UPDATE, nothing for the serverless ceiling to bite). Skips ids that don't exist, aren't `isOptimisableType` (raster + GLB; an SVG would get a ✓ badge for an optimise it was never offered), or already hold the requested value. Returns `{ ok, changed: string[], skipped: {id, reason}[] }`. Direction is a parameter, not always true, because this is an admin's assertion and marking hundreds by mistake must not be a one-way door. Backs "Mark as optimised" / "Mark as not optimised" on the selection bar, the detail panel footer and the context menu.
- `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-aspect` - `media.upload`. Body `{ ids: string[] }` + the same aspect fields as `[id]/aspect`. Runs `changeMediaAspectRatio` over each id sequentially, one failure never aborts the rest. Returns `{ changed: string[], skipped: {id, reason}[], failed: {id, error}[] }`. Backs the media library's multi-select "Change ratio…" bar, called once per id through `runBulkImageJob`'s 6-worker pool since 2026-07-20 (route unchanged, still accepts any length).
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/resize` - `media.upload`. Scale one raster image down via `resizeMediaImage` (`lib/media/upload.ts`). Body `{ width?, height?, mode:'replace'|'new', newName? }` (parsed by the shared `parseResizeRequest`, `lib/media/resize-request.ts`; at least one side required, each capped at `MAX_RESIZE_DIMENSION` 20000px). **Uniform downscale, never an upscale**: geometry from the pure `planResize` (`lib/media/resize-plan.ts`) fits the image inside the box keeping its own ratio, so the box is a ceiling not a target - `sharp().resize(w, h, {fit:'inside', withoutEnlargement:true})`, then `encodeToMime` keeps the source format. Output dimensions are **re-measured off the encoded bytes**, not taken from the plan (`fit:'inside'` can land a pixel under the box). Persists via the shared `persistDerivedImage` (same replace/new semantics as `[id]/edit` and `[id]/aspect`). Returns `{ ok, changed:true, item, width, height, capped, before, after }`, or `{ ok, changed:false, reason }` when the image already fits inside the box. Skips SVG/non-raster. Backs `MediaResizeDialog.tsx`.
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/replace` - `media.upload`. **Swap one item's file for a freshly uploaded one, keeping the item**: same `Media.id`, name, folder, alt text, decorative flag and tags, so every page/product/setting pointing at it keeps working and simply shows the new picture (the difference between this and "upload the new one, delete the old one", which breaks every page the old one was on). Two request shapes mirroring the two upload paths: **multipart `{ file }`** (serverless fallback, `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` 4 MB; the bytes pass through here so `validateUpload` sees them - real image, SVG sanitised) → `replaceMediaFile`; or **json `{ key, token, sizeBytes }`** (direct path, 50 MB) → `adoptReplacementBlob`, where the client already PUT the bytes to the Worker at a key this app signed. The direct path takes nothing that decides where the row points from the body (the /record rule): type comes from the signed key via `contentTypeForKey`, the token is re-verified, and the key is re-checked against `planMediaReplacement` - same directory (a token from a *plain* upload would otherwise quietly move the item to another folder), and for an exact-named item the one key it may occupy at all. Storage is the provider the ROW lives on, not the active selection (503 if that one's creds are absent). `optimised` resets to false (a freshly picked file has not been through the optimiser, exactly as a fresh upload of it would be). Raster→raster type swaps are allowed even on exact-named items (`planMediaReplacement`): the key follows the new extension and `repointMediaToBlob` rewrites Puck content plus module rewriters before dropping the old blob - previously refused with a 409, which broke bulk "Replace" over any previously-optimised folder (optimise stores WebP bytes but keeps the `.jpg` display name, so every re-upload of originals was a "type change"). If the swap's target exact key is held by ANOTHER row, the plan falls to the nanoid key form. Non-raster type changes (3D models, SVG) still 409. The direct path accepts model types too (`isDirectUploadType`, not raster-only - raster-only rejected a same-type `.glb` replace AFTER the Worker had stored the bytes). Returns `{ ok, item }`. Backs the media library's Replace button (card hover 🔄 / detail-panel footer / context menu) and the upload name-clash dialog's Replace choice (`MediaLibrary.enqueueFiles`, whose batches now run strictly one at a time via `uploadBatchChain` - a second drop while a clash dialog was open used to strand the first batch's files at "queued" forever).
- `planMediaReplacement` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) decides where a replacement blob lands: the item's own provider/folder/name, with only the extension following the new bytes' type (`withExtensionForMime`, so a JPEG replacing "hero.png" is filed and displayed as "hero.jpg"). **An exact-named item (`isExactNameKey`, see `lib/media/keys.ts`) may only be replaced by a file of its own type** → `MediaReplaceTypeError` → 409 with a plain reason, refused at `/upload-url` too so the client isn't told only after pushing the whole file up. Reason: its name IS its key, so a new extension means a new key. Module-owned url columns are now rewritten too (the `core.media-reference-rewriters` extension point), but the refusal is **kept as defence-in-depth** - an exact-named item may be referenced by a module that has registered no rewriter, and a type-changing replace would leave that reference pointing at the blob the swap then deletes, so the image would vanish from that surface while sitting intact in the library.
- `rewriteMediaReferencesInContent` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) swaps a media item's old url/key for its new one inside Puck builder JSON (`InfoPage` + `Layout`, both `builderData` and `publishedData`), then runs every module rewriter. Since 2026-07-20 the Puck half is one atomic SQL statement per table (`swapInBuilderJson`, private) instead of reading every row's JSON into node and writing the whole blob back - see the header entry: the old shape lost updates as soon as two images on the same page were rewritten concurrently, which is what let the bulk jobs go parallel.
- `repointMediaToBlob` (`lib/media/upload.ts`, private) is now the single owner of the tail **every** in-place rewrite shares - `optimiseMediaInPlace`, `persistDerivedImage` (crop/reshape/resize) and both replace paths: point the row at the new blob (id untouched), rewrite embedded url/key refs in Puck JSON **then run every module-registered `core.media-reference-rewriters` provider** (`getMediaReferenceRewriters`, so module-owned url columns follow the move too), then delete the superseded blob **last** and only if the key actually moved (a write that resolved to the key it started on has just put the new bytes there, so "deleting the old blob" would delete the image itself). The order is the point: a failure at any step leaves the old blob still serving the old url rather than a row pointing at bytes that were never written.
- `POST /api/admin/media/bulk-resize` - `media.upload`. Body `{ ids: string[] }` + the same resize fields as `[id]/resize`. Runs `resizeMediaImage` over each id sequentially, one failure never aborts the rest; sends no `newName` (one name across many would collide, so the server suffixes each with its own new size). Returns `{ ok, changed: string[], skipped: {id, reason}[], failed: {id, error}[], bytesSaved }`. Backs the media library's multi-select "Resize…" bar, called once per id through `runBulkImageJob`'s 6-worker pool since 2026-07-20 (route unchanged, still accepts any length).
- `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/optimise-video` - `media.upload`, `maxDuration 60`. Re-encode ONE video into the platform's single delivery format (MP4 / H.264 High / yuv420p / AAC / faststart) on the media worker. Body `{ quality?: 'high'|'balanced'|'small', maxWidth?: 1920|1280|1080|720 }` - both validated against `lib/media/video-quality.ts` and defaulted server-side, so the browser cannot ask for an encode the worker would clamp. Refuses anything that isn't `isVideoDirectType`, and anything not on the `B2` provider (the worker writes into that bucket with its own credentials). Destination key is `optimisedVideoKey(media.key)`: an `.mp4` is written back **over its own key** so every reference to it survives untouched; a `.webm` becomes `.mp4` and the route 409s if that key is already taken. Creates a per-job Fly machine exactly as `convert-sequence` does, signs a `{mediaId, machineId, name}` context token, enqueues `POST /video-jobs` on the worker, writes the `video-job:{jobRef}` notification and returns `{ jobId, destKey }`.
- `GET /api/admin/media/video-jobs` - `media.upload`. The video-optimise jobs, read back off their notifications (`lib/media/video-jobs.ts`); the Media › Video panel's list. Clearing a job is the ordinary notification delete.
- `GET/PUT /api/admin/media/video-worker-config` - GET `media.upload`, PUT `config.manage`. The media worker's Fly settings on `SiteConfig.mediaWorkerConfig` (`{fly:{token,appName}}`). `fly.token` is three-state (absent = keep, `''` = clear, string = save) and is NEVER echoed - responses report only `fly.source` ('saved'|'env'|null). Replaces `sequence-presets`, minus the conversion knobs (quality and largest-size are per video now).
- `GET /api/admin/media/video-status?jobId=` - `media.upload`. Twin of `sequence-status` for video jobs: settled state comes off the notification first (the job's machine is destroyed the moment the webhook lands, so a later poll cannot reach it), otherwise proxies the worker's `GET /jobs/{id}` through the machine-routed header and rewrites the notification. A bare 404 only fails the job once Fly agrees the machine is gone.
- `POST /api/webhooks/video-optimise` - no session; HMAC-gated on `X-Cactus-Signature` (raw body, keyed with `SEQUENCE_WORKER_SECRET`) with the enqueue-time context token as the bearer. On `optimised: true` calls `applyOptimisedVideo` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) → `repointMediaToBlob`, so the row keeps its id (and every reference) and simply weighs less; on `optimised: false` (the worker could not beat the source by `VIDEO_MIN_SAVING`, so it uploaded nothing) calls `markVideoAlreadyOptimised`, which stops the library offering a re-encode that has already been tried. Destroys the job's Fly machine either way, and settles the notification with a plain-words saving ("45.0 MB → 21.9 MB, 51% smaller").
- **Media usage index (`lib/media/references.ts`)** - `loadMediaUsageIndex()` (React `cache`, once per request) returns `{ referencedIds, haystack, referenced, degraded }`; **`referenced`** (2026-08-19) is every url / `media/...` key / id-shaped token `extractReferenceTokens` finds in the haystack, so `isMediaInContent` (also exported, and the content half of `isMediaInUse`) answers with a set lookup instead of three substring scans per row - the same three scans that made the stat bar time out on a 36k-row library. A value carrying a character extraction cannot capture (`isPlainReference` says no) still falls back to `haystack.includes()`, because a false "unused" arms a bulk delete. `isMediaInUse(row, index)` decides the library's in-use dot, the Unused tile and the folder-delete warning. `referencedIds` is core's own FK columns (site logo/favicon/app icons, page OG images, member avatars, data exports); `haystack` is every InfoPage `builderData`/`publishedData` + Layout `builderData` blob **plus every string returned by the new `core.media-usage-providers` extension point** (contract `lib/media/usage-providers.ts`: `() => Promise<string[]>`, raw urls/keys/`Media` ids in any mixture, JSON columns returnable whole as text). Without it core could only see its own tables, so every shop product image, option/attribute swatch, 3D model, product download, board icon, directory photo and gazette hero counted as **unused** and was offered up for bulk deletion. Providers run in parallel; one throwing sets `degraded`, which makes `isMediaInUse` return `true` for everything (unused count 0) rather than trusting a half-built index - an over-cautious "nothing to reclaim" is a wasted click, an under-cautious "unused" is a delete button aimed at live product photography. Registered providers: `shop` (`shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url`, `shp_products.og_image_id`, `shp_collections.image_id`/`og_image_id`, `shp_categories.og_image_id`/`image_url`), `shop-variations` (`svr_option_values.swatch`, `svr_uploads.media_ref`/`media_key`), `product-attributes-for-shop` (`pat_attribute_values.swatch`), `product-3d-views-for-shop` (`p3d_models.url`/`media_key`/`media_id` + `p3d_fabric_configs.config` as text), `product-downloads-for-shop` (`pdl_files.url`/`media_key`/`media_id`), `boards` (`brd_boards.icon_media_id`, `brd_user_profiles.avatar_id`), `directory` (`dir_entries.images` as text, `dir_categories.icon`), `gazette` (`gz_posts.featured_image_id`, `gz_author_profiles.avatar_id`).
- Media migration (`config.manage`): `GET /api/admin/media/provider-breakdown`, `POST migration-start`, `POST migration-batch` (one 15-item batch per call, driven by the open admin tab), `GET migration-status`, `POST migration-cancel`, `POST migration-retry`.
- `GET /api/admin/media/storage-check` - `config.manage`, `maxDuration = 60`. Reconciles `Media` rows against the objects storage actually holds (`reconcileMediaStorage`, `lib/media/reconcile.ts`). Rows are grouped by their own `provider` (a library that has been through a provider switch holds rows on several), each configured+listable provider is enumerated via `listStoredMediaKeys`, and the pure comparison lives in `diffStorageAgainstRows` (unit-tested in `lib/media/reconcile.test.ts`). Returns `{ providers: ProviderScan[], orphaned, claimed, missing, mismatched, orphanedBytes, claimedBytes, partial }` - `orphaned` = object with no row **and** nothing pointing at it (keys ending `/` skipped as folder placeholders), `claimed` = object with no row that page/layout/module content still references, `missing` = row whose object is gone, `mismatched` = row whose `sizeBytes` disagrees with the object. The claim test is built once per scan (`buildClaimTest`): `loadMediaUsageIndex()`'s haystack is run through `extractReferencedKeys` (regex `media/[^\s"'\\)>,\]}|]+`, query string stripped, raw + `decodeURIComponent` form both kept) into a `Set` so 30k+ objects cost a lookup each rather than a substring search each. A `degraded` index, or one that throws, claims **everything** (no leftovers reported) - same over-cautious direction as `isMediaInUse`. Without this, a module that writes a url straight into its own table without minting a `Media` row (bulk 3D attach, bulk product images) left live files reading as leftovers: on Deskwell 2026-08-15 that was 717 of 1,127, including 665 in-use `.glb` models and 52 live product photographs. `partial: true` (with a per-provider `skippedReason`) whenever a provider could not be listed: unconfigured, list threw, over the 50,000-object `KEYS_PER_PROVIDER_LIMIT`, or CLOUDINARY/IMAGEKIT (provider-minted ids, `listStoredMediaKeys` returns `null` = "cannot tell", never an empty list).
- `POST /api/admin/media/storage-check` - `config.manage`. `{ action: 'correct-sizes' }` rewrites every mismatched row's `sizeBytes` to the stored size (`correctRecordedSizes`, re-derives the list itself). `{ action: 'delete-orphans', keys: string[] }` additionally needs `media.delete` and re-runs the scan server-side, deleting only keys a fresh scan still calls orphaned; returns `{ deleted, skipped, reclaimedBytes }`. `{ action: 'purge-missing', keys: string[], force?: boolean }` also needs `media.delete` and deletes the `Media` rows whose object is gone (`purgeMissingRows`) - no blob call at all, since the object it names no longer exists; same re-scan-server-side guard, and without `force` a row `getMediaReferences` still finds in use is skipped and returned in `skipped: { key, originalName, references }[]` rather than deleted. Returns `{ purged, skipped, stale }` (`stale` = requested keys a fresh scan no longer calls missing).
- Menus (`menus.manage`): `GET/POST /api/admin/menus`; `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/menus/[id]` (GET also resolves each MODULE_ENTITY item's live label/href/publish-state via its provider, and returns `isMainMenu` (computed against `SiteConfig.mainMenuId`) for the admin editor's badge; PATCH accepts `name` and/or `isMainMenu` - `isMainMenu:true` sets `SiteConfig.mainMenuId` to this menu, `false` clears it only if this menu is the one assigned; delete clears `mainMenuId`, returns `wasMainMenu`); `POST [id]/duplicate` (deep-clones the menu + entire item tree into a new "<name> (copy)" menu, parents-first inside a transaction so child `parentId`s resolve; safe against the (menuId,pageId) unique since the copy is a fresh menu); `GET [id]/resolve` (public-shape resolved tree, anonymous viewer); `POST [id]/items` (PAGE unique per menu / EXTERNAL label+url / MODULE_ENTITY moduleId+entityKind+entityId, validated against the provider; optional `visibility` default PUBLIC; order auto-assigned per parent scope); `PATCH/DELETE [id]/items/[itemId]` (PATCH accepts label/url/openInNewTab and `visibility`); `POST [id]/items/reorder` (bulk parentId+order in a transaction); `GET /api/admin/menus/module-entities` (no moduleId/kind: lists registered modules+kinds; with both: searches that kind via its provider).
- Roles (`roles.manage`): `GET/POST /api/admin/roles` (unique name); `DELETE /api/admin/roles/[id]` (protected roles and roles with assigned users blocked); `POST/DELETE /api/admin/roles/[id]/permissions` (RolePermission upsert/remove; protected roles immutable).
- Users (`users.manage`): `GET /api/admin/users` (paginated); `PATCH /api/admin/users/[id]` (roleId / suspend; self-modification blocked; only protected-role actors may act on protected-role targets; last-admin guard on demotion); `DELETE /api/admin/users/[id]` (content ownership nulled; last-admin guard).
- `GET /api/admin/people` (`users.manage`, additionally unions in Member rows when `members.list` is also held) - unified staff+member directory backing `/cactus-admin/users`'s single Users tab: raw `UNION ALL` of `User`/`Role` and `Member`/`Role` (Prisma has no cross-model union), search across username/email/displayName, `type=staff|member` filter, sort by `username`/`createdAt`, real SQL pagination.
- Notifications (`config.manage`): `GET /api/admin/notifications`; `PATCH /api/admin/notifications` `{read: boolean}` (bulk - `updateMany` over the whole table, not the returned slice; true stamps every unread, false clears every read); `DELETE /api/admin/notifications` (bulk `deleteMany({ NOT: {type: 'deployment', deployInitiatedAt: null} })` - spares the open deployment notification, the one row nothing re-creates; returns `{deleted, kept}`); `PATCH /api/admin/notifications/[id]` (read/unread); `DELETE [id]`; `POST [id]/redeploy` (409 if already initiated; flips `pending_deploy` modules to `deploying`; `startDeferredRedeploy`; 503 in local mode).
- Pages: `GET /api/admin/pages` (`pages.read`); `POST` (`pages.write`, publish status additionally `pages.publish`, optional menu assignment with `menus.manage`, unique slug); `DELETE` bulk `{ids[]}` (`pages.delete`; blocked for pages referenced as privacy/terms). `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/pages/[id]` (PATCH cannot flip draft→published - Publish endpoint only). `POST [id]/autosave` (`pages.write`; writes only `builderData` + menu links; draft pages reconcile title/slug/meta/ogImage columns, published pages freeze them). `POST [id]/publish` (`pages.publish`; the only writer of `publishedData`/`status: published`; archives the previous live version into `history`, capped at 10; `revalidatePath`). `GET [id]/history` (`pages.read`; `?index=live|N` for full blobs, no param for the version list). `GET /api/admin/pages/perms` (session; returns canRead/canWrite/canPublish/canDelete/canManageMenus).
- Modules (`modules.manage`, `maxDuration 60`): `GET /api/admin/modules` (list); `POST` (install: GitHub required, DeployLock, fetch + zod-parse `cactus.module.json`, tablePrefix uniqueness, `requiresModules` dependency check with minVersion, latest GitHub release required by channel, `requiredEnvVars` presence check, permission registration, then `deploying` + `startDeferredRedeploy`). `PATCH /api/admin/modules` `{action: 'update-all'}` - bulk-updates every module with `status: 'update_available'` in one DeployLock + one `startDeferredRedeploy` (avoids the per-module 409 that calling `PATCH [id]` `update` repeatedly would hit); per-module release fetch failures are skipped and reported back in a `failed: string[]` array rather than aborting the batch; each module now also runs the same compat gate the single-module path uses, via `checkModuleUpdateCompat()` (`lib/modules/compat.ts`, reads the manifest at the target tag and checks `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules` against core + the current installed set) - an incompatible module is dropped from the batch into `failed[]` with its reason and is never pinned into `modules.json`, closing the hole where one incompatible latest tag bricked every future deploy; drives the Modules admin page's "Update all" button. `PATCH /api/admin/modules/[id]` - `updateChannel` | `enable` | `disable` | `check-status` (lazy Vercel deploy reconcile for Hobby plan) | `update` (new tag held in `pendingVersion` until the deploy succeeds; the row's stored `manifest` is **also refreshed** to the one already fetched at that tag - it was previously frozen at whatever was recorded on INSTALL, so a module adding a `requiredEnvVars` entry in a later version could never have that variable managed by `/api/admin/env`, which derives its allowed keys from these stored manifests. Written at update time rather than on deploy success on purpose: the new credentials have to be settable while the new code is going out, not after). `DELETE [id]` `{mode: code_only|code_and_data}` - dependent-module guard; `code_and_data` drops the manifest's `teardown` tables with verification and deletes the module's `ModuleMigration` rows (otherwise a later reinstall skips its migrations and the tables never come back); deletes module permissions and row; redeploy. `GET [id]` - per-module update check against the latest release for its channel; raises/clears the `module-update:{id}` notification. `GET /api/admin/modules/directory` - lists public repos of the GitHub org `cactus-foundation-modules` (5-minute in-memory cache, `?refresh=true` busts), merged with installed state; `directoryUnavailable` flag when GitHub is unreachable; each uninstalled repo probed for a stable GitHub release (`hasPublicRelease`) so the admin UI can hide the Public channel option and force Beta for modules with pre-releases only. Both routes also pre-check the manifest's `requiresModules` against the installed `Module` rows via the shared `findUnmetModuleDependencies(requiresModules, installed)` (`lib/modules/dependencies.ts`, the one place `minVersion` is compared): install rejects with the existing plain `errorResponse` message, while `update` reuses its single `requiresCoreVersion` manifest fetch and returns a structured `409 { error, code: 'module_version_required', moduleName, dependencyName, requiredVersion, currentVersion }` naming the module to update first (`currentVersion` null when the dependency is absent or inactive rather than merely out of date) - updating a module whose new release raised a dependency pin (shop-variations and product-attributes-for-shop both pin `shop >= 0.1.38`) would otherwise break the site's next build on a missing module import, exactly as the core check prevents for core imports. Both manifest pre-checks in `update` are skipped silently when the manifest can't be fetched, so a transient GitHub hiccup never blocks an otherwise-fine update. `fetchManifestFromRepo(repoUrl, filename, ref='HEAD')` now takes a ref: install and both update paths pass the exact `release.tag` they are about to ship, so `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`/permissions are validated against that tag's manifest, not default-branch HEAD. The `requiresCoreVersion` rejection on install/update no longer plain-texts the manifest's kebab-case `name` slug - both routes now return a structured `409 { error, code: 'core_version_required', moduleName, requiredVersion, currentVersion }`, `moduleName` from the new `formatModuleDisplayName(repoUrl)` (`lib/modules/manifest.ts`, same "cactus-module-foo-bar" → "Foo Bar" transform the Modules page already used for its cards). The Modules admin page catches `code === 'core_version_required'` in both its install and update handlers and opens a dedicated lightbox (title "Cactus needs updating first", message, a link to `../config?tab=general` - the Settings → General tab holding `UpdatesPanel`) instead of the page-top `alert-danger` banner used for every other install/update failure. **Custom-module hardening (2026-08-13, working tree):** `POST` validates `repoUrl` through `parseGitHubRepo` immediately after body parse (clear 400 - a well-formed non-GitHub URL previously travelled into `getLatestRelease` and threw unhandled as a 500), probes the repo with `octokit.rest.repos.get` before release resolution (404 → a message naming the real fix, granting the Cactus GitHub App access to the private repo, instead of the misleading "publish a release first"; other probe errors fall through to the release path's own handling), and refuses a private repo outright when the site holds no clone credential (`MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` / a `GithubAppConnection` in `ready` state) - installing anyway would commit a module into `modules.json` that the next build cannot fetch. `GET /api/admin/modules/directory`'s `buildInstalledEntry` now reads `description` off the stored manifest JSON, so a custom (off-directory) module's card is no longer permanently blank; no `Module` column was added.

Members admin API (Phase 5 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md; every route below is `getSessionFromCookie` + a specific `members.*` permission):

- `GET /api/admin/members` (`members.list`) - search (`q`, case-insensitive across username/email/displayName) + status/trusted filters + sortable columns (`createdAt`/`username`/`status`) + pagination.
- `GET /api/admin/members/dashboard-summary` (`members.list`) - counts by status + `pendingDeletion` + 5 most recent suspensions.
- `GET/PATCH/DELETE /api/admin/members/[id]` (`members.view`/`edit`/`delete`) - PATCH is displayName/bio/websiteUrl; DELETE is the admin hard-delete, bypassing the member's own grace period entirely (no `MemberAdminActionLog` row for this one - see the top-of-file summary for why).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/suspend` (`members.suspend`, optional `reason`/`until`) - also revokes every live `MemberSession` for the member immediately; `POST .../unsuspend` restores `ACTIVE` (there's no stored pre-suspension status to restore to - suspension is only ever expected on an already-ACTIVE member in practice).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/approve` (`members.approve`, only from `PENDING_APPROVAL`) - sends a plain "you're approved" email when configured; `POST .../reject` deletes the member outright (never became a real active member, so nothing to keep - like admin-delete, no action-log row survives this one).
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/trust` (`members.trust`, `{trusted}`).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/members/[id]/notes` (`members.notes`) - append-only, mirrors `MemberAdminNote`'s own no-PATCH/DELETE design.
- `GET/DELETE /api/admin/members/[id]/sessions`, `DELETE .../sessions/[sessionId]` (`members.view`/`edit`) - admin-side session list/revoke-all/revoke-one.
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/reset-password` (`members.edit`) - deletes `MemberPassword` + `MemberTwoFactor`; there's no admin-settable member password, so "reset" means forcing the member back onto passkey/magic link until they set new ones themselves.
- `POST /api/admin/members/[id]/export-trigger` (`members.edit`, `maxDuration 60`) - runs the same `createDataExportRequest` flow as the member's own Danger Zone button, e.g. to fulfil a support request; the member downloads it themselves once ready.
- `GET /api/admin/members/[id]/action-log` (`members.view`) - last 100 `MemberAdminActionLog` rows.
- `POST /api/admin/members/bulk` (`{ids[], action}`, permission checked per action type against `ACTION_PERMISSIONS`) - suspend/unsuspend/approve/reject/trust/untrust/delete, `{done, skipped}` response (same shape as Boards' bulk endpoints).
- `GET/POST /api/admin/members/invites`, `DELETE /api/admin/members/invites/[id]` (`members.invite`) - create returns the full shareable `inviteUrl` (`/{memberAreaPath}/register?invite=<token>`) once; delete only revokes an unused invite (`usedAt: null` guard).
- `GET/PATCH /api/admin/members/settings` (`members.settings`) - GET also returns the read-only `memberAreaPath`; PATCH is a partial merge-then-validate against `MembersConfigSchema` (same pattern as `designTokens`/`consentBannerConfig`), then refuses the save when `hasAnyAuthMethod()` is false (every sign-in method off locks the members system shut with no screen left to undo it from - refused here rather than in the schema so the message can say what to do about it), invalidates the config cache.
- `GET /api/admin/sms/templates` (`sms.templates`) - every registered text message from an installed module, grouped by module, defaults merged with any `SmsTemplate` override, plus `smsAvailable` and `maxLength`. `PATCH /api/admin/sms/templates/[key]` - save `body`/`isActive`; rejects an edit that dropped a `requiredTags` tag and rejects switching off a transactional message. `DELETE` resets the wording only. `POST /api/admin/sms/templates/preview` - renders unsaved content with stand-in values, returns `{text, chars, segments, unicode}`. `POST /api/admin/sms/templates/test-send` - same render, sent to a number typed into the form (prefixed `[Test]`), 503 when no SMS provider is configured.
- `GET /api/admin/emails/templates` (`emails.templates`) - every registered email (core + installed modules only), grouped by source, defaults merged with any DB override, plus the `emailWrapper` layouts available and which is the site default. `PATCH /api/admin/emails/templates/[key]` - save any of `subject`/`bodyHtml`/`wrapperLayoutId`/`isActive`; rejects an edit whose combined subject+body has dropped a `requiredTags` merge tag, rejects switching off a transactional template, rejects an unknown wrapper id. `DELETE` on the same path resets the **copy only** to the code default (nulls `subject`/`bodyHtml`), keeping the wrapper choice and on/off state. `POST /api/admin/emails/templates/preview` - renders unsaved editor content through the real send path with stand-in merge values, returns `{subject, html}` for the sandboxed preview iframe. `POST /api/admin/emails/templates/test-send` - same render, emailed to the requesting admin's own address only, subject prefixed `[Test]`. (Replaces `/api/admin/members/email-templates*`.)
- `GET /api/admin/members/gdpr` (`members.gdpr`) - one combined read: pending deletion requests, last 50 data-export requests, last 50 consent records, last 50 `MemberAdminActionLog` rows filtered to GDPR-relevant actions (export/reset-password/suspend/unsuspend).

Setup API (each returns 403/404 once setup is complete with users, except deployment-logs):

- `GET /api/setup/env-check` - required/optional env status, `missingRequired`, `databaseState` (`set` | `provisioned-redeploying` [checked via Vercel API] | `missing`), `neonAvailable`, `vercelConfigured`, `localMode`.
- `POST /api/setup/vercel-connect` - `list-projects` (token validation, projects + domains) | `list-account-domains` (every domain on the account/team owning the project, so already-bought domains can be attached) | `add-domain` (attaches a domain to the project; returns its full `DomainState`; a 409 from a re-add of an already-attached domain is reported as that domain's current state, not an error) | `domain-status` (re-reads a domain's `DomainState`, first POSTing Vercel's `/domains/{d}/verify` so a freshly-added ownership TXT is actually re-checked) | `configure` (writes VERCEL_API_TOKEN, VERCEL_PROJECT_ID, generated SESSION_SECRET + ENCRYPTION_KEY, SITE_URL, NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, optional NEON_API_KEY, GITHUB_REPO from the project's git link; deliberately does not redeploy yet). `DomainState` = `{ name, verified, verification[], misconfigured, recommended }` - `misconfigured` (from `GET /v6/domains/{d}/config`) means DNS isn't pointing at Vercel, `!verified` (from `GET /v9/projects/{p}/domains/{d}`) means Vercel hasn't accepted the ownership TXT challenge; the two are independent and both gate the wizard's Configure button. `.vercel.app` aliases short-circuit to ready.
- `POST /api/setup/configure-env` - writes optional allowlisted env vars during the wizard.
- `POST /api/setup/provision-db` - actions: `list` (Neon projects incl. org-scoped) | `check-existing` (counts user tables) | `save-url` (user-supplied DATABASE_URL → Vercel + redeploy) | `use-existing` (pooled URI via Neon API, optional `destroyData` = DROP SCHEMA public on the direct endpoint) | `create` (default: Neon project `cactus-<vercelProjectId>`, Postgres 18, chosen region, idempotent by name search; writes DATABASE_URL + NEON_PROJECT_ID; redeploys) | `ensure-redeploy` (self-heal for the "provisioned, awaiting redeploy" state: returns the in-flight deployment if one is running, otherwise triggers a fresh one; `status: 'missing'` if DATABASE_URL isn't in the Vercel env after all). Credentials may come from the body pre-redeploy. Env writes go through `upsertVercelEnvVars` (overwrites stale values; sensitive vars skip the `development` target Vercel rejects). Provisioning responses carry `deploymentId` on success or `redeployError` when the trigger failed - the wizard shows the error with a retry instead of a phantom "Redeploying…". No short-circuit on a stale DATABASE_URL already sitting in Vercel env vars.
- `POST /api/setup/read-state` - wizard resume state; 404 once complete.
- `POST /api/setup/create-admin` - seeds core permissions, ensures the protected Admin role, creates the admin user (email verification exempt); exact-match retry path preserves the WebAuthn user handle and clears stale passkeys.
- `POST /api/setup/set-admin-path` - 3–64 chars `[a-z0-9-]`, blocklisted values rejected; upserts SiteConfig.
- `GET /api/setup/suggest-path` - random `word-suffix` admin path suggestion.
- `POST /api/setup/essentials` - siteName + timezone.
- `POST /api/setup/complete` - seeds Home page (slug `home`, published), Main Menu, the default layouts (`seedDefaultLayouts`, not "all starters" - see `lib/setup/`), the Styles draft page; sets `setupCompleted`, status `comingSoon`, `hideFromCrawlers`, default design tokens; Edge Config sync; generates missing SESSION_SECRET/ENCRYPTION_KEY (Vercel write + redeploy, returns `needsRedeploy`, plus `redeployError` if the trigger failed so the wizard can point at a manual redeploy) or auto-logs the admin in; stamps `SiteConfig.starterTemplatesVersion`. Re-POST after setup is refused 403.
- `POST /api/setup/reset` - sets `setupCompleted = false`, only when zero users exist.
- `GET /api/setup/deployment-logs` - Vercel deployment state + log lines with a `since` cursor; post-setup requires session + `config.manage` and the server's own token; pre-setup accepts the wizard's token in the **`x-vercel-token` header** (never `?token=` - a live API credential in a URL lands in access logs and browser history) plus `?projectId=` for team-scope resolution. The setup-complete check tolerates a missing database (pre-setup there is none - previously this 500'd and the wizard never showed deploy state). Passes `teamId` to the Vercel API for team-owned projects.

GitHub App connect flow (under `app/cactus-admin/integrations/github/`, reached via the admin path rewrite):

- `GET start` (`config.manage`) - builds the GitHub App manifest (name "Cactus Foundation - {siteName}", permissions `contents: write` + `metadata: read`); state cookie `cactus_github_app_state` (10 min).
- `GET callback` (session) - state check; converts the manifest code via `POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions`; encrypts pem/webhook secret/client id/client secret with `ENCRYPTION_KEY`; replaces the GithubAppConnection row; uploads `cactus.svg` as the app logo (non-fatal); redirects with `github=connected|error&reason=…`.
- `GET install` (`config.manage`) - returns `github.com/apps/<slug>/installations/new` URL + state cookie.
- `GET installed` (session) - stores `installation_id` and the installation account login.
- `POST disconnect` (`config.manage`) - deletes the GithubAppConnection rows (the App itself remains on GitHub).

Loading/error boundaries: one exists - `app/cactus-admin/error.tsx` ('use client'), covering every page under the admin prefix including `/cactus-admin/login` (which sits in this segment but renders outside `AdminLayout`'s shell). Shows a card with "That didn't load", the `error.digest` reference when present, and a "Try again" button wired to `reset()`, which re-runs the server render - the right cure for the transient failures this catches. Note React's nesting rule: a throw from `AdminLayout` itself goes to the *parent* boundary (root), not this one, so the layout guards its own reads inline: `getSessionWithMeta()` is `try`-wrapped and a failure is treated as no-session → `redirect` to login (safe - proxy.ts is the primary gate, no session ever fabricated), while `getSiteConfig`/`getInstalledModules`/`getUnreadCount`/`hasPermissions` each `.catch()` to an empty fallback the shell already tolerates (`null`/`[]`/`0`/`{}` - the permission catch can only ever hide nav, never reveal it; `isProtected` admins take hasPermissions' no-DB all-true branch so the catch bites only non-admins). No `loading.tsx` and no `global-error.tsx` anywhere.

### Middleware

There is no `middleware.ts`. `proxy.ts` at the repo root is the Next.js 16 replacement, running on the Node runtime (so it uses Prisma directly).

- Matcher: everything except `_next/static`, `_next/image`, and static file extensions (ico/png/jpg/jpeg/svg/webp/gif/woff/woff2/ttf/eot/css/js).
- Security headers (production only; skipped in development): CSP (`default-src 'self'`; scripts `'unsafe-inline' 'unsafe-eval'`; styles allow Google Fonts; img allows self/data/blob/picsum/the Worker host; `frame-ancestors 'none'`; `form-action 'self' https://github.com`), `X-Frame-Options: DENY`, `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff`, `Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin`, Permissions-Policy (camera/mic/geolocation off, WebAuthn self), HSTS 2 years preload.
- Always-pass paths: `/api/health`, `/api/webhooks/`, `/_next/`, `/favicon.ico`.
- `resolveAdminPath()`/`resolveSiteStatus()` fall back to `getAdminPathCached()`/`getSiteStatusCached()` in `lib/config/site.ts` when Edge Config isn't writable. Both cached readers **serve the last known value when their query throws** rather than propagating: a throw in `proxy.ts` isn't an error page, it's a bare 500 on whatever the visitor asked for, and the 5-second TTL guarantees a cold instance always misses. `undefined` from the guarded query means "the read failed" and is kept distinct from `null`, which legitimately means "no SiteConfig row".
- Direct requests to `/cactus-admin*` return 404.
- Direct requests to `/cactus-account*` return 404 (Members system internal prefix, `MEMBER_INTERNAL` from `lib/members/paths.ts`).
- First-run gate: until `setupCompleted && userCount > 0`, everything redirects to `/setup` except `/setup`, `/api/setup`, `/api/auth/passkey/`, `/api/auth/totp/`, `/api/health`, `/_next/`, `/favicon.ico`. After setup, `/setup*` returns 404.
- Admin path enforcement: resolves the admin path from Edge Config (when write creds present) else a 5-second-TTL Prisma cache; rewrites `/<adminPath>/*` → `/cactus-admin/*`. The `/login` sub-path is rewritten without an auth check (header `x-cactus-is-login: 1`). All other sub-paths validate the `cactus_session` cookie; on success sets `x-cactus-admin-path`, `x-cactus-user-id`, `x-cactus-role-protected`; unauthenticated requests redirect to `/<adminPath>/login?next=…`. (The former full-page redeploy trap is gone - in-flight redeploys are surfaced by the admin shell's `DeployStatusBar` and the notification bell instead.)
- Member-area path rewrite: unconditionally rewrites `/<memberAreaPath>/*` → `/cactus-account/*` (sets `x-cactus-member-path` and `x-cactus-member-full-path` - the latter is the original public pathname+search, used by `app/(public)/cactus-account/layout.tsx` to build an accurate post-login `?redirect=` since the internal pathname alone can't reconstruct it), checked after admin enforcement so admin wins any prefix collision. Still no session validation in proxy itself - the account layout does its own gate. Unlike the admin rewrite, this currently runs before the site-status gate below, so member pages stay reachable during comingSoon/maintenance; revisit when Phase 8 wires `siteWideMembersOnly`.
- API requests pass through, with a CSRF origin check on non-GET/HEAD/OPTIONS: a present-but-mismatched `Origin` header returns 403.
- `/page-preview/` and `/layout-preview/` always pass (so editors can preview while the site is gated).
- Site status gate: when status ≠ `live`, public routes are rewritten to `/cactus-status/coming-soon` or `/cactus-status/maintenance` unless the session's role `isProtected`. That protected-role bypass now returns `withSecurity(NextResponse.next())` (2026-07-23) rather than a bare `NextResponse.next()` - it was the one path out of the proxy that shipped no CSP, no HSTS and no `X-Frame-Options`, so an admin previewing a gated site browsed it entirely unprotected.
- Members-only site access (Phase 8 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md, runs after the status gate, only for ordinary public content - admin/api/preview/member-area paths have already returned by this point): gated when `membersConfig.siteWideMembersOnly` is on OR the path resolves to a non-`PUBLIC` module route tier (`lib/members/access.ts`'s `resolveRouteTier`, cached module read). `siteWideMembersOnlyExceptions` prefix-exempts a path outright; admins bypass; else the `cactus_member_session` cookie is validated (`TRUSTED_MEMBER` tiers additionally require `member.trusted`). Unsatisfied + `guestPreviewEnabled` → passes through with `x-cactus-guest-preview: 1` (consumed by the Puck `MemberGate`/`TrustedMemberGate` blocks' teaser rendering only, for now). Unsatisfied + no preview: no session → redirect to `/{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=…`; signed in but insufficient tier → 404 (no sensible redirect target, no dedicated status page for this case).

### Environment Variables

Core:

- `DATABASE_URL` - PostgreSQL pooled connection string. Required. Consumed by Prisma (`lib/db/prisma.ts`), build scripts, setup routes.
- `DIRECT_URL` - optional non-pooled connection for migrations; `scripts/build-migrate.mjs` (falls back to stripping `-pooler` from DATABASE_URL).
- `SESSION_SECRET` - HMAC ingredient for session/trusted-device token hashing, min 32 chars. Required (auto-generated on Vercel during setup). `lib/config/env.ts:getSessionSecret`, `lib/auth/session.ts`.
- `SITE_URL` - canonical public URL; also the WebAuthn rpId/origin source. Required. `lib/config/env.ts` (`getSiteUrl`, `getWebAuthnRpId`, `getWebAuthnOrigin`), robots/sitemap, recovery links.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL` - browser-visible copy of SITE_URL shown in the setup wizard. Optional in code, written by setup.
- `VERCEL` - platform-injected. Its absence defines local-development mode (`isLocalMode()` in `lib/config/env.ts`), which disables env editing, redeploys, and core/module updates.
- `VERCEL_URL` - platform-injected fallback for site URL in robots/sitemap.
- `NODE_ENV` - dev/prod switches (security headers, cookie `secure`, WebAuthn localhost overrides, Prisma logging).
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` - injected by `next.config.ts` from `package.json` version.
- `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED` - set to `1` by `next.config.ts`.
- `PORT` - `scripts/dev-warm.sh` only (default 3000).

Vercel control plane:

- `VERCEL_API_TOKEN` - required on Vercel; env-var writes, redeploys, deployment logs/status, Edge Config writes. `lib/vercel/env.ts`, `lib/vercel/deploy.ts`, `lib/deploy/redeploy.ts`, setup + admin env routes.
- `VERCEL_PROJECT_ID` - required on Vercel; identifies the project for all of the above.
- `EDGE_CONFIG` - optional; Edge Config read connection string (`lib/config/edge-config.ts`, `@vercel/edge-config`).
- `VERCEL_EDGE_CONFIG_ID` - optional; Edge Config item writes via the Vercel REST API.
- `VERCEL_WEBHOOK_SECRET` - optional; verifies `/api/webhooks/vercel` (Pro/Enterprise; Hobby falls back to lazy polling).

Auth:

- `TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY` / `TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY` - optional; Cloudflare Turnstile on login/register/recovery and module forms. `lib/auth/turnstile.ts` fails open when unset, fails closed on network errors when set.
- `MEMBER_AREA_PATH` - optional; public URL prefix for the member account area (default `account`). Deploy-time only, changing it requires a redeploy. Read via `getMemberAreaPath()` in `lib/members/paths.ts` (sanitised, blocklist-checked, falls back to the default). Member-area pages live internally at `/cactus-account/*`, rewritten in `proxy.ts` (see Middleware section).

GitHub:

- `GITHUB_API_TOKEN` - optional; PAT fallback for all GitHub operations (`lib/github/client.ts`), `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs`.
- `MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` - optional; deploy-time-only credential for cloning private module repositories (a fine-grained PAT with read-only Contents access). First tier in `scripts/checkout-modules.mjs`'s credential order (then a GitHub App installation token minted from `GithubAppConnection`, then `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`, then anonymous). Registered optional in `getEnvStatus()`; never logged, never written to disk.
- `GITHUB_REPO` - `owner/repo` of the site's own repository; module registry commits and core-update pushes (`lib/modules/github.ts`, `lib/updates/core.ts`).
- `CACTUS_CORE_REPO` - optional upstream override for core updates; defaults to `usersaynoso/cactus-foundation` (`lib/updates/core.ts`).
- `WIKI_SOURCE_REPO` - optional; `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs` (defaults to GITHUB_REPO).

Encryption:

- `ENCRYPTION_KEY` - 64-char hex (32 bytes) AES-256-GCM key. Required for the GitHub App flow, TOTP secret storage, and the reply-catcher module's mailbox credentials. `lib/crypto/secrets.ts`.

Neon:

- `NEON_API_KEY` - optional; automatic database provisioning during setup (`/api/setup/provision-db`).
- `NEON_PROJECT_ID` - written by provisioning. **No longer surfaced by `/api/auth/config` (2026-07-23)**: it used to feed the lost-passkey Neon console deep link on the login screen, which is a pre-auth payload, so the link is now the plain console URL and the value stays server-side.

Media (one provider active at a time; per-provider keys defined in `lib/media/providers.ts`):

- `B2_APPLICATION_KEY_ID`, `B2_APPLICATION_KEY`, `B2_BUCKET_NAME`, `B2_ENDPOINT` - Backblaze B2.
- `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `R2_BUCKET_NAME` - Cloudflare R2.
- `S3_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `S3_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `S3_BUCKET_NAME`, `S3_REGION` - AWS S3.
- `SPACES_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `SPACES_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `SPACES_BUCKET_NAME`, `SPACES_REGION` - DigitalOcean Spaces.
- `WASABI_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `WASABI_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `WASABI_BUCKET_NAME`, `WASABI_REGION` - Wasabi.
- `MINIO_ENDPOINT`, `MINIO_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `MINIO_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `MINIO_BUCKET_NAME`, `MINIO_USE_SSL` - MinIO.
- `BLOB_READ_WRITE_TOKEN` - Vercel Blob.
- `SUPABASE_STORAGE_PROJECT_URL`, `SUPABASE_STORAGE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`, `SUPABASE_STORAGE_BUCKET_NAME` - Supabase Storage.
- `CLOUDINARY_CLOUD_NAME`, `CLOUDINARY_API_KEY`, `CLOUDINARY_API_SECRET` - Cloudinary (direct).
- `IMAGEKIT_PUBLIC_KEY`, `IMAGEKIT_PRIVATE_KEY`, `IMAGEKIT_URL_ENDPOINT` - ImageKit (direct).
- `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` - shared Worker URL for all proxied providers; required by every proxied provider (`envKeysForProvider` appends it).
- `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_HOSTNAME` - Worker hostname for `next.config.ts` remotePatterns and the proxy CSP img-src. Optional: when unset, both derive it from `CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` (`workerImageHost()` in `proxy.ts` and `next.config.ts`), so the admin auto-deploy needs no extra env var.
- `NEXT_PUBLIC_CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL` - client-side Worker URL fallback used by the custom image loader (`lib/media/loader.ts`).

Email:

- `BREVO_API_KEY` - Brevo transactional API; takes priority over SMTP. `lib/email/index.ts`.
- `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT` (default 587), `SMTP_USER`, `SMTP_PASS` - nodemailer SMTP fallback.

Other:

- `SENTRY_DSN` - optional. Read only for configured-status display (dashboard, env editor); no Sentry SDK is installed or initialised anywhere.
- `CRON_SECRET` - **core-owned and self-minting; never asked of the owner.** Vercel attaches it as `Authorization: Bearer` on every scheduled invocation (core's four `/api/cron/members/*` jobs and every module `cronJobs` entry), and each cron route 503s without it. `ensureCronSecret()` (`lib/vercel/cron-secret.ts`) generates `randomBytes(32).toString('hex')` and upserts it as a **sensitive** project var; called from setup (`vercel-connect` mints it inline with SESSION_SECRET/ENCRYPTION_KEY, `setup/complete` covers the pre-set-token path), from core update (`app/api/admin/updates/route.ts`, before the lock - heals sites predating this), and from module install when the manifest has `cronJobs` or names `CRON_SECRET` (`app/api/admin/modules/route.ts`, which then drops it from the required-env gate unless the outcome is `unavailable`). Outcomes: `present` | `provisioned` | `pending` (already on the project, this deployment predates it - **never overwritten**, rotating it would break live crons) | `skipped` (local mode) | `unavailable` (no Vercel creds or API refused). Only ever reaches `process.env` via the redeploy the caller triggers, never within the request that mints it. Shown as an optional entry in `getEnvStatus()`.
- `GOCARDLESS_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `GOCARDLESS_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `GOCARDLESS_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`live`) - gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop module; the API access token, the webhook endpoint secret, and the environment. Presence of the token + secret gates the Instant Bank Pay checkout method (`modules/gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop/lib/env.ts`).
- `CREZCO_API_KEY`, `CREZCO_USER_ID`, `CREZCO_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`production`) - crezco-direct-bank-payments-for-shop module; the Collect API key (header `X-Crezco-Key`), the merchant user id every pay demand is created under, and the environment. Presence of key + user id gates the Direct bank payment checkout method (`modules/crezco-direct-bank-payments-for-shop/lib/env.ts`).
- `SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT` (`sandbox`|`production`), `SQUARE_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SQUARE_LOCATION_ID`, `SQUARE_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_ACCESS_TOKEN`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_LOCATION_ID`, `SQUARE_SANDBOX_WEBHOOK_SIGNATURE_KEY` - square-payment-for-shop module. `SQUARE_ENVIRONMENT` picks the API host (connect.squareup.com vs connect.squareupsandbox.com) **and** which credential set is read: the `SQUARE_SANDBOX_*` trio for sandbox, the unprefixed trio for production (`squareEnvVarNames()`/`getSquareCredentials()` in `modules/square-payment-for-shop/lib/env.ts`). Both sets can be set at once. Access token + location ID for the live environment gate the Card payment (Square) checkout method; the signature key is optional and only gates the webhook route (`isSquareWebhookConfigured()`).
- `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK` - set to `1` by `scripts/build-migrate.mjs` at build time only.

Cloudflare Worker (separate deployment, `workers/media-worker`): `ALLOWED_ORIGIN`, `BLOB_BASE_URL`, `UPLOAD_SIGNING_SECRET`, `ASSET_SIGNING_SECRET`, plus the same provider secret sets as above, configured via `wrangler secret put` (the two signing secrets are pushed automatically on Deploy Worker).

**3D models on the direct path (v0.5.468).** The Worker's write path accepts model extensions as well as raster images, and `MAX_DIRECT_UPLOAD_BYTES`/`UPLOAD_MAX_BYTES` rose 25 → 50 MB in step. Why it had to: a module posting a 50 MB model through a serverless route was never going to work - Vercel 413s any body over ~4.5 MB *before* the handler runs, and that 413's body is not JSON, so `res.json()` threw and the 3D editor's `?? 'Upload failed'` fallback was all anyone ever saw. The direct path is the only route in for a file that size.

- `MODEL_EXTENSION_TYPES` (`lib/media/limits.ts`) is the ext→type map: `glb`→`model/gltf-binary`, `gltf`→`model/gltf+json`, `obj`→`model/obj`, `fbx`→`model/x-fbx`, `3ds`→`model/x-3ds`. **Mirrored verbatim in `workers/media-worker/index.ts`'s `EXTENSION_TYPES` - keep the two in step.** Keyed by extension because a 3D file's declared type is worthless (browsers send `application/octet-stream` for .glb, an empty string for .fbx) and because on this path the extension is the only claim a client cannot forge: it is baked into the key the token signs.
- `extensionForMimeType` (`lib/media/upload.ts`) consults `extensionForModelType` **first**. Model types are not derivable from their subtype - `model/gltf-binary` must land as `.glb`, not `.gltf-binary` - and a key whose extension names no type is one the Worker refuses. The old `application/octet-stream` produced exactly that: `.octet-stream`.
- Models are **not** in `SERVABLE_IMAGE_TYPES`, deliberately. GET serves every non-image as `application/octet-stream` + `Content-Disposition: attachment`, which is fine: a model is fetched by XHR inside a WebGL canvas, which reads the bytes and ignores both headers. GET already sends `Access-Control-Allow-Origin`, so the cross-origin fetch works.
- `isAcceptedUploadType`/`isRasterDirectType`/`preflightUploadError` are untouched - the media library UI still offers images only.
- **Every existing install must redeploy its Worker** (Settings → Media → Deploy Worker) before 3D uploads work; an old one 415s every model key. `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s client turns that 415 into a "redeploy your Worker" message rather than a bare refusal.
- Not fixed here, same latent bug: **shop's `admin/digital-files`** advertises a 200 MB cap through the serverless multipart path, so anything over ~4.5 MB dies the same way. It needs the same treatment (or an honest limit) whenever someone gets to it.

Media worker (video optimise, standalone service at `services/video-worker`, deployed on Fly.io app `cactus-seqworker` - the app keeps its old name because renaming it would change the hostname every install holds):
- `MEDIA_WORKER_URL` - the worker's base URL (`lib/config/env.ts:getMediaWorkerUrl`). Unset hides the Optimise video action.
- `MEDIA_WORKER_SECRET` - shared bearer secret for the worker API and the HMAC key its completion callback is signed with (`getMediaWorkerSecret`, header `X-Cactus-Signature`).
- `MEDIA_WORKER_FLY_TOKEN` - optional Fly.io API token fallback (`getMediaWorkerFlyTokenEnv`). A token saved under Media → Video (`SiteConfig.mediaWorkerConfig` `fly.token`) wins; either enables per-job Fly machines (see Media Layer).
- `MEDIA_WORKER_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` - optional ceiling on simultaneous per-job Fly machines (`getMediaWorkerMaxJobMachines`). Unset or 0 = no ceiling, which is the default: every video gets its own machine. A positive value refuses further jobs in plain English rather than queueing them.
- **The `SEQUENCE_WORKER_URL` / `SEQUENCE_WORKER_SECRET` / `SEQUENCE_FLY_TOKEN` / `SEQUENCE_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` names are still read**, as a per-variable fallback in `readEnv`, so an install that predates the rename needs no environment change.

### Database Schema

Single Prisma schema at `prisma/schema.prisma` (PostgreSQL). One init migration: `prisma/migrations/20260626000000_init/migration.sql`. All timestamps UTC.

- `User` - `id` (cuid PK), `email` (unique), `username` (unique), `displayName?`, `passwordHash?`, `roleId` → Role, `emailVerifiedAt?`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `suspendedAt?`, `acceptedPrivacyPolicyAt?`, `totpSecretEncrypted?`, `totpVerifiedAt?`, `totpLastStep? BigInt`, `smsOtpPhoneEncrypted?` (AES-256-GCM phone; when set and an SMS provider module is active, password-login OTPs go by text). Relations: passkeys, sessions, trustedDevices, emailChallenges, recoveryRequests, infoPages, mediaItems, consentRecords. Indexes: email, username.
- `Passkey` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `credentialId` (unique), `publicKey Bytes`, `counter BigInt default 0`, `transports String[]`, `label?`, `createdAt`. Index: userId.
- `Session` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique; sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `TrustedDevice` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `EmailChallenge` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `codeHash`, `purpose` (`login_otp` | `verify_email` | `recovery`), `expiresAt`, `attempts Int default 0`, `createdAt`. Indexes: (userId, purpose), expiresAt.
- `RecoveryRequest` - `id`, `userId` → User (cascade), `tokenHash` (unique), `createdAt`, `expiresAt`, `used Boolean default false`. Indexes: userId, expiresAt.
- `Role` - `id`, `name` (unique), `isProtected Boolean default false`, `createdAt`. Relations: users, members, permissions. A protected `"Members"` row is lazily created (name-unique-race-safe) the first time anyone registers via `/api/members/register` (`lib/members/default-role.ts`), and assigned as every new Member's `roleId`.
- `Permission` - `key` (PK), `description?`, `module?` (null = core, else the registering module name). Relation: rolePermissions.
- `RolePermission` - composite PK (roleId, permissionKey); both FKs cascade.
- `SiteConfig` - singleton (`id = "singleton"`): `siteName` (default "My Cactus Site"), `tagline?`, `description?`, `timezone` ("UTC"), `locale` ("en-GB"), `dateFormat` ("DD/MM/YYYY"), `timeFormat` ("HH:mm"), `adminPath` (unique), `setupCompleted` (false), `status SiteStatus` (comingSoon), `hideFromCrawlers` (true), `speedInsightsEnabled` (true; Settings → General - gates `<SpeedInsights />` in `app/layout.tsx` via `isSpeedInsightsEnabled()` in `lib/config/site.ts`, a 5s-TTL best-effort reader that falls back to on, matching the pre-switch behaviour), `trustDeviceDays` (28), `starterTemplatesVersion?` (core version whose starter templates were last seeded; mismatch with `package.json` version triggers `ensureStarterLayoutsCurrent`'s auto-refresh), `emailFromName?`, `emailFromAddress?`, `emailProvider?` ('brevo' | 'smtp'), `mediaProvider MediaProviderType?`, `lazyLoadImages` (true; Settings → Media - sets `loading="lazy"` vs `"eager"` on every core content image [Image block, Quote photo, Card cover, Panel image, logo strip] via Puck `metadata`, see `lib/puck/renderMetadata.ts` + `lib/puck/imgLoading.ts`;
