the Image block's original exemption [it can be the LCP element] was removed on the owner's call - the trade is real and is surfaced in the setting's help text rather than decided in code; module blocks don't consult it), `privacyPolicyPageId?`, `termsPageId?`, `logoMediaId?`, `logoDarkMediaId?` (optional dark-mode logo; frontend swaps to it via CSS keyed on `data-theme="dark"`), `faviconMediaId?`, `faviconDarkMediaId?` (optional dark-mode favicon; served via a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` media query, so it follows the browser/OS scheme not the in-site toggle), `appIconMediaId?` (square source image the admin uploads; favicon/apple/PWA icons auto-generated from it), `appleTouchIconMediaId?`, `webManifest192MediaId?`, `webManifest512MediaId?` (each independently overridable), `appName?`, `appShortName?`, `themeColor?`, `backgroundColor?` (web-app manifest identity; fall back to `siteName`/white via `lib/config/branding.ts`), `sessionPurgeAfterDays` (30), `recoveryPurgeAfterDays` (7), `mainMenuId?`, `homepageId?`, `pendingRedeployId?`, `pendingRedeployAt?`, `designTokens Json?`, `consentBannerConfig Json?`, `coreUpdateChannel` ("public"), `membersConfig Json?` (Members settings, Zod-parsed with defaults by `lib/members/config.ts`), `adminMenuConfig Json?` (admin-sidebar customisation - per-item order/rename/visibility set in Settings → Navigation; null = built-in defaults; parsed by `parseAdminMenuConfig`/`AdminMenuConfigSchema` in `lib/nav/admin-menu.ts`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`.
- `UserColourPreset` - user-created Styles > Colours presets: `id`, `name` (unique), `tokens Json` (`{primary:{light,dark}, linkColour, linkHoverColour, linkColourDark, linkHoverColourDark}` - same shape as the hardcoded `ColourPreset` in `lib/design/tokens.ts`), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. The 10 default presets (`COLOUR_PRESETS`) are still hardcoded in app code with no DB row and can't be overwritten/deleted through this model; the Styles preset bar shows these user rows first, then the defaults.
- `InfoPage` - `id`, `slug` (unique), `title`, `body Text`, `bodyFormat BodyFormat` (markdown), `builderData Json?` (working draft; autosave target), `publishedData Json?` (live content, written only by Publish), `publishedAt?`, `publishedById?` (no relation), `history Json?` (array of `{data, title, at, byId}`, max 10, newest first), `status PageStatus` (draft), `metaDescription?`, `ogImageId?` (Media id, no relation), `createdById?` → User (SetNull), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Relation: menuItems. Indexes: slug, status.
- `Media` - `id`, `key` (unique), `provider MediaProviderType`, `url`, `uploadedById?` → User (SetNull), `altText?`, `isDecorative` (false), `originalName?` (the filename the user uploaded, kept verbatim for display since `key` is deliberately mangled with a nanoid prefix; null for legacy rows + generated files - icons/avatars/exports - which fall back to the key basename; the media library card/lightbox/grid and the Puck media picker all show `originalName || key.split('/').pop()`, and both the `/api/admin/media` GET and the media library page search it alongside key/altText), `mimeType`, `sizeBytes Int`, `width Int?`/`height Int?`/`pixels Int?` (2026-08-20 - pixel size of a raster image; null = never measured, which is NOT zero: SVGs, videos and 3D files never carry one, and every row predating this starts null. `pixels` is `width*height`, stored because Prisma cannot order by an expression, indexed, and written only by `setMediaDimensions`/`dimensionFields` in `lib/media/dimensions.ts` so the three cannot disagree. Filled on the serverless upload path from the bytes in hand, on the direct path by reading the object's header back in `/api/admin/media/record`, on every in-place rewrite inside `repointMediaToBlob` (from the encoded buffer, or a cache-busted range read when the bytes were never in-process), and in bulk by `/api/admin/media/measure`), `optimised` (Boolean, false - set true once the media library's in-place optimise has re-encoded the item to WebP, drives the "Optimised" badge and stops it being offered again), `folderId?` → Folder (SetNull; null = library root; the folder's path is baked into the item's `key`/`url`), `tags MediaTag[]`, `createdAt`. Indexes: uploadedById, createdAt, provider, folderId, pixels.
- `Folder` - media library folder. `id`, `name`, `parentId?` → Folder self-relation "FolderTree" (`onDelete:Cascade`; null = root), `children Folder[]`, `media Media[]`, `createdAt`. `@@unique([parentId, name])` (root uniqueness also enforced in app since Postgres treats null parentId rows as distinct), index parentId. Folders are physical: the sanitised slash-joined ancestor path lives in each contained item's storage key/url, so rename/move/delete relocate or remove blobs (see `lib/media/organise.ts`).
- `Tag` - `id`, `name` (unique), `createdAt`, `media MediaTag[]`. Freeform, created on the fly.
- `MediaTag` - join: `mediaId` + `tagId` (composite PK), both FKs `onDelete:Cascade`, index tagId.
- `MediaMigrationJob` - `id`, `toProvider MediaProviderType`, `status` (pending | running | completed | failed | cancelled), `totalItems Int`, `migratedItems Int default 0`, `failedItemIds Json default []`, `cursor?`, `startedAt`, `completedAt?`, `lastError?`. Indexes: status, startedAt.
- `Layout` - `id`, `name`, `type` (header | footer | infoPage | notFound | statusPage | module type; default infoPage), `description?`, `builderData Json?` (working draft; autosave target), `publishedData Json?` (live content, written only on publish), `publishedAt?`, `publishedById?` (no relation), `history Json?` (array of `{data, title, at, byId}`, max 10, newest first - mirrors InfoPage), `displayConditions Json?` (`{include: Rule[], exclude: Rule[]}`), `priority Int default 0`, `status PageStatus` (draft), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. - `SavedBlock` - reusable Puck block snapshots, shared by the page and layout builders: `id`, `name`, `componentType` (the Puck component type, e.g. "Hero"), `data Json` (full ComponentData blob, reinserted verbatim on use), `createdAt`. Single-tenant, no categories/folders.
- `Module` - `id`, `name` (unique), `repoUrl`, `version` (confirmed live tag), `pendingVersion?` (in-flight target, promoted only on deploy success), `tablePrefix` (unique), `status ModuleStatus` (pending_install), `installedAt`, `lastError?`, `lastCheckedAt?`, `updateAvailable?`, `updateNotes? Text`, `updateChannel` ("public"), `manifest Json?` (parsed cactus.module.json), `layoutsSeededAt?` (set the one time this module's `publishByDefault` layouts were stamped, by `markModulesDeploySucceeded()`; never cleared, because a module *update* redeploys down the same path and a create-only upsert would resurrect layouts the owner deleted).
- `Notification` - `id`, `type NotificationType` (deployment), `title`, `reasons Json?` (deployment type: `{label, detail?, at}[]`), `link?` (admin-relative), `dedupeKey?` (core-update, module-update:{id}, contact-form:messages), `readAt?` (null = unread, drives nav badge), `deployInitiatedAt?` (null = open deployment notification), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Indexes: (type, deployInitiatedAt), readAt, dedupeKey.
- `ModuleMigration` - `id`, `moduleName`, `migrationName`, `appliedAt`, `checksum` (sha256 of the SQL). Unique (moduleName, migrationName); index moduleName. Tracked separately from Prisma's own history.
- `DeployLock` - singleton: `id = "singleton"`, `lockedAt`, `lockedBy` (module or update identifier), `expiresAt` (TIMESTAMP(3), nullable). Prevents concurrent installs/updates. Every acquire/check site goes through `lib/deploy/lock.ts` - `acquireDeployLock()` to take it (stamping `expiresAt` = now + `DEFAULT_LOCK_HOLD_MS`, 90s, which covers every current caller since all of them release the lock before the build they trigger and all cap at `maxDuration 60`), `getActiveDeployLock()` to read it (a row past `expiresAt` - or, with no expiry, older than `STALE_LOCK_MS`, 15 min - is deleted-if-still-stale and reported as absent), `lockBusyMessage()` for the 409 body (names the remaining wait). Without the expiry a hard-killed function (Vercel timeout / OOM, which runs no release path) stranded the row for the full 15 minutes, so on a bad GitHub day every retry cost the owner another quarter hour.
- `GithubAppConnection` - `id`, `appId`, `appSlug`, `installationId?`, `installationAccount?`, `privateKeyEncrypted Text`, `webhookSecretEncrypted? Text`, `clientIdEncrypted? Text`, `clientSecretEncrypted? Text`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Secrets AES-256-GCM encrypted with ENCRYPTION_KEY.
- `Menu` - `id`, `name`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Relation: items.
- `MenuItem` - `id`, `menuId` → Menu (cascade), `parentId?` self-relation (cascade), `type MenuItemType`, `pageId?` → InfoPage (cascade), `label?`, `url?`, `moduleId?`, `entityKind?`, `entityId?` (MODULE_ENTITY target - no FK, module tables live outside Prisma, resolved via `core.menu-entity-provider`), `openInNewTab` (false), `visibility MenuItemVisibility` (default PUBLIC - per-item front-end audience gate, filtered in `lib/menu/resolve.ts` against the current viewer; hiding an item hides its subtree), `order Int`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Unique (menuId, pageId); indexes menuId, pageId.
- `RateLimit` - `id`, `key` (`ip:<addr>` | `account:<id>` | `account_email:<email>` | `consent:<id>`), `action`, `attempts Int default 1`, `windowStart`. Unique (key, action); index windowStart. In-database rate limiting with atomic INSERT … ON CONFLICT.
- `ConsentRecord` - append-only: `id`, `consentId`, `userId?` → User (SetNull), `categoriesVersion Int`, `decision Json`, `action` (accept_all | reject_all | custom | withdraw | acknowledge), `ipTruncated?`, `uaHash?`, `createdAt`. Indexes (consentId, createdAt), userId.
- `WebAuthnChallenge` - transient: `id`, `userId?`, `memberId?` (member passkey flows), `challenge` (unique), `purpose` (registration | authentication | member_registration | member_authentication), `expiresAt` (5 min), `createdAt`. Indexes userId, memberId, expiresAt.

Members system (all cuid PKs, all token/code columns store hashes only, every child table FKs `Member` with cascade delete; see MEMBERS_SPEC.md):

- `Member` - `id`, `email` (unique), `username` (unique, stored lowercase), `displayName?`, `fullName?` (the member's real-world name, edited on the account overview and read by the shop checkout - separate from `displayName`, which is the public handle a site may not even collect; no phone number alongside it, a number belongs to a delivery address), `avatarMediaId?` (Media id, no relation), `avatarChoice AvatarChoice` (GENERATED), `bio?`, `websiteUrl?`, `trusted` (false), `status MemberStatus` (PENDING_VERIFICATION), `roleId?` → Role (SetNull; assigned to the seeded "Members" role at registration, nullable for rows predating the field), `emailVerified` (false), `emailVerifiedAt?`, `backupEmail?`, `suspendedUntil?`, `suspensionReason?`, `suspensionNotified` (false), `deletionRequestedAt?`, `deletionScheduledAt?`, `deletionExportReady` (false), `usernameChangedAt?`, `previousUsername?`, `previousUsernameExpiresAt?`, `userId?` (unique → User, SetNull - set when the row is the member half of a staff account; see the admin-link entry at the top), `createdAt`, `updatedAt`. Indexes (memberId, purpose), expiresAt.

Unique (memberId, channel, category). One row per channel per category, so a member can be emailed about something and texted about it too.

- `MemberConsentRecord` - `consentType`, `granted`, `ipAddress?`, `userAgent?`. Indexes memberId, createdAt.
- `MemberDataExportRequest` - `status DataExportStatus` (PENDING), `mediaId?` (Media id, no relation), `expiresAt?` (48h download cut-off), `completedAt?`. Indexes memberId, status.

Absent row, or a null copy column, = use the default; reset-to-default nulls `subject`/`bodyHtml` rather than deleting the row, so the wrapper choice and on/off switch survive it. `wrapperLayoutId` is deliberately NOT a relation - a deleted wrapper falls back to the site default instead of cascading away someone's rewritten copy.

### Authentication

WebAuthn (passkeys):

- `@simplewebauthn/server` v13 in `lib/auth/passkey.ts`; browser side `@simplewebauthn/browser` loaded on demand.
- rpName "Cactus Foundation"; rpId = hostname of SITE_URL (hard-coded `localhost` in development); origin = SITE_URL. rpId cannot change once passkeys exist.
- Challenges persisted in `WebAuthnChallenge` with a 5-minute TTL, deleted on use or expiry; verify calls extract the challenge from the assertion's `clientDataJSON`.
- Registration uses a stable user handle (userId bytes) so Safari/iCloud Keychain retries do not conflict; `excludeCredentials` from existing passkeys; `residentKey: preferred`, `userVerification: required`, `requireUserVerification: true` (both registration and authentication). Member passkeys (`lib/members/passkey.ts`) now match this exactly.
- Passkeys store credentialId, COSE public key bytes, signature counter (updated on every authentication), transports, and a label derived from the user agent ("Chrome on macOS").
- Zero-passkey accounts have **no** register-and-login path (`register-login` was deleted): a fresh attestation proves someone holds *an* authenticator, not that they hold *the account*. They sign in by password + OTP, authenticator app, or recovery link, then enrol a passkey from Account → Security.
- `authenticate-options` (admin `/api/auth/passkey/authenticate-options` + member equivalent) always returns an unscoped challenge with empty `allowCredentials` (discoverable-credential flow), byte-identical regardless of whether the email maps to an account or has a passkey - so it can't be used to enumerate registered emails or harvest stored credential IDs.
- **Step-up on enrolment:** adding a new authenticator (passkey `register-options`+`register-verify`, TOTP/2FA `setup-options`, admin + member) requires the current session to have authenticated within `STEP_UP_MAX_AGE_MS` (10 min; `isCurrentSessionFresh` / `isCurrentMemberSessionFresh`, keyed on the session row's `createdAt`). A stale session gets a 403 with `reauthRequired: true`; the first-run setup window is exempt. Prevents a borrowed unlocked browser from planting a durable sign-in method.

Sessions:

- Cookie `cactus_session`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, 24-hour lifetime (`SESSION_DURATION_MS` in `lib/auth/session.ts`).
- Server stores only `sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)` in `Session.tokenHash`. Validation (`validateSessionWithMeta`): row lookup by hash, expiry check (expired rows deleted on touch), suspended-user check; returns `{ user, expiresAt }`. `validateSession` is a thin wrapper returning just the user.
- Server-side validation happens twice per admin request: in `proxy.ts` and again in the admin layout/route handlers via `getSessionFromCookie()`.
- `getSessionWithMeta()` is the React-`cache()`d cookie→session lookup; `getSessionFromCookie()` derives from it, so a render wanting both the user and the expiry still costs one query. `msUntilExpiry(expiresAt)` converts the expiry to a duration (kept out of component bodies - reading the clock mid-render trips `react-hooks/purity`).
- **Stale-tab sign-out:** an admin tab left open past the 24-hour limit used to keep showing the last-rendered screen until the next request bounced. `components/admin/SessionExpiryWatcher.tsx` (mounted by `AdminShell`, fed `sessionExpiresInMs` from the admin layout) now shows a corner warning banner 2 minutes out and then sends the tab to `/<adminPath>/login?next=<path>&expired=1`. `LoginForm` renders an `alert-info` notice on `?expired=1`. No polling and no extra requests - it is arithmetic against the browser's own clock, anchored at mount from a *duration* (not an absolute timestamp) so a badly-set client clock can't sign anyone out early. Timers re-arm in 15-minute chunks and recheck on `visibilitychange`/`focus`, because long timeouts are throttled in background tabs and stop entirely while a laptop sleeps. Deliberately a non-blocking banner, not a modal, so anyone mid-edit can still reach their save button.
- Trusted devices: cookie `cactus_trusted`, same hashing scheme, N days from `SiteConfig.trustDeviceDays` (default 28), expiry refreshed on valid use; lets password logins skip the email OTP.

Other mechanisms:

- Password login: bcrypt (12 rounds), minimum 8 chars, Pwned Passwords k-anonymity breach check (fails open); always second-factored by a 6-digit OTP (`EmailChallenge`, 10-minute TTL, 5 attempts, sha256-hashed, timing-safe compare) unless the device is trusted. Unavailable when email is not configured. The OTP goes by SMS instead of email when `User.smsOtpPhoneEncrypted` is set and an active module contributes a configured SMS provider (`lib/auth/sms.ts` `getActiveSmsProvider()` over the generated `lib/modules/sms-providers.ts`); any SMS failure falls back silently to email, verification unchanged (`/api/auth/email-code`). Login response gained `channel`/`destination` (masked phone) for the OTP-step copy.
- TOTP: otpauth SHA1/6-digit/30s, issuer "Cactus Foundation", secret AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest, ±1 window, replay-protected via monotonically increasing `totpLastStep`.
- Recovery: 32-byte token, sha256-hashed, 30-minute TTL, single-use; completion revokes all sessions and trusted devices. The emailed link's GET hands the token to the login page via a short-lived HttpOnly `cactus_recovery_token` cookie + `?recovery=1` flag (never `?recovery_token=` in the URL, which would leak into history/logs/Referer); the POST reads it from that cookie (body token still accepted for older links) and clears it on success.
- Password change (`/api/account/password`, `/api/members/password`): on any successful change, unconditionally revokes every other session and every trusted device/browser, keeping only the caller's session. The old opt-in `signOutOtherSessions` flag is ignored (still parsed for client compatibility). Stops a pre-existing trusted device from surviving the change and bypassing OTP/2FA.
- Rate limiting: in-database (`RateLimit` table), atomic check-and-record. Admin OTP verify (`/api/auth/email-code`) keys on both `ip:` and `account:${userId}` (was IP-only). Limits: login 10/15min, register 5/60min, recovery_request 3/60min, email_code 5/15min, passkey_authenticate 20/15min, consent 30/15min, totp_verify 5/15min, member_register 5/60min, member_magic_link 5/15min, member_login 10/15min, member_2fa 5/15min (Members system).
- Turnstile: applied to login, register, and recovery-request; fail-open when unconfigured, fail-closed on network error when configured.
- CSRF: SameSite=Lax cookie plus an explicit Origin-mismatch 403 for unsafe methods in `proxy.ts`.

Admin path obfuscation:

- The real admin URL prefix is a per-site secret string (`SiteConfig.adminPath`, unique, suggested as e.g. `lemon-x7k2p9`), resolved at the proxy from Edge Config or DB and rewritten to the internal `/cactus-admin/*` tree. Direct `/cactus-admin` access 404s; wrong prefixes fall through to a plain Next.js 404 indistinguishable from any missing route.
- What it hides: the location of the login page and admin UI from casual scanning.
- What it does not protect: it is not an authentication factor. All admin API routes under `/api/admin/*` sit at fixed, guessable URLs and rely entirely on session + permission checks; the admin path leaks to anyone with a valid session.

Members authentication (Phase 2 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md, protected/isolated-diff-per-sub-feature; fully separate from everything above - no shared tables, cookies, or code):

- Cookie `cactus_member_session`: httpOnly, SameSite=Lax, secure in production, sliding expiry off `membersConfig.sessionDays` (default 30d, refreshed on every valid check). Server stores `sha256(token + SESSION_SECRET)` in `MemberSession.tokenHash` (`lib/members/session.ts`), same hashing scheme as admin sessions.
- `validateMemberSession` only returns a member whose `status` is `ACTIVE` - PENDING_VERIFICATION/PENDING_APPROVAL/SUSPENDED/DELETED are all rejected even with an unexpired session row.
- Trusted browser: cookie `cactus_member_trusted`, same scheme, `membersConfig.trustedBrowserDays` (default 30d).
- Passkeys (`lib/members/passkey.ts`, `@simplewebauthn`, same rpId/origin as admin): login with an existing passkey (`/api/members/auth/passkey/authenticate-options`+`authenticate-verify`) and adding a passkey from an authenticated session (`register-options`+`register-verify`). No bootstrap-without-a-session path - see the Routes section note on why that would be unsafe for members specifically (no narrow one-time setup window the way admin has).
- Magic link (`lib/members/magic-link.ts`): 15-minute single-use emailed link, `/api/members/auth/magic-link/request`+`consume`. This is how a brand-new member gets their *first* session (they have no passkey yet and passwords are off by default) - hence it, not passkey, is what makes `/{memberAreaPath}/login` actually usable end-to-end.
- `loginRejectionForStatus` (`lib/members/registration.ts`) is the shared status gate every login method calls before creating a session: only ACTIVE passes; PENDING_VERIFICATION returns a `redirectToVerify` hint back to the Phase 1 holding page.
- Password + mandatory 2FA (`/api/members/auth/password/login` + `2fa/verify`): only reachable when `authMethodPolicies.PASSWORD` ≠ `OFF`; a password without a `MemberTwoFactor` row is treated as unusable (403) rather than allowing a password-only session, since 2FA is mandatory whenever passwords are on - actually setting up that first 2FA method is a Phase 3 Security-page action. Trusted browser (`isMemberBrowserTrusted`) skips the 2FA step entirely. A verified `SMS` method (phone in `MemberTwoFactor.phoneEncrypted`) takes priority over other methods when an active SMS provider module can deliver; SMS codes share the member email-challenge store (`login_2fa`), so `2fa/verify` treats EMAIL and SMS identically, and delivery falls back silently to email when the provider is unavailable. Factor selection (both `password/login` and `2fa/verify`) only ever picks a `verified` factor - an unverified row (secret generated but never confirmed) never gates login, and there is no unverified fallback. Recovery codes (`lib/members/recovery-codes.ts`) are an alternate second factor for a member who's lost their email/authenticator access.
- `/{memberAreaPath}/login` (`app/(public)/cactus-account/login/page.tsx` + `components/members/LoginForm.tsx`): identifier-first - email + "Continue", then only the methods that address has (`POST /api/members/auth/methods`): passkey, a password step branching into 2FA/recovery-code, and/or "email me a sign-in link" (link-only addresses skip the choice and have the link sent on Continue); auto-consumes a `?magic_token=` on load; `?redirect=` is sanitised to same-origin relative paths only (open-redirect guard) - set by the account layout's session gate and by the shop's gated `/shop/account/*` pages, and additionally dropped when it points back at a signed-out member page (loop guard, see the Pages section).
- Logout: `POST /api/members/auth/logout` (single, redirects `/logged-out`) and `POST /api/members/auth/logout-all` (every session, forces full re-auth - unlike admin's "revoke all" which preserves the caller's own).
- **Phase 2 (Authentication) is now fully built.** Phase 3 (member account area) is also complete - see the Member account API and member-area Pages entries above. Next up: Phase 4 (public profile).

### Permissions System

Core keys (registered by `seedCorePermissions()` in `lib/permissions/check.ts` at setup):

- `pages.read` - view info pages including drafts (admin page list, page GET/history APIs, page-preview route).
- `pages.write` - create/edit pages (POST/PATCH/autosave).
- `pages.publish` - publish pages (publish endpoint; also required to create a page already published).
- `pages.delete` - delete pages (single + bulk).
- `users.manage` - view and manage users (users page + API).
- `media.upload` - upload media.
- `media.delete` - delete media.
- `roles.manage` - Settings → Users → Roles subtab + role/permission APIs.
- `modules.manage` - module list/install/update/uninstall/directory; also grants GitHub App status read.
- `config.manage` - settings GET/PATCH, notifications, updates, media migration, redeploy dismiss, deployment logs, GitHub App flow.
- `menus.manage` - all menu APIs; also gates menu assignment from the page editor.
- `appearance.manage` - design-token PATCH.
- `layouts.manage` - layout read/create/update/delete/publish, and `/layout-preview/[id]`. Every layout route gates on it, reads included.
- `sms.templates` - the text message templates API (`/api/admin/sms/templates*`) and, through it, the Twilio settings tab's Templates sub-tab. Kept apart from `emails.templates` on purpose: a text costs money per send.
- `members.manage` / `members.list` / `members.view` / `members.edit` / `members.suspend` / `members.delete` / `members.invite` / `members.approve` / `members.trust` / `members.notes` / `members.settings` / `members.gdpr` - Members system admin permissions (registered in Phase 0; enforcing routes/UI land in later Members phases - see MEMBERS_SPEC.md).

Module-registered keys (declared in each module's `cactus.module.json`, registered on install): `contact.view`, `contact.reply`, `contact.delete`, `contact.export` (contact-form); `replycatcher.manage` (contact-form-reply-catcher); `boards.access`, `boards.manage`, `boards.moderate` (boards); `directory.access`, `directory.manage` (directory); `gazette.access`, `gazette.contributor`, `gazette.author`, `gazette.editor` (gazette); `shop.access`, `shop.manage`, `shop.products`, `shop.orders`, `shop.customers`, `shop.discounts`, `shop.reports` (shop); `twilio.manage` (twilio); `googlesheets.manage` (google-sheet-products-for-shop, built but not yet registered). Stored in `Permission` with `module` set; deleted on module uninstall.

Where checks occur:

- Protected roles (`Role.isProtected`, only "Admin" is seeded) bypass every check (`hasPermission` short-circuits; `isAdmin()` = `role.isProtected`).
- `proxy.ts`: session validity only (plus `isProtected` for the site-status bypass and the redeploy trap); no per-permission checks.
- API routes: `getSessionFromCookie()` + `hasPermission(user, key)` per handler (see the Routes section for each route's key).
- UI: server components branch on `hasPermission`/`isAdmin` (page buttons, nav module entries via manifest `permission`); client editors fetch `/api/admin/pages/perms` for capability flags.
- Cross-cutting guards: `assertProtectedUserWouldRemain` (transactional last-admin invariant on delete/demote/self-delete), `canActOnUser` (only admins act on protected-role users).

### Admin UI

Navigation (defined in `components/admin/AdminNav.tsx`): Dashboard; Inbox (conditional - see below); then any ungrouped module nav entries (no `navGroupLabel` - after the 2026-08-10 sidebar tidy this is where most single-link modules land: Gazette, Boards, SEO, Space Planner, Search-less modules and so on); Content → Pages, Menus, Media (+ Directory); System → Users, Styles, Layouts, Modules, Settings; then labelled module nav groups (own named section - only Shop still uses one, for Catalogue + Sales); footer: My Account, Sign out, version.

**Sidebar tidy, 2026-08-10.** With every module installed the rail carried 48 links; it now carries 17 - core's own 10 (its 9, plus the new conditional Inbox) and 7 from modules, down from 39. The rule applied throughout: **one sidebar link per module wherever the surfaces are related, with everything else a tab on that page**, and anything that is really configuration living as a tab under Settings. Nothing was deleted - every retired route still exists and `redirect()`s to wherever its screen now lives, so bookmarks and older links keep working. What moved:

- **Core**: new conditional `inbox` item (id `inbox`, path `/inbox`) - the first `conditional: true` entry in `CORE_NAV_ITEMS`. A conditional item is dropped from both `resolveAdminMenu` and `resolveAdminMenuForEditor` unless the caller passes its id in `availableCoreItemIds`; passing nothing means "nothing available", so a missed call site hides a link rather than advertising a dead one. `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx` adds `inbox` when an installed manifest publishes into `core.inbox-tabs` **and** this role holds at least one contributor's permission; `config/page.tsx` adds it (unfiltered by permission, like the rest of the Navigation editor) whenever any manifest publishes into it.
- **Core**: `users` item's `defaultPermissions` widened from `['users.manage']` to `['users.manage', 'members.settings', 'roles.manage']`, because Roles and the member settings moved onto that page and a role holding only one of those keys would otherwise have lost them.
- **gazette** 6 links → 1, **boards** 4 → 1, **space-planner-for-shop** 4 → 1, **ultimate-seo** 4 → 1 (the first two already rendered their own cross-page `TabStrip`, so only the manifest changed; the other two gained `SpacePlannerNav.tsx` / `SeoNav.tsx` on the same pattern). Each dropped `navGroupLabel` too - a labelled section holding one link is noise.
- **contact-form** and **live-chat** both lost their link to the new core Inbox (see `core.inbox-tabs`). live-chat also dropped its `contact-form.inbox-actions` entry and `InboxLinkButton.tsx` - a button linking from one inbox to the other is pointless once they are tabs of the same screen.
- **gemini-watermark-remover** lost its link to a tab on core Media (see `core.media-tabs`).
- **search** and **twilio** lost their links into their own existing Settings tabs (a new "Index & searches" sub-tab on Settings > Search; a new "Calls & texts" sub-tab on Settings > Twilio).
- **shop** 9 links → 2 (**Catalogue** at `/m/shop/products`, **Sales** at `/m/shop/orders`), and its five companion modules lost theirs entirely - see the Shop module section.
- **Settings > Users** tab folded into the Users page (see below). Sidebar collapses to a rail (auto-collapses inside Puck editors), mobile drawer with backdrop; toolbar has collapse toggle, ThemeToggle, NotificationBell. When collapsed, each icon link shows a custom hover/focus tooltip to its right (label text) instead of the native `title`: a `createPortal`-to-`<body>` fixed-positioned `.admin-nav-tip` (visuals match `.theme-toggle-tip`), because the nav scroll container's `overflow-x: hidden` would clip a pure-CSS tooltip; collapsed links also carry `aria-label` for the accessible name. Each labelled section is independently collapsible (click the label, chevron flips) - state persisted per-label in `localStorage` (`cactus-sidebar-sections-collapsed`), defaults to all sections maximised; only visible when the rail itself isn't collapsed. There is no standalone Members section, People section, or Roles link any more (all removed in an admin-UI reorganisation - see below and the top-of-file changelog); Users lives in System now.

**Sidebar is now server-resolved (2026-07-15).** The hardcoded `NAV_SECTIONS` array is gone; `AdminNav` renders a `sections` prop the server layout builds via `resolveAdminMenu` (`lib/nav/admin-menu.ts`) from core items + module groups + the saved `SiteConfig.adminMenuConfig` + this user's permissions. Core items each declare a stable id and any-of default permission keys (`pages.read`, `users.manage`, …) so a role that can't use a screen no longer sees its menu item; `isProtected` admins bypass all visibility (seeing hidden/restricted items with a small lock/eye-off badge) so they can't hide the editor from themselves. Client UX added in `AdminNav`: a filter box, a Favourites pinned group + Recently-visited group (both `localStorage`), a per-item route-change loading spinner, roving Up/Down keyboard nav, auto-expand of the active section + scroll-into-view, a Quick "New…" create menu (deep-links collected from visible items), expand/collapse-all, and empty-section hiding. `AdminShell` mounts `CommandPalette` (Cmd/Ctrl+K fuzzy jump over all destinations; `?` opens a shortcuts overlay; also openable from a new sidebar-toolbar search button). The menu builder itself is the Settings → Navigation tab (see Settings tabs + `NavBuilder.tsx`).

Members/Roles/Users admin surface has been consolidated (previously a permission-filtered **Members** sidebar section per Phase 5 of MEMBERS_SPEC.md, plus a standalone `/cactus-admin/roles` page) - the section/page are gone; every permission gate that used to guard a nav entry now guards a tab instead:

- `app/cactus-admin/page.tsx` (main dashboard) - the former Members Overview counts (total/active/pending-verification/pending-approval/suspended/scheduled-for-deletion) now render as extra stat tiles alongside Pages/Users/Media, queried only when the viewer holds `members.list`.
- `app/cactus-admin/users/page.tsx` - a server component reading `?tab=` (href-based `TabStrip`, default = the first tab this role may open): **Users** (`PeopleListClient.tsx`, unified staff+member table, gated `users.manage`), **Pending Approval** (`PendingApprovalClient.tsx`, gated `members.approve`), **Invites** (`InvitesClient.tsx`, gated `members.invite`), **Roles** (gated `roles.manage`) and **Settings** (gated `members.settings`, a second row of five `?sub=` links - Registration / Avatars / Usernames / Account sections / Access control - feeding `MembersSettingsTab.tsx`). Roles and Settings arrived here from Settings on 2026-08-10; the roles query and the `core.roles-page` extension resolution moved with them out of `config/page.tsx` into a `RolesTab` server component on this page. The page gate is no longer `users.manage` alone - it now admits any of `users.manage` / `members.settings` / `roles.manage` and gates each tab separately, since a role with only `roles.manage` would otherwise have been locked out of the editor it moved to. `/config?tab=users` and the old `?sub=registration|avatars|usernames|sections|access|roles` deep links `redirect()` here. The former standalone **Members** tab was merged into Users (`MembersListClient.tsx` deleted) - a Member row's Type badge/Role-or-status column comes from the same `GET /api/admin/people` call as staff rows. `lib/members/admin-notify.ts`'s pending-approval alert links to `/users?tab=pending-approval`.
- `app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx` (Settings) - GDPR & Legal tab gained `MembersGdprClient.tsx` (was `members/gdpr/GdprClient.tsx`) rendered inline at the bottom, gated `members.gdpr`, showing the same pending-deletions/exports/consent/processing-log content plus any `members.gdpr-entry` extension contributions. A **Users** tab (only shown when the viewer holds `members.settings` or `roles.manage`) holds Registration/Avatars/Usernames/Account sections/Access control (`MembersSettingsTab.tsx`) and Roles (`RolesClient.tsx`) as state-driven subtabs, each only shown/rendered when its own permission is held. The **Email** tab gained its own two subtabs - Delivery (from name/address, Brevo/SMTP credentials, test send: everything that was on it before) and Templates (`EmailTemplatesClient.tsx`, gated `emails.templates`) - and the page-level Save button stands down on Templates, which saves each email itself - see the Admin UI section below for the current subtab layout.
- `app/cactus-admin/members/` now holds only `[id]/` (`MemberDetailClient.tsx` - edit profile, status actions, sessions, reset-password, export-trigger, append-only notes, action log, admin delete, `members.admin-member-detail` extension point) - unchanged.

No permission keys, API routes, or DB schema changed in this reorganisation - every `members.*`/`roles.manage` check still gates exactly what it used to, just relocated.

Pages and routes: listed in the Routes section above.

Settings tabs (`/cactus-admin/config`):

- General: siteName, tagline, description, homepageId, mainMenuId, timezone (9 options), dateFormat, timeFormat, adminPath, trustDeviceDays (1–365); core-updates panel (channel toggle, check, update-now with optional module bundling); Danger zone (Reset Database soft/hard, Reset Everything for Vercel env vars). (Refresh Starter Templates button removed - starter templates auto-refresh after core updates via `ensureStarterLayoutsCurrent`.)
- Branding: logo (+dark), a one-shot **App icon** source upload that auto-generates favicon/apple/PWA icons, per-slot overrides, and app name/short-name/theme+background colour fields (`BrandingImageField` + inline inputs in `ConfigPageClient.tsx` - preview/replace/remove, posts to `/api/admin/media`, stores returned ids on the matching `config.*MediaId`, persisted by the top "Save changes"). App-icon flow: `handleAppIconUploaded` stores the source then POSTs `{sourceMediaId}` to `POST /api/admin/branding/generate-icons` (`media.upload`; sharp resizes to favicon 96 / apple-touch 180 opaque-white / PWA 192 / 512, stores each via `uploadMedia`+`saveMediaRecord`, returns ids+urls) and drops them into `faviconMediaId`/`appleTouchIconMediaId`/`webManifest192MediaId`/`webManifest512MediaId` (each still hand-replaceable). Favicon/icon/app-name metadata now resolved site-wide at the root layout + `app/manifest.ts` (see `app/layout.tsx`), not in `app/(public)/layout.tsx` (its favicon `generateMetadata` was removed). Dark logo swaps in on the frontend via CSS `img[data-logo-variant]` rules in `globals.css` keyed on `data-theme`; dark favicon is emitted as a second `prefers-color-scheme: dark` icon. All dark + app-icon fields optional. Gated on real media state (`config.mediaProvider` set AND `envKeysForProvider(provider).every(k => envStatus[k])`, mirroring the server upload gate); shows the "configure a media provider first" note only when that gate is false. Accepts JPEG/PNG/WebP/GIF/SVG (server `ALLOWED_TYPES` in `lib/media/upload.ts`). This branding UI actually now lives in `BrandingTab.tsx` under `/appearance/styles`, not `ConfigPageClient.tsx`. Object-key extension for an upload is derived from its MIME subtype (`extensionForMimeType`, `lib/media/upload.ts`) with the `+xml`/`+json` RFC 6839 suffix stripped - a raw split previously produced keys like `…-favicon.svg+xml`, and the literal `+` broke the Cloudflare Worker's B2 fetch/signing (confirmed 502 in production; plain-extension PNGs served fine). `BrandingImageField` previews now show an inline "Image not found" state (`onError` on the `<img>`) instead of a broken-image icon when a stored file can't load. Below the icon upload fields, `IconPreviewGallery` renders illustrative mock-ups (browser tab, iPhone/Android home screen, installed-app splash) built from whichever icons are currently staged, so a non-technical owner can see where each generated size actually shows up. Logo field only (`allowOptimise` prop): an **Optimise** button `POST`s `config.logoMediaId` to `/api/admin/media/optimise` and, on success, swaps the logo to the returned lighter media id + shows a `240 KB → 38 KB (84% smaller)` note (`formatBytes` helper); "already about as small as it gets" when no gain.
- Email: emailFromName, emailFromAddress; Brevo/SMTP credential cards writing to Vercel env vars.
- Media: provider select (grouped Proxied/Direct, saved immediately), per-provider env-var checklist + CLOUDFLARE_WORKER_URL for proxied, per-provider media breakdown, client-driven migration with progress/cancel/retry; then a Delivery checkbox `lazyLoadImages` ("Load images only as visitors scroll to them", default on, anchor id `media-lazy-load`) which unlike the provider select saves via the page's normal Save button/fingerprint.
- Site Status: status select (live/comingSoon/maintenance), hideFromCrawlers, link to statusPage layouts.
- GDPR & Legal: privacyPolicyPageId, termsPageId, privacy-generator link, sessionPurgeAfterDays, recoveryPurgeAfterDays, cookie-consent banner editor (enable, style, copy fields, category table with pinned "necessary", module-suggested categories, reConsentDays, consentLogRetentionDays, categoriesVersion display); below all of that, if the viewer holds `members.gdpr`, `MembersGdprClient.tsx` renders Members-specific GDPR data (pending deletions, exports, consent records, processing log) plus `members.gdpr-entry` extension contributions.
- Integrations: GitHub App connect/install/disconnect card; env-var cards for Edge Config, Turnstile, Vercel webhook, Sentry, Neon.
- ~~Users~~ **(gone from Settings as of 2026-08-10 - moved to `/cactus-admin/users`; see the Users page bullet above. `/config?tab=users` redirects.)** For history, what it held: a second, state-driven `TabStrip`, defaulting to the first subtab the viewer can see. The old wrapping "Members" subtab is gone - `MembersSettingsTab.tsx` no longer owns its own nested `TabStrip`; instead it takes the active subtab as a `tab` prop (`MembersSettingsTabKey`), and its five subtabs (Registration, Avatars, Usernames, Account sections, Access control - all gated `members.settings`; Access control now carries one Off/Optional/Required select per sign-in method in place of the old checkbox list plus separate "enable password sign-in" tick, with an inline error while every method is off and a warning while the email sign-in link is off - see `lib/members/auth-policy.ts`) are promoted to sit directly in the outer `TabStrip`, in the slot the single "Members" tab used to occupy (i.e. before Roles/Email templates). Roles (`RolesClient.tsx`, gated `roles.manage`, same role picker + permission matrix as the former standalone `/cactus-admin/roles` page, `core.roles-page` extension point still rendered beneath it). The Email templates subtab moved off this tab entirely - see the Email tab.
- Navigation (conditional - only when the viewer holds `config.manage`): the admin-sidebar menu builder (`NavBuilder.tsx`). Lists every menu item - core and every module link, unfiltered by permission - grouped by section; ↑/↓ reorder items and sections, inline rename (blank = default label), and a per-item visibility select (Default / Everyone / Admins only / Chosen roles + role checkboxes / Hidden). Saves the whole customisation to `SiteConfig.adminMenuConfig` via `PUT /api/admin/navigation` then `router.refresh()`es so the live sidebar updates at once; "Reset to defaults" (two-click) clears it via a full-reload. Fed server-side by `resolveAdminMenuForEditor` + a lightweight roles list in `config/page.tsx`. Administrators always keep access regardless of any rule.
- Module tabs: rendered generically, appended after the core tabs (and after Users, when shown), one per `settingsTabs` entry in an active module's manifest (permission-filtered server-side, same gating as `navEntries`). Currently: `contact-form-reply-catcher` ("Reply Catcher", tab id `contact-form-reply-catcher`) - mailbox provider (IMAP/Outlook OAuth), credentials, folder overrides, last-poll status, check-now, OAuth connect; `gazette` ("Gazette", tab id `gazette`, `GazetteSettingsTab.tsx`) - posts-per-page, RSS feed title/description, comments (enable/visibility/moderation/threading), reactions (enable + emoji set), with the WordPress/Medium/Substack import wizard appended below as its own section, replacing the former standalone `/cactus-admin/m/gazette/settings` and `/cactus-admin/m/gazette/import` pages.
- Hosted settings panels (`host` on a `settingsTabs` entry): a `settingsTabs` entry that sets `host: "<slot-name>"` is **not** a top-level Settings tab. `app/cactus-admin/config/page.tsx` resolves and renders it server-side (via `moduleSettingsTabComponents`) into **two shapes** (both defined in `lib/modules/hosted-settings.ts`), passed through `ConfigPageClient` to each module settings tab: `hostedSettingsSlots: Record<slot, ReactNode>` (the panels for a slot merged into one node - for a host that just drops them into a section of its own UI) and `hostedSettingsPanels: Record<slot, {id, label, node}[]>` (the same panels kept separate, each still carrying its manifest `id`/`label` - for a host that gives each panel its own tab, which needs the label up front). A host takes whichever it needs; both are always passed. `host` is now declared in the manifest zod schema (`lib/modules/manifest.ts`, optional). `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx` skips `host`-ed tabs when building the command-palette `moduleSettingsTabs` list (no `/config?tab=` destination exists). Live uses: gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop's "Instant Bank Pay", square-payment-for-shop's "Square" and crezco-direct-bank-payments-for-shop's "Crezco Bank Payments" panels set `host: "shop.payments"` - taken as the **labelled** shape since shop 0.1.174, so each one gets its own chip on **admin > Shop > Payments** beside the built-in methods rather than being merged below the Stripe/PayPal cards; product-3d-views-for-shop's "3D Viewer", google-sheet-products-for-shop's "Google Sheet" and product-attributes-for-shop's "Product attributes" panels set `host: "shop.settings-sub-tabs"` (labelled shape), each rendering as its own sub-tab in **admin > Shop** (product-attributes moved there from a top-level Settings tab in 0.1.36). Both slot names are owned/rendered by the shop module (`modules/shop/components/admin/ShopSettingsTab.tsx`); core stays module-agnostic. An empty slot renders nothing, so a shop with no add-ons installed shows no extra tab.

Settings keys stored in the database = the SiteConfig columns (types and defaults listed in the Database Schema section). `designTokens` (Json) holds the v2 design-token object (defaults in `lib/design/tokens.ts:DEFAULT_DESIGN_TOKENS`: primary #2c7558/#459578, secondary white/#0f172a, system-ui font, heading sizes 2.5rem→1rem, link colours, status accents info #3b82f6 / success #16a34a / warning #f59e0b / error #ef4444 with brighter dark siblings, blockPadding 1.5rem, tabletBreakpoint 1024px, mobileBreakpoint 640px). `consentBannerConfig` (Json) holds `ConsentBannerConfig` (defaults in `lib/consent/types.ts`: disabled, bottom-bar, four categories necessary/preferences/analytics/marketing, `showPrivacyPagePanel` true, reConsentDays 365, retention null, versions 0).

Client-side storage keys used by the admin: `localStorage cactus-theme`, `localStorage cactus-sidebar-collapsed`, `localStorage cactus-sidebar-sections-collapsed`, `localStorage cactus-sidebar-favourites`, `localStorage cactus-sidebar-recents`, `sessionStorage cactus-core-update-check`, `sessionStorage cactus-module-update-check-<id>` (both 10-minute throttles).

Credentials/env vars are never stored in the database; they are written to Vercel project env vars via `/api/admin/env` (read-only display in local mode).

### Puck Integration

- Library: `@puckeditor/core` ^0.22. Editor components (`<Puck>`) are client-only, lazy-loaded with `ssr: false`; public rendering uses `<Render>` from `@puckeditor/core/rsc`.
- **Custom field widgets reach `config.tsx` through a registry, never a direct import** (`lib/puck/fields/registry.tsx` + `lib/puck/fields/editor.ts`). The 14 sidebar widgets are all `'use client'` and `ResponsiveValueField` imports the Puck editor entrypoint, so importing one from `config.tsx` (which has no `'use client'`) opens a client boundary in the RSC graph and drags the whole editor, plus its vendored TipTap/ProseMirror, into every public page's bundle. `registry.tsx` exports server-safe proxies typed via `import type` (erased, no runtime edge); `editor.ts` (`'use client'`) holds the only real imports and is imported solely by `PuckEditor.tsx` / `LayoutPuckEditor.tsx`, which call `registerEditorFields()` at module scope. The same registry also carries the RichTextBlock `renderMenu` renderer (`RichTextMenuWithLink`), not just sidebar field widgets, for the same bundle-isolation reason - it imports the Puck editor runtime. `lib/puck/fields/registry.test.ts` fails if the two lists drift or if anyone reinstates a direct import - without it a missing registration renders the field as nothing, silently.
- Central config: `lib/puck/config.tsx` (safe for both editor and RSC paths; no hooks/browser APIs). Exports: `puckConfig` (default, full-page editor), `puckRscConfig`, `footerPuckConfig(+Rsc)`, `layoutPuckConfig(+Rsc)` (adds `ContentSlot`), `headerPuckConfig(+Rsc)`, `fullPagePuckConfig(+Rsc)` (aliases of puckConfig). RSC variants swap `SiteLogo` to an RSC renderer and replace the `richtext` field type with textarea (TipTap JSON is converted to HTML via `@tiptap/html` for RSC rendering).
- Root ("nothing selected") fields, right sidebar: `puckConfig.root` (pages) and `headerPuckConfig.root`/`footerPuckConfig.root` define real fields, rendered via each config's own `root.render`. `puckConfig.root` gained `bg` (`PageBgColorField`, none/colour) and `paddingY` (none/sm/md/lg, padding above the first Section and below the last) - deliberately no page-level `maxWidth`, since every `Section` already owns its own maxWidth/full-bleed background and a shared root wrapper would clip it. `layoutPuckConfig.root` and `getModuleLayoutPuckConfig(type).root` still define no fields, so Puck falls back to its built-in `{title: text}` root field (`@puckeditor/core`'s `defaultPageFields`) - which would duplicate the Title/Name field our own Settings tab already owns, so `LayoutPuckEditor.tsx` passes `overrides={{fields: hideRootFieldsOverride}}` (`lib/puck/tabs/rootFieldsOverride.tsx`) whenever the active config has no `root.fields`, hiding just the field body (Puck always renders the "Page" breadcrumb header regardless). `PuckEditor.tsx` (pages) needs no such override since `puckConfig.root.fields` is always real.
- Core blocks by category - Layout: Section (background/overlay/padding/max-width/sticky/border/shadow/opacity + slot; `bgType: 'grid-scan'` renders a decorative graph-paper grid + looping scan-beam sweep behind nested content, purely cosmetic; **outer `overflow` is now conditional** - only `hidden` when the section actually clips to an edged box (borderRadius≠none, bg image, overlay scrim, boxShadow, grid-scan), otherwise `visible` so a `position:sticky` descendant - e.g. a sticky image column inside a nested Grid - isn't trapped by an overflow context it doesn't need), Grid2/Grid3/Grid4 (fixed-column-count variants, ratios, per-column align/width, `stackColumns` mobile|tablet|never - `GridBlock` derives a `stackMode` from it (falling back to the legacy `stackAtTablet:'on'`→tablet, else `mobile` for a normal grid / `never` for one already managing its own per-breakpoint columns) and emits `data-stack="<mode>"` on every grid; `buildTokenStyles` keys the collapse rules off it - `mobile` stacks to one column at the mobile breakpoint (with the 3/4→2-col tablet step), `tablet` stacks across the whole tablet band and below, `never` holds the columns at every width. The stack rules outrank a grid's own scoped `[data-grid-id]` override, so an explicit stack choice stacks even a Manual-width grid. Per-column widths (`col{n}Width`) now only apply in Manual `columnSizes` mode (per breakpoint), so switching the preset back to Equal drops stale custom widths immediately instead of a lingering width silently winning, per-column `col{n}Sticky` off|on + `col{n}StickyOffset` - `on` pins that column's grid track (`position:sticky`, `top:offset`, `align-self:start` so the box stays content-height inside the full-height row and has room to travel) while the taller sibling scrolls; the track carries `data-col-sticky` and the block emits media rules dropping it back to `position:static` once the grid stacks (per `stackMode`: mobile band when `mobile`/`tablet`, plus the tablet band when `tablet`; never when `never`), so a pinned image just sits in normal flow on small screens. NB the sticky must live on the track div itself, not a nested block wrapped in a Section: the per-block visibility/slot wrapper between the track and a nested block is content-height, which caps a sticky descendant's travel to zero, per-column "scale to width" (wraps that column's content in `lib/puck/components/ScaleToFit.tsx` - a client component that measures natural size + applies `transform:scale(min(1,colWidth/naturalWidth))` so any content, incl. fixed-size icon widgets like ThemeToggle/cart, shrinks to fit; transform-origin follows `col*Align`) - **no longer its own field**: `GridBlock` derives it (`colScaled`) from whether that column's `col*WidthShrunk` has a value, since a column's rendered width only ever changes at runtime via the shrink-on-scroll override; the standalone `col*Scale` radio (Grid2/3/4 and the legacy dynamic `Grid`) was removed, 2/3/4 slots respectively - split from a single dynamic "Grid" so Puck's Outline panel only ever lists the slots that variant actually has; legacy dynamic `Grid` stays registered as a safety net but is unlisted in every picker), Group (flex row/column + slot; gained `columns` responsive select auto|1-6 (`ResponsiveSelectField`) - `auto`/blank keeps the default flex-wrap flow (every legacy Group byte-identical), a number switches the slot wrapper to an equal-width CSS grid `repeat(N, minmax(0,1fr))` that reflows per breakpoint via `responsiveMediaCssFor` on the same `.group-rsp-<id>` class, so an arbitrary child count sits N-per-row and can differ desktop/tablet/mobile (e.g. 3/2/1) - the flow the fixed-track Grid2/3/4 can't do since they cap at 4 one-child tracks and orphan the odd item when a 3-track grid drops to 2 at tablet; grid branch skips the header-centring `nth-child` style), Split (**RETIRED 2026-08-15** - still registered in every config so existing data renders and edits unchanged, but removed from all three `categories` pickers and named in the `disallow` of every core slot field, because a Split inside a slot publishes two empty columns; use Grid2 `columnSizes: '70-30'` instead - see the Last updated note; ratio columns, legacy zones/DropZone API not slot fields; `ratio` gained an `auto` option 2026-07-16 - `grid-template-columns: fit-content(60%) 1fr`, sizing the left track to whatever width its content actually declares and giving the slack to the right, capped at 60% so a greedy left column can't starve the right one and floored at its min-content. Only content with a *definite* width has anything to hug - a left column of ordinary prose has no natural width and simply takes the 60%. First consumer: shop's Default Product Detail starter, whose square gallery sizes itself against the viewport height and so wants a column that hugs the photo rather than centring it in a fixed fraction), Spacer, Divider. Typography: Heading (gained `revealAnimation: 'none'|'stagger-lines'` - splits `text` on `\n` into per-line clipped spans that rise in on mount, independent of the existing scroll-triggered `aosFields` also on this block; `text` field is `textarea` to allow multi-line entry; `level` gained a `display` option - the largest level, above h2, renders as a real `<h1>` with a `cactus-display` class, styled from `themeStyle.display` tokens; also gained `highlightText` + `highlightMark` - `highlightText` is a substring that gets recoloured in `--color-primary` and wrapped in a non-italic `<em>`, and when `highlightMark: 'underline'` also carries a chunky mustard bar sitting UNDER the word (a thick `text-decoration: underline`, 0.16em / `skip-ink: none` / small offset - deliberately under the glyphs not behind them, and a solid `--color-heading-mark` token / `#E3A857` fallback rather than a translucent one so a tinted hero background can't bleed through and turn it olive) (works inside `stagger-lines` too, applied per line via the shared `renderHighlight` helper); also gained a swatch/manual colour picker (`color` is now `SiteColourField allowManual` - swatch/custom/None/typed CSS colour, legacy `dark`/`muted`/`brand` still resolve, empty = per-level heading token), whole-heading linking (`href` wraps the tag in a colour-inheriting block `<a data-heading-link>`), an optional hover underline on linked headings (`hoverUnderline` yes/no + `hoverUnderlineColor` swatch, scoped `<style>` on the id, defaults to `currentColor`), and vertical positioning (`minHeight` none/sm 240/md 400/lg 600/screen 100vh + `verticalAlign` top/middle/bottom - a set height makes the wrapper a flex column and drops the tag's bottom margin so centring is true); also gained `fitOneLine` ("Keep on one line (shrink text to fit)", no/yes, default no) - wraps the heading's content in `lib/puck/components/HeadingFitText.tsx`, a client component that measures the text's natural one-line width against the room the heading has and scales it down to fit, bringing the box height down with it; the Menu block's `fitOneLine` trick, see the dated notes at the top), TextBlock (gained `size` base/md/lg, `maxWidth` none/prose 46ch/wide 60ch and `color` secondary/muted/dark - defaults preserve the old full-width secondary-colour 1rem look; used together they turn a plain paragraph into a constrained "lede" that wraps to multiple lines like the concept), RichTextBlock (TipTap), Quote (quote/attribution/padding + optional photo; the photo is now rendered INSIDE the `<blockquote>` - first child of a flex row that also holds the text, so it sits between the left accent border and the quote - where it used to be a sibling `<img>` to the left of the whole panel, outside it. `imageSize` sets the photo's width (sm 72 / md 112 / lg 160), new `imageHeight` number field overrides its height in px (blank or 0 = square, i.e. the old behaviour; a circle shape with an unequal height renders as an ellipse, which is the point of asking), `imageShape` circle/rounded/square. All photo fields stay hidden by `resolveFields` until `mediaUrl` is set), Caption (text/align/padding, styled from `themeStyle.caption` tokens via a `cactus-caption` class - small label/footnote text usable anywhere, not just form-field labels). Actions: ButtonLink (label/href/variant/align/padding, plus six Custom-only props; 2026-07-14: `variant` gained a fourth option `custom` alongside primary/secondary/outline. The three presets take their colours from the Styles → Buttons design tokens; `custom` ignores those and paints from the block's own `bgColor`/`textColor`/`hoverBgColor`/`hoverTextColor` (each a `SiteColourField` - palette swatches + native colour picker + free-text CSS colour) and `borderWidth` (`BUTTON_BORDER_OPTIONS`: none/1px/2px/3px/4px) with `borderColor`. Any custom colour left blank falls back to the matching primary token, so a freshly-switched custom button is identical to the primary it came from; a border width chosen with no colour picked paints `currentColor`, never transparent. `resolveFields` strips all six colour/border props unless `variant === 'custom'`, and strips `borderColor` until a width is picked, so only applicable options show. Hover for `custom` is a block-scoped `a[data-btn-link="<id>"]:hover{…!important}` rule emitted by the block itself - the global hover rules in `lib/design/tokens.ts` are keyed on `[data-variant="primary"|"secondary"|"outline"]` and deliberately never match `custom`; `!important` beats the inline base style, same reason those rules carry it. `align` (2026-07-14) is a responsive select (`ResponsiveSelectField`, left/center/right) emitting `text-align` on the wrapper `div[data-btn-id]` via `responsiveMediaCssFor`, with the `<a>` staying `display:inline-block`; blank resolves to `inherit`, which for an inherited property is the same as declaring nothing, so buttons saved before the field existed keep taking their container's alignment rather than being yanked left), Phone (2026-07-15, `PhoneBlock` - click-to-call number. Registered in `puckConfig` (page/infopage), `layoutPuckConfig` (infoPage + generic layouts, in the `actions` category), `headerPuckConfig` (`actions` category) and `footerPuckConfig` (`site` category, `noGutterDefault`) - so it appears in the page/infopage editor and in every layout-editor type (header/footer/infoPage/statusPage/generic), not just the plain layout config. RSC parity automatic via the shared render + the `...components` spreads in `puckRscConfig`/`layoutPuckRscConfig`/`headerPuckRscConfig`/`footerPuckRscConfig`. `number` free-text (kept legible with spaces/brackets) is stripped to `[\d+]` with a single leading `+` for the `tel:` href; optional `label` overrides the displayed text (blank shows the number). `showIcon` none|mobile|always injects an inline phone SVG - `mobile` hides it by default and un-hides under `mobileMediaQuery()` via a block-scoped `[data-phone-id]` style. `mobileIconOnly` no|yes (2026-07-15): when the icon shows on phones, drops the number text under `mobileMediaQuery()` (a `[data-phone-text]{display:none}` rule) so only the dial glyph remains on mobile - the `<a>`'s `aria-label` still carries the number so taps and screen readers keep it; hidden by `resolveFields` unless `showIcon` puts an icon on mobile. Full typography set to recreate a heading-styled number: `align` responsive select, `size` sm/base/md/lg/xl/xxl (`PHONE_SIZE_MAP`), `weight` normal/medium/semibold/bold (`PHONE_WEIGHT_MAP`), `transform` none/uppercase/capitalize/lowercase, `letterSpacing` (`UnitValueField` em/px), `fontFamily` (`SiteFontField`, non-system Google families hoisted via `googleFontHrefForFamily()` + `<link precedence>`), `color`/`hoverColor` (`SiteColourField allowManual`). Underline: `underline` no|yes (base) and `hoverUnderline` ''(no change)|underline|none, with shared `underlineColor` + `underlineThickness` + `underlineOffset` (`UnitValueField`) that `resolveFields` shows when EITHER base or hover underline is on (so a hover-only underline - the common "underline the number when you point at it" look - can still be fully styled). **The underline is painted on the number `[data-phone-text]` span, not the `<a>`** (2026-07-15 fix): the `<a>` is pinned to `text-decoration:none !important` and the span carries `text-decoration-line/color/thickness/offset`, because the global `a:hover{text-decoration:underline}` in globals.css was re-underlining the link on hover at the browser's default thickness and wiping out a chosen thickness/colour (and decoration on the inline-flex link didn't reach the text reliably). Hover toggles the span's decoration via `a[data-phone-link]:hover [data-phone-text]{…}`; hover colour stays on the link (`:hover{color…!important}`). `fitOneLine` no|yes (2026-07-15) wraps the icon+number in `HeadingFitText` (same client shrink-to-fit as the Heading/Menu blocks; link is `display:block` so it has a full width to measure against). Vertical positioning (2026-07-15) mirrors Heading: `minHeight` (`BLOCK_HEIGHT_OPTIONS` incl. fill/screen, responsive) + `verticalAlign` top/middle/bottom turn the wrapper into a flex column (`PHONE_VALIGN_MAP`), desktop inline + tablet/mobile via `responsiveMediaCssFor` on `[data-phone-id]`, `blockFillCssResponsive` for fill; `verticalAlign` hidden by `resolveFields` until a height is set. **Icon visibility is stylesheet-only** (2026-07-15 fix): the icon span carries NO inline `display` - `showIcon: mobile` sets `display:none` at base + `inline-flex` under `mobileMediaQuery()`; an earlier inline `display:none` outranked the media rule so the icon never appeared on phones. `mobileIconOnly` yes drops `[data-phone-text]` under the mobile breakpoint so only the glyph shows (aria-label keeps the number). Plus the standard padding/sticky/aos/visibility fields), CTABanner, IconLink (2026-08-08 - lone linking icon for header icon rows; built-in outline set or media-library SVG/PNG upload recoloured via a currentColor CSS mask (or kept as-is with opacity hover), href/new-tab, title as the shared under-icon tooltip + aria-label, iconSize, iconColour/hoverColour SiteColourField light-dark() composites on --il-fg/--il-fg-hover defaulting to the theme toggle's tokens, `audience` everyone|admin gated only in IconLinkRsc (connection() + admin session cookie) across every published config incl. getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig - see the Last updated note for the file list). Media: ImageBlock, VideoEmbed (YouTube/Vimeo), FeatureVideo (self-hosted mp4/webm beside copy), Embed (iframe). Content: Hero, Eyebrow (pill label + optional pulsing dot; pill shape now `var(--radius-pill, 9999px)` instead of a hardcoded `9999`, shared with Badge), Card, ImageChipPanel (single `<img>` + a repeatable `chips` array field, each rendered via the standalone `Chip` component at one of 5 corner positions - deliberately an array field rather than a Puck slot, since Puck wraps each slot child in its own drag-handle `_DropZone-item` box which breaks a Chip's `position:absolute` in the editor canvas even though it renders correctly live; array-field items have no such wrapper so this block is WYSIWYG-correct in both; gained a "holo frame" set of settings - `framePadding` (none/sm/md/lg inner gutter that insets the `<img>` and rounds it to `calc(panelRadius - 6px)`), `frameBg` (none/subtle/gradient panel fill behind the inset image), `gridPattern` (reuses the Section block's `cactus-section-grid-scan` graph-paper background) and `scanEffect` (reuses `cactus-section-scan-beam` looping sweep) - the image carries no z-index so the grid stays in the background and the scan beam + chips paint over it via DOM order; gained `imageLoading` auto|eager (2026-08-19) - 'eager' renders `loading="eager"` + `fetchPriority="high"`, opting the panel image out of the Settings → Media lazy switch since this block is the designed hero-panel and its image is usually the LCP element), Callout (info/success/warning/error boxes - colours read the `--status-{key}`/`-bg`/`-title` vars from Styles → Colours → Status boxes, falling back to the original built-in hexes), Badge (blue/yellow/red/gray colours read `--badge-{key}-bg`/`-text` from Styles → Colours → Badges, falling back to the original hardcoded pastel hexes; `primary` option unchanged, still `--color-primary-subtle`; pill shape now `var(--radius-pill, 9999px)` instead of a hardcoded `9999`), Trustline (repeatable icon+text row, 6 built-in icons), Chip (small label+value card, static-in-flow or floating over a `position:relative` parent via 5 corner presets - fine as a freestanding block, but composing several as siblings inside a `Section`'s image slot is the broken pattern ImageChipPanel replaces), Accordion, FeatureList (gained `iconStyle` emoji|glyph - `glyph` swaps the leading emoji for a 46px solid `--color-primary` rounded square holding a white line-icon from the new `GLYPH_ICONS` map (share/tag/compass/check/shield/clock/star/truck, selected per-item via `item.icon`) and renders larger Fraunces `<h3>` titles + 48ch body; `emoji` default is byte-identical to before; `.cactus-feature-glyph-row` in globals.css adds a hover lift), SpecPanel (windowed "spec sheet" card - dot title-bar + `rows` array field of `{label, value, highlight?, badge?}`; `highlight: 'true'` renders the value in bold `--color-primary`, `badge` renders a green `--color-success` pill; reuses ImageChipPanel's shadow/radius knobs), Ticker (full-bleed teal marquee band - `items` array of `{text}` + `speed` slow/normal/fast; items are duplicated in render and the `.cactus-ticker` class scrolls to `translateX(-50%)` for a seamless loop via the `cactus-ticker` keyframe, Fraunces phrases with mustard `·` separators; respects the global reduced-motion block), Stats, Logos, SocialLinks. Site: SiteHeader (gained `alignment` field - left/center/space-between/space-around - to control horizontal menu item alignment when wrapping to multiple lines; gained the full MenuBlock nav-styling set for its built-in menu: `itemFontFamily` (SiteFontField), `hoverColor`/`hoverBackground`, `activeColor`/`activeFontWeight`/`activeUnderline`(+colour/thickness/offset, extras hidden via `resolveFields` unless underline on) and `showDropdowns` hover|click - all passed through to `MenuBlockClient`), SiteLogo, Copyright, MenuBlock (gained `alignment` field - left/center/space-between/space-around - to control horizontal menu item alignment when wrapping to multiple lines; gained 3 fluid min/max fields - `itemSpacingFluid`/`letterSpacingFluid`/`itemFontSizeFluid`, each `{min, max}` plain text inputs rendered side-by-side by the new `MinMaxPairField` custom Puck field - built into a `clamp(min, preferred, max)` via `fluidClamp()` (`lib/puck/responsiveValue.ts`) that hits `min` at the site's mobile breakpoint and `max` at its tablet breakpoint, continuously shrinking item gap/letter-spacing/font-size as the viewport narrows so a horizontal menu can stay on one line instead of wrapping; empty min/max falls back to the existing `spacing`/`itemFontSize` presets untouched; applied in `MenuBlock`'s vertical branch, `MenuBlockClient` (horizontal, live), and `MenuBlockEditorPreview` (both orientations) for editor/live parity; gained `hoverColor`, `activeColor`, `activeUnderline` (none|underline) + `activeUnderlineColor` (`SiteColourField` swatches; underline-colour field hidden via `resolveFields` unless underline on) - active = exact-path match (`isActiveHref` in `MenuBlockClient.tsx`, relative hrefs only, trailing-slash/query/hash normalised) detected client-side via `usePathname`, active links carry `aria-current="page"`; underline is `text-decoration` 2px thickness / 4px offset, taking the text colour when no separate underline colour set; vertical menus route each anchor through the exported `MenuVerticalLink` client component so hover/active work there too, since the RSC branch can't know the path; gained `itemFontFamily` (new `SiteFontField` custom field - site fonts from Appearance → Styles listed first under "Your fonts" via new cached `useSiteFonts` hook, then the Google Fonts catalogue searchable, or any typed CSS font-family value; empty inherits the site font) - non-system Google families load via a React-hoisted `<link rel="stylesheet" precedence="default">` built by new `googleFontHrefForFamily()` in `lib/design/tokens.ts` (wght 400-700), emitted from `MenuBlockClient`, the vertical RSC branch and the editor preview, so a font picked only on the block still loads without being in the site tokens; `POPULAR_FONTS`/`MAX_FONT_SEARCH_RESULTS` moved from the Styles page into shared `lib/design/font-options.ts`; audit fixes: "Dropdowns open on" now actually works - `showDropdowns` reaches `MenuBlockClient` and `click` mode toggles dropdowns on click (parent-with-children click prevents navigation, closes on outside mousedown via a per-item document listener) instead of hover; `itemColor` converted from free-text to `SiteColourField` swatches (matches SiteHeader, dark-mode-safe); new `hoverBackground` swatch field replaces the hardcoded `--color-primary-subtle` hover pill (which stays as the fallback), wiring up the previously-dead prop; new `activeFontWeight` select ('' = same as items) and `activeUnderlineThickness`/`activeUnderlineOffset` text fields (bare numbers treated as px via `cssLen()`, defaults 2px/4px, hidden with the underline extras); editors now pass `alignment` to `MenuBlockEditorPreview` so the canvas honours it like the live site), LoginButton, ThemeToggle (gained a `style` select - `segmented` icon pill (default), `expand` icon+hover menu, `dropdown` icon+click menu, `text` label pill, `switch` sun/moon two-state slider, `cycle` single icon click-to-step - passed to `ThemeToggleClient`; `style`'s label is now "Control type" since 2026-08-03 gave the block the same appearance set the Members: Sign In and shop basket blocks already had - `iconSize`, `iconColour`, `variant`, `bgColour`, `borderColour`, `borderRadius`, identical keys/labels/order so the three read as one set of controls when they sit together in a header, which they could not before: this block offered no appearance fields at all and always drew a 32px grey pill next to two plain icons. `variant` carries a fourth option `default` (the historic round icon button) and is the defaultProp, so a block saved before the fields existed is unchanged whether or not Puck fills defaults into it. Applied as `--tt-*` custom properties (see `components/ThemeToggle.tsx` below); `resolveFields` drops the appearance fields entirely for the multi-part `segmented`/`text`/`switch` styles - by deletion, never a whitelist, since the panel also carries the centrally-injected Visibility field - and hides the box colours/radius on `default` and `plain`, and the border colour on `filled`), CookieSettingsLink. Members (MEMBERS_SPEC.md Phase 7): `MembersSignIn` (label "Members: Sign In", 2026-08-03 - single click-to-sign-in control, deliberately modelled on the shop's `ShopCartSummary` cart widget so the two sit together in a header. Registered in `puckConfig` (`members` category, listed first), `layoutPuckConfig` (`members`) and `headerPuckConfig` (`site`), each with an RSC override in `config.rsc.tsx`. Client island `components/members/SignInWidgetClient.tsx` (look + click behaviour, `usePathname`), server half `MembersSignInRsc` in `MembersBlocksRsc.tsx` (audience gate, members-enabled gate, member session, avatar resolution, `sanitizeRedirect` on `redirectTo`), modal `components/members/SignInModal.tsx` (portal to `document.body`, escape/tab-trap/scroll-lock, `next/dynamic` `ssr:false` so `LoginForm` only ships once someone clicks). Fields: `icon` person|person-circle|lock|key|login|none + `iconSize`/`iconColour`, `label` (blank = icon only), `variant` bordered|filled|plain + `bgColour`/`borderColour`/`textColour`/`borderRadius`, `clickAction` link|modal, `redirectTo` (blank = current path, resolved client-side), `modalHeading`/`modalWidth`/`modalRadius`/`showRegisterLink`/`registerLabel`, `whenSignedIn` account|accountSignOut|hide + `signedInLabel`/`signOutLabel`/`showAvatarWhenSignedIn`, `audience` everyone|admin. **`audience`, never `visibility`** - core injects a same-named responsive-visibility field into every block and strips it from render props, which would silently swallow the gate (same trap `ShopCartSummary` hit). `resolveFields` hides inapplicable fields (panel options in link mode, sign-out label unless `accountSignOut`, colour/radius on `plain`, icon size/colour on `none`). Renders nothing when `membersConfig.enabled` is false, when `whenSignedIn: 'hide'` and a member session exists (server-side, so no flash), when `audience: 'admin'` and no admin session, or when the visitor is already on `<memberAreaPath>/login`. `registerAllowed` is false for `INVITE_ONLY`, which suppresses the panel's sign-up link), `MembersLogin`/`MembersRegister` (embed the real login/register client forms inline anywhere), `MembersAccountLink` (sign-in/register ↔ my-account/sign-out, the header-friendly member equivalent of `LoginButton` - also registered in `headerPuckConfig`), `MemberGate`/`TrustedMemberGate` (slot-field gates - any member vs `member.trusted`), `MembersProfile` (viewer's own avatar/name/bio). Editor renders always show a fixed preview (no member session to check under an admin editing session); live rendering is async Server Components in `lib/puck/components/MembersBlocksRsc.tsx` (`await connection()` then `getMemberFromCookie()`), swapped in via `rscComponents`/`layoutPuckRscConfig`/`headerPuckRscConfig` - kept out of `config.tsx` itself so the `next/headers`-dependent import chain never reaches the editor's client bundle. Modules category is populated from generated `lib/puck/module-components.ts` (currently: `ContactForm`).
- `headerPuckConfig` block palette (2026-07-13, ImageBlock added 2026-07-15): beyond the chrome/structure blocks (SiteLogo, MenuBlock, LoginButton, ThemeToggle, MembersSignIn, MembersAccountLink, Grid2/3/4, Group, Spacer, Divider) the header editor now also offers Heading, TextBlock, RichTextBlock (Text category), ButtonLink (Actions category) and ImageBlock (new Media category) - so an owner can put a phone number, strapline, "Call us" button or a logo/badge image in the header. These are static content blocks pulled straight from `puckConfig.components`; `headerPuckRscConfig` picks them up automatically via its `...headerPuckConfig.components` spread (no RSC data override needed, unlike SiteLogo/MembersAccountLink), so editor/frontend markup stays identical.
- `footerPuckConfig` gained a Media category (2026-07-15) holding `ImageBlock` (wrapped in `noGutterDefault` like the footer's other static content blocks, since the footer root already applies its own 1.5rem gutter) - previously the footer editor had no way to place a standalone image at all (only `SiteLogo`).
- FeatureVideo block (2026-08-02): `lib/puck/components/FeatureVideo.tsx` (client) + registration in `lib/puck/config.tsx` Media category. Plays a self-hosted `<video>` (media library mp4/webm) in NORMAL FLOW - no pin, no scrub, no spacer - with optional `title`/`body` beside it via the same `textSide` idiom as ScrollSequence (`above` | `left` | `right`, 2-track grid pinned to `gridRow: 1`, scoped by `useId()` + `mobileMediaQuery()` so editor and RSC markup match and it collapses to copy-above-video on phones). Props: `videoUrl`, `posterUrl`, `maxWidth` (applied as `min(cap,100%)`), `radius` (default `16px` - the shop `.spd-stage` product-image radius), `frame` (default true: 1px `--color-border` + `--color-bg-subtle`, which is what keeps a white studio clip from glaring on a dark page), `loop`, `controls` (default false), `ariaLabel`, plus `padding`/sticky/aos consumed by the config-level wrapper div. Playback: `muted` + `playsInline` (the only combination iOS autoplays), TWO IntersectionObservers - one at `rootMargin: 400px` that flips `preload` from `none` to `auto` and calls `load()` (six 4MB clips must not all fetch on paint), one at `threshold: 0.25` that plays/pauses. `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce` suppresses autoplay only. Editor path skips both observers. Media picker gained a `kind: 'video'` (`lib/puck/MediaPickerField.tsx`, `VIDEO_PICKER_FIELDS` + `VideoUrlPickerField`): fetched as `type=other` and narrowed on `mimeType.startsWith('video/')`, tiles and field preview are `<video preload="metadata">` first frames, upload accepts mp4/webm/quicktime. Deskwell product descriptions moved off ScrollSequence onto this block (see `.agents/skills/deskwell-sequence-description`); ScrollSequence stays for genuine scrub work. **Playback race, fixed same day:** when a block crosses the 400px preload margin and the 0.25 play threshold within a frame of each other, `load()` interrupts `play()` and the returned promise REJECTS - swallowing it (`.catch(() => {})`) left that one section paused at 0:00 permanently, reproducible on the live Eclipse Plus page (block #2 of 7, both runs, `readyState` 3-4, no `MediaError`). Now: `load()` only fires when `readyState === 0` (calling it on a loaded element restarts it anyway), a failed `play()` retries once on the next `canplay`, a `loadeddata` arriving after the block is already on screen starts it, and an `isIntersecting` flag gates the retry so a scrolled-past block does not spring to life.
- ScrollSequence `textSide` (2026-08-02): `'above'` (default) | `'left'` | `'right'` - where in-screen copy sits relative to the canvas on wide screens, always collapsing to stacked below `mobileMediaQuery()`. Beside-mode renders a 2-track grid INSIDE the faded stage element, which is the point: copy in a sibling Grid column fades independently (i.e. not at all) while the canvas fades, so text and animation only fade together when they share the stage. Both cells are pinned `gridRow: 1` - grid auto-placement never moves backwards, so `textSide:'right'` (copy col 2, canvas col 1) otherwise bumps the canvas to row 2 and stacks them. Scoped via `useId()` (editor/RSC markup parity). Block default `scrubScreens` is now **1** (was 2). Replaces the old "Grid2 + duplicate visibility-toggled blocks" recipe: one block now covers every viewport.
