**Scroll sequences: optional trim window (working tree, unreleased).** The convert dialog (`MediaSequenceDialog.tsx`) gains optional **Start time** / **End time** fields (accepts `90`, `1:30`, `0:01:30`; parsed client-side by `parseTime`, blank = whole video, live inline validation blocks submit on nonsense or end ≤ start). `POST /api/admin/media/[id]/convert-sequence` re-validates (`readSeconds`: finite number ≥ 0; end > start, end > 0) and forwards `trimStart`/`trimEnd` (seconds) on `EnqueueArgs`. Worker (`services/sequence-worker`, own repo - needs its own commit/deploy before the fields do anything): `CreateJobRequest.trimStart/trimEnd` → `JobSpec.trim_start/trim_end` → `_extract_frames` applies OUTPUT-side `-ss`/`-to` (decode-and-discard, frame-accurate regardless of keyframes; decode cost is noise next to matting). Omitted fields = no trim, old behaviour byte-for-byte.


**Scroll sequences: rembg premultiplies, and everything that followed from it (working tree, unreleased).** Chasing 'mesh still looks wrong on a black page' turned up the real defect underneath all of it: `rembg.remove` builds its cut-out with `Image.composite(frame, transparent_black, mask)`, which multiplies the COLOUR channels by the mask as well as setting alpha. PNG/WebP RGBA are STRAIGHT-alpha formats, so the worker has been writing premultiplied colour into a straight-alpha container since day one - every partly-transparent pixel darkened twice, once by rembg and again by the browser. Measured: returned RGB / source RGB = 0.217, 0.484, 0.995 at alpha 0.22, 0.50, 1.00. It also explains the v0.5.852 un-blend's worst behaviour: fed `a*C` instead of `C`, `255 - (255 - a*C)/a` drives mid-alpha hard to black, which is what turned the defocused Chiro Plus backrest into a blotchy mess. New `_straighten_alpha` undoes it, FIRST, before anything else runs.

`_matte_to_webp` is now one ordered pass: straighten -> `_floor_alpha_from_colour` -> `_white_gap_coverage` -> un-blend by THAT coverage -> (if seeThrough) cut alpha by the same coverage. `_key_white_gaps` and `_unblend_white` are gone as separate passes - having two passes each with their own idea of alpha is what made them fight. **The un-blend no longer divides by the matte's alpha**, which is the structural fix for the flashing: over a page of luminance bg an un-blended pixel is `C - (1-a)*(255-bg)`, so whatever you divide by becomes a flat offset on every pixel alike - matte alpha wobbles frame to frame, colour-derived coverage does not. Measured swing over ten frames: 8.66 originally, 3.24 at v0.5.861, **1.04 now** (1.88 with seeThrough off).

`_floor_alpha_from_colour`: `C = a*F + (1-a)*255` with `F>=0` forces `a >= (255-C)/255`, so where the matte is below that it was reporting UNCERTAINTY not coverage (isnet hedges ~0.5 across a defocused backrest). Raising to the bound cannot be wrong; gated on `ALPHA_FLOOR_TRUST_LO/HI` (0.20/0.45) so the deliberately dropped contact shadow stays dropped - verified alpha 0.0106 both before and after. Only valid on straightened colour; on premultiplied colour the bound is nonsense (it over-raised and left artefacts when tried that way).

`_white_gap_coverage` also re-gated. The old brightness test could not work: cream fabric sits at L~185 and mesh holes at L~215, overlapping. Neither can a local MINIMUM (pale upholstery beside a dark seam has a dark minimum too). The neighbourhood MEAN splits them cleanly - 128 in the mesh vs 202 on the cream chair, because a hole is ringed by thread while a seam is one dark line in a pale field. So `near_solid` now reads `_local_mean` (new, separable box mean), plus a `SEE_THROUGH_DEADZONE` on the wall fraction so woven fabric's few per cent is ignored. Radius 3 -> 5 (weave period measured at 5px by autocorrelation); `SEE_THROUGH_BRIGHT` dropped, `SEE_THROUGH_DARK` 110 -> 130 and now compared against the mean.

**birefnet is the WRONG engine for mesh** - measured, not assumed: on the same frame it returns 97.6% fully-opaque pixels in the mesh box against isnet's 78.6%, i.e. 'Detailed' fills a mesh panel in HARDER. The admin help text and wiki said the opposite and are corrected. Verified end to end by running both of the user's clips (chiro-plus-arm-height-adjustable, eclipse-plus-2-deluxe-arm) through the real `_matte_to_webp` at 8 sampled frames each and compositing over black AND white: both clean, no speckle, no blotching, no flicker. NB this changes the seeThrough=OFF path too (it must - the premultiply and blotch fixes are unconditional), so output is no longer byte-identical to v0.5.862 for any clip. tsc + eslint clean.
**Scroll sequences: see-through gaps, and why mesh sequences flashed (working tree, unreleased).** Two symptoms, one root cause. (1) The white sweep still showed through mesh chair backs: rembg's models return a SILHOUETTE, so a mesh panel comes back ~0.94-0.96 alpha when it is physically about half holes, and `_unblend_white` is the identity at alpha 1 - it never could fix this. (2) The v0.5.852 un-blend made sequences flash. Composited over a page of luminance `bg`, an un-blended pixel is exactly `C - (1-a)*(255-bg)`, so the alpha term is a FLAT OFFSET on every pixel alike; before un-blending an alpha wobble moved bright and dark pixels in opposite directions and largely cancelled across a region, after it the whole region shifts together. Measured on the live Eclipse Plus clip (isnet, 1400px, frames 38-47 over a mid-blue page): mesh brightness swing 8.66 levels with a 4.53 single-frame jump, versus 4.33 with no un-blend at all. A divisor floor / gain cap does NOT help - mesh alpha is high, so the cap never binds. The fix is the alpha, not the un-blend.

New `pipeline._key_white_gaps` (runs BEFORE `_unblend_white`, which reads the alpha the key corrects). The background is known pure white, so a gap is recognisable from the picture alone: `coverage = (255-L) / (255-L_localmin)` with L = max channel and L_localmin the darkest neighbour within `SEE_THROUGH_RADIUS`, scaled by two ramps - `near_solid` (is there genuinely dark product nearby, guards flat pale surfaces) and `near_white` (is the pixel bright enough to be the wall, guards dark textured fabric from going ~9% transparent). Coverage is identically 1 on a flat neighbourhood at ANY brightness, which is the self-gating that leaves ordinary products alone. `_local_min` is a separable two-pass erosion (a square min is separable) - identical to PIL `MinFilter` including borders (edge padding, verified against a brute-force sliding window), 7 ms vs 230 ms a frame at 1400px. Result with it on: swing 3.26 / jump 1.52, mesh luminance 44.77 vs 49.53, holes show the page colour.

DEFAULT OFF, deliberately: a blown-out specular on a dark glossy surface is locally indistinguishable from a mesh hole and gets keyed away (measured: a synthetic white strip on black drops to 2.2% alpha). Measured cost on real clips where it should do nothing - cream Eclipse Plus 99.07-99.96% of alpha kept (only the outermost anti-aliased rim), dark upholstered Chiro Plus 99.06-99.59%, synthetic flat surfaces at 150/200/240/250 and a 215-250 gradient all 100%. Wiring: it is a PER-VIDEO choice, not a site setting - deliberately the only conversion knob the browser picks, because whether it helps depends on the product in the clip and not on the site (`SettingsSchema` carries a comment saying so). `MediaSequenceDialog` checkbox, `useState(false)` so it never carries over to the next video -> POST body -> `convert-sequence` route (`body?.seeThrough === true`, so anything but an explicit true is off) -> `EnqueueArgs.seeThrough` -> worker `CreateJobRequest.seeThrough` -> `JobSpec.see_through` -> `_matte_to_webp`. Omitted = worker's `SEE_THROUGH` env default (off). Everything else (engine/fps/maxWidth) is still read server-side from the settings and the browser cannot touch it. A `seeThrough` key left in a stored `sequenceConfig` from v0.5.861 is stripped by the zod parse - no migration. New worker envs `SEE_THROUGH`/`_RADIUS`/`_DARK`/`_BRIGHT`/`_RAMP` (off/3/110/170/55). Worker is its own repo - needs its own commit + deploy before the field does anything. Only affects conversions run after saving; existing sequences keep the look they were built with. tsc + eslint clean.


**Scroll sequences removed (working tree, unreleased).** The converter is gone in full, not deprecated: `lib/puck/components/ScrollSequence.tsx` and its config block and picker field (`SEQUENCE_PICKER_FIELDS`, `SequenceUrlPickerField`, the picker's `kind: 'sequence'`), `MediaSequenceDialog.tsx`, `SequenceSettingsPanel.tsx`, the Media › Scroll sequences tab, `lib/media/sequence*.ts`, the five routes (`[id]/convert-sequence`, `sequence-status`, `sequence-jobs`, `sequence-presets`, `webhooks/sequence`), `SEQUENCE_MIME` / `isSequenceType`, and the worker's `pipeline.py` with rembg, onnxruntime, numpy, Pillow and ~1 GB of baked-in ONNX models.
- **What the shared plumbing became.** `lib/media/sequence.ts`'s job-ref helpers moved into `video-optimise.ts`; `sequence-presets.ts` became `media-worker-config.ts` (Fly settings only - encode quality is per video now); `sequence-notification.ts` became `video-job-notification.ts`; `components/admin/SequenceProgress.tsx` became `VideoJobProgress.tsx` (no `kind` prop - one status endpoint left); `services/sequence-worker` became `services/video-worker`. The Fly app is still `cactus-seqworker`: renaming it changes the hostname every install has in its environment for nothing.
- **`SiteConfig.sequenceConfig` → `mediaWorkerConfig`** (init migration edited in place for fresh installs; `prisma/core-reconcile/014_media_worker_config.sql` adds the column on existing ones and copies the `fly` key across - a saved Fly API token is worth carrying, the conversion knobs are not). The old column is deliberately not dropped, so a rollback survives.
- **Env vars renamed with fallbacks**, not swapped: `getMediaWorkerUrl` and friends read `MEDIA_WORKER_*` then `SEQUENCE_*` via `readEnv`, so no deployed site needs an environment change to keep optimising video.
- **Old sequence tiles are ordinary rows now.** With `SEQUENCE_MIME` gone they display as generic files (📄) and delete as one object, so an old sequence's frame folder is left behind in storage - Settings → Media's storage check finds those as orphans. `deleteMediaBytes` no longer special-cases a manifest key; `deleteMediaTree` stays for whoever needs it next.
- **Any page still holding a `ScrollSequence` block loses it**: Puck has nothing to render for an unknown component. Deskwell's descriptions had already moved to `FeatureVideo` (see the entry above it).

**Video optimise: multi-select (working tree, unreleased).** The library's selection bar gained **Optimise videos…** next to the image Optimise. It opens the same dialog with the whole selection (`videoSelected` = selected videos not already flagged optimised), which starts one job per video - `START_CONCURRENCY = 4` in flight, since starting a job waits ~20s for a machine to boot, while the jobs themselves all run at once on machines of their own. There is no ceiling on how many run: a machine exists only while its own job does, so ten at once costs what ten in a row would (`MEDIA_WORKER_MAX_JOB_MACHINES` puts a lid back if spend needs one). The working view shows a per-video row with its own bar, and a batch with failures does NOT auto-close - the rows naming what went wrong are the only place that is said. `markMediaOptimised` now accepts video too, so a batch can be marked by hand.

**Video optimise (working tree, unreleased).** The media library can now re-encode a video in place, on the off-platform media worker (`services/video-worker`, which was the sequence worker and already had ffmpeg in the image). One output format, deliberately: **MP4 / H.264 High / yuv420p 8-bit / AAC 128k / `+faststart`** - the only combination every browser, phone, tablet and TV plays with no fallback file. HEVC and AV1 compress better and both have holes, and covering the holes means shipping two renditions of everything.
- **The CRF ladder is measured, not guessed** (`lib/media/video-quality.ts`, VMAF against the 1080p 8-16 Mbps studio masters): CRF 20 → 54% of source, VMAF 96.6; **CRF 23 → 49%, VMAF 96.4 (the default)**; CRF 26 → 30%, VMAF 93.5; CRF 28 → 22%, VMAF 91.1. Above ~95 VMAF the copy is not distinguishable from the original on an ordinary screen, so 'balanced' is where the curve stops paying. hqdn3d denoise was tried and dropped: it cost 1-3 VMAF points for ~1% of file.
- **Only ever downscales.** `build_filters` (worker `video.py`) adds `scale`/`fps` only when the source is bigger/faster than the cap, so a 720p master is never stretched to 1080p and a 24 fps clip is never interpolated. An odd-sized source gets `trunc(iw/2)*2` because 4:2:0 cannot store odd dimensions and ffmpeg fails outright rather than rounding.
- **A silent audio track is dropped, not carried.** Product exports routinely ship a dead stereo track (the Deskwell masters measure ~2.3 kbit/s of nothing); `volumedetect` peak at or below -60 dBFS = drop it. An unreadable track is kept, because dropping what could not be measured would be silently destructive.
- **Same key in, same key out.** `optimisedVideoKey()` re-extensions only a non-MP4 source; an `.mp4` is re-encoded straight over its own key, which is the same reasoning that makes `optimiseModelInPlace` write back over itself - a video's url lives in Puck JSON, in module tables (`shp_product_media`) and in whatever an admin pasted somewhere, and only the first of those gets rewritten when a key moves.
- **Nothing is uploaded when nothing was gained.** The worker compares sizes before writing: within `VIDEO_MIN_SAVING` (5%) of the source it reports `optimised: false` and the platform just flags the row done. Proven on a 1000x1000 750 kbit/s clip, which re-encodes 15% *bigger*.
- Worker side: `services/video-worker/video.py` (own download/probe/encode/callback, no rembg/numpy/PIL, so it costs seconds on a cold machine), `POST /video-jobs` in `app.py` sharing the one queue, registry, auth, `GET /jobs/{id}` and per-job Fly machine with the sequence pipeline. `Job.kind` picks the runner and the callback. Tests: `services/video-worker/test_video.py` (15, real ffmpeg on a synthetic clip: format, profile, pixel format, caps, moov-before-mdat, silence detection, key guard).
- **Media Worker cache rule changed for video** (`workers/media-worker/index.ts`, so it needs a **Deploy Worker** to take effect): `cacheableForever` now excludes any key whose extension types as video. An exact-form key was already downgraded to `max-age=300, must-revalidate` because it can be replaced in place; a nanoid-form video would have kept `immutable` for a year and gone on serving the pre-optimise bytes long after the swap. A conditional revalidation every five minutes on a file this size is nothing beside that.
- Admin UI: **Optimise video…** in the media detail panel for any video that isn't already flagged optimised (`MediaVideoOptimiseDialog.tsx` - quality radio, largest-size select, then a live progress view the admin can walk away from). A video is now eligible for **Mark as optimised** too (`markMediaOptimised` accepts `isVideoDirectType`), while staying OUT of `isOptimisableType` so the in-process bulk image optimiser never tries to run sharp over an MP4.
### Email

- Provider chain (`lib/email/index.ts`): Brevo HTTP API when `BREVO_API_KEY` is set, else nodemailer SMTP (`SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS`); throws when neither is configured. From name/address come from `SiteConfig.emailFromName/emailFromAddress` (fallbacks: siteName / `noreply@example.com`). `SiteConfig.emailProvider` exists as a column but the chain is decided purely by env-var presence. `sendTestEmailWithCredentials(to, siteName, creds)` sends the standard test email through caller-supplied Brevo/SMTP credentials (unsaved form values; blank fields fall back to env) - used by the settings-page per-card "Send test email" button that appears next to "Save credentials" once new values are typed.
- Notification types sent by core (admin/User side): login OTP (password login), email verification code (registration), recovery link (recovery request), recovery-requested notice (same trigger), recovery-completed notice (recovery completion), password-changed notice (password add/change) - all plain `sendEmail` calls, no template override system.
- Module emails (contact-form): submission notification to the configured/admin address ("full" content or "notify"-only modes, optional CCs, reply-to submitter), auto-reply to the submitter (markdown with `{{name}}`/`{{email}}` placeholders), admin reply email (markdown + signature, reply-to the site address).
- In-app admin notifications (not email) live in the Notification table: "Changes awaiting deployment" (rolling, reasons deduped by label), `core-update`, `module-update:{id}`, `contact-form:messages` (rolling unread count); Members system re-uses the generic `message` type for pending-approval/deletion admin alerts (`lib/members/admin-notify.ts`, `upsertAlert` dedupe) - see below, it has no dedicated type of its own.
- `upsertAlert` (`lib/notifications/alerts.ts`) three-states `link`/`actionLabel`: a string sets it, `null` clears it (no button at all), **omitted leaves whatever is already stored** - so a progress tick that doesn't know the destination can't wipe a button an earlier, better-informed write put on. `resurfaceOnTitleChangeOnly: true` keeps a read alert read while only its reasons move, so a 5s progress poll doesn't re-light the bell every tick.
- Scroll-sequence jobs have no table: `upsertSequenceNotification` keeps one `message` notification per job keyed `sequence-job:{jobRef}`, state in the title, latest progress in `reasons[0].detail` ("42%" / "42% - detail"). `progress` in is the worker's **0-1 fraction**, rendered as `round(progress*100)%` (it was rounded as if already a percentage, so every conversion read 0% until finishing at "1%"). While queued/running the notification has `link: null` (no button - `SequenceProgress` draws the live bar instead); on done the webhook passes the `folderId` the tile was filed into and it becomes `/media?folder=<id>` labelled **Open media folder**. `lib/media/sequence-notification.ts` holds the pure parsers for that contract (`parseSequenceNotification`, `isSequenceInFlight`, `SEQUENCE_DEDUPE_PREFIX`) with **no server imports**, so the bell (client), the notifications page (RSC) and `lib/media/sequence-jobs.ts` all read a job the same way. Both notification surfaces prefer `actionLabel` over the per-type label and never show `message`'s "View Messages" on a sequence row.
- Video-optimise jobs use the same trick under `video-job:{jobRef}` with their own title verbs (`Optimising video:` / `Video optimised:` / `Video optimise failed:`, `videoJobTitle`) and `reasons[0].label` of `Encoding`. `parseMediaJobNotification` (`lib/media/sequence-notification.ts`) reads either kind and returns which it is, so the bell, the notifications page and `SequenceProgress` (now taking a `kind` prop that picks `video-status` vs `sequence-status`) handle both. `lib/media/sequence-jobs.ts` still lists sequence jobs only - the Media › Scroll sequences panel is about sequences.

Email templates (`lib/email/registry.ts`): ONE registry for every email the site sends - core's 14 `member.*`, 8 `auth.*` and 1 `system.*`, plus each installed module's, contributed through the manifest `emailTemplates` seam. Each has a code default and an optional `EmailTemplate` DB override (absence, or a null copy column, = default; reset nulls the copy and keeps the wrapper/on-off settings). A def carries `mergeTags`, optional `requiredTags` (an edit that drops one is refused - this is what stops an admin rewriting the login-code email without `{{code}}` in it), optional `rawTags` (merge values that are markup the sending code assembled itself, e.g. an order's item table - everything else is escaped) and `transactional` (always sends, cannot be switched off). `buildRegistry()` runs every def - core's and every module's - through `withSubjectHeading()`, which prepends `<h3>{subject}</h3>\n` to the default body: the heading tracks the subject instead of being retyped beside it, module templates get it without each module having to remember, and it arrives in the editor as ordinary copy an admin can reword or delete per email (`lib/email/registry.test.ts` asserts every registered template opens with its own subject). Transactional ones (verify-email, email-change-code, email-change-notice, magic-link, deletion-requested, deletion-cancelled, deletion-admin-notify, security-alert) always send; the rest (welcome, suspended, approved, digest-daily, digest-weekly) would check `MemberNotificationPreference` if the caller supplied a matching category, but core has no non-transactional categories of its own yet. `renderEmailTemplate(key, vars)` (`lib/email/render.ts`) does `{{#if flag}}` conditionals then `{{tag}}` interpolation (HTML-escaped in the body except `rawTags`, plain in the subject), injects `siteName`/`siteUrl`/`logoUrl`/`year` under any caller-supplied values, and wraps the result in the resolved `emailWrapper` design; it returns null when a non-transactional template is switched off. `sendTemplateEmail(to, key, vars, opts?)` (`lib/email/index.ts`) renders + sends and returns false when skipped; every `auth.*` helper (`sendLoginOtp`, `sendRecoveryLink`, …) is a one-line wrapper over it now. `sendMemberEmail(member, key, vars, opts?)` adds the members-only notification-preference gate on top. `previewEmailTemplate(key, draft, vars)` takes the same path with unsaved editor content and stand-in merge values - what the admin preview and test-send both use. It skips the stand-in for the four site-level tags (`siteName`, `siteUrl`, `logoUrl`, `year`), letting the real site context fill them: rendering an owner's own site name as `[siteName]` is what convinced one to delete the tag and type the name in by hand, which then survives every rename the site ever has (`lib/email/render.test.ts`). Digests: `lib/members/digest.ts`'s `runDigest('DAILY'|'WEEKLY')` batches each member's subscribed-category `MemberActivityEvent` rows (by `type`) from the last 24h/7d into one email, cron-driven (`GET /api/cron/members/digest?mode=daily|weekly`, `CRON_SECRET`-gated).

### Scripts

- `scripts/migrate-sitelogo-cell-height.mjs` - one-off data migration + read-only audit for the SiteLogo "Element height" rename (`logoHeight`/`logoHeightShrunk` → `cellHeight`/`cellHeightShrunk`). Recursively walks `Layout` (type='header') `builderData`/`publishedData` and `SavedBlock` (componentType SiteLogo/Grid/Group) Puck blobs, remapping SiteLogo keys 1:1; also reports header true-centering coverage (centre-aligned Grid columns, 3-item space-distributed Groups). DRY RUN by default (reads, reports, writes nothing); `--apply` persists. Reads `DATABASE_URL` from `.env`. Not part of any build step; the render fallback makes it non-load-bearing.
- `scripts/migrate-grid-columns-split.mjs` - one-off data migration for the Grid component split (the single dynamic "Grid" Columns-select block replaced by fixed-column variants). Rewrites the affected Puck blocks across `Layout`/`InfoPage`/`SavedBlock` blobs. Reads `DATABASE_URL`; not part of any build step. Same non-load-bearing one-off shape as `migrate-sitelogo-cell-height.mjs`.
- `scripts/prebuild.mjs` - the single prebuild entry point for `npm run build` (`node scripts/prebuild.mjs && next build`). Replaces the old serial `&&` chain, whose real dependency graph is a fan-out rather than a line: `checkout-modules` must land module code on disk first (a barrier - everything downstream reads `/modules`), after which three branches run **concurrently** because none reads another's inputs or outputs - (a) `prisma generate`, (b) the database chain `build-migrate` → `sync-module-manifests`, (c) `generate-all`. `prisma generate` does not need the database, the migration chain does not need a generated client, and the generators need neither, so the prebuild costs the slowest branch rather than the sum. Each branch's output is buffered and flushed as one labelled block on completion (concurrent logs cannot interleave); any non-zero exit aborts the build with that branch's status, exactly as `&&` did. Also sets `CHECKPOINT_DISABLE=1` and `PRISMA_HIDE_UPDATE_MESSAGE=true` for every child, killing the Prisma CLI's version-check network round trip and its unactionable "update available" banner. A child killed by a signal (OOM, for instance) reports a null exit code rather than a number, which read as success; since 2026-07-23 the checkout step treats a signal as a failure and exits non-zero, so a build whose module checkout was killed cannot carry on with an empty `/modules`.
- `scripts/build-migrate.mjs` - conditional migration runner for Vercel builds. Skips entirely without DATABASE_URL; swaps Neon pooler URL for the direct endpoint (or DIRECT_URL); sets `PRISMA_SCHEMA_DISABLE_ADVISORY_LOCK=1` (plus `CHECKPOINT_DISABLE`/`PRISMA_HIDE_UPDATE_MESSAGE`, set here as well as in `prebuild.mjs` so a direct invocation behaves the same); runs `prisma migrate deploy`, then `reconcile-core-schema.mjs`, then `run-module-migrations.mjs`, then `flush-pooled-plans.mjs`, each with 3 retries and backoff. `runWithRetry`'s options object takes `childEnv`, used for exactly one step: the flusher gets the site's real pooled `DATABASE_URL` instead of the direct-endpoint rewrite every other step needs, because it is the only step whose job concerns the pooler rather than the schema (see `flush-pooled-plans.mjs` - handing it the rewritten URL silently disabled it on every pooled install). Invokes the Prisma CLI through `node_modules/.bin/prisma` (falling back to `npx` only if that binary is absent) - `npx` re-runs npm's package resolution on every call for no gain. `migrate resolve --rolled-back` (which clears a failed-migration record left by an interrupted earlier apply, e.g. a Neon cold-start disconnect, that would otherwise block every later attempt with P3009) runs only **before a retry**, not before the first attempt: a stale failed record makes attempt 1 fail fast with P3009, the resolve then runs and attempt 2 applies cleanly, so recovery is unchanged while the happy path no longer pays a full Prisma CLI boot plus a DB round trip on every single build.
- `scripts/reconcile-core-schema.mjs` - build-step-only runner that closes core-schema drift on existing installs. The single core migration is edited in place and `prisma migrate deploy` never re-applies it, so additive changes made after an install was provisioned never reach its database. This runner applies every **unapplied** `.sql` in `prisma/core-reconcile/` (lexicographic) via a direct `pg` client (same SSL/direct-endpoint handling as `run-module-migrations.mjs`/`build-migrate.mjs`). Applied files are recorded, with their sha256, in the existing `ModuleMigration` ledger under the reserved module name `__core__` - deliberately not a new runner-owned table, which would show up in backups taken from one install and not another. Previously every file re-ran on **every** deploy for a guaranteed no-op; that list only grows, and each entry cost a statement batch and a database round trip per build. A file whose contents change is re-applied (checksum mismatch), so the self-heal guarantee is intact; an install predating the ledger simply applies each file once (a no-op on an up-to-date database) and records it. Each file is additive and idempotent (`IF NOT EXISTS` / `pg_constraint`-guarded FKs / `ADD VALUE IF NOT EXISTS`), so it is a no-op on fresh or up-to-date installs and adds only the missing objects on a drifted one. Skips without DATABASE_URL; 3 retries with backoff. Files: `001_media_folders_tags.sql` (Folder/Tag/MediaTag tables + `Media.originalName`/`folderId`/`optimised` columns and their indexes/FKs - the `/hq/media` crash on the deskwell install, 2026-07-11), `002_member_twofactor_phone.sql` (`MemberTwoFactor.phoneEncrypted`), `003_twofactor_sms_enum.sql` (adds `SMS` to the `TwoFactorMethod` enum - kept as the only statement in its own file because `ALTER TYPE ... ADD VALUE` cannot share a multi-statement transaction batch on older Postgres), `004_perf_indexes.sql` (the `Layout`/`Module.status` indexes, and drops three plain indexes duplicating a `@unique`), `005_retire_starter_layouts.sql` (deletes the legacy starter rows, *then* drops `Layout.isStarter` and its index - in that order), `006_module_layouts_seeded.sql` (`Module.layoutsSeededAt`, backfilled to `installedAt` for `active`/`inactive`/`update_available` modules only - one still mid-install or `failed` has never had its code in a build, so it stays NULL and is seeded when its deploy lands), `007_admin_menu_config.sql` (adds the nullable `SiteConfig.adminMenuConfig` jsonb for the admin-sidebar customisation; null = built-in defaults, so existing installs need no backfill), `008_menu_item_visibility.sql` (guarded `CREATE TYPE "MenuItemVisibility"` + `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS "MenuItem"."visibility"` defaulting PUBLIC, so every existing menu item keeps rendering to everyone with no backfill), `009_reseed_unseeded_module_layouts.sql` (clears `Module.layoutsSeededAt` on rows that provably never seeded, so `seedPendingModuleLayouts()` re-seeds them on the next request - see the Layout system section; the proof is `layoutsSeededAt < MIN(ModuleMigration.appliedAt)` for that module, i.e. the stamp predates the first moment the module's code was ever in a build, since the ledger rows are written by the build step with the code present. Nothing is cleared for a module seeded after its code landed - those either have their layouts or the owner deleted them, and re-minting deleted layouts is what the stamp exists to prevent. A module with no migration rows at all is left alone: nothing to prove it against, and none of them declare layout types).
- `scripts/checkout-modules.mjs` - clones every `modules.json` entry into `/modules`, pinned to the recorded `version` tag (`git clone --depth=1 --branch`). On Vercel always a fresh clone; locally tries `git checkout HEAD -- .` in the existing clone first (this reverts uncommitted local edits to tracked module files). **A PINNED entry no longer falls back to an unpinned HEAD clone on Vercel (2026-07-23)**: the pinned clone is retried once (a transient network blip should not sink a build) and, failing that, the whole build exits non-zero. Shipping HEAD instead would put unvetted module code - possibly wanting a newer core - live while the database and `modules.json` still claim the pin, which is a silent version lie rather than a build failure. Locally nothing is fatal: a deleted tag or a network blip still warns and falls back to HEAD so local work carries on. The HEAD clone remains the normal path for an entry with no recorded version at all. Modules are handled **in parallel** (each writes only its own directory and reads no other's, so the clones were never actually dependent - just serialised by the loop); each module's log lines are buffered and flushed as one block on completion so concurrent git output cannot interleave. **Private module repos (2026-08-13):** every clone is attempted anonymously first - public repos behave byte for byte as before, and no credential is even resolved until a clone fails - then retried once with a credential from `scripts/lib/module-clone-auth.mjs` in tier order `MODULE_CLONE_TOKEN` → GitHub App installation token (the `GithubAppConnection` row read with `pg` and decrypted/JWT-signed with node crypto - never Prisma, since this script runs before `prisma generate`, and never TS imports, since it is plain .mjs) → `GITHUB_API_TOKEN`. Auth is never attached up front because an App installation token presented for a public repo outside its own installation is refused by GitHub, which would break every directory module's clone. The credential rides as `-c http.https://github.com/.extraheader=` command-line config (never in the URL, so nothing persists into the deployed `.git/config`; the key form scopes the header to github.com), git runs with `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` so an anonymous clone of a private repo fails fast rather than hanging the build, and every captured git output string is scrubbed of the token and its base64 basic-auth form before it can reach a build log (which the deployment log viewer shows). Unit tests: `scripts/lib/module-clone-auth.test.mjs`.
- `scripts/generate-all.mjs` - the single entry point `npm run dev` and `npm run build` use to run all eight generators below (router, puck, cron, settings-tabs, sms-providers, extension-points, layout-types, media-worker), in that order, in **one** Node process via sequential `await import()`. They were previously eight `&&`-chained `node scripts/generate-module-*.mjs` invocations, i.e. eight Node boots (one of them loading the whole TypeScript compiler for `generate-media-worker`) for a few hundred milliseconds of real work. Semantics are identical: same generators, same order, and a generator that calls `process.exit(1)` on a bad manifest (the duplicate-`publicBasePath` check in `generate-module-router.mjs`) still aborts the build. Add new generators to the END of the list, not the middle.
- `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs` - scans `modules/*/app/api/**/route.ts` and `modules/*/app/cactus-admin/<name>/**/page.tsx`; writes the gitignored `lib/modules/router.ts` (API dispatch table + lazy page loaders). For any module declaring `publicBasePath` in its manifest, also scans `modules/<name>/app/public/<base>/**/{page.tsx,route.ts}` and emits `resolveModulePublicPage`, `dispatchModulePublicRoute`, `getModulePublicBases`, `resolveModuleRootSlugPage` (from the optional `publicRootSlug` manifest block - a lazy `(slug) => Promise<boolean>` claim plus the page to render when it says yes; independent of `publicBasePath`, no uniqueness check, asked in registry order), ; fails the build if two modules declare the same `publicBasePath`. **Sitemap and robots are scanned for EVERY module, `publicBasePath` or not** (core 0.5.1150): if `modules/<name>/lib/sitemap.ts` exists, exporting `getPublicSitemapEntries(siteUrl)`, it's wired into `collectModuleSitemapEntries`; same for `modules/<name>/lib/robots.ts` exporting `getPublicRobotsDisallow(): Promise<string[]>` into `collectModuleRobotsDisallow()`. Both checks used to sit behind the `if (!base) continue` guard, so a module with no public base of its own - `ultimate-seo`, `shop-variations` - was silently never collected, and the Sitemap & robots admin screen saved rules that changed nothing (called from `app/robots.ts`, merged into the `disallow` list alongside the fixed `/cactus-admin/`, `/setup/`, `/cactus-status/`, `/api/` entries). Shop's `modules/shop/lib/robots.ts` returns `['/shop']` when `shopStatus === 'CLOSED'`; `modules/shop/lib/sitemap.ts`'s `getPublicSitemapEntries` returns `[]` for the same state, so a closed shop drops out of both the sitemap and gets disallowed in robots.txt. Runs on every dev start and build. **Route ordering:** every emitted route table (`API_ROUTES`, `PUBLIC_ROUTE_HANDLERS`) and page-loader key set (`PAGE_LOADERS`, `PUBLIC_PAGE_LOADERS`) is sorted **literal-first per segment** by `comparePatternSegments`/`sortRoutesBySpecificity`/`sortPatternKeys` - at the first differing segment a literal beats a dynamic `[param]`. This matters because dispatch (`dispatchModuleApi`) is first-match-wins and `matchPattern` treats `[param]` as a wildcard, so without the sort a raw file-order `[id]` would shadow a sibling literal like `reorder`/`check-slug` (they start with `[` = 0x5B, which sorts ahead of letters), routing `…/categories/reorder` to the `[id]` handler with id="reorder" (405, no POST). Add new route tables through these sorters.
- `scripts/generate-module-puck.mjs` - collects `puckBlocks` from every module manifest; writes two gitignored files: `lib/puck/module-components.ts` (client-safe maps only) and `lib/puck/module-rsc-components.ts` (RSC maps only, server-only). Split into separate files (previously one) because a single shared file gave `lib/puck/config.tsx` a static import edge to any block's RSC half - if even one module block's RSC render used `next/headers` (e.g. Boards' cookie-based session checks), Next.js rejected the whole file the moment `lib/puck/config.tsx` was reached from the client Puck editor (`PuckEditor.tsx`/`LayoutPuckEditor.tsx`), regardless of which named export was actually used. Blocks whose RSC render needs server-only APIs must also split their own file in two (editor-safe placeholder + `.rsc.tsx` with the real render), and declare `rscImport` in the manifest pointing at the `.rsc` file (see `modules/boards/cactus.module.json`, `modules/gazette/cactus.module.json` for examples). RSC-only Puck config exports (`*RscConfig`, `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig`, `puckRscConfig`) live in `lib/puck/config.rsc.tsx`, not `config.tsx`, for the same reason.
- `scripts/generate-module-cron.mjs` - collects `cronJobs` from every module manifest; writes the gitignored `vercel.json` (`{crons: [...]}`); also prepends a hardcoded `CORE_CRONS` array (Members system: `/api/cron/members/purge`, `/api/cron/members/exports`) - core cron jobs are declared here rather than committed to `vercel.json` directly since that file is rebuilt from scratch on every build.
- `scripts/generate-module-settings-tabs.mjs` - collects `settingsTabs` from every module manifest (`{id, label, permission, import, component}`); writes the gitignored `lib/modules/settings-tabs.ts` (`moduleSettingsTabComponents: Record<id, Component>`). Consumed by `app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx` to render module-registered settings tabs generically (id/label/permission list comes from `app/cactus-admin/config/page.tsx`, which permission-filters live from `Module.manifest`, same pattern as `navEntries` in `layout.tsx`).
- `scripts/generate-module-sms-providers.mjs` - collects `smsProviders` from every module manifest (`{id, label, import, export}`); writes the gitignored `lib/modules/sms-providers.ts` (`moduleSmsProviders: Array<{module, id, label, provider}>`). Consumed by `lib/auth/sms.ts` (`getActiveSmsProvider()` - first configured provider from an active module, else null) to deliver login OTPs by text (admin password login + member SMS 2FA), always falling back to email.
- `scripts/generate-module-sms-templates.mjs` - the same job for the manifest's optional `smsTemplates`, writing the gitignored `lib/modules/sms-templates.ts` (`moduleSmsTemplates`). Same module-name key prefix rule, same first-registration-wins rule, same installed-module filter at the admin route. One module uses it: shop (9).
- `scripts/generate-module-email-templates.mjs` - collects the manifest's optional `emailTemplates` (`{groupLabel, import, export}`, one per module) and writes the gitignored `lib/modules/email-templates.ts` (`moduleEmailTemplates: Record<moduleName, {groupLabel, templates: EmailTemplateDef[]}>`). The module file exports the defaults; core's `lib/email/registry.ts` merges them in, **rejecting any key not prefixed with the module's own name** and refusing to overwrite an existing key, so two modules can never fight over one email. Whether a module is *installed* is a database fact and is not decided here - `GET /api/admin/emails/templates` filters the list by `getInstalledModuleNames()` before showing anything. Six modules use it: shop (10), quote-for-shop (4), reviews-for-shop (2), boards (2), twilio (2), contact-form (2).
- `scripts/generate-module-extension-points.mjs` - collects `extensionPoints` from every module manifest (`{point, id, permission, import, component}`); writes the gitignored `lib/modules/extension-points.ts` (`moduleExtensionPointComponents: Record<point, Record<id, Component>>`), grouped by the arbitrary `point` string. Core has no knowledge of any specific point name - a *publishing* module (e.g. `contact-form`) defines its own point names in its own page code and permission-filters live from `Module.manifest` (same pattern as `navEntries`/`settingsTabs`); a *contributing* module (e.g. `contact-form-reply-catcher`) declares entries against that point name in its manifest. See the "Module extension points" section in wiki/Authoring-a-module.md. First core (not module) publisher: `core.roles-page`, read the same way - since 2026-08-10 by `app/cactus-admin/users/page.tsx`'s `RolesTab` rather than `config/page.tsx`, the Roles editor having moved there. `config/page.tsx` still publishes `core.backup-page` (2026-08-09), rendered by `ConfigPageClient` under Settings → Backup via the `backupExtensions` prop - for modules whose data lives outside the site database (first consumer: live-chat's Chatwoot dump card).

**Whole-page tab points (2026-08-10).** `lib/modules/extension-tabs.tsx` (`resolveExtensionTabs(point, user)`) is the shared server-side resolver for extension points whose entries are *tabs on somebody else's page*: it reads the installed manifests, drops any entry whose `permission` this role lacks, falls back to a tidied entry id when the install-time schema has stripped the `label`, sorts by `order` (unset last) and returns `{id, label, order, Component}` for the host to render as it sees fit. Manifest entries for these points therefore carry two extra optional fields beyond the usual five: `label` and `order`. Core publishes two of them - `core.inbox-tabs` (the `/inbox` screen) and `core.media-tabs` (the Media page) - and the shop module publishes `shop.products-tabs` (Catalogue), `shop.orders-tabs` (Sales, new) and `shop.tax-shipping-tabs` (Tax & shipping, which still resolves its own rather than using the shared helper). This is the mechanism the 2026-08-10 sidebar tidy runs on: a companion module hands core or shop a panel instead of taking a sidebar link. **Import dedupe (2026-07-23, shared by this generator, `generate-module-puck.mjs`, `generate-module-settings-tabs.mjs` and `generate-module-sms-providers.mjs`):** each keeps an `ident → importPath` map and emits an import line once. A module legitimately contributes the same component to two extension points (or two settings tabs, or two Puck block types), and the emitted identifier is derived from module name + component name, so the same import line was written twice and the generated file did not compile. Re-emitting is silently collapsed; the same identifier mapping to a DIFFERENT path is a real name clash and throws, failing the build rather than emitting a duplicate declaration. `generate-module-puck.mjs` keeps two separate maps, one per generated file, since the client and RSC imports live in different modules.
- `scripts/generate-module-layout-types.mjs` - collects `layoutTypes` from every module manifest; writes the gitignored `lib/layout/module-layout-types.ts` (pure data: groups + flat type→group lookup, each type optionally carrying `editorPreview: {className?, maxWidth?}`) and `lib/setup/module-starter-layouts.ts` (starter-template loader functions, imported per module). See "Module-declared layout types" under Puck Integration above.
- `scripts/generate-media-worker.mjs` - build-step: transpiles the Cloudflare media Worker (`workers/media-worker/index.ts`) to a plain ES module via `typescript` and embeds it as a string constant the app reads at runtime, so the admin > Settings > Media "Deploy Worker automatically" flow (`POST /api/admin/media/deploy-worker`) can upload runnable JavaScript to the user's Cloudflare account without a runtime transpile (`typescript` is a devDependency, pruned from the production runtime).
- `scripts/run-module-migrations.mjs` - build-step-only runner: for modules with status active/deploying/update_available, applies unapplied `modules/<name>/migrations/*.sql` files in lexicographic order, each in a transaction, recording name+checksum in `ModuleMigration`. The applied-migration ledger is read **once** into a Set up front, not one SELECT per (module, migration file) pair - with seven modules and several migrations each that was dozens of Neon round trips on every deploy purely to establish that there was nothing to do, which is the outcome on every build except the one that introduces a migration. The skip decision itself is unchanged. **Stale-ledger self-heal (2026-07-15):** before the per-module skip loop, if a module has recorded migrations in the ledger yet **no** table with its `tablePrefix` exists, the ledger is treated as stale (a restored/branched DB that carried the `ModuleMigration` rows but not the module's actual tables - which are not in a backup's schema section), its ledger rows are purged and its migrations re-applied from scratch. Restricted to the zero-prefixed-tables case so a healthy install is untouched and a non-idempotent `CREATE TABLE` can't collide. This is what recovered the live dwoffice.furniture contact-form/twilio tables after a restore left the ledger lying.
- `scripts/flush-pooled-plans.mjs` - build-step-only, runs last in `build-migrate.mjs` after every DDL step. Ends idle backends on the database so Postgres rebuilds their cached query plans against the new schema. Postgres plans a prepared statement against the table shape it saw at prepare time, and `SELECT *` makes that shape every column of the table; change the table and the next execution on a connection still holding that plan fails with `cached plan must not change result type` (SQLSTATE 0A000). A deploy normally replaces its own connections, but Neon's pooled endpoint is pgBouncer and its **server** connections outlive the deployment, while our DDL deliberately runs on the direct endpoint and never touches them - so a schema change strands stale plans on the pool for as long as pgBouncer keeps those connections. The symptom is a half-working site: requests landing on a fresh pooled connection succeed, requests landing on an old one 500, varying request to request. This is what broke every product page on dwoffice.furniture after v0.5.578 (shop `005_price_types` dropped `compare_at_price` and added sale/retail/trade, leaving `SELECT * FROM "shp_products"` planned against the old column list; shop-variations' `getVariantSelectorPayload` and a Google Sheet push both threw P2010/0A000 until the connections aged out on their own). Terminates via the direct endpoint (asking pgBouncer to end pgBouncer's connections just routes back through the pool), **idle backends only** so nothing in flight on the still-serving old deployment is interrupted, in two passes 3s apart to catch backends that were mid-query on the first. Skips only without DATABASE_URL. Best-effort: it never exits non-zero, so it cannot fail a deploy. **It had never once run on a pooled install before 2026-07-19.** `build-migrate.mjs` gives its children a DATABASE_URL already rewritten to the direct endpoint, so this script's `-pooler` test was reading a hostname with `-pooler` stripped out, concluding "not a pooled connection" and exiting having cleared nothing - on exactly the installs it was written for. Fixed on both sides: `build-migrate.mjs` now passes the site's real `DATABASE_URL` to this step alone (`runWithRetry`'s `childEnv` option), and the pooled/direct test no longer gates the sweep - it only picks the log line, because a wrong answer there is silent and surfaces as a broken site one migration later. The runtime retry in `lib/db/stale-plan.ts` is the actual guarantee; this script keeps that retry rare rather than routine, and cannot cover connections opened after the build.
- `scripts/sync-module-manifests.mjs` - build-step-only: rewrites `Module.manifest` from each deployed module's `cactus.module.json` so nav entries/teardown stay in step with shipped code. Skips without DATABASE_URL.
- `scripts/sync-wiki.mjs` - `npm run sync-wiki`: pulls all `.md` files from the GitHub wiki repo (`WIKI_SOURCE_REPO` or GITHUB_REPO + `.wiki`) into `/wiki` via the API.
- `scripts/fetch-google-fonts.mjs` - standalone maintenance script (own npm script, not in the build): fetches the Google Fonts metadata catalogue and writes `lib/design/google-fonts.json`, the source for the admin font pickers. Run manually to refresh the available-fonts list.
- `scripts/dev-warm.sh` - `npm run dev:warm`: kills anything on the port, clears `.next`, starts `next dev --webpack` (webpack chosen over Turbopack to avoid an HMR chunk-hash reload cascade), and pre-warms `/`, `/home`, `/logged-out`, `/setup`, `/style-guide`, `/privacy-policy` in the background.

Build-time order (from `package.json` `build`, which is now just `prebuild.mjs && next build`): checkout-modules, then three concurrent branches - (a) prisma generate, (b) build-migrate (migrate deploy → reconcile-core-schema → run-module-migrations) → sync-module-manifests, (c) generate-all (generate-module-router → generate-module-puck → generate-module-cron → generate-module-settings-tabs → generate-module-sms-providers → generate-module-extension-points → generate-module-layout-types → generate-media-worker → generate-module-email-templates) - then `next build`. Dev (`npm run dev`) runs the generators then `next dev --webpack`.

### Build and Deploy

- Build steps in order: see Scripts above. `npm run build` is the single entry; Vercel runs it on every push. It is `node scripts/prebuild.mjs && next build`, where the prebuild is `checkout-modules` (barrier) followed by `prisma generate`, the `build-migrate` → `sync-module-manifests` database chain, and `generate-all` running concurrently.
- **Turbopack's build filesystem cache is on** (`next.config.ts` → `experimental.turbopackFileSystemCacheForBuild: true`). It persists the compilation cache in `.next/cache`, which Vercel already restores from the previous deployment (the "Restored build cache from previous deployment" line in the build log). Without it the full Turbopack compile - 41s of a measured 103s deploy - was paid on every push regardless of how small the diff was. It is still flagged experimental in Next 16, so if a deploy ever produces stale or impossible output, this is the first thing to switch off.
- **`next build` does NOT type-check.** `next.config.ts` sets `typescript.ignoreBuildErrors: true`. Measured on a real Vercel build, the `tsc` pass inside `next build` was 26s of a 123s deploy, and it duplicated the `tsc --noEmit` gate that CLAUDE.md's work loop already requires on every change. The check moved, it was not dropped: **`npm run typecheck` is now the only thing standing between a type error and production**, so it is not optional before a commit. There is deliberately no CI workflow enforcing it - `lib/updates/core-plan.ts` excludes only `modules/`, `modules.json` and `.gitmodules` from the core-update push, so a `.github/workflows/*` file would propagate into every customer's repo and run CI on their GitHub account. Adding one means excluding `.github/` from the core sync first.
- Prisma migrations run only inside the Vercel build step (`build-migrate.mjs` → `prisma migrate deploy`), never at runtime; the advisory lock is disabled because Vercel serialises builds and Neon cold starts exceed the lock timeout. One migration file exists, edited in place for schema changes (fresh-install platform). Because migrate deploy never re-applies an edited-in-place migration, additive core changes reach already-provisioned installs via idempotent `prisma/core-reconcile/*.sql` run by `reconcile-core-schema.mjs` immediately after migrate deploy.
- `prisma db push` is blocked (`npm run db:push` exits 1 with a message).
- Vercel-specific: `vercel.json` is generated (cron entries only) and gitignored; deployments are auto-triggered by pushes to `main`; env-var-only changes use the redeploy API (`POST /v13/deployments?forceNew=1` based on the latest production deployment); module/core changes deploy via Git Data API commits (registry sync / core sync) whose push triggers the build; the redeploy gate (`pendingRedeployId` sentinel → real id → cleared on READY / webhook / dismiss / 4-minute server timeout) drives the admin shell's deploy status bar and the notification bell's live section meanwhile. Deployment status arrives via webhook (Pro) or lazy polling (`getLatestDeploymentStatus`, Hobby).
- jsdom is pinned to `^26` (jsdom 29 breaks the Vercel serverless update check with ERR_REQUIRE_ESM).
- Tester repo relationship: `usersaynoso/Cactus-Foundation-Tester` is a downstream install of this platform used for live testing; local `.env.local` points at the same Neon database as the live Tester site. Pushes to the Tester repo use the identity `Chris Taylor-Guest <airings.snug-0m@icloud.com>` and version-prefixed commit titles; core code reaches it via the in-app core-update sync (blob-level tree diff of core files vs the matching upstream tag, skipping `modules/`, `.gitmodules`, `modules.json`).
- Release flow (per CLAUDE.md): patch-only version bumps, tag format `vX.Y.Z`, GitHub release created immediately after every push.

### Slash Commands

None. `.claude/commands/` does not exist. `.claude/` contains only `settings.json` (permission allowlist + `caveman@caveman` plugin enablement) and runtime state files. Available slash commands come from installed plugins, not this repo.

### Utilities and Lib

`lib/` root:

- `admin/search-index.ts` - `ADMIN_SEARCH_ENTRIES`: static, framework-agnostic registry the command palette adds on top of the nav (Settings tabs, their sections, and individual settings). Each entry: `{ id, label, section (breadcrumb), path (admin-relative, incl. `?tab=`/`?sub=`/`#hash`), keywords?, requires? (nav base path gate) }`. `search-index.test.ts` statically asserts unique ids, admin-relative paths, known `requires` values, and that **every `#hash` resolves to a real `id="…"` anchor** in `ConfigPageClient.tsx` (the one invariant tsc/eslint can't see). Adding a searchable setting = one entry here + a matching `id`/`admin-anchor` on the page.
- `deploy-log-translator.ts` - `translateLogLine(raw)`: maps Vercel build-log lines to friendly British-humour status messages (null = drop the line). Final line marker: "Bish bash bosh. You're live."
- `deploy-log-translator.test.ts` - vitest unit tests for the translator (run via `npm test`; no vitest config file exists).
- `markdown-client.ts` - browser-only markdown → sanitised HTML (marked + DOMPurify on `window`); identical allow-list to the server renderer.
- `sanitize.ts` - server/browser markdown → sanitised HTML; lazy-requires jsdom on the server; strips raw angle brackets pre-parse; also `markdownToPlainText`, `sanitizeRichText` (Puck RichText allow-list) and `sanitizeAndObfuscateRichText` (published RichText: sanitise first, obfuscate after - DOMPurify's re-serialisation decodes the obfuscator's entities, so the reverse order leaks the plain address; test: `lib/sanitize-obfuscate.test.ts`).
- `sanitize-config.ts` - shared `ALLOWED_TAGS`/`ALLOWED_ATTR` constants for both renderers.
- `email-obfuscate.tsx` - email spam-protection server half. `encodeEmail` = base64 of reversed address (the `data-eml` payload). For text: `linkifyEmails(text)` → React nodes (`<ObfuscatedEmail>` per match, entity-encoded visible text + `data-eml`); `obfuscateEmailsInHtml(html)` → same anchor markup spliced into text runs, entity-masking (not wrapping) inside `<a>`, rewriting a hand-written `href="mailto:…"` to `data-eml`, leaving `<code>/<pre>` verbatim. For owner-typed links: `emailSafeHref(href, obfuscate)` → `{href}` for ordinary links, `{'data-eml'}` and **no href** for a `mailto:` (query string preserved); `maskEmailText(label, obfuscate)` → entity-encoded `<span>` for label text inside an anchor, which can't be linkified without nesting an `<a>`. Consumed by every block in `config.tsx` (free text via the local `protectText` gate, hrefs via `emailSafeHref`) when `!puck.isEditing`, plus `MenuBlockClient.tsx`; client half is `components/EmailDeobfuscator.tsx`. Tests: `lib/email-obfuscate.test.ts`.
- `utils.ts` - `generateSlug`, `generateId` (nanoid), `parsePaginationParams` (page/perPage/skip, perPage ≤ 100), `errorResponse`, `successResponse`, `truncate`, `formatInTimezone`, `isHttpUrl` (2026-07-23). `isHttpUrl(value)` is the scheme allow-list for any owner- or member-supplied address that will end up in an `href` or an iframe `src`: it parses the trimmed value as a URL and accepts only `http:`/`https:`, so `javascript:` and `data:` (stored XSS) are rejected along with `mailto:`/`tel:`/relative values a website field is never meant to hold. Zod's `.url()` is not a substitute - it accepts `javascript:…` quite happily, which is exactly how a member `websiteUrl` reached the public profile page. Applied at every write path that stores such a URL (`app/api/members/profile/route.ts`, `app/api/admin/members/[id]/route.ts`) AND at the render path (`app/(public)/members/[username]/page.tsx`), since rows written before the guard existed are still in the database; also gates the Puck Embed block's `src` and, via a protocol test inside `toEmbedUrl`, the Video block's.

`lib/auth/`:

- `session.ts` - session + trusted-device create/validate/delete, cookie helpers, `listUserSessions`, `revokeSessionById`, `safeCompare` (timing-safe).
- `passkey.ts` - WebAuthn registration/authentication challenge creation and verification, `savePasskey`, `labelFromUserAgent`.
- `password.ts` - bcrypt hash/verify, strength check, Pwned Passwords check, `validateNewPassword`.
- `email-challenge.ts` - 6-digit OTP create/verify (10-min TTL, 5 attempts, hash compare).
- `rate-limit.ts` - action limits table (incl. Members system's `member_register`), `getClientIp`, `checkRateLimit`/`recordAttempt`, atomic `checkAndRecord` (raw INSERT … ON CONFLICT).
- `recovery.ts` - recovery token create/validate/consume (30-min TTL, single-use).
- `totp.ts` - secret generation, otpauth URI, QR data URL, `verifyTotpCode` with replay step guard.
- `turnstile.ts` - `verifyTurnstile` (fail-open unconfigured, fail-closed on error when configured).

`lib/config/`:

- `env.ts` - `isLocalMode`, `getEnvStatus` (single source of truth for the setup env-check and dashboard), `requiredEnvMissing`, `isEmailConfigured`, `isMediaProviderConfigured`, `getActiveMediaProvider`, `isMediaConfigured`, `configuredProxiedProviders`, `isGitHubConfigured`, `getGitHubConfigStatus`, `isVercelConfigured`, `isNeonConfigured`, `isEdgeConfigWritable`, `isTurnstileConfigured`, `getSiteUrl(+OrNull)`, `getWebAuthnRpId/Origin`, `getSessionSecret`.
- `site.ts` - 5-second in-memory caches for adminPath/status/pendingRedeployId (with the 4-minute redeploy auto-release), `invalidateSiteConfigCache`, `isSetupComplete`, the path/username BLOCKLIST, `isBlocklisted`, `generateSuggestedAdminPath`.
- `edge-config.ts` - Edge Config reads (`adminPath`, `siteStatus`) via `@vercel/edge-config`; `syncToEdgeConfig` writes via the Vercel REST API.
- `neon-regions.ts` - the 8 selectable Neon regions.

`lib/consent/`: `types.ts` (ConsentCategory/BannerConfig/Decision/CookiePayload + `DEFAULT_CONSENT_BANNER_CONFIG`), `gate.ts` (client: `hasConsent`, `onConsentChange`, `loadIfConsented`, `notifyConsentChange`; backs `window.cactusConsent`), `client.ts` (client: cookie names, `readCookie`/`writeCookie`, `getOrCreateConsentId`, `readStoredConsent`, `buildDefaultDecision`, `resolveCurrentDecision`, `saveConsentDecision` - shared by the banner and the privacy-page panel).

`lib/crypto/secrets.ts` - AES-256-GCM `encryptSecret`/`decryptSecret` using ENCRYPTION_KEY; format `iv:authTag:ciphertext` (hex).

`lib/members/`:

- `config.ts` - `MembersConfigSchema` (Zod, all Members settings with defaults: enabled false, registrationMode OPEN, emailVerificationRequired true, registrationCollectUsername/registrationCollectDisplayName/registrationCollectPassword true (off hides the field on the register form and makes the API ignore anything sent for it), authMethodPolicies { PASSKEY: OPTIONAL, MAGIC_LINK: OPTIONAL, PASSWORD: OFF }, trustedBrowserDays 30, sessionDays 30, avatar/gravatar toggles true, siteWideMembersOnly false + exceptions [], guestPreviewEnabled false, username changes off with 90/30-day cooldown/redirect, deletionGracePeriodDays 14, domain allow/blocklists [], profileVisibility PUBLIC, accountSectionsEnabled all true, accountSinglePage false (on: every enabled section is drawn down the overview and the core tabs scroll to it - see `account-layout.ts`), directoryEnabled false, smsTwoFactorPolicy OPTIONAL - OPTIONAL|REQUIRED, whether members with a password must enrol a mobile number for SMS sign-in codes; REQUIRED only bites while an SMS provider module is active, see `sms-policy.ts` below), `parseMembersConfig` (corrupt column falls back to defaults), `getMembersConfig`, `getMembersConfigCached` (5s TTL for proxy reads), `invalidateMembersConfigCache`. Also `AccountSectionKey` + `isAccountSectionEnabled(config, key)` - the one accessor for the account-tab switches, used by the tab bar, the Overview cards, the Profile page's own `notFound()` gate and the routes that page saves through. Also `AUTH_METHODS`/`AUTH_METHOD_LABELS` and the accessors `authMethodPolicy`/`registrationPasswordPolicy`/`isAuthMethodEnabled`/`isAuthMethodRequired`/`enabledAuthMethods` - every caller goes through these rather than reading the map directly, because `MAGIC_LINK`'s own type is only `OFF|OPTIONAL` (nothing to enrol: the credential is a verified mailbox, so REQUIRED would mean exactly what OPTIONAL already means) and a direct `=== 'REQUIRED'` on it is a type error. Each field carries a `.catch` so one unrecognised stored value falls back per method instead of dropping the whole members config - and with it `enabled` - back to defaults. `normaliseLegacyAuthMethods` reads rows written under the previous `allowedAuthMethods` array + `passwordsEnabled` boolean pair (both had to agree before passwords were offered, so only that combination maps to `PASSWORD: OPTIONAL`); nothing is written back, the first admin save persists the new shape and Zod drops the old keys. Covered by `lib/members/auth-policy.test.ts`.
- `account-layout.ts` - `ACCOUNT_SECTION_DEFS` (key/label/path/anchor for the five core sections, in tab order) + `accountSectionAnchor()`. Server-import-free by design: `AccountNav` is a client component, and the overview page, the nav and the summary-card links all read this one list so they cannot disagree about what exists or where it lives.
- `account-sections.ts` - `redirectWhenSinglePage(key)` (with `accountSinglePage` on, a section's own page redirects to its anchor on the overview - one canonical place rather than two pages that both work), `PROFILE_SECTION_OFF_MESSAGE` + `profileSectionOffResponse()`, the shared 403 returned by every route the member Profile page saves through (`/api/members/{profile,profile-visibility,avatar,username}`) when `accountSectionsEnabled.profile` is off. One message rather than four, so a member who left the page open before an admin switched it off gets a consistent answer. 403 not 404: the route exists, the site has stopped offering it, matching the `avatarUploadsEnabled` refusal alongside it.
- `auth-policy.ts` - what "required" actually means. `ENROLABLE_AUTH_METHODS = ['PASSKEY','PASSWORD']` (the two a member holds something for); `outstandingAuthSetup(config, held)` pure rules + `memberOutstandingAuthSetup(config, memberId)` I/O wrapper, returning the required methods a member has yet to set up - a password only counts as done once a verified `MemberTwoFactor` exists alongside it, since password login refuses outright without one and calling it satisfied would strand the member at the sign-in screen; `newMembersCanSignIn(config, emailConfigured)` (false without the email sign-in link: passkeys and passwords are both enrolled from inside an account a brand-new member cannot yet reach - drives the admin warning); `hasAnyAuthMethod(config)` (guards the settings save). Unit-tested in `lib/members/auth-policy.test.ts`.
- `paths.ts` - `MEMBER_INTERNAL = '/cactus-account'`, `DEFAULT_MEMBER_AREA_PATH = 'account'`, `getMemberAreaPath()` (sanitised MEMBER_AREA_PATH env var; invalid or blocklisted values fall back to the default, `account` itself exempt from the blocklist check), `MEMBER_PUBLIC_SUBPATHS = ['/login','/register','/verify-email']` and `isPublicMemberPath(fullPath, basePath)` (pure, unit-tested in `lib/members/paths.test.ts`; query-string tolerant, trailing-slash tolerant, prefix-exact so `/account/logins` does not match, and false for anything outside the member area so a site's own `/login` page is left alone). Used by the account layout's session gate and by the login page's redirect loop guard. Also `MEMBER_SETUP_SIGNIN_SUBPATH = '/setup-signin'` + `isSetupSignInPath(fullPath, basePath)` - the one page the required-setup gate must let through, or it would redirect to itself for ever; unlike the public subpaths it needs a session.
- `sms-policy.ts` - `memberNeedsSmsEnrolment(config, twoFactorConfigs)`: true only when `smsTwoFactorPolicy` is REQUIRED, the member has no verified SMS `MemberTwoFactor` row, AND an SMS provider module is active/configured (`getActiveSmsProvider`) - no provider means the policy silently behaves as OPTIONAL. Consumed by the password login + 2fa verify routes (`smsEnrolmentRequired` response flag → `LoginForm.tsx` `finishLogin` redirects to the account overview instead of `redirectTo`) and by the member account layout (warning banner, shown only to members who actually have a password).
- `tokens.ts` - hashed single-use tokens for member verification links (mirrors `lib/auth/recovery.ts`): `generateMemberToken`/`hashMemberToken`, `createVerificationToken`/`consumeVerificationToken` (`MemberVerificationToken`, 24h TTL), `canResendVerification` (60s per-member throttle, keyed off the latest token row regardless of used/unused).
- `registration.ts` - `isUsernameFormatValid`/`isUsernameAvailable` (format regex + blocklist + `Member.username` uniqueness), `generateUsernameFromEmail` (for sites with `registrationCollectUsername` off: email local part sanitised to `[a-z0-9_-]`, trimmed to 20 chars, `member` when nothing usable survives, plus 4 crypto-random digits - 8 after 15 collisions - re-checked through `isUsernameAvailable` each try and throwing after 25; covered by `lib/members/registration.test.ts`), `isEmailDomainAllowed` (allow/blocklist against `membersConfig`), `deriveInitialStatus`/`deriveActivatedStatus` (status a `Member` is created with vs. the status it moves to once verified, per `registrationMode`; verification is only "required" when both `emailVerificationRequired` is true AND email is actually configured, otherwise there'd be no way to ever satisfy it), `validateInviteToken`/`consumeInviteToken` (`MemberInvite`, single-use), `sendVerificationEmail` (shared by the register route and the resend route), `loginRejectionForStatus` (single source of truth for every login method: null when a status may sign in (ACTIVE only), else `{error, redirectToVerify?}`).
- `session.ts` - member session/cookie layer, fully separate from `lib/auth/session.ts`: `createMemberSession`/`validateMemberSession` (ACTIVE-only, sliding expiry) /`deleteMemberSession`/`deleteAllMemberSessions`/`listMemberSessions`/`revokeMemberSessionById`, cookie helpers (`cactus_member_session`), `getMemberFromCookie`; trusted-browser twin `createMemberTrustedBrowser`/`isMemberBrowserTrusted`/`revokeAllMemberTrustedBrowsers` (cookie `cactus_member_trusted`). Durations read from `membersConfig.sessionDays`/`trustedBrowserDays` via `getMembersConfigCached`.
- `passkey.ts` - WebAuthn registration/authentication for members, mirrors `lib/auth/passkey.ts` against `Member`/`MemberPasskey`; reuses `WebAuthnChallenge` with `memberId` set and `member_registration`/`member_authentication` purposes instead of a second challenge table.
- `magic-link.ts` - `sendMagicLink`/`consumeMagicLink`, hashed single-use `MemberMagicLink` tokens (15-min TTL, plain sha256 like `tokens.ts` - status gating happens at the route, not here).
- `email-challenge.ts` - mirrors `lib/auth/email-challenge.ts` against `MemberEmailChallenge`; `createMemberEmailChallenge(memberId, purpose, pendingEmail?)`/`verifyMemberEmailChallenge` (its success branch returns `pendingEmail`, the row's only survivor since verifying deletes it)/`pendingMemberEmailChange(memberId)`, purposes `login_2fa`/`setup_2fa`/`email_change`, 10-min TTL, 5 attempts, hash compare.
- `recovery-codes.ts` - `generateMemberRecoveryCodes` (10 codes, shown once, replaces any unused set), `consumeMemberRecoveryCode`, `countRemainingRecoveryCodes`.
- `activity.ts` - `recordMemberActivity` (`source: null` = core, else the contributing module name), `listMemberActivity`.
- `deletion.ts` - `requestMemberDeletion`/`cancelMemberDeletion` (grace period from `membersConfig.deletionGracePeriodDays`), `purgeScheduledDeletions` (cron target, hard-delete past the grace period).
- `export.ts` - `assembleMemberExport` (core tables + each active module's `memberExtensions.dataExportPath`, called over self-origin HTTP with an internal bearer derived from `SESSION_SECRET` - `verifyInternalExportBearer` is exported for a module's own handler to check it), `createDataExportRequest` (assemble→upload→ready, synchronously within the request; refuses a second request while one is in flight; deletes the stuck row on failure rather than leaving it stuck, since the schema has no FAILED status), `expireDataExports` (cron target, 48h).
- `admin-log.ts` - `logMemberAdminAction(actor, memberId, action, detail?)`, writes a `MemberAdminActionLog` row (actor snapshot, not a live relation - survives the admin user being deleted later).
- `admin-notify.ts` - `notifyAdminMemberPendingApproval`/`notifyAdminMemberDeletionRequested`: in-app alert (reuses the generic `message` `NotificationType` + `upsertAlert` dedupe - members have no dedicated notification type of their own) + an email to every protected-role admin when email is configured (both render through the registry now - `member.deletion-admin-notify` and the new `member.pending-approval-admin-notify`, which was the last inline send in here). Gating on `notifyAdminOnPendingApproval`/`adminNotifyOnDeletion` happens at the call site, not in here.
- `digest.ts` - `runDigest('DAILY'|'WEEKLY')`, see the Email section.
- `access.ts` - pure matching logic for `proxy.ts`'s Phase 8 site-access gate: `isPathExcepted`, `resolveRouteTier` (no I/O, unit-testable in isolation from the session/DB lookups that surround them in proxy.ts).
- `avatar.ts` - `resolveEffectiveAvatarChoice`, see Media Layer section.

`lib/db/prisma.ts` - global-singleton PrismaClient (query logging in development), extended with `stalePlanRetryExtension`: a `$allOperations` wrapper that replays a query once when Postgres rejects it with `cached plan must not change result type` (SQLSTATE 0A000). Migrations run in the build step against a database whose pooled connections outlive the deploy, so a migration adding a column leaves live backends holding prepared plans that no longer match the table and every query using one throws until replayed - this took the live shop's product pages, product editor and CSV export down after shop `006_supplier.sql` on 2026-07-19, and needed a Neon compute restart to clear. The extension covers raw queries as well as model calls, and every module imports this client, so the guard is platform-wide. `stalePlanRetryExtension` and the `ExtendedPrismaClient` type are exported: an extended client is structurally not a `PrismaClient` (no `$on`), so anything taking the shared client as a parameter is typed `ExtendedPrismaClient` (`lib/backup/restore.ts`, `lib/setup/stylesInfoPage.ts`), and clients built elsewhere (the backup round-trip test's throwaway database) apply the same extension so they behave like the one the site runs on.

`lib/db/stale-plan.ts` - `isStalePlanError` (matches on the message, deliberately not on SQLSTATE 0A000, which is Postgres's generic "feature not supported" and covers errors that must not be retried) and `retryOnStalePlan` (one replay only; the first failure is what evicts the stale plan). Unit-tested in `lib/db/stale-plan.test.ts` against the error shape captured from the live 2026-07-19 deployment log.

`lib/deploy/`: `lock.ts` (2026-07-23, expiry added 2026-08-17 - `acquireDeployLock(lockedBy, holdMs = DEFAULT_LOCK_HOLD_MS 90s)` stamps `DeployLock.expiresAt`; `isLockExpired`/`secondsUntilLockClears`/`lockBusyMessage` are pure and unit-tested in `lock.test.ts`; `STALE_LOCK_MS` (15 minutes) survives only as the fallback for rows carrying no expiry. `getActiveDeployLock()`, the single reader every acquire/check site uses for the `DeployLock` singleton: install, update, core update and uninstall. A lock is normally released by the handler that took it, by the Vercel deploy webhook or by the redeploy-status handler, but a function hard-killed by a Vercel timeout or OOM runs none of those, and the stranded row then made every later install/update return a permanent 409 "install in progress" with no way out from the UI. A lock older than the threshold is treated as orphaned, deleted, and reported as absent; the delete is scoped to the exact `id` + `lockedAt` pair so a fresh lock taken in the window between read and delete is never removed by mistake. The old "15 minutes comfortably exceeds the longest legitimate hold - a 60s route plus the Vercel build it triggers" reasoning was wrong twice over: every holder releases the lock BEFORE its build starts, so the true ceiling is the function's own `maxDuration 60`, and 15 minutes of lockout per failed attempt is punishing on a day when GitHub is degraded and each attempt dies at 60s), `reconcile.ts` (`markModulesDeploySucceeded` - promotes pendingVersion, clears alerts; `markModulesDeployFailed` - reverts to update_available or failed), `redeploy.ts` (`startDeferredRedeploy` - arms the redeploy gate synchronously, then in `after()` syncs modules.json or falls back to an env-var redeploy, and polls Vercel for the new deployment id). Both git-push paths (a modules.json commit, and `committedSince` mode where the caller already pushed) go through `captureOrTrigger`: poll first so the push's own build is adopted rather than double-deployed, then, only if no build ever appears, start one via `ensureVercelRedeploy`. Without that fallback a push that produces no build (missed webhook) is never retried by anything - the commit sits unbuilt while module rows are promoted to versions whose code never deployed.

`lib/design/tokens.ts` - `DesignTokens` v2 type, `DEFAULT_DESIGN_TOKENS`, `COLOUR_PRESETS`, `buildTokenStyles` (tokens → CSS custom properties for the public site), `buildAdminThemeStyles` (primary-colour family + `--font-sans` only, for admin white-labelling), `buildFontHref` (Google Fonts URL for non-system fonts). Every `themeStyle` colour has an optional `*Dark` sibling (`colourDark`, `hoverColourDark`, `textColourDark`, `bgColourDark`, `borderColourDark`, `labelColourDark`); `buildTokenStyles` emits each as a CSS var (`--color-link`, `--body-color`, `--btn-bg`, `--field-text`, `--h1-color`, …), redefines only the overridden ones in the `[data-theme="dark"]` + `@media(prefers-color-scheme:dark)` blocks, and its scoped `main …` rules reference those vars so a dark override cascades on the frontend (unset → inherits the light value). `ColourPreset` carries `linkColourDark`/`linkHoverColourDark` alongside the light pair, so applying a preset seeds dark-mode link colours too. `buttons.secondary`/`.outline` (`ButtonVariantStyle`) and `themeStyle.badges` (`Partial<Record<BadgeColourKey, BadgeStyle>>`, `BADGE_COLOUR_KEYS` export) follow the same optional-field/`*Dark`-sibling pattern; `themeStyle.pillRadius` is a plain string (no dark variant - a radius, not a colour), emitted as `--radius-pill` alongside the fixed `--radius-sm`/`-md`/`-lg` in the same `fixed` CSS-var string.

`lib/email/index.ts` - transport + the typed helpers, see Email section. `lib/email/registry.ts` - the single template registry (core defaults + the module seam). `lib/email/render.ts` - override lookup, `{{tag}}`/`{{#if}}` interpolation, wrapper resolution. `lib/email/blocks.ts` - the email block set as pure `toHtml()` functions (no React, no client imports; shared by the Puck editor config and the renderer). `lib/email/wrapper.ts` - walks an `emailWrapper` layout's Puck data into the final HTML document. `lib/email/palette.ts` - design tokens flattened to colour/font lookups (client-safe, so the layout editor can use it too). `lib/email/templates.ts` - the members-only sending rule (notification-preference gate) that survived the move.

`lib/github/client.ts` - see GitHub API Integration. `lib/github/retry.ts` - shared Git Data API resilience: `isTransientGitError` (BadObjectState / 5xx / "not a fast forward" / "Reference does not exist" / secondary rate limit), `retryTransient` (8-attempt equal-jitter backoff, cap 60s), `createReplicatedBlob` (createBlob + read-back confirm before referencing in a tree). Used by `lib/updates/core.ts` (`syncCoreFromUpstream`) and `lib/modules/github.ts` (`commitModulesJson`) - both now wrap the whole createTree→createCommit→updateRef write in `retryTransient`, re-reading HEAD each attempt so replication lag and HEAD races self-heal.

`lib/layout/`: `displayConditions.ts` (rule types, match + specificity scoring), `resolveThemeLayout.ts` (best published layout for a type/context), `starter-templates.ts` (**the single source of truth for starter templates** - `CORE_STARTER_TEMPLATES: Record<layoutType, StarterTemplate[]>` = header ×14 / footer ×5 / infoPage ×4 / notFound ×4 / statusPage ×4 / emailWrapper ×4 (Default Email `publishByDefault`, Plain, Branded, Blank), plus block-prop helpers; `getStarterTemplates(type)` merges core with the module-declared ones from the generated `lib/setup/module-starter-layouts.ts`, `allStarterTemplates()` flattens the lot for the seeder. **Must stay free of server-only imports** - the new-layout picker imports it straight into the browser. A `StarterTemplate` is `{id, name, description, data, publishByDefault?, defaultConditions?}`. Replaces both the old DB-seeded starter rows *and* the separate hardcoded `STARTERS_BY_TYPE` map that used to live inside `layouts/new/page.tsx` - the two had already drifted, 13 header variants vs 9), `layout-type-tabs.ts` (`CORE_LAYOUT_TYPES`, `TYPE_LABELS`, `CORE_TYPE_TABS`, `MODULE_GROUP_TABS` - shared by the Layouts list and the picker so their tab sets cannot disagree, which they previously did).

`lib/media/`: `providers.ts`, `loader.ts`, `upload.ts` (also `downloadMedia`, `deleteMedia`, `saveMediaRecord`, `getMediaReferences`), `migration.ts` - see Media Layer.

`lib/menu/resolve.ts` - `resolveMenu` (published-page filtering, nested tree build), `resolveMainMenu`.
