`lib/modules/`: `manifest.ts` (zod schemas for `cactus.module.json` and `cactus.theme.json`, `parseGitHubRepo` strict URL validation, `fetchManifestFromRepo`, `validateTablePrefixUnique`; **`fetchManifestFromRepo(repoUrl, filename, ref = 'HEAD')` gained the `ref` argument (2026-07-23)** - install and update now pass the `release.tag` they are actually shipping, so `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`/permissions are validated against the released manifest rather than whatever is on the default branch; `HEAD` remains the default only for callers that genuinely want the latest; gained an optional `memberExtensions` field - `activityTypes[]`, `notificationCategories[]`, `dataExportPath?`, `routeTiers[]` - for modules to declare Members-system contributions, see MEMBERS_SPEC.md amendment 5), `member-extensions.ts` (live reads of every active module's `memberExtensions`: `getModuleActivityTypes`, `getModuleNotificationCategories`, `getModuleDataExportPaths`, `getModuleRouteTiers` (+ `getModuleRouteTiersCached`, 5s TTL, for `proxy.ts`); pure data, no codegen step needed since none of it is a component import, unlike `extensionPoints`/`settingsTabs`), `github.ts` (`getLatestRelease` by channel, `syncModulesJson`, `getLatestDeploymentStatus`), `updates.ts` (`findModuleUpdates` - pure detection), `compat.ts` (2026-07-23 - `checkModuleUpdateCompat({ repoUrl, coreVersion, installed, ref })`: reads the manifest at the tag about to be installed and returns a short human-readable reason when the running core or the installed module set does not satisfy `requiresCoreVersion`/`requiresModules`, or null when it is fine. This is the pre-check the single-module install/update paths always ran, lifted out so the BULK "Update all modules" path applies it per module too - it previously pinned every latest tag blindly, so one incompatible module could break every future build on a missing import. Incompatible modules now land in `failed[]` instead of in `modules.json`. A manifest that cannot be fetched returns null (compatible), matching the single-module path, so a transient GitHub hiccup never blocks an otherwise-fine update), `router.ts` (AUTO-GENERATED, gitignored - API dispatch + page loaders for installed modules).

`lib/notifications/`: `alerts.ts` (`upsertAlert` keyed by dedupeKey - re-surfaces on title change; `clearAlert`; `recordCoreUpdate`; `recordModuleUpdate`), `deployment.ts` (`recordDeploymentNeeded` rolling reasons list, `getUnreadCount`, `labelForEnvKeys`).

`lib/permissions/check.ts` - see Permissions System.

`lib/privacy/template.ts` - privacy-policy generator: `WizardAnswers` type, `DATA_COLLECTED_OPTIONS`, `PURPOSE_OPTIONS`, `DISCLAIMER_TEXT`, `assemblePolicyMarkdown` (jurisdiction-aware GDPR/CCPA sections).

`lib/puck/`: `config.tsx` (all block definitions + per-context configs; TipTap HTML conversion for RSC richtext), `siteLogoAlign.ts` (`LOGO_ALIGN_OPTIONS` + `siteLogoAlign()`, shared by SiteLogo's two render halves so the editor and live markup cannot drift), `module-components.ts` (AUTO-GENERATED, gitignored), `editor-routes.ts` (`isPuckEditorRoute(pathname)` - the single definition of "this route is a full-viewport Puck editor", consumed only by `AdminShell`; matches `/pages/<id>`, `/layouts/<id>` and the legacy `/appearance/header|footer`, and deliberately NOT `/pages/new` or `/layouts/new`, which are an ordinary form and the starter-template picker. Unit-tested in `editor-routes.test.ts` because getting it wrong strips a normal admin page's padding and scrollbar, which typechecks fine), `resolveTemplateData.ts`, `renderInfoPage.tsx` (`resolveContentData`, `renderInfoPageContent`), `renderLayoutWithContent.tsx` (injects page content into a layout's ContentSlot), `MediaPickerField.tsx` (`OgImagePickerField`, `ImageUrlPickerField`, `withImagePickerFields` - media-library modal fields + the helper that swaps a config's image URL text fields for the picker in both editors; the shared `MediaPickerModal` now has a "+ Upload" button in its header that POSTs the chosen file to `/api/admin/media` and auto-selects the returned item, so the Image / Image+Floating Chips / Card / OG-image pickers can add a brand-new image without leaving the block, not just pick an existing one; the modal also browses the media folder tree - breadcrumb + subfolder tiles from `/api/admin/media/folders`, media scoped per-folder, search spans all folders), `MenuCheckboxField.tsx`, `MenuSelectField.tsx`, `MinMaxPairField.tsx` (two plain text inputs side-by-side in one custom field slot - min/max pair, used by MenuBlock's fluid spacing/letter-spacing/font-size fields), `UnitValueField.tsx` (`UnitValueField` + `ResponsiveUnitValueField` - number box + unit dropdown for CSS lengths, per-field `units:` list, stores the plain CSS string so saved data/render paths are untouched; responsive variant rides `ResponsiveFieldShell`; used by every length field that was previously free text - grid column widths, sticky offsets, image max-width, embed height, header shrunk height, underline thickness/offset, Section/Spacer custom sizes), `MenuBlockEditorPreview.tsx` (editor-side MenuBlock preview with live menu fetch), `SiteColourField.tsx` (palette swatch picker, dual light/dark preview per swatch, + custom native-picker swatch; optional `allowManual` prop adds a free-text CSS-colour box under the swatches - used by the border/icon/text-colour fields that were previously bare text inputs), `SiteFontField.tsx` (font-family picker for block fields - site fonts first, then Google Fonts catalogue search, free text allowed) + `useSiteFonts.ts` (cached `/api/admin/appearance` fonts fetch, mirrors `useSiteColours`), `BorderField.tsx` (show/hide + colour-swatch field, one box - colour swatches hide entirely when `show: 'hide'`), `useSiteColours.ts` (shared cached `/api/admin/appearance` fetch behind both of the above, avoids remount flicker), `SiteLogoEditorPreview.tsx` + `useSiteBranding.ts` (cached `/api/admin/config` fetch, injects real branding logo into the `SiteLogo` block's editor preview), `BgColorField.tsx` (`SectionBgColorField`/`HeroBgColorField`/`HeaderBgColorField`/`PageBgColorField` - background mode select + a mode-aware second input, one box: colour swatches only for the solid-colour modes (`color`, `transparent-scroll` - the SWATCH_MODES set), a CSS-gradient text box for `gradient`, and nothing at all for none/transparent/image/decorative modes, whose `color` value never paints. Shared body takes `allowOpacity` + `allowDark` flags (both on for Section + Hero only). `allowOpacity` adds a "Colour opacity" 0-100 slider for `mode: color`; a translucent colour is stored as `color-mix(in srgb, <base> N%, transparent)` - via `splitBgColour`/`composeBgColour` round-trip - so it still rides a `var(--color-N)` (rgba() can't). `allowDark` adds a "Dark mode colour" swatch row; when set, the whole value is encoded as CSS `light-dark(<light>, <dark>)` (round-tripped by `splitLightDark`/`composeLightDark`, paren-aware split since each arm may be a color-mix). The site sets `color-scheme: light|dark` with its theme (globals.css), so the browser resolves the right arm with NO render-side change - Section/Hero already paint `backgroundColor: color`. Lets a section/hero background colour be made see-through (translucent card over a hero photo) AND carry a separate colour per light/dark mode. One opacity applies to both arms), `ColourSwatchButton.tsx` (shared swatch button w/ hover tooltip, used by `SiteColourField`/`BorderField`/`BgColorField`; also exports `CustomColourSwatch` - a rainbow swatch wrapping a hidden native colour picker, appended to all three swatch rows so any colour can be set, not just the palette, storing a raw hex - and `isCustomColour` helper), `components/AosInit.tsx` (AOS init client component), `components/MenuBlockClient.tsx` (public interactive menu: dropdowns, mobile hamburger, and a per-breakpoint "Nav behaviour" of show/collapse-to-hamburger/dropdown-current-page - the `navToggle` responsive field; dropdown mode shows a current-page trigger via `NavDropdown`, revealed by `cactus-nav-dd-*` breakpoint classes from `buildTokenStyles`; the trigger carries `data-menu-dd-id="<block id>"` and takes two newer controls - the per-breakpoint **`navButtonWidth`** field (`auto` = fits its text, the old and default behaviour / `full` = spans its slot, which also sends the bars to the far edge like a select; at `auto` there is no free space so both render identically), and **`fitOneLine`**, which used to reach only the inline list: the trigger now also caps at `max-width:100%` and shrinks its label via `HeadingFitText` rather than wrapping to a second line or overflowing its column), `menuNavButton.ts` (`navButtonWidthCss()` - the dropdown trigger's per-breakpoint width rule, kept out of the client component so it is one shared emitter and unit-testable; `menuNavButton.test.ts`), `components/SiteLogoClient.tsx` (logo/site-name link with hover state), `components/ScaleToFit.tsx` (client wrapper that shrinks any content to fit its grid column via `transform:scale`, opt-in per column via Grid `col*Scale`; also see `getGridTemplateColumns` now using `minmax(0, W)` not `minmax(min-content, W)` so a set column width is honoured instead of propped open by content), `components/MembersBlocksRsc.tsx` (Members system Puck blocks' live async RSC render functions - see Puck Integration section).
- `lib/puck/tabs/`: `createPanelPlugin.tsx` (shared sidebar-tab factory + hand-rolled lucide-style tab icons), `rootFieldsOverride.tsx` (`hideRootFieldsOverride`), `headerBackLinkOverride.tsx` (`createBackLinkOverride(href, label)` - `overrides.header` factory that overlays a back-arrow link into Puck's own header, in the blank gutter it already reserves left of its title on desktop; see Puck Integration), `sidebarOverrides.css` (global CSS matched by class-name-prefix substring since `@puckeditor/core` hashes its CSS Modules class names - see Puck Integration), `LayoutSettingsTab.tsx`, `PageSettingsTab.tsx`, `SeoTab.tsx`, `PageHistoryTab.tsx`, `SavedBlocksTab.tsx`.
- `lib/puck/outline/`: `OutlineTree.tsx` (default export, wired as `overrides.outline` in both editors - draggable replacement for Puck's select-only Outline tab; pointer-event drag, drop indicator, auto-expand on hover, panel autoscroll, Alt+arrow keyboard moves), `tree.ts` (pure tree logic, no React: `buildOutline` walks root content + slot props + legacy `data.zones`, `indexOutline`/`ancestorIds`/`zoneIsInsideItem` for parent lookup and the drop-into-own-subtree guard, `flattenOutline` for visible rows, `computeMove` for Puck's remove-then-insert index shift), `tree.test.ts` (unit tests - the index shift and the subtree guard are the two things that silently corrupt a page if wrong).
- `lib/layout/layout-type-labels.ts` - `getLayoutTypeLabel(type)`: human label for a layout type (`Header`/`Footer`/`Page Layout`/`404`/`Status Page`, or the generated module-type label via `moduleLayoutTypeToGroup`). Used for Puck's `headerTitle` prop in `LayoutPuckEditor.tsx`.

`lib/setup/`: `starterLayouts.ts` - **no longer seeds starter rows**; starter templates are in-code data (`lib/layout/starter-templates.ts`). Jobs, deliberately kept apart:
  - `seedDefaultLayouts(db)` (**install only** - `/api/setup/complete`, `reset-database`): for each template flagged `publishByDefault` (core's default header/footer/full-width page/404 hero/coming-soon/maintenance, plus module templates whose pages have no hardcoded fallback, i.e. Shop's), seeds **one ordinary published Layout** at id `<template-id>-live` with the template's `defaultConditions`. Create-only upsert. The `-live` suffix is load-bearing: existing installs' live layouts already sit there, and renaming it would seed them a second header.
  - `seedPendingModuleLayouts(db)` (**request time**, from `ensureLayoutsCurrent()`): seeds any `active`/`inactive`/`update_available` module still carrying a **NULL** `layoutsSeededAt` whose code is in this build, then stamps it. Covers both the reconcile that ran on a build without the module's code (skipped unstamped) and the stamps `core-reconcile/009` cleared. It lives on a request path because reconcile only runs when a *module* deploy finishes - a site whose Shop was already mis-stamped would otherwise stay 404ing until the owner happened to install or update another module. **NULL-only**, so it can never re-mint a layout an owner deleted: a seeded module keeps its stamp regardless of what happens to the rows afterwards. Runs *after* the prune, so a module's fresh layouts are never binned by the same pass that made them, and outside the version gate (recovery must not wait for the next core update). `planPendingModuleSeeds(pending, inBuild)` is the **pure, unit-tested** half (5 cases in `starterLayouts.test.ts`).
  - `ensureLayoutsCurrent()` (**request time** - `app/(public)/layout.tsx`, `GET /api/admin/layouts`): runs `pruneLegacyStarterCopies` once per core version, gated on `SiteConfig.starterTemplatesVersion` vs `package.json` (module-level flag = one `SiteConfig` query per warm instance; a failed run leaves the stamp unwritten so a later request retries), then `seedPendingModuleLayouts` on every warm instance. **Never re-creates a layout a seeded module once had** - an existing site has its layouts already, and seeding a second `entire_site` header into it would silently change its design (Tester's live header is `starter-header-tall-live`, not `starter-header-live`, so a naive re-seed would have done exactly that).
  - `pruneLegacyStarterCopies(db)`: deletes the `<id>-live`/`<id>-edited` copies the old scheme spawned - its migration branch keyed off `status === 'published'`, which every starter row also was, so it minted a `<id>-live` copy of **every** starter on **every** core update (Tester had accumulated 54 published-but-condition-less rows + 21 `-edited` "(Copy)" drafts on top of 68 starters = 158 Layout rows). Deciding these is a **content** comparison against the in-code templates, which SQL cannot do, so it stays at runtime. **The starter rows themselves are NOT deleted here** - `prisma/core-reconcile/005_retire_starter_layouts.sql` does that at build time. That split is load-bearing, not cosmetic: the reconcile drops the `isStarter` column during the build, so a runtime `where: { isStarter: true }` would run *after* the column was gone, throw, get swallowed by `ensureLayoutsCurrent`'s catch, leave the stamp unwritten, and strand the rows forever. Delete-then-drop, in one SQL file, in that order. Everything this function keys on (row id, display conditions, `builderData`) survives the drop.
  - `planStarterCleanup(rows, templates)` - **pure, unit-tested** (`starterLayouts.test.ts`). Deletes a row only when all three hold: id is `<known-template-id>-live` or `-edited`; `displayConditions.include` is empty (renders nowhere); and `builderData` still `stableStringify`-equals the canonical template (nobody edited it). Anything the owner touched, published, or built fails one of the three and survives. `stableStringify` sorts object keys at every depth so a jsonb round-trip (Postgres does not preserve key order) still compares equal.

  `stylesInfoPage.ts` (`upsertStylesInfoPage` - seeds the draft `style-guide` page; `STYLES_PAGE_SLUG`/`TITLE`).

`lib/updates/core.ts` - `compareVersions`, `getCoreUpdateStatus` (channel-aware, cached 10 min / errors 30 s, aggregates release notes for all newer releases), `syncCoreFromUpstream` (reconcile-toward-target push, see GitHub API Integration), `invalidateCoreUpdateCache`; re-exports `planCoreSync`/`isSkippedCorePath`. `lib/updates/core-plan.ts` - pure dependency-free reconciliation planner `planCoreSync` (writes = target blob sha ≠ base blob sha; deletes = core-managed + removed upstream + present in base; none if base tree truncated) + `isSkippedCorePath`; unit-tested by `lib/updates/core.plan.test.ts`. `lib/updates/deadline.ts` - `ROUTE_WORK_BUDGET_MS` (60s ceiling minus `DEADLINE_HEADROOM_MS` 10s), `deadlineFromNow`, `msRemaining`, `assertWithinDeadline(deadlineAt, phase)`, `DeadlineExceededError`, `isDeadlineError`; unit-tested by `deadline.test.ts`. Consumed by `syncCoreFromUpstream({deadlineAt})` and `retryTransient({deadlineAt})` (`lib/github/retry.ts`, which will not sleep a backoff past the deadline). `lib/updates/read-json-response.ts` - `readJsonResponse(res, fallback)` + `UPDATE_TIMED_OUT_MESSAGE`; never throws a parser error at the owner, maps a 502/503/504 or an HTML body to the timed-out message, prefers the handler's own `error` field otherwise; unit-tested by `read-json-response.test.ts`; used by the core-update dialog and all four Modules page handlers. `lib/github/health.ts` - `checkGitHubHealth()` / `gitHubOutageNote()` / `resetGitHubHealthCache()`: reads `githubstatus.com/api/v2/summary.json` (60s cache, 2.5s timeout, any failure reports healthy) and names non-operational components among API Requests / Git Operations / Webhooks; called only on update failure. `lib/updates/github-outage.ts` - `looksLikeGitHubProblem(message)` (case-insensitive match on GitHub-side failure signatures: `resource not accessible by integration`, bad gateway / service unavailable / internal server error, `BadObjectState`, "was submitted too quickly", rate limit, socket hang up / ECONNRESET / ETIMEDOUT / ENOTFOUND / fetch failed / network error, plus `http 5xx` / `status: 5xx`, and this codebase's own `timed out` / `ran out of time` / `responding slowly` / `github is currently reporting problems`), `GITHUB_OUTAGE_HINT`, `GITHUB_STATUS_URL` (`https://www.githubstatus.com/`). Consumed by the core-update confirm dialog (`app/cactus-admin/config/ConfigPageClient.tsx`) and the Modules page alert (`app/cactus-admin/modules/page.tsx`), which append the hint + status-page link under the raw error when it matches.

`lib/vercel/`: `deploy.ts` (`triggerVercelRedeploy` - redeploy latest production deployment; `ensureVercelRedeploy` - same but adopts an already-in-flight production deploy instead of stacking another. Both build via `createRedeploy`, which passes `withLatestCommit: true` alongside `deploymentId`: without it Vercel inherits the source deployment's gitSource *including its commit sha*, so a "redeploy" replays the last-deployed commit rather than the branch's current HEAD - correct-looking whenever the two coincide, and a silent rollback when they don't), `env.ts` (list/upsert/delete project env vars; sensitive-key typing - sensitive vars skip the `development` target; `SENSITIVE_KEYS` set, which now includes `CRON_SECRET`), `cron-secret.ts` (`ensureCronSecret()` / `cronSecretSatisfied()` - see the `CRON_SECRET` entry under Environment variables; `cron-secret.test.ts` pins the never-overwrite and mint-fresh-each-time behaviour).

### Components

Admin (`components/admin/`):

- `AdminShell.tsx` - sidebar shell: mobile drawer, collapsible rail (persisted in localStorage, auto-collapse inside Puck editors - "inside a Puck editor" is `isPuckEditorRoute` from `lib/puck/editor-routes.ts`, which also decides the `admin-content--puck` chrome class), toolbar (collapse toggle, command-palette search button, ThemeToggle, NotificationBell), wraps children in `AdminPathProvider`; renders `DeployStatusBar` as a full-width strip above the whole shell (sidebar included) on every admin page; mounts `CommandPalette` once for the whole admin. Props: adminPath, siteName, version, sections (server-resolved `ResolvedNavSection[]`), moduleSettingsTabs (permission-filtered `{id,label}[]` of module Settings tabs, forwarded to `CommandPalette` for search), unreadCount, faviconUrl, faviconDarkUrl, sessionExpiresInMs (mounts `SessionExpiryWatcher` when present), children. Sidebar logo swaps `/cactus.svg` for the admin's uploaded favicon (via `resolveBranding()` in `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx`, `faviconUrl`/`faviconDarkUrl` - light/dark pair shown/hidden by the existing `data-logo-variant` + `data-theme` CSS toggle) once one's set, falling back to the Cactus mark otherwise; `.admin-sidebar-logo-text` wraps the site name onto up to 2 lines (`-webkit-line-clamp: 2`) before ellipsis-truncating, instead of clipping to one line.
- `SessionExpiryWatcher.tsx` - client component mounted once by `AdminShell`. Anchors a deadline at mount from the `expiresInMs` prop (client clock, so server/client skew can't sign anyone out early), shows a fixed bottom-right warning banner for the last 2 minutes with a live countdown and a "Sign in again" button, then navigates to `/<adminPath>/login?next=<path>&expired=1`. Timers re-arm in ≤15-minute chunks and recheck on `visibilitychange`/`focus` (background tabs throttle timers, sleeping laptops stop them). No polling, no network calls. Banner is non-blocking on purpose so unsaved work can still be saved; countdown is `aria-hidden` with a static `sr-only` sentence beside it so screen readers aren't re-announced to every second. Props: expiresInMs, adminPath.
- `DeployStatusBar.tsx` - always-mounted, self-hiding slim strip pinned (sticky) to the very top of the admin shell, above sidebar and content. Reads the shared client deploy-status store (`lib/deploy-status-client.ts`); shows spinner + state badge + latest translated log line, or a Dismiss button on failure. The store does the polling: `/api/admin/redeploy-status` until the `'pending'` sentinel resolves to a real deployment id (2s), then `/api/setup/deployment-logs` (4s); on READY tail-done it clears the gate (`DELETE /api/admin/redeploy-status`), drops the update-check sessionStorage cache and `window.location.reload()`s. `announceRedeployStarted()` (same store) is called by every redeploy-triggering client action - it flips the store active immediately and fires the `cactus:redeploy-started` window event, which pops the notification bell open.
- `AdminNav.tsx` - renders the server-resolved `sections` prop (`ResolvedNavSection[]` from `resolveAdminMenu`); no hardcoded nav array any more. Each item row is a link + hover pin (favourite) star + optional restricted badge (lock/eye-off, admins only) + route-change loading spinner; module icons are still manifest-supplied SVG innerHTML (sanitised server-side) or a fallback icon. Above the sections: a filter box (live-filters items to a flat result list), a Quick "New…" menu (deep-links collected from visible items' `createAction`), and an expand/collapse-all button. Optional Favourites and Recently-visited groups (both `localStorage`: `cactus-sidebar-favourites`, `cactus-sidebar-recents`) render above the real sections. That tools row and the Favourites group sit together in a `.admin-nav-pinned` wrapper that is `position: sticky; top: 0` inside `.admin-sidebar-nav-scroll` (needs `z-index` because the rows below are positioned; `background: var(--admin-sidebar-bg)` so scrolled rows don't show through), so both stay put while the rest of the tree scrolls; Favourites itself (`.admin-nav-pinned-favs`) is capped at `40vh` with its own scrollbar so a long pinned list can't swallow the rail, and a `ResizeObserver` keeps the scroll container's `scroll-padding-top` matched to the pinned block's height so scroll-into-view never parks the active item underneath it. Neither renders on the collapsed rail. Up/Down arrow keys rove focus between items; navigating auto-expands the active item's section and scrolls it into view. Section labels still toggle+persist per-label (`cactus-sidebar-sections-collapsed`); collapsed-rail tooltips (portal `.admin-nav-tip`) + account/sign-out/version(→`AboutModal`) footer unchanged. Props: adminPath, version, sections, collapsed, onNavClick.
- `CommandPalette.tsx` - Cmd/Ctrl+K command palette. Subsequence match (`scoreCommand`) over: every sidebar destination + `createAction` shortcut, **plus the static deep-settings index** `lib/admin/search-index.ts` (every Settings tab, the sections inside them, and individual settings - backup, SMTP, roles, cookie banner, colours, etc.). Each index entry matches on label **and** keyword synonyms (label hits rank above keyword hits above breadcrumb hits) and carries a breadcrumb hint + a deep-link `path` (query `?tab=`/`?sub=` and/or a `#section` hash). Deep entries are gated by `requires` (a nav base path): only offered when that page is visible in the user's resolved sidebar, so search never links to a screen the role hides. Also indexes **module-provided Settings tabs** (Shop, Gazette, …) as `${label} settings` → `/config?tab=<id>`, from the `moduleSettingsTabs` prop the admin layout resolves (permission-filtered server-side from each active module's `manifest.settingsTabs`, gated by the tab's own permission in the layout's existing batch query). Up/Down + Enter to jump (`router.push`); when the target `href` has a `#`, also fires a `cactus:scroll-hash` window event so a same-tab hash-only jump still scrolls. Esc to close; `?` (when not typing) opens the shortcuts overlay. Portals to `document.body`; also opened by `AdminShell`'s toolbar search button via `cactus:open-command-palette`. Props: adminPath, sections, moduleSettingsTabs?.
- `useScrollToHash.ts` - hook: scrolls the element named by the current URL hash into view (retries ~2s so it lands after tab-gated content mounts), then flashes it (`.admin-search-target-flash`). Listens to `hashchange` + the palette's `cactus:scroll-hash` event; re-attempts when caller-passed `deps` change (e.g. active tab). Powers the command-palette "jump straight to this setting" deep links. Used by `ConfigPageClient` (Settings). Anchors are plain `id="…"` + `className="admin-anchor"` (`scroll-margin-top` in globals.css) on the page's section wrappers.
- `AboutModal.tsx` - About Cactus Foundation dialog opened from the sidebar version number. Cactus mark (`/cactus.svg`) + name + slogan + blurb + grouped credits roll (from `lib/about/credits.ts` `ABOUT`/`CREDITS`, includes a Claude Code credit), footer with a "Release notes" button. That button opens a second stacked overlay `ReleaseNotesModal` (same file) which infinite-scrolls the full release history from `GET /api/admin/release-notes?page=N` (15/page), newest-first, rendering each release's sanitized notes HTML. **Portals to `document.body`** via `createPortal` (gated on a `useSyncExternalStore` mounted check) - required because `AdminNav` mounts it inside `.admin-sidebar` (`position: sticky`, which always creates its own stacking context), so a non-portaled `position: fixed` overlay nested there paints within that context and gets covered by `<main>` regardless of z-index. `ReleaseNotesModal` doesn't need its own portal call, it renders inside the already-portaled tree. Both layers are token-styled overlays (backdrop-click + Escape close; release notes on top; each `Overlay` sets `isolation: isolate`). Colours/radii via CSS vars only; header/body/footer rows each set their own `background: var(--color-bg)` and the card clips with `overflow: hidden`.
- `AdminPathContext.tsx` - React context (default `cactus-admin`); `useAdminPath()`.
- `LayoutPreview.tsx` - a small structural drawing of a layout, **derived from that layout's own Puck `data`** (`{type, data, height?}`). Containers (`Grid` cols/`columnSizes`, `Split` `ratio` + `zones`, `Section` `maxWidth`, `Group` `direction`/`justify`) give the shape; leaf blocks become boxes and bars (`SiteLogo`, `MenuBlock`, `LoginButton`, `ThemeToggle`, `SocialLinks`, `Copyright`, `Heading`, `TextBlock`, `Callout`, `Hero` (height from `minHeight`), `ContentSlot` (the dashed primary well - the one thing a page layout must show)). Header/footer render as a band with a ghost page body behind it, sized from `root.props.height` and inset from `maxWidth`, with the bottom/top border reflecting `border.show`. **Unknown block types - i.e. every block a module ships - fall back to a plain box**, with shape hints keyed on ordinary English words in the type name (`/Header$/`, `/List|Grid|Browser/`, `/Body|Comments|Detail/`); no module is named anywhere, so a module gets previews for free and core stays clean. Used by both the Layouts list cards and the starter picker; replaces the old `LayoutThumbnail` that guessed a layout's shape from substrings of its **name** (`n.includes('sidebar')`). Colour tokens only, no hex.
- `NotificationBell.tsx` - bell + unread badge, portal dropdown listing notifications with view/redeploy/read-toggle/delete actions (same handlers as the notifications page). The dropdown header carries "Mark all read" / "Delete all" text buttons (`.admin-bell-dropdown-headaction`) hitting the collection route, so they cover the whole table rather than the twenty rows the bell holds; both share the per-item loading/error maps under the `__bulk__` sentinel key. Delete all is disabled when nothing held passes the local `isDeletable()` (the mirror of the endpoint's open-deployment guard) and re-fetches afterwards rather than blanking the list. While a redeploy is in flight the dropdown shows a compact live status section at the top (spinner, state badge, ~3-line scrollable translated log fed by `lib/deploy-status-client.ts`); the dropdown auto-opens on the `cactus:redeploy-started` window event. Also renders the **live media-upload batch** (`UploadSection`) as its own section below the deploy status, fed by the shared `lib/upload-status-client.ts` store (subscribed via `useSyncExternalStore`) - per-file progress bars, a Clear for finished files, per-file dismiss; these entries have **no read/unread state** and don't touch `unreadCount`. The bell shows the spinner (not the count badge) while uploads are active, and auto-opens on the `cactus:upload-started` window event. Props: adminPath, unreadCount, collapsed.
- `SequenceProgress.tsx` - live progress bar for one scroll-sequence conversion, rendered on that job's notification in **both** the bell dropdown and the notifications page. Self-polls `GET /api/admin/media/sequence-status?jobId=` every 5s while the job is queued/running (that route proxies the worker's live figure AND rewrites the notification, so the bar is also what keeps the stored progress moving once the convert dialog is closed); its own polled value supersedes the server-rendered one until the job's `state` prop changes. On done/error it stops, calls `onSettled?.()` and `router.refresh()` **once** (`settledRef`), so the finished notification's button appears without a manual reload. Renders `.admin-seq-progress*` classes (globals.css); no hex. Props: jobId, state, progress (0-100|null), detail, onSettled?.
- `DeployLogViewer.tsx` - renders translated deploy-log messages (via `translateLogLine`), deduped, last 8 visible, `onComplete` on the final line. Props: rawLines, onComplete, onError.
- `UnsavedChangesModal.tsx` - cancel/discard/save-and-leave dialog. Props: pendingHref, saving, message, onCancel, onDiscard, onSave?.
- `useUnsavedChanges.ts` - hook: `dirtyRef` + beforeunload warning + in-app link interception → `pendingHref`.
- `TabStrip.tsx` - shared underline-style horizontal tab bar (flush edges, no side gaps); scrolls with edge fade + click arrow overlay when tabs overflow. Items render as `<Link>` (if `href`) or `<button>` (if `onClick`). Props: items (key, label, href?, onClick?, active), trailing?, style?. Used by Settings, Appearance→Styles, Layouts, and by Gazette/Boards/Contact-form module nav and list tabs.

Public/shared:

- `components/ThemeToggle.tsx` - light/auto/dark toggle; persists `cactus-theme`, applies `data-theme`, follows system in auto. `style` prop selects one of 6 presentations (`segmented` icon pill (default), `text` label pill, `expand` icon+hover menu, `dropdown` icon+click menu, `switch` two-state sun/moon slider light↔dark no-auto, `cycle` single icon click-to-step); admin `collapsed` prop still forces `cycle` regardless of `style`. Shared `useThemeMode` hook + `ThemeMenu` popover; CSS for all variants in `app/globals.css` (`.theme-toggle--text`, `.theme-switch*`, `.theme-menu-wrap`/`.tt-menu*`). 2026-08-03: optional `appearance` prop (`ThemeToggleAppearance`) + exported pure helper `themeToggleVars()` (unit-tested in `components/ThemeToggle.vars.test.ts`) turn `variant`/`iconSize`/`iconColour`/`bgColour`/`borderColour`/`borderRadius` into `--tt-*` custom properties set inline on the cycle button (and on `.theme-menu-wrap` for expand/dropdown, which inherits to the trigger). `.theme-toggle-cycle` in globals.css now reads `--tt-box`/`--tt-pad`/`--tt-radius`/`--tt-bg`/`--tt-border`/`--tt-shadow`/`--tt-fg` (+ `--tt-bg-hover`/`--tt-fg-hover`, and `--tt-icon` on a new `> svg` rule that beats the SVG's own width/height attributes), each falling back to the value it always had - so the admin rail, and any block that sets nothing, render byte-identically. Box vars are only emitted for `variant` bordered/filled/plain; the `default` variant keeps the round grey icon button, which is why filling defaults into a pre-existing block changes nothing.
- `components/consent/ConsentBanner.tsx` - GDPR banner (bottom-bar or modal): accept-all / reject-all / manage-per-category / notice-only dismiss; writes the `cactus-consent` cookie (versioned payload) + `cactus-consent-id`; POSTs `/api/consent`; re-prompts on categoriesVersion bump or reConsentDays expiry; registers `window.cactusConsent`. Props: config, privacyPolicyUrl. Cookie/POST work delegated to `lib/consent/client.ts`; `open()` re-reads the stored decision so the manage view shows the visitor's own choices.
- `components/consent/ConsentPreferencesPanel.tsx` - the same category switches rendered inline above the linked privacy policy page's content (Save preferences / Accept all / Reject all + an aria-live status line). Hydrates from the cookie in an effect, writes through `saveConsentDecision`, renders nothing when every category is required. Props: config.
- `components/EmailDeobfuscator.tsx` - client component mounted once in `app/(public)/layout.tsx`; after hydration walks every `a.cactus-eml[data-eml]` on the page, decodes the address (base64 of reversed string) and sets `href="mailto:…"`. Server half is `lib/email-obfuscate.tsx`; see Puck Integration → Email spam-protection.

Members (`components/members/`, listed with their routes above): `RegisterForm.tsx`, `LoginForm.tsx`, `TurnstileWidget.tsx`, `MemberAvatar.tsx`, `GeneratedAvatar.tsx`; `components/members/account/`: `AccountNav.tsx` (reuses `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`), `DeletionBanner.tsx`, `ProfileSection.tsx`, `SecuritySection.tsx`, `NotificationsSection.tsx`, `ActivitySection.tsx`, `DangerZoneSection.tsx`.

### Configuration Files

- `package.json` - name `cactus`, version 0.5.179, private; Node `22.x`; npm override `uuid ^11`. Scripts: dev, dev:warm, build, start, lint, typecheck, test(/watch), test:backup-roundtrip (`RUN_BACKUP_ROUNDTRIP=1 vitest run lib/backup/roundtrip.test.ts` - network + `NEON_API_KEY`, excluded from plain `npm test`), db:migrate/studio/generate/status, db:push (blocked), sync-wiki. Key deps: next ^16, react 19, @prisma/client 6, @puckeditor/core ^0.22, @simplewebauthn 13, @octokit/rest 21 + auth-app 8, AWS SDK S3, cloudinary, @imagekit/nodejs, @supabase/storage-js, @vercel/blob, @vercel/edge-config, aos, bcryptjs, dompurify + jsdom (pinned ^26), imapflow, mailparser, email-reply-parser, marked, nanoid, nodemailer, otpauth, pg, qrcode, sharp, zod, date-fns(-tz). Dev: vitest 2, eslint 9 + eslint-config-next 16, typescript 5.6, prisma 6.
- `next.config.ts` - injects `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_VERSION` + `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED`; image remotePatterns (Worker hostname from env, cloudinary, imagekit); custom image loader file; production-only CORS header for `/_next/static/*`; security headers deliberately not here (proxy.ts). `serverExternalPackages: ['draco3d', 'puppeteer-core', '@sparticuz/chromium']` - all three resolve paths against their own on-disk directory (draco3d reads its wasm by `fs`, chromium unpacks its packed browser), so bundling any of them breaks the path it looks itself up by; the two browser packages arrived with quote-for-shop's PDF route and are only ever dynamically imported.
- `proxy.ts` - see Middleware.
- `tsconfig.json` - strict, `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, `noImplicitOverride`, bundler resolution, path alias `@/*` → `./*`; excludes `workers/media-worker`.
- `vitest.config.ts` - exists only to mirror tsconfig's `@/*` → `./*` path alias into vitest's resolver. Without it any test that (transitively) imports an app module by its `@/lib/...` specifier fails to collect with "Failed to load url @/lib/...".
- `eslint.config.mjs` - flat config, `eslint-config-next/core-web-vitals`; ignores `lib/modules/**`, `lib/puck/module-components.ts`, `.next`, `node_modules`, `.claude`.
- `prisma/schema.prisma` - see Database Schema. `prisma/migrations/20260626000000_init/migration.sql` is the single init migration, edited in place.

## Modules

Modules live in `/modules` (gitignored), cloned at build time by `scripts/checkout-modules.mjs` from the tags pinned in `modules.json`. Wiring into core is exclusively via the generated files (router, puck components, cron, settings tabs, extension points). Twenty-eight modules are registered and present on disk (address-lookup-for-shop, advanced-shipping-for-shop, boards, contact-form, contact-form-reply-catcher, directory, filters-for-shop, gazette, gemini-watermark-remover, gocardless-instant-bank-pay-for-shop, google-sheet-products-for-shop, google-shopping-for-shop, live-chat, product-3d-views-for-shop, product-addons-for-shop, product-attributes-for-shop, product-downloads-for-shop, quote-for-shop, reviews-for-shop, search, shop, shop-variations, space-planner-for-shop, square-payment-for-shop, stock-import-for-shop, twilio, uk-bookkeeping, ultimate-seo). **live-chat** (2026-08-09) is registered unpinned and its `cactus-foundation-modules/live-chat` repo does not exist yet - pushing it, tagging v0.1.0 and pinning is a deferred release step, same situation as filters-for-shop below. **filters-for-shop** was written on 2026-08-03 and registered with pin v0.1.0, but its **GitHub repo/tag does not exist yet** - creating `cactus-foundation-modules/filters-for-shop`, pushing, and releasing v0.1.0 is a deferred release step (same situation google-sheet-products-for-shop sat in; a Vercel build before that release would fail the checkout). product-3d-views-for-shop joined the registry in v0.5.465. **quote-for-shop** was released and registered in v0.5.795 (pin v0.1.3, alongside shop's pin moving to v0.1.147 - the release publishing the two points it needs). **google-sheet-products-for-shop** is still built and on disk but **not registered in `modules.json` or released** - its GitHub repo/tag does not exist yet, so registration remains a deferred release step (see its own subsection below). **reviews-for-shop** was written, released and registered on 2026-07-30 (pin v0.1.0, core v0.5.799; 18 modules registered as of that release). Until an entry exists, `scripts/lib/module-names.mjs` filters a directory out of every generator, so nothing of it is wired into a build. **product-checks-for-shop** (2026-08-13) is present on disk and **deliberately unregistered** - it belongs in the owner's own GitHub account and installs by URL onto the site that wants it, not into core's dev registry; see its own subsection below.

**The pin is the build (v0.5.459).** The clone is `--branch <version>` at the pinned tag - "the build always gets exactly the module code the registry says it should, never silently ahead of it" - and default-branch HEAD is only the fallback for an entry with no `version` or a tag that has gone. So **releasing a module ships nothing on its own**; its `modules.json` pin has to move too. Every pin had drifted behind its module's latest release (shop v0.1.28 vs 0.1.39, shop-variations v0.1.0 vs 0.1.7, twilio v0.1.1 vs 0.1.12, …) and all eleven were reconciled to their latest release in v0.5.459. **A pin bump is not a free-standing act:** shop-variations 0.1.7 and product-attributes-for-shop 0.1.2 both declare `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.38`, so bumping either while shop sat at v0.1.28 would have cloned a shop with no `product-editor/context` and failed the build on a missing module import. Pins joined by a `requiresModules` edge move together; check the whole graph against the pinned set and the core version (`requiresCoreVersion`) before writing.

**"Installed here" vs "in this build" (working tree, core, unreleased).** `lib/modules/live-status.ts` owns the module status filter for every feature a module contributes. `status` conflates two questions - is the module installed on this site (database fact) and is its code in this build (build fact) - and the `status: { in: ['active', 'update_available'] }` filter that had been hand-copied to 21 call sites answered the wrong one. A module being **updated** moves to `deploying`, then `pending_deploy` if the deploy is deferred, while its code stays live in the running build; the old filter read that as uninstalled, so everything the module contributed silently vanished from the public site for the length of the deploy, or open-endedly for `pending_deploy`. Reported as "3D models stop working when we redeploy": `resolveShopGalleryExtras` dropped the product-3d-views provider, taking the swatches and the viewer with it, with no error anywhere. `INSTALLED_MODULE_WHERE` now answers only the database question (`active`, `update_available`, `deploying`, `pending_deploy`); the build question is already answered better at each call site, which looks the module up in a generated registry (`moduleExtensionPointComponents`, `moduleSmsProviders`, `moduleLayoutTypeGroups`, …) and skips anything absent - so a **first** install, which is `deploying` with no code in the build, still renders nothing. Only use it where such a registry does that second half. `app/cactus-admin/layout.tsx` is the exception: nav entries come straight off the stored manifest, so it intersects with `MODULES_IN_BUILD`, a new `ReadonlySet<string>` emitted into the generated `lib/modules/router.ts` by `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs`. `app/api/admin/env/route.ts` stays deliberately wider (adds `inactive`, so a switched-off module's env vars survive). `lib/modules/updates.ts` is the one deliberate holdout - a `deploying` row holds the old tag in `version` and the new one in `pendingVersion`, so including it would re-offer the update already in flight. `lib/modules/live-status.test.ts` is the backstop: it walks the tree and fails on any reintroduced hand-rolled filter, because tsc and eslint have nothing to say about any of them and the failure mode is a silently missing feature rather than an error.

**`npm run check:module-pins` enforces the above.** `lib/modules/pin-check.ts` is a pure planner (IO-free, mirroring `lib/updates/core-plan.ts`): given the registry, each module's latest release tag, the manifests at those tags and core's `package.json` version, it reports pins behind their release, entries with no `version` at all (the build silently takes HEAD), and - the part per-module staleness can't catch - whether the **current** and **proposed** sets actually resolve. It reuses `findUnmetModuleDependencies` (`lib/modules/dependencies.ts`, v0.5.458) and `compareVersions` rather than second-guessing them, and judges each module against the manifest **at the tag being proposed**, since 0.1.7 requiring `shop >= 0.1.38` says nothing about what 0.1.9 will require. An unread manifest is reported, never assumed dependency-free.

`lib/modules/pin-check.live.test.ts` is the network half (gh: `release list`, then the manifest via `contents/cactus.module.json?ref=<tag>`), gated on `CHECK_MODULE_PINS=1`. **It is deliberately not in the commit gate.** It needs network + gh auth, so in CI it would skip, and a check that skips where it matters is a false pass; and pin lag isn't a property of the working tree - it appears when someone *else* publishes a release, so gating commits on it would fail unrelated work. It is a manual/cron command that exits non-zero on lag, and skips cleanly (exit 0, loud warning) where gh is missing or unauthenticated. The resolution logic itself is covered offline with **no skip** in `lib/modules/pin-check.test.ts`, which encodes the v0.5.459 trap as a regression. gh calls retry 3× on transient failures (a 404 is definitive and isn't retried) - a first run failed on a blip reading a manifest that was plainly there a second later.

**Admin sidebar shape, 2026-08-10 (applies to every module below).** A module gets **one** `navEntries` link where its surfaces are related, with the rest as tabs on that page; a module whose admin UI is really configuration gets **no** link at all and lives as a `settingsTabs` tab (or a sub-tab of one); a module whose screen belongs inside somebody else's page publishes into a whole-page tab point (`core.inbox-tabs`, `core.media-tabs`, `shop.products-tabs`, `shop.orders-tabs`) and takes no link either. `navGroupLabel` is now only worth setting for a module keeping two or more links - just Shop. Every retired route still exists as a `redirect()` to its screen's new home, so nothing 404s. Versions cut in that pass: shop 0.1.209, shop-variations 0.1.130, product-attributes-for-shop 0.1.47, product-addons-for-shop 0.1.14, filters-for-shop 0.1.12, reviews-for-shop 0.1.4, quote-for-shop 0.1.12, contact-form 0.1.34, live-chat 0.1.15, gemini-watermark-remover 0.1.11, search 0.1.17, twilio 0.1.26, gazette 0.1.15, boards 0.1.16, space-planner-for-shop 0.1.24, ultimate-seo 0.1.3. The ones publishing into a new core or shop point set `requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.1026.

### Product Checks for Shop

- Slug: `product-checks-for-shop` (table prefix `pck_`), repo `github.com/usersaynoso/product-checks-for-shop` - **the owner's own account, not the module org**, which is what keeps it out of every other Cactus site's directory (the directory lists only public org repos). Written 2026-08-13; repo created private and **released v0.1.0** the same day (prerelease, matching every other module - which means the **Beta** channel is the one that can see it; the Public channel's `getLatestRelease` skips prereleases). **Installed on Deskwell by the owner the same day** (Module row `active` v0.1.0, `001_initial` in the ledger at 19:55 - which incidentally proves the Part 1 authenticated clone works in production against a private repo, since the build would have failed fatally rather than skipped it). **Live data change made that turn, at the owner's request:** the storefront strip needs the block actually placed in a layout - installing the module only makes it available - so `ShopProductChecks` was inserted at top-level `content` index 1 of the single published `shopProductDetail` layout row `starter-shop-detail-default-live`, immediately above the `Split` (`pdp-cols`, gallery left / buy column right) and below the existing `ShopDetailTabs`. `jsonb_insert` on `builderData` only; `zones` untouched (left 1, right 13, unchanged). Snapshot + `rollback.sql` in `~/DeskwellBackups/product-checks-block-2026-08-13/`. Verified live: page 200 and uncached (`private, no-store`), the RSC flight payload references the `ChecksPanel` client chunk (so the block executed rather than being silently skipped as an unknown type), and the module API answers **401** anonymously rather than 404 - route wired, correctly gated. **Nothing is visible to an anonymous fetch, and that is the design, not a fault**: the island renders null until the API confirms the viewer can manage products, which is what keeps shopper and staff HTML identical. **Deliberately absent from root `modules.json`** - it installs by URL (the Part-1 feature) onto the site that wants it, and this repo's registry is core's own dev list. Requires `shop >= 0.1.218`, `shop-variations >= 0.1.136`, core >= 0.5.1042.
- **What it is**: a staff-only record of when each of ten aspects of a product listing (Title, Short description, Long description, Images, 3D models, Variations, Add-ons, Downloads, Specification, Shipping) was last verified by a human, with one shared notes box per product and a staleness list showing what has gone longest unchecked. Six-month stale threshold (`STALE_AFTER_DAYS`, `lib/aspects.ts` - pure, unit-tested in `lib/aspects.test.ts`).
- **Database**: one table `pck_product_checks` - one row per product (`product_id` UNIQUE, FK CASCADE to `shp_products`), **twelve** nullable `timestamptz` `*_checked_at` columns (title, short/long description, images, 3D models, variations, add-ons, **add-on models**, downloads, specification, shipping, **categories and tags** - the last two added in `002_addon_models_and_categories.sql`, v0.1.4), `notes` (default ''), `checked_by`, timestamps. Flat columns rather than jsonb so the staleness list can sort on them. `teardown: ["pck_product_checks"]`.
- **API** (`/api/m/product-checks-for-shop/…`): `admin/product/[id]` GET (record or empty default) + PATCH (subset upsert: any of the twelve dates - string stamps, null clears - plus `notes`; merged over the current row in the route, full-row `ON CONFLICT` upsert in `lib/db/checks.ts`; stamps `checked_by` from the session). Both `requireShopUser('shop.products')`. **This route is the only authorisation in the feature** - see the block below. Four more, all `requireShopUser('shop.products')`, all admin-only with no storefront caller: `admin/products` POST (the card strip's batched read, max 200 ids), and from 2026-08-20 `admin/list` GET (one page of the admin list + the tile/chip counts, query string parsed by `lib/list-query.ts`), `admin/bulk` POST (`{ids, aspects, action: 'today'|'clear'}`, max 250 ids, inserts missing rows then one UPDATE in a transaction) and `admin/export` GET (the same filters as CSV, BOM, formula-injection guarded, 2000-row cap).
- **Storefront**: Puck block `ShopProductChecks` (layoutTypes `shopProductDetail`; editor/RSC split via `rscImport`). The RSC half resolves the product via shop-variations' `currentProductSlug()` bootstrap (renders nothing when unset - catalogue-hidden product or non-product page) and mounts `components/ChecksPanel.tsx`, an empty client island that fetches the record after mount: a shopper's fetch gets 401/403 and the island stays empty, so **every visitor receives identical HTML** and page caching can never serve an admin-shaped render to a shopper - deliberately no server-side session check. Collapsed to one line (`Checks: 7/10 current, oldest 4 months`), expands to the ten-aspect grid (tick = stamp today, date input = backdate), shared notes, visible save state.
- **Card strip** (0.1.1, 2026-08-15): second Puck block `ShopCardProductChecks` ("Card: Product checks", layoutTypes **`shopProductCard`**, `inline: true`, one file `components/puck/CardProductChecks.tsx` for editor and RSC alike since the view is a client island either way). Takes the product id straight off `CardPartContext.product` - no `shop.card-media` provider, because check data must never be resolved server-side into a card's HTML (a card is page-cached). `components/CardChecksStrip.tsx` is the island: `Checks n/10` heading, then all ten aspects each with a green tick / red cross (cross = never checked OR older than `STALE_AFTER_DAYS`, ages in the `title` tooltip), then a centred Note / No note row whose tooltip carries the note text - **inverted against the aspects (0.1.2)**: a note is work outstanding, so having one is the cross and an empty box is the tick. Same empty-until-the-API-answers gate as `ChecksPanel`. **Batched:** `lib/card-checks-client.ts` collects every tile's id for a tick and sends one `POST admin/products` (new route, `requireShopUser('shop.products')`, max 200 ids, answers every id asked for so a missing row reads as never-checked), caches per page, and latches `denied` on the first 401/403 so the other thirty-nine tiles never ask again. `getChecksForProducts(ids)` in `lib/db/checks.ts` is the one query behind it (`= ANY(...)`). No schema change, so the backup gate is untripped. Placed by the owner in **Admin → Layouts → Shop → Product Card**, under the Price part.
- **Admin**: `shop.product-editor-sections` entry "Checks" (order 54) reusing the same `ChecksPanel` initiallyOpen; and, from 2026-08-23 (v0.1.7), a `shop.products-tabs` entry **Checks** (order 60, `components/admin/ChecksTab.tsx`) at `/m/shop/products?tab=product-checks-for-shop` - the working list. **No sidebar link and no page of its own any more**: `navEntries` and `app/cactus-admin/product-checks-for-shop/` are both gone, and because a contributed tab receives no `searchParams`, `ChecksScreen` reads the query off the address bar on mount and mirrors only its own `LIST_QUERY_KEYS` back, leaving the host's `?tab=` alone. Still a LEFT JOIN from `shp_products` (never-checked products must appear - an inner join would hide exactly them) with catalogue-hidden and archived excluded, but from 2026-08-20 filtered, sorted and paged in SQL by `lib/db/list.ts` rather than in JS: six state filters, per-aspect state filter, notes filter, search, status, category-with-descendants, a per-view 3/6/12-month stale window, ten sorts and clickable column headings. `components/admin/ChecksScreen.tsx` (client) + `checks-screen-css.ts` (`pck-` prefix, tokens only) do the rendering: tiles, per-aspect backlog chips, twelve clickable squares per row (one PATCH each), inline `ChecksPanel` expander (`onSaved` refreshes the list), selection bar for bulk mark/clear, CSV export, query mirrored into the address bar.
- **Uninstall note**: remove the block from the Product Detail layout first; an orphaned block type renders nothing on the storefront (Puck's slot renderer skips unknown types) but tidier is tidier.

### Filters for Shop

- Slug: `filters-for-shop` (table prefix `flt_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/filters-for-shop` (v0.1.0 released 2026-08-03, v0.1.1/v0.1.2/v0.1.3 released 2026-08-04; registry pin v0.1.3). 0.1.1: price-band groups, attribute-sourced rules, sticky panel. 0.1.2: card-carousel handshake fix (see `shop.card-media` fourth-contribution entry) - requires `shop >= 0.1.189`. 0.1.3: the grid finally resolves `resolveShopCardExtras` into `buildCardContext` (it never had - so no contributed variation photos and the 0.1.2 constraint had nothing to match on the live site), mirrors shop's current div + stretched `.shop-card-link` card wrapper, and passes `partTypes` into `injectShopProductCardEmbed`; `shop-variations >= 0.1.107`; `product-attributes-for-shop` optional (probed, never imported). 0.1.4: automatic Category group on category pages - see the Puck block entry below (released 2026-08-04, registry pin moved to v0.1.4 in core v0.5.935/936). 0.1.6 (working tree): single-option groups dropped - the RSC now offers a group only when >= 2 filters survive the page's hide-empty pass (`.filter((g) => g.filters.length >= 2)`), and the synthetic Category group needs >= 2 offered children; a heading with one tick (e.g. "Height adjustable: Yes" on the sit-stand page) filters nothing. 0.1.5 (released 2026-08-04, pin bumped in core v0.5.937): storefront UX pass - overlay filter sheet at <= tablet breakpoint (bottom sheet on phones, right slide-over on tablets; floating "Filter" pill entry point, scrim, body scroll lock via position:fixed pin with instant-scroll restore, Escape/scrim close, focus trap + dialog semantics, sticky "Show N products" apply footer that scrolls back to the results), per-group selected-count badges, tick lists >10 fold behind "Show all" (ticked entries never fold away), bigger touch targets in the sheet, focus-visible outlines, `role="status"` on the "Showing X of Y" line; `FilterShell` gained a `tabletBp` prop (matchMedia drives the sheet-only behaviours). 0.1.7 (working tree): **Sort by dropdown** on every filter-grid surface - see the Puck block entry below; new `lib/sort.ts` + `lib/sort.test.ts`, new block prop `showSort`, new `FilterShell` props `sortKeys`/`showSort`, new `.flt-toolbar`/`.flt-sort`/`.flt-sort-select` CSS. Working tree 2026-08-23: block prop `defaultSort` (default and undefined-fallback `best-selling`) with the starting order applied server-side; `FilterShell` props `defaultSort`/`serverOrder`; `FLT_SORT_RECOMMENDED_PARAM`/`sortValueFromParam` in `lib/sort.ts`.
- Grouped storefront filters built for variation-heavy catalogues: an owner-defined filter (Colour > Blue) stands for any number of real `svr_option_values` matched by **(option name, value label)** pairs, so one Blue covers Blue/Stevia Blue/Sky Blue across every product with no per-product wiring. Matching is variant-driven: a product matches a filter when any **enabled** variant carries a matched value; the first such variant (owner's variant order) is the representative whose child-product photo the card swaps to and whose child slug the card links to (shop-variations' existing deep-link resolver turns that into the parent page with the options pre-selected - no shop/shop-variations changes were needed).

**Database** (`flt_`): `flt_groups` (`name`, unique `slug` = query param, `control_type` CHECK CHECKBOX|SWATCH|IMAGE|DROPDOWN, `kind` CHECK VALUES|PRICE from 002, `position`), `flt_filters` (`group_id` FK cascade, `label`, `slug` unique per group, `swatch` hex-or-URL, `price_min`/`price_max` NUMERIC from 002 - band bounds, min inclusive / max exclusive, NULL = open end, `position`), `flt_filter_rules` (`filter_id` FK cascade, `source` CHECK OPTION|ATTRIBUTE from 002, `option_name`, `value_label`, unique on the quadruple - 002 drops the old triple constraint), `flt_settings` singleton (`hide_empty_filters`, `swap_card_images`, `preselect_on_click`, all default true). Migration `002_price_and_attribute_rules.sql` is idempotent and ships in 0.1.1. Migration `003_filter_collections.sql` (0.1.25, idempotent) adds **`flt_collections`** (`name`, unique `slug` = the bare top-level address, `status` CHECK DRAFT|PUBLISHED, `source_type` CHECK CATEGORY|COLLECTION|TAG|ALL, `source_slug` - a plain slug, deliberately NOT an FK into shop's tables, `short_description`, `intro_puck` jsonb, `meta_title`, `meta_description`, `og_image`, `noindex`, `position`, `updated_at`) and **`flt_collection_filters`** (`collection_id` FK cascade, `filter_id` FK cascade into `flt_filters`, `position`, unique on the pair) - the filters a page arrives with ticked.

**Matching sources** (0.1.1): OPTION rules = original variant-driven svr matching (swap photo/deep link kept). ATTRIBUTE rules match `pat_attributes`/`pat_attribute_values`/`pat_product_values` by (attribute name, value label), read at product level AND via `svr_variants.child_product_id` (specs are stamped per-variant), behind a separate `lib/attributes-probe.ts` (`to_regclass`, module isolation - product-attributes code never imported); matrix only, no card swap. PRICE groups are matched in the RSC, not SQL, against `Number(ctx.fromPrice ?? ctx.prices.now)` - the same figure the card prints - via `priceInBand()` in `lib/types.ts`, so they also work for variation-less products. Admin catalogue (`admin/option-values`) now returns `source` per section and includes attributes only when their distinct label count is <= 60 (free-text specs like weights would flood the picker).

**Permissions**: none of its own - shop's `shop.products` (manage screen/APIs) and `shop.manage` (settings).

**Extension points provided**: `shop.products-tabs` x2 (Filters, Filter Collections), `core.media-reference-rewriters`, `core.media-usage-providers`, and from 0.1.28 **`shop.collection-index-sources`** → `filtersCollectionIndexSource` (`lib/collection-index-source.ts`, label "Filter collections") - published filter collections offered to shop's Collection Browser block as card items (`href` = the bare `/<slug>`, blurb = `short_description`, cover = `og_image`, no product count: counting means running each page's whole filtered query). Requires `shop >= 0.1.270`, which is where that point was added.

**API routes** (`/api/m/filters-for-shop/…`): `admin/groups` GET+POST, `admin/groups/[id]` PATCH+DELETE, `admin/groups/reorder` POST, `admin/filters` POST (accepts inline rules), `admin/filters/[id]` PATCH+DELETE, `admin/filters/[id]/rules` PUT (whole-set replace), `admin/filters/reorder` POST, `admin/option-values` GET (distinct (option, value) catalogue with product counts + representative swatch, sourced from `svr_*` behind a `to_regclass` probe), `admin/settings` GET+PUT. No public routes - the storefront is fully server-rendered. 0.1.25 adds `admin/collections` GET+POST, `admin/collections/[id]` GET+PUT+DELETE (the PUT is also what the intro builder writes `introPuck` through), `admin/collections/reorder` POST, and `admin/collection-sources` GET (shop's categories/collections/tags, name+slug, for the source picker).

**Filter collections** (0.1.25): SEO landing pages built out of the existing filters - "Green Office Chairs" is the Office Chairs category with Colour=Green ticked on arrival, at `/green-office-chairs`. Admin is a **second** `shop.products-tabs` entry, id `filters-collections`, label "Filter Collections", order 41 (`components/admin/FilterCollectionsTab` -> `FilterCollectionsScreen`); the intro is built full-screen at `app/cactus-admin/filters-for-shop/collections/[id]/intro`, reusing shop's `StandaloneDescriptionBuilder` through a private `filterCollectionIntro` layout type nothing registers blocks against (so: core's shared content parts, bare root). The public page is `app/root/[slug]/page.tsx`, reached through the manifest's new `publicRootSlug` claim (`lib/root-slug.ts` -> `filtersClaimsRootSlug`); the claim matches DRAFT rows too so staff keep a preview, and the page itself 404s a draft for everyone else. `generateMetadata` emits meta title/description, a self-canonical at the bare address (the panel writes the shopper's ticks into the query string, so without it every cut reads as a duplicate), `robots: noindex` when flagged **or** while still draft, and an og image. New `lib/sitemap.ts` lists published, non-noindex pages. New layout type **`filterCollection`** (manifest `layoutTypes`, group label "Filters") is one template stamped for every page - blocks `FilterCollectionHeader` and `FilterCollectionIntro` (both editor/RSC split, `[Anchor]`, `permissions.delete=false`) plus `ShopFilterGrid`, which gains `filterCollection` in its `layoutTypes`. `lib/inject-filter-collection-context.ts` writes `filterPageSlug` into all three and the source's `categorySlug`/`collectionSlug`/`tagSlug` + `preselectFilterIds` into the grid, mirroring shop's `inject-category-context.ts`; blocks resolve the record from the slug rather than being handed a copy, so the injection stays a two-string write however big the intro grows. No published layout = a plain built-in shell (breadcrumb, H1, blurb, intro, grid), same pattern as shop's fallback category page. **Preselection is a starting point, not a lock**, per Chris: the panel is unchanged and every tick can be cleared. `lib/preselect.ts` (new, + `preselect.test.ts`, 16 tests) owns the three-state URL rule - unchanged group = no parameter, changed = the parameter, **cleared = an EMPTY parameter** (without which an untick cannot survive a refresh, the page's own tick going straight back on). `FilterShell` gained one `preselect` prop and delegates both the read and the write to it; with no preselection every rule collapses to exactly what it did before. **Trap closed while building:** the grid's own culling (`hideEmptyFilters`, and dropping any group left with < 2 filters) would have eaten a page's own preselection - "Chairs Under £200" on a source with one matching band would drop the band and show the lot at any price. Both rules now step aside for a preselected id; a preselected filter matching nothing yields an empty grid, which is the honest answer. `lib/media-reference-rewriter.ts` and `lib/media-usage-provider.ts` extended to cover `og_image` and `intro_puck` (the intro swap is one in-database `replace(replace(...))` statement, same atomicity reasoning as core's `swapInBuilderJson`). Teardown drops `flt_collection_filters` before `flt_collections`. **Core diffs: none.**

**Admin**: nav entry Shop > Filters → `/cactus-admin/m/filters-for-shop/filters` (`FiltersScreen`: groups, filters, searchable value picker keyed `source␀optionName␀valueLabel` with attribute sections labelled "Spec: ...", auto-borrowed swatches; group creation offers Product values vs Price bands - a PRICE group is forced CHECKBOX and its filter rows swap the value picker for from/up-to band inputs via `PriceBandEditor`); settings sub-tab hosted at `shop.settings-sub-tabs`.

**Puck block** `ShopFilterGrid` ("Shop: Filters & Product Grid", layoutTypes shopIndex/shopCategory/shopCollection, editor/RSC split via `rscImport`). RSC half mirrors product-attributes-for-shop's grid: shop's own `listProducts` (perPage cap 100 is the honest ceiling) + card template render, cards stamped `data-flt-product`; client `FilterShell` shows/hides/re-dresses cards in place (never re-renders), with facet-style live counts (`facetCount` - a tick never counts against its own siblings), active-filter chips, collapsible groups with selected-count badges, URL sync via `replaceState` after mount (hydration-safe), and the image/href swap. From 0.1.5 the <= tablet experience is an overlay sheet (bottom sheet <= mobile bp, right slide-over between the breakpoints; one DOM - desktop unwraps the sheet chrome via `display:contents`), opened by a fixed bottom-centre "Filter" pill with an active-count badge; the sheet has a scrim, a body scroll lock (position:fixed pin, scroll restored instantly on close - smooth scroll gets cancelled by the unlock's own layout work, so both restore and the apply button's back-to-results jump use `behavior:'instant'`), Escape/scrim/× close, a light focus trap with dialog semantics gated on a `tabletBp` matchMedia (never CSS alone), and a "Show N products" apply footer with live count; CHECKBOX lists longer than 10 fold to 8 behind "Show all" with ticked entries always kept visible. On cards carrying shop's `ShopCardMedia` carousel island the swap goes through shop's constraint contract (`data-shop-media-sources` + `shop:card-media-sources` event, allowed ids = the ticked filters' `FltSwap.sourceId` child-product ids in owner order) so the island shows the first ticked colour, the arrows flick between ticked colours only and hover cannot snap back to an unfiltered photo; plain single-photo cards keep the direct `<img src>` swap, parking originals in `data-flt-*` attributes for exact restore. Pure logic in `lib/filter-logic.ts` (unit-tested: `matchesSelection` OR-within-group/AND-across-groups, `facetCount`, `pickSwapFilter`, `pickSwapFilters`). From 0.1.4 the block also takes `categoryFilter` (`yes`/`no`, default yes): on a category page the RSC prepends a synthetic **Category** group of the page's direct sub-categories (CHECKBOX, filter ids `cat:<childId>`, group slug `category` unless an admin group owns it, then `sub-category`); a product earns a child's filter id when filed anywhere on that child's branch (`lib/category-filter.ts`: `buildBranchIndex` cycle-safe over shop's `listCategories`, `productBranchFilterIds` deduped, unit-tested), children matching nothing in the grid are dropped, and no `FilterShell` change was needed - counts, chips and URL sync all fall out of the matrix. From 0.1.1 the desktop left panel is sticky (`position:sticky; top:var(--flt-sticky-top,7rem)`, own overflow scroll) - tablet/mobile drawer untouched. From 0.1.7 the block takes `showSort` (`yes`/`no`, default yes) and the results column carries a **`.flt-toolbar`** row - "Showing X of Y" left, a **Sort by** `<select>` right (full-width row <= mobile bp) - offering Recommended (the server's own order, and no query string at all) / Price low-high / Price high-low / Name A-Z / Name Z-A / Newest / Oldest. Pure half in `lib/sort.ts` (`FLT_SORT_OPTIONS`, `isFltSortValue`, `sortProductIds`; unit-tested in `lib/sort.test.ts`): a stable sort over the server's own id order so ties never shuffle, `Intl.Collator` with `numeric:true` so "800mm" precedes "1200mm", and null prices last in **both** directions. The RSC builds `sortKeys` (`{name, price, created}` per product id) from the same `Number(ctx.fromPrice ?? ctx.prices.now)` the PRICE bands and the cards use, so the order can never disagree with the printed figures; `createdAt` comes off `ShpProduct`. Sorting is **real DOM moves** (one `DocumentFragment` re-append of `:scope > [data-flt-product]`), not CSS `order` - the cards carry links and carousel buttons, so a visual order disagreeing with the tab order would fail WCAG 2.4.3; safe under React because `children` is a stable server-passed node it never re-reconciles. First render captures the server order in a ref, and the effect no-ops entirely until something has actually moved. The choice mirrors into the query string through the same single writer as the ticks (`?sort=`, or `?order-by=` if an admin group already owns the `sort` slug), read back post-mount and validated against the whitelist. It sorts exactly the products the block rendered - same honest ceiling as the filtering. A grid with no groups worth offering still gets the toolbar (the early return now wraps grid + toolbar in `.flt-results`). Deskwell note (2026-08-04): 47 per-category `shopCategory` Layout rows (`deskwell-category-<slug>`, page_slug display conditions, hardcoded `categorySlug` prop - core's `injectCategoryContext` allowlist covers shop's own blocks only) plus seeded groups Colour/Finish/Width/Depth/Arms/Headrest (37 filters, 272 option rules, swatch hues measured from the CDN swatch images); Phase-B seed (Price/Desk shape/Usage) ran 2026-08-04 after the owner updated onto 0.1.1. Same day: new spec attribute `Height Adjustable` (Yes/No) + `Shape (spec)` value `Corner`, stamped product-level onto all 63 visible desk listings (derived from names: 'height adjustable' => Yes 25/No 38; corner|crescent => Corner 9, else Rectangular 54 - sheet sync never touches pat_ tables so the stamps are safe), with a new `Height adjustable` filter group and a Corner rule on Desk shape; seed + rollback in `~/DeskwellBackups/filters-2026-08-04/desk_shape_height_*.sql`. Later same day (data only, live at once - filters are rows, not code): ten more groups seeded from the existing pat_/svr_ catalogues - Upholstery (Fabric/Mesh/Leather, ILIKE-built over `Material (spec)` labels), Frame colour (SWATCH; option `Frame Colour` + attr `Frame Colour (spec)`, Silver bucket includes Aluminium, Wooden bucket the wood-finish labels), Seats (bench desks, option+attr `Seats`), Sit-stand features (Memory presets/Anti-collision/Dual motor), Back height (`Back Type` High/Medium/Low), Lumbar support (Adjustable + Integral), Weight rating (four bands bucketed numerically from `Maximum Weight Capacity` 'NNNkg' labels), Drawers (1/2/3/4+, attr `Drawers (spec)` + option `Drawers`), Lock type (option `Locking`: Key/Electronic/Fingerprint/Combination), Guarantee (overlapping 5+/10+ year bands); `Desk shape` group renamed **Shape** (slug `desk-shape` kept) and given Round/Square/Curved & D-end filters plus `Top Shape` rules grafted onto Rectangular and Corner & crescent; all 20 groups re-positioned into one deliberate panel order. 37 new filters, 169 rules, every filter verified matching >= 2 active listings and the groups confirmed rendering on live executive-chairs / meeting-boardroom-tables / safes-security / sit-stand-desks-electric pages. Backup `flt_tables_before_category_filters.sql`, seed `category_filters_seed.sql`, rollback `category_filters_rollback.sql`, all in `~/DeskwellBackups/filters-2026-08-04/`.

### Product Add-ons for Shop

- Slug: `product-addons-for-shop` (table prefix `pad_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/product-addons-for-shop` (manifest 0.1.6, 2026-08-09). Requires `shop >= 0.1.203` and `shop-variations >= 0.1.121`; product-3d-views and space-planner are optional companions reached only through documented window events and probed SQL - never imported.
- **What it is**: link real products to a main product as add-ons ("Accessories" on the storefront - `pad_settings.noun_singular/noun_plural` is the sitewide wording, "Add-ons" in admin). Since 2026-08-09 each add-on row has its OWN quantity input + Add to cart button (styled to mirror svr's add-to-cart part) and add-ons never ride the main press: lines carry `deterministicGroupKey(mainTargetId, [])` (mainTargetId = resolved variation child, else the listing), the companion provider stamps the main line's group only when related add-on lines already sit in the basket, and `addAddonToBasket` retro-stamps a main line already there (`setLineMeta`, untouched if any pad meta exists) - so the group forms in either buying order; an add-on alone stays a flat line. Stable lineIds still merge identical re-adds. Each line keeps its own price, stock, tax class and advanced-shipping rules. Chains (an add-on's add-ons) allowed to depth 3 with cycle refusal at link save AND payload build.
- **Database**: `pad_links` (main `product_id` → `addon_product_id`, both FK CASCADE to shp_products, UNIQUE pair, `enabled`, `position`, `model_context_key`, `planner_standalone`, `config` jsonb) + `pad_settings` singleton (nouns + `showcase_surface` TAB|BLOCK|NONE). Config references svr options by NAME and values by SLUG - never ids, which sheet re-imports regenerate.
- **Config shapes** (`lib/types.ts`): per add-on option a mapping mode - `match` (derived from a main option, hidden: screen width follows desk width), `default` (pre-selected, overridable, follows live until overridden: frame colour), `recommend` (admin-picked value via the shared `fixedValueSlug`, pre-selected and marked "recommended", overridable, degrades to a plain choice if the value vanishes), `choose` (shopper picks: fabric), `fixed`. Value translation: explicit `valueMap` (slug→slug) first, then shared `source_ref` (pat attribute), then slug, then label (`lib/mapping.ts`, pure, shared browser+server). Quantity rule per link: `recommended` (base × per-main-value multipliers, e.g. Seats 2/4/6 Person → ×1/×2/×3, gentle auto-note when overridden, restated in the basket when quantities drift) or `free` (stepper from 1, no opinions).
- **Storefront**: `ShopProductAddons` block (place under ShopVariantAddToCart; renders nothing without links) - the box listens to `cactus-shop-variant-selection`, resolves variants through svr's own `selection-logic` (row thumbnail switches to `variant.imageUrls[0]` once resolved), publishes `cactus-shop-model-context` `{slug, parentProductId, contextKeys, extraValueIds}` for the 3D stage, adds its own lines via shop's `addToCart` with `meta.productAddons` + the planner `modelContext` bag (`stage: plannerStandalone?'self':'none'`, `bundleOf`, `qtyPerMain`; the main line gets no combined-context stamp any more), and registers the purchase companion solely as the main-line group stamp. "Learn more" modal iframes shop's `/details` bare view (needs core's same-origin framing headers, 2026-08-09) with a Close button footer. Separately, the row thumbnail and the showcase card picture are BUTTONS opening `AddonImageModal` (0.1.4): big stage + thumbnail strip, arrow keys/Escape, resolved `variant.imageUrls` first then `selector.baseImages`, deduped by URL (a `plain` add-on has no variation shots); `.pad-head` became a div with an id-linked `.pad-title` label so the picture button is not nested in a label. Showcase: `shop.product-detail-tabs` provider (order 25, after Specification's 20 since 2026-08-09; label = the owner's plural noun via `labelFor`; stands down unless surface is TAB) and the `ShopAddonsShowcase` block for BLOCK mode - cards with "Learn more" and "Add" (fires `cactus-shop-accessory-focus`, box ticks that add-on open and scrolls to `spd-buy`).
- **Stock visibility** (0.1.6, `lib/stock.ts`): `isAddonOutOfStock` = `plain.inStock` false, or EVERY enabled variation out of stock (no enabled variations = the owner's own switch, left alone; backorder/pre-order children count as in stock, svr's own rule). `buildBoxPayload` resolves shop's `canSeeStockLevels()` once into `PadBoxPayload.staffView` and, for everyone else, prunes sold-out add-ons AND their chain children out of the payload before it leaves the server - so a shopper's HTML never mentions them and the showcase (built from the same box payload) cannot disagree; every add-on gone that way = no box and no tab, exactly as zero links. Staff keep the lot, badged "Out of stock" with a "shoppers cannot see this" line. Per-value: `isValueOutOfStock(selector, constraints, optionId, valueId)` - constraints are every LOCKED value (match/fixed - settled by definition, whatever their display order) plus picks made ABOVE the option in display order, mirroring svr's `isValueAvailable` directional rule so a downstream pick can never grey out an upstream row; true only when carriers exist and all are dry (a value carried only by switched-off variations is not a stock answer). Sold-out values render struck-through with an "Out of stock" sub-line and are `disabled` for shoppers, live for staff; the Add to cart button was already gated on `variant.inStock`, which is what stops staff buying one. `outOfStock` on `PadAddonPayload` (required) and an optional `outOfStock` on `ShowcaseCard` (payload-cache compatible, like `images`).
- **Cart-line resolver** (`shop.cart-line-resolver` + prefetch): priceAdjust always 0. Declares the generic group (captions "Accessory for X", collective label for shop's remove-together wording), persists `line_meta.data.productAddons` (`linkId` is what the attach-rate report reads), validates the link still exists and still points at the line's product (deleted link degrades to a plain line; wrong product fails the line), drops group/caption for orphans (which keep the "Accessory for" field; grouped lines drop that field since the ↳ caption already says it - 2026-08-09), and adds the "Recommended" advisory field when quantities drift (computed in the prefetcher - the only pass that sees both quantities).
- **Admin**: product editor section (order 52, "Add-ons") - search-link products (refuses cycles and products with REQUIRED svr personalisation, which the box cannot collect - optional fields are simply not offered), per-option mode/mapping editors with automatic-match preview, quantity rule editor, 3D context key + per-variation tagged-file coverage readout (probes `p3d_models.context` via information_schema, absent = hidden), planner-standalone toggle, live coverage warnings (missing width translations etc), and ↑/↓ reordering (0.1.4 - `position`, which every read already sorts by, so the order reaches both storefront surfaces). Sidebar Shop > Product add-ons → `/m/product-addons-for-shop/addons` (`AddonsScreen`: Overview of every link; Attach rate report - orders containing the main vs orders with the add-on attached by persisted linkId, units + revenue, date range; permission `shop.reports` for the report route, `shop.products` elsewhere). Settings tab at `shop.settings-sub-tabs` (nouns + showcase surface, `shop.manage`).
- **API routes** (`/api/m/product-addons-for-shop/…`): `admin/settings` GET+PUT, `admin/products/[id]/links` GET(editor payload)+POST, `admin/products/[id]/links/reorder` POST (0.1.4, whole-list `orderedIds`, 409 on drift), `admin/links/[id]` PATCH+DELETE, `admin/product-search` GET, `admin/overview` GET, `admin/report` GET. No public routes - the box payload is server-rendered into the block (svr's `currentProductSlug()` bootstrap).
- **3D truthfulness rules**: an add-on contributes its context key only at the recommended quantity (free mode always contributes `key:qty`); overridden counts drop the key and the box says "3D preview shows the standard arrangement". Exact-or-base everywhere - a missing combo file shows the plain product, never a nearest guess.
