Files each `IMAGE` in `shp_product_media` into the core media library under **Shop / <master category trail> / <product name>** (no master → "Uncategorised") via core's `getOrCreateFolderByPath(['Shop', ...<category ancestor names>, <product name>])` + `moveOrRenameMedia(id, {targetFolderId, exactName:true, collision:'suffix'})` - **no `newName` is passed, so the file keeps whatever name it was uploaded under; this only organises into the folder, it never renames** (until 2026-07-26 it also renumbered every image to `<product-slug><n>` on each save - removed, along with the now-dead `planImageRenames` renumber-ordering helper and its test, because renaming a file the owner uploaded was never something asked for). A same-folder name clash is given a numeric suffix (`collision:'suffix'`) rather than overwritten (`'replace'`, the old behaviour). **Category nesting (working tree):** the category segment is the master's whole `getCategoryAncestorPath` trail (root → … → leaf), so a sub-category product nests inside its parent's folder (`shop/office-tables/meeting-boardroom-tables/<product>`) rather than a flat leaf folder - `productFolderSegments` (shared by `getProductMediaFolderId`/`findProductMediaFolderId`, and therefore by the 3D/downloads/variations subfolder resolvers) builds it. **Existing products relocate on save:** before the per-image filing, `relocateProductFolderIfMoved` finds the product's current folder (off an existing managed image's `folderId`) and, if the category tree has moved its home, `moveFolder`s the whole folder under its new parent - one re-key carries the product's images, 3D models and downloads together, and each module's stored url follows (shop/variations media-reference rewriters repoint their tables; the downloads route heals `pdl_files` from `media_id` on next read). No-op when already in place, when the product has no folder yet, or on a destination name clash (two products sharing a name → per-image filing is the fallback and 3D/downloads re-file on next upload). Only urls resolving to a managed core `Media` row are moved (external urls / video embeds left as-is); the row's `url` is rewritten to the relocated one. Idempotent (an already-filed image is a no-op) and best-effort per image (one relocate failure doesn't fail the save). The editor refetches after save so thumbnails follow the moved blobs. `exactName` keeps the stored key nanoid-free so the url reads `…/shop/<category>/<product>/<slug><n>.<ext>` exactly - this filing is the **only** consumer of `exactName`, so it owns the uniqueness contract `lib/media/keys.ts` now keeps (a shared 40-char clip used to break it; see the Media section). `folderProductId` files a product's images under a **different** product's folder while still naming them from its own slug - the one consumer is shop-variations' variant `PATCH`, which passes the parent so variant images land beside the parent's (a variant child is a hidden, category-less product, so unaided it would file under "Uncategorised"). Two products sharing a name share a folder; filenames stay unique because the slug is.
- Category picture filing (`lib/media/category-media.ts`, v0.1.151): a category's own picture belongs in **Shop / <the category's ancestor trail>** - the folder holding its products' folders - not the library root it used to land in. `categoryFolderSegments(categoryId, {name?, parentId?})` builds `['Shop', ...<parent trail names>, <category name>]` through `sanitizeFolderSegment` (lower-cased, so the folder IS the storage path); the two overrides carry what the edit panel currently holds so a picture picked after a rename or a move is filed where the save is about to put the category. `getCategoryMediaFolderId` creates the path, `findCategoryMediaFolderId` walks it look-only (deepest existing folder, so browsing creates nothing) - the same create/find pair, and the same `GET`/`POST` route split (`app/api/admin/categories/[id]/media-folder`, gate `shop.products`), that products and `product-attributes-for-shop` swatches use. `fileCategoryImage(categoryId)` moves the picture with `moveOrRenameMedia(id, {targetFolderId, exactName:true, collision:'suffix'})` - no `newName`, so the uploaded name survives - and writes the relocated url back to `shp_categories.image_url` (the shop's media-reference rewriter would also catch it; the explicit write keeps the filing correct on its own terms). No-op unless the url resolves to a managed `Media` row, so nothing is created for a category with no picture or an externally hosted one, and best-effort: a failure `console.warn`s rather than failing the save. Callers: the category `PUT` (after the write, so it follows a rename or re-parent), the `POST` when it carries an `imageUrl`, and `categories/reorder` for each id when `parentId` is sent (a drag-drop re-parent; the arrows omit it). Descendant categories' pictures re-file on their own next save, mirroring how products under a moved category do. `CategoriesScreen` passes `resolveFolderId`/`resolveInitialFolderId` to `MediaPickerModal`, so uploads go straight into the folder and the picker opens there.
- `lib/media/upload.ts` - purely additive `NonImageUploadMode` type + `validateNonImageUpload(mimeType, sizeBytes, mode)` export for the digital-file upload path (declares its own mime/size allowlist, skips the sharp image-decode sniff entirely since there's no universal "valid PDF/zip" magic-byte check the way there is for images). The existing image-only `validateUpload`/`uploadMedia`/`deleteMedia`/`downloadMedia`/`saveMediaRecord` are untouched. Shop's digital files are **not** wired into the core `Media` table at all (no `saveMediaRecord` call) - they're stored in shop's own `shp_digital_files` table via `uploadMedia()`'s returned key/url only, since they're not part of core's page/logo Media referencing system.
- `.env.example` - added the seven Stripe/PayPal env var rows (all optional; a payment method with unset keys is filtered out of `enabledPaymentMethods` server-side, never offered at checkout - `modules/shop/lib/env.ts`'s `isStripeConfigured`/`isPayPalConfigured`).
- `app/api/admin/env/route.ts`'s `ALLOWED_KEYS` - added the same seven Stripe/PayPal vars so they're settable through the core env-var UI/API (Vercel project env vars, admin-only per `isAdmin()`). `lib/notifications/deployment.ts` gained a `PAYMENT_KEYS` set feeding `labelForEnvKeys()` → "Payment provider keys updated" on the existing deployment-needed notification.

**Admin pages** (`/cactus-admin/m/shop/…`)

`products` (**redesigned list, `ProductsScreen.tsx` + `products-screen-css.ts` prefix `sps-`, tokens only**: 40px thumbnails from the GET response's `images`, coloured type/status/stock badges (stock badge derives In/Low/Out/Not-tracked from `trackInventory`+`stockCount`+`lowStockThreshold`), a pre-order chip, compare-at strike-through price, and a per-row `⋯` menu (fixed-positioned so the table's overflow container never clips it - Edit / Duplicate / Delete). A filter toolbar drives the server: debounced name/SKU search, a status segmented control (All/Active/Draft/Archived), type + stock selects, and a sort select; results paginate 20/page (server `page`/`perPage`, `total` shown as "Showing X–Y of Z"). Row checkboxes + a select-all (indeterminate) header raise a sticky **bulk bar** - Set active / Set draft / Archive / Delete - posting to `admin/products/bulk`; selection is dropped on every reload so a bulk action can never touch an off-page row. Delete (single via the row menu, or bulk) confirms through the shop's own `useConfirm` dialog. Distinct empty states for no-products-at-all vs no-filter-match. Still carries the back-in-stock "N waiting" link, Export/Import-template buttons, and the "Import CSV" button opening `ImportModal.tsx` - upload → auto-detects header mismatches via `headerMatchesFormat()` and only then shows a column-mapping step → polls job progress, recent-imports log), `products/[id]` (**tabbed editor, rebuilt v0.1.38** - see "Product editor" below), `categories` (indented tree: search box, collapsible branches, **drag-and-drop** to reorder among siblings or re-nest under any category plus ↑/↓ arrows and an inline edit panel that renames/reparents/sets the per-category display mode), `collections` (flat list + inline rename/delete, no drag-reorder UI yet), `orders` (**redesigned list, `OrdersScreen.tsx` + shared `orders-screen-css.ts` prefix `sox-`, tokens only**: four overview tiles (Awaiting payment / To send / Pre-orders / last-30-days revenue) that double as one-click filters - the revenue tile deliberately does not link, since it counts by `paid_at` and the list filters on `created_at`; a debounced order-number/name/email search, a status segmented control, payment (incl. a synthetic `UNPAID` = PENDING+AWAITING_CONFIRMATION), dispatch-state and date-preset selects with custom from/to, "Pre-orders only" and "Hide cancelled" toggles, a sort select and 25/50/100 per page. Every control round-trips through the query string via `history.replaceState`, so a filtered list is linkable and the back button works. Rows carry payment / dispatch / status badges, item counts, a "Account" chip for a member order and a `⋯` menu (open, customer, mailto, copy email, quick status change); checkboxes + select-all raise a sticky bulk bar posting to `orders/bulk` with an "Email the customers" tick, and any per-order refusal is listed by order number. Export CSV carries the current filters. Distinct empty states for no-orders vs no-match), `orders/[id]` (**redesigned, `OrderDetailScreen.tsx`, two columns collapsing at 980px**: header with status/payment/dispatch badges and an action bar (Dispatch items / Email customer / Refund / Print); main column = items table (SKU, unit price, per-line sent/to-go/refunded/pre-order pills, `lineMeta` fields, link back to the product), Parcels with a per-parcel **Undo** wired to the long-unused `DELETE .../dispatch?shipmentId=`, digital downloads with a copy-link button (`/shop/downloads/<token>`, download count + expiry), "Agreed at checkout", and a single **History** timeline merging placed/paid/notes/emails/parcels/refunds newest-first with the note composer on top - the four separate lists it replaces made the chronology a mental exercise; sidebar = status select + email-on-change tick + "Payment received" for manual methods, customer panel (guest vs account, mailto/tel, prior-order count and spend, link to their orders), delivery and billing addresses with copy-to-clipboard, payment details, and totals incl. coupon code, shipping rate name, tax mode, refunded and kept. `EmailCustomerModal.tsx` finally gives `POST .../email` a UI (plain text escaped and wrapped to HTML here, logged to the order's history like any automatic email). A `@media print` block turns the page into a packing slip. Still renders the Customer Communications section only when another module - e.g. Reply Catcher - actually contributes to the `shop.order-messages` extension point, now in a matching card), `customers`, `customers/[id]`, `discounts` (Coupons/Automatic tabs via the shared core `TabStrip`, real forms - not `prompt()` - covering type incl. fixed-amount/free-shipping, expiry window, usage/per-customer limits, minimum order value, free-shipping threshold, priority; edit + delete on both coupons and automatic discounts), `reports` (Revenue/Tax tabs via the shared core `TabStrip`), `back-in-stock` (no nav entry - reached from the products list), `tax-shipping` (`TaxShippingScreen.tsx` - tax classes CRUD (new tax class's `code` auto-slugs from `name`, read-only until unlocked via a pencil button), zones (name + postcode-prefix list, empty list = catch-all matched when no other zone's prefix matches, so one zone can cover a whole country without listing postcodes) picker+detail, per-zone tax rate per class, per-zone shipping rates (flat/weight-banded/free) picker+detail). `ShopSettingsTab` renders on core `/cactus-admin/config`, internal `TabStrip` sub-tabs (General/Checkout/Payments/Notifications) covering the full `ShpConfig` shape: store identity+units/SEO/shop status, tax mode+checkout rules (guest checkout, min/max order value, phone requirement, per-step checkout-steps editor, back-in-stock account prompt, pre-order mixed-cart behaviour), the Payments sub-tab (delegated whole to `PaymentsSettings.tsx` - see the Payments settings entry below), and the order/low-stock alert addresses. The Email templates sub-tab is gone: the shop's ten order emails are registered with core through the manifest `emailTemplates` seam and edited on Settings > Email > Templates with every other email on the site (a line on the Notifications sub-tab says so). **Publishes two hosted-panel slots** (v0.1.53) for other modules' `settingsTabs` `host` entries: `shop.payments` (taken as the labelled shape since 0.1.174 - one chip per panel on the Payments sub-tab, matched to its payment method by `getModuleProviderEntryIds()` - GoCardless, Square, Crezco) and `shop.settings-sub-tabs` (each contributed panel gets its own labelled sub-tab after shop's own, in module-load order - product-3d-views-for-shop's "3D Viewer"). Contributed sub-tabs save through their own module's API, so shop's own "Save settings" button stands down while one is showing. Both slots are empty (render nothing) on a shop with no such add-ons. `requiresCoreVersion` **0.5.490** from v0.1.53 (imports `lib/modules/hosted-settings.ts`).

**Payments settings** (`components/admin/PaymentsSettings.tsx`, new in v0.1.174 - the whole Payments sub-tab, delegated out of `ShopSettingsTab.tsx`)

Chip strip, then one panel. First chip **Payment methods** (count badge "live/total"), then one chip per method that has settings of its own - shop's four built-ins, then each module-contributed method whose `panelId` matches a panel in the `shop.payments` slot, then any hosted panel no method claimed. Chips carry a status dot (green/amber/muted). Chip order follows the arranged method order, so the strip and the list agree.

- **The list** renders every entry of `paymentMethods[]` from `GET admin/settings`: drag handle (HTML5 DnD - `dragstart` is cancelled unless the event target is inside `[data-drag-handle]`, so the row's own buttons never start a drag) + ▲▼ buttons (which restore focus to the moved row's arrow afterwards, falling back to the opposite arrow when the one just pressed has become disabled at an end), label, a status badge derived from `methodState()` (**Showing at checkout** / **Not finished** / **Off**), a one-line reason, a Set up / Settings link into that method's chip, and a `role="switch"` on/off. Under it, "What a shopper will see" spells the live order out in a sentence, or warns in an `alert-warning` when nothing can be paid with at all.
- **Every mutation writes the order out in full** (`writeOrder(ordered.map(m => m.id))`), including a plain on/off - otherwise switching a method off and on again would send it to the back of the checkout queue, since the fallback order is `enabledPaymentMethods` and toggling appends.
- **The on/off writes both lists**: on = added to `enabledPaymentMethods`, removed from `disabledPaymentMethods`; off = the reverse. One rule for built-in and contributed methods alike, and it is the veto list that makes the switch mean something for a contributed method (whose own module still has its own enable toggle - shop cannot and does not write to it).
- **Built-in panels** (`BuiltInMethodPanel`) carry the switch, an honest alert when a method is switched on but not ready, the instructions textarea for BANK_TRANSFER/CASH (`bankTransferInstructions`/`cashInstructions`, saved by shop's own Save button) with a **Show this on the checkout page too** switch beneath it (`bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout`/`cashInstructionsOnCheckout`, default true; off makes the method's `createIntent` return `{}` so the wording never reaches the checkout response at all - the thank-you page and the order page read it from config separately and are unaffected), and for STRIPE/PAYPAL the `/api/admin/env` credential boxes (own Save button, own "live from the next deployment" note, `envAdminAllowed === false` explains the gate) plus a read-only webhook address (`/api/m/shop/webhooks/stripe`, `/api/m/shop/webhooks/paypal`) built from `window.location.origin` in an effect.
- **A contributed panel gets no switch and no Save button** - it saves itself, exactly as a contributed sub-tab does. `ShopSettingsTab` hides its own Save whenever `isHostedPaymentPanelTab(paymentTab)`, which is why the active payments chip is lifted into the parent. A status band at the top of the panel says what state the method is in and links back to the list to change it.


**Product editor** (`components/admin/ProductEditor.tsx` + `components/admin/product-editor/`, rebuilt v0.1.38)

Tabbed shell with a sticky sidebar, replacing the single 700px column of stacked sections. Sidebar (collapses above the tabs under 1100px) carries status, a "View on the shop" link, cover thumbnail, at-a-glance price/stock/SKU, **the only Save button on the page**, and a **Manage card** (Duplicate product → POST `[id]/duplicate` then navigates to the new draft; Delete product → `useConfirm` then DELETE then back to the list). Both clear `dirtyRef` before their hard navigation so the unsaved-changes guard doesn't prompt - the product is being replaced or removed, so in-progress edits are moot. Own tabs: Details, Images, Pricing, Stock & delivery, Organisation, Recommendations, Search, plus Download (only when `type === 'DIGITAL'`). Files: `model.ts` (form shape, `toEditorState`/`toProductBody`, per-tab dirty compare, validation), `fields.tsx` (Field/Control/Select/Switch primitives; every field has a real `<label>`, hint and inline error wired through `aria-describedby`), `editor-css.ts` (prefix `spe-`, tokens only, injected once - real CSS so focus rings/hover/responsive work), `panels/*.tsx`, `context.tsx`.

- **Fields the old editor never exposed, all already accepted by the `PUT` and stored**: `barcode`, `weight`+`weightUnit`, `dimensionL/W/H`+`dimensionUnit` (these feed weight-priced shipping rates), and `regenerateSlug` (a "rebuild the web address from the name on save" switch; the API takes the flag, not a free-text slug). `catalogueHidden` is deliberately **not** exposed - it is the internal marker for variant child products, not a "hide from catalogue" toggle, and the page refuses to open a `catalogueHidden` product at all.
- **Numeric fields are held as strings** and converted once in `toProductBody`, so a half-typed `12.` or a cleared box stays what was typed. Validation is computed from the first keystroke but only shown after a save is attempted (`showErrors`); a failed save jumps to the offending tab via `tabForField`.
- **Position is the only cover.** `toProductBody` re-stamps `isPrimary: i === 0` from the array order. `setProductMedia` honours a supplied `isPrimary` over order and `card-template.tsx` reads `media.find(m => m.isPrimary) ?? media[0]`, so round-tripping the loaded flag unchanged would have meant drag-to-reorder moved the image but not the cover.
- **Save races.** The form stays interactive during a save. The post-save reload (needed because images may be re-filed server-side) only takes the server's copy wholesale when nothing was touched since the save started (`prev === current`); otherwise the admin's edits stand and the new baseline just marks them unsaved again. Silently binning what someone typed is the worst kind of bug.
- **`shop.product-editor-sections` is now a tab contract.** Manifest entries gained optional `label` (tab name; falls back to a prettified id) and `order` (sorted among the editor's own via `SHOP_TAB_ORDER`, default 999 = last). The page renders each contributed **server** component and passes it as a `ReactNode` into the client shell, which renders it inside `ProductEditorTabScope`. All panels stay mounted (`hidden` on the inactive ones) so a half-finished edit survives a trip to another tab and contributed tabs can report state while unopened.
- **`shop.product-editor-media-sections` (shop 0.1.216)** - the sibling point for a contribution that does not deserve a tab: `app/cactus-admin/shop/products/[id]/page.tsx` resolves it through the same `resolveEditorEntries(point, user)` helper and passes the rendered server components into `ProductEditor` as `mediaSections: ReactNode[]`, which hands them to `MediaPanel`, which renders them under its own Images section. No `label` (there is no tab to name); manifest `order` only sorts contributions against each other. Because they render inside the Images tab, `useProductEditorSave` registers them against tab id `media` with no extra plumbing. Live consumer: `shop-variations`' `ProductGalleryOrderSection`. **Since shop 0.1.259 a contribution here can also put its own pictures INSIDE the grid** rather than sitting under it, through `components/admin/product-editor/gallery-extras.tsx`: `MediaPanel` wraps itself and the contributed sections in `GalleryExtrasProvider`, a contributed client component calls `useRegisterGalleryExtras(items, handlers)`, and the tiles are drawn among the product's own with one set of arrows. Tiles carry a `position` - their index in the finished gallery, the product's own counted in - and shop reports drags/descriptions/× back to the contributor without deciding what any of them mean. Live consumer: `shop-variations`' promoted variation photos.
- **`product-editor/context.tsx` is the public API for contributed tabs** (`shop-variations` and `product-attributes-for-shop` are the live consumers): `useProductEditorSave({dirty, save})` registers a tab's unsaved edits with the single Save button (throw an `Error` from `save` to fail it; the message is shown, prefixed with the tab name, and one failing tab does not roll the others back); `useProductEditorTabBadge(text)` puts a count on the tab label; `useProductEditorCurrency()` hands over the already-loaded currency symbol so a tab need not re-fetch shop config. All three are inert outside the editor. Registration keys off `useId()` + the scope's tab id, so a tab never names itself. Dirty tabs get an amber dot and a chip in the sidebar; errored tabs get a red one. Navigation away while dirty is guarded by core's `useUnsavedChanges` + `UnsavedChangesModal`.
- Tab selection mirrors to `?tab=<id>` via `replaceState` (deep-linkable; `tab` is read once on the server and passed as `initialTab`, so no `useSearchParams` Suspense boundary). The active tab is **derived**, not stored, so a `?tab=` naming an uninstalled module, or a tab that vanishes when a product stops being digital, falls back to the first tab instead of stranding the view.
- **Panels must be allowed to shrink (v0.1.39).** `.spe-panel>*,.spe-grid>*{min-width:0}` in `editor-css.ts` is load-bearing for any tab holding something wide. Grid children default to `min-width:auto` (their content-based minimum), and a scroll container still propagates its contents' min-content size up through block flow, so without the floor a wide panel overflows the `minmax(0,1fr)` main column and the sticky sidebar paints over it - `shop-variations`' nowrap variants table hit exactly this. A contributed tab wanting a wide surface should wrap it in its own `overflow-x:auto`, which only works because of this rule. Note `minmax(0,1fr)` on `.spe-grid-2/3/4` floors the track, not the item, hence the separate `.spe-field{min-width:0}`.

**Public pages** (`/shop/…`, via `publicBasePath: "shop"`)

**CLOSED gate (v0.1.51).** `getShopGate()` (`modules/shop/lib/access.ts`) is the single check for `shopStatus === 'CLOSED'`, and **every** public page above calls it first, rendering `<ShopClosedNotice message={gate.message} />` (`components/public/ShopClosedNotice.tsx`) when `gate.blocked`. Staff who pass `canPreviewClosedShop()` (`shop.access`/`shop.manage`, and any protected role via `hasPermission`) instead get `gate.staffPreview` and see the real page with a `<ShopStaffPreviewBanner />` on top. Until v0.1.51 only `/shop` itself had this check inline, so a closed shop's product/category/collection/cart/checkout/order/account/download pages all rendered in full to anyone with the URL. The gate is per-page by necessity: module public pages are dispatched individually through `resolveModulePublicPage`, so there is no shared Next layout to hang it on - **a new page under `app/public/shop/` is unprotected until it calls `getShopGate()` itself.** `generateMetadata` on the product/category/collection pages checks it too, so a closed shop does not publish its product names. The same check backs the public data routes as `shopClosedResponse()` (503 + the owner's closed message), on `products`(+`[slug]`/`related`/`upsells`), `categories`(+`[slug]`), `collections`(+`[slug]`), `tags`, `cart/validate`, `cart/upsells`, `orders/status`, `downloads/[token]`, and back-in-stock `POST` - otherwise the catalogue stayed readable as JSON while the shop was shut. Deliberately **not** gated: `config` (carries `shopClosedMessage` itself and feeds the sitewide header cart), back-in-stock unsubscribe (`GET`/`DELETE` - links already in inboxes must keep working), and `checkout/confirm` (must not strand a payment already taken); `checkout/payment-intent` + `checkout/session` keep their own stricter `!== 'OPEN'` rejection, which also blocks staff.

`/shop` (index, resolves the `shopIndex` layout via `resolveThemeLayout`, honours `shopStatus` CLOSED), `/shop/products/[slug]` (resolves `shopProduct`, 404s if none published; `productSlug`/`productId`/`inStock` injected into `ShopProductDetail`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopUpsellProducts`/`ShopBackInStockForm` block props via `lib/inject-product-context.ts` - mirrors core's `resolveTemplateData` context-injection pattern for MenuBlock etc, since these blocks have no per-instance slug of their own in the stored template), `/shop/categories/[slug]` (resolves `shopCategory`, falls back to the original hardcoded plain grid when none published), `/shop/collections/[slug]` (resolves `shopCollection`, same fallback pattern), `/shop/cart` (resolves the `shopCart` layout via `resolveThemeLayout` and renders it with `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig('shopCart')`; the `<h1>Your cart</h1>` stays in the page shell; falls back to the original hardcoded client-side cart UI + coupon field + `ShopUpsellProducts` when no `shopCart` layout is published, so never blank), `/shop/checkout` (resolves `shopCheckout`; wrapper is 1100px when a layout is published (v0.1.158 - two-column designs were unusable in the old 640px) and 640px for the fallback; no published layout -> renders the full hardcoded default flow (order summary + contact + shipping + payment + review), matching the cart page's fallback pattern, instead of a bare heading), `/shop/checkout/confirmation` (resolves `shopConfirmation`), `/shop/orders/[orderNumber]` (guest lookup form), `/shop/downloads/[token]` (friendly expired/limit-reached states, real download via the API route), `/shop/account/orders`(+`[id]`, +`[id]/receipt`)/`/shop/account/addresses` (titled **Addresses & Phone Numbers**, same wording as its account tab - each saved address carries its own phone number, editable inline; member-session-gated, 404 when Members disabled, redirect to `{memberAreaPath}/login?redirect=` when signed out). From v0.1.181 all three wrap `MemberAccountShell` so they carry the account tab bar instead of rendering bare. **Orders list**: status/fulfilment/open-request pills, up to four product thumbnails, item count, total, and four filter chips (All / In progress / Completed / Cancelled) driven by `?show=` rather than client state, so it works with JS off. **Order detail**: the manual-payment instructions first of all on a bank transfer or cash order (warning-toned with the amount while the money is outstanding, plain once it is not, absent entirely on a cancelled or refunded one), then per-line thumbnails + `lineMeta` fields + dispatched/refunded/pre-order badges + a Buy again button, every parcel with carrier and tracking number and its contents, digital downloads, the full totals breakdown (items, coupon-named discount, named shipping rate, VAT with inclusive/exclusive wording, total, refunds, remainder), completed refunds itemised, delivery + billing addresses, the request panel, and a history of decided requests with the owner's reply. **Receipt**: one-page printable, deliberately called a receipt not a VAT invoice since the shop settings hold no registration number or trading address to back that claim.

**Extension Points**
- `core.admin-dashboard-widgets` (id `shop-summary`) - 30-day revenue/orders/AOV, low-stock chip, pending-manual-payment chip, active-pre-order chip.
- `members.account-section` (id `shop-orders`, **first module to use this point** - it existed in core unused until now) - was two text links; since v0.1.181 it is a "Your orders" card showing the latest order (number, status pill, date, item count, total, "Request open" pill) because the links became real tabs.
- `members.account-nav` (id `shop-account`, `lib/member-account-nav.ts` exporting `shopMemberAccountNav`, **v0.1.181, first module to use this core point**) - contributes the **Orders** and **Addresses** tabs to the member account nav, with a count pill on Orders for the member's PENDING cancel/return requests. Returns `[]` when Members is disabled or `getShopGate()` is blocked, so a tab never leads to a "we are closed" notice.
- `core.menu-entity-provider` (id `shop`, `lib/menu-entity-provider.ts` exporting `shopMenuEntityProvider`) - lets the admin menu builder's "Module content" picker link to shop pages. Four kinds: Shop home (`/shop`), Product (`/shop/products/{slug}`, `publiclyVisible` only when status `ACTIVE`), Category (`/shop/categories/{slug}`), Collection (`/shop/collections/{slug}`). Same shape as Gazette/Directory/Boards providers; URL scheme mirrors `lib/sitemap.ts`.
- `core.media-reference-rewriters` (id `shop`, `lib/media-reference-rewriter.ts`) - repoints the shop's url-holding columns when core moves a blob (optimise/resize/crop/replace/rename): `shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url` and, from v0.1.150, `shp_categories.image_url`. Equality match, never substring - each column IS the whole url, so it cannot touch an unrelated row and the same image used twice is repointed on both.
- `core.media-usage-providers` (id `shop`, `lib/media-usage-provider.ts`) - contributes `shp_product_media.url`, `shp_digital_files.url`, `shp_products.og_image_id`, `shp_collections.image_id`/`og_image_id`, `shp_categories.og_image_id`/`image_url` - the catalogue's entire photography used to read as unused in the media library to core's media usage index, so the library's Unused tile and delete warning can see them.
- `shop.order-messages` (shop is the **consumer** here, not a publisher - no manifest entry needed) - the order detail page looks up any active module's `extensionPoints` for this point name and renders its contributed component with `orderId`/`orderNumber`/`customerEmail` props, mirroring the exact mechanism `members.admin-member-detail` already uses. Reply Catcher does not currently publish to this point (Q12 - shop builds only its own side; the reply-catcher-side contribution is out of scope), so the section never renders out of the box today.
- `shop.product-detail-parts` (**published by shop, v0.1.35**; contract + resolver in `lib/detail-slot.ts`, precedent `lib/line-meta.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **claim-and-replace** point, unlike the additive ones above. `resolveShopDetailSlot(product)` is awaited once per product page inside `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`, one extra query) and asks each active provider's `claimsProduct(product)`; the first to claim supplies optional `Gallery`/`Price`/`PurchaseArea` components, which ride to the parts as `DetailPartContext.slot` via the existing `_ctx` injector (`inject-part-context.ts`, attached by reference so components survive). `ShopDetailGalleryRsc`/`ShopDetailPriceRsc`/`ShopDetailAddToCartRsc` render the slot component instead of their own markup when `slot` is set, and shop's own markup unchanged when it is null (shop-only site, or any unclaimed product) - the starter layout's block list is **not** touched, which is how a variations-aware default PDP stays free of variations-specific blocks. Shop hands the provider its own `.spd-*` class names plus its server-loaded images/price so a replaced part looks native and paints on first byte. Replace (not render-alongside) because a claimed product has no single price/stock of its own - both rendering would show two prices and two buttons. **A claimed product's `PurchaseArea` owns availability outright: shop's `outOfStock` gate is deliberately skipped**, since stock lives on the chosen combination and gating on the parent row would strand a parent that tracks no stock of its own (`ShopDetailBadges` still reads the parent's `outOfStock`, so a mis-configured parent can show an out-of-stock badge above a working buy button). Nothing in shop names variations; the point is generic and the `git grep` leak check stays clean.

- `shop.product-detail-tabs` (**published by shop, v0.1.50**; contract + resolver in `lib/detail-tabs.ts`; live consumers `product-downloads-for-shop` and `reviews-for-shop`) - **additive**: a module contributes a tab to the product page's own tab strip, beside Description/Specification/Dimensions, rather than a block bolted underneath. Modelled on `shop.gallery-media` line for line, and additive for the same reason - a tab replaces nothing, so every provider resolves and one whose `load` throws is dropped and logged rather than taking the product page down. `resolveShopDetailTabs(productId)` is awaited once per page in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`) and rides to the parts as `DetailPartContext.detailTabs`, **not** awaited inside `ShopDetailTabsRsc` - the parts render synchronously, and `detail-parts.tsx` is dual-compiled into the client editor bundle, so it cannot import the extension-point registry (which reaches prisma) at all. Provider supplies `label`, optional `order`, `load(productId)` (server-only; payload crosses the RSC boundary so must be JSON-serialisable; **null means no tab**, which is what keeps the strip unchanged on products with nothing to add) and a `Panel` **client** component. `label`/`order` live on the provider object rather than in the manifest - unlike `shop.product-editor-sections`, whose manifest `label` is stripped by the install-time zod schema and only restored by `sync-module-manifests.mjs` on the next deploy, leaving a tab named after its own id in the meantime. Shop's own tabs are numbered in `detail-parts.tsx` (`TAB_ORDER`: desc 10, spec 20, dims 30, downloads 40); an unordered contribution lands at 50 and ties keep shop's own first (stable sort). Shop never learns what a tab holds.
- `shop.product-page-resolver` (**published by shop, v0.1.108-to-be, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/product-page-resolver.ts`, `resolveAliasedProduct`, precedent `lib/detail-slot.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **slug-alias** point. Shop's product page and `generateMetadata` (`app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx`) resolve the URL slug; when what they find is not renderable - a `catalogue_hidden` row, an inactive or unknown slug - they await `resolveAliasedProduct(slug, found)`, which asks each active provider's `resolve(slug, found)` and takes the first product handed back as the one to render under that URL (first-claim-wins in active-modules order, exactly like `resolveShopDetailProvider`). Shop then renders that product off `product.slug` (layout scoring + `injectProductContext`), so a parent page can render while the address bar keeps the original link; nothing claims → `notFound()` as before. This is what turns a variation's own link - the `/shop/products/<variant-child-slug>` URL the cart builds and shoppers share - from a 404 into the parent page opened on that combination. Generic: shop names no variants and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. A resolver may record request-scoped state as a side effect (shop-variations stashes which combination to preselect), mirroring how the detail-parts provider's `claimsProduct` records the product slug.
- `shop.product-card-prices` (**published by shop, v0.1.116-to-be, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/card-price.ts`, precedent `lib/detail-slot.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a **batched "From £…"** point for product cards. A product priced by a companion module (variations) has no single price of its own, so shop's card must show a range. `resolveCardFromPrices(productIds)` is awaited once per card surface (`ShopProductGrid`/`ShopFeaturedCollection`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopProductCard` `.rsc` files, plus `product-attributes-for-shop`'s filter grid) - **batched deliberately**, one pair of queries for the whole grid rather than one per card - and asks each active provider's `fromPrices(ids)` for the cheapest figure per product it prices; results merge, first-to-price wins, a provider that throws is swallowed so its products just fall back to shop's own price (exactly as a shop-only site). The map rides into `buildCardContext(..., fromPrice)` → `CardPartContext.fromPrice` (decimal-pound string, null = price normally); `ShopCardPrice` and `MinimalCard` render `From £x` in place of the single price, dropping the struck-through "was"/RRP (no single figure to strike against a range). shop-variations' provider (`lib/card-price-provider.ts`) computes `min` over each parent's **enabled** variants' `effectivePrice` (shop's own, so a card's "from" and the till can never disagree). Generic: shop names no variants and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. **Admin counterpart (no new point):** the product editor registry (`product-editor/context.tsx`) gained a `priceManaged` flag - `useSetProductEditorPriceManaged(managed)` (set by `shop-variations`' `VariationsPanel` when the product has ≥1 variant) / `useProductEditorPriceManaged()` (read by the shop `PricingPanel`), which then locks its Price/sale/reference boxes behind a "priced per variation" note. The stored parent `price` is left untouched, so it stays valid; only the input stands down. On the product page, `shop-variations`' `VariantPricePart` shows `From £<cheapest enabled variant>` until every option is chosen, then the resolved combination price (`fromPrice` added to `use-variation-selection.ts`). **Missed surfaces, live bug, fixed shop v0.1.117 + product-attributes-for-shop v0.1.32:** three card renderers turned out not to be Puck part components at all and so never went through `buildCardContext`/`ctx.fromPrice` in the first place - `shp_products.price` (0.00 on a variation parent, since only its variants are ever priced) rendered straight through, and none of the three render a photo either. (1) `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx`'s own local `renderTaggedCards` duplicates `MinimalCard` for its no-template-published fallback (comment: "shop's helper has nowhere to hang" the `data-pat-product` tag) - that duplicate read `product.price`/had no image branch at all; now mirrors `MinimalCard` exactly (`ctx.fromPrice` → image via `ctx.image`). (2) `app/public/shop/categories/[slug]/page.tsx` and (3) `app/public/shop/collections/[slug]/page.tsx` are the **bare fallback pages** rendered when no custom `shopCategory`/`shopCollection` Puck layout has been published for that site - a plain hand-rolled card, `effectivePrice(p, ...)` on the raw product row, image slot a permanently-empty `<div>` (no `<img>` ever, by design, unrelated to variations). Both now batch-fetch `getProductMediaForProducts` + `resolveCardFromPrices` alongside their product list and render a real photo + `From £` the same as everywhere else. Found by reproducing the live Deskwell "office-tables" category bug: DB-verified via direct psql over SSH to the OVH VPS (see [[reference_deskwell_vps_migration]]) that the parent had 42 enabled, correctly-priced variants and its own primary photo, then traced via the live RSC payload (`curl -H "RSC: 1"`) that the rendered markup (`<span style={{fontWeight:600}}>`, no className) matched neither `ShopCardPrice` nor `MinimalCard` - only the categories-page fallback's inline styles. **"From" is now conditional (shop + shop-variations + product-attributes-for-shop, working tree):** a product whose variations all cost the same was still labelled `From £x`, which is a range of one. The point's value type went from a bare string to `ShopCardFromPrice { price: string; varies: boolean }` (`lib/card-price.ts`); call sites are untouched (they still pass `fromPrices.get(id) ?? null` straight into `buildCardContext`), which flattens it into `CardPartContext.fromPrice` (unchanged, decimal string) plus new `fromPriceVaries: boolean`. All three renderers (`ShopCardPrice`, `MinimalCard`, `ShopAttributeFilterGrid`'s duplicate) prefix `From ` only when `fromPriceVaries`; the "was"/RRP stay suppressed either way, since the parent's own price boxes stand down on a variation product and its figures are not maintained. The provider tracks `max` alongside `min` and sets `varies` on a **>0.005 spread** (half a penny, so float crumbs cannot invent a range of nothing). Product page: `use-variation-selection.ts` gained `priceVaries` (same tolerance over enabled variant prices) and its `basePrice` fallback now prefers the single variant price over `payload.basePrice` when nothing is chosen and nothing varies - so the un-prefixed figure is the one the shopper will actually be charged, not the parent's unshown, unmaintained one; `VariantPricePart`'s `showFrom` gained `&& sel.priceVaries`. `VariantSlotPriceClient` needed no change - it reads `sel.price` and never printed "From" - but now shows the variation price rather than the parent's on an untouched all-same-price product. Needs patch bumps + releases + `modules.json` pins to reach a deployed site.
- `shop.product-detail-images` (**published by shop, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/detail-images.ts`; live consumer `shop-variations`) - **additive, and data rather than components**: a provider's `load(productId)` returns `{ images: {url, alt}[], placement: 'before' | 'after' }` and the host renders. Written for the chrome-free `/shop/products/<slug>/details` view (the one `product-addons-for-shop`'s "Learn more" modal iframes), which `shop.gallery-media` could not serve - that point hands over `Thumbs`/`Stage` client components that assume an interactive gallery with a notion of the chosen combination, and the details view is a bare row of `<img>`s with no stage and no selection. Every provider resolves, a throwing `load` is dropped and logged, and the host de-duplicates by url at the join (first occurrence wins, so the requested order stands). `placement` is the CONTRIBUTOR's to state: whether promoted variations sit in front of the product's own photographs is a per-product setting shop would have to learn about variations to work out. Consumer `shop-variations`' `lib/detail-images-provider.ts` reproduces the product page's own selection rule (enabled + `show_image_in_gallery`, matrix order, one picture each, `'before'` when `baseImagesLast`), so the two views cannot drift.
- `shop.gallery-media` (**published by shop, v0.1.43**; contract + resolver in `lib/gallery-media.ts`; live consumer `product-3d-views-for-shop`) - **additive**, the counterpart to the claim-and-replace point above: a module contributes extra items to a product's gallery (a 3D model) that appear as further thumbnails and take over the stage when picked. It exists *because* `shop.product-detail-parts` is winner-takes-all - shop-variations already claims Gallery on every product with options, so a second claimant could never reach exactly the products that need it most. Being additive, nothing replaces a part of shop's, so there is no two-prices failure to design around and **every** provider is resolved, not just the first; one whose `load` throws is dropped and logged rather than taking the product page down. `resolveShopGalleryExtras(productId)` is awaited once per page in `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (in the existing `Promise.all`) and rides to the parts as `DetailPartContext.galleryExtras` - resolved by the injector, **not** awaited inside the part, because `wrapResponsiveRender` (`lib/puck/config.tsx`) calls a block's `render` as a plain function. Provider supplies `load(productId)` (server-only; the returned payload crosses the RSC boundary so must be JSON-serialisable) plus `Thumbs`/`Stage` **client** components - a function cannot cross that boundary, which is why filtering by the chosen variation is the provider's own job rather than a callback shop calls into. Shop hands over its `.spd-thumb` class names and owns the strip, the stage box and which item is picked; it never learns what the item is. **`ShopGalleryExtraThumbsProps.featuredProductIds?: string[]` (v0.1.196)** carries OTHER products whose media should show too - shop's own gallery passes none, a variant-aware one passes the variation children its owner ticked "Show up front". Optional, so a gallery written before it compiles unchanged. **The host keeps it up until a whole combination RESOLVES and empties it from then on (2026-08-12)** - deliberately not narrowed as the shopper works down the options, since a part-made choice is not an answer and swapping the media mid-configure moves the picture out from under them. Rendered by **all three** galleries - shop's `ProductGallery`, shop-variations' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` (which passes the chosen child's id as `activeProductId`, the bit shop cannot know) and shop-variations' granular `ShopVariantGallery` block (which covers shop's Gallery slot, so it is the only strip on those layouts and must resolve extras itself).

- `shop.card-media` (**published by shop, working tree**; contract + resolver in `lib/card-media.ts`, precedent `lib/card-price.ts` + `lib/gallery-media.ts`; live consumers `shop-variations` and `product-3d-views-for-shop`) - **additive, batched** point that adds two things to a product CARD (the grid tile): extra **images** folded into the card's arrow carousel, and an **overlay** control pinned over the picture. `resolveShopCardExtras(productIds)` is awaited once per card surface (`ShopProductGrid`/`ShopFeaturedCollection`/`ShopRelatedProducts`/`ShopProductCard` `.rsc` files, alongside `resolveCardFromPrices`), asks each active provider's `load(ids)` (one query set for the whole grid) and merges into `{ images, overlays }` per product; a provider that throws is dropped + logged. Rides into `buildCardContext(..., extra)` → `CardPartContext.images` (product media first, then contributed, deduped by url) + `CardPartContext.overlays` (`{ id, Overlay, payload }`; `Overlay` a **client** component passed by reference like `gallery-media`'s Thumbs/Stage, `payload` JSON-serialisable). Rendered by the new client island `components/public/ShopCardMedia.tsx` (mounted by `ShopCardImage` only when `images.length > 1` or an overlay exists; single-image cards stay a plain `<img>`, and the editor canvas is untouched). **Card wrapper changed** (`card-template.tsx renderCards`): `<a class="shop-card">` → `<div class="shop-card"><a class="shop-card-link" …>` (a stretched link), so the carousel arrows and overlay controls are valid focusable buttons above the link rather than interactive content nested in an anchor; `shopCardCss` gained `.shop-card-link`/`.shop-card-nav*`/`.shop-card-overlay` and a fill-mode `pointer-events:none` on the floated text. Consumers: `shop-variations`' `lib/card-media-provider.ts` adds one photo per enabled variation (images only, no overlay); `product-3d-views-for-shop`' `lib/card-media-provider.ts` adds the "view in 3D" overlay (`components/public/CardModel3dOverlay.tsx`), which mounts `Viewer3d` in-place on tap, one live viewer at a time (a `window` `p3d-card-open` event closes any other). Generic: shop names no consumer in code and the `git grep` leak check stays clean. **Third contribution added in shop 0.1.128**: `ShopCardMediaPayload.facts` - an opaque, JSON-serialisable per-product blob shop renders **nothing** of. It merges into `ShopCardExtra.facts: CardFact[]` (`{ id, payload }`, tagged with the contributing entry's id) and rides through `buildCardContext` into `CardPartContext.facts`; the contributing module registers its OWN Puck block against the `shopProductCard` layout type and looks its payload up by id (`shop-variations`' `ShopCardVariationOptions`). Named `card-media` for history only - it is the one seam for everything a module pins to a card, which is why the resolved type is `ShopCardExtra`. Chosen over a new point deliberately: every card surface already awaits this resolver, so a facts contributor needs no per-grid wiring and can never be half-wired. **Companion change, same release**: `injectShopProductCardEmbed(data, ctx, extraPartTypes?)` - `CARD_PART_TYPES` was a hardcoded set of shop's own six blocks, so a module-contributed card block got `_ctx === undefined` and rendered its editor skeleton on the live storefront. `renderCards` now passes `config.categories.blocks.components` (every block registered for `shopProductCard`, which it already has from `getModuleLayoutPuckRscConfig`); shop's six stay as a floor rather than being replaced. Passed in rather than read from the generated registry here because `module-rsc-components.ts` imports the very surfaces that call this (import cycle). **Fourth contribution (shop v0.1.189, 2026-08-04): a client-side carousel constraint** - not through the resolver at all, a DOM contract on the island itself (`ShopCardMedia.tsx` header documents it): a filtering module writes allowed `sourceId`s, space-separated, into `data-shop-media-sources` on the `.shop-card` element and dispatches `shop:card-media-sources` there; the island re-reads the attribute (also once at mount, in case the filter dressed the cards before hydration), shows only the listed contributed photos with the first leading, suspends the hover-swap while constrained, falls back to the full set when nothing matches, and restores everything when the attribute goes. Live consumer: `filters-for-shop`'s `FilterShell`. **Fifth contribution (shop v0.1.222, 2026-08-15): `ShopCardMediaPayload.leadImages`** - images that go in FRONT of the product's own rather than after them, merged into `ShopCardExtra.leadImages` and composed by `buildCardContext` as `[...leadImages, ...ownImages, ...images]`, so the tile's main picture (`CardPartContext.image`) can come from a contributor while the product's own photographs still follow behind the arrows. Still additive - nothing of the product's is dropped, and several providers leading at once is first-registered-first, the same rule the appended images follow. `buildCardContext` also fills a blank `alt` on `images[0]` alone with the product name, since a contributed image's empty alt is right for a supplementary picture and wrong for the one the card leads with. **Superseded in shop 0.1.260 by `PartImage.position`** - a contributed picture's index in the FINISHED carousel, the product's own counted in - which says "lead" as slot 0 and much else besides, and is what makes the tile's arrows and hover-swap follow the arrangement the owner made on the Images tab. The merge lives in `lib/card-image-order.ts` (`mergeCardImages`), out of `card-template.tsx` so it is testable without Prisma. `leadImages` is still honoured: with no positions of their own those images claim slots 0..n, so a provider built against the older contract leads exactly as it did. Live consumer: `shop-variations`' `card-media-provider.ts`, which sets `position` from `svr_variants.gallery_position` on every promoted variation (the old `svr_product_gallery.card_image_from_variation` tick box went in 0.1.153).

**Contributed media leads the strip and opens the stage (shop v0.1.54, shop-variations v0.1.21, product-3d-views-for-shop v0.1.6).** In all three galleries the `extras.map` now renders **before** the photo thumbnails, so a 3D thumbnail sits at the front of the strip rather than trailing the photos. Order only - the host still owns the strip and the pick, and pick behaviour is unchanged. The opening view is the provider's call: `Gallery3dThumbs` (`product-3d-views-for-shop`) picks its first visible item once, on first paint, when nothing else is picked - so a product that carries a model opens the stage on the model instead of a photo. It fires only on mount (`ledWithModel` ref guard), so a later variation change that brings a model in does not yank the stage off a photo the shopper chose; a variation change that drops the picked model still hands the stage back to the photos via the existing `stale` guard.

**Puck Blocks** (all 20, registered in the generated `lib/puck/module-components.ts`)

`ShopProductGrid`, `ShopProductCard`, `ShopFeaturedCollection`, `ShopCategoryBrowser`, `ShopPromoBanner` (colour prop is a semantic token name, never hex), `ShopCartSummary` (client, reads localStorage cart, untagged - header-placement widget, not part of any `layoutTypes` page; from v0.1.201 the trigger - drawer `<button>` and link-mode `<Link>` alike - carries class `shop-cart-trigger` (`position: relative` from v0.1.202, as the tooltip's containing block) with resting/hover colours on `--sc-fg`/`--sc-fg-hover` custom properties (rules shipped as the island's own inline `<style>`), blank `hoverColour` field falling back to `--color-primary` so it hovers in step with core's theme toggle, Icon Link and sign-in widgets; **click behaviour** field `clickAction: link|drawer` - 'link' is the original `<Link href="/shop/cart">`, 'drawer' turns the widget into a `<button aria-haspopup="dialog">` that opens the slide-out basket `components/public/CartDrawerClient.tsx` (portalled to `document.body` - the widget lives in the site header, routinely a clipped/positioned stacking context), plus 13 `drawer*` look/wording props whose shape and defaults live in `components/public/cart-drawer-options.ts` so the header bundle can read them without pulling the panel in; the panel itself is `next/dynamic` with `ssr:false`, fetched on the first click and kept mounted afterwards, open/shut being one `scd-in` class rather than a mount/unmount so both slide directions animate - the way IN is a `scd-slide-right`/`scd-slide-left` keyframe animation, NOT the transition, because that lazy mount paints its first frame already `.scd-in` and a transition has no previous frame to move from (the panel simply appeared until then); the transition still does the way out, and both are 240ms ease-out so an already-mounted panel behaves the same either way; the widget also **auto-opens the panel on add-to-cart** - `subscribeCartAdd` in `components/public/cart.ts` (a `cactus-shop-cart-added` window event fired by `addToCart` only, on top of the `cactus-shop-cart-changed` every write fires, so a quantity nudge or removal inside the panel cannot trigger it, and deliberately NOT wired to `storage` so another tab's add doesn't fling a panel open here); the add is counted into state and acted on in a follow-up effect rather than in the listener, because the same event has just changed the count and a `hideWhenEmpty` widget is only in the DOM one render later, and the effect skips when `triggerRef.current.offsetParent === null` so a theme rendering the widget twice (desktop + mobile header, one `display:none`) doesn't portal two panels onto `document.body`; the drawer re-runs the same `/cart/validate` + `subscribeCart` loop as `CartFullClient` including the bootstrap-from-`validated-cache` and monotonic-seq guards, shows the whole-basket `notes` above the total, and renders any per-line resolver control through the shared `components/public/CartLineControlView.tsx` (summary / radios / select, lifted verbatim out of `CartFullClient` - **CartFullClient still carries its own copy** and should adopt this component once its in-flight subgrid work lands, or the two cart surfaces will drift); styling is `components/public/cart-drawer-css.ts` (`scd-*`, reusing `cart-line-css.ts` chrome) - the panel's own line layout is a two-row grid `"thumb main side" / "deliv deliv deliv"`: price, quantity stepper and the `Remove` link are one stacked `.scd-side` track (single grid child, `justify-items:stretch` + a `min-width` floor, so all three are exactly as wide as each other and the price sets the width for any longer figure), and the resolver control spans the full width beneath the thumbnail and name because its option wording is the longest thing on a line; `.scd-side` compacts the shared `.scl-qtybox` (32px tall, 24px buttons) and overrides the shared `pointer:coarse` 44px button rule with its own taller/wider coarse rule, since a 5rem column cannot host it; `.scd-deliv` re-sizes the shared summary card for the panel - every padding and text size at 0.9x its cart-page value (written out, not scaled with `em`, because the shared card sizes itself in rem), the card's two lines re-grouped by `summaryLayout='stacked'` (date on top, service + price on `.scl-s-foot` at the bottom left), both rows shrink-to-fit through `components/public/fit-line.ts` and ellipsising via `sfit-clip` only once the 0.8 font floor is reached; **panel only** - `CartFullClient`/the cart page keep the `scl-*` layout unchanged; Esc/overlay/cross close it, body scroll is locked while open, Tab is trapped inside and focus returns to the trigger; **hidden on `/shop/cart`** - `CartSummaryClient` reads `usePathname()` and renders `null` there in BOTH click modes (the full basket is already on the page; the editor path is exempt via `preview` or the block would vanish from the header while that page is designed); **inert in the Puck editor** - the same `<button>` markup renders so editor/RSC parity holds, but clicking does nothing, because a `document.body` portal would cover the design canvas), `ShopCartFull` (client, full editable cart display - `CartFullClient` localStorage island wrapped by `components/puck/ShopCartFull.tsx`; ~33 look/behaviour options: rows/cards/table layout, spacing/dividers, optional heading, product-image toggle+size+radius, unit/line-price toggles, quantity control style (stepper/number/read-only), remove button text-or-bin, stock + pre-order badges, coupon field labels, item-count/subtotal toggles + labels, checkout button label/colour/text-colour via core `SiteColourField`/full-width/radius, empty-state copy + continue-shopping link, price-accent + panel colours; the delivery `<select>` stays width-capped so it can't push the row wide), `ShopCartItems`/`ShopCartTotals` (the same `CartFullClient` island as `ShopCartFull`, told which half to render via its non-Puck `section: 'items'|'totals'` prop, so a page can put another block - `ShopDeliveryArrivals`, typically - between the basket lines and the totals; items = list + empty-basket copy + undo toast, totals = coupon + item count + Subtotal/charges/VAT/Total + checkout button + sticky bar; an empty basket makes the totals block render `null` so the message and the checkout button are not duplicated/stranded; each is its own island and each re-validates, which costs nothing extra because `postCartValidate` single-flights identical concurrent payloads; fields come from the shared groups in `components/puck/cart-fields.tsx`, so the three cart blocks cannot drift apart), `ShopCheckoutItems` (`[ANCHOR]`, v0.1.157 - checkout order summary: every basket line with thumbnail, quantity, line price, variant secondary title and the per-line `lineMeta.fields` a resolver persisted - which is where advanced-shipping's chosen delivery service + promised date appear - plus whole-basket `notes` and an Edit basket link; the Two Column starter turns it on and moves upsells below the split so the summary has its column to itself) + `stickyOffset` (CSS length, set to clear a sticky site header), a mobile-only Show/Hide fold (collapsed by default under 640px via matchMedia at mount, count+total stay in the heading), an 'N items · £X' heading line, and a distinct "items no longer available" message when a non-empty cart resolves to zero live products (previously a bare heading)), `ShopCheckoutContact`/`ShopCheckoutShipping`/`ShopCheckoutPayment`/`ShopCheckoutReview` (all `[ANCHOR]` - `permissions:{delete:false,duplicate:false}` - client components sharing state via a sessionStorage-backed `checkout-state.ts` store since Puck blocks don't share React state; from shop v0.1.157 the steps follow checkout-form best practice - Contact carries `autoComplete`/`inputMode` attrs plus reasons for asking (email = where the confirmation goes, phone = only for delivery problems); Contact also fetches `public/config` for itself and, when `requirePhone` is on, drops the "(optional)" from the Phone label, sets `required`, and shows a blur-time "Enter a phone number." the same way Shipping does - up to and including shop 0.1.177 the setting was inert end to end (saved, published on `public/config`, read by nothing), so the box stayed labelled optional and the order route took orders without a number, Shipping is retitled 'Delivery address' with real <label>s (no placeholder-as-label), per-field `autoComplete` (given-name/family-name/address-line1/2/address-level2/postal-code) and blur-time specific error messages (`role="alert"`, `aria-invalid`, danger border), the shop-rate radios are headed 'Delivery method', Review's button states the amount ('Place order - £84.20') with encrypted-payment reassurance beneath, and Payment shows a padlock line beside the mounted card fields), `ShopOrderConfirmation`, `ShopProductDetail` (`[ANCHOR]`, add-to-cart non-removable; RSC render also emits the schema.org Product JSON-LD script tag), `ShopBackInStockForm` (auto-hidden via an `inStock` prop the product page injects), `ShopRelatedProducts`, `ShopUpsellProducts` (client, one `POST /cart/upsells` for the whole cart; refreshes only when cart MEMBERSHIP changes - qty tweaks and per-line option picks no longer reload the strip), `ShopCategoryHeader`/`ShopCollectionHeader` (both `[ANCHOR]`, added with the layout system integration above - breadcrumb + name + description, re-fetched server-side from an injected `categorySlug`/`collectionSlug`; from v0.1.150 the category header prints `short_description` and only falls back to `description`, the long one having moved to its own block), `ShopCategoryDescription` (`[ANCHOR]`, v0.1.150, `shopCategory` only - the category's long description in whichever form it exists: the designed `description_puck` document when it has any content, else the plain `description`, else nothing; deletable/duplicatable, unlike the header, since a layout may legitimately not want it), `ShopCollectionDescription` (`[ANCHOR]`, v0.1.270, `shopCollection` only - the collection twin of the above, sharing `ShopDesignedDescriptionBody` with it; **Configuration**

`ShpConfig` (`modules/shop/lib/config.ts`, Zod-validated, stored as the single `config` JSONB column on the `shp_settings` singleton, Q2): `currency`/`currencySymbol`/`storeEmail`/`orderNumberPrefix`/`weightUnit`/`dimensionUnit`, `enabledPriceTypes` (subset of sale\|retail\|trade\|cost, default `['sale','cost']`) + `showRetailPrice` (default false - prints the RRP beside the price on cards/detail when it beats the charged figure), `taxMode` (INCLUSIVE\|EXCLUSIVE), `priceDisplayTax` (AS_ENTERED\|INCLUSIVE\|EXCLUSIVE, default AS_ENTERED) + `priceDisplayTaxSuffix` (default '') - **what the storefront PRINTS, as against what `taxMode` says the stored figures MEAN**; see the price-display subsection below, `weightBasedShippingEnabled` (default true - the switch at the top of the Tax & shipping screen, saved through `PUT admin/settings` like any other config key and exposed on `public/config` so the product editor can read it alongside the price types; off drops the `WEIGHT_BASED` option from the shipping-rate Type dropdown, the Weight field from the product editor's Stock tab, and the Weight column from shop-variations' grid. Nothing is blanked: stored weights and existing weight-based rates are untouched, and an existing weight-based rate still lists its own type when opened for editing so it can't silently become a flat rate), `guestCheckoutEnabled`/`postPurchaseAccountPrompt`/`minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue`/`requirePhone` (enforced from the working tree after 0.1.177: contact-step label + `required`, the shared `isContactAndShippingComplete({ phoneRequired })` gate the Payment and Review blocks run, and a 400 from `POST public/checkout/payment-intent` - the same belt-and-braces shape as `businessNameRequired`)/`checkoutSteps` (ordered step array), `enabledPaymentMethods` (which of the four BUILT-IN methods are on; a module-contributed method never needed listing here and still doesn't) + `disabledPaymentMethods` (the shop-wide veto that beats everything, incl. a module provider reporting itself ready - the only off switch a contributed method has) + `paymentMethodOrder` (the order checkout offers them in, as arranged on the Payments tab; empty means fall back to `enabledPaymentMethods` order). All three are resolved at read time by `getAvailablePaymentMethods()`, which gates each provider through `paymentMethodAvailability()` then sorts by `sortPaymentMethods()`/`resolvePaymentMethodOrder()` from `lib/payments/admin-methods.ts`, `bankTransferInstructions`/`cashInstructions` + `bankTransferInstructionsOnCheckout`/`cashInstructionsOnCheckout` (default true - whether those words are also served to the checkout page as soon as the method is picked; gated inside `lib/payments/bank-transfer.ts`/`cash.ts` `createIntent`, the only caller of which is `POST public/checkout/payment-intent`, so off withholds them from the wire rather than hiding them in the browser. `public/orders/status` reads the config directly for the thank-you page, ungoverned by that switch, but only while the order's payment is outstanding - a settled order returns `instructions: null`, as does the account order page's own read), `adminOrderAlertEmail`/`lowStockAlertEnabled`/`lowStockAlertEmail`, `shopStatus` (OPEN\|BROWSE_ONLY\|CLOSED)/`shopClosedMessage`, `shopTitle`/`shopMetaDescription` (`shopBasePath` dropped per Q3 - fixed to `"shop"` via the manifest's `publicBasePath` instead of being runtime-configurable), `outOfStockVisibility` (SHOW\|HIDE_FROM_LISTS\|HIDE_EVERYWHERE, default SHOW) + `outOfStockHiddenFromStaff` (default false) - the out-of-stock hiding block on the General tab, resolved only in `lib/stock-visibility.ts`; SHOW is a no-op on every surface and reads no cookie, `backInStockAccountPrompt`, `buyAgainEnabled` (default true - whether a past order line offers Buy again at all; read server-side in the member order detail page, no `public/config` exposure because nothing in the browser needs it), `cancelRequestsEnabled`/`returnRequestsEnabled` (both default true) + `returnWindowDays` (default 30, counted from the last parcel out; 0 takes returns off the website entirely), `preOrderMixedCartBehaviour` (HOLD_ALL\|PROMPT_SPLIT - a fulfilment policy, wired up 2026-07-23, see the Part-dispatch subsection below; also returned by `POST /public/checkout/session` so the checkout review step can word its pre-order notice), `supplierFieldEnabled` (default false) + `supplierLabelPreset` (Supplier\|Manufacturer\|Retailer\|Importer\|custom, default Supplier) + `supplierLabelCustom` (default '') + `supplierShowOnFrontend` (default false) + `supplierFieldScope` (PRODUCTS\|PRODUCTS_AND_VARIATIONS, default PRODUCTS) - the supplier field block on the General tab. `resolveSupplierLabel(config)` (same file) is the one place the preset/custom pair resolves to a display string, falling back to "Supplier" when custom is blank. Enabled adds the **Suppliers** sidebar entry and screen (see `shp_suppliers`) and a supplier dropdown to the product editor's Details tab; `supplierShowOnFrontend` additionally puts it on the Product Detail Specification tab (via `DetailPartContext.supplierLabel`, null when either switch is off); `supplierFieldScope` = PRODUCTS_AND_VARIATIONS adds the column to shop-variations' grid. Nothing is blanked by switching any of them off. Exposed on `public/config` as a `supplierField` object (enabled/label/showOnFrontend/scope) because the admin product editor reads its config from there.

**Price display tax - what the storefront prints, as against what is stored (shop 0.1.137, shop-variations 0.1.98, advanced-shipping-for-shop 0.1.21, working tree)**
`taxMode` says what the figures in the price box MEAN (INCLUSIVE = tax already in them, EXCLUSIVE = added at the till); the new `priceDisplayTax` says what the storefront PRINTS. `AS_ENTERED` (the default) converts nothing, so an upgrade moves no price. Arithmetic in the client-safe `modules/shop/lib/tax-display-shared.ts` (`displayPriceFactor`, `displayAmount`, `displayIncludesTax`, `displayTaxMode`, `displayOrderTotals`, `withPriceSuffix`; unit-tested in `tax-display-shared.test.ts`) - the `breakpoints-shared` split, because the basket does this in the browser. Server resolution in `modules/shop/lib/tax-display.ts`: `resolveTaxDisplay()` reads the config and, only when a side has actually been chosen, the rate table for `getDefaultTaxZoneId()` (a shelf price is printed long before an address exists); `makeDisplayAdjuster(taxDisplay, taxClassId)` returns **null** when the factor is 1, so the untouched-setting path is a no-op with no queries. **`effectivePrice` is deliberately NOT converted** - it is the checkout's, so what is SHOWN can never move what is CHARGED; `priceView(product, enabled, adjust?)` takes the converter and applies it to `now`/`was`/`rrp` only.
Applied at: `buildCardContext` (a `taxDisplay` on the existing `pricing` param, resolved once per surface in all six card call sites - grid, single card, related, featured, category page, collection page - and applied to the product's own figures AND a companion module's `fromPrice`, so the two can never end up on opposite sides of tax); `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx` (incl. the JSON-LD `offers.price`, so a search result cannot quote a figure the page does not); `POST public/cart/validate` (`unitPrice`, `lineSubtotal`, `charges[].amount` and a control option's numeric `priceAdjust` - a resolver's own already-formatted option LABELS are passed through untouched, as ever, so a module that prices options formats them itself); `POST public/checkout/session` (rows above the Total via `displayOrderTotals`, which scales `goodsSubtotal`/`charges` by one exact ratio so Subtotal − Discount + Shipping still lands on the server's Total to the penny; the Total itself and the persisted order are untouched); `POST public/cart/upsells`. `public/config` gains `priceDisplay { mode, storedIncludesTax, suffix, displayTaxMode }` - `CartFullClient` now takes its INCLUSIVE/EXCLUSIVE branch from `displayTaxMode`, because a basket handed converted lines adds up like an inclusive shop's whatever `taxMode` says. New `priceSuffix` on both `CardPartContext` and `DetailPartContext` (rendered as `.shop-card-taxnote` / `.spd-price-taxnote`) and an optional `priceSuffix` on `ShopDetailPriceSlotProps`. Admin UI is a **Prices on your shop** card at the top of `TaxShippingScreen` (three radios + a wording box; choosing a converted mode pre-fills "inc. VAT"/"ex. VAT" only where the owner has not written their own).
**shop-variations 0.1.98**: `getVariantSelectorPayload` converts the whole payload server-side at the PARENT's tax class - `basePrice`, each variant's `price`/`compareAtPrice`, and every add-on surcharge (`flatPrice`, `pricePerChar`, `choices[].price`, via `adjustAddonPrices`) - and adds `priceSuffix`. Deliberately one conversion on the way out rather than a multiplier in `use-variation-selection`: it keeps tax arithmetic off the client entirely and means a personalisation surcharge can never land on the other side of tax from the price it is added to. `sel.priceSuffix` renders in `VariantParts` and `VariantSlotPriceClient`. Nothing here is authoritative - the cart re-resolves each line from the products.
**advanced-shipping-for-shop 0.1.21**: a service charge is folded into `priceAdjust`, so it is taxed at the product's own rate and has to print on that same side. `line-resolver` converts the figure passed to `tierOptionLabel`/`tierOptionSummary` (its own wording, which shop never re-words) while leaving the numeric `priceAdjust` raw for shop's validate route to convert - converting both would double it. `estimate-service` converts `tiers[].priceEffective` (the printed figure; `tiers[].price` stays the raw configured setting) and now reads `tax_class_id` alongside the product name on the same query. Both dependants raise `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.137`.
**Known gap:** `minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue` are still measured against the stored subtotal, not the printed one.

`imageZoomOnHover` moved out of `ShpConfig` into the Puck "Product: Gallery" block itself (`shopDetailGalleryPuckComponent`, `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`) as a per-block `zoomOnHover` radio field (default off), so it's set per layout in the shop layout editor rather than shop-wide in admin settings. Flows straight from the block's own prop into the `zoom` prop on `ProductGallery`/`ShopDetailGallerySlotProps`, same as before - `DetailPartContext.zoomImages` is gone, `ShopSettingsTab`'s "Product images" section is gone.

**Product photos are square everywhere; the `shape` prop is gone (shop v0.1.44, shop-variations v0.1.11)**
One ratio, 1:1, for every product photo: the Product Detail stage (`.spd-stage`) and the card image (`.shop-card-img` in `card-parts.tsx`, `.spc-img` in `product-card-css.ts`, both previously `4/3`). The per-instance `shape` select (square/portrait/landscape) is **removed** from both the `ShopDetailGallery` and `ShopCardImage` Puck blocks, from `GalleryProps`/`ImageProps`/`ProductGallery`, from `ShopDetailGallerySlotProps` (so `shop-variations`' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` stopped reading it and no longer sets `aspectRatio` inline - it inherits the ratio from shop's `.spd-stage` via `classNames`, one definition rather than two modules agreeing to keep saying `1/1`), and from every `starterLayouts.ts` block (two set `landscape`). The `.shape-*` CSS classes are gone. Its only real effect was letting one shop's photos be three shapes depending on the layout a page used. Saved `Layout` rows may still carry `props.shape`; Puck passes unknown props through and nothing reads it, so they resolve square with no data migration - correct on this fresh-install platform. **Exempt: Overlay cards** (`.shop-card-img.fill-mode`, `aspect-ratio:auto` inside a `3/4` card) - the photo being the whole card is that design, not a shape. Non-square originals crop rather than distort (`object-fit:cover` in an `overflow:hidden` box). `shop-variations` declares `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.44`, since its gallery now leans on shop's square `.spd-stage`.

**Product: Tabs strip - one segmented track instead of loose pills (shop, working tree)**
The tabs now sit inside a single pill-shaped `.spd-tab-track` (`display:inline-flex`, 4px padding, 1px `--color-border`, `--color-surface` fill, `flex:none`), so the strip reads as a segmented control with a current position rather than a row of separately outlined buttons. `.spd-tab-btn` accordingly loses its own fill and outline (`border:1px solid transparent` kept so a tab does not resize when it lights up) and hovers to `--color-bg-subtle`; `.on` and `.spd-tab-action` are unchanged, still `--color-primary` over `--color-on-primary` with the `!important` that beats a site theme's own button fill. The track is the nav's **only child**, so the nav keeps doing the alignment (`justify-content`), the sticky pin, the divider and the sideways scroll exactly as before - which matters because `ProductSectionTabs`' overflow measurement, its `data-spd-anchor` nudge and the shell's fades/arrows all measure the NAV. Breakpoints: at `mobileBp` the track takes `width:100%` so the shrink-to-fit tabs have a row to share; at `SMALL_PHONE_BP` it goes back to `width:auto` so it is wider than the nav and the nav is what scrolls. Rendered in all four places for editor/RSC parity: `ProductSectionTabs` (island), `ShopDetailTabs` (editor preview), `ShopDetailSectionNav` (editor preview) and `ShopDetailSectionNavRsc`.

**Product: Tabs strip - own background colour, and the active tab scrolls itself into view**
Two per-block fields on `shopDetailTabsPuckComponent` (`modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`): `bgColour` (custom field, core `SiteColourField`, so it carries the light and dark arms in one stored `light-dark(l, d)` value - `lib/puck/lightDark.ts`) and `bgOpacity` (number, 0-100, default 100). `navBgVars()` folds the opacity into **each arm separately** via `color-mix(in srgb, <arm> N%, ...)` rather than wrapping the whole `light-dark()`, matching what `SectionBgColorField` already writes; `rgba()` can't wrap a `var(--color-N)` swatch, hence `color-mix`. It emits **two** custom properties on `.spd-tab-shell`: `--spd-tabnav-bg` (mixed over `transparent`, the strip's own fill) and `--spd-tabnav-fade` (the same colour mixed over `var(--color-page-bg, var(--color-bg))`, i.e. already composited onto the page). The edge fades and arrow buttons use the **fade** var, because they paint over the shell's own fill - a see-through colour applied twice would darken both edges relative to the middle. A blank colour sets neither var, so the CSS falls back to `transparent` / page-background exactly as before, and sticky still fills so the panel can't show through as it scrolls under. Editor preview (`ShopDetailTabs`) sets the same vars on the same wrapper for markup/class parity.

The mobile bug it shipped with: on a small phone the strip is an `overflow-x:auto` row, and the scroll-spy would light a tab (Downloads, typically last) that sat off the right-hand edge - the highlight was correct and invisible. `ProductSectionTabs` (`modules/shop/components/public/ProductDetailIslands.tsx`) now tags every pill `data-spd-anchor` (including the leading CTA, whose anchor is `spd-buy`) and, on `active` change only, nudges `nav.scrollTo` so the lit pill clears the 32px arrow/fade overlay at whichever edge it came in from. Guarded on `scrollWidth > clientWidth`, so it is a no-op on desktop and on the larger-phone shrink-to-fit tier, and it never fights a shopper dragging the strip by hand. Honours `prefers-reduced-motion` (jumps instead of smooth-scrolling). The standalone **Section links** block is static server markup and is untouched.

**Product Detail gallery, viewport fit (v0.1.42, reworked v0.1.44)**
The gallery column (`.spd-stage-col`, CSS in `galleryCss()`, `modules/shop/components/puck/parts/detail-parts.tsx`) is `position:sticky` so the photo stays with a shopper scrolling a taller buy column, and the stage fits the leftover viewport **by giving up width** - `aspect-ratio` takes the height with it, so it stays square and merely gets smaller. `--spd-fit` (`calc(100dvh - var(--spd-header-h) - 32px - var(--spd-thumbs-h))`) is that width budget; the stage is `flex:none;align-self:center;width:min(100%,var(--spd-fit));min-width:140px`. **v0.1.42 capped the column's height instead and let the stage flex-shrink into it, which squashed the square stage into a letterbox and cropped the photo** - the bug the square rule exists to prevent. `beside` mode overrides `--spd-fit` (the strip sits alongside, costing the stage no height) and uses `flex:1 1 auto;max-width:var(--spd-fit)`, since the strip is spending some of the row's width too.
