**The Split's media track is `min(N%, var(--spd-gallery-fit))`, not `minmax(0,N%)`** - a track is a floor as well as a ceiling, and `minmax(0,N%)` always grew to the full N% however narrow the column inside it went. The two only agreed while `--spd-thumbs-h` was wrong: the moment the strip started being measured the column shed those 76px, the track did not, and the difference showed as dead white space between the photo and the buy column. `min()` sizes the cell to the same number the column is about to take, so the `1fr` beside it collects the slack (measured on `deskwell.co.uk` at 1800x760: cell 518 → 486, buy column 602 → 634, gap 32 → 0; at 1800x1010 the `45%` arm still binds and nothing moves). Not `fit-content(N%)` for the reason above - it floors the track at the item's definite width and sails past the cap - and `min()` takes no contribution from its contents at all. The calc is hoisted to `:root` as `--spd-gallery-fit` / `--spd-gallery-fit-beside` because the track needs it on the *Split*, which is not the element `--spd-fit` is declared on. `beside` keeps `minmax(0,N%)`: that column is `width:auto` and stretches to fill its track, so there was never a gap to close, and its budget is the stage's rather than the column's. **The mobile collapse rule now spells out all three variants** (`:has(.spd-stage-col)`, `:has(.spd-stage-col.beside)`, `:has(> :last-child .spd-stage-col.beside)`) - `:has()` counts what is inside it, so the `.beside` track rules outrank a bare `:has(.spd-stage-col)` and a phone would otherwise keep two columns.

Both numbers need measurements CSS cannot get. The site header's height: core does **not** publish it - the header is the Site Header Puck block (`lib/puck/config.tsx`), whose height is a per-site prop that may be `auto`, whose stickiness is a second prop, and which a site may omit. So `modules/shop/components/public/GalleryViewportFit.tsx` (client island, renders null) measures it and publishes `--spd-header-h` on `:root`, counting only `<header>` elements computing to `position:sticky|fixed` with `top <= 4px` (a static header scrolls away and costs the column nothing) and summing `height + top` (a header parked below an announcement bar). It also publishes `--spd-thumbs-h` - the stacked strip's height plus the column's `gap:12px`, `0` when there's no strip (no strip, no gap). Re-measures on `ResizeObserver` (headers + strip) and `resize`: late-decoding logo, wrapping nav, condense-on-scroll header, strip rewrapping rows. Fallbacks `96px`/`76px` cover pre-hydration and the editor canvas.

**The strip is not necessarily on the page when the island mounts, and a `MutationObserver` on `document.body` (childList + subtree) now watches for it arriving.** Observing "whatever exists right now" assumed it did. On a product with options - shop-variations' replacement gallery, i.e. the interesting half of a real catalogue - `VariantSlotGalleryClient` renders no strip until `thumbs.length + extras.length > 1`, which on Deskwell means until the shopper has picked a combination and the variant's own photographs arrive. The one measurement at mount therefore published `--spd-thumbs-h: 0px`, nothing was left observing anything, and the value never moved: the stage kept the strip's 76px share of the viewport **as well as its own**, so the sticky column ran 76px past the bottom of the screen and the thumbnails were cut off by the viewport edge (measured live on `deskwell.co.uk` at 1100x700: column bottom 722 against a 700px viewport, versus 684 - the intended `100dvh - 16px` - once the value is right). A window resize was the only thing that ever corrected it, which is why it read as intermittent. The callback is gated on the strip **element identity** changing, so an unrelated re-render costs one `querySelector`; `apply()` re-points the `ResizeObserver` at the new strip (and unobserves the old), and height changes stay the `ResizeObserver`'s job. Measurement is not deferred to `requestAnimationFrame` on purpose - a background tab pauses rAF, so a shopper configuring in one tab and returning to another would find the measurement still pending.

**A pinned section strip is the third measurement (`--spd-tabnav-h`, shop v0.1.148)**
The gallery is not the only thing pinned below the header: the **Product: Tabs** strip (sticky on `.spd-tab-shell`) and the standalone **Product: Section links** block (sticky on `.spd-tab-nav` itself) both pin at `top:var(--spd-header-h)`. A gallery clearing only the header therefore pinned *underneath* the strip, hiding the top of the photo and, on a configurable product, shop-variations’ "Your choice" pill in the same band. `.spd-stage-col` (and `.beside`) now read `var(--spd-tabnav-h,0px)` in **both** places: added to the sticky `top`, and subtracted from `--spd-fit`, because the width budget is what keeps the square stage inside the viewport and a strip left out of the sum pushed the stage off the bottom by its own height.

`modules/shop/components/public/StickyStripHeight.tsx` (client island, renders `null`) is the single publisher. It measures **by selector** (`.spd-tab-shell.sticky, .spd-tab-nav.sticky`) rather than by ref, because a page may carry both blocks and two mounts must agree on one number instead of each overwriting the other with its own strip’s height; it takes the **tallest, not the sum**, since both pin at the same `top` and so overlap rather than stack. The Tabs island moves `sticky` UP to its shell and leaves its own nav unpinned, so the two selectors never count one strip twice. A module-level refcount leaves clearing the property to the last unmount, and a `signal` prop re-runs the measurement when the markup changes rather than merely its size (the editor toggling `sticky`, or the tab count moving) - the dependency the old `[sticky, tabs]` effect provided. Mounted by `ProductSectionTabs`, by `ShopDetailSectionNavRsc` and by `ShopDetailSectionNav` (editor preview) for parity; renders nothing, so Puck editor/RSC markup parity is untouched. **The Section links block published this variable nowhere before**, being server-only, so with it pinned the sections’ own `scroll-margin-top` was short by the strip’s height and every jump link landed its heading behind the strip.

**The strip's width is deliberately NOT tied to `--spd-fit`.** Its height feeds that sum, so sizing it from the result would let a narrower strip wrap to more rows → taller strip → smaller budget → narrower strip: a loop the ResizeObserver would chase. It keeps its full column width (`flex:none`); only the stage moves. Rendered by `ShopDetailGalleryRsc`, **not** by `ProductGallery`, so a `shop.product-detail-parts` provider's replacement gallery gets it too - it wears `.spd-stage-col`. No `overflow` on the column: it would clip `.spd-thumb.on`'s `box-shadow: 0 0 0 1px` ring on the edge thumbnails of every page, to catch only a ~35-image outlier. Below `tabletBp` the column goes `position:static` and the stage back to `width:100%` - stacked, it has the width to itself and shouldn't shrink for a viewport it no longer shares.

**Thumbnail strip overflow affordance (`GalleryThumbStrip`, v0.1.48)**

The strip below the stage is one nowrap `overflow-x:auto` row (above), which on a product with a dozen photos simply looked like it ended at the column's edge - nothing said the row ran on. `modules/shop/components/public/GalleryThumbStrip.tsx` (client) wraps it in `.spd-thumbs-wrap` and renders, at whichever end still has scroll left in it, a `.spd-thumbs-fade` gradient and a `.spd-thumbs-arrow` button - the same affordance, geometry (2rem fade inboard of a 1.5rem arrow) and 160px step as core's admin `components/admin/TabStrip.tsx`. State is `scrollLeft` vs `scrollWidth - clientWidth` on a `scroll` + `resize` + `ResizeObserver` check; both ends start "at" so the server's markup carries no arrows and the effect earns them. Keyed on `Children.count`, **not `children`**: the gallery re-renders on every pointer move while the magnifier is tracking, and keying on the nodes would tear the listeners down and rebuild them on each one.

`beside` strips pass straight through unwrapped - left/right means nothing to a column - so that layout's markup and CSS are exactly as before. `ShopDetailGallery` (editor preview) mirrors the same wrapper for markup/class parity; its four placeholders never overflow, so no arrows are earned there.

**The new rules are scoped to `.spd-thumbs-wrap`, not to `.spd-thumbs`, and that is load-bearing.** A `shop.product-detail-parts` provider's replacement gallery (shop-variations' `VariantSlotGalleryClient` / `ShopVariantGallery`) wears the `.spd-thumbs` class it is handed via `classNames` but renders it straight into `.spd-stage-col` with no wrapper. `flex:1 1 auto` reaching it there would read as grow-to-fill on the **vertical** axis (the column's main axis) and stretch its strip down the page; hiding the scrollbar would leave it with no overflow hint at all, having no arrows to replace it with. Hence `.spd-thumbs-wrap .spd-thumbs{flex:1 1 auto;scrollbar-width:none}` and an untouched `.spd-stage-col:not(.beside) .spd-thumbs`.

**`VariantSlotGalleryClient` now adopts `GalleryThumbStrip` (shop-variations v0.1.15), which is what actually put the arrows in front of shoppers.** The affordance shipped in shop v0.1.48 and, on a real catalogue, almost nobody saw it: any product with options is claimed by shop-variations' replacement gallery, and that is the half of the catalogue with the most photos. The strip on Deskwell's Chiro Plus overflowed (804px of thumbnails in a 796px column) with no arrow, no fade and a hidden scrollbar. The slot gallery now renders `<GalleryThumbStrip beside={thumbPosition === 'beside'} className={classNames.thumbs}>` - the `className`/`beside` props existed from v0.1.48 for exactly this caller and had no consumer until now - so `requiresModules: shop` moved 0.1.44 → **0.1.48**, the release that carries the component (the `product-downloads` lesson at the top of this file, applied on purpose rather than after the fact). Its thumb buttons gained `role="tab"`/`aria-selected` to earn the wrapper's `role="tablist"`, matching `ProductGallery`. `ShopVariantGallery` (the hand-placed Puck block, own `svr-gallery-thumb` styling, 56px) is a separate surface and is **not** wrapped - no live consumer asked for it. `GalleryViewportFit` is unaffected: it queries `.spd-stage-col:not(.beside) .spd-thumbs` as a **descendant**, so an interposed wrapper changes nothing it measures.

The hidden scrollbar slightly *raises* the photo's budget: its height was being charged to `--spd-thumbs-h`.

**Part-dispatch (shipments)**
An order used to be either shipped or not - the SHIPPED status was the whole record of dispatch, which cannot describe "three of the five went out on Tuesday". Data layer: `modules/shop/lib/db/shipments.ts` exports `createShipment`, `getShipmentsForOrder`, `getDispatchedQtyByOrderItem`, `getOrderDispatchSummary`, `isOrderFullyDispatched`, `deleteShipment`, plus the pure `isFullyDispatched`/`isPartiallyDispatched` so the UI can answer the same question from a summary it already holds. Types in `lib/types.ts`: `ShpShipment`, `ShpShipmentItem`, `ShpShipmentWithItems`, `ShpOrderItemDispatch` (`quantity`/`refundedQty`/`dispatchedQty`/`outstandingQty`, the last being `quantity - refundedQty - dispatchedQty` floored at zero), `ShpOrderDispatchSummary`. Load-bearing details:
- **Dispatched totals are aggregated in a subquery BEFORE the join to the order lines.** Joining `shp_shipment_items` straight onto `shp_order_items` fans a line out once per shipment and any later arithmetic counts it several times - the same trap that caused the real overselling bug in `decrementStockOnShip`.
- **The advisory-lock namespace is shared with refunds** (`0x53485250`, transaction-scoped `pg_try_advisory_xact_lock` keyed on the order id). Refunds and dispatch police the same units of the same order, so they have to be mutually exclusive: a refund landing between a shipment's validation and its insert would otherwise refund units the dispatch had just decided were still dispatchable. One of the two simply waits, or is turned away with a 409 and a "something else is updating this order" message.
- **This layer records dispatch and nothing else - it does NOT touch `stock_count`.** Stock still moves in exactly two places: normal lines at payment (`lib/order-fulfillment.ts`) and pre-order lines when an admin sets the order to SHIPPED (`decrementStockOnShip`). Adding a decrement here would double-count against one of those and silently oversell. If dispatch is ever meant to own the pre-order decrement, the decrement has to MOVE, not be added alongside.
- Two lines for the same order item in one request are folded together before anything is validated, or each would validate against the same starting figure and together sail past the cap. "Fully dispatched" excludes an order with nothing dispatchable (empty, or refunded down to nothing) - there was never a parcel to send.
Admin UI: new `components/admin/DispatchModal.tsx` (built on `RefundModal`'s bones - a quantity per line capped at what is still owed, optional parcel details, server rejections shown verbatim; the real caps are server-side, so a refund landing while the modal is open is caught there). `components/admin/OrderDetailScreen.tsx` gains a Dispatched column on the items table, a "Dispatch items" action beside "Refund items", a Dispatches list, the HOLD_ALL banner, and a derived "Partly dispatched"/"All dispatched" pill next to the status select - **a marker, not a new `ShpOrderStatus` value**; it fetches `/admin/orders/[id]/dispatch` alongside the order.
Email: `lib/shipment-email.ts`'s `sendShipmentDispatchedEmail({orderId, shipmentId})` renders the `PARTIAL_SHIPPED` template. `STATUS_SHIPPED` says the whole order is on its way and only knows orderNumber/customerName/shopName, so sending it for three of five items would be a straight untruth; this one lists what went and what is still owed. It covers the final parcel too - the copy switches to "the last part of your order" via the `isFinalPart`/`hasOutstanding` flags - so the dispatch route calls it for EVERY shipment and never has to choose between templates. Item lists go in as ONE plain-text variable (`- name xN`, newline-joined) because `lib/email.ts` HTML-escapes every `{{variable}}`, so any `<br>`/`<li>` built here would reach the customer as visible angle brackets - the same trade-off `ORDER_CONFIRMED` already makes. Silent no-op when the order, shipment or its lines cannot be found: an email is not worth failing a dispatch that has already committed.
**`preOrderMixedCartBehaviour` is now actually implemented, as a FULFILMENT policy rather than a checkout restriction.** Neither value forbids a mixed basket, and nothing on the storefront blocks the Place order button - the payment-intent route carries an explicit comment saying so, since "add the gate here" is the obvious wrong fix. HOLD_ALL: `[id]/status` refuses SHIPPED with a 409 while any pre-order line is outstanding, naming how many items and the latest expected date and pointing at the two ways out (take the products off pre-order, or switch the setting to split shipping); the checkout review step tells the shopper the whole order is sent together once everything has arrived. PROMPT_SPLIT: part-dispatch is permitted and the shopper is told anything in stock can be sent straight away with the pre-order to follow. The shared rule is `outstandingPreOrderItems(items)` in `lib/db/orders.ts` - the line's snapshotted dispatch date is the primary signal, a line with no date falls back to the product's own `is_pre_order` flag (so unticking it once stock lands is the owner's escape hatch), and a line whose product row has gone is treated as ready rather than jamming the order shut for good. It lives in the data layer precisely because the status route enforces the policy and the dispatch route explains it, and two copies would drift into disagreeing about whether the shop is holding the order.

**Order, stock and money correctness (2026-07-23)**
- `decrementStockOnShip` aggregates `SUM(quantity) GROUP BY product_id` before joining to the product row. The plain join updated each product once however many order-item rows pointed at it, so a basket with two lines of the same product (which personalised lines deliberately allow) decremented by the larger line only - qty 1 + qty 3 took 3 off, not 4 - and silently oversold.
- Coupon usage is keyed on the resolved `coupon_id`, never the raw code: `fulfillPaidOrder` bumps `usage_count` only when `order.couponId` is set, `countPriorCouponOrdersByEmail` takes a coupon id (also immune to a later rename), and the payment-intent route stores `couponCode` only when a coupon genuinely resolved. A rejected or expired code previously burned the coupon's usage and the customer's per-customer allowance against an order it never discounted.
- Refunds go through `processRefund` (`lib/db/refunds.ts`), split into a short validation transaction and a settle transaction with the provider call between them. The validation half takes the order's transaction-scoped advisory lock, re-reads every cap under it and commits a PENDING refund row that reserves the order; a second overlapping request sees the live reservation and gets a 409 instead of validating against quantities that are about to move (the old code read the caps, called the provider and wrote afterwards, so two requests could both slip past). A PENDING row older than 5 minutes can only have been left by a request that died mid-flight - module routes are capped at 60 seconds - so it stops blocking, but its amount still counts against the caps because the provider may well have refunded it. The provider HTTP call runs with NO database transaction open, so a slow provider never pins a pooled connection, and the refund row id is passed as the idempotency key (Stripe's `idempotencyKey` request option, PayPal's `PayPal-Request-Id` header, GoCardless's equivalent) so a retried call cannot refund twice. A FAILED provider refund no longer increments `refunded_qty`.
- `markOrderPaymentFailed(id, reason)` takes `'FAILED' | 'CHARGEBACK'`. FAILED (the default, used by the Stripe/PayPal failure webhooks and the confirm route) still only touches a PENDING order, so a stray late failure cannot undo a paid one. CHARGEBACK (the GoCardless settle handler, when a settled payment is later charged back or fails at the bank) moves an already-PAID order to ON_HOLD with `payment_status='FAILED'` and writes an internal note telling the owner to check whether anything shipped against money that has since been clawed back - previously that case was a silent no-op, because the guard only matched PENDING.
- Stripe's `charge.refunded` handler resolves the order through `charge.payment_intent` and the new `getOrderByPaymentReference`. The `shpOrderId` metadata it used to read only ever exists on the PaymentIntent; Stripe does not copy it onto the Charge, so a dashboard refund matched nothing and the order was never marked refunded.
- `minimumOrderValue`/`maximumOrderValue` are enforced at `POST /public/checkout/payment-intent` as well as at `/checkout/session`. The session route only advises the browser, while the payment-intent route is what actually creates a payable order, so a direct POST skipping the session step produced a chargeable below-minimum order.
- `updateOrderStatus` is idempotent (`WHERE … AND status != status`) and returns whether the row changed; every once-per-transition side effect now hangs off that boolean. SHIPPED → COMPLETED → SHIPPED used to decrement the pre-order stock a second time, and `decrementStockOnShip` clamps at zero rather than erroring, so the shop quietly undercounted itself.
- `decrementPreOrderCount` (`lib/db/products.ts`) is the counterpart to `incrementPreOrderCount`, called by `releasePreOrderAllocationForOrder` on a genuine transition to CANCELLED; the refund settle path runs the identical statement inlined, because it has to execute on the transaction client rather than the shared one. `pre_order_count` previously only ever went up, so a cancelled pre-order kept its slot forever and, once the count had touched `pre_order_max_quantity`, the auto-flip left `is_pre_order = false` permanently - quietly taking a product out of pre-order mode with nobody actually waiting on those units. One statement, so the counter and the flag cannot disagree; re-enabling is deliberately narrow (only a product that was sitting at its cap, which is precisely the state the increment creates, and never one with no cap), so a product the owner switched off by hand is never switched back on. The release is guarded on `paid_at IS NOT NULL` (the allocation is only ever consumed by `fulfillPaidOrder`, so an order cancelled before it paid never took a slot) and on `quantity - refunded_qty`, so units a refund has already returned cannot be double-released.
- The CSV import engine rejects a negative price (`lib/import-engine.ts`), matching the same fix in google-sheet-products-for-shop's preview.

**Admin dialogs**
The shop admin no longer calls the browser's `confirm()`/`prompt()`/`alert()`. `modules/shop/components/admin/dialogs.tsx` exports three promise-based hooks - `useConfirm()`, `usePrompt()`, `useAlert()` - each returning `[invoke, node]`: call `await invoke(...)` and render `{node}` once in the screen. Styling matches the module's other overlays (colour tokens only, `role="dialog"`/`aria-modal`, Escape cancels, Enter confirms, delete confirms use the `btn-danger` class). Wired through CategoriesScreen, CollectionsScreen, ProductsScreen (new-item name prompts), DiscountsScreen (delete confirms + save-error alerts), TaxShippingScreen (delete confirms), ProductEditor (upload/save-error alerts).

**Money formatting**
All prices render through one helper - `modules/shop/lib/money.ts` `formatMoney(amount, symbol='£')` - which coerces the string/number a price arrives as and always emits `symbol` + 2dp (e.g. `£7.99`). Storefront pages/blocks and order emails pass `config.currencySymbol`; admin screens (client-rendered, no server config) read it via `components/admin/use-currency-symbol.ts` `useCurrencySymbol()` (fetches `/api/m/shop/public/config` once, module-cached, `£` fallback). Prices are decimal pounds end to end (`NUMERIC(10,2)`); nothing is stored or displayed in pence (the Stripe `×100` in `lib/payments/stripe.ts` is API-only). Discount "value" cells format per type: `%` for PERCENTAGE, `formatMoney` for FIXED_AMOUNT, `—` for FREE_SHIPPING.

**External Integrations**
Stripe (Payment Intents + Elements + webhooks, `stripe` npm SDK), PayPal (Orders v2 REST API directly, no SDK), core Members system (optional, guest checkout always works regardless), core Media/upload pipeline (`uploadMedia()` reused for digital files, but not `saveMediaRecord` - see core diffs above), core email (`renderEmailTemplate` + `sendEmail`; from v0.1.180 the shop's ten order emails are declared in `modules/shop/lib/email-templates.ts` and registered through the manifest `emailTemplates` seam, so core's `EmailTemplate` overrides, wrapper designs and editor cover them - `shp_email_templates` is retired and unread, left in place only so a rollback survives, and migration `014_email_templates_to_core.sql` copies across just the rows an owner had genuinely edited plus every `is_active` decision).

**Cron Jobs**
`0 7 * * *` → `/api/m/shop/cron/low-stock-alerts` - low-stock digest email (deduped via `low_stock_alerted_at`, re-arms on any stock_count write) + `shp_import_jobs` retention (30 days) + abandoned-PENDING-order pruning (24h, Q8). `CRON_SECRET` bearer-gated.

**Scripts**
None.

**Known Limitations** (v0.1.2 - flagged here rather than silently shipped as if finished)

- Categories have an indented nested-tree admin UI with ↑/↓ sibling reorder, reparent, and per-category display-mode override; collections still have no reorder UI (the `position` column and API support it; only rename/delete are wired up in the collections screen). Neither uses drag-to-reorder (↑/↓ buttons only, like Directory).
- `shop.products-toolbar` (**published by shop, v0.1.61**; live consumer `google-sheet-products-for-shop`) - a module hangs a control beside the Products **list** header buttons (Export/Import-template/Import/New product). Resolved server-side in `app/cactus-admin/shop/products/page.tsx` (`resolveToolbarExtras`: reads each active module's manifest `extensionPoints`, permission-filters per entry, looks the component up in `moduleExtensionPointComponents['shop.products-toolbar']`) and passed as a single `toolbarExtras` `ReactNode` into the client `ProductsScreen`, which renders it after the New product button. Empty (renders nothing) on a plain shop. google-sheet uses it for its Google Sheet dropdown.
- `shop.products-tabs` (**published by shop, v0.1.92**; live consumer `shop-variations`) - a module hangs a whole-page **tab** beside "Products" on the Products **list** page. Same resolution shape (`resolveProductsTabs` in `products/page.tsx`: manifest read + permission filter + `moduleExtensionPointComponents['shop.products-tabs']`), building `ProductsTab[]` `{id,label,order,node}` passed to the client `ProductsScreen` with `initialTab` (from `?tab=`). `ProductsScreen` renders a `TabStrip` only when at least one tab is contributed (so a plain shop is unchanged), keeps the built-in "Products" list as the first tab, and mounts only the active contributed tab's `node` (its products fetch is skipped while a contributed tab is active). shop-variations uses it for the cross-product Variations browser.
- Reply Catcher's contribution to the `shop.order-messages` extension point is out of scope of this build (Q12) - the Communications tab section is real and will render the moment another module publishes to that point, but nothing does yet.
- The module-side rate limiter (`lib/rate-limit.ts`) is in-memory, not table-backed - resets on a cold start and doesn't share state across concurrent serverless instances. Acceptable for a secondary guard behind normal validation, but weaker than contact-form's DB-backed one.

v0.1.1 fixed five review findings from the original v0.1.0 build: Stripe/PayPal `confirmPayment` now validates charged amount/currency against the order (not just status/reference); `GET /downloads/[token]` streams the file through the endpoint instead of redirecting to the permanent storage URL; the `product`/`checkout` default page layouts now seed `ShopBackInStockForm`/`ShopUpsellProducts` (new installs only, per `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`); the product editor gained a real Recommendations panel, image picker, and digital-file upload; the Discounts screen, refund flow, CSV import, and page-layouts editor were all rebuilt from `prompt()`/raw-JSON placeholders into proper UI (see the Admin pages entry above for each).

### Shop Variations

- Slug: `shop-variations` (table prefix `svr_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/shop-variations`, manifest version 0.1.154 in the working tree (`requiresCoreVersion 0.5.1150`, `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.260`).
- **`lib/sitemap.ts`** (0.1.154) - one sitemap URL per enabled variation, as the parent's address carrying the storefront's own option parameters (`?headrest=with-headrest&upholstery-colour=rivet-forge`, the exact form `lib/url-selection.ts` reads back). Three queries; the CHILD row is aliased `p` so `outOfStockSql()` splices in against the row that carries the stock; shopper's stock answer only, never the staff exemption; `[]` on a closed shop; 5-minute in-process memo keyed `siteUrl|urlStyle|outOfStockVisibility`. Only COMPLETE combinations are published (options read in their own query so an option with no values still counts towards "every option answered"), a product whose options slugify to one parameter name is dropped whole, and the 45,000 cap plus every drop is `console.warn`ed rather than silent - the protocol rejects a whole file over 50,000 URLs. Pure half `buildVariationEntries` with 10 tests in `lib/sitemap.test.ts`. Live Deskwell: 19,700 publishable combinations across 344 products.
- **`lib/canonical-query-provider.ts`** (0.1.154) - the `shop.product-canonical-query` provider, so the product page declares those addresses canonical instead of disowning them. Declines on a partial selection; runs the storefront's own `withStrandedFilled` -> `withAutoSelected` -> `resolveVariant`; spells its answer from the variation's own `optionValueIds` (not from what was typed), so alias values and a reordered query string fold onto one address. Shares `buildVariationQuery` with the sitemap - two spellings and the sitemap would recommend a URL the page refuses. A variation's own child-slug deep link still canonicalises to the bare parent, unchanged. `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.205` (0.1.173 adds the `shop.product-saved` seam the tax-class sync needs; 0.1.92 added the `shop.products-tabs` host slot the Variations tab needs; `GalleryThumbStrip` needed v0.1.15; previously 0.1.44, and before that 0.1.43 for `shop.gallery-media` - `product-editor/context` needed only 0.1.38 and `shop.product-detail-parts` only 0.1.35), `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.493`. Reuses shop's `shop.products`/`shop.reports` permissions (declares none of its own) and joins the existing **Shop** admin nav group with one entry ("Variation tools", was "Product options" until v0.1.72).
- **Tells shop which listings are reduced (v0.1.132, working tree):** shop's automatic "On Sale" tag has to include a variations listing whose discount sits on a hidden child, because the parent's own `sale_price` is always empty. Two one-line contributions, no schema change: `lib/sale-provider.ts` fills shop's new `shop.product-on-sale` point with an `EXISTS` over `svr_variants` joined to the child `shp_products` row (enabled variant, ACTIVE child, `sale_price` set, non-negative and under `price` - the SQL twin of shop's `isOnSale`), which is what makes the tag's page and any `tagSlug` filter find these listings; and `lib/card-price-provider.ts` now also returns `onSale` on each `ShopCardFromPrice`, which is what makes the card print the badge. `requiresModules: shop` floor moved to 0.1.212 (the version that ships the point and the field).
- **Findable by SKU, on both the admin product list and the site search (v0.1.122, working tree):** a shop using variations keeps its real supplier codes on hidden `catalogue_hidden` child `shp_products` rows - the parent listing's own `sku` column is usually blank - so neither the admin Products search box nor the storefront search box nor the site-wide search module ever found a listing by the code that's on the customer's paperwork. Two providers, one file each, no schema change. `lib/product-search-provider.ts` fills shop's new `shop.product-search` point (see Shop entry above): `matchSql(term)` is an `EXISTS` against `svr_variants` joined to `shp_products` on `child_product_id`, matching the child's `sku` `ILIKE`; covers the admin product list AND the public product search box, since both go through shop's `listProducts`. `lib/search-text-provider.ts` fills the `search` module's new `search.shop-product-text` point: `textFor(productIds)` returns each parent's variations' SKUs space-joined (one `string_agg` query, `GROUP BY product_id`), folded into the indexed body ahead of the description; `changedSince(since)` returns parent ids whose child `sku` or whose `svr_variants` row moved since the high-water mark, because a child's edit never touches the PARENT's `updated_at` and the incremental indexer would otherwise never revisit it (a variation deleted since the last run is the one gap left open on purpose - its code stays findable until the next full rebuild, judged milder than either a live query per keystroke or a bespoke per-source deletion diff). Both providers return the parent, never the child: a variation code is a door into the listing it belongs to, not a link to a product that isn't meant to have its own page. Disabled variations still match on both providers - the code was real once and staff still need to find it. `requiresModules: shop` floor bumped to 0.1.205 (the version that ships `shop.product-search`). Checks: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, full module suite unaffected (no test file added - matches the untested-glue precedent of `card-price-provider.ts`/`listability.ts`/`availability-provider.ts`, which are the same shape).
- **Publishes the chosen variation page-wide (v0.1.102):** `lib/selection-broadcast.ts` - `publishVariantSelection` fires window event `cactus-shop-variant-selection` with `{slug, parentProductId, productId, allOptionsChosen, chosenValueIds}` (`chosenValueIds` added in 0.1.104: every option value picked so far, in option order, so a consumer can say something sensible about a HALF-built combination - `productId` only lands once the last option is settled) and parks the same detail on `window.__cactusVariantSelection` for a late-mounting listener; called from `useVariationSelection` (so it reflects the resolved variant every part shows) and deduped by JSON equality, since every island on the page runs the hook. `productId` is null until a full combination is chosen. A browser event rather than an export ON PURPOSE: a consumer must not import `@/modules/shop-variations/...` (the path does not exist on an install without this module and would break that build), which is the same rule advanced-shipping's `variations-bridge.ts` follows server-side. First consumer: that module's `ShopShippingOptions` picker.
- **A variation's tax class follows the listing (v0.1.108):** `lib/tax-class-sync.ts` - `syncVariantChildTaxClass(parentId)` is one `UPDATE` putting every child of that parent onto the parent's `tax_class_id` (skipping the ones that already agree, so it is safe to repeat and a no-op on a product with no variations), and `syncVariationsOnProductSaved(productId, changed)` is the `shop.product-saved` listener that calls it, gated on `changed.includes('taxClassId')` so a price, a description or a stock count costs nothing. The children still copy the class at creation (`generateMatrix`, `createSingleVariant`, `upsertVariantForCombination`); this is what keeps them right when it is set or changed AFTERWARDS, which nothing did before - the basket rates a line from the child while the product page prices from the parent, so the two disagreed silently. Deliberately one-directional: a per-variation class was never selectable, so a child that differs is drift, not a decision. Unit-tested in `lib/tax-class-sync.test.ts` (the gate, and that the parent id rides as a bound parameter).
- `core.media-usage-providers` (`lib/media-usage-provider.ts`) - contributes `svr_option_values.swatch` + `swatch_small` (0.1.120) + `svr_uploads.media_ref`/`media_key` to core's media usage index.
- Adds product options to the shop: fixed **variant matrices** (e.g. Size × Colour, each combination its own price/SKU/barcode/stock/weight/image) and free-form **personalisation add-ons** (text, long text, number, priced dropdown, checkbox, date, file upload). A variant is a real but `catalogue_hidden` child `shp_products` row created through shop's own `createProduct`, so basket, checkout, inventory, orders and refunds work unchanged; the storefront selector resolves the chosen combination to that child id and calls shop's `addToCart(childId, qty, {meta})`. Personalisation rides in the generic `line_meta` carrier, priced server-side by the registered resolver.

**Database**
Table prefix: `svr_` (8 tables). Full DDL in `modules/shop-variations/migrations/001_initial.sql` (idempotent); later per-change files are numbered (`002_image_option_type.sql` widens the `svr_options.control_type` CHECK to admit `IMAGE`, also mirrored in 001; `003_requires_previous_option.sql` adds `svr_options.requires_previous_option`, also mirrored in 001; `004_option_source.sql` adds `svr_options.source_provider`/`source_ref` + `svr_option_values.source_ref` and the `(option_id, source_ref)` index, also mirrored in 001; `005_option_name_overridden.sql` adds `svr_options.name_overridden`, also mirrored in 001; `007_delete_children_with_parent.sql` adds function `svr_delete_variant_child()` + AFTER DELETE row trigger `svr_variants_delete_child` on `svr_variants` - deleting a variant row deletes its child `shp_products` row, which is what finally cleans up when a PARENT product is deleted from shop's own UI: the parent's cascade removes `svr_variants` but no module code runs, so children used to survive as orphans still holding SKU + slug. Module code paths delete the child first (cascade removes the variant row), so for them the trigger's re-delete matches nothing; TRUNCATE (backup restore) fires no row triggers); `009_variant_tax_class.sql` adds **no DDL at all** - it is the one-off data catch-up that puts every existing variation child onto its parent listing's `tax_class_id`, touching only the children that disagree, so it is idempotent by construction and matches nothing on a fresh install; `011_variant_show_in_gallery.sql` adds `svr_variants.show_image_in_gallery` + `show_model_in_gallery`, also mirrored in 001; `012_card_fit_lines.sql` adds `svr_options.card_fit_lines`, also mirrored in 001; `013_swatch_small.sql` (0.1.120) adds `svr_option_values.swatch_small`, deliberately **not** mirrored in 001 - the ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS is idempotent and runs on fresh installs too; `014_product_gallery_order.sql` (0.1.134) creates `svr_product_gallery`, and `015_card_image_from_variation.sql` (0.1.137) adds its second flag - **both since superseded**: `016_variant_gallery_position.sql` (0.1.153) adds `svr_variants.gallery_position` (mirrored in 001), backfills it from those two flags inside a guarded `DO $$` block, and then DROPs `svr_product_gallery`, so 001 no longer creates it and a fresh install runs create-then-drop rather than carrying a dead table). Cross-module FKs to `shp_products` are safe because shop installs first.

- `svr_options` - `id`, `product_id` FK→shp_products (cascade, the parent), `name`, `control_type` (DROPDOWN\|SWATCH\|PILL\|IMAGE - IMAGE added by `002_image_option_type.sql`, which drops and re-adds the CHECK constraint, and mirrored in 001 for fresh installs), `position`, `requires_previous_option` (BOOLEAN, default false - added by `003_requires_previous_option.sql`, mirrored in 001; when true the storefront holds this option back until **every** option before it by position has a value chosen, not just the one immediately before - see `isOptionVisible`), `source_provider?`/`source_ref?` (TEXT, both added by `004_option_source.sql`, mirrored in 001 - the extension-point provider id that built this option and that provider's own opaque ref for the source; both null on a hand-typed option, set together or not at all), `name_overridden` (BOOLEAN, default false - added by `005_option_name_overridden.sql`, mirrored in 001; true once the owner named the option something other than the source's own name, set on create when the two differ and on every PATCH rename. Suppresses the refresh's `nameDiffers` report, so a deliberately renamed copy is never nagged - which is what makes adding one source to a product twice, under two names, liveable), `card_display` (BOOLEAN, default false), `card_label?` (TEXT), `card_limit?` (INTEGER) - all three added by `006_card_display.sql`, mirrored in 001; the per-option "Display in categories" switch, the heading the product CARD prints instead of `name` (null/blank = use `name`), and how many values a card shows before the "+N" marker (null or <= 0 = all of them). `card_fit_lines?` (INTEGER 1-6, added by `012_card_fit_lines.sql`, mirrored in 001) - the other spelling of that cap: fill exactly N lines of the tile, counted in the browser since only it knows the card's width; wins over `card_limit` when both are set, null = the `card_limit` rule. See the card-summary note below.
- `svr_option_values` - `id`, `option_id` FK (cascade), `label`, `slug` (TEXT NOT NULL, UNIQUE `(option_id, slug)` - added by `008_value_slug.sql` with a slugified+per-option-deduped backfill from `label`, mirrored in 001. **The value's identity within its option**: labels may duplicate ("Black" in two materials, told apart by swatch), slugs may not; the CSV/sheet round-trip writes every Value cell as `(slug)Label` via `lib/value-cell.ts` and resolves slug-first on import. Copies from an option source take the source's slug where free, deduped by `ensureUniqueOptionValueSlug`), `swatch?` (hex colour for SWATCH, image url for IMAGE, null otherwise and for a value nobody has styled yet), `swatch_small?` (TEXT, `013_swatch_small.sql`, 0.1.120 - url of the shrunk copy the storefront's thumbnails/cards prefer; null = fall back to `swatch`. Synced from product-attributes wherever `swatch` is; hand-editing a copy's swatch nulls it, since only a source module makes the files. The 3D module never reads it), `position`, `source_ref?` (TEXT, added by `004_option_source.sql`, mirrored in 001 - the source value this one was copied from, opaque here; null on a hand-added value, which a refresh then never touches. Indexed `(option_id, source_ref)` because a refresh matches on that pair).
- `svr_variants` - `id`, `product_id` FK (parent, cascade), `child_product_id` FK→shp_products (cascade, unique - the hidden child), `enabled`, `show_image_in_gallery` + `show_model_in_gallery` (BOOLEAN, default false, independent of each other - added by `011_variant_show_in_gallery.sql`, mirrored in 001; the grid's two "Show up front" tick boxes. When true this variation's FIRST image (resp. its 3D model) joins the parent's gallery and stays there until a whole combination resolves, dropping out only when the chosen variation's own media takes over (see 2026-08-12). Split rather than one flag: the combination worth leading with in 3D is not always the one with the best photo), **`gallery_position`** (INTEGER NULL, `016_variant_gallery_position.sql` 0.1.153, mirrored in 001 - where a promoted variation's photo sits in the parent's gallery: its index in the FINISHED strip with the parent's own photographs counted in, arranged by dragging its tile in the product editor's Images grid. NULL means "after the parent's own", the starting state and the old fixed behaviour. Read through `lib/gallery-order.ts`, never by index arithmetic at the call site; meaningless while `show_image_in_gallery` is off, and cleared when it goes off), `position`.
- `svr_variant_values` - composite PK (`variant_id` FK cascade, `option_value_id` FK cascade) - which values define a variant.
- `svr_addons` - `id`, `product_id` FK (cascade), `type` (TEXT\|TEXTAREA\|NUMBER\|SELECT\|CHECKBOX\|DATE\|FILE), `label`, `required`, `position`, `config` JSONB (max length, min/max, flat/per-char price, priced choices, file limits).
- `svr_uploads` - `id`, `token` (unique), `media_ref` (public url, used as the line_meta href), `media_provider?`/`media_key?` (for orphan blob cleanup), `filename?`, `size`, `mime_type`, `order_item_id?` (unused link, retained), `ip_hash?`, `created_at`. Not FK'd to order items - orphan cleanup cross-checks `media_ref` against `shp_order_items.line_meta`.
- `svr_settings` - singleton (`id='singleton'`): `max_upload_mb` (10), `allowed_upload_types`, `upload_retention_days` (30), `max_variants` (200).
- `svr_product_gallery` - **GONE as of 0.1.153.** Held `base_images_last` (014, 0.1.134) and `card_image_from_variation` (015, 0.1.137): two tick boxes on the product's Images tab deciding which of two piles led the product page, and which one a grid tile took its picture from. Replaced by **`svr_variants.gallery_position`** (016), which says outright where each promoted variation sits among the parent's own photographs, so there are no piles left to order and both questions are answered by "is a variation holding slot 0?". 016 backfills, then drops the table.

**Permissions**: none of its own - admin writes gate on `shop.products` (via shop's `requireShopUser`), the report on `shop.reports`.

**API Routes** (through `/api/m/shop-variations/…`)

- Admin (`shop.products`): `GET admin/variations` (v0.1.72 - cross-product variations list for the Variations tab on Shop › Products; every variation with its primary image, option-value label, price/SKU/stock and any contributed columns; filters by product, by missing image, by missing SKU (`missing=sku` - `c."sku" IS NULL OR btrim(c."sku") = ''`, alongside the image one in SQL rather than in JS, since both live on the variation's own child product row), by a missing contributed column, or - `missing=lost:image` / `missing=lost:<column id>` - by a **lost file**, one still recorded against the variation whose url no longer resolves; all resolved in `lib/variations-list.ts`, which merges contributed columns by heading through `lib/variation-columns.ts` and checks urls through `lib/lost-files.ts`), `GET admin/products/[id]` (deep-editor payload), `POST admin/products/[id]/options`, `POST admin/products/[id]/generate-matrix`, `POST admin/products/[id]/clear-variants`, `POST admin/products/[id]/delete-variants` (bulk delete a chosen set - `{variantIds: string[]}` → `deleteVariants(parentId, ids)`, each id verified to belong to the parent before its hidden child is deleted; backs the grid's select-all + **Delete selected**), `POST admin/products/[id]/variants` (create one hand-picked combination - `{optionValueIds: string[]}` → `createSingleVariant`; rejects a partial combination or a duplicate value-set, builds a hidden child like the matrix does, then `resequenceVariantPositions` renumbers every row so the new variant lands in the slot a full generate would have given it), `POST admin/products/[id]/addons`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/options/[id]`, `POST admin/options/[id]/values`, `POST admin/options/[id]/refresh` (re-read a sourced option from its provider - additive only, see the option-source point below), `GET admin/option-sources` (every contributed source with its values + a suggested control type, for the picker; empty list when no module contributes one), `PATCH/DELETE admin/option-values/[id]`, `POST admin/products/[id]/resequence-variants` (0.1.61 - renumber a parent's existing variants into matrix order after an option/value drag, and re-compose the child names option order feeds; a renumber, never a regenerate, so ids and their stock/prices/photos/orders are preserved), `PATCH/DELETE admin/variants/[id]` (PATCH edits the child product via shop's `updateProduct`/`setProductMedia` + `enabled`, and as of 0.1.52 carries the **optional price types** as well as `price` - `salePrice`/`retailPrice`/`tradePrice`/`costPrice`, each `.nullable()` so clearing a variant's sale price stays distinct from setting it to zero; the image field is **`imageUrls: string[]`**, not a single url - the whole ordered set is written to `shp_product_media` (index 0 `is_primary`, `position` = index, duplicates dropped) and an empty array clears them; on a non-empty set, calls shop's `reorganiseProductMedia(childProductId, {folderProductId: parentId})` so the variant images file into the parent product's media folder. DELETE removes one variant by deleting its hidden child product, which cascades the `svr_variants` + `svr_variant_values` rows away - the same path `clear-variants` takes per row), `PATCH/DELETE admin/addons/[id]`, `GET/PUT admin/products/[id]/gallery` (0.1.134, reshaped 0.1.153 - GET returns `{images:[{variantId,label,url,altText,position}]}`, one representative picture per variation ticked "Image up front" with its slot in the finished gallery; PUT takes `{images:[{variantId,position,altText}], demoted:[variantId]}`, verifies every id against `getVariants(id)` before writing, unticks the demoted ones and clears their slot, writes each description onto the variation's own first `shp_product_media` row, and returns the reloaded set. GET allows read-only shop access, PUT is a write), `GET admin/export` (CSV), `POST admin/import` (CSV). `GET admin/reports` gates on `shop.reports`.
- Public: `GET public/by-slug/[slug]/variations` (storefront selector payload - options, per-variant price/stock/image, base images, add-ons; looked up by slug so no product-context injection is needed in shop), `POST public/upload` (anonymous, rate-limited, size/type-validated personalisation file upload → core media provider + `svr_uploads` row, returns a token).
- Member: `GET member/gdpr-export` (internal bearer; the member's personalisation from their orders' `line_meta`).
- Cron: `GET/POST cron/cleanup-uploads` (`Bearer $CRON_SECRET`, daily 03:00) - prunes orphaned uploads past the retention window, deleting the blob then the row.

Admin pages (`/cactus-admin/m/shop-variations/…`): `reports` (parent-grouped variant sales), `import` (CSV import/export). A shared `VariationsTabs` sub-nav keeps these two under one Shop-group nav entry, **"Variation tools"** (landing on `import`), renamed from "Product options" in v0.1.72. **The cross-product variations list moved out (v0.1.72) to the Variations tab on Shop › Products** via `shop.products-tabs` (below); the old `products` admin page, its `admin/products` overview route and `VariationsListScreen` are gone. **Extension point consumed: `shop.products-tabs` (v0.1.72)** - `VariationsBrowser` (client, id `variations`, permission `shop.products`) fetches `GET admin/variations` and renders a searchable product filter plus a two-group filter dropdown: **Nothing set** ("Without Image", "Without SKU" (0.1.111), "Without <attribute>"/"Without 3D Files" - each contributed column, for free through the `variant-field-provider` values; the first two are built in, listed in `BUILT_IN_MISSING` in `lib/variations-list.ts` so a non-built-in target is the thing that means "contributed column") and **Broken links** ("Lost Image", "Lost 3D Files" - only the image and the columns whose provider declares `kind: 'file'`, since asking whether an attribute is a broken link is nonsense). No 3D or attribute code lives here. Contributed columns are **merged by heading** server-side (`lib/variation-columns.ts`), so an attribute used across the catalogue is one column and one filter entry rather than one per product. Read-only overview; each row links to its product's Variations tab. **There is no standalone per-product editor** (`products/[productId]` was deleted in v0.1.6): the whole thing is now the **Variations tab** on shop's product editor, contributed via `shop.product-editor-sections` → `ProductVariationsSection` (server wrapper; returns `null` for a `catalogue_hidden` variant child, since a variant of a variant is not a thing) → `VariationsPanel` (client: options builder with inline rename and drag-to-reorder (v0.1.18 - options are draggable cards, values draggable pills within their own option; only a grab handle is `draggable`, so the inline rename/swatch/delete controls keep their click and text-select behaviour, and a value drag is pinned to its option id and never crosses; a drop reassigns `position` on the moved rows through the existing `PATCH admin/options/[id]` / `PATCH admin/option-values/[id]` routes, then refreshes. **"No variant re-sync is needed" was wrong and is fixed in 0.1.61**: the grid *label* is indeed composed live from option order in `getEditorPayload`, but `svr_variants.position` is stored, so a drag left every variant sitting in the running order the old value order implied - visible as a grid whose rows no longer match the options above them, until the next generate. `persistPositions` now fires one `POST admin/products/[id]/resequence-variants` after all the moved rows have landed, which calls `resequenceVariantPositions` + `syncVariantChildNames`. **Once per drag, not once per PATCH**: the row PATCHes go out concurrently, and hanging the resequence off each one would both repeat the work N times and race - every call re-reads the option order to recompute slots, so a slow early one could write its now-stale answer last. Names are re-composed on both drags even though only an *option* reorder can move one (a child is named from its value labels joined in option order), because the sync only writes rows whose name actually differs), matrix generate/rebuild/clear, bulk variant grid, personalisation fields). **The grid carries every price type the shop has switched on** (0.1.52): the panel takes an `enabledPriceTypes` prop, read server-side by `ProductVariationsSection` from shop's `getShopConfigCached()` (rather than a second config fetch of the panel's own), and renders a column per switched-on type - Sale, RRP, Trade, Cost - beside the mandatory Price. The same wrapper reads `weightBasedShippingEnabled` off that config and passes it down (0.1.58): false drops the Weight column and its inputs, matching what shop's own Stock tab does, while per-variant weights already stored are left alone. Emptying one of those boxes writes `null`, not `0`: a blank sale price means "not on offer" and a zero one means free. Two save models on purpose: structural work (add option, generate matrix, add addon) applies immediately because it is an action, while per-variant grid edits are held locally and written by the product editor's single Save via `useProductEditorSave` (dirty rows tint, and only the rows actually written are cleared, so a row edited mid-save survives). Tab badge = variant count. A stale-matrix warning appears when the option combinations no longer match the variant count; because `generateMatrix` only fills the gap (existing rows kept), a big matrix that timed out part-built is resumable, so the action button reads **Continue building options** while the count is short of expected (and the warning says as much, "build a batch at a time, keep pressing Continue"), falling back to **Rebuild from options** when there are more variants than the options now call for. The grid also offers a per-row **Delete** (the DELETE route above) for the odd variant a big matrix throws up that is never actually sold, and its first column (the variant label) is `position: sticky; left: 0` so it stays put while the rest of the grid scrolls sideways. An **Add a single variant** control below the grid (`AddSingleVariant` in `VariationsPanel.tsx`) builds one hand-picked combination - a dropdown per option, each defaulting to its first value - via `POST admin/products/[id]/variants`, for the site owner who wants to grow the list one row at a time rather than generate the whole matrix. Ordering is the point: the server's `resequenceVariantPositions` (`variants-service.ts`) recomputes every variant's `position` as its canonical cartesian index (mixed-radix over the options in display order, the last option moving fastest - the same order `generateMatrix` walks), written back in one bulk `setVariantPositions` statement, so an individually-added variant appears exactly where the full auto-generate would have placed it, not tacked on the end.

**Filtering the variants grid by option (working tree, unreleased).** `VariationsPanel` gained an `optionFilter` state (`Record<optionId, valueId>`, `''`/absent = Any) and a `VariantFilterBar` sub-component rendered above the bulk-controls row - one plain `<select>` per option in option order, values off the same `data.options[].values` rows the storefront renders, so the admin asks the question the shopper's way. Deliberately plain selects regardless of `controlType`: a swatch grid sells a colour, this files one. Three derived memos, no new fetch and no server change (`data.variants[].optionValueIds` was already on the editor payload): `activeFilter` (filter READ through a live-value-id set rather than pruned into state on reload - a retired value stops counting and the select falls back to Any, which avoids a `setState` in an effect), `visibleVariants` (a variant is shown when it carries EVERY chosen value; options on Any ask nothing, so a partial choice narrows rather than matching nothing - the opposite of the storefront's "half a choice is not a product"), and `reachableValues` (per option, the value ids present among variants matching every OTHER option's choice, so the dropdowns narrow each other; the option's own choice is excluded from its own test, and the currently-chosen value is always kept in its list or the select renders blank with no way back to Any). **Scope changes that matter:** the header tick box and `toggleAll` now act on `visibleVariants` (add/remove them from `selected`, leaving off-screen selections alone) and `bulkSet` takes the row list as an argument and is handed `visibleVariants` - a filtered "fill every row" that rewrote all 625 prices would be the expensive kind of surprise. `BulkControls` gained a `scoped` boolean that only changes its wording ("Fill the rows shown:" + matching aria-labels). `Delete all`, `Rebuild from options` and the `matrixStale` warning still count the whole matrix, which is what they are about. `tbody` maps `visibleVariants` with a `colSpan={99}` "nothing matches those choices" row when empty.

**Option control types: DROPDOWN, PILL, SWATCH, IMAGE (v0.1.16).** All four are one column, `svr_options.control_type`, and the two swatch types share one nullable `svr_option_values.swatch` column - a hex colour for SWATCH, an image url for IMAGE. No second column: the column already meant "whatever the control shows beside the label", so IMAGE only needed the CHECK constraint widening (`002_image_option_type.sql`). The API-edge cap on it is `SWATCH_MAX_LENGTH` (`lib/types.ts`, 1000), shared by the three routes that accept a swatch - it was 200, which is roomy for `#ff0000` and too tight for a hosted media url carrying a folder path.
- Admin: `InlineImageSwatch` (`VariationsPanel.tsx`) sits where `InlineSwatch` sits for colours - a 22px thumbnail on the value pill, click to open shop's `MediaPickerModal` (the shared core media library, `GET/POST /api/admin/media`, with its own upload button, so picking a filed image and uploading a new one are the same two clicks). It saves on the pick rather than behind a tick, because unlike the colour control there is no hand-typed hex box to half-finish and therefore no draft to hold.
- A value's picture is set **after** the value exists, not while adding it: `AddValueInline`'s extra field stays colour-only, so the comma-separated "S, M, L" flow still works for an IMAGE option and each value is then given its picture from the dotted placeholder. A value with no picture renders as the bare label on the storefront - the same fallback an uncoloured SWATCH value gets.
- Storefront (`OptionControl` in `VariantParts.tsx`, shared by the granular blocks and the slot path): SWATCH, IMAGE and PILL are all one row of buttons; IMAGE adds a 28px thumbnail and **keeps the label** beside it, because a shopper who can't see the picture would otherwise have nothing to go on.

**Guided configuration (shop-variations, working tree).** The option controls and the buy row read as a numbered sequence with a locked destination, rather than a stack of loose pickers over a live button. Everything below is shared by both storefront hosts (the granular `VariantOptionsPart`/`VariantAddToCartPart` and the slot path's `VariantSlotPurchaseClient`), because the controls are the same components.
- **Numbered option titles.** `OptionControl` takes an optional `index` (1-based) and renders `OptionNumber` before the option's name: an outlined circle while the option is unanswered, filled with `--color-primary` once it has a value. Both hosts number the options **as shown**, not by payload index, so one held back by `requires_previous_option` leaves no gap in the count (`VariantOptionsPart` numbers its already-filtered `visibleOptions`; the slot path maps → filters on `isOptionVisible` → numbers). The accordion layout draws the marker on its own section heading instead, since that heading IS the label there (the control inside runs with `hideLabel`). The label span became `inline-flex` to sit the marker on the name's baseline, with a `display:block` wrapper (`labelRow`) on the stacked path so it still occupies its own line - the `beside` float path is unchanged and still floats the whole span.
- **Price hints under a choice.** `valuePriceRange(payload, selection, optionId, valueId)` and `optionAffectsPrice(payload, selection, optionId)` in `lib/selection-logic.ts` (pure, unit-tested in `lib/selection-logic.pricing.test.ts`, 18 cases) are surfaced on the hook as `sel.valuePrice()` / `sel.optionAffectsPrice()`. Both filter variants **directionally** - buyable, carrying the value, and consistent with the picks ABOVE the option only - exactly as `isValueAvailable` does, so a later pick can never move what an earlier option says it costs. The control prints `from £246` (or the bare figure where the value pins the price exactly) as a second line under the value's label, and only where `optionAffectsPrice` is true: an option whose choices all start from the same figure would otherwise print the same number four times. A dropdown has nowhere for a second line, so the hint rides the `<option>` text as ` - from £246`. `moneyShort` trims a bare `.00` for these hints only.
- **Chosen state.** A picked value keeps its 2px `--color-primary` border and gains a `color-mix(in srgb, var(--color-primary) 16%, var(--color-surface))` wash (tinted, not filled - the label and its second line still have to read, in both schemes), a `ChosenTick` badge overlapping its top-right corner, and `Selected` in place of the price hint. The badge is absolutely positioned, so the button is now `position: relative` and nothing in the row may take `overflow: hidden`. The swatch-only look has deliberately given up its text and gets the tick but no second line.
- **Locked buy button + selection summary.** `sel.canAdd` now spells out `allOptionsChosen` rather than relying on `inStock` implying it (the two agreed, but only by accident of the stock check needing a resolved variant). `sel.missingOptionNames` (display order) feeds `missingOptionsSentence()` → "Choose Width and Storage first", which since **shop-variations 0.1.123** is the buy button's OWN LABEL while it is locked (previously a written note under the row), in both hosts - `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` and the granular `VariantAddToCartPart`. The same string covers "Out of stock" and the add-on `Complete the required fields` reason; the note under the row is gone, the wrapper's tooltip stays. `FitLabel` (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`) keeps a long reason inside a fixed-height pill. **Three things had to be right; 0.1.123 shipped with none of them fully correct, fixed across 0.1.124 and 0.1.127:**
  1. *The host doesn't set the button's own size* (0.1.124). Host span is `width: 0; min-width: 100%` - a nowrap line's min-content width is the WHOLE line, so a plain `width: 100%` host hands the button an intrinsic minimum the length of the sentence and the BUTTON grows instead of the text shrinking (it took the buy row's whole width, wrapped off the end of the quantity stepper, and the measurement then found all the room it wanted and shrank nothing); percentages are ignored in intrinsic sizing, so `width: 0` is what the button sizes against.
  2. *One line, verified rather than trusted* (0.1.127, after being reported live as "trimming the end instead of shrinking"). The one-line size is first ESTIMATED by arithmetic (`room ÷ natural × base`), but glyph widths scale with font-size only approximately - subpixel rounding and hinting - so a trusted estimate could land a fraction too big, and since the label always carries `overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis`, the shortfall never overflowed visibly, it just ate the last word or two under the ellipsis: looked exactly like clipping instead of shrinking, because that is what it was. Now the estimate is a seed only: applied, measured for real (`label.scrollWidth`), crept down 0.5px at a time until the actual box holds the actual text, at or above `SINGLE_LINE_FLOOR` (**13px**) - below that the label drops to a SECOND line instead (measured the same way: seed at `estimate × 1.8`, crept down until the wrapped text fits `room` and `size × 1.15 × 2`, since where a wrap falls is not something arithmetic can predict).
  3. *The floor genuinely holds* (0.1.127, caught by the same test pass). The two-line seed (`estimate × 1.8`) was applied and checked before being clamped to `min` - so an extreme case (four-plus options outstanding on a phone) could settle a hair under the documented 11px floor if that first seed happened to fit outright on the first try. Seed is now `Math.max(min, Math.min(base, ...))` before the first attempt, not just during the step-down.

  Hard floor `min` = **11px** either way. The chosen state is written straight onto the element AND into React state, so a `ResizeObserver` firing between paints never leaves an unfitted measurement on screen for a frame; also re-measured on `document.fonts.ready`, and reset during render when the wording changes. Every measurement starts from the same known state (base size, nowrap) so re-runs can never disagree and the fit cannot oscillate. Proof for both rounds was a standalone Playwright repro of shop's actual `.spd-buy-row`/`.spd-add` CSS: 0.1.124's before/after (button 524px in a 342px column, off the stepper's line → 343px, beside it); 0.1.127's four-sentence/four-width sweep (37-97 characters, 700/560/390/300px) checked for zero clipped width, zero clipped height, and font size never below 11px. The tooltip's `title` sits on a wrapper `<span>` because a disabled control takes no pointer events and so never shows its own; on the slot path that wrapper carries `flex:1` with **no** `min-width`, so shop's `.spd-add` 200px floor still makes the row wrap rather than squeezing the CTA (the granular part, whose button has no such floor, does set `minWidth:0` now that the label no longer sets one of its own). `SelectionSummary` (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`, `role="status"`) prints "Ready to add: 140cm · 2 Drawer Fixed Pedestal · Black" above the row from `sel.chosenSummary`, only once every visible option is answered, on the `--color-success-bg`/`-border`/`--color-success` token trio.
- **"Your choice" pill + reset clears the chosen view.** `YourChoicePill` (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`) sits top-left inside the gallery stage - shop's `.spd-stage` is already `position: relative`, so it is clipped to the same rounded box - whenever every option is answered AND the stage is showing the shopper's own configuration: a contributed stage (their variation's 3D model) or one of the variant's own photographs. A base photo they clicked back to earns no pill. Pressing **Reset options** bumps a new `resetEpoch` counter on the store entry (`resetOptionValues`), surfaced as `sel.resetEpoch`; both galleries watch it and clear the thumbnail override, the tap-zoom and the contributed stage, and put the reset counter in the `<extra.Thumbs>` key so a contributor holding its own memory of the settled variation (`Gallery3dThumbs`' `lastResolved`) is remounted back to the product's own media. A counter, not "nothing is chosen": a page OPENS with nothing chosen and must keep the view it opened on.

**Option summaries on product cards (shop-variations 0.1.88 / shop 0.1.128).** An option ticked **Display in categories** (`svr_options.card_display`) summarises its values on the product CARD wherever cards render - category grids, shop home, related/featured rows. Three moving parts:
- `lib/card-options.ts` - prisma-free: the `CardOptionSummary`/`CardOptionsFacts` types, the `CARD_OPTIONS_FACT_ID = 'variations-card-options'` tag, and the pure `summariseOptionForCard()` (label fallback `card_label?.trim() || name`; `kind` = swatch/image/text from `control_type`, PILL folds into text; `card_limit` null **or <= 0** means no cap; `card_fit_lines` 1-6 sets `fit: N` on the summary instead and ships every value up to `FIT_VALUE_CAP` (120, the most any card could draw; the tail goes in `more`) for the browser-side trim - clamped defensively to 1-6, wins over `card_limit`; `more` = the remainder, 0 when everything fitted; returns null when not ticked or the option has no values). Unit-tested in `lib/card-options.test.ts` (14 cases). **Kept separate from the provider on purpose**: the card block below is registered as an editor component too, so anything it imports at runtime lands in the client bundle, and the provider reaches for prisma.
- `lib/card-options-provider.ts` - registered at shop's **`shop.card-media`** point under id `variations-card-options` (a second entry at the same point alongside `variations-card-media`; the resolver keys providers by entry id, so two are fine). Batched: one `getOptionsWithValuesForProducts` for the whole grid.
- `components/puck/card-variation-options.tsx` - the `ShopCardVariationOptions` Puck block (`layoutTypes: ["shopProductCard"]`, label **Card: Variation options**, `inline: true`, `dragRef` on its own root, no fields). Reads its payload out of `_ctx.facts` by id; inline styles only (no CSS file in this module, and a `<style>` per part would repeat once per card). No `_ctx` = editor canvas = a two-row sample skeleton. Same render fn for the editor and RSC halves, so markup is identical by construction.
- **Placement is the owner's**: nothing shows until they drag the block into the published `shopProductCard` layout. `VariationsPanel` prints a one-off reminder in the Options section the moment any option on the product has `cardDisplay` set.
- Admin: `CardDisplayControls` in `VariationsPanel.tsx` - the tickbox plus a **Label** text box (placeholder = the option name) and a **Swatches shown**/**Options shown** number box (placeholder "All"; the wording follows the control type). Both commit on blur/Enter, not per keystroke (each commit is a PATCH + full refetch). Drafts are seeded from the saved values and **never** synced by an effect - the parent keys the component on `` `${cardLabel}|${cardLimit}` `` so a commit remounts it (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect otherwise fires). Empty box sends `null`, which the PATCH route treats as "clear the override" - a blank `card_label` is stored as null, never as `''`.
- Wire format: `PATCH admin/options/[id]` gained `cardDisplay?: boolean`, `cardLabel?: string|null` (max 80), `cardLimit?: number|null` (int 1-50). All three nullable-optional on purpose: undefined = leave alone, null = clear. `updateOption()`'s whitelist and `mapOption()` extended to match.
- **Not wired**: `product-attributes-for-shop`'s `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx` has its own `renderTaggedCards` and never called `resolveShopCardExtras`, so that surface shows no option summary (and, pre-existing, no variation photos or 3D badge either). Deskwell does not use it - both `/shop` and the category pages go through shop's `renderCards`.

**Dependent options - "reveal in order" (`requires_previous_option`).** Any option from the second onward can be flagged to stay hidden on the storefront until the option immediately before it (by display order) has a value chosen, so a shopper works through them one step at a time. Pure progressive disclosure: it changes nothing about the variant matrix or `resolveVariant`, only which controls are on screen. The gate is one pure helper, `isOptionVisible(payload, selection, index)` (`lib/selection-logic.ts`), surfaced on the hook as `sel.isOptionVisible(index)` and applied in both storefront render paths (`VariantOptionsPart` in `VariantParts.tsx` and `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` in `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx`). It chains: if the option before is itself hidden and unchosen this one stays hidden too, and it is dormant on the first option (nothing before it to wait on), so a flag left on an option later dragged to the front simply does nothing. Admin: a checkbox on each option card from the second onward (`VariationsPanel.tsx`, gated on `oi > 0`), labelled with the previous option's name, saving through `PATCH admin/options/[id]` (`requiresPreviousOption` boolean).

**Pinned mobile gallery (`lib/use-sticky-mobile-gallery.ts`, working tree).** On a stacked (mobile) product page, and only for a product that actually has options, `VariantSlotGalleryClient` pins the gallery under the site header while the shopper scrolls the option pickers: the hook flips the column to `position:fixed` via the `svr-mstick` class (CSS emitted by the client, restyling shop's `spd-*` classes at equal specificity but later in the document - stage at half width, thumbnails beside it as a 2×2 grid whose overflow scrolls vertically; the `spd-thumbs-wrap` collapses to `display:contents` so the same rules land whether the strip arrives wrapped (below) or bare (beside)), while a hidden sibling spacer holds the column's slot in the flow so pinning never jumps the scroll. The options' extent is found through the `svr-options` marker class worn by both option hosts (`VariantSlotPurchaseClient`'s inline area and the granular `VariantOptionsPart`). It releases both ways: scrolled back toward the top the gallery drops back into the flow unchanged; scrolled on past the options' bottom edge it lets go and leaves with them. "Mobile" is detected from geometry (options stacked below the gallery in the same column) rather than a breakpoint, so per-site breakpoint settings are honoured without widening shop's slot contract; the pin's top edge rides shop's live-measured `--spd-header-h`, so shrink-on-scroll headers stay snug. Desktop layouts (options beside the gallery) never match and keep shop's own sticky column.

**Extension point published: `shop-variations.option-source` (v0.1.49, working tree).** Another module offers ready-made options - "here is a Colour list with twelve values" - which the Variations tab turns into a real `svr_options` row. Live consumer: `product-attributes-for-shop` v0.1.9 (`lib/option-source-provider.ts`, `productAttributesOptionSourceProvider`), offering each attribute as a source and each attribute value as a source value.

- **Data-only by design.** A provider contributes no UI at all: `listSources()` / `getSource(ref)` return plain `{ref, name, groupLabel?, values: [{ref, label, swatch}]}`, and shop-variations owns the whole picker (`components/admin/OptionSourcePicker.tsx`). That keeps the word "attribute" out of this module entirely and keeps the provider free of admin-UI code. Contrast `variant-columns`/`variant-field-provider`, which do cross a component over.
- Resolver `lib/option-sources.ts` (`resolveOptionSourceProviders` / `resolveOptionSourceProvider`, same manifest-read + permission-filter + registry-lookup shape as the variant-field resolver), plus `suggestControlType(values)` - all-hex swatches suggest SWATCH, all-non-hex suggest IMAGE, mixed or none falls back to DROPDOWN rather than rendering half a swatch grid as blanks.
- **The browser never supplies the labels.** `POST admin/products/[id]/options` takes `source: {provider, ref, valueRefs[]}` and re-reads the source server-side, so what lands in the DB is what the provider says now; only the option name, control type and the picked refs come from the client. The name is the deliberate override - it starts as the source's name and is the shop owner's from then on.
- **Refresh is additive, never destructive** (`lib/option-refresh.ts`, `POST admin/options/[id]/refresh`). Matching is by `source_ref`, not label, so a renamed source value updates its copy rather than orphaning it. New source values are appended; copies whose source value is gone are **kept and reported as stale**, never deleted, because each option value has real variants (hidden child products with their own price/stock/SKU) hanging off it; hand-added values (`source_ref` null) are always left alone; the option's own name is never overwritten, only reported as differing. Renames that would collide with an existing label on the same option are skipped, matching the rename endpoint's own duplicate refusal. The route re-runs `fileSwatchImage` for any swatch that came across and `syncVariantChildNames` when anything changed, since variant child names are composed from value labels.
- **One source may be added to a product more than once** (v0.1.50, working tree) - a frame colour and a seat colour off one Colour attribute. Nothing keys on `source_ref` per product, so the only constraint is the option-name one, now enforced on **create** as well as rename: `POST admin/products/[id]/options` trims the name and 409s on a case-insensitive duplicate (previously unchecked, so the typed-in path could make the duplicates the importer and the rename endpoint both refuse). The picker takes `existingOptions` (name + source refs) instead of `existingNames`, badges a source that is already on the product with the names it uses, starts the name box **empty** when the source's own name is taken, warns live and disables Add while the typed name clashes. `name_overridden` is set on create when the chosen name differs from the source's and on every PATCH rename, and `refreshOptionFromSource` reports `nameDiffers` only when it is false - otherwise every refresh of a deliberately renamed copy would nag about a name the owner chose.
- **A source is now the only way in** (shop-variations v0.1.55). The typed-in "Add an option" form (name + control type + comma-separated values) is gone from `VariationsPanel`; the tab offers `Add from attributes` alone, so every option on every product traces back to one source row and one colour cannot exist under three spellings across three products. `POST admin/products/[id]/options` still accepts its `{name, controlType, values}` shape - the CSV importer and `lib/csv.ts` build options through the db layer, and the route's manual branch is left as the documented contract - so the gate is the UI, not the route.
- **New values travel back to the source** (shop-variations v0.1.55 + product-attributes-for-shop v0.1.15). `OptionSourceProvider` gains an **optional** `createValue(ref, {label, swatch})` returning the stored `OptionSourceValue`. `POST admin/options/[id]/values` calls it on the hand-typed branch whenever the option is sourced and the provider implements it, then copies the returned `ref`/`label`/`swatch` down - so a value typed on the Variations tab lands on the attribute too and is **sourced from birth**, matching on a later Refresh instead of being an orphan. The source is the authority on what it stored: a reused label comes back with the source's own spelling and swatch. A provider that refuses (source deleted, blank label) is a **hard 400, not a quiet local write** - a local-only row would look saved while the attributes screen silently disagreed. Providers without `createValue` keep the old local-only behaviour. `attributes` implements it with the same reuse-by-label rule its own `reuseExisting` POST body uses, plus `ensureUniqueValueSlug` / `nextValuePosition` / `fileSwatchImage` so a value made this way is indistinguishable from one made on the Attributes screen. `VariationsPanel.addValue` now surfaces the refusal in `optionError` instead of ignoring the response.
- Degrades to a dead end rather than to nothing: no contributing module means an empty `GET admin/option-sources`, and since the typed-in form has gone, the tab now says so in words and points at setting attributes up first, rather than showing a button with nothing behind it. shop-variations still does **not** declare `requiresModules: product-attributes-for-shop` (that would invert the dependency - attributes is the optional companion), so a variations-only install can price and edit existing options but cannot add a new one. Uninstalling the provider later leaves the copied options fully working - they are the product's own rows - and only removes the Refresh and Add affordances.
