**Extension point published: `shop-variations.variant-columns` (v0.1.12)** - another module hangs an extra column on the variants grid, one cell per variant, resolved in `ProductVariationsSection` (manifest read + permission filter + registry lookup, none of which can happen in the browser) and passed to `VariationsPanel` as `columns: VariantColumn[]`. **No live consumer as of the current working tree**: `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s **3D** column used to ride this point, but moved to the dynamic `variant-field-provider` sibling (below) so its 3D files round-trip through the CSV/Google Sheet. The static point stays published for any column that genuinely needs no CSV presence.

- It exists because the alternative broke module isolation: setting a variation's picture and its 3D model are the same errand, but the grid belongs to this module and the model to one this module has never heard of and does not depend on. So the grid learned about *columns*, not about 3D - there is **no 3D code in shop-variations**, and without that module installed there is no such column.
- Contract: a cell gets `productId`, `variantId`, `childProductId` (the knowledge only this module has - a variation IS a hidden child product) and `label`, and owns its own storage, fetching and saving.
- **A contributed cell must be a client component.** `VariationsPanel` is a client island that fetches its own variants, so cells render per row in the browser and only client references survive the crossing - same rule as `shop.gallery-media`'s `Thumbs`/`Stage`.
- Contributed cells **save themselves** and are deliberately not wired into the editor's Save button: this point exists for uploads, and holding a 40 MB file as a pending in-memory edit would be a lie that costs the admin their upload.
- `label`/`order` ride along on the manifest entry (the `shop.product-editor-sections` trick), each with a fallback for manifests written before they existed.

**Extension point published: `shop-variations.variant-field-provider` (v0.1.29)** - the *dynamic* sibling of `variant-columns`. A static variant-column is one manifest entry = one column resolved without knowing the product; a **field provider** returns a set of columns that **depends on the product** (`listColumns(productId)`), so one module can contribute a different number of columns per product - e.g. one per attribute a product uses for its variations. `lib/variant-field-providers.ts` holds the contract + `resolveVariantFieldProviders(user?)` (manifest read + optional permission gate). The provider object is one export carrying: `listColumns`, `getValues(productId, childIds)` (per-child column values, for CSV export), an **optional** `beginImport(productId, childIds)` (v0.1.37 - preload once per parent, returns an opaque ctx), `applyImportedRow(productId, childId, row, ctx?)` (CSV import writes its own columns back, using the preloaded ctx), an **optional** `rowChanged(productId, childId, row, ctx?)` (v0.1.64-to-be, working tree - **read-only** twin of `applyImportedRow`: would applying this row write anything? Must create/update/delete nothing, including the lazily-created rows `applyImportedRow` may make - an attribute value for an unseen label counts as a change without being created. Lets the google-sheet Pull preview count changed provider columns instead of always previewing "0 to update" for them then applying anyway. A provider without it is invisible to the preview, as all were before), and a client `Cell` (the admin grid control, `columnKey` telling it which column it is). `VariantFieldColumn` is `{key, label, order?, kind?}`; **`kind: 'text' | 'file'`** (working tree, default `'text'`) says the value holds file urls rather than a label, which is the only thing that lets the cross-product browser offer its **Lost <column>** filter without knowing what any provider contributes. Note the key is **per product** (attributes key by assignment), so `variations-list.ts` merges contributions by heading before they reach the browser - see `lib/variation-columns.ts`. **Import batching (v0.1.37):** `applyImportedRow` used to be one round-trip *per row* per provider - the last per-row DB ceiling after the v0.5.519 shop/shop-variations batch. `csv.ts` now calls each provider's `beginImport` once per parent (child ids from `upsertCtx.existing`) and threads the returned ctx into every `applyImportedRow`, so provider reads drop from O(rows) to O(parents). Fully back-compatible: a provider with no `beginImport` gets `ctx === undefined` and behaves as before. A variant **created mid-import** is absent from the preload snapshot, so a ctx miss MUST default to empty current state - a brand-new variant still gets its values written (contract spelled out in `variant-field-providers.ts`, covered by each provider's `variant-field-provider.test.ts`). The **same object drives three surfaces**: `ProductVariationsSection` builds dynamic `VariantColumn`s from it for the grid, and `csv.ts` appends the columns to `exportVariationsCsv` (union of labels, after Weight) and feeds every row of `importVariationsCsv` back through `applyImportedRow`. Because the columns live in the CSV, **the Google Sheet sync carries them with no google-sheet code change** (`gridToImportCsv` is generic; the importer round-trips whatever the header names). `upsertVariantForCombination` now returns `childProductId` for the import path. **This module knows nothing of what the columns mean** - no `pat_` reference - exactly the isolation `variant-columns` was built for. Live consumers: `product-attributes-for-shop`'s per-variant attribute columns (its **Use for variations** attributes), and `product-3d-views-for-shop`'s **3D Files** column (a `|`-separated list of the variant's model urls, always offered - any variant can carry a model; attach-by-url on import, `deleteModelCascade` for a url the sheet dropped).

**The variant's own price types ride the CSV (shop-variations' own columns, not a provider).** `exportVariationsCsv` emits **Sale Price, RRP, Trade Price, Cost Price** (constant `PRICE_TYPE_COLUMNS`) straight after **Price**, blank where a variant hasn't set one - the same optional figures the product editor's Pricing tab holds, read off `VariantEditorRow.{salePrice,retailPrice,tradePrice,costPrice}` which already come from the hidden child product. `importVariationsCsv` reads them by header (`optPrice`: present-but-empty clears to null, a number sets it, unparseable → null - Products-import parity) and threads them into `upsertVariantForCombination`'s `fields`; that function's change-detection and update object grew the four, and `getChildProductFields` (the pre-loaded diff source) selects `sale_price`/`retail_price`/`trade_price`/`cost_price` so a re-import diffs them in memory. On the google-sheet side only two touch-points were needed: `FIXED_VARIATION_COLUMNS` lists the four (so a narrowing Push treats them as owned), and `pull-diff.ts`'s `variationRowChanged` compares them (blank = cleared) so the Pull preview counts a changed RRP/trade/cost as an update. No `shp_*`/`svr_*` column was added - the child rows have carried these since shop's `005_price_types.sql`.

**The variant's own image also rides the CSV (shop-variations' own column, not a provider).** `exportVariationsCsv` emits an **Image** column carrying `VariantEditorRow.imageUrls[0]` (the hidden child product's primary media url; the CSV/Sheet carries **one** image per variant, so a variant with several exports only its first, and a changed cell replaces the lot) after Weight and before the provider columns; `importVariationsCsv` reads it (`imageCol`) and writes it via shop's `setProductMedia` + `reorganiseProductMedia(child, {folderProductId: parent})` - the same write `PATCH admin/variants/[id]` makes. Empty cell clears the image; a value failing the `http(s)` `isHttpUrl` guard is pushed to `errors`, not stored; and the whole block is skipped when the sheet carries no Image column, so a sheet made before this column existed never wipes an image. This is what makes the Google Sheet's Variations tab carry variant pictures.

**Puck Blocks** (editor + RSC parity, colour tokens only): composite `ShopVariantPurchase` (layout `shopProduct` - gallery + options + personalisation + live price + variant-aware add-to-cart) and five granular parts on `shopProductDetail` mirroring shop's `ShopDetail*`: `ShopVariantOptions`, `ShopVariantPersonalisation`, `ShopVariantPrice`, `ShopVariantAddToCart`, `ShopVariantGallery`. Each is a server wrapper → a client island; editor render is a labelled skeleton (preview), RSC render is live. Parts share one selection per product keyed by slug (`lib/use-variation-selection.ts`), so they sync when placed independently. `ShopVariantOptions` carries a field **Option name position** (`labelPlacement`, radio, `above` | `beside`, default `above`): `above` is the long-standing stacked look, `beside` puts each option's name on the same row as its choices for a narrow column. It threads block → `VariantOptionsPart` → `OptionControl`; the slot host (`DetailSlotPartsClient`) passes nothing and so keeps `above`, since a slot render has no block props to read. **Choices this combination cannot have** (`unavailable`, radio, `show` | `hide`, default `show`, v0.1.100) governs what becomes of a value the picks above it have ruled out: `show` keeps it in the row struck through and disabled with a line underneath saying where it IS to be had ("available in 160 to 180cm"), `hide` is the older behaviour of dropping it from the row entirely (the current pick and a stranded "ghost" pick always stay either way, so a control never blanks out). The sentence comes from `availableWith` + `availableWithSentence` in `lib/selection-logic.ts`, surfaced on the hook as `sel.availableIn(optionId, valueId)`: `availableWith` names each chosen upstream value that single-handedly rules the target out and, for each, which values of that same option would allow it (held against the upstream picks that are NOT culprits, buyable variants only), flagging whether they are one unbroken run of the option's display order; `availableWithSentence` collapses an unbroken run of 3+ measurements to "160 to 180cm" (shared trailing unit said once, and only where both ends end in a digit - "Oak, Ash or Walnut" is listed out) and otherwise lists them with a final "or". Empty when no single pick is the culprit (a clash needing a combination, or a value nothing buyable carries at all), where the choice just reads "unavailable" - it never invents a reason. Unavailable pills are dashed-bordered and `--color-text-muted` rather than the old `opacity: 0.4`, and the strike-through moved from the button onto the label span alone, or it would have struck out the one line the shopper is meant to read. In the accordion layout a section is collapsible on `option.values.length > 1` when `show` (vs reachable-count > 1 when `hide`), or an option narrowed to one pickable value would hide its "available in …" lines behind a disclosure that refuses to open. Covered by `lib/selection-logic.available.test.ts`. **`beside` is a float, not flex, and cannot become one** (v0.1.44): the name is `float: left` inside a `flow-root` container and the choices stay inline-level, so the first row clears the name and every wrapped row after it runs the full width. Flex was tried twice and is wrong in both directions - as a flex item the choices div is measured at its full unwrapped width when the row breaks its lines and gets pushed below the name entirely (v0.1.43 patched that with `flex: 1 1 0` + `min-width: 0`), and even once it sits beside the name a flex container is a block formatting context, so it is shoved aside by the float whole instead of flowing around it, leaving every wrapped row in a column beside the name with the space beneath the name wasted. Consequences: the choices' `gap` moves onto the buttons as margins (`gap` does nothing to inline layout) with a `-0.5rem` bottom margin on the wrapper swallowing the last row's, buttons get `vertical-align: top` so an image swatch's baseline cannot drag its row about, and containment is `flow-root` rather than `overflow: hidden` because hidden would clip the image swatch's absolutely positioned hover peek. Indicative storefront pricing and the authoritative server pricing use the same pure `computeAddonPricing` (`lib/addon-pricing.ts`), so they can't disagree.

**The page opens with nothing chosen (v0.1.13).** `firstPreselect` is gone from `lib/selection-logic.ts` and neither entry path (`seededEntry`, `ensureLoaded`) seeds a selection: the opening `optionValues` is `{}`, so the price shows the parent's `basePrice`, `resolveVariant` returns null and `canAdd` is false until the shopper picks. Preselecting the first buyable variant meant a combination nobody had chosen sat in the controls looking chosen, and the buy button was live over it. Two consequences worth knowing:
- **"Out of stock" must gate on `allOptionsChosen`, not just `!inStock`** (`VariantPricePart`). `inStock` is `hasOptions ? !!(variant && enabled && inStock) : true`, and with nothing chosen there is no variant - so the unguarded check labelled *every* options product sold out on load. The purchase parts were already safe: their `reason` chain tests `!allOptionsChosen` first and says "Choose your options".
- **`ResetOptionsLink`** (exported from `VariantParts.tsx`) renders after the last option in **both** hosts - the granular `VariantOptionsPart` and the slot path's `VariantSlotPurchaseClient` - and calls `resetOptions()` → `resetOptionValues(slug)`, clearing `optionValues` only. Personalisation (`addonValues`) survives on purpose: it's typing, not a click. It renders only when `anyOptionChosen`, which is also why RSC and hydration agree - a server render never has a selection, so neither emits the link.

- **The RSC halves live in their own files (v0.1.7): `components/puck/variant-parts.rsc.tsx` and `ShopVariantPurchase.rsc.tsx`, pointed at by the manifest's `rscImport`** (same split, same reason, as shop's `ShopProductDetail.rsc.tsx`). They resolve the selector payload server-side via `lib/variation-bootstrap.ts` and pass it to the island as `initial`, so the option controls are in the page's first HTML. Before this the RSC halves were pass-throughs that rendered nothing but the editor's skeleton, and every island waited for hydration → read the slug off `window.location` → `GET public/by-slug/[slug]/variations` + `GET /api/m/shop/public/config`, which is why the options arrived a beat after the rest of the page.
- **`lib/variation-bootstrap.ts` (server-only, pulls prisma - never import from a `'use client'` file).** `getVariationBootstrap(slug)` is React-`cache`d, so all six blocks share one query per request; it returns the payload plus shop's currency symbol (killing the second fetch). Puck's `<Render>` gives a block only its own saved props and shop injects context into its own part types alone (`inject-part-context.ts`), so there is no prop carrying the slug - instead `rememberProductSlug` records it into a `cache()`-scoped, therefore per-request, slot from the detail-parts provider's `claimsProduct`, which shop calls once per product page before any block renders. `currentProductSlug()`/`bootstrapForCurrentProduct()` read it back. A null is survivable, not fatal: the island falls back to the old fetch-after-mount path (the composite block on a bare `shopProduct` layout, say).
- **The selection store must not be written during a server render.** Module state is per-tab in the browser but per-process on the server, outliving the request: an entry seeded into `store` server-side would sit there marked loaded and hand the *next* shopper of that product whatever price and stock that render happened to see, until the instance recycled. So `useVariationSelection` builds a throwaway entry from `initial` when `typeof window === 'undefined'` and touches no module state; the browser seeds the shared store as normal (first seed per slug wins, so a re-render can't discard a live selection). The currency symbol rides on the entry rather than the module-level `let` for the same reason - otherwise a server render prints the `£` default and hydrates into the real symbol.

**Extension points provided**: `shop.product-editor-sections` → `ProductVariationsSection` (component); `shop.product-editor-media-sections` → `ProductGalleryOrderSection` (0.1.134, component - the "Show these images after the variation images" and (0.1.137) "Use the variation image on category pages" tick boxes at the foot of shop's own Images tab; returns null for a variant child or a product with no options, and its client half `GalleryOrderPanel` registers with the editor's Save button through `useProductEditorSave`, so the unsaved dot lands on **Images**); `shop.cart-line-resolver` → `resolveVariationLineMeta` (server function; maps a variant child back to its parent, loads the parent's add-ons, re-resolves file tokens from `svr_uploads` server-authoritatively, prices via `computeAddonPricing`, and returns a `displayTitle` - base name + chosen options, split by stripping the authoritative parent-name prefix in `lib/variant-title-cache.ts` (request-scoped batch, warmed by `prefetchVariationLineMeta`) - so the cart renders a variant's name and its options on separate lines); and `shop.product-detail-parts` → `shopVariationsDetailParts` (`lib/detail-parts-provider.ts`, an object, id `variations-detail-parts`) - **this is what makes shop's default Product Detail layout handle options with no layout editing**. `claimsProduct` runs server-side once per product page and returns true when the product has options or add-ons and is not itself a `catalogue_hidden` variant child; shop then renders this module's `Gallery`/`Price`/`PurchaseArea` in place of its own `ShopDetailGallery`/`ShopDetailPrice`/`ShopDetailAddToCart`. Those slot components are distinct from the granular Puck blocks below: they render into shop's own `.spd-*` class names (handed down as props) and from shop's server-loaded images/price, so the swap is invisible and paints on first byte. As of v0.1.7 they are split like the Puck blocks: `components/public/DetailSlotParts.tsx` holds **async server** halves that await `getVariationBootstrap(props.slug)` (shop hands the slug down on every slot prop, so no request-scoped lookup is needed here) and pass it to the islands in `DetailSlotPartsClient.tsx` as `initial`. Awaiting is within shop's contract - it types the slots as plain components but only ever renders them from its own RSC halves (`ShopDetail*Rsc`). `OptionControl`/`AddonControl` are shared with `VariantParts.tsx` so the hand-placed blocks and the automatic slot render the identical control. Unclaimed products, and shop-only sites, are untouched. **Also consumes `shop.product-page-resolver`** (id `variations-deep-link`, `lib/product-page-resolver.ts` `shopVariationsProductPageResolver`) - resolves a hidden variant child's own URL (the cart's product link) to its parent so the deep link opens the parent page with that combination pre-selected. `resolveVariantDeepLink` (`variants-service.ts`) does the child→parent + option-value-ids lookup (`getVariantByChildProductId` + `getVariantValueMap`); the resolver records the ids via `rememberPreselectOptionValues` (`variation-bootstrap.ts`, a second request-scoped `cache()` slot beside the product slug), which `getVariationBootstrap` surfaces as `VariationBootstrap.preselectOptionValueIds` (filtered to values the payload holds) and `use-variation-selection`'s `seededEntry` seeds as the opening `optionValues`. Because the page renders under the parent's slug (shop injects it) and every part reads that slug from its explicit prop, all three storefront paths key the selection store by the parent slug on server AND client, so the preselect hydrates with no slug mismatch - `window.location` (the child slug) is never consulted. **Also provides `shop.card-media`** (id `variations-card-media`, `lib/card-media-provider.ts` `shopVariationsCardMedia`, working tree) - one representative photo per enabled variation (its primary, else first still image), batched across the grid and folded into the product card's arrow carousel; images only, no overlay.
  - **`coveredSlots(blockTypes)` - not claiming a job the layout already does by hand.** The point assumed shop's part was the only thing doing each job. Layouts written before it existed do the same job with this module's granular blocks (Deskwell's product page carries `ShopVariantPrice` and `ShopVariantOptions` beside shop's `ShopDetailPrice`/`ShopDetailAddToCart`), so taking the slot as well rendered the price and the option picker twice. Shop now passes every block type in the layout (`collectLayoutBlockTypes`, walks `content` **and** `zones` - the default Product Detail keeps its parts in a Split's zones) and this module returns the covered slots: `ShopVariantGallery`→Gallery, `ShopVariantPrice`→Price, `ShopVariantAddToCart`→PurchaseArea. Shop then renders **nothing** for those (`ctx.slot.covered`), rather than falling back to its own part - a static parent price beside a live variant price is two different figures for one product. Only applies to claimed products; an unclaimed one never consults `covered`, so shop's parts render normally.
  - **A replaced part inherits none of shop's behaviour, only its classes (v0.1.9).** Shop's `imageZoomOnHover` setting (shop settings > General) reached `VariantSlotGalleryClient` as the optional `zoom` prop from shop 0.1.40 and was simply ignored, so the shop-wide zoom silently did nothing on exactly the products this module claims - anything with options. The island now implements it: pointer-tracked `transformOrigin` + `transform: scale(2.5)` on the stage image, mouse magnifying on hover, touch on tap-drag-tap, reset when the variant image or thumbnail pick changes. Shop's behaviour is **reimplemented, not imported** - its copy lives inside `ProductGallery`, which knows nothing of variant images, and the `zoomable`/`zoomed` modifier classes behind it are shop CSS the `classNames` contract does not hand over; the two declarations they carry (cursor, and `touch-action` while magnified) go on inline instead, keeping the fix inside this module. The scale constant is duplicated deliberately and must stay level with shop's, or one setting means two things depending on the product. Generalises: any future prop shop adds to a slot is inert until a provider reads it, and nothing fails loudly when it doesn't.
  - Options and personalisation have no shop part to replace, so they can't be handled that way: they ride inside `VariantSlotPurchase`, which drops them itself when `layoutBlockTypes` (on every slot prop) shows `ShopVariantOptions`/`ShopVariantPersonalisation` already placed. Shop only ever passes block-type strings it attaches no meaning to; this module is the only side that knows what they mean. Resolution is split - `resolveShopDetailProvider(product)` (the claim, still parallel with the template fetch) then the pure `narrowShopDetailSlot(provider, blockTypes)` once the template's blocks are known.

**Cron Jobs**: `0 3 * * *` → `cron/cleanup-uploads`.

**Known Limitations**: a layout that *hand-places* a granular `ShopVariant*` block next to shop's equivalent (`ShopVariantPrice` beside `ShopDetailPrice`, etc.) now double-renders on a claimed product, because shop's own part is variant-aware via the slot as of shop 0.1.35 - the two can't see each other (the slot is per-product, the blocks are per-layout, and shop knowing about `ShopVariant*` types is exactly the coupling the point exists to avoid). Stock layouts are unaffected (they contain shop's parts only); the fix for a hand-built one is to drop the now-redundant `ShopVariant*` block. Also: a variant's image set can only be cleared wholesale (the × drops all of them) - there is no per-image remove in the grid cell; `svr_settings` has no admin UI (defaults only) in v1; CSV import requires the parent product to exist by slug (creates options + child variants, not parents); deleting a parent product leaves its hidden children orphaned (retention cleanup covers uploads; child-product cleanup on parent delete / uninstall is a documented follow-up); a hidden child 404s on its own URL rather than redirecting to its parent.

### Product Attributes for Shop

- Slug: `product-attributes-for-shop` (table prefix `pat_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/product-attributes-for-shop`, manifest version 0.1.39 in the working tree (registry pin v0.1.17). `requiresModules: shop >= 0.1.65` (raised in 0.1.6 for `MediaPickerModal`'s `resolveInitialFolderId`), `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.493` (raised in 0.1.6 for `core.media-reference-rewriters` + `moveOrRenameMedia`). Reuses shop's `shop.products` permission (declares none of its own) and joins the existing **Shop** admin nav group with one entry ("Product attributes").
- Adds shop-wide **filterable attributes** (Material, Colour, Room) with values. Each product carries a **set** of them (`pat_product_attributes`, v0.1.3): tick values for ordinary attributes, or flag one **Use for variations** to set its value per variant (a column on the Variations tab) and **Show in shop filters** off to keep it internal to that product. A storefront Puck block filters the catalogue by them. shop-variations is an **optional** companion, not a `requiresModules` entry: every `svr_` read goes through `lib/variations-bridge.ts` as raw SQL guarded by a `to_regclass` probe (30s cache, `resetVariationsProbeCache()` test seam), because `@/modules/shop-variations/...` does not resolve on an install without it and a static import would break that build. It also registers a **field provider** on shop-variations' `variant-field-provider` point (see below), likewise inert without shop-variations.

**Database**
Table prefix: `pat_` (6 tables). Full DDL in `modules/product-attributes-for-shop/migrations/001_initial.sql` (idempotent); later per-change files numbered (`002_product_attribute_sets.sql` adds `pat_product_attributes`; `003_image_control_type.sql` widens the control-type CHECK - no new column; `004_attribute_groups.sql` adds `pat_attribute_groups` + `pat_attributes.group_id`; `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql` swaps both composite PKs for surrogate ids, adds `pat_product_attributes.name_override`/`position` and `pat_product_values.assignment_id`, and backfills each existing product-level tick onto the one helping it can have come from; `006_variation_columns_per_helping.sql` adds **no DDL at all** - it stamps `assignment_id` onto the per-variant rows 005 deliberately left NULL, so a variations column can belong to a helping rather than to an attribute; `007_swatch_size.sql` adds `pat_attribute_values.swatch_size`; `009_repoint_renamed_option_values.sql` adds **no DDL** - it is a data repair that re-points `svr_option_values.source_ref` onto the attribute value its label actually names, for copies a sheet rename left linked to their old value; `010_swatch_small.sql` (0.1.45) adds `pat_attribute_values.swatch_small`, not mirrored in 001 - idempotent, runs on fresh installs too. 001/002 are **not** mirrored for these - both are idempotent and run on a fresh install too, so the end state is the same either way. 006 skips itself via `to_regclass('public.svr_variants')` when shop-variations is absent). Cross-module FKs to `shp_products` are safe because shop installs first.

- `pat_attribute_groups` (v0.1.7) - `id`, `name`, `slug` (unique), `position`, `created_at`. Admin-side folders only; nothing public reads them.
- `pat_attributes` - `id`, `name`, `slug` (unique; the storefront filter's query key), `control_type` (CHECKBOX\|SWATCH\|DROPDOWN\|IMAGE - IMAGE added 0.1.6), `position`, `show_in_filters` (shop-wide gate), `group_id?` FK → `pat_attribute_groups` **ON DELETE SET NULL** (v0.1.7 - deleting a folder must tip its attributes back onto the ungrouped pile, never cascade them and every product assignment away), `source_option_name?` (the shop-variations option name it was imported from, so a re-import updates rather than duplicates), `created_at`.
- `pat_attribute_values` - `id`, `attribute_id` FK (cascade), `label`, `slug` (unique per attribute), `swatch?` (**one column, two mediums as of 0.1.6**: a hex colour for a SWATCH attribute, a media url for an IMAGE one - same arrangement as `svr_option_values.swatch`), `swatch_small?` (TEXT, **`010_swatch_small.sql`, v0.1.45** - url of the shrunk webp copy made by `lib/swatch-small.ts`; null = no small copy, renderers fall back to `swatch`. Made on upload/edit and by the `generate-small-swatches` backfill; moved with its original by `fileSwatchImage`; never a hex colour), `swatch_size?` (**`007_swatch_size.sql`, v0.1.14** - the real-world size of the picture swatch, free text as typed: "20cm", "200mm", "0.2m" or a bare number; NULL/empty means "not given", which every value written before 007 is, so nothing may read a missing size as an error), `position`.
- `pat_product_values` - `id` PK (surrogate, added by `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql`; was a composite PK on `(product_id, value_id)`), `product_id` FK→shp_products cascade, `value_id` FK cascade, `assignment_id?` FK→`pat_product_attributes` cascade, UNIQUE **NULLS NOT DISTINCT** `(product_id, value_id, assignment_id)`. `product_id` covers **both** parent products and shop-variations' hidden variant children - that is what makes per-variant attributes work with no second table. `assignment_id` says which *helping* of an attribute a tick belongs to. Since `006_variation_columns_per_helping.sql` that includes rows on a **variant child** (they carried NULL under 005, when one attribute meant one column and the row needed no further identity) - it is the only thing telling "Oak on the main finish" from "Oak on the edge", which are otherwise the same product, value and attribute. Still **nullable**: a row whose parent no longer uses that attribute for variations, or one written before 005, has no helping to name. The `NULLS NOT DISTINCT` clause keeps those de-duplicating properly.
- `pat_product_attributes` (v0.1.3) - `id` PK (surrogate, added by `005_repeatable_product_attributes.sql`; was a composite PK on `(product_id, attribute_id)`), `product_id` FK→shp_products cascade, `attribute_id` FK cascade, `name_override?` (TEXT, 005 - the name this helping goes by; NULL means "call it whatever the attribute is called"), `position` (INTEGER, 005), `use_for_variations` (bool, default false), `show_in_filters` (bool, default true - **per-product** filter gate, narrower than `pat_attributes.show_in_filters`; both apply), UNIQUE **NULLS NOT DISTINCT** `(product_id, attribute_id, name_override)`. The product's attribute "set" plus its per-helping flags. **A product may hold the same attribute several times** (005) - "Top material" and "Frame material" both off Material - with all but one carrying a `name_override`; the unique constraint is what enforces that, and the editor + PUT both state it in words first so the constraint is never what the owner meets. Membership is *not* a filter gate on its own - an assigned value still filters unless hidden here, and `getEffectiveValueIdsByProduct` only counts an attribute hidden when **every** helping of it on that product is (`HAVING bool_or(show_in_filters) = false`).
- `pat_settings` - singleton (`id='singleton'`): `hide_empty_values` (true), `include_variant_values` (true).

**A picture swatch carries its own real-world size (working tree, v0.1.14, unreleased)**: `007_swatch_size.sql` adds `pat_attribute_values.swatch_size` (nullable TEXT), surfaced as `PatAttributeValue.swatchSize` and validated at `SWATCH_SIZE_MAX_LENGTH` (40) in `lib/types.ts` - a length cap only, since the units are the reader's problem, not the store's. Set on the **Attributes** screen and, crucially, **editable afterwards**: an IMAGE attribute's add-value row gains a "Size, e.g. 20cm" box, and every existing value chip gains a small size button (shows the size, or "size?" when unset) that prompts for a new one and clears on blank - the figure usually arrives from the supplier after the photograph does, and deleting the value to re-add it with a size would drop every product ticked against it. Routes: `POST /attributes/[id]/values` and `PATCH /values/[id]` both take an optional `swatchSize`, normalising `''` to NULL so a cleared box and a never-filled one are one thing downstream; `createAttributeValue`/`updateAttributeValue` carry it (`!== undefined` guard on the update, so an explicit null clears). Column is deliberately **not** constrained to IMAGE attributes - an attribute can be switched between control types and losing the size on the way through would be a data-loss trap, the same reasoning `swatch` already follows. Not imported from shop-variations (no such field there) and not propagated to `svr_option_values` by `syncSourcedOptionValues` - the size is this module's fact about its own picture. Consumed by product-3d-views-for-shop's material configurator (see below).

**Permissions**: none of its own - all reads/writes gate on `shop.products` via shop's `requireShopUser` (GETs pass `allowAccess: true`).

**API Routes** (through `/api/m/product-attributes-for-shop/…`, all admin, all `shop.products`)

- `GET/POST admin/attributes`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/attributes/[id]` (rename re-slugs; case-insensitive duplicate name **within the same group** → 409 - see Attribute groups), `POST admin/attributes/[id]/values`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/values/[id]`. The values POST takes an optional `reuseExisting: true` (v0.1.5) that turns the duplicate-label 409 into "return the value that already has that label" - set by the two in-context add boxes on the product editor, left off by the attributes screen so a duplicate typed *there* is still reported as the mistake it is. Either way the response now carries the whole value row (`{ id, slug, value, reused }`), so a client can splice it into its list without a refetch. Both the values POST and the value PATCH validate `swatch` through `isValidSwatch` (hex **or** picture url, `SWATCH_MAX_LENGTH` 1000) rather than the old hex-only regex, and file a picked picture via `fileSwatchImage` before responding - filing can rewrite the url, so both re-read the row and hand back the **stored** url (`value.swatch` / `{ ok, swatch }`) instead of echoing what was sent.
- `POST admin/attributes/[id]/values/reorder` (v0.1.17) - whole-list drag reorder for one attribute's values; also pushes the order into any variation option copied from the attribute and renumbers the variants already generated from it. See "Value ordering" below.
- `POST admin/attributes/reorder`, `POST admin/groups/reorder` (v0.1.7) - take `{ ids: string[] }`, the **whole** running order, and write `position = index` in one transaction (`setAttributePositions` / `setAttributeGroupPositions`). Whole-list rather than "move this one up" because `position` is not unique-enforced, so two rows on the same number would make a swap a silent no-op; restating every row repairs the order as a side effect. A list with duplicates is 400; one that does not exactly match the ids on record is **409** ("reload the page") - a partial list would renumber the named rows to 0..n and leave everything else on its old number, shuffling rows nobody touched. Static-vs-dynamic precedence is safe: `scripts/generate-module-router.mjs` sorts static segments above `[param]` ones, so `attributes/reorder` cannot be swallowed by `attributes/[id]`.
- `GET/POST admin/groups`, `PATCH/DELETE admin/groups/[id]` (v0.1.7) - the attribute folders. POST/PATCH slugify and refuse a case-insensitive duplicate name with 409, same shape as attributes. PATCH on a rename and DELETE both **re-file the picture swatches** of every attribute involved (the group name is a folder segment); DELETE reads the membership *before* dropping the row, because the FK nulls `group_id` on the way out and there would be nothing left to walk. `PATCH admin/attributes/[id]` gains `groupId` (`string | null`, `null` meaning ungrouped - the zod field is `.nullable().optional()` so "take it out" and "leave it alone" stay distinct), 404s an unknown group, and re-files that attribute's pictures afterwards; `POST admin/attributes` takes the same optional `groupId` to create straight into a folder.
- `GET/POST admin/attributes/[id]/media-folder` (v0.1.6) - where the picture picker opens (GET, look-only, creates nothing) and where an upload should be filed (POST, creates). Same two-verb split, same reasoning, as shop's `products/[id]/media-folder`.
- `POST admin/refile-swatches` (working tree, unreleased) - walks every attribute and runs `refileAttributeSwatches`, moving each picture swatch (and, 0.1.45, its small rendition) into its `Shop/Attributes/[group]/<attribute>` folder. Idempotent (already-filed pictures are no-ops). Surfaced as a **Tidy picture folders** button on the attributes screen. Exists to repair pictures that older shop-variations builds dragged into product `colours` folders (see the swatch-filing invariant below).
- `POST admin/generate-small-swatches` (0.1.45) - cursor-batched backfill (`{limit ≤25, default 8; afterId}` → `{made, skipped, lastId, remaining, done}`) that makes the small rendition for every picture swatch still without one (`generateSmallSwatch`), reusing a sibling value's small when two values share one picture, and syncing each result to the svr copies. Batched for the 60s module-route ceiling; a value that yields nothing (external host, already tiny) is skipped and the cursor moves, so the loop always ends. Surfaced as **Make small copies** on the attributes screen, which loops it to done with a running narration.
- `GET/PUT admin/products/[id]/assignments` - one round trip returning the vocabulary + this product's `own` assignments + its **set** (`membership`) + its variants. `assignments.own` is a **`Record<assignmentId, valueId[]>`**, not a flat list: two helpings of one attribute hold separate ticks, including the same value ticked under both. PUT takes `{membership}` alone - each entry is `{id?, attributeId, nameOverride?, useForVariations, showInFilters, values[]}`, so the set and its ticks are submitted together and an existing helping keeps its id (recreating it would cascade its ticks away mid-save). It 409s on two helpings of one attribute sharing a name. It **no longer** refuses a repeated attribute that is also marked use-for-variations (**v0.1.13**): the Variations column is now per helping, so a product can raise Finish as both a "Main finish" and an "Edge finish" column, and the name rule is the only thing needed to keep the two (and their CSV headers) apart. It still **clears assignments for any attribute dropped from the set** - only genuinely gone attributes count, not one that merely lost a second helping - and **strips a use-for-variations attribute's value off the parent** (that value belongs per variant, not to the product).

**A variations column belongs to a helping, not an attribute (v0.1.13)** - `listVariationColumns` groups by `pat_product_attributes.id` (heading = `COALESCE(NULLIF(TRIM(name_override),''), a.name)`, ordered by `ppa.position`), `getVariantAttributeValues` joins `pat_product_values.assignment_id`, and `setVariantAttributeValue(childProductId, assignmentId, valueId)` scopes its clear-out to the assignment. That last one is the whole fix: scoped to the attribute, as it was, saving the edge finish deleted the main finish on the same variant. The field provider's `VariantFieldColumn.key` is therefore the assignment id, `PatVariationColumn` carries both `assignmentId` and `attributeId` (values and any newly-typed one still belong to the attribute, so `addLocalColumnValue` and `ensureAttributeValueByLabel` stay attribute-keyed - a finish typed into the edge column is offered by the main one too), and `variation-attributes` returns both ids per column. `importVariationOptions` files its per-variant links against the assignment `upsertProductAttribute` now returns. Covered by `lib/variant-field-provider.test.ts`, whose fixture is deliberately one attribute standing up as two columns.
- `GET admin/products/[id]/variation-attributes` (v0.1.3) - the use-for-variations columns (with their selectable values) + each variant's current value, keyed child→attribute; feeds the Variations-tab cells in one fetch.
- `POST admin/products/[id]/variant-attribute-value` (v0.1.3; body takes `assignmentId` not `attributeId` since **v0.1.13**) - sets (or clears) one variant's value for one use-for-variations **helping**; single-select per (variant, helping). Every id checked against the product: variant belongs to it, the helping is used-for-variations **on this product** (which is also what stops a crafted request writing against someone else's helping), value belongs to that helping's attribute.
- `POST admin/products/[id]/import-variations` - turns the product's `svr_options`/`svr_option_values` into attributes (matched by option **name**, so two products' "Colour" feed one shop-wide filter), attaches values to the variant children carrying them, and (v0.1.3) adds each to the set marked **use-for-variations** so it shows as a column. Idempotent: clears prior imported assignments for the touched attributes first. 409 when shop-variations is absent or the product has no options.

Admin pages (`/cactus-admin/m/product-attributes-for-shop/…`): `attributes` (define the vocabulary + values). The per-product `ProductAttributesSection` is the **Attributes tab** on shop's product editor via `shop.product-editor-sections` (server wrapper → `ProductAttributesEditor` client island, **redesigned v0.1.3**: add attributes to the product's set, per-attribute **Use for variations** / **Show in shop filters** tick-boxes, value ticks for ordinary attributes, "Copy from variations"; the old collapsible per-variant tick-grid is gone - per-variant values live on the Variations-tab column). It has **no save button of its own**: it registers with the product editor's single Save through `useProductEditorSave`, diffing set + ticks against a baseline. Tab badge = count of attributes in the set. The Variations-tab column is a **client cell** (`ProductAttributesVariantCell.tsx`) fed by a server field provider (`lib/variant-field-provider.ts`) and its own `lib/db/membership.ts`; fifty variants share one `variation-attributes` fetch via a module-scoped store and each cell saves itself on change (`variant-attribute-value`), not through the grid's Save.

**Values added in context (v0.1.5)** - a value no longer has to be created on the attributes screen first. `ProductAttributesEditor` renders an `AddValueBox` under every attribute in the product's set (label + a colour input when `controlType === 'SWATCH'`, `preventDefault` on Enter so the product editor's form does not submit); the variant cell's dropdown gains a `+ New value…` option (sentinel `__new__`, safe against value ids because those are uuids) that swaps the `<select>` for an input, Escape cancelling. Both POST `attributes/[id]/values` with `reuseExisting: true` and splice the returned row into local state - the editor into `data.attributes[].values` (and ticks it in `own` unless the attribute is use-for-variations, where the value belongs to a variant), the cell into the shared store's `columns` via `addLocalColumnValue` so every row in the grid offers it at once, then saves the assignment through the usual `variant-attribute-value` POST. **The value itself is written immediately, not deferred to the product's Save**: it is a change to the shop-wide vocabulary, not to this product, and the deliberate choice is that a value stays global rather than being scoped per product - a private "Oak" per product would give the storefront filter one option per product carrying it. The cost is that abandoning a product edit leaves the value behind (documented on the wiki page).

**Picture swatches (IMAGE control type, v0.1.6)** - a fourth control type whose values are offered as picture tiles. No new column: the value's one visual lives in `swatch` either way, and `lib/types.ts` gains `SWATCH_MAX_LENGTH` (1000) plus `isHexSwatch` / `isImageSwatch` / `isValidSwatch`. `isImageSwatch` accepts `http(s)://…` and site-relative `/…` **only** - it is the sole guard between the API and an `<img src>`, so `javascript:`/`data:` are refused. `isValidSwatch` deliberately accepts *either* medium regardless of the attribute's current control type, so switching an attribute from colours to pictures and back is a change of mind rather than a data-loss trap; each render site picks what it can show and falls back (an image-typed value holding a hex renders the empty tile, label intact).

**Swatch-filing invariant (working tree, unreleased)** - a sourced variation value's picture belongs to the attribute, never the product. Three co-ordinated changes: (1) shop-variations' `fileSwatchImage` now no-ops when the value carries a `source_ref` (it used to move the shared attribute picture into the product's `colours` folder, rewriting the url under the attribute and every other copy); (2) product-attributes' `fileSwatchImage` calls `syncSourcedOptionValues(valueId, { swatch })` after a move that rewrites the url, so `svr_option_values` copies follow it; (3) the option-source provider's `listSources` now returns attributes in attributes-screen order (each group's attributes together, ungrouped last) - the picker draws one heading per consecutive run, so the old flat position order repeated a group's heading once per run (the "three Dynamic groups" bug), and shop-variations' `groupSources` additionally merges any repeated non-null heading into its first section as a belt-and-braces guard.

**The Specification tab follows the chosen variation (working tree, v0.1.39, unreleased)** - this module's `shop.product-detail-spec` provider (`lib/detail-spec-provider.ts`: `load` = `getProductSpecView`, `Panel` = `components/public/SpecificationPanel.tsx`) now serves a per-variation payload, and the panel swaps rows as the shopper picks options.

- **Server (`lib/db/spec-view.ts`)**: the per-variant query dropped its `use_for_variations = true` filter - **every** `show_in_spec` helping's child-product values are read now. The two flags answer different questions ("is this a dropdown on the page" vs "does this differ between the things in the dropdown"), and a chair's seat height is the second without being the first, so the chair-spec import files per-variant values against ordinary helpings. It also selects `sv.child_product_id` instead of `GROUP BY`-ing to distinct labels, ordered by `sv.position, sv.created_at`, because the panel needs to know *which* variation holds which value. Still guarded on `hasVariationsTables()`; enabled variants only.
- **Payload** (`PatProductSpecView`) gains `parentProductId` (so the panel can ignore another product's broadcast) and `variantIds?: string[]` listed **once**, with each varying row carrying `perVariant?: (string|null)[]` **positionally aligned** to it. Deliberately not a `Record<uuid, string>` per row: the biggest Deskwell listing runs to 536 variations across several varying rows, and repeating the uuid per row would dwarf the page. `variantIds` is omitted entirely when no row varies. Variation ids are collected from the value rows themselves, so a variation with no spec values is absent from the list and simply falls back to the range text.
- **Row resolution**: a variation with no value of its own falls back to the parent's own ticks; **null means the line does not apply** to that variation (a bespoke-only range on a stock chair, arm dimensions on an armless one) and the panel drops the whole row, rather than printing a blank. A row whose value is identical on every variation collapses to a plain row (no `perVariant`), so a "3 Years" guarantee is never badged as a choice it never was.
- **`lib/spec-format.ts`** (pure, unit-tested in `spec-format.test.ts`, 12 cases) holds `summariseSpecValues` / `distinctSpecValues` - what a varying row says before a selection. Three shapes in order of preference: all values measurements sharing one unit → the span by outer extremes ("44-56cm" + "89.5-99.5cm" → `44cm - 99.5cm`); ≤ 6 distinct → joined with `, ` (the pre-0.1.39 behaviour); more → `"N choices - select your options to see yours"` (one listing's Finish row has 92 distinct values, where a list is a wall, not a spec).
- **Client**: `SpecificationPanel` reads `window.__cactusVariantSelection` and listens for the `cactus-shop-variant-selection` CustomEvent, both **duplicated as local literals** - it must not import from `@/modules/shop-variations/...` (that path does not resolve without the module and a static import would break the build). Events whose `parentProductId` names a different product are ignored. The selection is applied **post-mount only**, so the first render equals the server's range text and hydration cannot mismatch - the SSR HTML remains the complete, crawlable specification. A "Your choice" pill (solid `--color-primary` / `--color-on-primary`, check icon - a deliberate literal copy of shop-variations' `YourChoicePill` so the spec table and gallery stage wear the same badge; copied not imported, same reason as the event) leads the table once a full combination is picked; tokens only, no hex. (The earlier subtle pill + explanatory sentence and the per-row left `inset` box-shadow accent were replaced by this single pill, working tree 2026-08-02.)
- **Group layout is CSS multi-columns, not grid (v0.1.42)**: `.pat-spec-cols{columns:3}` (2 tablet / 1 mobile at the site breakpoints) with `break-inside:avoid` groups - a grid row takes its tallest group's height and leaves a well of whitespace under every short one; columns stack tightly and re-balance free when a chosen variation drops rows. **Auto-sort**: `SpecificationPanel` gained an optional `autoSort` prop - true sorts groups tallest-first (stable; weight = the RANGE's row count + 1 for a heading, counted pre-filter so a selection cannot shuffle the order). Fed through shop's seam: `ShopDetailSpecPanelProps` gained `autoSort?: boolean` (`modules/shop/lib/detail-spec.ts`, a layout hint providers may ignore), set by a new **Auto-sort specification groups** yes/no field on shop's **Product: Sections** Puck block (`detail-parts.tsx`: `specSort`, default no, passed as `buildDetailSections(ctx, { specAutoSort })`). Sections block only - the Tabs block is nav-only and renders no spec content. Needs shop + product-attributes-for-shop releases together (the module's new prop is optional, so it tolerates an older shop).
- **The 16px rhythm is padding on a `.pat-spec-item` wrapper, never a margin on `.pat-spec-group` (v0.1.43)** - a margin left at a column break is dangling and the engines disagree: **WebKit carries it to the TOP of the next column**, so column three's first group sat 16px lower than columns one and two, while Blink placed it at zero. Not reproducible in Chromium at any width, which is why it has to be measured in WebKit (`playwright.webkit`, per [[reference_webkit_emulation_and_jsonld]]) - confirmed on the live Deskwell page at 1600/1440/1390/1366/1280/1200, `tops={c1:0,c2:0,c3:16}` before and `{0,0,0}` after, inter-group gaps 16 throughout both. Padding belongs to the wrapper's own box and `break-inside:avoid` keeps that box whole, so neither engine has a stray edge to place. **Do not "simplify" this back to a margin on the group.**
- **Filter-grid isolation, checked**: child-product values cannot reach the storefront filter as a *new* attribute - `ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx` offers only `listAttributes({ filtersOnly: true })`. But the import adds tens of thousands of child rows, so `getEffectiveValueIdsByProduct`'s variant rollup now pushes the existing per-product hidden rule (`HAVING bool_or(show_in_filters) = false`) into SQL as a `NOT EXISTS`, plus `SELECT DISTINCT`, instead of fetching every child row and discarding it in JS afterwards. Same answer, a fraction of the rows. **Caveat**: both `show_in_filters` columns default **true**, so spec-only helpings must be created with the per-product flag off or their values will be rolled into the matrix and the `data-pat-values` card attributes - a data-side requirement of the chair-spec import, not something the code can infer.

Admin: one shared `components/admin/SwatchImagePicker.tsx` client component (shop's `MediaPickerModal` + `uploadOneFile`/`preflightUploadError`, drag-and-drop onto the thumbnail, dashed box when empty) used by both the attributes screen (add-value row, and per-value so an existing picture can be swapped) and `AddValueBox` on the product editor. The Variations-tab cell is unchanged - a `<select>` cannot hold a picture, and the label is the identifier there.

**Attribute groups (v0.1.7)** - folders for the attribute vocabulary, **admin-side only**: `listAttributes()` ordering, the filter block, `matchesSelection` and every public read are untouched, so grouping cannot change what a shopper sees. `lib/db/groups.ts` holds the CRUD plus `listAttributeIdsInGroup`. The attributes screen fetches `attributes` and `groups` in one `Promise.all`, renders one section per group in `position` order followed by a **Not in a group** section (drawn only when non-empty, and it also catches any attribute pointing at a group row that has gone), gives every card a Group `<select>` that PATCHes `groupId`, and puts Rename/Delete on each group heading (delete confirms with the count and says the attributes stay put). Empty groups render a prompt rather than vanishing, otherwise a freshly-made group would look like it failed.

**Attribute names are unique per group, not shop-wide (v0.1.8).** The duplicate-name guard was global, so a shop that wanted "Size" under both Chairs and Desks simply could not create the second one - the whole point of folders. `attributeNameTaken(name, groupId, exceptId)` now scopes the check with `"group_id" IS NOT DISTINCT FROM ${groupId}::text` (the ungrouped pile counts as one group; the `::text` cast is needed or Postgres cannot resolve the operator for an untyped null parameter). `POST admin/attributes` resolves and validates `groupId` **before** judging the clash, and `PATCH admin/attributes/[id]` now checks on a `groupId` change too, against the post-patch `(name, group)` pair - moving an attribute into a folder that already has that name is as much a duplicate as renaming it into one. **No schema change**: nothing ever enforced name uniqueness in the DB, only the API, and slugs stay globally unique via `ensureUniqueAttributeSlug` so the storefront filter's query key is still unambiguous. The attributes screen's "Add an attribute" row gains a Group `<select>` (hidden when no groups exist, falls back to "No group" if the chosen folder has since been deleted, and deliberately **not** reset after an add - filling one folder in a row is the common case); without it every new attribute landed ungrouped and was judged against the ungrouped pile, so the second "Size" was still unreachable. Picture-swatch folders need no change - the group name is already a path segment, so two same-named attributes in different groups file to different folders.

**Ordering (v0.1.7)** - up/down buttons on every attribute card and group heading (`MoveButtons`, `aria-label`ed per row; buttons rather than drag-and-drop, which gets keyboard and screen-reader support for free on lists this short). Groups reorder among themselves. An attribute moves **within its section**, but the POST carries the flattened order of *every* section - the attribute `position` is global (it is the storefront filter order), so sending only one group's slice would let a move inside "Materials" leapfrog an attribute in another group on the shop. Both handlers go through the screen's existing `send()`, so a failure surfaces in the same banner and the list re-reads from the server.

**Value ordering (v0.1.17)** - attribute values get native HTML5 drag-and-drop instead of up/down buttons: a value list (colours, materials) commonly runs far longer than the attribute list itself, where the short-list case for buttons made sense, and a chip has no spare room for two more controls anyway. `draggable` sits on a small handle (`⠿`) inside each value chip, not the chip itself, so a drag gesture starting on the rename/delete buttons or the colour input is never misread; `onDragOver`/`onDrop` are on the chip, tracked via a per-card `draggedValueId` state. Same whole-running-order contract as attributes/groups: `POST admin/attributes/[id]/values/reorder` takes `{ ids: string[] }` scoped to one attribute, 400s on a duplicate id, 409s ("reload the page") on a list that doesn't exactly match the attribute's known value ids, then `setValuePositions(ids)` rewrites `position = index` for the whole list in one transaction (`lib/db/attributes.ts`, mirrors `setAttributePositions`). New `listAttributeValues(attributeId)` backs the 409 check. No new DB column - `pat_attribute_values.position` already existed and `listAttributes()` already ordered by it. The product Attributes tab, the Variations column dropdown (`listVariationColumns` orders `av."position"`) and the storefront filter block all re-read live and inherit the new order with no further work.

**A value reorder follows through to shop-variations (v0.1.17)** - `syncSourcedValueOrder(orderedValueIds)` in `lib/variations-bridge.ts`, called by the values reorder route, the third sibling of `renameSourcedOptions` / `syncSourcedOptionValues` and guarded by the same `hasVariationsTables()` probe. **Needed because shop-variations' own "refresh from source" syncs labels and swatches but never `position`** (`shop-variations/lib/option-refresh.ts:84-87` updates label/swatch; `nextPosition` at :72/:95 only numbers *newly added* values), so without this a copy keeps whatever slot it was created in for ever and a PAT reorder would move the filter and the product editor while every variations dropdown stayed as it was. Two set-based statements, no per-product loop, because a popular attribute can be an option source on hundreds of products and module routes share a hard 60s dispatcher ceiling:
- **Option values** - one `UPDATE ... FROM (WITH src(ref,rank) AS (VALUES …))` that renumbers **every** value on a touched option via `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY option_id ORDER BY (src.rank IS NULL), src.rank, position, id)`. Renumbering the whole option, not just the sourced rows, is what guarantees a clean collision-free 0..n; `src.rank IS NULL` sorting last parks **hand-typed values (no `source_ref`) after the sourced block in their existing relative order** - PAT owns the values it supplied and nothing else, and interleaving them by a rule nobody wrote down would be worse than a documented tail. The VALUES list casts `${id}::text, ${index}::int` explicitly, since an untyped bind in a VALUES list arrives as text and would sort "10" below "9".
- **Variants** - `resequenceVariants(productIds)` renumbers `svr_variants.position` from `ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY product_id ORDER BY array_agg(ov.position ORDER BY o.position, o.created_at, o.id))`. Postgres compares arrays element by element, which **is** the odometer `generateMatrix` used (options left to right, last option fastest), so this reproduces the order a fresh generation would give. Deliberately a **renumber, never a regenerate**: a variant carries stock, price, photographs and any order placed against it, so ids are preserved absolutely. Child product **names are not touched** - a name is built from option order, and reordering values *within* an option cannot change any variant's label.
- Route returns `{ optionValuesMoved, variantsResequenced }`; the screen reports it through the existing `renameNote` line, staying silent at 0 so the common no-variations case says nothing.
- **Verified by real execution, not just tsc**: the two statements were run against a throwaway Neon project with a 2-option / 3-value / 6-variant fixture (one hand-typed value, one wholly local option). Result: sourced values took PAT order, the hand-typed one settled last, the local option was untouched, all six variant ids survived, positions came out a clean 0..5 in the new odometer order. Project deleted afterwards. Raw SQL of this shape is invisible to `tsc`/`eslint`, so a fixture run is the only check that means anything.

The equivalent gap on shop-variations' own screen is fixed in shop-variations 0.1.61 (see its section). The two odometers agree: PAT's SQL sorts on `array_agg(position ORDER BY option position)` and shop-variations' JS sums `value_index * radix[option_index]`, and mixed-radix ordering is lexicographic tuple ordering, so a reorder driven from either screen leaves the variants in the same order. That equivalence holds because both paths renumber values to a clean 0..n before resequencing; it would not survive duplicate positions within one option.

**Groups move the picture swatches with them** - the folder path became `shop / attributes / [group name /] <attribute name>`, so `attributeFolderSegments(attributeName, groupName?)` takes an optional group segment and the private `segmentsForAttribute(attributeId)` resolves it from the row (both `resolveAttributeFolderId` and the look-only `findAttributeFolderId` go through it). The group segment is **omitted entirely** when an attribute is ungrouped, so an existing install's folders are byte-identical to before and nothing shuffles on upgrade. `refileAttributeSwatches(attributeId)` walks that attribute's values (new `listAttributeSwatches` - returns every non-null swatch, hex ones filtered out in JS by `isImageSwatch` rather than by a LIKE pattern, so the validator stays the single authority on what a picture is) and re-runs `fileSwatchImage` on each, moving the file and rewriting the stored url; `refileGroupSwatches(groupId)` does the lot for a group. Called on: move into/out of/between groups, group rename, group delete, **and attribute rename** - that last one had quietly stranded pictures in the old folder since 0.1.6. Per-picture failures stay swallowed-and-warned inside `fileSwatchImage`, so one unmovable file cannot strand the rest.

**Media filing is by attribute, not by product** - `lib/media-folder.ts` files pictures under `shop / attributes / [group /] <attribute name>` (lower-cased through `sanitizeFolderSegment`, same as shop's tree), NOT the product folder that shop-variations, the 3D module and the downloads module all use. Deliberate: an attribute value is shop-wide vocabulary (one "Oak" picture serves every product carrying it), so filing it under whichever product happened to be open would mislead, and would strand the picture the day that product is deleted. `fileSwatchImage` is a no-op unless the url resolves to a managed `Media` row, so the folder is never created for an attribute that only uses colours; a filing failure is warned and swallowed rather than failing the save. Pictures **imported** from shop-variations keep that module's filing - re-filing them would move a file shop-variations owns and break its own swatch. `lib/import-service.ts` now carries url swatches across instead of dropping everything non-hex, and infers the control type as IMAGE if any value has a picture, else SWATCH if any has a hex, else CHECKBOX (pictures win when an option holds both - picture tiles with an empty tile or two beat colour dots for the minority that have one). A bare media id, which shop-variations may also hold there, is still dropped: nothing renderable can be made of it.

**`core.media-reference-rewriters` (v0.1.6)** - `lib/media-reference-rewriter.ts` repoints `pat_attribute_values.swatch` (and `swatch_small`, 0.1.45) when core moves a blob (optimise/resize/crop/replace/rename), matching on url **equality** (for an image swatch the column is the whole url, so it cannot hit a hex colour). Without it the tile 404s while the library looks healthy. Registered in the manifest under this module's own id, alongside shop-variations' rewriter for its equivalent columns.

**`core.media-usage-providers`** - `lib/media-usage-provider.ts` returns every `pat_attribute_values.swatch` + `swatch_small` (colour swatches come back too - a hex string matches no media item) so picture swatches and their small copies stop counting as unused library clutter.

**Puck Blocks**: `ShopAttributeFilterGrid` ("Shop: Filtered Product Grid", layouts `shopIndex`/`shopCategory`/`shopCollection`, editor + RSC split via `rscImport`, colour tokens only). RSC renders every matching product up front with shop's **own** Product Card template (`resolveCardTemplate` + `buildCardContext` + `injectShopProductCardEmbed`), tagging each `.shop-card` anchor `data-pat-product`/`data-pat-values`; the `AttributeFilterShell` client island then shows/hides them in place. It deliberately mirrors shop's `renderCards` rather than calling it - the only difference is the data tag, which shop's helper has nowhere to hang. Facet semantics: OR within an attribute, AND across attributes - the rule itself is the pure `matchesSelection()` in `lib/filter-logic.ts` (7 tests in `lib/filter-logic.test.ts`), which the shell calls rather than keeping its own copy. Selection mirrors into the URL via `replaceState` (read post-mount only, so hydration cannot mismatch the server-rendered cards). Filter CSS in `components/public/filter-css.ts` (prefix `pat-`, tokens only, site breakpoints baked in like shop's grids; `.pat-images`/`.pat-image*` added in 0.1.6 for the picture tiles).

**Variant rollup**: `getEffectiveValueIdsByProduct()` unions a parent's own values with those of its **enabled** variants (disabled ones excluded - not buyable, so a filter hit would be a dead end), then (v0.1.3) **drops any value whose attribute the product has hidden** (`pat_product_attributes.show_in_filters = false` for that `(product, attribute)`); `countProductsByValue()` counts the same way, powering the per-option counts and `hide_empty_values`. Both are consumed only by the public filter grid (`ShopAttributeFilterGrid.rsc.tsx`), so the hide never touches admin. **`countProductsByValue(productIds, opts)` now takes the same `includeVariantValues` the grid builds its matrix with (2026-07-23)** and passes it through to `getEffectiveValueIdsByProduct`. Left to its own devices it rolled variants up regardless of the setting, so with the setting off a variant-only value showed a non-zero count, survived `hide_empty_values` on the strength of it, and then matched nothing when a shopper ticked it - a dead-end filter option. The counts and the matrix must see products the same way or the panel lies about itself.

**Extension point consumed**: `shop-variations.variant-field-provider` (id `product-attributes`) → `productAttributesVariantFieldProvider`. The provider is inert (no columns) unless the product has use-for-variations attributes, and unreachable unless shop-variations hosts the point, so an install without it sees no change. **Import batching (v0.1.4):** implements the optional `beginImport(productId, childIds)`, preloading every child's current variation-attribute value via `getVariantAttributeValues` in one query. `applyImportedRow` now (a) resolves each label once via a per-import cache over `ensureAttributeValueByLabel`, and (b) only calls `setVariantAttributeValue` when the resolved value id **differs** from the preloaded current one - killing the old unconditional per-row write. A ctx miss (new variant) reads as no current value, so its first non-empty cell still writes. **Preview `rowChanged` (v0.1.19-to-be, working tree):** read-only twin resolving each cell via new `findAttributeValueByLabel` (a non-creating lookup added beside `ensureAttributeValueByLabel` in `lib/db/membership.ts`) and comparing to the preloaded value; an unseen label resolves to null ≠ stored, so it counts as a change without materialising the value. **Auto-assign removed (working tree, 2026-07-28):** the provider used to walk every heading in an imported row and, on a non-empty cell whose heading named an existing attribute the product did not use for variations, call `upsertProductAttribute(productId, { useForVariations: true, showInFilters: false })` to attach it as a new variation column (guarded only by a fixed `RESERVED_VARIATION_HEADERS` deny-list of shop-variations' own headings plus an `Option N`/`Value N` pattern). Because `upsertProductAttribute` does `DO UPDATE SET use_for_variations = EXCLUDED`, it also **flipped an existing product-level helping** into a variation one. The new column then went into `exportVariationsCsv`'s header union, so Push wrote it back and the next Pull re-asserted it - deleting it in admin never stuck. Live Deskwell evidence: `Range` on 22 products, `Catalog` on 20, `Finish` on 28, plus `Commodity Code` / `ISPC Code` / `Catalogue Code` / `Overall Height`, all standing as per-variant columns on the Variations tab. Now: `applyImportedRow` fills only columns `listVariationColumns` already returns for that product, and its `rowChanged` twin's auto-assign detection is gone with it. Dropped with it: `attributesByName`/`attrNameCache`, `RESERVED_VARIATION_HEADERS`, `OPTION_PAIR_HEADER`, `isAutoAssignHeader`, `AttrImportCtx.assigned`, and the `listAllAttributes` / `upsertProductAttribute` imports in this file (both still used by `lib/import-service.ts` and the assignments route). The Products-tab twin in `lib/product-field-provider.ts` (via `upsertProductLevelAttribute`) is untouched. Behaviour tested in `lib/variant-field-provider.test.ts`.

**Known Limitations**: filtering only covers what the block rendered, and `listProducts` clamps `perPage` to 100 - so 100 products is the honest ceiling per grid (a larger catalogue wants a paginated, server-filtered grid). `pat_settings` has no admin UI (defaults only) in v1. No `settingsTabs` entry. Renaming an attribute re-slugs it, breaking any bookmarked filter URL. Imported swatches take hex only (shop-variations also allows a media id there).

### Product Downloads for Shop

- Slug: `product-downloads-for-shop` (table prefix `pdl_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/product-downloads-for-shop`, manifest version 0.1.2 (registry pin v0.1.2, landed in core v0.5.540).
- `core.media-usage-providers` (`lib/media-usage-provider.ts`) - contributes `pdl_files.url`/`media_key`/`media_id`, so attached downloads aren't counted as unused media.
- `requiresCoreVersion` **0.5.472**, `requiresModules` **shop >= 0.1.50** (the release adding `shop.product-detail-tabs`). Manifest v0.1.0 named 0.1.47 - the shop of the day it was written against, which shipped without the point; corrected in module v0.1.1, since a min version naming a release that lacks the feature installs cleanly and then silently renders no tab at all.
- Free downloadable literature on a product - manuals, spec sheets, care cards, drawings - each named in plain English, shown on the product page under a **Downloads** tab that anyone can take them from. Distinct from shop's `shp_digital_files`, which is the product being *sold* and is delivered post-purchase behind a token with an expiry and a download count.

**Database**
Table prefix: `pdl_`

- `pdl_files` - `id` (text PK, gen_random_uuid), `product_id` FK → `shp_products` (cascade), `name` (what the shopper reads and saves it as), `filename` (as uploaded), `url`, `media_provider?`, `media_key?`, `media_id?` (the core `Media` row, nullable), `mime_type`, `size` (int), `position` (int), `created_at`. Index: product_id.

**Extension points consumed**: `shop.product-editor-sections` (id `product-downloads-inline`, label "Downloads", order 50, permission `shop.products`) and `shop.product-detail-tabs` (id `product-downloads`, label "Downloads", order 45).

**Routes**: `GET|POST|PATCH /api/m/product-downloads-for-shop/admin/products/[id]/files` (list / upload / save order - PATCH scopes the renumber to the product in the WHERE clause, so a posted foreign id renumbers nothing), `PATCH|DELETE /api/m/product-downloads-for-shop/admin/files/[id]` (rename / drop our row + the `Media` row + the blob), `GET /api/m/product-downloads-for-shop/public/files/[id]` (the download).

**Upload path - through the server, and it has to be (4 MB)**: the direct-to-Worker path photographs and 3D models use is **closed to a document**. The Worker types an upload from its object key's extension (`contentTypeForKey`) and 415s anything that is not a raster image or a 3D model, so a signed PDF key is refused no matter what. The bytes therefore go multipart through the serverless function, where Vercel's ~4.5 MB body cap applies, so the module advertises `MAX_UPLOAD_BYTES` (4 MB) and preflights on the client rather than promising more and dying on the doorstep - the exact failure `product-3d-views-for-shop` v0.1.2 was released to fix, and the reason shop's own `digital-files` route claiming `maxSizeBytes: 200 MB` is a lie the platform overrules. Lifting it needs a core release teaching the Worker about document types **plus** every install redeploying its Worker.

**Why downloads are proxied rather than linked (`app/api/public/files/[id]`)**: core's `extensionForMimeType` derives a key's extension from the MIME **subtype**, so a `.docx` is stored under a key ending `.vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document`, with a nanoid prefix. Link the shopper at storage and they save a file their machine cannot open; the `<a download>` attribute would rename it but is ignored cross-origin, and storage is always another origin. So the route sets `Content-Disposition` itself from `lib/download-name.ts` (owner's name + the *original* file's extension, so "Instructions.exe" cannot rename a PDF, and a typed ".pdf" does not double). Also: reads by `provider`+`key` via core's `downloadMedia` rather than fetching the stored url, so a site that later moves its Worker keeps working (shop's digital files store only a url and every link dies at that point); `Content-Length` from the bytes in hand, never the `size` column; always `attachment` + `nosniff`.

**Self-healing storage details (`lib/db/heal.ts`, `withFreshStorage`)**: `pdl_files` copies `media_provider` / `media_key` / `url` off the core `Media` row at upload time so the download route needs no join - a snapshot the core library then invalidates behind its back. Renaming a product renames its media folder, the folder path is baked into the object key, so every file inside gets a new key **and a new nanoid**, and core updates only its own `Media` rows. Both of `chiro-plus-high-back-ergonomic-posture-24-hour-office-chair`'s assembly PDFs went to "That file could not be retrieved." this way (stale key 404s at the Worker, live `Media.key` 200s; verified against the Deskwell library). `media_id` is the column that survives a move, because it names the row rather than the address, so the public GET and the admin DELETE both resolve through it first: mismatch → serve/delete the live key and write it back to `pdl_files`. Repair is per-request and needs nobody to press anything - the next click on a stale download fixes it and serves it. Rows with no `media_id`, or whose `Media` row is gone, pass through untouched. Write-back is best-effort (a lost race just heals again next time). The DELETE side matters separately: deleting by a dead key leaves the real bytes billed forever with nothing pointing at them. `p3d_models` and `svr_uploads` cache the same three columns beside a `media_id` and have the same latent exposure (0 stale rows on Deskwell today).

**Status gating**: the public route loads the owning product and 404s unless `status === 'ACTIVE' && !catalogueHidden` - the same line `app/public/shop/products/[slug]/page.tsx` draws. Without it an id would hand out an unlaunched product's manual or a withdrawn one's spec sheet; the uuid makes it unguessable, not access-controlled.

**Type policy** (`lib/file-kinds.ts`, single source for server and browser): pdf, zip, doc(x), xls(x), ppt(x), rtf, txt, csv, dwg, dxf, jpg/jpeg, png. **No html/svg/xml/js, deliberately** - the module serves stored bytes from the site's own origin, and a type the browser renders markup from is stored XSS rather than a download. The extension decides, not the declared MIME (a .zip arrives as `application/zip` or `application/x-zip-compressed`; a .dwg as nothing).

**Known limitations**: 4 MB per file (above). No per-variation downloads - files attach to the product only. On a DIGITAL product that also carries free literature, shop's own "Downloads" tab and this module's sit side by side, both labelled "Downloads"; rare (it means an ebook with a manual) and cosmetic, but a per-product label would need the point's contract to grow.

### Reviews for Shop

- Slug: `reviews-for-shop` (table prefix `rvw_`), repo `github.com/cactus-foundation-modules/reviews-for-shop`, manifest version **0.1.1** (registry pin v0.1.1, pinned in core **v0.5.812**; initial 0.1.0 landed in core v0.5.799). 0.1.1 adds the reviews CSV export/import; no schema change.
- `requiresCoreVersion` **0.5.793**, `requiresModules` **shop >= 0.1.144** (the version on disk when it was written; it needs `shop.product-detail-tabs` from 0.1.50 and the `shop.settings-sub-tabs` slot from 0.1.53).
- Customer reviews: a rating out of five plus prose, shown on the product page as a **Reviews tab** or as blocks placed by hand, moderated (or not) from **Shop → Reviews**, with owner replies, verified-purchase badging and optional invitation emails.
- Own permission keys **`reviews.access`** (read the queue - which means reading reviewers' email addresses) and **`reviews.manage`** (publish / hold / reject / reply / delete / settings), gated by `lib/access.ts` in the shape of shop's `requireShopUser`. Shop's own keys are deliberately **not** accepted, following quote-for-shop's reasoning.

**Database**
Table prefix: `rvw_`

- `rvw_settings` - singleton (`id` text PK default `'singleton'`, seeded by the migration with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`): `auto_publish` (bool, **default false** - moderation is the unchosen default), `who_can_review` (CHECK ANYONE | MEMBERS | VERIFIED_BUYERS), `product_surface` (CHECK TAB | NONE), `show_verified_badge`, `ask_for_title`, `min_comment_length` (int, default 20), `one_per_product_per_email`, `notify_email` (text, `''` = send none), `reviews_per_page` (int, default 10), `thanks_published` / `thanks_pending` (text), `invites_enabled` (bool, **default false**), `invite_delay_days` (int, default 14), `updated_at`.
- `rvw_reviews` - `id` (text PK, gen_random_uuid), `product_id` FK → `shp_products` (**cascade**), `member_id?` (no FK - Members is optional), `author_name`, `author_email` (never rendered on the storefront; it is the verified-purchase match, the one-per-product key and the reply address), `rating` (int, CHECK 1-5), `title?`, `body`, `status` (CHECK PENDING | PUBLISHED | REJECTED), `verified_purchase` (bool), `order_id?` FK → `shp_orders` (**SET NULL**), `reply_body?` / `reply_at?`, `submitted_ip?`, `created_at`, `updated_at`, `published_at?`. Indexes: (product_id, status, published_at), (status, created_at), author_email.
- `rvw_invites` - `id`, `order_id` FK → `shp_orders` (cascade), `product_id` FK → `shp_products` (cascade), `email`, `sent_at`, **UNIQUE (order_id, product_id)**. The constraint is the guard, not the query: two overlapping cron runs would both read "not asked yet", and the second insert failing quietly is the correct outcome.

**Statuses**: `published_at` is stamped the first time a review goes live and then left alone (`COALESCE`), so taking one down and putting it back does not shuffle it to the top of the product page as though it were new. The storefront orders on `COALESCE(published_at, created_at)`.
