The `number` query is load-bearing, not decorative: a recording lives in the Region its call was processed in and the SID alone doesn't say which, so `TwilioAdminScreen`'s `CallLogCard` passes the active tab's number and the route resolves the Region from it - guess wrong and it reads as "Recording not found"), `admin/make-call` (POST `{ fromNumber, to, callMeAt }` - two-leg click-to-dial: validates both numbers E.164 and `fromNumber` against the live account listing (must be voice-capable), places a call to the admin from that number whose TwiML `<Gather>`s one digit then hits `webhooks/outbound-connect?to=`), `webhooks/outbound-connect` (POST, X-Twilio-Signature-validated over the full URL including the query string; on any digit returns `<Dial callerId="<From = the site's Twilio number>">` to the E.164 `to`, else `<Hangup/>`), `webhooks/voice` (POST, X-Twilio-Signature-validated, returns TwiML: optional `<Say voice="...">` greeting (XML-escaped `greeting_message`, voice from the curated `lib/voices.ts` list, both rule voices passed through `voiceForRegion` for the number's Region first - v0.1.19, us1-only Generative voices are Twilio 13520 elsewhere) then `<Dial>` to the enabled rule's target - with `record="record-from-answer-dual"` when `record_calls`, and `callerId="<called number>"` when `show_called_number` so the forwarded leg shows the site's Twilio number instead of the caller's. Looks the rule up with `getRuleForNumber` (**not** enabled-only: a number can have forwarding off and voicemail on, and the webhook still has to answer). When the call can't be forwarded - forwarding off, no valid E.164 target, or `isRuleOpenNow` says the number is shut - it returns the voicemail TwiML if `voicemail_enabled`, else `<Reject/>`; that path deliberately skips the call greeting, which promises a forward that isn't going to happen. With voicemail on, the `<Dial>` also carries `timeout="<ring_timeout>"` and `action="<voicemail webhook>"`; with voicemail off it keeps Twilio's default timeout and no action, so the pre-v0.1.9 behaviour is byte-identical), `webhooks/voicemail` (POST, X-Twilio-Signature-validated **over the full URL including the query string**, the follow-on step for a dialled call. Twilio hits it twice over a voicemail's life and **the URL says which stage it is** - the `<Record>`'s `action` carries `?stage=recording` (`RECORDING_STAGE`/`voicemailRecordingUrl()`), the `<Dial>`'s doesn't. All the branching is the pure `planVoicemailRequest` (`lib/voicemail.ts`), the route only does the IO: `log-message` → `recordVoicemail` then `<Hangup/>`, `take-message` → re-read the rule (hang up if voicemail was switched off mid-call), swap a us-only voicemail voice via `voiceForRegion` (v0.1.19) and return `voicemailTwiml`, `hangup` → `<Hangup/>`. The hangup on the recording stage is **load-bearing**, since a `<Record>` left without an explicit `action` re-requests the current document's URL and would loop. The `recordVoicemail` call is wrapped in a try/catch that only logs: the caller has already rung off and Twilio would just retry the webhook, so a DB failure must not turn a recorded message into an error. The recording SID comes from `RecordingSid`, falling back to the trailing `RE...` segment of `RecordingUrl`).
- `lib/twilio.ts` is a dependency-free REST client (Basic auth, `AbortSignal.timeout(15s)`), Region-aware throughout - every account-API call takes an optional `region` defaulting to `HOME_REGION`: `sendSms(to, body, from, region)`, `listIncomingNumbers` (global pool, always `us1`; includes `smsCapable`/`voiceCapable` from Twilio's capability flags), `listCallsForNumber(number, region, limit)`/`listMessagesForNumber(number, region, limit)` (To+From listings merged newest-first, capped 50; calls carry completed recording SIDs from a Region-wide `Recordings.json` listing), `fetchRecordingAudio(sid, region)` (30s timeout), `setNumberVoiceUrl` (account-level, `us1`), `fetchAccountName(region)` (doubles as the per-Region credential check), `placeCall(to, from, twiml, region)`, `getNumberRegion`/`setNumberRegion` (Routes v3, `us1`), `escapeXml`, `validateTwilioSignature` (HMAC-SHA1, timing-safe, tried against every configured Region's token). `lib/numbers.ts` owns the site-number store: `getSiteNumbers`, `addSiteNumber` (takes `region`), `removeSiteNumber`, `setDefaultSmsNumber`, `setSiteNumberRegion` (Twilio first, then the row), `syncSiteNumbers` (refreshes name/capability **and** re-reads each on-site number's Region from the Routes API in parallel, so a change made directly in the Twilio console is picked up; a failed lookup keeps the stored value rather than wiping it), `resolveNumberRegion` (stored value for on-site numbers, live Routes lookup otherwise - the admin log tabs cover every account number, not just on-site ones, so the fallback is load-bearing), `getDefaultSmsNumber` (now returns `{ phoneNumber, region } | null`), `isSmsReady`, `sendSiteSms` (throws when no text-enabled number is selected; sends through the default number's own Region).
- **Voicemail / v0.1.9.** Per number: switch voicemail on, set how long the forward-to number rings before it takes over (`ring_timeout`), write its own greeting with its own voice (separate from the forwarding notice - reuses `admin/greeting-preview` unchanged for the "call me to hear it" button, since that route already takes an arbitrary message + voice), and optionally restrict the number to opening hours. Recordings need **no new storage**: `<Record>` attaches to the call SID, and `listCallsForNumber` already merges a Region-wide `Recordings.json` listing keyed by call SID, so voicemails appear in the existing call log player for free. Max message length is a fixed `MAX_VOICEMAIL_SECONDS = 120` in `lib/voicemail.ts`, not a setting. `lib/voicemail.ts` holds the shared `<Say>`+`<Record>` builder, `voicemailUrl()`/`voicemailRecordingUrl()`, the `planVoicemailRequest` planner and its constants, used by both the voice and voicemail webhooks; an empty greeting falls back to a stock line so voicemail-on-with-no-message still works. `lib/voicemail-log.ts` owns the `tw_voicemails` store and the notification: `recordVoicemail` (idempotent `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` + `upsertAlert`), `filterVoicemailSids` (the call log's SIDs that are voicemails).
- **Voicemail marking + admin notification / v0.1.10.** The one thing Twilio's flat `Recordings.json` listing can't tell you is whether a recording is a voicemail message or a recorded forwarded call - both are just recordings against a call SID. The distinction only exists at the moment the voicemail `<Record>` finishes, a request `webhooks/voicemail` already handles, so that stage now writes a `tw_voicemails` row (`recordVoicemail` in `lib/voicemail-log.ts`) and raises an admin notification via the core `upsertAlert` (`lib/notifications/alerts.ts`, `type:'message'`, `dedupeKey` `twilio-voicemail:<recordingSid>` so each message rings the bell once and reading one doesn't hide the next, `link:'/m/twilio'`, title `New voicemail from <caller>` with a withheld/anonymous From shown as "a withheld number"). The call log API marks the voicemails among a page's recordings (`filterVoicemailSids`, an `IN (...)` over the page's SIDs rather than listing the table) and `CallLogCard` shows a **Voicemail** badge (`--color-primary` outline) beside those recordings' Listen buttons. Recordings made before v0.1.10 have no row and read as ordinary recordings - the log isn't back-filled because Twilio never knew the difference either. Migration `005_voicemails.sql` (mirrored into `001_initial.sql`); `tw_voicemails` added to `teardown`. Backup round-trip re-run green (3/3).
- **Voicemail marking: two false-positive fixes / v0.1.11.** v0.1.10 decided "this is the recording stage" by looking for `RecordingSid`/`RecordingUrl` in the payload. Both halves of that were wrong. (1) **A `<Dial record="...">` sends `RecordingUrl` to its own `action` URL** (Twilio documents it as included "only if record is set on `<Dial>`"; `RecordingSid`/`RecordingDuration` are not sent there, only to a `recordingStatusCallback`) - so on a `record_calls` number every answered forwarded call's dial callback read as a finished voicemail, tagging the *conversation's* recording as a voicemail and ringing the admin's bell for it. The stage is now stated on the URL instead of inferred: `voicemailRecordingUrl()` puts `?stage=recording` on the `<Record>`'s action and the route matches on that (signature validation now covers `request.nextUrl.search`, as `webhooks/outbound-connect` already did). Branch order matters - the dial stage is checked by `DialCallStatus`, which every dial callback carries, so a recorded-but-unanswered dial still reaches voicemail instead of having its recording params swallow the message. (2) **Twilio saves silent recordings by default** ("By default, silent recordings are saved by Twilio"), so a caller who rings off at the beep still produces one; `trim-silence` shrinks it to ~0-1s rather than to nothing. New `MIN_VOICEMAIL_SECONDS = 2` (a named constant beside `MAX_VOICEMAIL_SECONDS`, not a setting): a shorter recording is a hang-up, gets no row and no notification. That is deliberately the cheap direction to be wrong in - an unlogged recording still sits in the call log with its Listen button, it just isn't announced as a message. The decision logic moved into the pure `planVoicemailRequest(req): {action:'log-message'|'take-message'|'hangup'}` in `lib/voicemail.ts`, covered by `lib/voicemail.test.ts` (13 tests, incl. both regressions above and the no-stage-marker in-flight-across-a-deploy case, which hangs up rather than looping). No schema change.
- `lib/business-hours.ts` - opening-hours type, validator (`parseBusinessHours`), `defaultBusinessHours()` (Mon-Fri 09:00-17:00), `MIN_RING_TIMEOUT`/`MAX_RING_TIMEOUT` (5/120) and the pure `isOpenAt(hours, timezone, at)`. **Deliberately free of DB imports** so the admin form can share the type, the validator and the defaults; the `SiteConfig.timezone` lookup that feeds it lives in `forwarding.ts` (`isRuleOpenNow`), which is server-only. Semantics, all covered by `lib/business-hours.test.ts` (16 tests): empty schedule = always open (so every pre-v0.1.9 rule behaves exactly as before); the clock is read in the site timezone via `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with `hourCycle: 'h23'` (`hour12: false` emits `24` for midnight on some ICU builds); an unknown timezone falls back to UTC rather than throwing mid-call; closing time is exclusive; a window whose close is earlier than its open runs **overnight** and belongs to the day it starts on (a Monday 18:00-02:00 window still counts at 01:00 Tuesday, and does not spill out of a day marked closed); `open == close` is a zero-length window = shut (use the Closed toggle); and a day **missing** from an otherwise-populated schedule is treated as unrestricted, not closed - an absent rule should never be the thing that stops a call getting through. The admin form always writes all seven days.
- Admin page `/m/twilio` (`TwilioAdminScreen`): one core `TabStrip` tab per account number (label `phoneNumber · friendlyName`, logs lazy-loaded per tab, Refresh button in the strip's trailing slot), each tab holding a "Make a call" card (number to call + "your phone" input remembered in localStorage `twilio-call-me-at`, hits `admin/make-call`), a call log table (when/direction/from/to/status/length + a Listen button per completed recording swapping to an inline `<audio controls autoPlay>` on the `admin/recordings/[sid]` proxy, with a **Voicemail** badge beside recordings that are voicemail messages) and a message log table (when/direction/from/to/status/body). Forwarding configuration moved to the Settings Twilio tab in v0.1.6: `TwilioForwardingSection` (rendered by `TwilioSettingsTab` below the phone-numbers picker once connected) keeps the per-number rows - forward-to, on/off, greeting textarea (max 500 chars), voice `<select>` (optgroups from `lib/voices.ts` `TWILIO_VOICES` - Basic/Polly Standard/Neural/Generative; server validates via `isValidVoice`; v0.1.19 `VoicePicker` takes the number's `region` and disables us-only Generative voices off-us1, noting the substitute callers actually hear), record-calls checkbox (recordings playable from the Twilio page's call log), show-this-number-as-caller-ID checkbox (with a you-won't-see-who-rang note), "Call me to preview" (shown when a greeting is typed: number input + button hitting `admin/greeting-preview`). The admin's own SMS login-code card moved off this `twilio.manage`-gated page to the admin account page via `admins.account-section` (`TwilioAdminSmsSection`, wrapping the shared `SmsTwoFactorCard` also used by the member section) so every admin can enrol, not just Twilio managers.

- **Settings redesign + call features / v0.1.22.** `TwilioSettingsTab` was one endless scroll (credentials card, phone-numbers card, then the whole per-number forwarding form stacked for every number). It is now five core `TabStrip` sub-tabs, shop-settings style: **Account** (country picker, Account SID, per-region tokens, connection status, and the new Test connection button; the four-step set-up walk-through collapses into a `<details>` once connected), **Phone numbers** (unchanged picker), **Call handling** (`TwilioForwardingSection`), **Texting** (which number texts go out from + Send a test text), **Alerts & data** (the new `tw_settings` row). `TwilioForwardingSection` itself now edits **one number at a time**, picked from a nested `TabStrip` (shown only when the account has more than one number), with the controls grouped under Forwarding / Missed calls / Voicemail / Opening hours headings and a per-number "Unsaved changes" marker (`dirtySids`) so switching numbers never silently loses edits. Nine features landed with it:
  1. **Test connection** - `admin/test-connection` (POST `{ homeRegion, accountSid, tokens }`) calls the new `testCredentials(region, accountSid, authToken)` in `lib/twilio.ts`, which takes credentials as arguments instead of reading the env, so **typed-but-unsaved** values can be checked before the save-and-redeploy round trip. Blank fields fall back to the saved env values; every region with a token in play is tested separately.
  2. **Voicemail + missed-call email alerts** - `lib/notify.ts` `sendVoicemailEmail`/`sendMissedCallEmail`, gated on the `tw_settings` toggles + a `notify_email` address, sent through the core `sendEmail`. Both link to `/{adminPath}/m/twilio` (admin path read from `SiteConfig`). All failures are logged, never thrown: the call itself went fine and Twilio must not be told otherwise. The voicemail email only fires on the request that actually inserted the row (`$executeRaw` rowcount), so a repeated callback cannot double-send.
  3. **Auto-text on missed call** - per number (`missed_call_sms_enabled`/`missed_call_sms_message`, 320 chars, stock line when empty). `sendMissedCallText` sends from the called number where it is SMS-capable, else the site default sender. Withheld callers are skipped - there is nowhere to text.
  4. **Holiday dates** - per number `holiday_dates` JSONB, an array of `"YYYY-MM-DD"`. `parseHolidayDates` (same reject-don't-guess contract as `parseBusinessHours`, sorts + dedupes) and the pure `isHolidayOn(dates, timezone, at)` in `lib/business-hours.ts`, matched on the calendar date **in the site timezone** (`Intl.DateTimeFormat('en-CA')`, same UTC fallback as `clockIn`). `isRuleOpenNow` checks holidays before the weekly schedule; a holiday closes the whole day regardless of hours.
  5. **Send a test text** - `admin/test-sms` (POST `{ to }`) sends one fixed test message through `sendSiteSms`, proving credentials + number + region without going near a sign-in code.
  6. **Voicemail transcription** - per number `transcribe_voicemail` adds `transcribe="true" transcribeCallback=...` to the voicemail `<Record>`; the new `webhooks/transcription` route (signature-validated, returns 204) files the text onto `tw_voicemails.transcription_text`/`transcription_status` via `recordTranscription`. `admin/calls` returns a `transcriptions` map per call and `CallLogCard` prints the words (or "on its way" / "could not make out") under the Listen button. Twilio only transcribes 2-120s recordings, which is exactly the `MIN`/`MAX_VOICEMAIL_SECONDS` window already enforced.
  7. **Anonymous callers** - per number `anonymous_callers` `'allow'|'voicemail'|'reject'`. The voice webhook treats a non-E.164 `From` (or Twilio's `+266696687` ANONYMOUS marker) as withheld: reject outright, force the voicemail path, or ring through as before (the default, so nothing changes for existing rules).
  8. **Retention** - `tw_settings.retention_days` (0 = forever, the default and the historical behaviour; ceiling `MAX_RETENTION_DAYS` 3650). `lib/retention.ts` `runRetentionSweep` lists recordings older than the cutoff **per configured region** (`listRecordingSidsBefore`), deletes each (`deleteRecording`), then prunes `tw_voicemails` rows by `created_at`. One page (400) per region per night, so a backlog drains over successive runs rather than holding the cron open. Driven by `cron/retention` on the standard `CRON_SECRET` bearer check.
  9. **Sequential ring** - per number `forward_to_second`. The voice webhook's `<Dial>` now gets its action URL whenever there is anything to do after an unanswered ring (voicemail, a second number, an auto-text, or an email alert). `planVoicemailRequest` takes a second argument `{ hasSecondLeg }` and can return the new `dial-second` action; the second leg's own `<Dial>` carries `?leg=2` (`SECOND_LEG`/`secondLegUrl()`) so it cannot loop - same URL-marker trick as `RECORDING_STAGE`, and for the same reason (the two dial callbacks are otherwise indistinguishable). `take-message` is now the single point where a call is known to be definitively missed, so the auto-text and email alert hang off it and fire exactly once.
  10. **Bank-holiday import** (added same release, after the nine above). `lib/holidays.ts` + `admin/holidays` (GET): with no `region` param it returns the picker's own country options (single source of truth for the list); with one it returns that country's public holidays **for the twelve months starting today** - `fetchHolidayWindow(region, from)`, `from` inclusive / `to` exclusive, where `from` is `todayIn(await getSiteTimezone())`. A rolling window, not a calendar year: a calendar year is the wrong window for eleven months of the year (an October import would offer ten months of dates that had already been and none of the spring ones). The window straddles two calendar years so both are fetched - one cached document read twice for gov.uk, two parallel requests for Nager - then filtered by ISO string compare (ISO dates sort correctly as strings, so no parsing). `oneYearOn` builds the end bound through `Date.UTC`, which rolls a 29 February start to 1 March rather than producing a date that does not exist. Five regions: England and Wales / Scotland / Northern Ireland from **gov.uk's own `bank-holidays.json`** (authoritative, one document covering ~2019-2028, filtered by division and year), Republic of Ireland and United States from **Nager.Date** (`/api/v3/PublicHolidays/{year}/{code}`, `global !== false` only so a US state-only holiday cannot shut a line three thousand miles away). Results are deduped by date, sorted, and cached a day (`next: { revalidate: 86400 }`). Nothing is stored by this route - `HolidayImporter` in `TwilioForwardingSection` shows the list with already-added dates ticked-and-disabled, the rest pre-ticked, and the admin adds what they want. A missing gov.uk division **throws** rather than returning `[]`: gov.uk always publishes all three, so absence means the feed changed shape, and an empty list would read as "no bank holidays that year". `getSiteTimezone` is now exported from `lib/forwarding.ts` for the route's use. `lib/holidays.test.ts` (26 tests, `fetch` stubbed) covers both payload shapes, the division/year slicing, the nationwide filter, dedupe, name fallbacks, both failure modes, `todayIn`/`oneYearOn` (leap day included), and the window boundaries - inclusive start, exclusive end, and the two-year merge.
  Schema: module migration `008_call_features_and_settings.sql` (mirrored into `001_initial.sql` for fresh installs) adds the six `tw_forwarding_rules` columns, two `tw_voicemails` transcription columns, and the new singleton `tw_settings` table (`notify_voicemail_email`, `notify_missed_call_email`, `notify_email`, `retention_days`), added to `teardown`. New lib files: `lib/settings.ts` (`getTwilioSettings`/`updateTwilioSettings`, `DEFAULT_SETTINGS`, `MAX_RETENTION_DAYS`), `lib/notify.ts`, `lib/retention.ts`. New API routes: `admin/settings` (GET/PUT - rejects an alert toggle with no address rather than letting it silently do nothing), `admin/test-connection`, `admin/test-sms`, `cron/retention`, `webhooks/transcription`. `getForwardingRules`/`getRuleForNumber` moved to `$queryRawUnsafe` with a shared `RULE_COLUMNS` constant (column list only, no interpolated values). Tests: `voicemail.test.ts` gains the second-leg and transcription cases, `business-hours.test.ts` gains `parseHolidayDates`/`isHolidayOn`.

### Gemini Watermark Remover

Module `gemini-watermark-remover` (tablePrefix `gwr_`, v0.1.7, requiresCoreVersion 0.5.346). Locates the Google Gemini watermark and **erases it by reverse alpha-blend at a pixel-verified candidate position**, saving the cleaned result into a dedicated root `gemini-processed` folder in the core media library under its original filename. No database tables (the `gwr_` prefix is reserved but unused), no Puck blocks, no public pages, no cron, no settings tab. Declares no permissions of its own - reuses the core `media.upload` permission.

- **Why the v0.1.6 rewrite (drops MI-GAN):** v0.1.3-0.1.5 erased the mark with client-side MI-GAN inpainting, but MI-GAN *hallucinates* the hole from its surroundings, so when the sparkle sits on a sharp geometric line (e.g. a desk edge) it smears the edge into a blur. Root cause of the earlier "reverse-blend leaves residual" belief was actually the library's **adaptive detector drifting off the mark** (picking an 80px box above the true 96px mark on a 2816x1536 image), so the reverse-blend was applied at the wrong place. Fix: skip the adaptive detector for placement entirely - reverse-blend at the exact catalog position (`detectWatermarkConfig`+`calculateWatermarkPosition`) with the matching embedded alpha map. Reverse-blend reconstructs the true underlying pixels (edges intact) and never smears; worst case on a non-catalog size is a faint leftover, not a destructive smear.
- **Why the v0.1.7 rewrite (pixel-verified placement):** the v0.1.6 blind catalog erase backfired when Gemini shipped a second geometry for the same size. 2752x1536 exports now carry the mark 192px from the corner (`alphaVariant '20260520'`, weaker blend curve) while the catalog still answers 64px - so v0.1.6 left the real mark AND burnt a black sparkle where it reverse-blended clean pixels (reverse-blend on unmarked pixels = over-subtraction = dark stamp). v0.1.7 never erases blind: it builds candidate boxes (library's own `meta.position` pick, catalog position, 192px new-margin variant), scores each by Pearson correlation between the alpha map and box luminance (real mark ≥ ~0.25, unmarked texture ≤ ~0.17, threshold 0.2), then picks the blend curve by trial erase on a copy (lowest leftover |correlation| wins; the wrong curve leaves 0.4+, the right one ~0). Two rejection gates fall back to the server pipeline instead of touching pixels: presence below threshold (`unlocated`), or best trial residual ≥ 0.3 / ≥ the presence score (erase would burn rather than clean, seen on scaled non-official-size exports).
- **Processing is all client-side** (kills the old >4MB lossy pre-upload re-encode and upload-cap failures). `components/admin/WatermarkRemoverScreen.tsx`: `createImageBitmap` at full res → `detectWatermark` (canvas) → if a box is found, `eraseWatermark` (reverse-blend, no ONNX) → encode under the 4MB cap (output only) → POST with `mode=save-cleaned`. Any browser-path failure falls through to `mode=server-fallback`.
- `lib/detect.ts` - `detectWatermark(canvas, rgba)` calls `removeWatermarkFromImage` for the `meta.applied` yes/no gate **and** takes its `meta.position`/`meta.config` as a candidate, alongside the catalog answer and the 192px new-margin variant. Candidates are deduped, bounds-checked, presence-scored against the pristine pixels, and the winner's blend curve is picked by trial erase (see v0.1.7 note above). Returns `{found:true, box, alphaKey}`, `{found:false, unlocated:false}` (genuinely clean), or `{found:false, unlocated:true}` (mark exists but no safe local erase → caller uses server fallback). `residualVisibility.visible` is unreliable both ways, so it is not used.
- `lib/erase.ts` - `eraseWatermark(rgba,imgW,box,alphaKey)`: pure reverse alpha-blend (`original = (watermarked - a*logo)/(1-a)`), constants copied verbatim from the library's `blendModes.js`. Fetches the embedded alpha map via a cached `WatermarkEngine` (no network, no ONNX). Only pixels the alpha map actually tinted are touched. Also exports the verification maths: `scoreSparklePresence(rgba,imgW,box,alphaKey)` (Pearson correlation between alpha-map magnitude and box luminance over signal pixels) and `pickAlphaMap(rgba,imgW,box,keys)` (trial erase per candidate map on a copied patch, returns the key with the lowest leftover |correlation| plus that residual).
- `lib/remove.ts` - server-fallback reverse-blend wrapper (library `/node` path, unchanged maths), returns `residualVisible` from `meta.detection.residualVisibility.visible`. `lib/pilio-gwr.d.ts` - ambient types for `/node` + `/browser` entry points (`getAlphaMap` widened to accept variant-key strings like `'96-20260520'`).
- API route `POST /api/m/gemini-watermark-remover/remove` (`app/api/remove/route.ts`) - session + `media.upload` gated, media provider required (503 otherwise), multipart `file` (PNG/JPEG/WebP) + `mode`. `save-cleaned`: skip removal, `validateUpload`→`uploadMedia`→`saveMediaRecord`, return `{ status:'erased', media }` 201. `server-fallback`: run reverse-blend; no watermark → `{ status:'clean', reason }` 200 (saves nothing); else save + `{ status: residualVisible ? 'partial' : 'removed', media }` 201. **Honesty gate: never returns a clean `removed` when residual is still visible.**
- Core deps: `@pilio/gemini-watermark-remover` (MIT), `sharp` `^0.34.5` (used by the server fallback). **`onnxruntime-web` was dropped from core `package.json`** (2026-07-14): MI-GAN was its only consumer, and the ONNX runtime the browser actually executes is vendored inside `@pilio/gemini-watermark-remover`'s own bundle. It was 132MB of `node_modules` - roughly half the 290MB Vercel build cache - contributing nothing to any bundle. The About-dialog credit for ONNX Runtime (`lib/about/credits.ts`) stays: the runtime still runs in the browser, just via the vendored copy. The `next.config.ts` `outputFileTracingIncludes[...] = ['./modules/*/assets/**']` glob now matches no module (kept: module-name-agnostic, future-proof).
- **2026-08-10:** no sidebar link any more. The tool is a tab on core's Media page, published as `core.media-tabs` → `WatermarkRemoverMediaTab` (`components/admin/MediaTabPanel.tsx`, `media.upload` gated in the panel itself, not just by the host). `/m/gemini-watermark-remover` survives as a `redirect()` to `/media` for old bookmarks. `requiresCoreVersion` 0.5.1026. Previously: an admin page of its own with a plain ungrouped `navEntries` link. Outcome list statuses: erased / removed / partial / clean / error.
- Shipped as `cactus-foundation-modules/gemini-watermark-remover` (registered in `modules.json`; bump the tag pin at release), listed in the core README's Available modules, wiki page at `wiki/Gemini-Watermark-Remover.md`.

### Ultimate SEO

Module `ultimate-seo` (repo `cactus-foundation-modules/ultimate-seo`), tablePrefix `seo_`, v0.1.6 (requiresCoreVersion 0.5.1150 - earlier core builds never collected this module's `lib/sitemap.ts`/`lib/robots.ts` at all, see the generator note above). The SEO command centre: unified content inventory (core InfoPages + gazette posts + shop products + directory entries when those modules are installed, detected live from the `Module` table - never a hard import), a ~20-rule on-page analyser with 0-100 scoring and one-click fixes for core pages, a live HTTP crawl audit (manual + weekly cron), admin-managed robots disallow rules and extra sitemap entries (served through the standard `lib/robots.ts`/`lib/sitemap.ts` module hooks), and two Puck blocks for JSON-LD structured data. Zero core changes - integration is entirely existing hook mechanisms.

- Permissions: `seo.view` (dashboard/pages/audit read + run analyser), `seo.manage` (apply fixes, run audits, robots/sitemap rules, settings).
- **`lib/shop-og-image.ts` (v0.1.8, working tree).** `shopCategoriesWithSocialImage(ids | null)` / `shopCollectionsWithSocialImage(ids | null)` return the set of ids whose page actually publishes an og:image, mirroring shop 0.1.267's `lib/catalogue-social-image.ts` chain: `og_image_id`, then the category's `image_url` / the collection's `image_id`, then a photograph off the products the page lists. Replaces the bare `!!og_image_id` in `lib/inventory.ts` (`shopCategories`/`shopCollections`) and `lib/run-analysis.ts` (`loadShopCategories`/`loadShopCollections`) - the same correction `shopProducts` already carried as `!!og_image_id || photo_count > 0`. Raw SQL only, so the module still works with no shop installed; the shop-wide `categoryProductDisplayMode` is read out of the `shp_settings` singleton jsonb (default `'rollup'`, shop's own) so an `'exact'` category cannot borrow a descendant's photograph it never lists. Knowingly coarser than shop in three ways, each commented in the file: ANY listed product rather than shop's first-twelve scan, no out-of-stock hiding (it lives behind shop's code and a request scope), and a dangling `og_image_id` counted as present. On live Deskwell this moves categories and collections from 0/87 to **87/87**. Filter collections are untouched - they store an `og_image` URL that `filters-for-shop` has always emitted.
- Manifest surfaces (**2026-08-10: 4 sidebar links → 1**): one `navEntries` link, "SEO" → `/m/ultimate-seo`, and no `navGroupLabel`. The four screens are now tabs on the page via `components/admin/SeoNav.tsx` (a `TabStrip` of Dashboard / Pages / Site audit / Sitemap & robots, the last gated `seo.manage`), mounted at the top of all four page components. The dashboard sits at the module root so its tab matches the path exactly rather than by prefix - a prefix match there lights up on every other tab. `settingsTabs` → `ultimate-seo` "SEO" tab (`UltimateSeoSettingsTab`); `puckBlocks` → `SeoStructuredData` (Organisation/LocalBusiness/WebSite/custom JSON-LD `<script type="application/ld+json">` in a zero-height wrapper; editor-only `resolveData` pre-fills org fields from saved settings; same sync component both paths so editor/RSC parity is exact) + `SeoFaq` (visible `<details>` accordion + FAQPage JSON-LD); `cronJobs` → `/api/m/ultimate-seo/cron/audit` weekly (`0 4 * * 1`, `CRON_SECRET` bearer).
- Tables (`migrations/001_initial.sql`, all idempotent, all in `teardown`): `seo_settings` (singleton: `organization`/`social`/`targets` jsonb), `seo_page_meta` (per-entity focus keyword + latest analysis, UNIQUE(`entity_type`,`entity_id`); entity types `core-page`/`gazette-post`/`shop-product`/`directory-entry`, no FKs - source tables may not exist on a given install), `seo_audit_runs` + `seo_audit_issues` (FK CASCADE, severity error/warning/notice), `seo_robots_rules`, `seo_sitemap_entries` (NUMERIC priority - Decimal at read time, normalised in the API layer).
- API routes (all `/api/m/ultimate-seo/`, session + permission gated via `lib/auth.ts` `requireSeoPermission`): `admin/overview` GET (dashboard aggregates + hideFromCrawlers/siteStatus), `admin/pages` GET (inventory joined with `seo_page_meta`), `admin/pages/analyze` POST (runs analyser, persists, returns checks + a description suggestion drafted from page copy), `admin/pages/analyze-bulk` POST (`{ items: [{entityType, entityId}] }`, max 100 per request, `seo.view`; one chunk of a site-wide sweep - the client walks the inventory so no request nears the shared 60s module-route ceiling), `admin/pages/apply` POST (core pages only: writes `InfoPage.title`/`metaDescription` columns AND mirrors into `builderData`/`publishedData` `root.props` so the Puck editor and the next publish don't revert the fix; re-analyses in the same request), `admin/settings` GET/PUT (module settings + takes over `SiteConfig.hideFromCrawlers`), `admin/robots` GET/POST + `admin/robots/[id]` DELETE, `admin/sitemap` GET/POST + `admin/sitemap/[id]` DELETE, `admin/audit` GET/POST (POST 409s if a run younger than 10 min is still `running`), `admin/audit/[id]` GET (run + issues), `cron/audit` GET.
- `lib/`: `analyze.ts` (pure rule engine: title/desc length + uniqueness, slug hygiene, H1 count, content depth, image alts, internal links, focus-keyword title/desc/slug/density checks, readability, published status; score = pass 1 / warn 0.5 / fail 0 over check count), `content.ts` (generic Puck-data text extraction - block-palette-agnostic traversal, HTML stripping, heading/link/image-alt harvesting), `inventory.ts` (source collectors behind `Promise.allSettled` so a half-installed module can't 500 the screen), `run-analysis.ts` (entity loaders incl. gazette `builder_data`, shop `description` HTML, directory `description`; loaders take **id arrays** - `loadEntities(entityType, ids)` with `= ANY($1::text[])`, one query per content type, single-page path is the batch of one), `bulk-analysis.ts` (`analyzeBatch()`: dedupes the batch, loads inventory + settings once, batch-loads content, scores in memory, writes back through one multi-row upsert; leaves focus keywords alone), `duplicates.ts` (`DuplicateIndex` - counted title/description index discounting the page's own contribution, so a whole-site sweep is linear not quadratic; unit-tested in `duplicates.test.ts`), `apply.ts` (core-page write-through), `audit.ts` (crawler: URL list from live `/sitemap.xml` with inventory fallback, concurrency 4, 45s time budget → `partial` status, 10s per-fetch timeout, jsdom parse; checks HTTP status, title, meta description, noindex, H1s, img alts, OG tags, canonical, thin content, response time), `sitemap.ts`/`robots.ts` (the standard module hooks serving the admin-managed rows), `settings.ts` (singleton normalise/save), `db.ts` (raw SQL accessors), `auth.ts`, `types.ts`.
- Admin pages (`app/cactus-admin/ultimate-seo/…`): Dashboard (stat cards, hidden-from-crawlers warning banner, quick wins deep-linking `?focus=type:id`, recent audits), Pages (see `lib/page-view.ts`: eight sortable columns with per-column `INITIAL_DIR` and nulls pinned to the bottom in both directions, eight clickable stat tiles, type/status/score-band/issue filters with the issue list derived from the stored `checks` plus synthetic `_unanalysed`/`_stale`, tick-box selection with **Analyse selected** and **Select all *N* matching**, 25/50/100/all pagination, CSV export of the current view, `localStorage`-remembered view state; **Analyse all *N*** bulk sweep over the filtered rows - 25 per request, progress bar, `AbortController`-backed Stop - and a detail side panel: SERP preview, focus keyword, analyse, inline title/description editing with Use-suggestion for core pages, deep links `/m/gazette/posts/:id` / `/m/shop/products/:id` / `/m/directory/entries/:id` for module content; the panel is sticky and capped at `calc(100vh - 2rem)` with its own scroll, since the admin shell scrolls the document), Site audit (run list, expandable per-run issue tables), Sitemap & robots (both rule CRUDs + links to live `/sitemap.xml` `/robots.txt`).
- Module-to-module isolation: reads other modules' tables for analysis only; never writes them, never adds UI to their screens. One-click apply is core-`InfoPage`-only by design.
- Shipped as `cactus-foundation-modules/ultimate-seo`, listed in the core README's Available modules, wiki page at `wiki/Ultimate-SEO.md`.

### Search

Site-wide frontend search over every public content type. Written and **released 2026-08-01**: `cactus-foundation-modules/search` v0.1.0, registered in `modules.json` alongside shop's pin moving to v0.1.156 (core v0.5.828). Plan: `plans/search-module-plan.md`. Manifest: `search`, prefix `srch_`, `publicBasePath: search`, `requiresCoreVersion: 0.5.825`, permissions `search.view`/`search.manage`, one flat nav entry, one settings tab, cron `0 4 * * *`, layout type `searchResults` (starter: box + results; `publishByDefault` from 0.1.18, so a fresh install is seeded a published Results layout - the arrangement `/search` renders by hand anyway when nothing is published, so no visual change either way; before that it was unflagged and an install got no row at all, permanently - see the top entry). Manifest 0.1.18, pinned in `modules.json` to v0.1.18 (core v0.5.1050).

- **Architecture: own index table, never live federated queries.** Body text lives in five differently named Puck JSONB columns across modules; JSONB can't carry a text index and module isolation forbids touching other modules' schemas. `srch_documents` holds extracted plain text + a **plain tsvector column** (NOT generated DDL - the regconfig language is a setting; changing it prompts a rebuild), GIN indexed, weighted title A / excerpt B / body C. `srch_settings` singleton (language allowlisted in `lib/types.ts`, per-source master switches + rank weights, query logging + retention, excerpt length, `last_index_at` high-water mark). `srch_queries` logs query text + result counts only - no IPs, no user ids.
- **Adapters** (`lib/adapters/*`, one per source: `page`, `shop-product`, `shop-category`, `shop-collection`, `gazette-post`, `directory-entry`, `boards-thread`, `member`): raw SQL through the shared prisma client, **never imports from other modules**; each re-implements the source's public-visibility predicate with a comment naming the source of truth (gazette's lazy scheduled-publish window, shop `status='ACTIVE' AND catalogue_hidden=false`, directory `published` + category join for the two-segment URL, boards per-board visibility - PUBLIC indexes as tier `public`, MEMBERS as tier `members`, PRIVATE never indexed; members gated on `directoryEnabled` + site-wide `profileVisibility`, honouring per-member `showBio`). Homepage indexed once as `/` via `SiteConfig.homepageId`. `lib/extract.ts` is a standalone copy of ultimate-seo's block-agnostic Puck text walker (alt text folded in) - deliberately not imported from ultimate-seo.
- **Indexer** (`lib/indexer.ts`): batched (50) + cursored `runIndex` stopping cleanly at ~45s (module routes have the un-overridable 60s ceiling); deletion diff per source against the full current public id set every run (this is also what catches gazette scheduled posts going live and boards visibility flips); only a full pass moves `last_index_at`. Absent/disabled source = its rows are deleted. Nightly cron (incremental + query-log purge, CRON_SECRET-gated) + admin rebuild loop.
- **Query** (`lib/query.ts`): `websearch_to_tsquery` OR'd with a sanitised last-token `:*` prefix query (typeahead), `ts_rank_cd` × per-source weight from settings, `ts_headline` snippets with « » markers (renderers escape text and swap markers for `<mark>` - never HTML), tier `members` only with a session (admin or member cookie), shop sources stripped at query time when `shopStatus='CLOSED'`, and **product prices/stock live-joined per page of hits, never read from the index**. Malformed queries return empty, never 500.
- **API** (`/api/m/search/`): `public/query` (zod-validated, logs first page only when logging on), `public/suggest` (8 hits, never logged), `public/sources` (resolveFields probe: available sources + whether the shop-cards provider is registered), `admin/reindex` POST (cursored batch, `search.manage`), `admin/status`, `admin/queries` (top/zero-result/volume, 30 days), `admin/settings` GET/PUT, `cron/reindex`.
- **Puck blocks** (editor/`.rsc` pairs): `SiteSearch` (Search Box) - behaviour (results on page / inline dropdown / full overlay, min chars, debounce, max results, grouping, `/` or Cmd-K hotkey, autofocus, results path), 8 per-source toggles (resolveFields narrows to installed modules via a 60s-cached `public/sources` fetch; all-on stores as "all enabled" so future sources join automatically), appearance (field / field+button / icon-button-opens-overlay, **size is per-breakpoint** - the desktop value rides the `srch-size-*` class and any breakpoint that differs re-declares `--srch-pad/--srch-font/--srch-icon` in a media rule scoped to `[data-srch-id="<block id>"]`, so a header box can read smaller on phones without touching desktop; `searchSizeStyles()` in `SiteSearchBlock.tsx` is shared by the editor and RSC halves and unit-tested in `searchSizeStyles.test.ts` - corners, field style, accent token, width mode/px/alignment), dropdown (match-field / wide / full-viewport width via the 100vw margin trick - no portals, editor/RSC parity), products as rows or **search-owned card lookalikes** (`ProductCardLite`), thumbnails/excerpts/badges/prices/highlighting, view-all + empty text, and **`audience`** (Who can see this: Everyone / Admins only - key deliberately not `visibility`, which core owns and strips). `SiteSearchResults` - same source toggles, list/grid/compact + columns, per-page, numbered/load-more pagination (load-more is a client island appending via the API; forced numbered in shop-card mode), group-by-type, filter tabs, sort control, thumbnail shape, snippet length, highlight, badges/prices/dates/authors/URLs, heading/count templates, empty state. Both blocks carry **`audience`** (Who can see this: Everyone / Admins only). Reserved-name trap avoided (no `visibility`/`sticky`/`animation*` fields - `audience` is deliberately named around the core field core strips). `/search` page injects `searchQuery`/`searchPageNum`/`searchSort`/`searchSourcesParam` via `lib/inject-search-context.ts` (gazette pattern); no published layout falls back to rendering the starter arrangement directly.
- **Designed shop cards**: new extension point **`search.shop-cards`** - shop (working tree) registers `shopSearchCardProvider` from `modules/shop/lib/search-cards.tsx`, wrapping its own `resolveCardTemplate` → `buildCardContext` → `renderCards` pipeline by product ids in caller (relevance) order, so `productCardStyle: shopCard` on the results block is pixel-identical to the shop grids by construction. Server-side only (the extension registry eagerly imports server libs - **never reference it from a `'use client'` file**); the live dropdown keeps the lookalike cards. Provider absent (shop old or missing) = silent fallback to standard cards and resolveFields hides the option. **The shop half needs a shop module release + pin bump to ship.**
- Client-boundary discipline: only display-subset config objects cross to `'use client'` islands (`SearchBoxClient`, `LoadMoreButton`); `lib/db/client-bundle.test.ts` caught the settings-tab → `lib/settings` → prisma taint, fixed by moving `ALLOWED_LANGUAGES` into database-free `lib/types.ts`.
- `lib/robots.ts` disallows `/search`; no sitemap entries; the page sets `robots: noindex`.
- v0.1.1 (same day): `navGroupLabel: Search` (the unlabelled module bucket renders headerless beside the sidebar's Recents and reads as part of it), `SiteSearch` gains `layoutTypes: [header, searchResults]` (footer palette takes no module blocks), and an empty index raises a dedupe-keyed admin bell notification (`lib/alerts.ts`, `search:index-empty`) linking to the dashboard, which auto-starts the first build on arrival; synced from status/reindex/cron/sources routes and empty first-page queries. Pinned in core v0.5.829.
- v0.1.5: both blocks gain the `audience` field ('everyone' | 'admin'). Gates live entirely in the `.rsc` halves (`getSessionFromCookie()` → `null` for the public); editor halves stay client-safe and always preview. `SiteSearchBlock.rsc` calls `connection()` only on the admin branch, so the `everyone` default stays cacheable; `SiteSearchResultsBlock.rsc` already called `connection()` unconditionally, and its gate sits above all index work (session lookup is React-`cache`d, so the members-tier read below reuses it). Mirrors shop's `ShopCartSummary` audience gate. Gates blocks only - `/search` and `/api/m/search/public/*` stay reachable, so it is "not announced yet", not access control.
- Released 2026-08-01: repo + `v0.1.0` prerelease, `modules.json` entry, README module list, shop provider in shop v0.1.156 (both pins moved together in core v0.5.828), wiki `Search.md` pushed to both trackers.
- **New extension point `search.shop-product-text` (v0.1.15, working tree):** the shop adapter (`lib/adapters/shop.ts`) only ever read what shop's own `shp_products` row holds, so a companion module's data - shop-variations' hidden-child SKUs, in particular - never reached the index and a customer searching a variation code off their paperwork found nothing. `lib/shop-product-text.ts` mirrors `shop.product-card-prices`'s resolution shape exactly: `ShopProductTextProvider = { textFor(productIds): Promise<Record<string,string>>, changedSince(since): Promise<string[]> }`, resolved through the generated registry (never a static import - a build with no shop-variations must still compile), a throwing provider contributes nothing rather than emptying the batch. `resolveShopProductText` folds every provider's text (space-joined) into the product document's `body`, ahead of the description (short and precise beats a 100k-char truncation point). `listChangedSince` now unions shop's own `updated_at` diff with `resolveShopProductTextChanges(since)`, so a parent whose ONLY change was a variation's code still gets re-indexed on an incremental run - without this a code added after the last full rebuild would never become searchable until the next full one. First (and so far only) consumer: `shop-variations` v0.1.122.

### Space Planner for Shop

Module `space-planner-for-shop`, tablePrefix `spl_`, **v0.1.23** (released; repo `cactus-foundation-modules/space-planner-for-shop`). Core `modules.json` pins **v0.1.23**. **v0.1.1 was tagged from a mid-pass snapshot** by another session and does NOT contain the room-shape editor, the 3D wall culling, the wall-snap fix or opening a saved plan - never pin it. `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.940`; `requiresModules` shop >= 0.1.192 (the member-cart release - the planner writes the basket through shop's own utility and must not lose its cross-device sync), product-3d-views-for-shop >= 0.1.82, shop-variations >= 0.1.107, quote-for-shop >= 0.1.8. `publicBasePath: space-planner`. Now **pinned in core's `modules.json`** so the generators wire it into a local build; the live install adopts a release when the owner chooses. Built to `plans/space-planner-plan.md`.

- **`adminOnly` (default true) is the master switch**, gated through `lib/visibility.ts` - `plannerVisible()` on every storefront surface and `plannerHiddenResponse()` (404) on the data routes, with `requireMember()` carrying the whole member API. Cookie read only while the switch is on; the Puck teaser checks the setting without a session on purpose (prerendered pages); shared plans and the render page are exempt. Full reasoning in the top Last-updated entry.
- **Zero core diffs, and no new npm dependency.** Routes, cron, email templates, permissions, settings tab, Puck blocks, extension points, member extensions and the public pages all declare in `cactus.module.json`. three/draco/meshoptimizer already exist at the core root; polygon triangulation with holes comes from three's own `ShapeGeometry`/`Path` (earcut is inside three), 3D labels are canvas sprites, and the floor plan is a print stylesheet.
- **Tables** (`migrations/001_initial.sql`, applied by hand to live Deskwell 2026-08-04 at the owner's request, additive-only, idempotent, re-run verified clean): `spl_settings` (singleton config jsonb), `spl_rooms` (member-owned geometry; `owner_user_id` exists and stays null, keeping the owner-revises-a-plan loop open; CHECK enforces exactly one owner), `spl_plans` (FK -> rooms ON DELETE CASCADE, the only FK in the schema because both ends are ours; `share_token` UNIQUE and **null until shared**; `product_snapshot` jsonb), `spl_plan_versions`, `spl_model_meta` (split-scope file/product with a stated precedence), `spl_category_defaults`, `spl_dimension_cache`, `spl_backfill_jobs`, `spl_render_jobs`, `spl_events`. No enums, no arrays, no sequences - TEXT+CHECK, INTEGER, BOOLEAN, JSONB, TIMESTAMP(3) only. Rollback SQL in the session scratchpad (`spl-rollback.sql`); it names only `spl_` tables. **`migrations/002_render_worker.sql`** (v0.1.4, working tree, NOT applied anywhere) adds `spl_render_worker` and `spl_render_jobs.machine_id`; same type discipline, so the backup serialiser needs nothing new. **`migrations/003_room_views.sql`** (v0.1.8, working tree, NOT applied anywhere) adds `spl_room_views` (TEXT / INTEGER / JSONB / TIMESTAMP(3), FK -> `spl_rooms` ON DELETE CASCADE, no ownership column - the room is the authority), and is listed in `teardown` **before** `spl_rooms`. Backup round-trip re-run on it: 3 passed, no skips.
- **The picture is no longer the preview at a larger size (0.1.8).** For four versions it was, and two things that were supposed to prevent that did nothing at all: `RenderFrame` set `shadowMap.enabled` over a scene where **no light had `castShadow` and no mesh had `castShadow`/`receiveShadow`**, and the header comment at `planner-scene.ts:46` claimed procedural room lighting that was never wired - `scene.environment` was never assigned, which is the single biggest reason standard materials read as plastic. `dressForRender()` (planner-scene, called from `RenderFrame` **only** - the live view is a thing dragged about on a phone and wants none of it) now does three things: `RoomEnvironment` -> `PMREMGenerator` -> `scene.environment` at 0.85, with ambient 0.85 -> 0.22 and fill 0.45 -> 0.3 so the corners are not washed out twice; the key light **moved out of the room** (its fixed `(4, 8, 6)` is inside anything over ~8 m, so it was a lamp on the carpet) with an orthographic shadow camera fitted to the room bounds, 4096 map, `normalBias 0.02` because the room is large flat planes at a shallow angle; and per-mesh shadow flags, floor receiving only. It returns a dispose for the PMREM target, which is a GPU allocation the scene does not collect. `GTAOPass` + `OutputPass` on an `EffectComposer` are built in `RenderFrame` behind a **dynamic import** (40 KB the 3D view has no use for) and behind try/catch - a failed composer still gives a lit, shadowed room rather than an error page on a machine already billed. `OutputPass` is what applies ACES and sRGB, because a composer's intermediate targets are linear and untoned. All four modules ship inside three 0.180, so **no npm dependency and no core release**.
- **The chrome was in every photograph, and it is an architecture fact rather than a slip (0.1.8).** Module public pages hang off the core public catch-all, so the render page renders inside `app/(public)/layout.tsx` - site header, footer, and the consent banner, which always fires because the worker's browser is new and has consented to nothing. The page's own comment claimed "no chrome, no controls" and had been wrong since it was written. There is no full-screen opt-out in the router, so the page emits a **server-rendered** `BLANKING_CSS` (`body > *:not(main)`, blunt on purpose - the public layout returns a fragment, so header, footer, banner and anything Next appends are all direct body children). Server-rendered rather than applied on mount because the worker screenshots the moment `__splRenderReady` goes true.
- **The picture is taken from where the shopper is standing (0.1.8).** `eyeLevel()` ignored them completely and `SceneDescription` had no camera field. New `SavedCamera` type - position, target, fov, projection, zoom, in world **metres**, the only thing in this module that is not millimetres, because it describes the three.js scene and is written and read by the viewer alone. It rides on `spl_render_jobs.params.camera` (jsonb, no migration), is validated by `SavedCameraSchema` on the way in and again on the way out, and an absent or unparseable one falls back to `eyeLevel()` rather than refusing to draw. `readCamera`/`applyCamera` take the OrbitControls **target** rather than deriving one: a camera knows its direction, not how far away the thing it is pointing at is, and inventing a distance is what silently decides how far one scroll notch zooms after a restore. The photo dialog offers where-I-am-now / the canned wall standpoint / any saved view.
- **Saved views are ROOM-scoped (0.1.8), `spl_room_views`.** A camera pose is expressed in room coordinates: meaningless anywhere else, identical for every layout in one room - so "Option A from the doorway" and "Option B from the doorway" are two pictures from one view, which is the plan-comparison behaviour §the plan doc wanted. 12 per room, capped in the route as well as the UI. `lib/db/room-views.ts` takes **no member id anywhere**: the table has no ownership column, so every handler proves the room with `getRoomForMember` first and that IS the access check - a second copy of that answer is what drifts, always permissively. `position` is computed inside the INSERT so two tabs cannot both decide they are number three. A stored camera that will not parse is **dropped from the list** rather than offered, because a reshaped room can leave a pose describing nowhere and a button that yields a black picture is worse than no button. Views are in the GDPR export, gathered per room.
- **Eye height (0.1.8).** A vertical slider (`writing-mode: vertical-lr`, which keeps it a real range control with real arrow-key behaviour where a rotate transform leaves the hit area on its side) with Sitting/Standing presets, labelled in the room's units; **Alt+wheel** and PageUp/PageDown as accelerators. The slider is primary deliberately: a modifier key nobody is told about is a feature nobody has, phones have no key to hold, and somebody changing their height wants to know what height they reached. `setEyeHeight` moves the camera **and the orbit target together**, so the horizon holds - moving the camera alone is a pitch control, and that is already the left mouse button. The wheel listener is on the wrapper in the **capture** phase because OrbitControls owns the wheel on the canvas and treats it as zoom; a listener alongside theirs is a coin toss on registration order. The slider's value is mirrored into React and re-synced on OrbitControls `'end'` (not `'change'`, which fires every damped frame) because orbiting up and down is itself a change of height.
- **The photoreal render had no trigger until 0.1.7** (released, pinned in core `modules.json`). Every server-side part shipped in 0.1.4 - `POST/GET /member/plans/[id]/render`, the Fly machine-per-picture dispatch, the `/space-planner/render/[id]` worker page, the callback, the admin Renders screen - and no client code ever called any of it, in any commit on any branch. Deskwell had `rendersEnabled: true` and a provisioned worker (`spl-render-58ba3442`) with **0 rows in `spl_render_jobs`**. 0.1.7 adds the trigger: `SpacePlannerProps.rendersAvailable` (computed in `app/public/space-planner/page.tsx` as `config.rendersEnabled && await renderWorkerConfigured()` - switched on and wired up are different things, and a button that answers "not set up on this site yet" is worse than none), a **Make a photo** button beside Export PDF in the toolbar (`spl-secondary`, so it collapses behind **More** on a phone), and `PhotoDialog` in `SpacePlanner.tsx`. The dialog polls rather than holds a request open: 4s interval, only while a QUEUED/RUNNING job exists, re-armed by a `tick` counter so one dropped poll does not end it, and a "taking longer than usual" note past 4 minutes. Two lint rules shaped it - `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` forbids the obvious `setSlow(false)` at the top of the timer effect, and `react-hooks/purity` forbids `Date.now()` during render, so the slow flag is computed from the live job's `createdAt` **inside the poll callback**, which is the clock anyway. Every ask calls `savePlan({ quiet: true })` first, not just the first: the picture is built server-side from the saved layout, so a desk moved after the dialog opened would otherwise be photographed where it used to be. Opening the dialog does NOT save - a plan that was never saved has no pictures by definition. `stale`/`depicts` from the GET label an out-of-date picture with the date it shows. Styles are `.spl-dialog-wide` / `.spl-photo*` in `planner-css.ts`, tokens only, capped to the stage with `max-height: 100%` + scroll.
- **The side panel's tabs did nothing at all for four versions (0.1.14).** `hidden={activeTab !== 'catalogue'}` on the catalogue tabpanel was inert: the UA stylesheet's `[hidden] { display: none }` is user-agent origin, so ANY author `display:` on the same element wins whatever the specificity - and `.spl-stack { display: grid }` (planner-css.ts:199) was on that very div. Proven on live before touching anything: `hidden` true, `getComputedStyle().display` `grid`, catalogue 5,878px tall, `#spl-panel-items` at y=6597 inside a 190px scroll box. So Selected, Item list and Cart rendered thousands of pixels below the fold and clicking a tab looked like a dead button. Fixed with one rule, `.spl-root [hidden] { display: none !important; }` - `!important` on purpose, so the next `display:` somebody adds to a panel class cannot bring it back. Re-verified by injecting the rule into the live page: one panel visible per tab, each at offset 0.
- **The room's name is on screen and editable (0.1.14).** `roomName` had a `useState` with no setter and was never rendered - it reached the shopper only as a PDF filename. Now under the heading in `.spl-bar-heading` with a pencil button, edited in place (`namingRoom` + a `nameAbandoned` ref so Escape-then-blur does not commit the abandoned text). `renameRoom` PUTs `/member/rooms/[id]` with `{ name, geometry }` and **no `notes`** - the route treats an absent one as "leave it alone", where `savePlan`'s `notes: ''` clears it. Only when `roomIdRef.current` is set: an unsaved room has nowhere to write to, so the name just travels with the first save.
- **Saved rooms are offered on the opening screen (0.1.14).** New `SavedRoomLink[]` prop, built in `app/public/space-planner/page.tsx` by `loadSavedRooms()` - `listRoomsForMember` + one `listPlansForMember` grouped in memory (not a query per room), capped at 6, each pointing at the room's most recently worked-on plan. Skipped entirely when `openPlan` is set or nobody is signed in, so the common paths cost nothing. Rows link to `?plan=` / `?room=` on the **same route**, which is why `SpacePlanner` is now `key`ed on `openPlan?.planId ?? openPlan?.roomId ?? 'new'`: names, save ids and history are first-render state, so a soft navigation between two saved rooms would otherwise draw the new room under the old one's name and save over the old one's layout. That was a latent bug the moment any same-route link existed.
- **Furniture could not be overlapped, and it was the SNAP doing it (0.1.14).** There is no collision rule in this module - `findClashes` warns and never blocks, `clampItemIntoRoom` only holds the outline - so "the model stops when it hits another model" was `snapToItems`' two FACE offers (`box.minX - halfWidth` / `box.maxX + halfWidth`, `ITEM_SNAP_MM` 150). Push a chair past a desk's front edge and the face offer sits a few centimetres away, inside tolerance, and ejects the chair back to flush on every pointer event - so a chair could never get more than the snap radius in, for ever. `movingAwayFromItems` is no escape either: `nearestItemGapMm` returns 0 for overlapping, so pushing in reads as from-0-to-0 and never counts as moving away. Fix is one predicate, `const apart = gapX > 0 || gapY > 0`, gating **only** the two face offers - the far-edge and centre alignments stay on, because centring the chair under the desk is the other half of what the shopper is doing. Approach from outside and it still clicks flush (bank-of-desks unaffected); drive past and the tool gets out of the way. Three tests in `geometry.test.ts`, and the middle one was **verified to fail without the guard** (`expected 2225 to be 2125`) - the first draft of it used a 200mm overlap, which is outside the 150mm radius, so no offer fired either way and it proved nothing.
- **A placed column was inert scenery (0.1.14).** `Plan2d`'s obstruction hit-test lived entirely inside `if (props.mode === 'obstructions')`, so in the ordinary `furnish` mode a column could not be clicked, dragged or removed - the only way back to one was Room -> Columns & pillars. Now hit-tested in `furnish` too, **after** `hitTest` misses: a desk over a column wins the click, since the desk is what is being arranged. Picking one clears the item selection and vice versa - the two are never both the thing being edited. The toolbar branch is now `planMode === 'obstructions' || (planMode === 'furnish' && obstructionSelection)`, written out rather than `|| obstructionSelection` so a leftover selection cannot hijack the shape or drawing bars; the plan's highlight is gated the same way. Escape clears the selection (the bar takes the toolbar over while one is picked, so there has to be a way out) and Delete removes the column - placed **before** the `state.selection.length === 0` bail, because picking a column empties that.
- **The size ladder** (`lib/resolve-dimensions.ts`, cached in `spl_dimension_cache`): measured model -> parsed spec attributes -> category default -> typed by hand -> labelled block. Nothing guesses: an unreadable value goes to the junk tail on the Sizes screen **with its actual text**. Rung 1 is written by the **Measure** pass on the Sizes screen (0.1.6) - `GET/POST /admin/dimensions/measure` + `applyMeasurements()`, measured in the admin's browser because a route has 60s and a model averages 4MB - and a cached `glb`/`manual` row is never overwritten by a spec edit, nor a `manual` one by a measurement; the attribute rung still runs regardless, because it is what recomputes the disagreement flag. Rung 2 reads the **child's values then its listing's, child first** (0.1.6): in this catalogue a listing states its dimensions once and its colours state only their colour. Model vs spec disagreement over 10% on any axis sets `conflict` rather than resolving it. Freshness is three-layered (plan-load spot check on `updated_at` plus `parentMovedSince()` against `resolved_at`, bounded nightly sweep, admin rebuild) because catalogue edits arrive by sheet Pull and fire no save event.
- **`lib/three/planner-model.ts` is the file to read first if rooms ever look convincingly wrong.** p3d's loader ends in `frameModel()`, which normalises every model to a 2-unit longest side - right for a product viewer, fatal here. The planner takes the **pre-normalisation** world bounding box (`Box3.setFromObject(object, true)`, node transforms applied), grounds to y=0, recentres, applies the per-file yaw offset, and never calls `frameModel`. The `true` is **precise**, added in the working tree after 0.1.8 for the same reason p3d 0.1.84 added it to AR: the cheap form transforms the eight corners of each mesh's local box and reads an off-axis part up to 30% large, which cancelled while this number was only compared with the plan's and does not cancel now the recorded real size is divided by it. Paid once per file, before decimation, cached with the prepared model.
- **Decimation is off below 30,000 triangles and pins the border above it** (`DECIMATION_FLOOR_TRIANGLES` + the `['LockBorder']` flag on `simplify()`, working tree after 0.1.10). A glTF loader splits one mesh into one geometry per material, so parts finished differently arrive as separate geometries **sharing a rim**; simplified independently, the two ends of that rim move by different amounts and come apart. `target_error` is a fraction of the mesh extent, not an absolute, so `0.01` on a 2.4 m table permits ~24 mm - larger than the feature it destroyed. The per-file `no_decimation` tick still wins over both.
- **Budgets are per unique model, with instancing** - a 20-desk bank is one download, one parse, one crunch and 20 transforms. `maxUniqueModels` (default 14) caps distinct files; placed items are capped separately at 200 by `maxItemsPerPlan`. Prepared models are cached **in memory only**; persisting the crunched result to IndexedDB is named in the README as not-in-this-build. From 0.1.6 the instancing key is **file plus paints** (`instanceKey()`, `ResolvedModel.fabricKey`): the download, parse, crunch and measurement stay per file and shared across colours, and only the materials are per colour - `paintedModel()` clones the materials named in the slots before painting them, because three.js clones share materials by reference and the shared prepared model must not be repainted.
- **The recorded real size outranks the plan** (`realSizeScale()` in `lib/three/model-scale.ts`, working tree after 0.1.8): where p3d's material setup has a real overall size for the variation (`FabricBundle.realCm` along `scaleAxis`), the model is scaled **uniformly** to it and the plan's figures are not consulted at all. Carried as `realMetres`/`realAxis` on `PlannerModel` -> `ClientModel` -> `SceneModelSource`, cm converted to metres once in `lib/model-resolver.ts`. Read in `buildItems` **per node's `productId`**, never off the deduped `bySource` entry - that map is keyed file-plus-paints, so two seat heights of one chair in one fabric share an entry and would otherwise share a height. Guarded to 0.02-20 m, so a units slip ("1110" read as metres) falls back rather than putting a building in the room. Live coverage: 138 of 213 modelled listings have a config, all with a size source set, 137 on the height axis and 1 on width; the other 75 keep the reconciliation below.
- **Fitting the mesh to the plan's size** (`lib/three/model-scale.ts`, 0.1.6, pure + tested) - now the FALLBACK, for a product with no recorded real size: an axis ratio outside 0.4-2.5 is treated as a data fault and dropped; an `approximate` size (category default or marker) never deforms a real mesh; axis ratios disagreeing with each other by more than 1.5x fall back to a uniform fit. Per-axis stretch survives below those thresholds on purpose - this catalogue's suppliers widen a desk by sliding its ends apart, so one model legitimately serves several widths.
- **What the red outline means** (`itemsFight` -> `tucksUnder`/`spaceUnderneathMm` in `lib/geometry.ts`, revised in the working tree after 0.1.8): overlapping footprints plus overlapping height bands, MINUS the arrangements people are aiming for. A pair is legitimate when the lower one has space beneath it - published `Height Under Top`, else height 600-1100 **and** width >= 800 **and** depth >= 550 - and the upper one is not itself a worktop, is under 1500 tall, and fits the published clear width. There is deliberately no depth comparison between the two: chairs are 640-690 deep, half these desks are 600, and requiring the chair to be shallower painted the commonest arrangement in the catalogue red. Warns, never blocks - and `PlanItem.parentId` is honoured by the clash and snap code but is still set by nothing, so there is no "these two belong together" escape hatch in the UI.
- **The browse panel places a VARIATION, not a listing** (`components/public/VariationPicker.tsx` + `POST /public/variations`, working tree after 0.1.8). A card with `hasVariations` opens the picker instead of placing anything; the picker is shop-variations' own payload and its own selection maths, trimmed of add-ons and gallery, and it looks the chosen child's real size up through `/public/products` before placing so the panel and the room cannot disagree. Falls back to placing the listing when a family turns out to have no options left. The old behaviour is why a listing's `category_default` size mattered so much: it was what got placed.
- **Placeholders are the main path**, not the fallback: ~19 listings in 20 carry no model, so a clean box at the ladder size with the product photo on its front and a canvas-sprite name label is what this mostly draws. A GLB fetch/parse failure degrades to the same box, badged, never an error page.
- **Ownership lives in the WHERE clause** (`lib/db/rooms.ts`, `lib/db/plans.ts`): there is no function that reads a room or plan without being told whose it is, except `getPlanByShareToken`, which takes a secret instead of an id (192-bit token, constant-time compared, robots-disallowed page).
- **Saving requires a member account** - guests get the whole tool with their scratch room in localStorage (`lib/client/scratch.ts`). That deletes `client_id`, guest retention sweeps, adoption reconciliation and every unauthenticated write endpoint.
- **Routes**: member `rooms` / `rooms/[id]` (PUT re-validates every plan in the room and moves displaced items to that plan's **staging tray**, archiving a version first - never deletes) / `rooms/[id]/plans` / `plans/[id]` / `.../versions` / `.../share` / `.../bom` / `.../quote` / `.../email` / `.../render`, plus `member/gdpr-export` (internal bearer). Public: `public/catalogue`, `public/products` (POST - a plan can name 200 ids), `public/render-callback` (per-job token, not a deployment secret). Admin: `admin/settings`, `admin/plans[/id]`, `admin/dimensions[/rebuild]`, `admin/models`, `admin/renders`. Cron `cron/sweep` (`20 3 * * *`): bounded dimension refresh, **orphaned-dimension delete** (`spl_dimension_cache.product_id` has no FK to `shp_products` - the shop owns that table - so stranded rows are swept actively; unswept they inflate the dimension report, which counts rows not products), event purge, **orphaned-room delete** (core owns `Member`, no FK, so deletion is handled actively), stale render ageing.
- **The rebuild is resumable** (`lib/backfill-run.ts`): job row banking a cursor, `STEP_TIME_BUDGET_MS` 25s, 100-product chunks, deterministic `ORDER BY id`, cancel checked every chunk, and the admin screen loops the endpoint and draws the bar. Copied from `google-sheet-products-for-shop`'s pull-run shape rather than rediscovered.
- **Quotes ride quote-for-shop** - no quote table here. `lib/quote.ts` calls that module's exported `buildQuoteSnapshot` / `createQuote` / `sendQuoteRequestAck` / `sendQuoteAlertToOwner` directly, so the plan-quote assumption in the plan (§18.1) resolved with **no quote-for-shop release needed**. Only `spl_plans.quote_id` is planner-side state.
- **Extension points implemented**: `shop.cart-header-actions` (third control in that row, hidden on an empty basket), `members.account-section` + `members.account-nav` ("My spaces", contributed only when something is saved), `core.admin-dashboard-widgets`, `core.media-usage-providers`, `core.media-reference-rewriters`. **`shop.product-detail-parts` is deliberately NOT claimed** - it is a slot-REPLACEMENT contract already claimed by shop-variations, and a second provider there is how a page ends up with two option pickers. The product-page button is a Puck block instead (`SpacePlannerProductButton`, layouts `shopProductDetail`/`shopProduct`), which resolves its product from the address bar at click time because shop's `injectProductContext` fills a hard-coded list of block types that is shop's to change, not ours.
- **Delivery dates** are wired to a `shop.delivery-estimates` extension point read out of the generated registry by name (`lib/delivery.ts`) - never a build-time import, since advanced-shipping is optional and that path does not exist on an install without it. It publishes no such point yet, so the column simply does not appear.
- **Emails**: `space-planner.plan-emailed` (transactional) and `space-planner.render-done` (non-transactional, with a `space-planner.render` notification category - the module's single declaration is what lights up the member Notifications tab, which core hides until some module contributes one). Sent through `sendTemplateEmail` with the preference check done in `lib/email.ts`, because core's `sendMemberEmail` takes a closed union of core template keys.
- **0.1.1 - the planner became usable rather than merely complete.** Load-bearing changes, each of which was a real defect:
  - **The workspace has a definite height** (`components/public/planner-css.ts`). It had none, so the browse panel - a catalogue page two dozen cards long - set the row height, the plan canvas stretched to match and the page ran to ~7,800 px with the room drawn postage-stamp size in the middle. Now `height: calc(100dvh - chrome)`, both panes scroll themselves, and the first-run screen opts out with `.spl-root-intro` so it does not prop open an empty viewport.
  - **`Plan2d` fit was fighting a ResizeObserver.** The user's zoom was recovered by dividing current scale by fit scale, and the observer fires the moment you observe - before the render carrying the new scale lands - so it read the pair mid-flight and clamped the room to a quarter size. Zoom is now its own ref.
  - **Clicking bare floor always opened the wall-length prompt**: the tolerance was `400 / view.scale`, i.e. ~5 m of room, not 400 mm. Now `WALL_HIT_PX / scale`, and the prompt is a proper dialog rather than `window.prompt`.
  - **The 3D view could not be moved.** No controls at all - a fixed camera reads as a rendering fault. `OrbitControls` (inside the three package, so no new dependency), damped, floor-limited, and re-framed only on a change of ROOM (`roomSignature`), never on moving the furniture.
  - **The 3D view was a closed crate.** `updateWallVisibility()` hides each wall whose outward normal faces the camera, per frame - the dolls-house effect. `frameRoom` now answers both fields of view (a distance derived from the vertical FOV alone is hopelessly wrong on a phone's aspect), `eyeLevel` stands at the end of the longest wall instead of in the middle of the furniture, and labels are `sizeAttenuation: false` so a name tag is not the size of a doormat up close. `disposeGroup` no longer disposes sprite geometry - three shares ONE geometry across every sprite, so that took every future label with it.
  - **Prices read £0.00** for any listing priced through its variations. Both the browse panel (`lib/catalogue.ts`) and `/public/products` now go through shop's own `resolveCardFromPrices`, with the "From " prefix only where the range genuinely varies.
  - **A "3D" badge could still draw a plain box**: `resolveModelsForProducts` asked only about the listing, while the badge counts a listing as modelled when any of its children is. It now falls back to a child's model, re-keyed onto the listing, in two set-wide queries.
  - **Placing from the browse panel never fetched the model.** `place()` pre-populated `products` from the card, so the missing-products effect had nothing to fetch. It now asks for the product explicitly.
  - **`stageProductId` was accepted and ignored**, so the product page's "See it in your room" staged nothing.
  - Everything lands in the first free spot (`findFreeSpot`) instead of stacking dead centre; `set-wall-length` translates the furniture with the origin instead of letting the room drift out from under it; Redo, a Room dialog, a dismissible message, a print sheet with the item list, `useId` on the number fields, and a phone toolbar that folds Room/Undo/Redo/Print behind **More**.
  - **AA in light and dark, measured**: `--color-text-muted` is #b0a896 on this theme, about 2.4:1 on white. The planner mixes its own `--spl-muted` from the theme's text and background, and the canvas fades the ink rather than reading that token. Nine text roles measured in both schemes, all pass.
- **Furniture welded to walls (0.1.2 fix).** `snapToWall` runs on every pointer event, and a drag arrives as a stream of them a few pixels apart - so an item already flush against a wall had every small step away from it undone by the very next snap, and no amount of dragging could accumulate the 250 mm needed to escape. `move-items` now skips the snap for a step that INCREASES the distance to the nearest wall (`movingAwayFromWall`): snapping pulls an item in and never pulls it back, and dragging towards a wall snaps exactly as before. Two reducer tests pin both halves.
- **Opening something already saved (0.1.2).** `/space-planner/spaces` rows are links: a layout to `?plan=<id>`, a room to `?room=<id>` for a fresh layout in an already-measured space. The planner page loads either **server-side** (`loadOpenPlan`, ownership enforced by the query - neither `getPlanForMember` nor `getRoomForMember` has a form that does not take a member id) and hands it in as the `openPlan` prop, so the room is on screen at first paint instead of flashing the first-run screen at somebody who has plainly been past it. The plan's own name and its room's name travel with it and are used on save - saving over "Ground floor, east wing" and calling it "My space" would be a small theft - and scratch localStorage is not written while a saved plan is open, or "continue where you left off" would resurrect it as unsaved work.
- **"Start the room again" is on the toolbar (0.1.2)**, not two dialogs deep, with a confirmation that says what survives (the room goes, the furniture is kept and put back). `set-geometry` now stages anything the new outline no longer contains, which is what makes that promise true when the new room is smaller.
- **Rooms of any number of walls (0.1.2).** `Plan2d` has a `mode`: **furnish** (default), **shape** (drag corners, double-tap a wall to split it, remove a corner) and **draw** (tap out an outline from scratch, walls snapping to 45s and writing their own length as they go). Reached from the first-run screen and from **Room**. One reducer action, `set-shape`, with a `settle` flag: mid-gesture the vertices are taken exactly as given - re-winding renumbers the corner under the finger and re-originning slides the room out from under it - and on release the outline is wound, re-originned, the furniture is translated by the same delta, and anything now outside the walls is moved to the staging tray rather than left outside. A self-intersecting outline is refused on release and the previous one restored. On narrow screens the browse panel is hidden while either editing mode is on (`.spl-body-editing`), because half a screen is not enough to tap out an office.
  - **CSS trap worth remembering**: media queries add no specificity, so the narrow-screen block now sits at the END of the stylesheet. Written above an equally specific base rule it loses to it, which is how the phone overflow toggle ended up hidden on the one screen it exists for.
- **Bug-hunt pass, module v0.1.3 (2026-08-04).** Whole-module read, every finding fixed; no schema change, so no migration and no backup-gate trigger.
  - **Three in the 3D pipeline, each one silent.** (a) `disposeGroup` walked clones of cached prepared models and disposed their geometry and materials - `Object3D.clone` shares BOTH by reference, so tearing down the items group (which happens on every change to the room) freed the geometry the next rebuild was about to draw with. It now walks by hand and skips any subtree flagged `userData.sharedModel`, which `buildItems` sets.
