(b) `buildItems` set `position`/`rotation.y` **on the clone**, overwriting the recentre-and-ground transform that is the entire point of `prepareModel` - so every GLB stood wherever its exporter put the origin. The clone now goes inside a holder Group and the holder is what gets placed and scaled. (c) `prepareModel` measured before applying the file's yaw offset, and the local matrix is translate-then-rotate, so a non-zero offset broke the recentre; it now zeroes the position, applies the yaw, then measures.
  - **The per-file fix-ups reached nothing.** `SpacePlanner` hard-coded `yawOffsetDeg: 0`/`noDecimation: false` into every `ResolvedModel` and `buildItems` passed one scene-wide `PrepareOptions` to every file - so the admin's "turn it" and "leave the detail alone" controls had no effect on anything. Both now travel per model from `/public/products` (which was already sending them).
  - **`downscaleTextures` was a no-op** - it set a `userData` hint and trusted three to act on it, which three does not. `textureMaxPx` was a setting with no consequence. It now resamples through a canvas.
  - **A WebGL context restore left the view stuck** on "Putting the room together" for ever: the handler set the busy flag, rebuilt nothing, and replaced the scene handles so the room and item groups were orphaned. It now bumps a nonce the build effect depends on.
  - **A runaway request loop.** The missing-products effect keyed on `products`, and `fetchProducts` replaced that object even when the reply carried nothing - so one product a plan references but the catalogue will not answer for (deleted, hidden) meant an unbounded stream of POSTs. An `askedFor` ref makes it once per id, and only failed requests go back in the queue.
  - **Undo after a drag did nothing.** The history snapshot was banked on `onDragEnd`, i.e. AFTER the move, so the first undo restored the state the drag had just produced. New `onDragStart` prop banks it at the start; `onDragEnd` now only marks the plan dirty.
  - **A refused room stayed on screen.** Shape edits never banked an undo step, so the self-intersecting-outline refusal called `undo()` on either nothing or something unrelated and the folded outline stayed. `applyShape` now keeps the pre-gesture geometry in a ref and puts it back itself.
  - **Wheel zoom scrolled the page** - React registers `wheel` at the root as passive, so `preventDefault` from a JSX `onWheel` is ignored. Now a hand-registered non-passive listener.
  - **The plan re-fitted mid-drag**: the fit effect keys on the room and a corner drag changes the room on every pointer event, so the view recentred and the canvas was resized (and cleared) between them. Skipped while `cornerDragRef` is set.
  - **Quote expiry was doubled** - `config.expiryDays * 2 * 86_400_000` in `lib/quote.ts`, so every plan quote claimed twice the validity the quote module says it has, on the quote module's own document.
  - **A failed render dispatch locked the plan out of pictures.** The job was created, the worker POST failed, and the QUEUED row counted as live under "one live job per plan" until the nightly sweep aged it out. The route now fails the job before answering.
  - **`upsertFileMeta`/`upsertProductMeta` clobbered fields not in the patch** - and the admin screen sends one field at a time, so setting a yaw offset cleared the "checked" mark and marking checked cleared the footprint override. `CASE WHEN <absent> THEN existing` per field.
  - **`{{#if stale}}` never fired**: core's conditional compares against the literal string `'true'` and `sendRenderDoneEmail` passed `'yes'`, so the "this is the room as it was on the fourth" line has never been sent. `stale` was also missing from `mergeTags`.
  - **`hideWhenCartEmpty` never hid anything.** `subscribeCart` does not fire on subscribe, so the state only settled when the basket next changed - which on an empty basket it does not. Reads once as well now.
  - **A dead line in the size ladder**: `if (source === 'attribute' && usedDefault) source = 'attribute'`. A desk with a parsed width and a guessed depth was badged as measured, against the module's own "never a silent guess" rule. Now demotes to `category_default`.
- **Snapping, turning, doors and windows, PDF (same pass, v0.1.3).**
  - **Furniture snaps to furniture** (`snapToItems`, `nearestItemGapMm` in `lib/geometry.ts`). Each axis takes the nearest of five offers from every square-on neighbour - two that put the faces together, two that line the far edges up, one that lines the centres up - and a neighbour only gets a say on an axis when it is beside the item on the other one. Works in the dragged item's own frame, so a neighbour at a quarter turn snaps on its real footprint. Same escape as the wall snap (`movingAwayFromItems`) and the same alt-key override.
  - **A turn handle on the selected item** in `Plan2d`, fixed in screen pixels off the front edge, 15° steps unless alt is held. The delta is measured against what the gesture has already applied rather than against the item's current angle, because state arrives a render later than the pointer does. `rotate-items` now brings children round about the parent's centre, by the delta the parent ACTUALLY turned (snapping rounds it), and the "Turn 90°" button goes through the same action.
  - **Clash warnings understand furniture.** A chair pushed under a desk overlaps in plan and in height, so the height-band test painted the arrangement people were aiming for red. New `tucksUnder`/`itemsFight`: an item offers space underneath when the catalogue publishes "Height Under Top" (which only desks and worktops carry), or failing that when it is desk-shaped (600-1100 mm tall, >= 800 mm wide); something tucks under it when it fits the clearance width and is no deeper than the top. Two desks in one spot stay red.
  - **Doors and windows** - the data model, the 2D wall breaks and the 3D lintels all existed and nothing could create one. New `openings` plan mode (tap a wall to add, drag to slide), three reducer actions, and `fitOpeningToWall`, which every write goes through: slid along when it hangs off the end, narrowed when the wall is shorter than it is, dropped only when the wall cannot hold it. Applied to every geometry change, so shortening a wall past a door does something honest with the door.
  - **Perspective on/off** in the 3D view. `createCamera`/`applyCameraAspect` and a `PlannerCamera` union; the swap replaces the camera AND the controls (OrbitControls binds to one camera for life) while the renderer and scene carry on, and the render loop reads both out of the ref rather than its own closure.
  - **Print became Export PDF.** `POST member/plans/[id]/pdf`, rate limited on the pictures window because it starts a headless browser. `lib/pdf.ts` is quote-for-shop's chromium arrangement copied (a dependent module does not add exports to the module it depends on) but printing `setContent` rather than a URL, because half the document is a canvas that only exists in the shopper's tab. The two drawings are photographed in the browser and posted as data URLs; prices are built server-side from the saved plan through shop's own resolution, never accepted from the client. The optional quote page takes its heading, intro, terms, validity and hide-prices rule from quote-for-shop's settings and carries the real quote number when the plan has been quoted. **No build change needed** - `/api/m/**` already traces `@sparticuz/chromium/bin` and both packages are already in `serverExternalPackages`.
  - **Views renamed** Flat plan -> **Edit**, 3D -> **Preview**; "Stand in it" removed (`eyeLevel` stays - the render worker's params still name an eye-level view). "Start the room again" -> **Start again**, with a tick to clear the furniture as well.
- **The three flagged follow-ups, same pass.** (a) `/public/products` returned name, price and image for **any** id, so an unauthenticated caller could read a DRAFT or ARCHIVED product by guessing. Now filtered on `status === 'ACTIVE'` **only** - `catalogue_hidden` is what marks a variation child, and variation children are exactly what that route exists to size. A plan holding a since-withdrawn product still draws: the sizes are on the item and the name and price are in `product_snapshot`. (b) Clearance guides measured to the room's **bounding box** along the screen axes - in an L-shape that is a wall that is not there, and a turned desk was measured across its own diagonal. New `distanceToWallAlong` casts from the middle of each face to whichever wall it actually reaches; three tests pin the L-shape case. (c) `resolveDimensions` wrote one row per product one statement at a time (24 on a browse page, up to 500 on the nightly sweep, four round trips each through PgBouncer); new `saveDimensionsMany` does it in one chunked upsert.
- **Live data, 2026-08-04**: all saved plans deleted from live Deskwell at the owner's explicit request - **one row**, theirs (`chris@dwoffice.furniture`), created that evening, not quoted, not shared, no renders. `spl_plan_versions` and `spl_render_jobs` cascade; `spl_rooms` deliberately untouched, so one empty room remains. Backup and per-row rollback SQL in the session scratchpad (`spl-backup.json`, `spl-plans-rollback.sql`). No DDL.
- **Checks**: `tsc --noEmit` and `eslint .` clean, 111 unit tests (geometry incl. the new snapping/clash/openings cases, units, the dimension parser, the ladder, the scene builder, the planner reducer + undo). The **backup round-trip gate ran for real and passed 3/3** on the 0.1.2 release; the bug-hunt pass changes no schema, no module migration and nothing under `lib/backup/**`, so it is not re-triggered. `lib/calibrate.live.test.ts` is the gated catalogue survey (`RUN_SPL_CALIBRATION=1`) - model-file inventory deduped by query-stripped url, parser dry run with the junk tail listed, categories with no fallback size.

### UK Bookkeeping

Module `uk-bookkeeping`, tablePrefix `bk_`, **v0.2.4 tagged** (repo `cactus-foundation-modules/uk-bookkeeping`). Core `modules.json` pins **v0.2.4**. `requiresCoreVersion 0.5.1156`. No `requiresModules`, no `publicBasePath`, no Puck blocks - everything it does happens behind the admin. Built to `plans/PLAN-uk-bookkeeping.md`; the 0.2.0 work (PDF statements, reconciliation, journals, director's loan) goes beyond that plan and is described below.

- **Sales handed over by another module (working tree, rides 0.2.0).** `migrations/008_external_sales.sql` adds `external_sales_enabled` (TRUE), `external_sales_category_id` (FK to `bk_categories`, NULL means the seeded `sales` code) and `external_sales_status` ('posted'|'draft') to `bk_settings`, plus `bk_transactions_source_ref_idx` on `("source","source_ref")`. `lib/external-sales.ts` exports `recordExternalSale` and registers `ukBookkeepingShopSaleRecorder` at shop's **`shop.invoice-issued`** point, and `reverseExternalSale` / `ukBookkeepingShopSaleVoider` at **`shop.invoice-voided`** (pure `planSaleRemoval` decides delete vs reversing adjustment; `reversalLines` negates the original's lines; reversal `source_ref` is `<invoice>:void`). The publisher's own PDF is filed as evidence against the entry (`fileDocument`), idempotent on the filename. It imports nothing from shop - the payload type is a structural copy, since this module has no `requiresModules` and compiles on sites with no shop. One transaction line per VAT rate (percent to rate code: 0 zero-rated, >=15 standard, else reduced - zero-rated rather than exempt or outside-scope, because only zero-rated belongs in box 6 and a shop's tax table only knows the rate it charged); `vat_treatment` always `domestic`. Idempotent on `source`+`source_ref`, so the shop's own re-send button cannot book a sale twice. A tax point inside a filed period is caught (`BackdatedIntoClosedPeriodError`) and re-saved as a **draft** with a sentence back to the caller, rather than being lost. Never throws: it runs inside the shop's write path. Settings section "Sales from elsewhere on this site" on `BookkeepingSettingsTab`, with the double-count warning for anyone also importing bank statements.
- **One ledger, since 0.2.4** (`lib/ledger.ts`). `LEDGER_SQL` is a `Prisma.Sql` projection with nine UNION ALL branches: posted cashbook lines become the debits and credits they always implied (net to the category's account or to `fixed-assets` when the line is capital; VAT to `vat-control`, or to `vat-deferred` under cash accounting; gross to `debtors`/`creditors` at the tax point; then bank and the clearing entry on settlement; plus the cash-scheme VAT transfer, and bank opening balances against `opening-balances`), unioned with posted journal lines. **Never a table.** A postings table would have to stay in step with rows that go hard-locked the moment a return is filed, and through a restore, and any drift would be silent. Debits and credits are non-negative by construction, so nothing downstream copes with a negative debit, and every branch balances on its own - which is why `trialBalance().balanced` being false is proof of interference rather than of rounding. `accountBalances`, `trialBalance` and `nominalLedger` live here; `lib/accounts.ts` re-exports them because that is where callers already look. `ledgerHealth()` reports missing control accounts, unmapped categories, duplicate category->account links, a non-zero suspense balance and an out-of-balance ledger, and rides along with `/health`.
- **`009_ledger_mapping.sql`** is the mapping that projection needs. `report_group`, `bs_group` and `disallowable_percent` on `bk_accounts`, all plain text with no CHECK on the first two (HMRC renumbers form groupings; that should be an edit, not a release). Every category now points at an account - the five 006 skipped are wired to `fixed-assets`, a new `dividends-drawings` EQUITY account, `capital-introduced`, `vat-control` and `corporation-tax`, so taking profit out stops being a "cost". New accounts: `stock`, `vat-deferred`, `loans`, `opening-balances`, `pl-corporation-tax`. New categories `entertaining` (disallowable 100) and `interest-received` (`non-trade-income`, so it lands in CT600 box 170 rather than in turnover). One ledger account per `bk_bank_account`, created here for existing rows and by `lib/bank-accounts.ts` thereafter, with the name kept in step on rename. Resolution is `DISTINCT ON`, not a unique index: a migration that failed on a live install would be worse than a deterministic choice.
- **Financial years** (`010_accounting_periods.sql`, `lib/accounting-periods.ts`). `bk_accounting_periods` with an open/closed lifecycle. Closing posts the retained-earnings journal (`source = 'year_end'`) and freezes the year; reopening deletes it, and refuses while a later year is closed or a final CT computation sits on it. **Application-enforced, never a trigger**, for the same restore reason `assertDatesNotInClosedPeriod` is - and `findClosedYearFor`/`assertNotInClosedYear` live in `lib/guards.ts` rather than here, to break the cycle (closing needs `createJournal`, journals need the check). `assertDatesNotInClosedPeriod` now calls it, so every cashbook path inherits it; `createJournal`/`updateJournal`/`deleteJournal` call it directly, and `updateJournal` checks BOTH the old and new dates. `previewYearEnd` produces the journal the screen shows AND the one that gets posted, so the two cannot differ. The close race is handled with a plain `DELETE` rather than `deleteJournal`, because by then the year is closed and `deleteJournal` would rightly refuse.
- **Fixed assets** (`011_fixed_assets.sql`, `lib/fixed-assets.ts`). `bk_fixed_assets` answers two questions from one row: depreciation for the accounts (`depreciation_method`, rate, residual) and `ca_pool` for the tax. Charges are pro-rated by the days the asset was OWNED, not the days in the period, never take it past its residual, and post as one journal for the whole run. `bk_depreciation_charges` has a unique index on `(asset_id, period_start, period_end)`, which is what makes a second run a no-op rather than a double charge, and cost and acquisition date go immutable once anything has been charged against them. **Since `013_asset_prompts.sql`** an asset can be raised by the module itself: `bk_transaction_lines.register_asset` is a per-LINE tick on the entry form (shown only on capital lines, and separate from `is_capital`, which stays the accounting treatment), and each ticked line raises one `status = 'draft'` asset keyed on `(transaction_id, transaction_line_position)` under a partial unique index. Drafts are inert - `listFixedAssets` returns `active` only unless asked, and `lib/corporation-tax.ts` filters to `active` - so nothing is depreciated and nothing is claimed until a human finishes it off on `FixedAssetsScreen`. `syncAssetDraftsForTransaction` after create/update/`postDraft`, `removeAssetDraftsForTransaction` before delete; unticking removes a draft and never an `active` row. The `ca_pool` choice is six radio cards with the case for each rather than a dropdown, and `unfinishedAssets` counts them on the dashboard.
- **Corporation tax** (`012_corporation_tax.sql`, `lib/corporation-tax.ts`). `bk_ct_rates` seeded FY2015-FY2026 (data, not code); `bk_ct_computations` with frozen `computation`/`boxes` JSONB and pool/loss figures carried forward; `bk_ct_adjustments` with 14 kinds, always entered positive, the kind deciding the direction. The computation runs profit-before-tax -> automatic add-backs from each account's `disallowable_percent` -> manual adjustments -> non-trade and property income lifted out of the trade -> capital allowances -> losses b/f capped at the trading profit -> TTP -> rates. **Marginal relief is F x (U - A) x N/A**, augmented profits deciding the rate and TTP deciding what it applies to, limits scaled by days in each FY and divided by associated companies + 1. `splitIntoTaxPeriods` splits a period of account over twelve months into two tax periods. Capital allowances cover AIA (capped, pro-rated, excess spilling to the main pool), full expensing (and its immediate balancing charge on disposal), 50% FYA with the balance to the special pool, 18%/6% WDA, the small pools write-off, disposals capped at cost and negative pools becoming charges; rates are days-weighted across the FYs a period touches. **Box numbers were transcribed from HMRC's own CT600 (2026) Version 3 PDF.** It produces the computation and the boxes; **it does not file**, because there is no HMRC API for a small company to self-file corporation tax, and the screen says so. R&D, patent box, group relief arithmetic, ring fence, NI rates, s455, SBA and the super-deduction are absent on purpose and can each be entered as a named adjustment.
- **Reports, rebuilt on the ledger** (`lib/reports.ts`). `profitAndLoss` in Companies Act Format 1 order with a same-length prior period beside it; `balanceSheet` with a `balanced` flag and the un-transferred profit shown as its own reserve line; `agedAnalysis` for both directions read straight off unsettled entries so it agrees with the balance sheet by construction; `monthlyBreakdown` moved onto the ledger so journals appear in it. `categorySummary` deliberately still reads the cashbook - it answers "what did I code where, and what VAT was on it", which is a cashbook question - and `groupForTaxReturn` is now the sole trader's SA103 grouping only.
- **New screens and routes.** Routes: `reports/balance-sheet`, `reports/trial-balance`, `reports/nominal`, `reports/aged`, `accounting-periods[/id][/close]`, `fixed-assets[/id][/dispose]`, `depreciation`, `corporation-tax[/id][/adjustments/[adjustmentId]][/finalise]`. Screens: `ReportsScreen` rebuilt as six tabs over one date range, with any figure clicking through to that account's full history; `YearEndScreen`, `FixedAssetsScreen`, `CorporationTaxScreen`; `components/admin/ui.tsx` holds the shared table chrome. Nav tabs gain Assets, Year end and Corporation tax. Permissions: reads `bookkeeping.access`, assets/adjustments/computations `bookkeeping.record`, closing a year and finishing a computation `bookkeeping.submit`.
- **Tests added.** `lib/corporation-tax.test.ts` - 30 pure tests covering the 1 April boundary, long-period splitting, small/main/marginal bands and the exact boundary, associated companies, franked investment income raising the rate without being taxed, short-period scaling, FY straddles, and each capital allowances pool. `lib/ledger-projection.live.test.ts` - 14 tests against a throwaway Postgres (gated with the other live suites), asserting the figures and, after every one of them, that total debits equal total credits. Added to `npm run test:ledger-guards`.
- **What it is**: UK bookkeeping with Making Tax Digital VAT returns. Records with evidence, a pure SQL layer that turns records into the nine VAT boxes, periods with a three-state lifecycle and a frozen snapshot, and an HMRC client behind one interface. **No box value is ever typed by a human, in any code path** - there is no service function anywhere that accepts a box value as an argument, and no input field on any screen for one. That is the digital-links requirement and it is the reason the module exists in this shape.
- **Permissions**: `bookkeeping.access` (see it), `bookkeeping.record` (record entries and evidence, bulk-review drafts, form suggestions, import a statement, match and unmatch, write journals), `bookkeeping.submit` (finalise, file, generate periods, and - since the hardening pass - the HMRC liabilities/payments reads, because `buildCallContext` can rotate the single-use refresh token), `bookkeeping.settings` (settings, categories, bank accounts, ledger accounts, the HMRC connection). One `navEntries` link -> `/m/uk-bookkeeping/overview`, tabbed to Overview / Entries / Journals / Reconcile / Director's loan / VAT returns / Reports / Import; settings as a `settingsTabs` panel. Admin API: `GET admin/dashboard` (overview figures, `lib/dashboard.ts`), `POST admin/transactions/bulk` (post/delete drafts, per-row outcomes), `GET admin/transactions/suggest` (known counterparties; with `?counterparty=` the usual category), `admin/bank-accounts[/id]`, `admin/bank-transactions[/id]` (one POST carrying match / unmatch / ignore / unignore), `admin/journals[/id]` (POST on the id posts a draft, or reverses with `{action:'reverse'}`), `admin/accounts[/id]`, `GET admin/director-loan`. `admin/import` GET lists presets and accounts, POST previews (CSV or PDF, `runtime = 'nodejs'` because the PDF reader inflates streams with node:zlib), PUT commits. Export kinds: transactions, lines, attachments, journals, journal-lines, accounts, bank-transactions, reconciliations, periods, snapshots, snapshot-lines, hmrc-calls, audit - keyset-paged, formula-escaped.
- **Env vars**: `HMRC_CLIENT_ID` and `HMRC_CLIENT_SECRET`, both `required: false`. Read from `process.env` only - never written to the database, rendered in a page, or logged. Missing them is a normal state and is what every install looks like on day one; the module then works in full except for filing. Since 0.1.5 the settings tab takes both as paste-in fields saving through core's `/api/admin/env` (already in the managed set via the manifest's `requiredEnvVars`), with a numbered Developer Hub walkthrough; they still take hold only on the next deployment.
- **Tables** (`001_initial.sql`): `bk_categories` (22 seeded system rows, SA103F box and a coarse CT600 grouping on each), `bk_vat_periods`, `bk_transactions`, `bk_transaction_lines`, `bk_attachments`, `bk_period_snapshots`, `bk_period_snapshot_lines`, `bk_audit_log`, `bk_settings` (singleton; gains `first_period_end` DATE in `004_first_period_end.sql` - the HMRC first-period end from the registration letter, month-end aligned, from which `lib/period-dates.ts` lays every later period out on calendar months with computed due dates), `bk_hmrc_connection` (singleton), `bk_hmrc_oauth_states`, `bk_hmrc_api_calls`, `bk_import_batches`. **No Postgres ENUM types anywhere** - TEXT + CHECK. Money is **NUMERIC(10,2)** throughout, matching shop; every FK is `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` because a backup restore inserts row by row and a self-reference (`corrects_transaction_id`) or forward reference (`locked_period_id`) is routinely unsatisfied halfway through.
- **`002_immutability.sql` is the schema half of "a filed return cannot be edited", and it is written around the restore path.** `lib/backup/restore.ts` truncates and re-inserts inside one transaction **without** `session_replication_role = replica` and without disabling triggers, so row triggers fire on restore. TRUNCATE fires none, so UPDATE/DELETE guards are free; the two BEFORE INSERT guards only ever read the NEW row's own `locked_period_id`, which a restored child already carries, so they are never reached. **There is deliberately NO trigger on backdating into a closed period** - a restore re-inserts years of transactions dated inside long-submitted periods, and such a trigger would reject most of a restore and only show it during an actual disaster recovery. That rule lives in `lib/guards.ts` instead, with the reason written above it.
- **Two carve-outs in the guards, both load-bearing.** `bk_attachments` allows the four storage-pointer columns (`url`, `media_key`, `media_provider`, `media_id`) to change on a locked row and refuses everything else - core moves a media blob on optimise/rename/replace/re-file and repoints every module's copy through `core.media-reference-rewriters`, so without it moving one filed receipt in the media library would fail with an accounting error and leave the download 404ing. Since `003_attachment_guard_columns.sql` (2026-08-21) the refusal genuinely covers everything else - 002's function left `position`, `uploaded_by_user_id` and `created_at` mutable on locked rows despite its comment claiming only the pointers got through; 003 supersedes the function (`CREATE OR REPLACE`, same trigger name) rather than editing the released 002. `bk_hmrc_api_calls` is write-once rather than append-only: the row is inserted BEFORE the request goes out (so a timeout leaves a trace) and completed after, and the guard permits exactly that one completion - filling outcome columns that are still null - and nothing else.
- **The lock is one-way by construction.** The trigger tests `OLD."locked_period_id" IS NOT NULL`, so submission's own `UPDATE ... WHERE locked_period_id IS NULL` is permitted (OLD is still null) and every write after it is refused, including one clearing the lock.
- **What layer 3 does not protect against, stated rather than implied**: the app connects as the table owner, and a table owner can `ALTER TABLE ... DISABLE TRIGGER`. So `lib/health.ts` reads `pg_trigger` for all ten triggers and any missing or `tgenabled <> 'O'` puts a red banner on every bookkeeping page plus an audit row. `EXPECTED_TRIGGERS` is unit-tested against a count, so the migration and the health check cannot drift apart silently. (`FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` was considered and rejected for v1 - it does bind the owner, but the lock-setting update would then need its own policy or a SECURITY DEFINER function, and RLS produces "no rows updated" rather than a sentence a site owner can read.)
- **The box query** (`lib/vat-boxes.ts`). One `CLASSIFY` SQL fragment, used by both the totals query and the workings query, so the explanation cannot drift from the answer. The scheme decides **one thing only** - which date column selects the rows (`tax_point_date` for accrual, `settled_date` for cash, an unpaid invoice being in no cash period at all) - so both schemes are one code path. `entry_type` is carried through and never filtered on: an adjustment is an ordinary line for box purposes, which is how a correction reaches a return. A period stores the scheme it was worked under, so recomputing a 2024 return in 2027 after a scheme change gives the 2024 answer.
- **Money discipline.** `NUMERIC(10,2)` arrives as `Prisma.Decimal`; `lib/money.ts` is the only file allowed to turn one into a string, and `Number()` on one is a named code-review item. **Box values are decimal STRINGS everywhere**, and `lib/hmrc/payload.ts` composes the submission body as TEXT rather than through `JSON.stringify` over parsed numbers - HMRC's schema wants JSON numbers, and `1234.55` written into a JSON document is a valid number literal, so no float ever exists on our side. Every value is validated against a two-decimal shape (and a `.00` shape for boxes 6-9) before it goes near the string.
- **Two corrections to the plan, both from reading HMRC's own current documents rather than from memory.** (1) Boxes 6-9 are described by the VAT (MTD) API as "a monetary value (to 2 **zeroed** decimal places)", so they are whole pounds carrying `.00` - not bare integers, which is what the plan assumed. (2) **Form VAT652 was withdrawn on 5 September 2025**; the separate notification is now made through HMRC's online error-correction service, so every reference points at VAT Notice 700/45 instead. The Method 1 thresholds themselves (£10,000, or £10,000-£50,000 where it does not exceed 1% of box 6) were confirmed current on 2026-08-20 and ship as three settings with those defaults, so a rule change is an edit rather than a release.
- **The one open question the plan flagged that HMRC does not answer: rounding for boxes 6-9.** VAT Notice 700/12 says what goes in each box and nothing about pence, and 700 covers rounding on invoices rather than on the return. So it is a `box_rounding` setting - `nearest` (default) or `down` - applied exactly once, identically to all four, with `boxes_unrounded` kept in every snapshot. `down` uses `ROUND_FLOOR` rather than `ROUND_DOWN` so a negative box goes the same way as a positive one.
- **Fraud prevention headers** (`lib/hmrc/fraud-spec.ts`). Transcribed from HMRC's WEB_APP_VIA_SERVER page, **read in full on 2026-08-20**, with the URL and date in the file - it is not to be edited from memory. Sixteen headers. Note what is NOT in that set, because the plan assumed otherwise: `Gov-Client-Local-IPs`, `-Local-IPs-Timestamp`, `Gov-Client-Browser-Plugins` and `-Do-Not-Track` do not appear on that page at all, and `Gov-Vendor-Product-Name` (which the plan omitted) is required. Browser-only signals are collected by `lib/hmrc/fraud-client.ts` and posted in the body; `Gov-Client-Public-IP` comes from the **leftmost** `x-forwarded-for` entry and never from anything the browser claims about itself.
- **Q3 answered.** `Gov-Vendor-Public-IP` is "the public IP of the servers the originating device sent their requests to" - which is the edge answering for the site's own hostname, not the function's egress address. So it is resolved with `dns.resolve4` on the site's own host and cached for the warm function, with a settings override for an operator behind a static-IP proxy. A hostname with no A record omits the header, which HMRC's page allows for.
- **Token handling.** AES-256-GCM through core's `lib/crypto/secrets.ts`. Every read goes through `tryDecryptSecret`, and null means "reconnect" rather than an error - a restored backup carries ciphertext written under a different `ENCRYPTION_KEY`, and the owner should be told to reconnect, not shown an OpenSSL message. Refresh is lazy with a 60s margin, the refresh token **rotates on use** and is re-stored every time, and because PgBouncer runs transaction pooling (no session advisory locks) two concurrent refreshes are resolved by a conditional `UPDATE ... WHERE date_trunc('milliseconds', last_refresh_at) IS NOT DISTINCT FROM date_trunc('milliseconds', :seen)` - **truncated both sides on purpose**: the column carries microseconds, a JS Date carries milliseconds, and comparing them raw made every refresh look like a lost race and killed the connection at every expiry. The loser re-reads the winner's token rather than using its own (already superseded), and a 5xx/429 refresh failure is surfaced as transient rather than burning the connection to 'expired'.
- **The OAuth callback is `/api/m/uk-bookkeeping/hmrc/callback` and is deliberately outside the admin path**, so the string is identical on every install and printing it in the setup guide is possible. It is the module's only ungated route - HMRC is the caller and holds no session - and is protected by a single-use ten-minute `state` plus a check that the returning browser is the same signed-in admin who started it. It resolves the admin path with `getAdminPathCached()` rather than `x-cactus-admin-path`, because core only stamps that header on admin PAGE rewrites and an API route never sees it.
- **Submission is deliberately not one transaction** - a network call sits in the middle. Before sending, the boxes are recomputed and compared against the finalised snapshot and **any** difference aborts. Inside the closing transaction the lock goes on LAST, after the receipt is stored, so a crash between the two leaves a period that is submitted-and-unlocked (recoverable, visible) rather than locked-with-no-receipt. A `DUPLICATE_SUBMISSION` never rolls the period back to open; it offers "check with HMRC", which reads `viewReturn` and completes the local record only if HMRC's figures match ours exactly.
- **The hash chain, and the honest caveat.** `bk_audit_log` and `bk_period_snapshots` both carry `chain_index`/`prev_hash`/`row_hash`, computed in application code and **never in a trigger** - a trigger would recompute hashes during a restore and destroy the chain it was meant to protect. A chain alone proves nothing to somebody whose only copy is the database, so every filing emails the operator a receipt carrying the chain head, which then lives in a mailbox this software cannot reach; the same head is in the settings panel and in every export.
- **Evidence.** PDF/JPEG/PNG/WebP, 15 MB (a setting), through core's media abstraction with `provider` + `key` + `media_id` stored, so a download survives deletion of the library row. Magic-byte sniffing is in-module (`lib/file-kinds.ts`) because core's sharp-based sniff is image-only and does not cover PDF. HEIC gets its own sentence. **No virus scanning anywhere in Cactus, and this does not invent any** - said plainly in the upload panel and the wiki.
- **Reports and export.** Category summary and P&L read the tax point regardless of VAT scheme (a P&L is about when the trade happened). Exports stream rather than buffer, so six years fits inside the module dispatcher's fixed `maxDuration = 60`.
- **Bank import** lands every new entry as `status = 'draft'`, which reaches no box. Since 0.2.0 the import is statement-shaped rather than row-shaped: the bank's own lines are kept, matched against what is already recorded, and only what is left becomes a draft. All parsing, mapping and arithmetic happen before the first database round trip - the ordering lesson the Google Sheets importer already paid for - and both the duplicate check and the match suggestions are ONE query for the whole file, never one per line.
- **PDF statements, with no dependency** (`lib/pdf/lexer.ts`, `lib/pdf/document.ts`, `lib/pdf/text.ts`, ~700 lines). Every PDF library that does this properly is built to RENDER pages; this needs one narrow thing, "what text is on the page and where", which is the whole of those three files. Objects are found by scanning for `N G obj` rather than by following the xref (statement generators leave wrong xrefs often enough that every real reader has this fallback); PDF 1.5 object streams are unpacked; `/Encrypt` and a page with no text operators are refused in sentences a site owner can act on rather than returning noise. **The trap that cost the most: a hex string in a content stream is BYTES, two hex digits each.** Reading `<000A>` as one 16-bit code unit rather than as two bytes silently drops that glyph and every other glyph written that way - the statement came out missing its capital Cs, its pound signs and half its digits, with no error anywhere. `hexToBytes` and `hexToUnicode` are separate functions for that reason. Second trap: `[` and `]` must NOT clear the operand stack, or every `TJ` array's strings are gone before the operator runs. Third: row grouping sorts by **page first**, then y - sorting on y alone interleaves two pages wherever they put text at the same height, which for a statement is everywhere, and then no row gathers more than one cell.
- **Reading the table is layout-driven, not bank-specific** (`lib/statement-pdf.ts`). Find the header row (a row naming a date column and at least one money column), take the columns from where its words sit, put every later cell in the column its x position says it belongs to, and attach wrapped description lines to the nearest dated row within 34pt. The only bank knowledge is header SYNONYMS ("Paid out", "Money out", "Debit", "Withdrawn" are one column under four names). **The statement's own running balance is the check**: line n's balance should be line n-1's plus line n's amount, and the direction that agrees settles both "were the columns read the right way round" and "does this statement run newest-first" - the latter being the only thing that can order two payments made on the same afternoon, which a date sort cannot. Statement totals are checked against what was read and shown to the reviewer before anything is written.
- **`005_bank_statements.sql`**: `bk_bank_accounts`, `bk_bank_statements`, `bk_bank_transactions` (the bank's version, never edited to agree with the books - that is the whole point of keeping it), `bk_reconciliations` (many-to-many: one line can settle several entries and one entry can be settled by several lines). `bk_transactions` gains `bank_account_id` + `statement_id`; `bk_settings` gains `year_end_month` / `year_end_day`. Duplicate imports are stopped by a **unique index on (bank_account_id, fingerprint)** where the fingerprint is sha256 over date + amount + heavily normalised details; a statement genuinely can print the same payment twice on one day (two identical £1.20 charges from one host, which the statement this was written against does), so twins are salted by position rather than folded into one. `bk_import_batches` is kept for its historic rows and no longer written to.
- **Reconciliation** (`lib/reconciliation.ts`). A line is reconciled only when the entries matched to it account for ALL of it, to the penny - a part-matched line stays open and says how much is unexplained. The matcher requires the amount to agree **exactly** (a matcher willing to be approximate about money will eventually tie a £95 invoice to a £59 one) and uses date proximity, name similarity and reference equality only to rank. A suggestion is auto-ticked only when it is clearly the only one (`confidentMatch`: score >= 140 and >= 30 clear of the runner-up), because a wrong match is worse than no match - it looks explained, so nobody looks again.
- **`006_accounts_and_journals.sql`**: `bk_accounts` (one list: balance-sheet accounts plus one `pl-*` account per trading category, so a depreciation journal and a receipt coded to Depreciation land in the same place on a report), `bk_journals`, `bk_journal_lines` (debit and credit as two columns, never one signed one). Seeds a UK chart plus a `directors-loan` account AND a matching `directors-loan` category, pointed at each other - without that link a bank transfer to the director and a journal to the loan account would land in two different places.
- **A journal reaches no VAT box, ever, and that is not a gap to fill in later.** "No box value is ever typed by a human" is the guarantee the module exists for, and a journal that could reach box 1 would be exactly such a figure. Anything with VAT on it is a transaction. Consequence worth knowing: journals are also **not locked by filing a VAT return** - depreciation and year-end accruals are dated at the year end and posted months later, inside a long-filed quarter, and refusing those would refuse the main thing journals are for. The lock columns and their guards exist for a closed accounting year, when there is one; nothing sets them today.
- **`007_journal_immutability.sql`.** The balance check is a **CONSTRAINT TRIGGER, DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED**, and it has to be: a per-row check would fail on the first line of every journal ever written (the second line has not arrived yet) and would reject a backup restore, which inserts rows one at a time in exactly that shape. Deferred to COMMIT it is right in both cases. Drafts are exempt - a journal being typed is half-finished by definition. `EXPECTED_TRIGGERS` in `lib/health.ts` now covers 16 triggers, and the unit test **parses the migration files** for `CREATE [CONSTRAINT] TRIGGER` and asserts the two lists match exactly, rather than checking a hardcoded count that only catches drift if somebody remembers to update it.
- **Director's loan** (`lib/director-loan.ts`). One SQL statement unions the two sources (journal lines on the account, cashbook entries coded to the loan category) and runs the running balance as a window function, so the arithmetic is exact decimal throughout and it is a single round trip. Sign convention stated once: it is a LIABILITY, so a credit balance means the company owes the director and a debit balance means the director owes the company - and the screen says which in words, never as a bare negative. `balance` is the position **today** regardless of any date filter, and a filtered statement carries `broughtForward` so its running balance does not restart at zero and read as though the loan began on whatever date was typed into the filter. Reports the year-end position, the nine-months-and-a-day section 455 date and the £10,000 benefit-in-kind question; **works out nobody's tax** and says so.
- **`lib/ledger-guards.live.test.ts` + `npm run test:ledger-guards`** (gated on `RUN_LEDGER_GUARDS=1` or the round-trip flag, uses the same `cactus_rt_*` throwaway databases). Nine tests against a real Postgres, because a trigger that does not fire looks exactly like one that does until the day it matters: an unbalanced posted journal is refused, a balanced one built one line at a time is accepted, a draft may sit half-written but may not be posted, both-sides/neither-side/negative lines are refused, a locked journal cannot be changed/deleted/added to, one statement line cannot be imported twice (but the same payment on a different account can), and **every migration re-runs cleanly**, which is what an install update actually does. Note `pg` now reads `sslmode=require` as full verification and the VPS certificate is issued for the site hostname, so the test appends `uselibpqcompat=true`.
- **The raw-`pg` blind spot, and what closed it (0.2.2).** `ledger-guards.live.test.ts` drives a raw `pg` client, so it proves what is in `migrations/*.sql` and nothing about the SQL in the service layer - and every service query goes through Prisma's parameter binding, which types things differently. That gap shipped a statement importer that could not run once: `${dates[0]}::date - ${DATE_WINDOW_DAYS}` became `date - bigint`, which Postgres has no operator for, so every import 500'd. `lib/import-roundtrip.live.test.ts` now runs preview -> match -> commit -> re-import through the **real Prisma client** against a throwaway database, and `npm run test:ledger-guards` runs both files. **Rule for any module: a JS number in raw SQL arithmetic needs an explicit cast** (`::int`); assignment into an int4 column is fine, because there Postgres has an assignment cast where it has no operator.
- **Checks (0.2.0)**: `tsc --noEmit` clean, `eslint .` clean, `npm test` **2453 passed / 29 skipped**, `npm run test:backup-roundtrip` a real **3 passed / 0 skipped** (new module migrations, so the gate applies), and `npm run test:ledger-guards` a real **9 passed / 0 skipped**. `lib/backup/schema-coverage.test.ts` parses all seven migration files and confirms every column type has a serialiser branch. `lib/statement-pdf.test.ts` builds its PDFs in the test rather than checking one in - a real statement is somebody's bank details, and a hand-built one can carry the exact awkwardness that broke the reader (two-byte fonts, hex strings, kerning instead of spaces, descriptions wrapped over three lines) rather than whatever a convenient real file happens to have.
- **Not in v1, and each stated in the wiki rather than hidden**: Flat Rate Scheme, partial exemption, margin schemes, bad debt relief, MTD for Income Tax, more than one VRN per install, and partial payments under cash accounting (a single `settled_date` puts an invoice wholly in or wholly out of a period; the upgrade is a `bk_settlements` child table and a change to one CTE).
